diff --git a/test/jido_ai/skill/agent_integration_test.exs b/test/jido_ai/skill/agent_integration_test.exs
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..45bc5763
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/jido_ai/skill/agent_integration_test.exs
@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+defmodule Jido.AI.Skill.AgentIntegrationTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
+
+  alias Jido.AI.Actions.Skill.LoadSkill
+  alias Jido.AI.Skill.AgentIntegration
+
+  @moduletag :tmp_dir
+
+  defmodule TestCalculator do
+    use Jido.Action,
+      name: "calculator",
+      description: "A simple calculator"
+
+    def run(_params, _ctx), do: {:ok, %{result: 0}}
+  end
+
+  # The contract requires a `use Jido.AI.Agent` `agent_skills` option together
+  # with a publicly callable operation that prepares the integration from a
+  # configuration. These tests exercise the integration exclusively through
+  # that documented surface, the `agent_skills` macro option, which validates
+  # and prepares the configuration when the agent instance initializes. No
+  # internal module or function name is pinned.
+  #
+  # The agent module is defined through Code.compile_string/1 with the
+  # configuration embedded as a literal so the `agent_skills` macro option
+  # receives exactly the value under test, mirroring the consumer-facing macro.
+  defp define_agent(config) do
+    module_name =
+      Module.concat(__MODULE__, :"Agent#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}")
+
+    Code.compile_string("""
+    defmodule #{inspect(module_name)} do
+      use Jido.AI.Agent,
+        name: "integration_test_agent",
+        tools: [#{inspect(TestCalculator)}],
+        system_prompt: "Base instructions.",
+        agent_skills: #{inspect(config)}
+    end
+    """)
+
+    module_name
+  end
+
+  # Read the documented error category from the public preparation result,
+  # rather than depending on how agent initialization wraps plugin failures.
+  defp prepare_operation do
+    [
+      {AgentIntegration, :prepare},
+      {Jido.AI.Skill.Integration, :prepare},
+      {Jido.AI.Agent, :prepare_agent_skills},
+      {Jido.AI.Agent, :prepare_skills},
+      {Module.concat([Jido.AI, Skill, AgentSkills]), :prepare},
+      {Module.concat([Jido.AI, Agent, Skills]), :prepare},
+      {Module.concat([Jido.AI, Agent, Skills]), :prepare_skills}
+    ]
+    |> Enum.find(fn {module, name} ->
+      Code.ensure_loaded?(module) and function_exported?(module, name, 1)
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp assert_prepare_error(category, options) do
+    assert prepare_operation(), "agent skills integration must expose a public preparation operation"
+    {module, name} = prepare_operation()
+
+    # `paths` and `roots` are both used by public integration facades; supplying
+    # both keeps this behavioural check independent of a particular facade.
+    options =
+      case Keyword.fetch(options, :paths) do
+        {:ok, paths} -> Keyword.put_new(options, :roots, paths)
+        :error -> options
+      end
+
+    result = apply(module, name, [options])
+    assert {:error, reason} = result
+    assert inspect(reason) =~ category
+  end
+
+  defp assert_any_raise(fun) do
+    fun.()
+  rescue
+    error -> error
+  else
+    result -> raise "expected agent initialization to raise, but succeeded with: #{inspect(result)}"
+  end
+
+  test "disabled integration is empty" do
+    for skills_config <- [false, []] do
+      agent = define_agent(skills_config).new()
+      config = Jido.Agent.Strategy.State.get(agent, %{}).config
+
+      # No specs are prepared: no skill-loading tool is added, the disclosure
+      # index contributes nothing, and the tool context gains no prepared specs.
+      refute LoadSkill in Jido.AI.list_tools(agent)
+      assert config.system_prompt =~ "Base instructions."
+      assert config.base_tool_context[LoadSkill.context_skills_key()] in [nil, %{}]
+    end
+  end
+
+  test "prepares progressive disclosure from explicitly trusted roots", %{tmp_dir: tmp_dir} do
+    skill_dir = Path.join(tmp_dir, "review")
+    File.mkdir_p!(Path.join(skill_dir, "references"))
+
+    File.write!(Path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"), """
+    ---
+    name: review
+    description: Review code when asked for feedback.
+    ---
+    """)
+
+    File.write!(Path.join([skill_dir, "references", "checks.md"]), "Checks")
+
+    # Explicitly trusted roots yield a named spec catalog, a disclosure index
+    # of names and descriptions only, the skill-loading tool, and the specs
+    # under the reserved tool-context key.
+    agent = define_agent(paths: [tmp_dir], roots: [tmp_dir], trust: true).new()
+    config = Jido.Agent.Strategy.State.get(agent, %{}).config
+
+    assert LoadSkill in Jido.AI.list_tools(agent)
+    assert config.system_prompt =~ "Base instructions."
+    assert config.system_prompt =~ "review"
+    assert config.system_prompt =~ "Review code when asked for feedback."
+    refute config.system_prompt =~ "# Review instructions"
+
+    specs = config.base_tool_context[LoadSkill.context_skills_key()]
+    assert %{"review" => review_spec} = specs
+    assert %Jido.AI.Skill.Spec{name: "review"} = review_spec
+  end
+
+  test "public preparation returns the integration data", %{tmp_dir: tmp_dir} do
+    skill_dir = Path.join(tmp_dir, "direct-preparation")
+    File.mkdir_p!(skill_dir)
+
+    File.write!(
+      Path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"),
+      "---\nname: direct-preparation\ndescription: Prepared directly.\n---\nHidden body.\n"
+    )
+
+    assert prepare_operation(), "agent skills integration must expose a public preparation operation"
+    {module, name} = prepare_operation()
+
+    assert {:ok, %{specs: specs, index: index, tools: tools, tool_context: tool_context}} =
+             apply(module, name, [[paths: [tmp_dir], roots: [tmp_dir], trust: true]])
+
+    assert tools == [LoadSkill]
+    spec_values = if is_map(specs), do: Map.values(specs), else: specs
+    assert Enum.any?(spec_values, &(&1.name == "direct-preparation"))
+    assert index =~ "direct-preparation"
+    assert index =~ "Prepared directly."
+    refute index =~ "Hidden body."
+    assert %{"direct-preparation" => _spec} = tool_context[LoadSkill.context_skills_key()]
+  end
+
+  test "keyword path configuration does not expose an untrusted root", %{tmp_dir: tmp_dir} do
+    skill_dir = Path.join(tmp_dir, "keyword-trust")
+    File.mkdir_p!(skill_dir)
+
+    File.write!(
+      Path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"),
+      "---\nname: keyword-trust\ndescription: A valid skill.\n---\nSkill body.\n"
+    )
+
+    assert prepare_operation(), "agent skills integration must expose a public preparation operation"
+    {module, name} = prepare_operation()
+    result = apply(module, name, [[paths: [tmp_dir]]])
+
+    case result do
+      {:error, reason} ->
+        assert inspect(reason) =~ "untrusted_skill_path"
+
+      {:ok, %{specs: specs}} ->
+        refute Map.has_key?(specs, "keyword-trust"),
+               "a keyword path without explicit trust must not load its root"
+    end
+  end
+
+  test "supports an explicit trust gate", %{tmp_dir: tmp_dir} do
+    # An explicitly disabled trust policy rejects the root with the documented
+    # untrusted-path category.
+    assert_prepare_error("untrusted_skill_path", paths: [tmp_dir], trust: false)
+
+    # The same roots initialize successfully once trust is explicitly enabled:
+    # an agent instance is produced without raising.
+    agent = define_agent(paths: [tmp_dir], roots: [tmp_dir], trust: true).new()
+    assert is_struct(agent)
+  end
+
+  test "rejects invalid path entries" do
+    # Integration preparation rejects non-binary path entries with the
+    # documented invalid-configuration error category.
+    assert_prepare_error("invalid_discovery_option, :paths", paths: [:not_a_path])
+  end
+
+  test "rejects specification-invalid skills instead of silently normalizing them", %{tmp_dir: tmp_dir} do
+    skill_dir = Path.join(tmp_dir, "actual-name")
+    File.mkdir_p!(skill_dir)
+
+    File.write!(
+      Path.join(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"),
+      "---\nname: different-name\ndescription: Invalid directory match\n---\n"
+    )
+
+    assert_prepare_error("directory_name_mismatch", paths: [tmp_dir], trust: true)
+    assert_any_raise(fn -> define_agent(paths: [tmp_dir], roots: [tmp_dir], trust: true).new() end)
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
[Feature]: Handle slightly broken JSON in structured outputs
### Feature Type

Provider feature extension

### Provider (if applicable)

_No response_

### Description

We sometimes see slightly broken JSON emitted from some models (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`) even when defining a JSON response schema. Maybe we could integrate [JsonRemedy](https://github.com/nshkrdotcom/json_remedy) before we decode the model output to try repair any fixable issues?

### Example Usage

Ideally this would be transparent to the user with the ability to optionally disable it.

### Can you contribute this?

Yes, with guidance

### Additional contract requirements

Structured output from model providers may contain lightly malformed JSON
(for example a trailing comma after the last entry, content wrapped in a
markdown code fence, or delimiters missing at the end of the payload). The
library makes a best-effort attempt to repair such structured output before
decoding it, and this repair behavior is controllable by the caller.

Observable requirements:

- A boolean keyword option `:json_repair` controls the repair behavior.
  Repair is applied by default; passing `json_repair: false` keeps decoding
  strict. The base generation options schema exposed by
  `ReqLLM.Generation.schema/0` includes the `:json_repair` option declared
  as a boolean with a default of `true`.

- `ReqLLM.Generation.generate_object/4` honors `json_repair` end to end.
  This holds for tool-call based structured output, for content-based
  structured output, and for the Google Gemini family of models. With
  repair enabled, a lightly malformed structured-output payload (for
  example a trailing comma or a missing final delimiter) still yields the
  decoded object on the returned response; with `json_repair: false` the
  same payload is left untouched and the response object is `nil`.

- `ReqLLM.ToolCall.args_map/2` accepts an optional keyword list as its
  second argument and honors the repair option: with repair enabled, a
  lightly malformed arguments string decodes to its map; with
  `json_repair: false` the same string decodes to `nil`. `ReqLLM.ToolCall.find_args/3`
  accepts an optional keyword list as its third argument and applies the
  same behavior.

- `ReqLLM.Response.unwrap_object/2` accepts an optional keyword list as
  its second argument and honors the repair option: with repair enabled,
  lightly malformed JSON in the response text content (including JSON
  wrapped in a markdown code fence) decodes successfully; with
  `json_repair: false` a payload that is not valid JSON as-is returns
  `{:error, %ReqLLM.Error.API.Response{}}`.
- Repairing malformed JSON must preserve UTF-8 string values in the payload.

- The repair behavior is available in the library's standard test
  environment for every supported provider option set; no additional
  runtime setup or package dependency is required to exercise it.

diff --git a/lib/req_llm/json.ex b/lib/req_llm/json.ex
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..cc008d387
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/req_llm/json.ex
@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
+defmodule ReqLLM.JSON do
+  @moduledoc false
+
+  @spec decode(term(), keyword()) :: {:ok, term()} | {:error, term()}
+  def decode(json, opts \\ [])
+
+  def decode(json, opts) when is_binary(json) do
+    case Jason.decode(json) do
+      {:ok, _parsed} = ok ->
+        ok
+
+      {:error, error} ->
+        if json_repair_enabled?(opts) do
+          repaired = repair(json)
+
+          if repaired == json do
+            {:error, error}
+          else
+            Jason.decode(repaired)
+          end
+        else
+          {:error, error}
+        end
+    end
+  end
+
+  def decode(_json, _opts), do: {:error, :invalid_json}
+
+  defp json_repair_enabled?(opts) when is_list(opts), do: Keyword.get(opts, :json_repair, true)
+  defp json_repair_enabled?(opts) when is_map(opts), do: Map.get(opts, :json_repair, true)
+  defp json_repair_enabled?(_opts), do: true
+
+  defp repair(json) do
+    json
+    |> strip_bom()
+    |> normalize_quotes()
+    |> strip_code_fences()
+    |> extract_json_payload()
+    |> remove_trailing_commas()
+    |> close_unbalanced_delimiters()
+  end
+
+  defp strip_bom(<<239, 187, 191, rest::binary>>), do: rest
+  defp strip_bom(json), do: json
+
+  defp normalize_quotes(json) do
+    json
+    |> String.replace(["\u201c", "\u201d"], "\"")
+    |> String.replace(["\u2018", "\u2019"], "'")
+  end
+
+  defp strip_code_fences(json) do
+    case Regex.run(~r/\A```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```\z/s, String.trim(json),
+           capture: :all_but_first
+         ) do
+      [inner] -> inner
+      _ -> json
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp extract_json_payload(json) do
+    trimmed = String.trim(json)
+
+    case first_json_boundary(trimmed) do
+      nil ->
+        trimmed
+
+      {start_index, _opening, closing} ->
+        candidate = String.slice(trimmed, start_index..-1//1)
+
+        case last_grapheme_index(candidate, closing) do
+          nil -> candidate
+          end_index -> String.slice(candidate, 0, end_index + 1)
+        end
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp first_json_boundary(json) do
+    json
+    |> String.graphemes()
+    |> Enum.with_index()
+    |> Enum.find_value(fn
+      {"{", index} -> {index, "{", "}"}
+      {"[", index} -> {index, "[", "]"}
+      _ -> nil
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp last_grapheme_index(json, target) do
+    json
+    |> String.graphemes()
+    |> Enum.with_index()
+    |> Enum.reduce(nil, fn
+      {^target, index}, _acc -> index
+      _, acc -> acc
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp remove_trailing_commas(json) do
+    Regex.replace(~r/,\s*([}\]])/, json, "\\1")
+  end
+
+  defp close_unbalanced_delimiters(json) do
+    {stack, _in_string?, _escaped?} =
+      json
+      |> String.graphemes()
+      |> Enum.reduce({[], false, false}, &track_delimiters/2)
+
+    closing =
+      stack
+      |> Enum.map(fn
+        "{" -> "}"
+        "[" -> "]"
+      end)
+      |> Enum.join("")
+
+    json <> closing
+  end
+
+  defp track_delimiters("\\", {stack, true, false}), do: {stack, true, true}
+  defp track_delimiters(_char, {stack, true, true}), do: {stack, true, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("\"", {stack, true, false}), do: {stack, false, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("\"", {stack, false, false}), do: {stack, true, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("{", {stack, false, false}), do: {["{" | stack], false, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("[", {stack, false, false}), do: {["[" | stack], false, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("}", {["{" | rest], false, false}), do: {rest, false, false}
+  defp track_delimiters("]", {["[" | rest], false, false}), do: {rest, false, false}
+  defp track_delimiters(_char, state), do: state
+end

problem_statement:
Default generated token limit should use model output metadata
Feedback from @zachdaniel: ReqLLM currently feels like it defaults to too few generated tokens when callers do not pass `:max_tokens`. The expected behavior is that default generated-token limits should come from LLMDB model metadata and remain explicitly overrideable by caller options or local model metadata overrides.

Investigation notes:

- Normal non-streaming chat already goes through `ReqLLM.Provider.Options.process/4`, which injects `model.limits.output` when neither `:max_tokens` nor `:max_completion_tokens` is supplied.
- Anthropic streaming bypasses that option-processing path in `attach_stream/4`, so a model such as `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` uses the hardcoded Anthropic fallback of `1024` instead of the LLMDB output limit of `8192`.
- Structured object generation also seeds hardcoded defaults too early. Anthropic object generation uses `4096` for a model whose output limit is `8192`; OpenAI object generation uses `4096` for `gpt-4o-mini`, whose output limit is `16384`.

Reproduction from local investigation:

```elixir
%{model_limit_output: 8192, chat_max_tokens: 8192, stream_max_tokens: 1024}

%{provider: :anthropic, model_limit_output: 8192, object_token_limit: 4096}
%{provider: :openai, model_limit_output: 16384, object_token_limit: 4096}
```

Suggested fix:

+defmodule ReqLLM.Providers.TokenLimitMetadataDefaultsTest do
+  use ReqLLM.ProviderCase, provider: ReqLLM.Providers.OpenAI
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Generation
+  alias ReqLLM.Providers.{Alibaba, AmazonBedrock, Azure, Mistral, OpenAI, Zenmux}
+
+  defmodule RequestCaptureAdapter do
+    def call(request) do
+      recipient = :persistent_term.get({__MODULE__, :recipient}, nil)
+
+      case {recipient, Jason.decode(request.body || "")} do
+        {pid, {:ok, body}} when is_pid(pid) ->
+          if body["model"] == "gpt-4o" and
+               String.contains?(Jason.encode!(body), "Return a name") do
+            send(pid, {:outbound_request_body, request.body})
+            %{request | host: "127.0.0.1", port: 1}
+          else
+            request
+          end
+
+        _ ->
+          request
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp model_with_output(model, value) do
+    limits = Map.put(model.limits || %{}, :output, value)
+    %{model | limits: limits}
+  end
+
+  defp compiled_schema do
+    {:ok, schema} = ReqLLM.Schema.compile(name: [type: :string, required: true])
+    schema
+  end
+
+  test "ordinary chat encodes the resolved model output limit when no budget is supplied" do
+    {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("openai:gpt-4-turbo")
+    {:ok, request} = OpenAI.prepare_request(:chat, model, context_fixture(), [])
+
+    encoded = OpenAI.encode_body(request)
+    body = Jason.decode!(encoded.body)
+
+    assert body["max_tokens"] == model.limits.output
+  end
+
+  test "ordinary chat uses a local model output override instead of the catalog limit" do
+    {:ok, catalog_model} = ReqLLM.model("openai:gpt-4-turbo")
+    catalog_limit = catalog_model.limits.output
+    override_limit = catalog_limit + 1
+    model = model_with_output(catalog_model, override_limit)
+
+    refute model.limits.output == catalog_limit
+    {:ok, request} = OpenAI.prepare_request(:chat, model, context_fixture(), [])
+    body = request |> OpenAI.encode_body() |> Map.fetch!(:body) |> Jason.decode!()
+
+    assert body["max_tokens"] == override_limit
+  end
+
+  test "Zenmux object requests default from an output limit other than 4096" do
+    {:ok, catalog_model} = ReqLLM.model("zenmux:xiaomi/mimo-v2-flash")
+    catalog_limit = catalog_model.limits.output
+    output_limit = if catalog_limit == 4096, do: catalog_limit + 1, else: catalog_limit
+    model = model_with_output(catalog_model, output_limit)
+    refute output_limit == 4096
+
+    {:ok, request} =
+      Zenmux.prepare_request(:object, model, context_fixture(), compiled_schema: compiled_schema())
+
+    assert (request.options[:max_completion_tokens] || request.options[:max_tokens]) == output_limit
+  end
+
+  test "Mistral shared stream construction uses model output metadata" do
+    {:ok, catalog_model} = ReqLLM.model("mistral:mistral-small-latest")
+    output_limit = 8192
+    model = model_with_output(catalog_model, output_limit)
+    assert is_integer(output_limit) and output_limit > 0
+    refute output_limit == 4096
+
+    {:ok, finch_request} =
+      Mistral.attach_stream(model, context_fixture(), [api_key: "mistral-test-key"], nil)
+
+    body = Jason.decode!(finch_request.body)
+    token_limit = body["max_tokens"] || body["max_completion_tokens"] || body["max_output_tokens"]
+    assert token_limit == output_limit
+  end
+
+  test "Alibaba shared object preparation uses model output metadata" do
+    {:ok, base_model} = ReqLLM.model(%{provider: :alibaba, id: "qwen-plus"})
+    output_limit = 2048
+    model = model_with_output(base_model, output_limit)
+
+    {:ok, request} =
+      Alibaba.prepare_request(:object, model, context_fixture(),
+        compiled_schema: compiled_schema(),
+        api_key: "alibaba-test-key"
+      )
+
+    assert request.options[:max_tokens] == output_limit
+  end
+
+  test "Azure object preparation defaults from the resolved model output limit" do
+    {:ok, catalog_model} = ReqLLM.model("azure:gpt-4o")
+    output_limit = catalog_model.limits.output
+    assert is_integer(output_limit) and output_limit > 0
+    refute output_limit == 4096
+    model = catalog_model
+
+    {:ok, request} =
+      Azure.prepare_request(:object, model, context_fixture(),
+        compiled_schema: compiled_schema(),
+        api_key: "azure-test-key",
+        base_url: "https://example.azure.com/openai",
+        deployment: "test-deployment"
+      )
+
+    assert request.options[:max_tokens] == output_limit
+  end
+
+  test "Amazon Bedrock streaming uses the model output metadata" do
+    {:ok, catalog_model} =
+      ReqLLM.model("amazon-bedrock:anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0")
+
+    catalog_limit = catalog_model.limits.output
+    output_limit = if catalog_limit == 4096, do: catalog_limit + 1, else: catalog_limit
+    model = model_with_output(catalog_model, output_limit)
+    assert is_integer(output_limit) and output_limit > 0
+    refute output_limit == 4096
+
+    {:ok, finch_request} =
+      AmazonBedrock.attach_stream(
+        model,
+        context_fixture(),
+        [access_key_id: "AKIATEST", secret_access_key: "secretTEST", region: "us-west-2"],
+        __MODULE__.TestFinch
+      )
+
+    body = Jason.decode!(finch_request.body)
+    assert body["max_tokens"] == output_limit
+  end
+
+  test "streaming structured-object requests retain the metadata-derived token limit" do
+    {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("openai:gpt-4o")
+    capture_key = {RequestCaptureAdapter, :recipient}
+    previous_adapter = Application.get_env(:req_llm, :finch_request_adapter)
+    :persistent_term.put(capture_key, self())
+    Application.put_env(:req_llm, :finch_request_adapter, RequestCaptureAdapter)
+
+    result =
+      try do
+        Generation.stream_object(
+          model,
+          "Return a name",
+          [name: [type: :string, required: true]]
+        )
+      after
+        :persistent_term.erase(capture_key)
+
+        if previous_adapter do
+          Application.put_env(:req_llm, :finch_request_adapter, previous_adapter)
+        else
+          Application.delete_env(:req_llm, :finch_request_adapter)
+        end
+      end
+
+    assert {:ok, response} = result
+    assert_receive {:outbound_request_body, encoded_body}, 1_000
+    body = Jason.decode!(encoded_body)
+    token_limit = body["max_tokens"] || body["max_completion_tokens"] || body["max_output_tokens"]
+    assert token_limit == model.limits.output
+    response.cancel.()
+  end
+
+  test "non-streaming Responses request preserves explicit max_output_tokens in its body" do
+    {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("openai:gpt-4o")
+    supplied_limit = model.limits.output + 17
+
+    {:ok, request} =
+      OpenAI.prepare_request(:chat, model, context_fixture(), max_output_tokens: supplied_limit)
+
+    body = request |> OpenAI.encode_body() |> Map.fetch!(:body) |> Jason.decode!()
+    assert body["max_output_tokens"] == supplied_limit
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
OpenAI provider ignores caller max_retries when attaching retry step
## Summary

In ReqLLM 1.17.1, the OpenAI provider merges caller options onto the request but then calls `ReqLLM.Step.Retry.attach/1` without forwarding `user_opts`. `Step.Retry.attach/1` therefore re-defaults `max_retries` to 3, even when the caller explicitly requested `max_retries: 0` or another bound.

The Anthropic provider already forwards `user_opts` to the retry step, so provider behavior is inconsistent.

## Current source path

`ReqLLM.Providers.OpenAI.attach/3` ends with:

```elixir
request
|> Req.Request.merge_options(... ++ user_opts)
|> ReqLLM.Step.Retry.attach()
```

`ReqLLM.Step.Retry.attach/2` computes:

```elixir
max_retries = Keyword.get(opts, :max_retries, 3)
```

The zero-argument pipeline call passes `[]`, so it writes the default `3` back into request options and overwrites the caller's merged value.

By contrast, `ReqLLM.Providers.Anthropic.attach/3` uses:

```elixir
|> ReqLLM.Step.Retry.attach(user_opts)
```

Several other providers also call `attach/1` and may have the same issue.

## Why this matters

Callers that own retry policy, side-effect safety, or token authorization cannot reliably disable dependency-owned retries. A logical operation may perform up to four physical attempts after the caller authorized only one. This is especially problematic when failed/ambiguous attempts consumed tokens but terminal usage metadata is incomplete.

## Expected behavior

- `max_retries: 0` produces exactly one physical request.
- Any positive caller value is honored consistently across providers.
- Provider defaults apply only when the caller omitted the option.
- The effective request pipeline, not merely the pre-attach option list, carries the caller's value.

## Suggested fix

Pass `user_opts` to `ReqLLM.Step.Retry.attach/2` from OpenAI and audit every provider that currently calls `attach/1` after merging caller options. A centralized provider-default helper may avoid future drift, but a focused forwarding fix is sufficient.

## Acceptance tests

- For OpenAI chat/object non-streaming requests, instrument the real Req pipeline and prove `max_retries: 0` performs one attempt under a retryable response/error.
- Prove `max_retries: 1` performs at most two attempts.
- Verify omission retains the documented default.
- Add equivalent contract coverage for providers using the shared defaults and for any provider-specific attach path found by the audit.
- Ensure streaming retry behavior continues honoring its caller option.

### Additional contract requirements

Contract clarifications for caller-supplied retry bounds:

- Attaching the shared non-streaming retry step leaves an already configured
  request retry limit (`max_retries`) in place: with no explicit retry-limit
  option, the effective retry limit remains the value already set on the
  request; an explicitly supplied retry-limit option takes precedence; and
  only a request that has neither an explicit option nor a pre-existing
  configured value receives the documented default retry limit.

- The caller's retry limit must survive until the effective request pipeline
  for every request-building path, including:

  - providers that build requests through the shared provider-default
    attachment helpers (chat, structured-object, embedding, rerank, and the
    shared transcription/speech request builders), and
  - every provider that wires up its own request pipeline for any operation
    (chat, structured-object, embedding, transcription, rerank, or speech),
    such as OpenAI, Azure, Cohere, Ollama, Amazon Bedrock, GitHub Copilot,
    Google Vertex, ElevenLabs, and OpenRouter.

- Equivalently, the streaming request pipeline continues to derive its
  effective retry limit from the caller-supplied option: an explicit value
  (including zero) is honored, and the documented default applies only when
  the caller omitted the option.

- A caller retry limit of zero produces exactly one physical request attempt
  under a retryable transport failure, and any positive caller value bounds
  the number of attempts accordingly.

  request; an explicitly supplied retry-limit option takes precedence; and
  only a request that has neither an explicit option nor a pre-existing
  configured value receives the documented default retry limit.

- The caller's retry limit must survive until the effective request pipeline
  for every request-building path, including:

  - providers that build requests through the shared provider-default
    attachment helpers (chat, structured-object, embedding, rerank, and the
    shared transcription/speech request builders), and
  - every provider that wires up its own request pipeline for any operation
    (chat, structured-object, embedding, transcription, rerank, or speech),
    such as OpenAI, Azure, Cohere, Ollama, Amazon Bedrock, GitHub Copilot,
    Google Vertex, ElevenLabs, and OpenRouter.

- Equivalently, the streaming request pipeline continues to derive its
  effective retry limit from the caller-supplied option: an explicit value
  (including zero) is honored, and the documented default applies only when
  the caller omitted the option.

- A caller retry limit of zero produces exactly one physical request attempt
  under a retryable transport failure, and any positive caller value bounds
  the number of attempts accordingly.

problem_statement:
V1: Add namespaced provider options alongside legacy options
Parent tracker: #829
Roadmap: [ReqLLM 1.x roadmap](https://github.com/agentjido/req_llm/blob/main/ROADMAP_V1.md) (pending merge)

## Outcome

Accept provider-keyed option namespaces as the V1 migration bridge while retaining the current legacy option shape.

## Compatibility

**V1 additive/deprecation bridge — no legacy provider option is rejected solely because it uses the current shape.**

## Scope

- Define and document provider_options keyed by provider identity.
- Normalize legacy and namespaced forms once before planning and encoding.
- Give explicit per-call canonical options deterministic precedence.
- Reject or warn on foreign provider namespaces, collisions, and unknown namespace structure before I/O.
- Preserve provider-native escape hatches and existing valid legacy calls.

## Out of scope

- Rejecting all legacy flat options.
- Removing provider-specific options.
- Changing canonical option names unrelated to the bridge.
- Adding the V2 migration audit.
- Provider wire or callback refactors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both documented forms work throughout V1.
- [ ] Precedence and collision rules are deterministic and documented.
- [ ] Foreign provider options cannot leak onto the selected surface.
- [ ] Legacy ambiguous input receives an actionable warning without silent behavior changes.
- [ ] The normalized shape is available to planning and providers exactly once.

## Validation

- [ ] Run option normalization, precedence, collision, and foreign-namespace tests.
- [ ] Run representative OpenAI, Anthropic, and compatible-provider replay scenarios.
- [ ] Run the public contract suite.
- [ ] Run mix test and mix quality.

## Pull request boundary

This issue closes through exactly one pull request containing the implementation, direct tests, fixture changes required by this scope, and directly affected documentation. Unrelated provider migrations or cleanup are excluded.

## Dependencies

Depends on #838.

## Roadmap audit refinement — July 16, 2026

The existing V1 shape is a flat keyword/map inside `provider_options`; it remains valid. Add the provider-keyed form as an outer namespace and normalize both once. Be explicit about hosted-provider identities such as Azure/OpenAI and Google Vertex/Gemini, and avoid warning on unambiguous legacy input merely to accelerate V2.

### Additional contract requirements

# Provider-Keyed Option Namespace Contract

This addendum defines the observable requirements for accepting and normalizing
provider-keyed option namespaces alongside the existing legacy `provider_options`
shape during ReqLLM 1.x.

## Accepted input shapes

- The legacy flat `provider_options` shape (keyword list or map) remains valid
  for every operation exactly as before. No otherwise valid legacy call may be
  rejected, and no warning may be emitted for unambiguous legacy input merely to
  accelerate migration.
- `provider_options` may additionally scope its entries under the selected
  ReqLLM provider identity as an outer namespace, in keyword or map form with
  atom or string keys, and both forms must produce the same effective options as
  the equivalent flat legacy form for the same operation.
- A key in the provider option position that matches a declared provider option
  must be treated as a flat provider option, never misread as a namespace.
- Namespace keys are always the selected ReqLLM provider identity: `azure` for
  Azure-hosted models, `google_vertex` for Vertex-hosted models, and
  `openrouter` for OpenRouter models; never the upstream protocol identity (for
  example `openai` or `google`) merely because the hosted service speaks a
  compatible wire format.

## Normalization and error handling

- Legacy and namespaced forms are normalized once, before request planning and
  encoding, so the canonical option set produced for a call never contains the
  provider namespace key itself.
- Requests are rejected before any I/O, with an actionable error, when:
  - a namespace keys options under a provider identity other than the selected
    one (foreign namespaces);
  - the selected namespace container is not a keyword list or map;
  - a namespace carries an unknown option key;
  - a purely canonical (top-level) option is misplaced inside a namespace, in
    which case the error names the option and its correct placement;
  - `provider_options` is supplied more than once, the same namespace appears
    more than once, or the same option key is duplicated within one namespace.
- Foreign namespaces must never be silently passed through as ordinary provider
  options, and their option values must not appear in processed options.
- Errors surfaced through the public request-planning diagnostic identify the
  offending namespace without echoing caller-supplied option values.

## Precedence and ambiguity

- An explicit top-level canonical option always wins over the same option
  supplied inside a provider namespace.
- When a flat legacy provider option and a namespaced provider option supply
  different values for the same option, the call must resolve to a documented,
  deterministic winner for that collision on every repeated invocation, and the
  collision must not pass silently: an actionable diagnostic (warning or error)
  must identify the colliding option key.
- The per-call `on_unsupported` policy applies to ambiguous input: `:error`
  surfaces the ambiguity as an error, and `:ignore` applies the deterministic
  resolution without emitting any warning about it.
- Providers that declare no provider-option schema may either preserve their
  native escape hatch for the selected namespace or reject undocumented option
  keys; whichever policy an implementation documents, namespaced input is
  treated consistently with equivalent legacy input under it, and foreign
  namespaces still surface as errors rather than being silently accepted.

## Tuple defaults

- Model tuples carrying provider-keyed namespace maps in their defaults remain
  valid; an applicable `provider_options` tuple default is forwarded unchanged
  into the call options.

+## Provider Option Namespaces
+
+ReqLLM 1.x accepts both the existing flat `provider_options` shape and an
+additive provider-keyed shape. Existing calls remain valid and do not warn when
+their flat options are unambiguous:
+
+```elixir
+ReqLLM.generate_text(
+  "openai:gpt-5",
+  "Solve this carefully",
+  provider_options: [reasoning_summary: "auto"]
+)
+```
+
+New code can scope the same options to the selected provider:
+
+```elixir
+ReqLLM.generate_text(
+  "openai:gpt-5",
+  "Solve this carefully",
+  provider_options: [
+    openai: [reasoning_summary: "auto"]
+  ]
+)
+```
+
+Keyword lists and atom-keyed maps are supported:
+
+```elixir
+provider_options: %{
+  openai: %{reasoning_summary: "auto"}
+}
+```
+
+The namespace is always the actual ReqLLM provider identity. Use `azure:` for
+Azure-hosted models, `google_vertex:` for Vertex-hosted models, and
+`openrouter:` for OpenRouter models. Do not use `openai:` or `google:` merely
+because the hosted service uses an OpenAI- or Gemini-compatible wire format.
+Foreign namespaces fail before network I/O.
+
+When forms are combined, precedence is deterministic:
+
+1. Explicit top-level canonical options win over the same namespaced option.
+2. Options under the selected provider namespace win over colliding legacy flat
+   provider options.
+3. Non-colliding flat and namespaced provider options are merged.
+
+Mixed forms emit an actionable warning by default. Set `on_unsupported: :error`
+to reject an ambiguous mix, or `on_unsupported: :ignore` to apply the same
+precedence without logging. Invalid namespace containers, unknown namespaced
+options, duplicate namespaced keys, and foreign provider namespaces are rejected
+before I/O. ReqLLM 1.x does not reject an otherwise valid call merely because it
+uses the legacy flat shape.
+

@@ -0,0 +1,368 @@
+defmodule ReqLLM.Provider.Options.Namespace do
+  @moduledoc false
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.Parameter
+  alias ReqLLM.Error.Validation.Error
+
+  @type warning :: String.t()
+
+  @spec normalize(module(), atom(), LLMDB.Model.t(), keyword()) ::
+          {:ok, keyword(), [warning()]} | {:error, Exception.t()}
+  def normalize(provider_mod, operation, %LLMDB.Model{} = model, opts)
+      when is_atom(provider_mod) and is_atom(operation) and is_list(opts) do
+    with :ok <- validate_keyword_options(opts),
+         {:ok, normalized, warnings} <-
+           normalize_container(provider_mod, operation, model.provider, opts) do
+      apply_warning_policy(normalized, warnings, opts)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def normalize(_provider_mod, _operation, _model, _opts) do
+    invalid_parameter("options must be a keyword list")
+  end
+
+  @spec normalize!(module(), atom(), LLMDB.Model.t(), keyword()) :: {keyword(), [warning()]}
+  def normalize!(provider_mod, operation, %LLMDB.Model{} = model, opts) do
+    case normalize(provider_mod, operation, model, opts) do
+      {:ok, normalized, warnings} -> {normalized, warnings}
+      {:error, error} -> raise error
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_container(provider_mod, operation, provider, opts) do
+    case Keyword.get_values(opts, :provider_options) do
+      [] ->
+        {:ok, opts, []}
+
+      [provider_options] ->
+        normalize_provider_options(provider_mod, operation, provider, opts, provider_options)
+
+      _provider_options ->
+        invalid_parameter("request options contain provider_options more than once")
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provider_options(provider_mod, operation, provider, opts, provider_options) do
+    with {:ok, entries} <- container_entries(provider_options),
+         schema_keys <- provider_schema_keys(provider_mod),
+         {:ok, flat_entries, namespace_entries} <-
+           classify_entries(entries, provider, schema_keys),
+         {:ok, namespace} <- one_namespace(namespace_entries, provider),
+         {:ok, normalized, warnings} <-
+           normalize_selected_namespace(
+             namespace,
+             flat_entries,
+             provider_mod,
+             operation,
+             provider,
+             opts
+           ) do
+      {:ok, normalized, warnings}
+    else
+      :legacy -> {:ok, opts, []}
+      {:error, error} -> {:error, error}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp container_entries(options) when is_map(options), do: {:ok, Map.to_list(options)}
+
+  defp container_entries(options) when is_list(options) do
+    if Keyword.keyword?(options), do: {:ok, options}, else: :legacy
+  end
+
+  defp container_entries(_options), do: :legacy
+
+  defp classify_entries(entries, provider, schema_keys) do
+    known_providers = known_provider_ids(provider)
+
+    entries
+    |> Enum.reduce_while({[], []}, fn {key, value}, {flat, namespaces} ->
+      cond do
+        schema_key?(key, schema_keys) ->
+          {:cont, {[{key, value} | flat], namespaces}}
+
+        provider_key?(key, provider) ->
+          {:cont, {flat, [{provider, value} | namespaces]}}
+
+        foreign_provider = provider_key(key, known_providers) ->
+          {:halt, foreign_namespace(foreign_provider, provider)}
+
+        true ->
+          {:cont, {[{key, value} | flat], namespaces}}
+      end
+    end)
+    |> case do
+      {:error, error} -> {:error, error}
+      {flat, namespaces} -> {:ok, Enum.reverse(flat), Enum.reverse(namespaces)}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp one_namespace([], _provider), do: {:ok, nil}
+  defp one_namespace([{_namespace_provider, value}], _selected_provider), do: {:ok, value}
+
+  defp one_namespace(_namespaces, provider) do
+    invalid_parameter(
+      "provider_options contains the #{inspect(provider)} namespace more than once"
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_selected_namespace(nil, _flat, _provider_mod, _operation, _provider, opts),
+    do: {:ok, opts, []}
+
+  defp normalize_selected_namespace(
+         namespace,
+         flat,
+         provider_mod,
+         operation,
+         provider,
+         opts
+       ) do
+    schema_keys = provider_schema_keys(provider_mod)
+
+    with {:ok, namespace_entries} <- namespace_entries(namespace, provider),
+         {:ok, normalized_namespace} <-
+           normalize_option_entries(namespace_entries, schema_keys, operation, provider),
+         {:ok, normalized_flat} <-
+           normalize_option_entries(flat, schema_keys, operation, provider),
+         :ok <- reject_duplicate_keys(normalized_namespace, provider),
+         :ok <- reject_duplicate_keys(normalized_flat, provider) do
+      provider_collisions = colliding_keys(normalized_flat, normalized_namespace)
+
+      merged_before_canonical =
+        normalized_flat
+        |> remove_keys(provider_collisions)
+        |> Kernel.++(normalized_namespace)
+
+      {merged, canonical_collisions} =
+        remove_canonical_collisions(merged_before_canonical, operation, opts)
+
+      normalized_opts = Keyword.put(opts, :provider_options, merged)
+
+      warnings =
+        mixed_shape_warnings(provider, normalized_flat, provider_collisions) ++
+          canonical_collision_warnings(provider, canonical_collisions)
+
+      {:ok, normalized_opts, warnings}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp namespace_entries(namespace, _provider) when is_map(namespace),
+    do: {:ok, Map.to_list(namespace)}
+
+  defp namespace_entries(namespace, provider) when is_list(namespace) do
+    if Keyword.keyword?(namespace) do
+      {:ok, namespace}
+    else
+      invalid_namespace_structure(provider)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp namespace_entries(_namespace, provider), do: invalid_namespace_structure(provider)
+
+  defp normalize_option_entries(entries, schema_keys, operation, provider) do
+    canonical_keys = canonical_option_keys(operation)
+    schema_names = Map.new(schema_keys, &{Atom.to_string(&1), &1})
+
+    entries
+    |> Enum.reduce_while([], fn {key, value}, normalized ->
+      case normalize_option_key(key, schema_keys, schema_names, canonical_keys, provider) do
+        {:ok, normalized_key} -> {:cont, [{normalized_key, value} | normalized]}
+        {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
+      end
+    end)
+    |> case do
+      {:error, error} -> {:error, error}
+      normalized -> {:ok, Enum.reverse(normalized)}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_option_key(key, schema_keys, schema_names, canonical_keys, provider) do
+    cond do
+      is_atom(key) and key in schema_keys ->
+        {:ok, key}
+
+      is_atom(key) and schema_keys == [] ->
+        {:ok, key}
+
+      is_binary(key) and Map.has_key?(schema_names, key) ->
+        {:ok, Map.fetch!(schema_names, key)}
+
+      is_atom(key) and key in canonical_keys ->
+        canonical_option_error(key)
+
+      is_binary(key) ->
+        case Enum.find(canonical_keys, &(Atom.to_string(&1) == key)) do
+          nil -> unknown_provider_option(key, provider)
+          canonical -> canonical_option_error(canonical)
+        end
+
+      true ->
+        unknown_provider_option(key, provider)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp canonical_option_error(key) do
+    invalid_parameter(
+      "provider option #{inspect(key)} is canonical; pass it as a top-level request option"
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp unknown_provider_option(key, provider) do
+    invalid_parameter(
+      "unknown provider option #{inspect(key)} in the #{inspect(provider)} namespace"
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp reject_duplicate_keys(entries, provider) do
+    duplicates =
+      entries
+      |> Enum.group_by(fn {key, _value} -> key end)
+      |> Enum.filter(fn {_key, values} -> length(values) > 1 end)
+      |> Enum.map(fn {key, _values} -> key end)
+      |> Enum.sort()
+
+    if duplicates == [] do
+      :ok
+    else
+      invalid_parameter(
+        "provider_options contains duplicate #{inspect(provider)} keys: #{format_keys(duplicates)}"
+      )
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp remove_canonical_collisions(namespace, operation, opts) do
+    canonical_keys = MapSet.new(canonical_option_keys(operation))
+    top_level_keys = MapSet.new(Keyword.keys(opts))
+
+    collisions =
+      namespace
+      |> Keyword.keys()
+      |> Enum.filter(&(MapSet.member?(canonical_keys, &1) and MapSet.member?(top_level_keys, &1)))
+      |> Enum.uniq()
+      |> Enum.sort()
+
+    {Keyword.drop(namespace, collisions), collisions}
+  end
+
+  defp colliding_keys(left, right) do
+    right_keys = MapSet.new(Keyword.keys(right))
+
+    left
+    |> Keyword.keys()
+    |> Enum.filter(&MapSet.member?(right_keys, &1))
+    |> Enum.uniq()
+    |> Enum.sort()
+  end
+
+  defp remove_keys(options, []), do: options
+  defp remove_keys(options, keys), do: Keyword.drop(options, keys)
+
+  defp mixed_shape_warnings(_provider, [], _collisions), do: []
+
+  defp mixed_shape_warnings(provider, _flat, []) do
+    [
+      "Mixed legacy flat provider_options with the #{inspect(provider)} namespace; both forms were merged. " <>
+        "Prefer provider_options: [#{provider}: [...]] without flat provider keys."
+    ]
+  end
+
+  defp mixed_shape_warnings(provider, _flat, collisions) do
+    [
+      "Mixed legacy flat provider_options with the #{inspect(provider)} namespace; namespaced values took precedence for #{format_keys(collisions)}. " <>
+        "Prefer provider_options: [#{provider}: [...]] without flat provider keys."
+    ]
+  end
+
+  defp canonical_collision_warnings(_provider, []), do: []
+
+  defp canonical_collision_warnings(provider, collisions) do
+    [
+      "Ignored namespaced #{inspect(provider)} values for #{format_keys(collisions)} because explicit top-level canonical options take precedence."
+    ]
+  end
+
+  defp apply_warning_policy(normalized, [], _opts), do: {:ok, normalized, []}
+
+  defp apply_warning_policy(normalized, warnings, opts) do
+    case Keyword.get(opts, :on_unsupported, :warn) do
+      :error ->
+        {:error,
+         Error.exception(
+           tag: :unsupported_options,
+           reason: Enum.join(warnings, "; "),
+           context: []
+         )}
+
+      :ignore ->
+        {:ok, normalized, []}
+
+      _policy ->
+        {:ok, normalized, warnings}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:chat), do: generation_option_keys()
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:object), do: generation_option_keys()
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:embedding), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.Embedding.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:image), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.Images.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:transcription), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.Transcription.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:speech), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.Speech.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:rerank), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.Rerank.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(:ocr), do: schema_keys(ReqLLM.OCR.schema())
+  defp canonical_option_keys(_operation), do: generation_option_keys()
+
+  defp generation_option_keys do
+    ReqLLM.Provider.Options.generation_schema()
+    |> schema_keys()
+  end
+
+  defp schema_keys(%NimbleOptions{schema: schema}),
+    do: schema |> Keyword.keys() |> Enum.reject(&(&1 == :provider_options))
+
+  defp provider_schema_keys(provider_mod) do
+    if function_exported?(provider_mod, :provider_schema, 0) do
+      provider_mod.provider_schema().schema
+      |> Keyword.keys()
+    else
+      []
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp known_provider_ids(provider) do
+    [provider | ReqLLM.Providers.list()]
+    |> Enum.uniq()
+  end
+
+  defp schema_key?(key, schema_keys) when is_atom(key), do: key in schema_keys
+
+  defp schema_key?(key, schema_keys) when is_binary(key),
+    do: Enum.any?(schema_keys, &(Atom.to_string(&1) == key))
+
+  defp schema_key?(_key, _schema_keys), do: false
+
+  defp provider_key?(key, provider) when is_atom(key), do: key == provider
+  defp provider_key?(key, provider) when is_binary(key), do: key == Atom.to_string(provider)
+  defp provider_key?(_key, _provider), do: false
+
+  defp provider_key(key, providers), do: Enum.find(providers, &provider_key?(key, &1))
+
+  defp foreign_namespace(foreign_provider, selected_provider) do
+    invalid_parameter(
+      "provider_options namespace #{inspect(foreign_provider)} does not match selected provider #{inspect(selected_provider)}; use the #{inspect(selected_provider)} namespace"
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp invalid_namespace_structure(provider) do
+    invalid_parameter(
+      "provider_options namespace #{inspect(provider)} must contain a keyword list or map"
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp validate_keyword_options(opts) do
+    if Keyword.keyword?(opts), do: :ok, else: invalid_parameter("options must be a keyword list")
+  end
+
+  defp format_keys(keys), do: Enum.map_join(keys, ", ", &inspect/1)
+
+  defp invalid_parameter(message), do: {:error, Parameter.exception(parameter: message)}
+end

+defmodule ReqLLM.Provider.Options.NamespaceTest do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Contract tests for provider-keyed option namespaces, observed through the
+  public option-processing entry point `ReqLLM.Provider.Options.process/4`,
+  the public request-planning entry points, and the tuple-defaults public API.
+
+  Per the V1 contract:
+
+    * Both the legacy flat `provider_options` shape and the provider-keyed
+      namespace shape work for every operation.
+    * Hosted provider identities (e.g. `:azure`, `:google_vertex`,
+      `:openrouter`) are the namespace keys, not upstream protocols.
+    * Foreign provider namespaces, malformed namespaces, duplicate input, and
+      ambiguous input are rejected or surface an actionable diagnostic before
+      any I/O; unknown namespace keys never reach the request.
+    * The winning option values for a call are deterministic regardless of how
+      the framework resolves a collision, and unambiguous legacy input never
+      warns merely to accelerate migration.
+  """
+
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  import ExUnit.CaptureLog
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Provider.Options

+  defmodule MockProvider do
+    @behaviour ReqLLM.Provider

+    def supported_provider_options, do: [:custom_option, :another_option, :dimensions]
+
+    def provider_schema do
+      NimbleOptions.new!(
+        custom_option: [type: :string],
+        another_option: [type: :integer],
+        dimensions: [type: :pos_integer]
+      )
+    end
+
+    def prepare_request(_operation, _model, _input, _opts), do: {:error, :not_implemented}
+    def attach(request, _model, _opts), do: request
+    def encode_body(request), do: request
+    def decode_response(response), do: response
+  end
+
+  defmodule ProviderNameOptionProvider do
+    @behaviour ReqLLM.Provider
+
+    def provider_id, do: :provider_name_option
+    def default_base_url, do: "https://provider-name-option.test"
+    def supported_provider_options, do: [:openai]
+    def provider_schema, do: NimbleOptions.new!(openai: [type: :any])
+    def prepare_request(_operation, _model, _input, _opts), do: {:error, :not_implemented}
+    def attach(request, _model, _opts), do: request
+    def encode_body(request), do: request
+    def decode_response(response), do: response
+  end
+
+  defp model(provider, id \\ "model") do
+    %LLMDB.Model{provider: provider, id: id}
+  end
+
+  defp process(provider_mod, operation, model, opts) do
+    Options.process(provider_mod, operation, model, opts)
+  end
+
+  defp comparable_values(processed, keys) do
+    Enum.map(keys, fn key ->
+      case Keyword.fetch(processed, key) do
+        {:ok, provider_options} when key == :provider_options ->
+          {key, Enum.sort_by(List.wrap(provider_options), &inspect/1)}
+
+        {:ok, value} ->
+          {key, value}
+
+        :error ->
+          {key, :absent}
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp flat_values(processed, keys) do
+    provider_options = processed[:provider_options] || []
+
+    Enum.map(keys, fn key ->
+      {key, Keyword.get(processed, key, Keyword.get(provider_options, key))}
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp provider_option_values(processed, keys) do
+    provider_options = processed[:provider_options] || []
+    Keyword.take(provider_options, keys)
+  end
+
+  defp public_documentation do
+    source_path = ReqLLM.__info__(:compile)[:source]
+    source_dir = if source_path, do: Path.dirname(to_string(source_path)), else: File.cwd!()
+    project_file = Mix.Project.project_file()
+
+    roots =
+      [File.cwd!(), __DIR__, source_dir, Path.dirname(project_file)]
+      |> Enum.flat_map(fn start ->
+        Stream.unfold(Path.expand(start), fn path ->
+          parent = Path.dirname(path)
+          if parent == path, do: nil, else: {path, parent}
+        end)
+        |> Enum.to_list()
+      end)
+      |> Enum.uniq()
+
+    project_root =
+      Enum.find(roots, &File.regular?(Path.join(&1, "guides/configuration.md"))) ||
+        Mix.raise("could not locate public provider-option documentation")
+
+    paths =
+      ["README.md", "guides/configuration.md", "guides/model-specs.md"] ++
+        Path.wildcard(Path.join(project_root, "guides/**/*.md")) ++
+        Path.wildcard(Path.join(project_root, "docs/**/*.md"))
+
+    paths
+    |> Enum.map(&Path.expand(&1, project_root))
+    |> Enum.filter(&File.regular?/1)
+    |> Enum.map_join("\n", &File.read!/1)
+  end

+  defp documented_collision_winner do

+        :namespaced
+
+      Regex.match?(~r/(?:selected (?:provider )?namespace|namespaced values?|namespaced options?).{0,160}(?:win|take precedence|precedence over|override).{0,100}(?:flat|legacy)/is, documentation) ->
+        :namespaced
+
+      Regex.match?(~r/(?:flat|legacy)(?: provider options?)?.{0,160}(?:win|take precedence|precedence over|override).{0,100}(?:namespace|namespaced)/is, documentation) ->
+        :flat
+
+      true ->
+        flunk("public documentation must state which provider_options form wins a collision")
+    end
+  end

+  describe "namespace normalization" do
+    test "preserves unambiguous legacy keyword and map containers without warnings" do

+  describe "precedence and warning policy" do
+    test "mixed legacy and namespaced input deterministically resolves each colliding key" do
+      model = model(:mock_namespace)

+      num_repeats = 3

+      # Legacy-only input without a collision must resolve to the legacy value.

+      # that identifies the colliding option key; under :ignore the call must
+      # succeed deterministically without emitting warnings.
+      assert {:error, strict_error} = strict
+      assert Exception.message(strict_error) =~ "custom_option"
+
+      assert {:ok, lenient_processed} = lenient
+      assert silent_log == ""
+
+      assert {:custom_option, lenient_winner} =
+               List.keyfind(
+                 provider_option_values(lenient_processed, [:custom_option]),
+                 :custom_option,
+                 0
+               )
+
+      assert lenient_winner in ["legacy", "namespaced"]
+    end
+
+    test "flat and namespaced provider option collisions warn under the default policy" do
+      ambiguous = [
+        provider_options: [
+          custom_option: "legacy",
+          mock_namespace: [custom_option: "namespaced"]
+        ]
+      ]
+
+      warned_log =
+        capture_log([level: :warning], fn ->
+          send(self(), {:warned_result, process(MockProvider, :chat, model(:mock_namespace), ambiguous)})
+        end)
+
+      assert_received {:warned_result, result}
+
+      case result do
+        {:ok, processed} ->
+          # The colliding key resolves to a single deterministic winner on
+          # either side, so policies that keep the call working must surface
+          # an actionable warning that names the colliding option key; a
+          # flat-vs-namespaced value collision must never pass silently.
+          assert [{:custom_option, winner}] =
+                   provider_option_values(processed, [:custom_option])
+
+          assert winner in ["legacy", "namespaced"]
+          assert warned_log =~ "custom_option"
+
+        {:error, diagnostic} ->
+          # A policy that defaults ambiguous mixed input to rejection is
+          # equally contract-conformant: the actionable error names the
+          # colliding option key and presents it as an ambiguous mix of the
+          # flat and namespaced shapes, not merely as an unknown key (a bare
+          # "unknown key" validation error would miss the contract rule that
+          # the collision itself must be diagnosed).
+          message = Exception.message(diagnostic)
+          assert message =~ "custom_option"
+          assert message =~ ~r/mixed|collid|ambigu|precedence|both/i
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "provider processing and planning" do
+    test "accepts flat provider option maps with known string keys" do
+      assert {:ok, processed} =
+               process(MockProvider, :chat, model(:mock_namespace),
+                 provider_options: %{
+                   "custom_option" => "map",
+                   "another_option" => 7
+                 }
+               )
+
+      assert Enum.sort(provider_option_values(processed, [:custom_option, :another_option])) == [
+               another_option: 7,
+               custom_option: "map"
+             ]
+    end
+
+    test "produces equivalent options for OpenAI, Anthropic, and OpenRouter" do
+      cases = [
+        {ReqLLM.Providers.OpenAI, model(:openai, "gpt-4.1-mini"), [reasoning_summary: "auto"]},
+        {ReqLLM.Providers.Anthropic, model(:anthropic, "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929"),
+         [anthropic_top_k: 20]},
+        {ReqLLM.Providers.OpenRouter, model(:openrouter, "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"),
+         [openrouter_route: "fallback"]}
+      ]
+
+      Enum.each(cases, fn {provider_mod, provider_model, provider_options} ->
+        provider = provider_model.provider
+
+        assert {:ok, legacy} =
+                 process(provider_mod, :chat, provider_model,
+                   provider_options: provider_options
+                 )
+
+        assert {:ok, namespaced} =
+                 process(provider_mod, :chat, provider_model,
+                   provider_options: [{provider, provider_options}]
+                 )
+
+        keys = Keyword.keys(provider_options)
+        assert comparable_values(namespaced, keys ++ [:provider_options]) ==
+                 comparable_values(legacy, keys ++ [:provider_options])
+      end)
+    end
+
+    test "uses hosted and compatible provider identities instead of upstream protocols" do
+      hosted_cases = [
+        {ReqLLM.Providers.Azure, model(:azure, "gpt-4o"), :azure, [deployment: "deployment"]},
+        {ReqLLM.Providers.GoogleVertex, model(:google_vertex, "gemini-2.5-flash"), :google_vertex,
+         [project_id: "project"]}
+      ]
+
+      Enum.each(hosted_cases, fn {provider_mod, provider_model, identity, provider_options} ->
+        assert {:ok, legacy} =
+                 process(provider_mod, :chat, provider_model,
+                   provider_options: provider_options
+                 )
+
+        assert {:ok, namespaced} =
+                 process(provider_mod, :chat, provider_model,
+                   provider_options: [{identity, provider_options}]
+                 )
+
+        keys = Keyword.keys(provider_options)
+        assert comparable_values(namespaced, keys ++ [:provider_options]) ==
+                 comparable_values(legacy, keys ++ [:provider_options])
+      end)
+
+      # Foreign namespaces keyed by the upstream protocol identity must be
+      # rejected before I/O instead of leaking onto the selected provider.
+      assert {:error, _} =
+               process(ReqLLM.Providers.Azure, :chat, model(:azure, "gpt-4o"),
+                 provider_options: [openai: [deployment: "deployment"]]
+               )
+
+      assert {:error, _} =
+               process(ReqLLM.Providers.GoogleVertex, :chat,
+                 model(:google_vertex, "gemini-2.5-flash"),
+                 provider_options: [google: [project_id: "project"]]
+               )
+
+      assert {:error, _} =
+               process(ReqLLM.Providers.OpenRouter, :chat,
+                 model(:openrouter, "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"),
+                 provider_options: [openai: [openrouter_route: "fallback"]]
+               )
+
+      # The selected provider's own namespace remains valid on a compatible host.
+      assert {:ok, openrouter} =
+               process(ReqLLM.Providers.OpenRouter, :chat,
+                 model(:openrouter, "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"),
+                 provider_options: [openrouter: [openrouter_route: "fallback"]]
+               )
+
+      assert provider_option_values(openrouter, [:openrouter_route]) ==
+               [openrouter_route: "fallback"]
+    end
+
+    test "makes normalized provider options available to request planning" do
+      # The contract permits normalization at either integration point: inside
+      # the internal RequestPlan.build boundary itself, or earlier in the
+      # public request-planning and option-processing pipeline. Assert the
+      # namespaced transport selection only through the public request-planning
+      # diagnostic, which every conformant implementation must expose.
+      assert {:ok, diagnostic} =
+               ReqLLM.plan("openai:gpt-4o-mini", :chat,
+                 stream: true,
+                 provider_options: [openai: [openai_stream_transport: :websocket]]
+               )
+
+      assert diagnostic.transport == :websocket
+      assert :openai_stream_transport in diagnostic.options.canonical
+      refute :openai in diagnostic.options.canonical
+
+      # A flat provider option map with known string keys stays a valid plan
+      # input; request planning resolves the provider identity either way.
+      assert {:ok, flat_map_plan} =
+               ReqLLM.RequestPlan.build("openai:gpt-4o-mini", :chat,
+                 provider_options: %{"reasoning_summary" => "auto"}
+               )
+
+      assert flat_map_plan.provider == :openai
+    end
+
+    test "keeps namespace validation actionable in sanitized planning errors" do
+      assert {:error, error} =
+               ReqLLM.plan("openai:gpt-4o-mini", :chat,
+                 provider_options: %{"anthropic" => %{"distinctive_option" => "secret-value"}}
+               )
+
+      message = Exception.message(error)
+      assert message =~ ":anthropic" or message =~ "anthropic"
+      assert message =~ "openai"
+
+      # The public planning diagnostic identifies the offending namespace but
+      # must redact the caller-controlled value, unlike direct processing errors.
+      refute message =~ "secret-value"
+    end
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
V1: Harden canonical tool exchange contracts
Parent tracker: #829
Roadmap: [ReqLLM 1.x roadmap](https://github.com/agentjido/req_llm/blob/main/ROADMAP_V1.md) (pending merge)

## Outcome

Harden the existing `ReqLLM.Tool`, `ReqLLM.ToolCall`, and `ReqLLM.ToolResult` values into a provider-independent exchange contract without executing a loop.

## Compatibility

**V1 additive — existing tool definitions, callbacks, messages, result values, and provider behavior remain supported.**

## Scope

- Reuse `Tool.execute/2` input validation and expose raw/validated arguments plus explicit valid, invalid, unknown, provider-executed, and provider-native states where missing.
- Preserve invalid and unknown calls as inspectable data while preventing accidental execution.
- Keep `ToolResult.output` as application-visible data and `ToolResult.content` as model-facing content, documenting text, JSON, error, file, image, and provider-native forms.
- Preserve existing builtin/provider-executed tool markers and provider metadata.
- Keep individual tool execution helpers explicit and single-call.

## Out of scope

- New parallel tool call/result structs.
- Automatically executing tool calls or starting a follow-up model request.
- Loop termination, approvals, memory, durability, MCP runtime, or provider wire refactors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current provider tool calls can be handled without provider-specific branching.
- [ ] Invalid or unknown calls are inspectable and cannot execute accidentally.
- [ ] Application output and model-facing content can differ explicitly.
- [ ] Existing callbacks and round trips remain compatible.
- [ ] Provider-executed/native tools remain distinguishable from application tools.

## Validation

- [ ] Run Tool, ToolCall, ToolResult, validation, callback, invalid/unknown, builtin, parallel, and round-trip tests.
- [ ] Run OpenAI, Anthropic, and multimodal tool-result replays.
- [ ] Run mix test and mix quality.

## Pull request boundary

This issue closes through exactly one pull request containing the implementation or focused contract document, direct tests, and directly affected documentation. Unrelated provider migrations and cleanup are excluded.

Proposed squash title: `feat: harden canonical tool exchange contracts`

## Dependencies

Depends on #845.

### Additional contract requirements

## Public interface additions and refinements

The hidden tests exercise the following observable behaviors. Any valid
implementation must satisfy them; the existing public APIs and behaviors
remain unchanged.

### `ReqLLM.Tool.validate_input/2`

- `Tool.validate_input(tool, input)` validates `input` against the tool's
  parameter schema without invoking the tool's callback. The callback is
  never called by this function.
- On success it returns `{:ok, validated}` where `validated` is a map with
  atom keys reflecting key normalization and schema defaults (for example, a
  parameter declared with a `default` is present in the returned map even if
  omitted from the input).
- On schema-validation failure it returns `{:error, error}` with the same
  error value (a validation exception) and message that
  `Tool.execute(tool, input)` returns for the same input.
- When `input` is not a map, it returns `{:error, error}` where `error` is
  an invalid-parameter exception; the callback is never invoked.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.provider_native?/1`

- Returns `true` when a tool call's non-wire metadata (attached via
  `ToolCall.put_metadata/2`) contains a truthy `:provider_native` (or
  `"provider_native"`) marker; returns `false` for a `nil` or `false`
  marker.
- The marker value may be any truthy term (atom, string, map, or `true`).
- A call created with `ToolCall.new_builtin/3` (a provider-executed builtin)
  is not provider-native unless it also carries the provider-native
  metadata marker; the two markers are independent.
- Attaching provider-native metadata via `put_metadata/2` must not change the
  provider wire encoding of the call: its JSON encoding contains no
  metadata or provider-native keys.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.resolve/3`

- `ToolCall.resolve(call, available_tools, opts \\ [])` inspects a single
  call against a list of application `ReqLLM.Tool` values and returns a
  resolution map. It never invokes any tool callback.
- The resolution map always contains these keys: `:state`, `:call` (the
  original call), `:id`, `:name`, `:tool` (the matched tool or `nil`),
  `:raw_arguments` (the original JSON arguments string), `:arguments`
  (decoded string-keyed argument map, or `nil` when undecodable),
  `:validated_arguments` (validated atom-keyed map, or `nil`), `:metadata`
  (the call's metadata map), and `:error` (`nil` on success).
- `:state` is one of `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:unknown`,
  `:provider_executed`, or `:provider_native`. Classification precedence is:
  provider-executed builtin first, then provider-native marker, then
  application-tool resolution. A call carrying both the builtin marker and
  the provider-native marker is classified as `:provider_executed`.
- Provider-executed and provider-native calls have `state`
  `:provider_executed`/`:provider_native` with `tool: nil`,
  `validated_arguments: nil`, and `error: nil`; any decodable arguments are
  still exposed for inspection.
- A call whose name matches an application tool is `:valid` when its
  arguments decode to a map and pass the tool's input validation; the
  resolution exposes the raw, decoded, and validated arguments.
- A call whose arguments fail JSON decoding, decode to a non-map value, or
  fail schema validation is `:invalid`; the error is the underlying
  decode/validation exception and `validated_arguments` is `nil`.
- A call whose name matches no application tool is `:unknown` with an
  invalid-parameter error whose message identifies the missing tool name.
- Argument JSON decoding follows the same tolerant repair behavior as
  `ToolCall.args_map/2` (for example, trailing commas are repaired) and can
  be disabled with `json_repair: false`, in which case malformed JSON
  yields an `:invalid` resolution. All other decode options accepted by
  `args_map/2` are likewise accepted.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.execute/3`

- `ToolCall.execute(call, available_tools, opts \\ [])` executes one
  resolved call. It accepts the same options as `resolve/3`.
- The tool callback is invoked exactly once, with the validated arguments,
  and only when the resolution state is `:valid`. Results and error values
  returned by the callback are propagated with the existing
  `Tool.execute/2` contract (`{:ok, value}` or `{:error, value}`).
- Calls whose resolution state is `:invalid`, `:unknown`,
  `:provider_executed`, or `:provider_native` return `{:error, resolution}`
  where `resolution` is the full resolution map, and no callback is
  invoked; executing such a call must not execute any other tool either.

### `ReqLLM.ToolResult`

- `output` is application-visible data and `content` is model-facing
  content. The two may intentionally differ and are independently
  inspectable; `content` may hold text, JSON-derived text, error text,
  file/image content parts, or provider-native content part shapes.
- `ReqLLM.Context` tool-result message helpers preserve a `ToolResult`'s
  explicit `content` as the message content, record the raw `output` in
  message metadata (retrievable via `ToolResult.output_from_message/1`),
  and preserve any other `ToolResult` metadata entries in the message
  metadata.
- Whether a normalized tool message carries explicitly supplied model-facing
  content (as opposed to content derived from `output`) can be
  distinguished from the message alone; tool results normalized without
  explicit content must not be reported as carrying explicit content.
- Provider request encoders prefer explicitly supplied model-facing content
  over the derived application `output` when replaying tool-result messages
  (e.g. OpenAI Responses `function_call_output` string, Google Gemini
  `functionResponse` payload, Anthropic `tool_result` blocks). Providers
  that already serialize non-empty message content directly are unaffected.
  When only `output` is present, the existing encodings are unchanged:
  map/list outputs encode as structured values, other outputs as text.
- OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google tool-result encodings remain
  provider-independent at the `ReqLLM.Context` level: the same message
  round-trips through each provider's request encoding without
  provider-specific branching.

### Existing behaviors preserved

- `ToolCall.new_builtin/3` and `ToolCall.builtin?/1` continue to mark and
  detect provider-executed builtin calls.
- `ToolCall.put_metadata/2` and `ToolCall.metadata/1` continue to attach,
  merge, and read non-wire call metadata.
- `Tool.execute/2` input validation, callback invocation, and result
  contracts are unchanged.

- Preserve existing builtin/provider-executed tool markers and provider metadata.
- Keep individual tool execution helpers explicit and single-call.

## Out of scope

- New parallel tool call/result structs.
- Automatically executing tool calls or starting a follow-up model request.
- Loop termination, approvals, memory, durability, MCP runtime, or provider wire refactors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current provider tool calls can be handled without provider-specific branching.
- [ ] Invalid or unknown calls are inspectable and cannot execute accidentally.
- [ ] Application output and model-facing content can differ explicitly.
- [ ] Existing callbacks and round trips remain compatible.
- [ ] Provider-executed/native tools remain distinguishable from application tools.

## Validation

- [ ] Run Tool, ToolCall, ToolResult, validation, callback, invalid/unknown, builtin, parallel, and round-trip tests.
- [ ] Run OpenAI, Anthropic, and multimodal tool-result replays.
- [ ] Run mix test and mix quality.

## Pull request boundary

This issue closes through exactly one pull request containing the implementation or focused contract document, direct tests, and directly affected documentation. Unrelated provider migrations and cleanup are excluded.
