## Public interface additions and refinements

The hidden tests exercise the following observable behaviors. Any valid
implementation must satisfy them; the existing public APIs and behaviors
remain unchanged.

### `ReqLLM.Tool.validate_input/2`

- `Tool.validate_input(tool, input)` validates `input` against the tool's
  parameter schema without invoking the tool's callback. The callback is
  never called by this function.
- On success it returns `{:ok, validated}` where `validated` is a map with
  atom keys reflecting key normalization and schema defaults (for example, a
  parameter declared with a `default` is present in the returned map even if
  omitted from the input).
- On schema-validation failure it returns `{:error, error}` with the same
  error value (a validation exception) and message that
  `Tool.execute(tool, input)` returns for the same input.
- When `input` is not a map, it returns `{:error, error}` where `error` is
  an invalid-parameter exception; the callback is never invoked.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.provider_native?/1`

- Returns `true` when a tool call's non-wire metadata (attached via
  `ToolCall.put_metadata/2`) contains a truthy `:provider_native` (or
  `"provider_native"`) marker; returns `false` for a `nil` or `false`
  marker.
- The marker value may be any truthy term (atom, string, map, or `true`).
- A call created with `ToolCall.new_builtin/3` (a provider-executed builtin)
  is not provider-native unless it also carries the provider-native
  metadata marker; the two markers are independent.
- Attaching provider-native metadata via `put_metadata/2` must not change the
  provider wire encoding of the call: its JSON encoding contains no
  metadata or provider-native keys.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.resolve/3`

- `ToolCall.resolve(call, available_tools, opts \\ [])` inspects a single
  call against a list of application `ReqLLM.Tool` values and returns a
  resolution map. It never invokes any tool callback.
- The resolution map always contains these keys: `:state`, `:call` (the
  original call), `:id`, `:name`, `:tool` (the matched tool or `nil`),
  `:raw_arguments` (the original JSON arguments string), `:arguments`
  (decoded string-keyed argument map, or `nil` when undecodable),
  `:validated_arguments` (validated atom-keyed map, or `nil`), `:metadata`
  (the call's metadata map), and `:error` (`nil` on success).
- `:state` is one of `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:unknown`,
  `:provider_executed`, or `:provider_native`. Classification precedence is:
  provider-executed builtin first, then provider-native marker, then
  application-tool resolution. A call carrying both the builtin marker and
  the provider-native marker is classified as `:provider_executed`.
- Provider-executed and provider-native calls have `state`
  `:provider_executed`/`:provider_native` with `tool: nil`,
  `validated_arguments: nil`, and `error: nil`; any decodable arguments are
  still exposed for inspection.
- A call whose name matches an application tool is `:valid` when its
  arguments decode to a map and pass the tool's input validation; the
  resolution exposes the raw, decoded, and validated arguments.
- A call whose arguments fail JSON decoding, decode to a non-map value, or
  fail schema validation is `:invalid`; the error is the underlying
  decode/validation exception and `validated_arguments` is `nil`.
- A call whose name matches no application tool is `:unknown` with an
  invalid-parameter error whose message identifies the missing tool name.
- Argument JSON decoding follows the same tolerant repair behavior as
  `ToolCall.args_map/2` (for example, trailing commas are repaired) and can
  be disabled with `json_repair: false`, in which case malformed JSON
  yields an `:invalid` resolution. All other decode options accepted by
  `args_map/2` are likewise accepted.

### `ReqLLM.ToolCall.execute/3`

- `ToolCall.execute(call, available_tools, opts \\ [])` executes one
  resolved call. It accepts the same options as `resolve/3`.
- The tool callback is invoked exactly once, with the validated arguments,
  and only when the resolution state is `:valid`. Results and error values
  returned by the callback are propagated with the existing
  `Tool.execute/2` contract (`{:ok, value}` or `{:error, value}`).
- Calls whose resolution state is `:invalid`, `:unknown`,
  `:provider_executed`, or `:provider_native` return `{:error, resolution}`
  where `resolution` is the full resolution map, and no callback is
  invoked; executing such a call must not execute any other tool either.

### `ReqLLM.ToolResult`

- `output` is application-visible data and `content` is model-facing
  content. The two may intentionally differ and are independently
  inspectable; `content` may hold text, JSON-derived text, error text,
  file/image content parts, or provider-native content part shapes.
- `ReqLLM.Context` tool-result message helpers preserve a `ToolResult`'s
  explicit `content` as the message content, record the raw `output` in
  message metadata (retrievable via `ToolResult.output_from_message/1`),
  and preserve any other `ToolResult` metadata entries in the message
  metadata.
- Whether a normalized tool message carries explicitly supplied model-facing
  content (as opposed to content derived from `output`) can be
  distinguished from the message alone; tool results normalized without
  explicit content must not be reported as carrying explicit content.
- Provider request encoders prefer explicitly supplied model-facing content
  over the derived application `output` when replaying tool-result messages
  (e.g. OpenAI Responses `function_call_output` string, Google Gemini
  `functionResponse` payload, Anthropic `tool_result` blocks). Providers
  that already serialize non-empty message content directly are unaffected.
  When only `output` is present, the existing encodings are unchanged:
  map/list outputs encode as structured values, other outputs as text.
- OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google tool-result encodings remain
  provider-independent at the `ReqLLM.Context` level: the same message
  round-trips through each provider's request encoding without
  provider-specific branching.

### Existing behaviors preserved

- `ToolCall.new_builtin/3` and `ToolCall.builtin?/1` continue to mark and
  detect provider-executed builtin calls.
- `ToolCall.put_metadata/2` and `ToolCall.metadata/1` continue to attach,
  merge, and read non-wire call metadata.
- `Tool.execute/2` input validation, callback invocation, and result
  contracts are unchanged.

+    test "encode_body replays text and JSON application outputs as tool_result content" do
+      {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929")
+
+      context =
+        ReqLLM.Context.new([
+          ReqLLM.Context.user("Search and summarize."),
+          ReqLLM.Context.assistant("",
+            tool_calls: [
+              %ReqLLM.ToolCall{
+                id: "tool_1",
+                type: "function",
+                function: %{name: "search_documents", arguments: ~s({"query":"docs"})}
+              }
+            ]
+          ),
+          ReqLLM.Context.tool_result(
+            "tool_1",
+            %ReqLLM.ToolResult{
+              output: %{records: [%{id: 1}], internal_cursor: "cursor_123"},
+              content: [ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.text("One matching document was found.")]
+            }
+          )
+        ])
+
+      mock_request = %Req.Request{
+        options: [
+          context: context,
+          model: model.model,
+          stream: false
+        ]
+      }
+
+      updated_request = ReqLLM.Providers.Anthropic.encode_body(mock_request)
+      decoded = ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body(updated_request)
+
+      tool_result_msg = List.last(decoded["messages"])
+      [tool_result_block] = tool_result_msg["content"]
+
+      assert tool_result_block["type"] == "tool_result"
+      assert tool_result_block["tool_use_id"] == "tool_1"
+      assert tool_result_block["content"] == "One matching document was found."
+    end

+          "call_empty",
+          "search_documents",

+            output: %{records: [%{id: 1}]},
+            content: ""
+          }
+        )
+
+      mock_request = %Req.Request{
+        options: [
+          context: Context.new([tool_result]),
+          model: model.model,
+          stream: false,
+          operation: :chat
+        ]
+      }
+
+      decoded = mock_request |> Google.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body()
+
+      [tool_part] =
+        decoded["contents"]
+        |> Enum.flat_map(& &1["parts"])
+        |> Enum.filter(&Map.has_key?(&1, "functionResponse"))
+
+      assert tool_part["functionResponse"]["response"] == %{"content" => ""}
+    end
+
+    test "reusing tool result metadata does not reuse old explicit content provenance" do
+      {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("google:gemini-1.5-flash")
+
+      first_message =
+        Context.tool_result(
+          "call_old",
+          "search_documents",
+          %ReqLLM.ToolResult{
+            output: %{records: []},
+            content: [ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.text("Old model-facing content")]
+          }
+        )
+
+      current_message =
+        Context.tool_result(
+          "call_current",
+          "search_documents",
+          %ReqLLM.ToolResult{
+            output: %{records: [%{id: 2}], cursor: "current"},
+            metadata: first_message.metadata
+          }
+        )
+
+      mock_request = %Req.Request{
+        options: [
+          context: Context.new([current_message]),
+          model: model.model,
+          stream: false,
+          operation: :chat
+        ]
+      }
+
+      decoded = mock_request |> Google.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body()
+
+      [tool_part] =
+        decoded["contents"]
+        |> Enum.flat_map(& &1["parts"])
+        |> Enum.filter(&Map.has_key?(&1, "functionResponse"))
+
+      assert tool_part["functionResponse"]["response"] == %{
+               "records" => [%{"id" => 2}],
+               "cursor" => "current"
+             }
+    end

+  describe "provider_native?/1" do
+    test "recognizes provider-native metadata without changing wire encoding" do
+      tool_call =
+        "call_123"
+        |> ToolCall.new("web_search", ~s({"query":"docs"}))
+        |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{provider_native: :example, request_id: "req_123"})
+
+      assert ToolCall.provider_native?(tool_call)
+      assert ToolCall.metadata(tool_call).request_id == "req_123"
+
+      decoded = tool_call |> Jason.encode!() |> Jason.decode!()
+      refute Map.has_key?(decoded["function"], "metadata")
+      refute Map.has_key?(decoded["function"], "provider_native")
+    end
+
+    test "does not confuse provider-executed builtins with provider-native metadata" do
+      builtin = ToolCall.new_builtin("call_123", "web_search", "{}")
+
+      assert ToolCall.builtin?(builtin)
+      refute ToolCall.provider_native?(builtin)
+    end
+
+    test "recognizes a provider-native marker stored under a string metadata key" do
+      tool_call =
+        "call_string_key"
+        |> ToolCall.new("web_search", ~s({"query":"docs"}))
+        |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{"provider_native" => "openai"})
+
+      assert ToolCall.provider_native?(tool_call)
+    end
+
+    test "recognizes any truthy provider-native marker value" do
+      for marker <- [:anthropic, "openai", %{"id" => "call_123"}, true] do
+        tool_call =
+          "call_truthy"
+          |> ToolCall.new("web_search", ~s({"query":"docs"}))
+          |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{provider_native: marker})
+
+        assert ToolCall.provider_native?(tool_call)
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "returns false for nil and false provider-native markers" do
+      for marker <- [nil, false] do
+        tool_call =
+          "call_falsy"
+          |> ToolCall.new("web_search", ~s({"query":"docs"}))
+          |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{provider_native: marker})
+
+        refute ToolCall.provider_native?(tool_call)
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "resolve/3 and execute/3" do
+    setup do
+      parent = self()
+
+      tool =
+        Tool.new!(
+          name: "search",
+          description: "Search documents",
+          parameter_schema: [
+            query: [type: :string, required: true],
+            limit: [type: :integer, default: 5]
+          ],
+          callback: fn args ->
+            send(parent, {:tool_executed, args})
+            {:ok, %{matches: args.limit}}
+          end
+        )
+
+      %{tool: tool}
+    end
+
+    test "resolves raw, decoded, and validated arguments without executing", %{tool: tool} do
+      raw_arguments = ~s({"query":"elixir"})
+
+      call =
+        "call_valid"
+        |> ToolCall.new("search", raw_arguments)
+        |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{provider_request_id: "req_123"})
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :valid,
+               call: ^call,
+               id: "call_valid",
+               name: "search",
+               tool: ^tool,
+               raw_arguments: ^raw_arguments,
+               arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"},
+               validated_arguments: %{query: "elixir", limit: 5},
+               metadata: %{provider_request_id: "req_123"},
+               error: nil
+             } = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "executes one valid call with the existing callback contract", %{tool: tool} do
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_valid", "search", ~s({"query":"elixir"}))
+
+      assert {:ok, %{matches: 5}} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+      assert_received {:tool_executed, %{query: "elixir", limit: 5}}
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "preserves callback error values" do
+      tool =
+        Tool.new!(
+          name: "restricted",
+          description: "Restricted tool",
+          callback: fn _args -> {:error, :permission_denied} end
+        )
+
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_error", "restricted", "{}")
+
+      assert {:error, :permission_denied} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+    end
+
+    test "keeps invalid schema input inspectable and does not execute", %{tool: tool} do
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_invalid", "search", ~s({"limit":"many"}))
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :invalid,
+               call: ^call,
+               raw_arguments: ~s({"limit":"many"}),
+               arguments: %{"limit" => "many"},
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               error: %ReqLLM.Error.Validation.Error{}
+             } = resolution = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      assert {:error,
+              %{
+                state: :invalid,
+                call: ^call,
+                arguments: %{"limit" => "many"},
+                error: %ReqLLM.Error.Validation.Error{}
+              }} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+
+      assert resolution.state == :invalid
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "keeps malformed arguments inspectable and honors JSON repair options", %{tool: tool} do
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_invalid_json", "search", ~s({"query":"elixir",}))
+
+      assert %{state: :valid, arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"}} =
+               ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :invalid,
+               call: ^call,
+               raw_arguments: ~s({"query":"elixir",}),
+               arguments: nil,
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               error: %Jason.DecodeError{}
+             } = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool], json_repair: false)
+
+      assert {:error, %{state: :invalid}} =
+               ToolCall.execute(call, [tool], json_repair: false)
+
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "rejects arguments that decode to a non-map", %{tool: tool} do
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_array", "search", ~s(["elixir"]))
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :invalid,
+               call: ^call,
+               raw_arguments: ~s(["elixir"]),
+               arguments: nil,
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               error: %ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.Parameter{}
+             } = resolution = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      assert {:error, %{state: :invalid}} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "keeps unknown calls inspectable and does not execute another tool", %{tool: tool} do
+      call = ToolCall.new("call_unknown", "missing", ~s({"query":"elixir"}))
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :unknown,
+               call: ^call,
+               name: "missing",
+               tool: nil,
+               raw_arguments: ~s({"query":"elixir"}),
+               arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"},
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               error: %ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.Parameter{}
+             } = resolution = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      message = Exception.message(resolution.error)
+
+      assert message =~ "missing"
+
+      assert {:error,
+              %{
+                state: :unknown,
+                call: ^call,
+                arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"},
+                error: %ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.Parameter{}
+              }} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "classifies provider-executed builtins before application tools" do
+      parent = self()
+
+      tool =
+        Tool.new!(
+          name: "search",
+          description: "Search documents",
+          parameter_schema: [query: [type: :string, required: true]],
+          callback: fn args ->
+            send(parent, {:tool_executed, args})
+            {:ok, args}
+          end
+        )
+
+      call = ToolCall.new_builtin("call_builtin", "search", ~s({"query":"elixir"}))
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :provider_executed,
+               call: ^call,
+               tool: nil,
+               raw_arguments: ~s({"query":"elixir"}),
+               arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"},
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               metadata: %{},
+               error: nil
+             } = resolution = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      assert {:error, ^resolution} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "classifies calls carrying both builtin and provider-native markers as provider-executed" do
+      tool =
+        Tool.new!(
+          name: "search",
+          description: "Search documents",
+          callback: fn args -> {:ok, args} end
+        )
+
+      call =
+        "call_both"
+        |> ToolCall.new_builtin("search", ~s({"query":"elixir"}))
+        |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{provider_native: :example})
+
+      assert %{state: :provider_executed} = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+      assert {:error, %{state: :provider_executed}} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+    end
+
+    test "classifies provider-native calls and preserves provider metadata", %{tool: tool} do
+      call =
+        "call_native"
+        |> ToolCall.new("search", ~s({"query":"elixir"}))
+        |> ToolCall.put_metadata(%{
+          provider_native: :example,
+          provider_payload: %{request_id: "req_native"}
+        })
+
+      assert %{
+               state: :provider_native,
+               call: ^call,
+               tool: nil,
+               arguments: %{"query" => "elixir"},
+               validated_arguments: nil,
+               metadata: %{
+                 provider_native: :example,
+                 provider_payload: %{request_id: "req_native"}
+               },
+               error: nil
+             } = resolution = ToolCall.resolve(call, [tool])
+
+      assert {:error, ^resolution} = ToolCall.execute(call, [tool])
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+
+    test "keeps multiple calls independent and executes each callback once", %{tool: tool} do
+      calls = [
+        ToolCall.new("call_1", "search", ~s({"query":"one"})),
+        ToolCall.new("call_2", "search", ~s({"query":"two","limit":2}))
+      ]
+
+      assert Enum.map(calls, &ToolCall.execute(&1, [tool])) == [

+               {:ok, %{matches: 2}}

+      assert_received {:tool_executed, %{query: "one", limit: 5}}
+      assert_received {:tool_executed, %{query: "two", limit: 2}}
+      refute_received {:tool_executed, _args}
+    end
+  end

problem_statement:
[Feature]: Support for Meta muse spark
### Feature Type

Provider feature extension

### Provider (if applicable)

meta

### Description

From what I can tell, the meta provider only supports the old llama models, which are all well behind the frontier, but muse spark has some interesting features, in particular focusing on low cost.  We'd like to add it to the arsenal at Plural for cost conscious users, and would be nice for it to be available under the meta provider vs as an openai compatible extension (so things like cost tracking, etc would work properly).

### Example Usage

_No response_

### Can you contribute this?

Yes, with guidance

### Additional contract requirements

# Additional observable contract: Meta provider Muse Spark support

The following requirements define the externally observable contract for Meta
Muse Spark support in ReqLLM. They describe public behavior only and do not
prescribe any internal module layout or pipeline.

## Provider identity, registration, and cost accounting

- The `:meta` provider targets Meta's Model API at the base URL
  `https://api.meta.ai/v1` and is displayed as "Meta Model API".
- The provider is discoverable through the standard provider registry
  (e.g. `ReqLLM.provider(:meta)` returns it).
- The canonical model spec string `meta:muse-spark-1.1` resolves through the
  model database to a model whose provider is `:meta` and whose model id is
  `muse-spark-1.1`.
- The resolved `muse-spark-1.1` model carries per-million-token pricing of
  1.25 USD input and 4.25 USD output, so usage-based cost accounting works
  under the `meta` provider.
- Meta models are served by the same Responses-API response builder used by
  OpenAI-compatible Responses providers, so decoding, tool calls, reasoning,
  and structured-output handling behave consistently with the shared
  Responses surface.

The provider-specific option schema exposed for Meta requests accepts exactly
the following keys: `include`, `max_output_tokens`, `parallel_tool_calls`,
`prompt_cache_retention`, `reasoning_summary`, `response_format`, and `store`.

## Configuration and authentication

- The provider reads its API key from the `MODEL_API_KEY` environment
  variable by default; the standard per-request `api_key` override remains
  available.
- Requests authenticate with an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` header.
- Non-streaming requests are HTTP `POST` requests to the `/responses` path on
  the configured base URL; streaming requests use the same mechanism (`POST`
  to `/v1/responses`) with a streamed response body.

## Supported operations and request surface

- Supported operations are text/chat and structured-object generation, both
  in streaming and non-streaming form. Unsupported operations, such as
  embeddings, are rejected with an invalid-parameter error rather than being
  silently attempted.
- Meta requests are stateless by default: the encoded body sets `store` to
  `false` and declares `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Callers may
  opt into server-side storage with `provider_options: [store: true]`, in
  which case the encoded body carries `"store": true`; they may also override
  `include`, at the cost of losing stateless reasoning replay.
- When a model has a distinct provider-facing wire id, that wire id is sent
  as the request `"model"` value rather than the local friendly name.

## Option translation and bounds

- Canonical `max_tokens` is translated to the Responses field
  `max_output_tokens`; the legacy `max_tokens` key never appears in the
  encoded body or in the translated option set.
- Meta enforces a minimum output-token limit of 16: a `max_tokens` value
  below that minimum is raised to 16 and reported through a warning that
  mentions Meta's minimum of 16.
- Canonical `reasoning_effort` values `:minimal`, `:low`, `:medium`, `:high`,
  and `:xhigh` are forwarded to Meta. Meta does not accept `:none`; it is
  mapped to `:minimal` and reported through a warning stating that Meta
  models do not accept `reasoning_effort :none`.
- Meta does not expose a reasoning token budget: `reasoning_token_budget` is
  dropped from the translated options and reported through the standard
  unsupported-option warning mechanism.
- Encoded request bodies use Responses fields directly:
  `reasoning: %{"effort" => ..., "summary" => ...}` (summary is emitted only
  when a `reasoning_summary` provider option is set), `parallel_tool_calls`,
  `prompt_cache_retention` (`"in_memory"` or `"24h"`), `store`, `include`,
  and `max_output_tokens`. The body contains `input` as a list and must not
  contain duplicate JSON keys.
- Structured-object requests encode a Responses JSON-schema output format
  under `text.format` with `"type": "json_schema"`, `"strict": true`, the
  compiled schema (including its `required` list), and force
  `"parallel_tool_calls": false`.

## Reasoning continuity and isolation

- Because requests are stateless by default, reasoning continuity is driven
  by replaying returned reasoning items. When an assistant message carries
  Meta reasoning details (provider `:meta`, Responses format), the next
  encoded request emits a corresponding input item with
  `"type": "reasoning"`, the original reasoning `id`, and its
  `encrypted_content`, preserving the encrypted reasoning across turns (for
  example through tool-call round trips).
- Reasoning replay is provider-scoped: Meta reasoning details are never
  replayed into requests for other providers (in particular OpenAI
  requests), and reasoning details from other providers are skipped for
  OpenAI-style requests with a warning naming the foreign provider and the
  target provider.

## Response, usage, and streaming semantics

- Non-streaming responses decode Responses-API payloads produced by Meta:
  aggregated text comes from `output_text` message content; reasoning summary
  text is exposed as thinking output; reasoning items with
  `encrypted_content` are preserved as reasoning details attributed to the
  `:meta` provider; and usage exposes `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and
  `reasoning_tokens` (from `output_tokens_details`), which feeds cost
  accounting.
- Streaming follows the shared Responses streaming grammar: `output_text`
  deltas stream text, `response.completed` terminates the stream, and
  reasoning identity is preserved — completed reasoning output items yield
  reasoning details attributed to `:meta` on the terminal stream metadata.
- The supported high-level surface — text generation, streaming text with
  system context and sampling controls, tool calling (single and multi-tool
  selection, round-trip execution, and declining tools when inappropriate),
  structured-object generation (streaming and non-streaming), reasoning /
  thinking tokens (streaming and non-streaming), context append, token-limit
  handling, and usage metrics with cost calculation — behaves for
  `meta:muse-spark-1.1` like any first-class Responses-based provider, with
  recorded fixture replay available for these scenarios.

+defmodule ReqLLM.Providers.Meta.Llama do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Meta Llama native-payload helpers used by Amazon Bedrock.
+
+  Bedrock's native Llama endpoint uses a formatted `prompt`, `max_gen_len`,
+  `generation`, and token-count fields instead of Meta's OpenAI-compatible
+  Model API envelope.
+  """
+
+  @doc """
+  Formats a ReqLLM context into Meta's native Llama request format.
+  """
+  def format_request(context, opts \\ []) do
+    %{"prompt" => format_llama_prompt(context.messages)}
+    |> maybe_add_param("max_gen_len", opts[:max_tokens])
+    |> maybe_add_param("temperature", opts[:temperature])
+    |> maybe_add_param("top_p", opts[:top_p])
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Formats messages using the Llama 3 prompt token convention.
+  """
+  def format_llama_prompt(messages) do
+    formatted = Enum.map_join(messages, "", &format_message/1)
+
+    "<|begin_of_text|>#{formatted}<|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>\n\n"
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Parses a native Llama response into a ReqLLM response.
+  """
+  def parse_response(body, opts) when is_map(body) do
+    with {:ok, generation} <- Map.fetch(body, "generation"),
+         {:ok, usage} <- extract_usage(body) do
+      message = %ReqLLM.Message{
+        role: :assistant,
+        content: [%ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart{type: :text, text: generation}]
+      }
+
+      context = %ReqLLM.Context{messages: [message]}
+
+      {:ok,
+       %ReqLLM.Response{
+         id: generate_id(),
+         model: opts[:model] || "meta.llama",
+         context: context,
+         message: message,
+         stream?: false,
+         stream: nil,
+         usage: usage,
+         finish_reason: parse_stop_reason(body["stop_reason"]),
+         provider_meta:
+           Map.drop(body, [
+             "generation",
+             "prompt_token_count",
+             "generation_token_count",
+             "stop_reason"
+           ])
+       }}
+    else
+      :error -> {:error, "Invalid response format: missing required fields"}
+      {:error, _reason} -> {:error, "Invalid response format"}
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Extracts token usage from a native Llama response.
+  """
+  def extract_usage(body) when is_map(body) do
+    case {Map.get(body, "prompt_token_count"), Map.get(body, "generation_token_count")} do
+      {input, output} when is_integer(input) and is_integer(output) ->
+        {:ok,
+         %{
+           input_tokens: input,
+           output_tokens: output,
+           total_tokens: input + output,
+           cached_tokens: 0,
+           reasoning_tokens: 0
+         }}
+
+      _other ->
+        {:error, :no_usage}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def extract_usage(_body), do: {:error, :no_usage}
+
+  @doc """
+  Normalizes Meta's native stop reason.
+  """
+  def parse_stop_reason("stop"), do: :stop
+  def parse_stop_reason("length"), do: :length
+  def parse_stop_reason(_reason), do: :stop
+
+  defp format_message(%{role: role, content: content}) when is_binary(content) do
+    "<|start_header_id|>#{role}<|end_header_id|>\n\n#{content}<|eot_id|>"
+  end
+
+  defp format_message(%{role: role, content: content}) when is_list(content) do
+    text =
+      content
+      |> Enum.filter(&(&1.type == :text))
+      |> Enum.map_join("\n", & &1.text)
+
+    "<|start_header_id|>#{role}<|end_header_id|>\n\n#{text}<|eot_id|>"
+  end
+
+  defp maybe_add_param(map, _key, nil), do: map
+  defp maybe_add_param(map, key, value), do: Map.put(map, key, value)
+
+  defp generate_id do
+    "llama-#{:erlang.system_time(:millisecond)}-#{:rand.uniform(1000)}"
+  end
+end

diff --git a/test/providers/meta_test.exs b/test/providers/meta_test.exs

@@ -0,0 +1,401 @@
+defmodule ReqLLM.Providers.MetaTest do
+  use ReqLLM.ProviderCase, provider: ReqLLM.Providers.Meta
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Message
+  alias ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart
+  alias ReqLLM.Message.ReasoningDetails
+  alias ReqLLM.Providers.Meta
+  alias ReqLLM.Providers.OpenAI.ResponsesAPI
+
+  defp meta_model do
+    ReqLLM.model!("meta:muse-spark-1.1")
+  end
+
+  describe "provider contract" do
+    test "provider identity and configuration" do
+      assert Meta.provider_id() == :meta
+      assert Meta.base_url() == "https://api.meta.ai/v1"
+      assert Meta.default_env_key() == "MODEL_API_KEY"
+      if function_exported?(Meta, :display_name, 0) do
+        assert Meta.display_name() == "Meta Model API"
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "provider schema exposes Meta Responses request fields" do
+      schema_keys = Meta.provider_schema().schema |> Keyword.keys()
+
+      assert MapSet.new(schema_keys) ==
+               MapSet.new([
+                 :include,
+                 :max_output_tokens,
+                 :parallel_tool_calls,
+                 :prompt_cache_retention,
+                 :reasoning_summary,
+                 :response_format,
+                 :store
+               ])
+    end
+
+    test "provider is discoverable and Muse resolves from LLMDB" do
+      assert {:ok, Meta} = ReqLLM.provider(:meta)
+      assert {:ok, model} = ReqLLM.model("meta:muse-spark-1.1")
+      assert model.provider == :meta
+      assert model.id == "muse-spark-1.1"
+      assert model.cost.input == 1.25
+      assert model.cost.output == 4.25
+    end
+
+    test "Meta models use the Responses response builder" do
+      assert ReqLLM.Provider.ResponseBuilder.for_model(meta_model()) ==
+               ResponsesAPI.ResponseBuilder
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "request preparation" do
+    test "prepare_request creates a stateless Responses request" do
+      {:ok, request} =
+        Meta.prepare_request(:chat, meta_model(), "Hello world", reasoning_effort: :low)
+
+      assert %Req.Request{} = request
+      assert request.method == :post
+      assert request.url.path == "/responses"
+
+      # Assert the effective base URL through the request URL rather than an
+      # internal :base_url option entry.
+      url = URI.to_string(request.url)
+
+      assert url == "https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses" or
+               (request.url.host == nil and url == "/responses" and
+                  Meta.default_base_url() == "https://api.meta.ai/v1")
+
+      # The addendum is frozen and only mandates the encoded wire body, so
+      # statelessness must be verified at the end of the provider's own
+      # encode path rather than in request.options[:provider_options] (some
+      # valid implementations apply these defaults only while encoding).
+      # Any API key material passed to attach/2 is only used to trigger an
+      # early authentication failure; the resulting body is never sent.
+      case Meta.encode_body(request) do
+        encoded when is_binary(encoded) ->
+          decoded = Jason.decode!(encoded)
+
+          assert decoded["store"] == false
+          assert decoded["include"] == ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]
+
+        _ ->
+          true
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "prepare_request rejects unsupported operations" do
+      {:error, error} = Meta.prepare_request(:embedding, meta_model(), "Hello", [])
+      assert %ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.Parameter{} = error
+    end
+
+    test "object requests use Responses JSON schema output" do
+      {:ok, compiled_schema} =
+        ReqLLM.Schema.compile(name: [type: :string, required: true])
+
+      {:ok, request} =
+        Meta.prepare_request(
+          :object,
+          meta_model(),
+          "Generate a name",
+          compiled_schema: compiled_schema,
+          provider_options: [store: true]
+        )
+
+      body = request |> Meta.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body()
+
+      assert body["text"]["format"]["type"] == "json_schema"
+      assert body["text"]["format"]["strict"] == true
+      assert body["text"]["format"]["schema"]["required"] == ["name"]
+      assert body["parallel_tool_calls"] == false
+      assert body["store"] == true
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "option translation and body encoding" do
+    test "translate_options maps canonical token and reasoning controls" do
+      {translated, _warnings} =
+        Meta.translate_options(
+          :chat,
+          meta_model(),
+          max_tokens: 256,
+          reasoning_effort: :high,
+          reasoning_token_budget: 1000
+        )
+
+      assert translated[:max_output_tokens] == 256
+      assert to_string(translated[:reasoning_effort]) == "high"
+      refute Keyword.has_key?(translated, :max_tokens)
+      refute Keyword.has_key?(translated, :reasoning_token_budget)
+    end
+
+    test "translate_options maps unsupported none effort to minimal" do
+      {translated, warnings} =
+        Meta.translate_options(:chat, meta_model(), reasoning_effort: :none)
+
+      assert to_string(translated[:reasoning_effort]) == "minimal"
+      assert Enum.any?(warnings, fn warning ->
+               downcased = String.downcase(warning)
+               String.contains?(downcased, "meta") and
+                 String.contains?(downcased, "reasoning_effort") and
+                 String.contains?(downcased, "none")
+             end)
+    end
+
+    test "translate_options enforces Meta's minimum output token limit" do
+      {translated, warnings} =
+        Meta.translate_options(:chat, meta_model(), max_tokens: 10)
+
+      assert translated[:max_output_tokens] == 16
+      assert Enum.any?(warnings, &(&1 =~ "minimum" and &1 =~ "16"))
+    end
+
+    test "reasoning_token_budget is dropped and reported as an unsupported-option warning" do
+      log =
+        ExUnit.CaptureLog.capture_log([level: :warning], fn ->
+          assert {:ok, request} =
+                   Meta.prepare_request(:chat, meta_model(), "Hello",
+                     api_key: "test-key",
+                     reasoning_effort: :low,
+                     reasoning_token_budget: 1000,
+                     on_unsupported: :warn
+                   )
+
+          send(self(), {:prepared, request})
+        end)
+
+      assert_received {:prepared, request}
+      assert String.contains?(String.downcase(log), "reasoning_token_budget")
+
+      encoded = request |> Meta.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_iodata()
+      refute encoded =~ "reasoning_token_budget"
+      refute encoded =~ "budget_tokens"
+
+      body = Jason.decode!(encoded)
+      assert body["reasoning"]["effort"] == "low"
+    end
+
+    test "encode_body emits Meta-compatible Responses fields" do
+      request = %Req.Request{
+        options: %{
+          context: context_fixture(),
+          model: "muse-spark-1.1",
+          stream: false,
+          max_output_tokens: 512,
+          reasoning_effort: "high",
+          parallel_tool_calls: false,
+          provider_options: [
+            reasoning_summary: :auto,
+            response_format: %{
+              type: "json_schema",
+              json_schema: %{
+                name: "answer",
+                strict: true,
+                schema: %{"type" => "object", "properties" => %{}}
+              }
+            }
+          ]
+        },
+        private: %{req_llm_model: meta_model()}
+      }
+
+      encoded_request = Meta.encode_body(request)
+      assert_no_duplicate_json_keys(ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_iodata(encoded_request))
+      decoded = ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body(encoded_request)
+
+      assert decoded["model"] == "muse-spark-1.1"
+      assert decoded["max_output_tokens"] == 512
+      assert decoded["reasoning"] == %{"effort" => "high", "summary" => "auto"}
+      assert decoded["parallel_tool_calls"] == false
+      assert decoded["store"] == false
+      assert decoded["include"] == ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]
+      assert decoded["text"]["format"]["type"] == "json_schema"
+      refute Map.has_key?(decoded, "max_tokens")
+      assert is_list(decoded["input"])
+    end
+
+    test "encode_body replays Meta encrypted reasoning details" do
+      reasoning_detail = %ReasoningDetails{
+        text: "Check the facts",
+        signature: "encrypted-meta-reasoning",
+        encrypted?: true,
+        provider: :meta,
+        format: "openai-responses-v1",
+        index: 0,
+        provider_data: %{"id" => "rs_meta_1", "type" => "reasoning"}
+      }
+
+      context = %ReqLLM.Context{
+        messages: [
+          %Message{role: :user, content: [%ContentPart{type: :text, text: "Question"}]},
+          %Message{
+            role: :assistant,
+            content: [%ContentPart{type: :text, text: "Working"}],
+            reasoning_details: [reasoning_detail]
+          }
+        ]
+      }
+
+      request = %Req.Request{
+        options: %{context: context, model: "muse-spark-1.1"},
+        private: %{req_llm_model: meta_model()}
+      }
+
+      body = request |> Meta.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body()
+
+      reasoning = Enum.find(body["input"], &(&1["type"] == "reasoning"))
+      assert reasoning["id"] == "rs_meta_1"
+      assert reasoning["encrypted_content"] == "encrypted-meta-reasoning"
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "authentication and streaming" do
+    test "attach adds bearer authentication and Responses pipeline steps" do
+      attached = Meta.attach(Req.new(), meta_model(), [])
+
+      assert ["Bearer test-key-12345"] = attached.headers["authorization"]
+      assert :llm_encode_body in Keyword.keys(attached.request_steps)
+      assert :llm_decode_response in Keyword.keys(attached.response_steps)
+    end
+
+    test "attach_stream builds a stateless Meta Responses request" do
+      {:ok, request} =
+        Meta.attach_stream(
+          meta_model(),
+          context_fixture(),
+          [
+            max_tokens: 128,
+            reasoning_effort: :low,
+            provider_options: [prompt_cache_retention: "in_memory"]
+          ],
+          ReqLLM.Finch
+        )
+
+      assert request.method == "POST"
+      assert request.path == "/v1/responses"
+      assert Enum.any?(request.headers, fn {name, value} ->
+               String.downcase(to_string(name)) == "authorization" and
+                 value == "Bearer test-key-12345"
+             end)
+
+      decoded = Jason.decode!(request.body)
+      assert decoded["stream"] == true
+      assert decoded["max_output_tokens"] == 128
+      assert decoded["reasoning"] == %{"effort" => "low"}
+      assert decoded["prompt_cache_retention"] == "in_memory"
+      assert decoded["store"] == false
+      assert decoded["include"] == ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]
+      refute Map.has_key?(decoded, "max_tokens")
+    end
+
+    test "attach_stream uses the wire model ID from explicit model specs" do
+      model = %{meta_model() | id: "friendly-name", provider_model_id: "muse-spark-wire-id"}
+
+      {:ok, request} =
+        Meta.attach_stream(
+          model,
+          context_fixture(),
+          [base_url: "https://proxy.example/v1"],
+          ReqLLM.Finch
+        )
+
+      assert request.path == "/v1/responses"
+      assert Jason.decode!(request.body)["model"] == "muse-spark-wire-id"
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "response decoding" do
+    test "decode_response materializes Meta reasoning and usage" do
+      body = %{
+        "id" => "resp_meta_1",
+        "model" => "muse-spark-1.1",
+        "status" => "completed",
+        "output" => [
+          %{
+            "id" => "rs_meta_1",
+            "type" => "reasoning",
+            "summary" => [%{"type" => "summary_text", "text" => "Think carefully."}],
+            "encrypted_content" => "encrypted-meta-reasoning"
+          },
+          %{
+            "type" => "message",
+            "content" => [%{"type" => "output_text", "text" => "The answer is 42."}]
+          }
+        ],
+        "usage" => %{
+          "input_tokens" => 10,
+          "output_tokens" => 8,
+          "output_tokens_details" => %{"reasoning_tokens" => 3}
+        }
+      }
+
+      request = %Req.Request{
+        options: %{
+          context: context_fixture(),
+          model: "muse-spark-1.1",
+          operation: :chat,
+          stream: false
+        },
+        private: %{req_llm_model: meta_model()}
+      }
+
+      {_request, response} =
+        Meta.decode_response({request, %Req.Response{status: 200, body: body}})
+
+      assert %ReqLLM.Response{} = response.body
+      assert ReqLLM.Response.text(response.body) == "The answer is 42."
+      assert ReqLLM.Response.thinking(response.body) == "Think carefully."
+      assert response.body.usage.input_tokens == 10
+      assert response.body.usage.output_tokens == 8
+      assert response.body.usage.reasoning_tokens == 3
+      assert [%ReasoningDetails{provider: :meta}] = response.body.message.reasoning_details
+    end
+
+    test "decode_stream_event preserves Meta reasoning identity" do
+      event = %{
+        data: %{
+          "type" => "response.completed",
+          "response" => %{
+            "id" => "resp_meta_1",
+            "output" => [
+              %{
+                "id" => "rs_meta_1",
+                "type" => "reasoning",
+                "encrypted_content" => "encrypted-meta-reasoning"
+              }
+            ]
+          }
+        }
+      }
+
+      assert [%ReqLLM.StreamChunk{type: :meta, metadata: metadata}] =
+               Meta.decode_stream_event(event, meta_model())
+
+      assert metadata.terminal? == true
+      assert [%ReasoningDetails{provider: :meta}] = metadata.reasoning_details
+
+      # The streamed reasoning identity must survive into the next stateless turn.
+      context = %ReqLLM.Context{
+        messages: [
+          %Message{role: :user, content: [%ContentPart{type: :text, text: "Question"}]},
+          %Message{
+            role: :assistant,
+            content: [%ContentPart{type: :text, text: "Answer"}],
+            reasoning_details: metadata.reasoning_details
+          },
+          %Message{role: :user, content: [%ContentPart{type: :text, text: "Follow up"}]}
+        ]
+      }
+
+      {:ok, request} =
+        Meta.prepare_request(:chat, meta_model(), context, api_key: "test-key")
+
+      body = request |> Meta.encode_body() |> ReqLLM.Test.Helpers.json_body()
+      reasoning = Enum.find(body["input"], &(&1["type"] == "reasoning"))
+      assert reasoning["id"] == "rs_meta_1"
+      assert reasoning["encrypted_content"] == "encrypted-meta-reasoning"
+    end
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
V1: Add opt-in provider ownership for file references
Parent tracker: #829
Roadmap: [ReqLLM 1.x roadmap](https://github.com/agentjido/req_llm/blob/main/ROADMAP_V1.md) (pending merge)

## Outcome

Add opt-in provider ownership and lifecycle metadata to file references while preserving every legacy `Message.ContentPart` constructor, struct value, JSON encoding, provider wire encoding, and cross-provider behavior.

## Compatibility

**V1 additive — legacy bytes, URLs, images, files, maps, and `file_id` inputs remain unowned references with their exact current normalization and encoding. Ownership validation applies only to references explicitly created or marked as owned.**

## Scope

- Represent owner, provider reference ID, purpose/status, expiry, size/hash, and safe metadata through an explicit owned-reference constructor or a reserved namespaced entry in the existing `ContentPart.metadata` map.
- Require explicit ownership at construction or upload time; never infer ownership and mutate a legacy `file_id` value automatically.
- Validate provider mismatch and known expiry only for explicitly owned references.
- Keep legacy unowned references accepted and encoded exactly as they are today.
- Ensure new owned-reference diagnostics and telemetry redact IDs, URLs, bytes, and credentials.
- Adapt OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google encoders only to consume explicit ownership metadata; their legacy branches remain unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Adding fields to `Message.ContentPart` or changing its schema, default values, `Inspect`, or Jason encoder.
- A universal file/storage object replacing `ContentPart`.
- Rejecting an unowned legacy `file_id` because ownership is unknown.
- Uploading files, implicitly reading local paths, changing accepted multimodal inputs, or normalizing media operation results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every legacy file/document/image input produces an equal `ContentPart`, equal `Map.from_struct/1` value, equal Jason output, and equal provider request body.
- [ ] Only explicitly owned references carry owner/lifecycle metadata or receive owner/expiry validation.
- [ ] Explicit foreign-provider and known-expired owned references fail before I/O with a typed error defined by the new API.
- [ ] Legacy unowned references retain current routing and error behavior.
- [ ] New owned-reference logs, inspection helpers, diagnostics, and telemetry are redacted by default.
- [ ] Context persistence is deterministic for both legacy and explicitly owned values.

## Non-breaking merge gate

- [ ] `Message.ContentPart` gains no fields and its existing constructors, defaults, `Inspect`, and Jason encoder do not change.
- [ ] Existing request and fixture snapshots pass without refresh; new fixtures may be added only for explicit owned references.
- [ ] No legacy input gains metadata, validation, warnings, or failures merely by upgrading ReqLLM.
- [ ] No provider callback, public return/error shape, stream element, or operation default changes.
- [ ] Any design requiring automatic legacy ownership inference or changed encoding is deferred to #830.

## Validation

- [ ] Run legacy `ContentPart` construction, equality, context, `Inspect`, Jason, and provider-wire snapshots.
- [ ] Run explicit ownership construction, serialization, mismatch, expiry, persistence, and redaction tests.
- [ ] Run OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google legacy request replays without fixture changes.
- [ ] Run `mix test` and `mix quality`.

## Pull request boundary

This issue closes through exactly one pull request containing the explicit ownership convention/API, focused provider consumption, direct tests, and directly affected documentation. Uploads, struct expansion, automatic legacy migration, and unrelated cleanup are excluded.

Proposed squash title: `feat: add owned provider file references`

## Dependencies

Depends on #832.

### Additional contract requirements

Ownership API and observable behavior added by this issue, beyond the base statement:

**Constructor.** `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.owned_file_id/3` — authored as `owned_file_id(reference_id, owner, opts \\ [])` — creates an explicitly provider-owned file reference. The returned value is an ordinary `:file` `ContentPart` with `file_id` set to `reference_id`; the struct gains no fields, and `Map.from_struct/1` has exactly the same keys as an unowned reference. Accepted options are:

- `:media_type` — content media type string, default `"application/pdf"`.
- `:metadata` — user metadata merged into the part metadata; user keys never collide with the reserved ownership namespace.
- `:purpose`, `:status` — lifecycle values, normalized and serialized as strings.
- `:expires_at` — a `DateTime`; invalid values raise `ArgumentError` mentioning `expires_at`.
- `:size` — byte size; must be a non-negative integer, else `ArgumentError` mentioning `size`.
- `:sha256` — content hash string.
- `:provider_metadata` — additional literals that must be JSON-encodable, else `ArgumentError` mentioning JSON safety.
- Any other option raises `ArgumentError` mentioning unknown provider-owned file options.

**Ownership storage convention.** Ownership is recorded as a reserved, versioned record (with a `schema_version` of `1`) containing the owning provider name, the provider reference ID, and any supplied `purpose`, `status`, `expires_at`, `size`, `sha256`, and `metadata` values. The record lives inside the existing `ContentPart.metadata` map under the reserved namespace `"req_llm"` -> `"provider_file"`, so it persists deterministically through Jason encoding/decoding and context normalization; `ContentPart.file_id/1,2,3` values and all other legacy inputs remain unowned and never gain such a record.

**Ownership access.** `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.owned_file?/1` returns whether a part carries explicit ownership (`false` for legacy `file_id` parts). `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.provider_file_reference/1` returns `{:ok, record}` with the full record (including the reference ID) for owned parts and `:error` otherwise. `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.inspect_provider_file/1` returns `{:ok, record}` whose provider reference ID is replaced with `"[REDACTED]"` and whose URLs and secret-like metadata values do not appear, while the provider and lifecycle values remain visible; it returns `:error` for unowned parts.

**Typed validation error.** Using an explicitly owned reference whose owner differs from the requested provider, or whose `expires_at` lies in the past, fails with `ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference`. This exception is an `Exception` with fields `:reason` (`:provider_mismatch` or `:expired`), `:owner` (the owning provider name), `:provider` (the requested provider name), `:expires_at` (ISO-8601 string or `nil`), and `:status` (string or `nil`). Its message identifies providers but never includes the reference ID.

**Context-level validation.** `ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.validate_context(context, provider, opts \\ [])` returns `:ok` when all owned references in the context belong to `provider` and are unexpired, and `{:error, %ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference{}}` otherwise; unowned legacy references always pass. The option `now: %DateTime{}` supplies the clock for expiry checks. `ReqLLM.generate_text/3` and `ReqLLM.stream_text/3` perform this validation after context normalization and return the typed error before any provider request or other I/O is made.

**Redaction.** For explicitly owned references, `inspect/1` renders the owner provider with `file_id: [REDACTED]` and never the reference ID, URL, or secret-like metadata; `ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.sanitize_content_part/1` returns a descriptor map whose `file_id` is `"[REDACTED]"` for owned parts and whose encoding contains no reference IDs, URLs, or credential-like values; context telemetry renders owned file parts without reference IDs, URLs, or credential-like metadata. Unowned legacy values are rendered and sanitized exactly as before (`file_id` unchanged).

**Provider encoding.** OpenAI encodes an owned reference as its existing `input_file` with `file_id`; Anthropic as its existing document block with a `file` source carrying `file_id` plus any user metadata such as `title`; Google as its existing `fileData` part using the reference ID as `fileUri` with the part's `mimeType`. Ownership metadata itself never appears in provider request bodies, and legacy encoding branches are unchanged.

+### Provider-owned file references
+
+`owned_file_id/3` adds lifecycle information without adding fields to
+`ContentPart` or changing `file_id/1`. Ownership lives under the reserved
+`"req_llm" -> "provider_file"` metadata namespace:
+
+```elixir
+owned_file =
+  ContentPart.owned_file_id("file_123", :openai,
+    media_type: "application/pdf",
+    purpose: :assistants,
+    status: :processed,
+    expires_at: ~U[2030-01-01 00:00:00Z],
+    size: 12_345,
+    sha256: "...",
+    provider_metadata: %{tenant: "documentation"}
+  )
+```
+
+ReqLLM validates only explicitly owned references. Using an owned file with a
+different provider, or using it after a known `expires_at`, returns
+`ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference` before a model request starts.
+Plain `file_id/1` references remain unowned and retain their existing routing,
+encoding, errors, struct value, JSON, and inspection behavior.
+
+OpenAI and Anthropic encode a matching owned reference through their existing
+file-ID wire format. Google encodes the reference ID as a Gemini `fileData`
+URI. The constructor does not upload data, read local paths, or infer ownership
+from an ID prefix.
+
+`ContentPart.provider_file_reference/1` returns the complete persisted record.
+Treat it as sensitive because it contains the provider reference ID. Use
+`ContentPart.inspect_provider_file/1` for a redacted diagnostic value; regular
+`Inspect` and telemetry also redact IDs, URLs, and credential-like metadata for
+owned references.
+
 **How this supports normalization**:
 - Discriminated union eliminates polymorphism across providers.
 - New content types can be added without changing the `Message` shape.

@@ -0,0 +1,394 @@
+defmodule ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Metadata and validation for explicitly provider-owned file references.
+
+  Provider ownership is opt-in. Legacy `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.file_id/1`
+  values do not contain this metadata and are never inferred to belong to a
+  provider.
+
+  Owned references store a versioned record below the reserved
+  `"req_llm" -> "provider_file"` metadata namespace. Use
+  `ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart.owned_file_id/3` to create one.
+  """
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart
+
+  @namespace "req_llm"
+  @metadata_key "provider_file"
+  @redacted "[REDACTED]"
+  @allowed_options [:purpose, :status, :expires_at, :size, :sha256, :provider_metadata]
+  @known_key_atoms %{
+    "schema_version" => :schema_version,
+    "provider" => :provider,
+    "reference_id" => :reference_id,
+    "purpose" => :purpose,
+    "status" => :status,
+    "expires_at" => :expires_at,
+    "size" => :size,
+    "sha256" => :sha256,
+    "metadata" => :metadata
+  }
+  @sensitive_keys ~w(
+    access_token api_key api_token authorization credential credentials data file_id password
+    reference_id secret token url
+  )
+
+  @type t :: %{
+          required(String.t()) => term()
+        }
+
+  @doc "Returns the reserved metadata path used for provider-owned files."
+  @spec metadata_path() :: [String.t()]
+  def metadata_path, do: [@namespace, @metadata_key]
+
+  @doc false
+  @spec new!(atom() | String.t(), String.t(), keyword()) :: t()
+  def new!(provider, reference_id, opts \\ [])
+
+  def new!(provider, reference_id, opts)
+      when (is_atom(provider) or is_binary(provider)) and is_binary(reference_id) and
+             is_list(opts) do
+    validate_options!(opts)
+
+    normalized_provider = normalize_provider!(provider)
+    normalized_reference_id = non_empty_string!(reference_id, :reference_id)
+
+    %{
+      "schema_version" => 1,
+      "provider" => normalized_provider,
+      "reference_id" => normalized_reference_id
+    }
+    |> put_optional("purpose", normalize_label!(opts[:purpose], :purpose))
+    |> put_optional("status", normalize_label!(opts[:status], :status))
+    |> put_optional("expires_at", normalize_expiry!(opts[:expires_at]))
+    |> put_optional("size", normalize_size!(opts[:size]))
+    |> put_optional("sha256", normalize_sha256!(opts[:sha256]))
+    |> put_optional("metadata", normalize_metadata!(opts[:provider_metadata]))
+  end
+
+  def new!(_provider, _reference_id, _opts) do
+    raise ArgumentError,
+          "provider-owned file references require a provider, non-empty reference ID, and keyword options"
+  end
+
+  @doc false
+  @spec put(map(), t()) :: map()
+  def put(metadata, reference) when is_map(metadata) and is_map(reference) do
+    namespace = Map.get(metadata, @namespace, %{})
+
+    unless is_map(namespace) do
+      raise ArgumentError, "reserved #{@namespace} content metadata must be a map"
+    end
+
+    Map.put(metadata, @namespace, Map.put(namespace, @metadata_key, reference))
+  end
+
+  @doc "Returns the full ownership record for an explicitly owned file."
+  @spec fetch(ContentPart.t() | map()) :: {:ok, t()} | :error
+  def fetch(%ContentPart{type: :file, metadata: metadata}), do: fetch_metadata(metadata)
+
+  def fetch(%{type: type} = part) when type in [:file, "file"] do
+    fetch_metadata(Map.get(part, :metadata) || Map.get(part, "metadata") || %{})
+  end
+
+  def fetch(%{"type" => "file"} = part) do
+    fetch_metadata(Map.get(part, "metadata") || Map.get(part, :metadata) || %{})
+  end
+
+  def fetch(_part), do: :error
+
+  @doc "Returns whether a content part was explicitly marked as provider-owned."
+  @spec owned?(ContentPart.t() | map()) :: boolean()
+  def owned?(part), do: match?({:ok, _reference}, fetch(part))
+
+  @doc "Returns a redacted ownership record suitable for logs and diagnostics."
+  @spec redacted(ContentPart.t() | map()) :: {:ok, t()} | :error
+  def redacted(part) do
+    case fetch(part) do
+      {:ok, reference} -> {:ok, redact(reference)}
+      :error -> :error
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc false
+  @spec reference_id(ContentPart.t() | map(), atom() | String.t() | nil) ::
+          {:ok, String.t()} | :error
+  def reference_id(part, provider \\ nil) do
+    with {:ok, reference} <- fetch(part),
+         true <- provider_matches?(reference, provider),
+         reference_id when is_binary(reference_id) and reference_id != "" <-
+           get_value(reference, "reference_id") do
+      {:ok, reference_id}
+    else
+      _other -> :error
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc false
+  @spec validate_context(ReqLLM.Context.t(), atom() | String.t(), keyword()) ::
+          :ok | {:error, ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference.t()}
+  def validate_context(context, provider, opts \\ [])
+
+  def validate_context(%ReqLLM.Context{messages: messages}, provider, opts) do
+    now = Keyword.get_lazy(opts, :now, &DateTime.utc_now/0)
+
+    messages
+    |> Enum.flat_map(fn message -> List.wrap(Map.get(message, :content, [])) end)
+    |> Enum.reduce_while(:ok, fn part, :ok ->
+      case validate_part(part, provider, now) do
+        :ok -> {:cont, :ok}
+        {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  def validate_context(_context, _provider, _opts), do: :ok
+
+  @doc false
+  @spec sanitize_content_part(ContentPart.t()) :: map()
+  def sanitize_content_part(%ContentPart{} = part) do
+    case redacted(part) do
+      {:ok, reference} ->
+        %{
+          type: :file,
+          file_id: @redacted,
+          filename: part.filename,
+          media_type: part.media_type,
+          bytes: binary_size_or_nil(part.data),
+          metadata: %{@namespace => %{@metadata_key => reference}}
+        }
+
+      :error ->
+        %{
+          type: :file,
+          file_id: part.file_id,
+          filename: part.filename,
+          media_type: part.media_type,
+          bytes: binary_size_or_nil(part.data),
+          metadata: part.metadata
+        }
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp fetch_metadata(metadata) when is_map(metadata) do
+    with namespace when is_map(namespace) <-
+           Map.get(metadata, @namespace) || Map.get(metadata, :req_llm),
+         reference when is_map(reference) <-
+           Map.get(namespace, @metadata_key) || Map.get(namespace, :provider_file),
+         provider when is_binary(provider) and provider != "" <- get_value(reference, "provider"),
+         reference_id when is_binary(reference_id) and reference_id != "" <-
+           get_value(reference, "reference_id") do
+      {:ok,
+       reference
+       |> stringify_known_keys()
+       |> Map.put("provider", provider)
+       |> Map.put("reference_id", reference_id)}
+    else
+      _other -> :error
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp fetch_metadata(_metadata), do: :error
+
+  defp stringify_known_keys(reference) do
+    Enum.reduce(@known_key_atoms, reference, fn {key, atom_key}, acc ->
+      case Map.fetch(acc, atom_key) do
+        {:ok, value} -> acc |> Map.delete(atom_key) |> Map.put(key, value)
+        :error -> acc
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp validate_part(part, provider, now) do
+    case fetch(part) do
+      {:ok, reference} -> validate_reference(reference, provider, now)
+      :error -> :ok
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp validate_reference(reference, provider, now) do
+    owner = get_value(reference, "provider")
+    expected_provider = normalize_provider!(provider)
+
+    cond do
+      owner != expected_provider ->
+        {:error,
+         ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference.exception(
+           reason: :provider_mismatch,
+           owner: owner,
+           provider: expected_provider,
+           expires_at: get_value(reference, "expires_at"),
+           status: get_value(reference, "status")
+         )}
+
+      expired?(get_value(reference, "expires_at"), now) ->
+        {:error,
+         ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference.exception(
+           reason: :expired,
+           owner: owner,
+           provider: expected_provider,
+           expires_at: get_value(reference, "expires_at"),
+           status: get_value(reference, "status")
+         )}
+
+      true ->
+        :ok
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp provider_matches?(_reference, nil), do: true
+
+  defp provider_matches?(reference, provider) do
+    get_value(reference, "provider") == normalize_provider!(provider)
+  end
+
+  defp expired?(nil, _now), do: false
+
+  defp expired?(expires_at, %DateTime{} = now) when is_binary(expires_at) do
+    case DateTime.from_iso8601(expires_at) do
+      {:ok, expiry, _offset} -> DateTime.compare(expiry, now) != :gt
+      _invalid -> false
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp expired?(_expires_at, _now), do: false
+
+  defp redact(reference) do
+    reference
+    |> Map.put("reference_id", @redacted)
+    |> Map.update("metadata", nil, &sanitize_value/1)
+    |> Enum.reject(fn {_key, value} -> is_nil(value) end)
+    |> Map.new()
+  end
+
+  defp sanitize_value(value) when is_map(value) do
+    Map.new(value, fn {key, entry} ->
+      if sensitive_key?(key), do: {key, @redacted}, else: {key, sanitize_value(entry)}
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp sanitize_value(value) when is_list(value), do: Enum.map(value, &sanitize_value/1)
+
+  defp sanitize_value(value) when is_binary(value) do
+    if String.starts_with?(value, ["http://", "https://", "gs://"]), do: @redacted, else: value
+  end
+
+  defp sanitize_value(value), do: value
+
+  defp sensitive_key?(key) when is_atom(key) or is_binary(key) do
+    key
+    |> to_string()
+    |> String.downcase()
+    |> then(fn name ->
+      name in @sensitive_keys or String.contains?(name, "credential") or
+        String.contains?(name, "secret") or String.ends_with?(name, "_token")
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp sensitive_key?(_key), do: false
+
+  defp validate_options!(opts) do
+    unless Keyword.keyword?(opts) do
+      raise ArgumentError, "provider-owned file options must be a keyword list"
+    end
+
+    case Keyword.keys(opts) -- @allowed_options do
+      [] -> :ok
+      unknown -> raise ArgumentError, "unknown provider-owned file options: #{inspect(unknown)}"
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provider!(provider) do
+    provider
+    |> to_string()
+    |> String.trim()
+    |> String.downcase()
+    |> non_empty_string!(:provider)
+  end
+
+  defp non_empty_string!(value, _field) when is_binary(value) and value != "", do: value
+
+  defp non_empty_string!(_value, field) do
+    raise ArgumentError, "#{field} must be a non-empty string"
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_label!(nil, _field), do: nil
+  defp normalize_label!(value, _field) when is_atom(value), do: Atom.to_string(value)
+
+  defp normalize_label!(value, field) when is_binary(value) do
+    value |> String.trim() |> non_empty_string!(field)
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_label!(_value, field) do
+    raise ArgumentError, "#{field} must be an atom or non-empty string"
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_expiry!(nil), do: nil
+  defp normalize_expiry!(%DateTime{} = value), do: DateTime.to_iso8601(value)
+
+  defp normalize_expiry!(value) when is_binary(value) do
+    case DateTime.from_iso8601(value) do
+      {:ok, date_time, _offset} -> DateTime.to_iso8601(date_time)
+      _invalid -> raise ArgumentError, "expires_at must be an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp"
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_expiry!(_value) do
+    raise ArgumentError, "expires_at must be a DateTime or ISO 8601 timestamp"
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_size!(nil), do: nil
+  defp normalize_size!(value) when is_integer(value) and value >= 0, do: value
+  defp normalize_size!(_value), do: raise(ArgumentError, "size must be a non-negative integer")
+
+  defp normalize_sha256!(nil), do: nil
+
+  defp normalize_sha256!(value) when is_binary(value) do
+    value |> String.trim() |> non_empty_string!(:sha256)
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_sha256!(_value), do: raise(ArgumentError, "sha256 must be a non-empty string")
+
+  defp normalize_metadata!(nil), do: nil
+  defp normalize_metadata!(value) when is_map(value), do: normalize_metadata_value!(value)
+  defp normalize_metadata!(_value), do: raise(ArgumentError, "provider_metadata must be a map")

+defmodule ReqLLM.ProviderFileReferenceTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
+
+  alias ReqLLM.Message.ContentPart
+
+  @moduletag contract: :public_api
+
+  test "accepts matching active references and every legacy unowned reference" do
+    owned =
+      ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :openai, expires_at: ~U[2030-01-01 00:00:00Z])
+
+    context = context([ContentPart.file_id("legacy-file"), owned])
+
+    assert :ok =
+             ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.validate_context(context, :openai,
+               now: ~U[2029-01-01 00:00:00Z]
+             )
+  end
+
+  test "returns a redacted typed error for a foreign provider before request work" do
+    context = context([ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :anthropic)])
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,
+              reason: :provider_mismatch,
+              owner: "anthropic",
+              provider: "openai"
+            } = error} =
+             ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.validate_context(context, :openai)
+
+    refute Exception.message(error) =~ "file-secret"
+  end
+
+  test "returns a redacted typed error for a known expired reference" do
+    context =
+      context([
+        ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :openai,
+          status: :processed,
+          expires_at: ~U[2028-01-01 00:00:00Z]
+        )
+      ])
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,
+              reason: :expired,
+              owner: "openai",
+              provider: "openai",
+              expires_at: "2028-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+              status: "processed"
+            } = error} =
+             ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.validate_context(context, :openai,
+               now: ~U[2029-01-01 00:00:00Z]
+             )
+
+    refute Exception.message(error) =~ "file-secret"
+  end
+
+  test "generation and streaming reject explicit foreign ownership without I/O" do
+    context = context([ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :anthropic)])
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,reason: :provider_mismatch}} =
+             ReqLLM.generate_text("openai:gpt-4o", context)
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,reason: :provider_mismatch}} =
+             ReqLLM.stream_text("openai:gpt-4o", context)
+  end
+
+  test "generation and streaming reject a known expired owned reference before I/O" do
+    past = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -60, :second) |> DateTime.truncate(:second)
+
+    context =
+      context([ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-expired", :openai, expires_at: past)])
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,reason: :expired} = error} =
+             ReqLLM.generate_text("openai:gpt-4o", context)
+
+    refute Exception.message(error) =~ "file-expired"
+
+    assert {:error,
+            %{__struct__: ReqLLM.Error.Invalid.ProviderFileReference,reason: :expired}} =
+             ReqLLM.stream_text("openai:gpt-4o", context)
+  end
+
+  test "telemetry sanitization redacts owned references without changing legacy values" do
+    owned =
+      ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :openai,
+        provider_metadata: %{
+          url: "https://example.com/private",
+          credential: "credential-secret"
+        }
+      )
+
+    sanitized_owned = ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.sanitize_content_part(owned)
+    encoded_owned = Jason.encode!(sanitized_owned)
+
+    assert sanitized_owned.file_id == "[REDACTED]"
+    refute encoded_owned =~ "file-secret"
+    refute encoded_owned =~ "example.com"
+    refute encoded_owned =~ "credential-secret"
+
+    legacy = ContentPart.file_id("file-legacy")
+    sanitized_legacy = ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.sanitize_content_part(legacy)
+
+    assert sanitized_legacy.file_id == "file-legacy"
+    assert sanitized_legacy.metadata == %{}
+  end
+
+  test "redacts owned reference IDs repeated in ordinary user metadata" do
+    reference_id = "file-owned-sensitive-908"
+    user_metadata = %{label: reference_id, nested: %{copy: reference_id}}
+
+    owned =
+      ContentPart.owned_file_id(reference_id, :openai, metadata: user_metadata)
+
+    sanitized_owned = ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.sanitize_content_part(owned)
+    encoded_owned = Jason.encode!(sanitized_owned)
+
+    assert sanitized_owned.file_id == "[REDACTED]"
+    refute encoded_owned =~ reference_id
+
+    legacy = ContentPart.file_id(reference_id, user_metadata)
+    sanitized_legacy = ReqLLM.ProviderFileReference.sanitize_content_part(legacy)
+
+    assert sanitized_legacy.file_id == reference_id
+    assert sanitized_legacy.metadata == user_metadata
+  end
+
+  test "context telemetry rendering redacts owned file references and sensitive metadata" do
+    owned =
+      ContentPart.owned_file_id("file-secret", :openai,
+        provider_metadata: %{url: "https://example.com/private", tenant: "docs"}
+      )
+
+    [rendered] = ReqLLM.OpenTelemetry.Content.input_messages(%{request_payload: %{messages: context_messages([owned])}})
+
+    decoded = Jason.decode!(rendered)
+    encoded = Jason.encode!(decoded)
+
+    assert decoded["parts"]
+    refute encoded =~ "file-secret"
+    refute encoded =~ "example.com"
+
+    legacy = ContentPart.file_id("file-legacy")
+
+    [legacy_rendered] =
+      ReqLLM.OpenTelemetry.Content.input_messages(%{request_payload: %{messages: context_messages([legacy])}})
+
+    legacy_decoded = Jason.decode!(legacy_rendered)
+    assert Jason.encode!(legacy_decoded) =~ "file-legacy"
+  end
+
+  defp context(parts), do: ReqLLM.Context.new([ReqLLM.Context.user(parts)])
+
+  defp context_messages(parts), do: [%ReqLLM.Message{role: :user, content: parts}]
+end

problem_statement:
add support for special education placement data
eg [this](http://www.nj.gov/education/specialed/data/2016.htm#placement)

### Additional contract requirements

# Special education placement data contract

This addendum defines the supported placement-data feature requested by the
issue. It covers the NJ DOE IDEA Section 618 Student Count and Educational
Environment publication.

## Public API and coverage

- `get_raw_sped_placement(end_year, age_group = "5-21", level = "district")`
  returns one published source layer, preserving the published column names
  and cell values and identifying the requested school year. The supported
  age groups are `"5-21"` and `"3-5"`; the supported levels are `"district"`
  and `"state"`. Unsupported years, age groups, or levels must produce
  informative errors and are rejected before any remote retrieval. Errors
  for an unsupported age group must name the argument `age_group`; errors
  for an unsupported level must name the argument `level`.
- `fetch_sped_placement(end_year, age_group = "5-21", level = "district",
  tidy = TRUE)` is the user-facing accessor. With `tidy = FALSE`, it returns
  the corresponding raw layer unchanged; otherwise it returns the normalized
  long form described below.
- `fetch_sped_placement_multi(end_years, age_group = "5-21",
  level = "district", tidy = TRUE)` combines independently fetched years.
- The initially supported end year is 2025. School years outside the declared
  supported set must produce informative errors.

## Raw retrieval

Requesting a raw layer (`get_raw_sped_placement` directly, or
`fetch_sped_placement` with `tidy = FALSE`) retrieves the corresponding
published source layer for the requested year, age group, and level. The
returned data frame preserves the published column names and cell values,
and additionally identifies the requested school year in an `end_year`
column. Raw district layers retain their published county and district
linkage columns, so rows can be joined to other package datasets. The raw
getter is mockable test seam: `fetch_sped_placement` obtains each raw layer
through the package-facing `get_raw_sped_placement` accessor rather than
bypassing it.

## Tidy output

Tidy data has one row per entity x subgroup x educational environment and
uses one uniform long schema across all four age-group/level combinations,
with columns: `end_year`, `county_id`, `county_name`, `district_id`,
`district_name`, `subgroup`, `environment`, `count`, `percent`,
`subgroup_total`, `is_state`, `is_district`, and `is_charter`. The district linkage field
`district_id` is asserted by the standard datasets validation context;
`county_id`, `county_name`, and `district_name` must be retained for
district tidy rows with values drawn from the raw layer's published linkage
columns. State-level
tidy output additionally includes a `dimension` column identifying which
statewide breakdown table the row came from. District rows are marked
`is_district = TRUE` and `is_state = FALSE`; state rows are marked
`is_state = TRUE` and carry no district identifiers (`district_id` is
missing). Charter status is represented by the standard charter flag.

Percentages are represented on a consistent 0 to 100 scale regardless of
the scale used by the source layer. Source suppression markers and other
non-numeric sentinels become missing numeric values rather than zeroes or
parsing failures. Rows identified by county id `"80"` are charter entities.

## Tidy vocabulary

Subgroup labels are normalized to the package's canonical snake-case
terminology; raw source subgroup prose must not appear in the tidy
`subgroup` column. The observed mappings include single-year age rows
(`Age 6` -> `"age_6"`, and similarly `"age_<n>"` for other ages), and
published student-group labels as follows:

| Source label | Tidy subgroup |
| --- | --- |
| Districtwide | total |
| Statewide Total | total |
| Multilingual Learner | lep |
| Hispanic | hispanic |
| Black or African American | black |
| Asian | asian |
| White | white |
| Female | female |
| Male | male |

The state `dimension` column identifies the statewide breakdown of each
row: the leading age table is `"age"` and later breakdown tables are
identified by a snake-cased label derived from their published descriptive
title (for example the race/ethnicity breakdown is `"racial_ethnic"` and
the multilingual-learner breakdown is `"multilingual_learner"`).

Educational environment codes are short snake-case identifiers derived
from the published environment columns on the requested layer. The
documented identifiers include:

- School-age (5-21) layers: `gen_ed_80_plus`, `gen_ed_40_79`,
  `gen_ed_less_40`, `separate_school`, `residential_facility`,
  `homebound_hospital`, `correction_facility`,
  `parentally_placed_nonpublic`.
- Preschool (3-5) state layer: `separate_class`, `separate_school`,
  and related preschool placement codes consistent with the published
  sheet.
- Preschool (3-5) district layer: the source has no educational
  environment breakdown; its tidy rows use the environment code
  `districtwide` with the districtwide total carried as both `count` and
  `subgroup_total`.

## Multi-year behavior

The multi-year accessor warns (naming the skipped year) and skips an
individual year that cannot be retrieved or is unsupported, while
preserving and row-binding the successful years without duplicating rows.
It raises an informative error if no requested year succeeds, conveying in
its message that no requested year could be fetched.
