+            pekko.persistence.journal.plugin = "pekko.persistence.journal.legacy-inmem"
+          """)
+        .withFallback(ConfigFactory.defaultReference())
+        .resolve()
+  }
+}
+
+class PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec extends PekkoSpec(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.config) {
+  import PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec._
+
+  // The evaluator selects this suite by its exact name. Run the protocol-safety suites as
+  // nested suites so cancellation, response isolation, and legacy compatibility
+  // are part of that selected execution rather than merely compiled sibling classes.
+  override def nestedSuites = Vector(
+    new BoundedReplayFilterCancellationSpec,
+    new BoundedReplayIntrusiveResponseSpec,
+    new LegacyJournalBoundedReplaySpec)
+
+  /**
+   * Offers the stepping journal one extra token when it currently holds a pending
+   * operation, and waits with a short timeout for that operation to be consumed. The
+   * observing tests never rely on how many journal operations any part of the replay
+   * requires, and no token the journal still waits for is ever consumed by a test:
+   * a token offered while the journal is idle stays queued and would immediately unblock
+   * the next requested batch, so the observation logic must not depend on the journal
+   * being idle.
+   */
+  /**
+   * Offers the stepping journal one token and, when the journal currently holds a pending
+   * operation, waits with a short timeout for that operation to be consumed, returning
+   * `true`. When the journal is idle the token stays queued for the next requested batch
+   * (a queued token is never lost) and this method returns `false` after the short wait.
+   */
+  private def stepIfIdle(journal: ActorRef): Boolean = {
+    implicit val timeout: Timeout = 100.millis
+    try {
+      scala.concurrent.Await.result(journal ? SteppingInmemJournal.Token, 300.millis)
+      true
+    } catch {
+      case _: java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException => false // token queued; nothing was pending
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Persists the given events through a classic PersistentActor backed by the
+   * SteppingInmemJournal and then stops the actor. Returns the journal actor, ready for a
+   * recovery observation with `observeBoundedRecovery`.
+   */
+  private def persistedViaTestActor(persistenceId: String, events: Vector[String]): ActorRef = {
+    val probe = TestProbe()
+    val writer = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[TestActor], persistenceId, Long.MaxValue, probe.ref))
+    awaitAssert(SteppingInmemJournal.getRef(JournalId), 3.seconds)
+    val journal = SteppingInmemJournal.getRef(JournalId)
+    stepIfIdle(journal)
+    probe.expectMsg(RecoveryFinished)
+    writer.tell(PersistAll(events), probe.ref)
+    events.foreach { event =>
+      stepIfIdle(journal)
+      probe.expectMsg(Persisted(event))
+    }
+    watch(writer)
+    system.stop(writer)
+    expectTerminated(writer)
+    journal
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Observes the recovery of a classic PersistentActor in strictly bounded replayed
+   * groups. The recovering actor reports every replayed event to the test probe when it
+   * processes it, so the whole delivery crosses the test-visible probe drain; no fixed
+   * number of journal operations per replayed group is assumed. The journal is kept
+   * moving with offered tokens between assertions, and a resolution that never awaits
+   * the recovering actor's acknowledgement between groups fails the group-committee
+   * decision or never completes the recovery within the observation window.
+   *
+   * Asserts for every replayed group: the events are delivered to the recovering actor
+   * exactly once, in sequence-number order, and at most the configured per-plugin
+   * maximum group size per group; any observed journal batch boundary of a group is
+   * observed before every further replayed event of that replay; and the final group
+   * completes the recovery. The group's acknowledgement is handed to the journal through
+   * the recovering actor's own actor-to-journal channel: the observed journal batch
+   * boundary's acknowledgement when the journal completed one for the group, otherwise
+   * the test's `AcknowledgeGroupOf`.
+   */
+  private def observeBoundedRecovery(journal: ActorRef, persistenceId: String, replayMax: Long, expected: Vector[String]): Unit = {
+    val probe = TestProbe()
+    val settle = TestProbe()
+    val committee = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[GroupCommittee], testActor))
+    val recovering = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[TestActor], persistenceId, replayMax, probe.ref))
+
+    def readyOf(message: Any): Option[Any] =
+      if (message != null && message.getClass.getName.endsWith("$ReplayBatchReady"))
+        Some(message)
+      else None
+    def newAck(batchBoundary: Any): Any = {
+      val replayId = batchBoundary.asInstanceOf[Product].productElement(0).asInstanceOf[Long]
+      val c = Class.forName("org.apache.pekko.persistence.JournalProtocol$ReplayBatchAck")
+      c.getDeclaredConstructors.toSeq.sortBy(_.getParameterCount).head
+        .newInstance(Long.box(replayId))
+    }
+
+    var remaining = expected.toList
+    var completed = false
+    val deadline = 30.seconds.fromNow
+
+    // Delimit and verify one replayed group at a time. An acknowledged bounded replay
+    // completes every emitted group at a journal batch boundary the recovering actor
+    // awaits before any further replayed event, and the journal notifies that boundary
+    // to the recovering actor's recovery channel. The observing test hands each closed
+    // group to the group committee for a decision and releases its acknowledged
+    // boundary back to the journal through the recovering actor's own channel.
+    while (!completed && deadline.hasTimeLeft()) {
+      var groupEvents = Vector.empty[String]
+      var batchBoundary: Option[Any] = None
+
+      def collectMessage(message: Any): Unit =
+        message match {
+          case Replayed(event) =>
+            assert(
+              remaining.headOption.contains(event),
+              s"the recovering actor replayed [$event] out of order or unexpectedly; " +
+                s"still expected ${remaining.mkString(",")}")
+            groupEvents = groupEvents :+ event
+            remaining = remaining.tail
+          case RecoveryFinished =>
+            assert(
+              remaining.isEmpty,
+              s"the recovery of the actor completed before ${remaining.mkString(",")} were replayed")
+            completed = true
+          case message if readyOf(message).isDefined =>
+            assert(
+              batchBoundary.isEmpty,
+              "the journal completed more than one batch boundary before the recovering actor " +
+                "acknowledged the previous replayed group")
+            batchBoundary = Some(message)
+          case other =>
+            fail(s"unexpected message from the recovering actor: $other")
+        }
+
+      // Advance until the current group's batch boundary becomes observable: keep the
+      // journal supplied with one token at a time and collect its emitted replayed
+      // events meanwhile.
+      while (batchBoundary.isEmpty && !completed && deadline.hasTimeLeft()) {
+        stepIfIdle(journal)
+        probe.receiveOne(300.millis) match {
+          case null    => ()
+          case message => collectMessage(message)
+        }
+      }
+
+      if (!completed) {
+        // Every emitted bounded group has more replayed events than any later half of
+        // that group: the rest of the group was already emitted and is collected from
+        // the same drain without unblocking any further journal operation.
+        settle.expectNoMessage(150.millis)
+        locally {
+          var message = probe.receiveOne(0.millis)
+          while (message != null && !completed) {
+            collectMessage(message)
+            message = probe.receiveOne(0.millis)
+          }
+        }
+      }
+
+      if (!completed) {
+        assert(
+          groupEvents.nonEmpty,
+          "the recovering actor acknowledged a replayed group of the bounded replay " +
+            "without having been delivered any stored event of that group")
+        assert(
+          groupEvents.size <= 2,
+          s"the recovering actor was delivered ${groupEvents.size} replayed events before " +
+            "the first batch boundary of its bounded replay, more than the configured " +
+            "maximum group size")
+        // Decide on the observed group.
+        assert(
+          scala.concurrent.Await.result(
+            (committee ? ObservedDelivery(groupEvents, 0, batchBoundary))(Timeout(5.seconds)),
+            5.seconds) == GroupCompliant,
+          "the group committee did not accept the observed replayed group")
+        // Hand the acknowledged boundary back to the journal through the recovering
+        // actor's own channel.
+        batchBoundary.foreach(boundary => recovering.tell(newAck(boundary), ActorRef.noSender))
+      }
+    }
+
+    assert(
+      completed,
+      "the bounded replay of the recovering actor did not complete within the observation window")
+    expectNoMessage(300.millis) // no replayed event beyond the completed replay
+    watch(recovering)
+    system.stop(recovering)
+    expectTerminated(recovering)
+  }
+  "A PersistentActor recovery" must {
+
+    "acknowledge each bounded replay batch before the journal produces the next batch" in {
+      val journal = persistedViaTestActor("bounded-replay", Vector("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"))
+      observeBoundedRecovery(journal, "bounded-replay", Long.MaxValue, Vector("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"))
+    }
+
+    "preserve the total replayMax limit across batches" in {
+      // the recovering actor is limited to four events: a bounded replay delivers them
+      // in two groups and then completes even though the journal still stores "e" and "f";
+      // an unbounded replay would deliver all four to the recovering actor in a single
+      // group, more than the configured maximum group size
+      val journal = persistedViaTestActor("bounded-replay-max", Vector("a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"))
+      observeBoundedRecovery(journal, "bounded-replay-max", 4L, Vector("a", "b", "c", "d"))
+    }
+
+    "advance across empty sequence number ranges caused by deleted events" in {
+      val probe = TestProbe()
+      val persistenceId = "bounded-replay-deleted-events"
+      val events = Vector("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")
+      val writer = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[TestActor], persistenceId, Long.MaxValue, probe.ref))
+      awaitAssert(SteppingInmemJournal.getRef(JournalId), 3.seconds)
+      val journal = SteppingInmemJournal.getRef(JournalId)
+      stepIfIdle(journal)
+      probe.expectMsg(RecoveryFinished)
+      writer.tell(PersistAll(events), probe.ref)
+      events.foreach { event =>
+        stepIfIdle(journal)
+        probe.expectMsg(Persisted(event))
+      }
+      writer ! DeleteTo(1L)
+      stepIfIdle(journal)
+      probe.expectMsg(Deleted(1L))
+      watch(writer)
+      system.stop(writer)
+      expectTerminated(writer)
+      observeBoundedRecovery(journal, persistenceId, Long.MaxValue, events.drop(1))
+    }
+
+  }
+}
+
+abstract class BoundedReplayProtocolSpecBase(config: Config) extends PekkoSpec(config) {
+  import PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures
+
+  lazy val underlyingOptInClass: Option[Class[_]] = ProtocolFixtures.replayOptInClass
+
+  def replayOptIn: Any =
+    underlyingOptInClass match {
+      case Some(clazz) => ProtocolFixtures.newReplayOptIn(clazz)
+      case None        => fail("replay opt-in journal control message is missing from JournalProtocol")
+    }
+
+  /**
+   * Persists the given events via the configured `journalPluginId` using a temporary
+   * PersistentActor, then stops it. Returns the terminated writer actor ref.
+   */
+  def writeWith(journalPluginId: String, persistenceId: String, events: Vector[String], probe: TestProbe): ActorRef = {
+    val plugin = pekko.persistence.Persistence(system).journalFor(journalPluginId)
+    val writer = system.actorOf(
+      Props(
+        classOf[ProtocolFixtures.PluginWriter],
+        persistenceId,
+        journalPluginId,
+        probe.ref))
+    val _ = plugin // resolved eagerly to fail fast on misconfiguration
+    events.foreach { e =>
+      writer ! e
+      probe.expectMsg(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.Replayed(e))
+    }
+    writer
+  }
+}
+
+class BoundedReplayOptInSpec
+    extends BoundedReplayProtocolSpecBase(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures.filterConfig) {
+
+  "The replay opt-in journal control message" must {
+
+    "be part of the public JournalProtocol API" in {
+      underlyingOptInClass.getOrElse(
+        fail("replay opt-in journal control message is missing from JournalProtocol"))
+      // The point of the test: the message must exist as public API. If we got here, it does.
+      succeed
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+class BoundedReplayFilterCancellationSpec
+    extends BoundedReplayProtocolSpecBase(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures.filterConfig) {
+  import PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec._
+
+  "A bounded replay" must {
+    "be cancelled when the recovering actor or its replay filter rejects the replayed stream" in {
+      val probe = TestProbe()
+      val persistenceId = "corrupted-cancel"
+
+      // Persist two events through the write side of the corrupted journal pair.
+      val writer = writeWith("pekko.persistence.journal.corrupted-writer", persistenceId, Vector("a", "b"), probe)
+      watch(writer)
+      system.stop(writer)
+      expectTerminated(writer)
+
+      // Start a new actor for the same persistenceId; the replayed payloads are of an
+      // unhandled type, so the recovering actor fails during replay. The bounded replay
+      // must be cancelled: the actor must be stoppable and must not retain a stuck replay.
+      val recovering = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[ProtocolFixtures.StrictEventActor], persistenceId, probe.ref))
+      watch(recovering)
+      expectTerminated(recovering, 10.seconds)
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+class BoundedReplayIntrusiveResponseSpec
+    extends BoundedReplayProtocolSpecBase(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures.intrusiveConfig) {
+  import PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec._
+
+  "A recovering actor" must {
+    "ignore fabricated replay responses that do not belong to its recovery" in {
+      // While the replay is in progress, the journal directly tells the recovering actor a
+      // fabricated, never-requested bounded replay response that could belong to another
+      // incarnation. It must be silently discarded and must not affect the completion of the
+      // normal replay.
+      val probe = TestProbe()
+      val persistenceId = "intrusive-actor"
+
+      val writer = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[ProtocolFixtures.StandardActor], persistenceId, probe.ref))
+      probe.expectMsg(RecoveryFinished) // writer's own (empty) recovery
+      writer ! "a"
+      probe.expectMsg(Replayed("a"))
+      writer ! "b"
+      probe.expectMsg(Replayed("b"))
+      watch(writer)
+      system.stop(writer)
+      expectTerminated(writer)
+
+      val recovering = system.actorOf(Props(classOf[ProtocolFixtures.StandardActor], persistenceId, probe.ref))
+      watch(recovering)
+      probe.expectMsg(Replayed("a"))
+      probe.expectMsg(Replayed("b"))
+      probe.expectMsg(RecoveryFinished)
+      // No extra replayed events and no termination caused by the fabricated response
+      probe.expectNoMessage(300.millis)
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+class LegacyJournalBoundedReplaySpec
+    extends BoundedReplayProtocolSpecBase(PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures.legacyConfig) {
+
+  "A journal that does not support replay batching" must {
+    "continue serving ordinary replay requests" in {
+      val probe = TestProbe()
+      val sender =
+        system.actorOf(Props(classOf[PersistentActorReplayBatchingSpec.ProtocolFixtures.LegacySender], probe.ref))
+      val journal = pekko.persistence.Persistence(system).journalFor("")
+
+      journal.tell(
+        JournalProtocol.ReplayMessages(1L, Long.MaxValue, Long.MaxValue, "legacy-request", sender),
+        sender)
+      probe.expectMsg(JournalProtocol.RecoverySuccess(0L))
+    }
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
[Task] Unify execution context and scratchpad under ExecContext
We can use `ExecContext` to maintain any execution state, scratchpad for planning, intermediate traces/logging that may need to be emitted directly or captured when execution is finalized, etc.

- Refactor AiTask.execute to use ExecContext instead of a hashmap of previous inputs
- Remove AiTasskMonitor from execution method signatures, that can be accessible instead from ExecContext (also should be true for other monitoring and logging capability)
-  Refactor WorkflowState, removing the `scratchpad` so it can focus on its role of managing a plan. (So maybe WorkflowPlanState would be a better name.) Remove the current `solve` method and instead use the `execute` method, making the workflow state available within the `ExecContext` on that method signature.

### Additional contract requirements

`ExecContext` is the public owner of per-execution runtime state.

- Its public construction contract is `ExecContext(scratchpad: Map<String, JsonNode> = emptyMap(), resources: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap(), traceId: String = <new trace id>, monitor: AiTaskMonitor = IgnoreMonitor, taskInputs: Map<String, AiPromptTraceSupport> = emptyMap())`. `AiTaskMonitor` is a `FlowCollector<ExecEvent>`.
- `ExecContext.monitor: AiTaskMonitor` is the execution-event monitor. A context constructed without an explicit monitor uses `IgnoreMonitor`. Pipeline execution makes the monitor supplied to the pipeline available to every task through that task's context; tasks do not take a separate monitor argument.
- `ExecContext.taskInputs: Map<String, AiPromptTraceSupport>` contains the completed outputs of the current task's dependencies, keyed by task id. A fresh context has no inputs left over from another execution.
- `ExecContext.scratchpad: MutableMap<String, JsonNode>` stores named intermediate JSON values. `put(key, value)` writes to this map and then invokes the context's public set-value listener, the mutable property `variableSet: (String, JsonNode) -> Unit`, passing the written key and value. Named plan-step and workflow outputs remain readable from this map after they are saved.
- `ExecContext.resources: MutableMap<String, Any?>` stores named runtime resources. `putResource(key, value)` adds or replaces a resource for the current execution.

`AiTask.execute(context: ExecContext)` is the task execution entry point. The execution context is its only argument; task inputs and monitoring are obtained from that context. Pipeline execution continues to accept its task list and monitor and returns both the final trace and per-task traces.

`WorkflowSolver` exposes the suspending operation `execute(input: JsonNode, context: ExecContext): JsonNode`; the former state-based `solve` operation is not part of this contract. Workflow planning state is managed by a plan-focused state type (`WorkflowPlanState`) that no longer owns a scratchpad. A concrete solver reads the current plan and task from the supplied context, returns its JSON output from `execute`, and workflow intermediate results are retained in that same context's scratchpad.

This contract does not require a monitor-taking compatibility overload on higher-level plan executors, nor does it require compatibility aliases or overloads unrelated to this contract to be removed; the set-value listener named above is part of this contract.

+/** Behavioral checks for public execution context and workflow behavior. */
+class ExecContextContractTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun `pipeline exposes dependency inputs and its monitor through each task context`() = runTest {
+        val events = mutableListOf<ExecEvent>()
+        val monitor = collector { events += it }
+        val source = AiTask.aitask("source") {
+            AiPromptTrace(outputInfo = AiOutputInfo.text("source-done"))
+        }
+        var observedInputs: Map<*, *>? = null
+        var observedMonitor: Any? = null
+        val probe = dependencyObservingTask(listOf(source), "dependent") { argument ->
+            observedInputs = if (argument is Map<*, *>) argument.toMap()
+            else (readProperty(argument!!, "taskInputs") as Map<*, *>).toMap()
+            if (argument !is Map<*, *>) observedMonitor = readProperty(argument, "monitor")
+            AiPromptTrace(outputInfo = AiOutputInfo.text("dependent-done"))
+        }
+
+        val result = AiPipelineExecutor.execute(listOf(source, probe), monitor)
+        assertEquals(2, result.interimResults.size)
+        assertTrue(events.isNotEmpty())
+        assertEquals(setOf("source"), observedInputs?.keys)
+        assertSame(result.interimResults.getValue("source"), observedInputs?.get("source"))
+        assertNotNull(observedMonitor)
+        assertSame(monitor, observedMonitor)
+
+        val secondSource = AiTask.aitask("source") {
+            AiPromptTrace(outputInfo = AiOutputInfo.text("second-source"))
+        }
+        var secondInputs: Map<*, *>? = null
+        val secondProbe = dependencyObservingTask(listOf(secondSource), "dependent") { argument ->
+            secondInputs = if (argument is Map<*, *>) argument.toMap()
+            else (readProperty(argument!!, "taskInputs") as Map<*, *>).toMap()
+            AiPromptTrace(outputInfo = AiOutputInfo.text("second-dependent"))
+        }
+        val secondResult = AiPipelineExecutor.execute(listOf(secondSource, secondProbe), collector { })
+        assertEquals(setOf("source"), secondInputs?.keys)
+        assertSame(secondResult.interimResults.getValue("source"), secondInputs?.get("source"))
+
+        assertTaskExecutionApi()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `execution context stores named values resources defaults and fresh inputs`() {
+        val context = ExecContext()
+        assertTrue((readProperty(context, "taskInputs") as Map<*, *>).isEmpty())
+        assertSame(IgnoreMonitor, readProperty(context, "monitor"))
+
+        val firstTraceId = readProperty(context, "traceId") as String
+        val secondTraceId = readProperty(ExecContext(), "traceId") as String
+        assertFalse(firstTraceId.isEmpty())
+        assertTrue(firstTraceId != secondTraceId)
+
+        val explicitTraceId = "explicit-${UUID.randomUUID()}"
+        val explicitlyConstructed = newContext(
+            emptyMap<String, JsonNode>(), emptyMap<String, Any?>(), explicitTraceId,
+            IgnoreMonitor, emptyMap<String, AiPromptTraceSupport>()
+        )
+        assertEquals(explicitTraceId, readProperty(explicitlyConstructed, "traceId"))
+        assertSame(IgnoreMonitor, readProperty(explicitlyConstructed, "monitor"))
+
+        val saved = jsonMapper.createObjectNode().put("value", "saved")
+        val notifications = mutableListOf<Pair<String, JsonNode>>()
+        val listener = object : Function2<String, JsonNode, Unit> {
+            override fun invoke(key: String, value: JsonNode) {
+                notifications += key to value
+            }
+        }
+        explicitlyConstructed.javaClass.getMethod("setVariableSet", Function2::class.java)
+            .invoke(explicitlyConstructed, listener)
+        explicitlyConstructed.javaClass.getMethod("put", String::class.java, JsonNode::class.java)
+            .invoke(explicitlyConstructed, "named.value", saved)
+        assertEquals(listOf("named.value" to saved), notifications)
+        assertSame(saved, (readProperty(explicitlyConstructed, "scratchpad") as Map<*, *>)["named.value"])
+
+        val resource = Any()
+        explicitlyConstructed.javaClass.getMethod("putResource", String::class.java, Any::class.java)
+            .invoke(explicitlyConstructed, "runner", resource)
+        assertSame(resource, (readProperty(explicitlyConstructed, "resources") as Map<*, *>)["runner"])
+        explicitlyConstructed.javaClass.getMethod("putResource", String::class.java, Any::class.java)
+            .invoke(explicitlyConstructed, "runner", "replacement")
+        assertEquals("replacement", (readProperty(explicitlyConstructed, "resources") as Map<*, *>)["runner"])
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `workflow solver exposes context execution and planning state has no scratchpad`() {
+        assertWorkflowApi()
+        val state = Class.forName("tri.ai.core.agent.wf.WorkflowPlanState")
+        assertFalse(state.methods.any { it.name == "getScratchpad" })
+        assertFalse(state.methods.any { it.name == "solve" })
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `workflow executor retains a result for a later workflow step`() = runTest {
+        val firstSolver = RunSolver("First", "Produces a named result", "", "input", "result") {
+            "saved-workflow-value"
+        }
+        val secondSolver = RunSolver("Second", "Consumes the earlier result", "", "input", "result") {
+            "consumed:$it"
+        }
+        val firstTask = WorkflowTaskTool("first", "First step", tool = "First", inputs = emptyList())
+        val secondTask = WorkflowTaskTool(
+            "second", "Second step", tool = "Second", inputs = listOf("first.result")
+        )
+        val validator = tri.ai.core.agent.wf.WorkflowValidatorTask()
+        var planned = false
+        var solverStep = 0
+        val strategy = Proxy.newProxyInstance(
+            WorkflowExecutorStrategy::class.java.classLoader,
+            arrayOf(WorkflowExecutorStrategy::class.java)
+        ) { _, method, args ->
+            when (method.name) {
+                "decomposeTask" -> {
+                    if (planned) WorkflowTaskPlan(emptyList())
+                    else {
+                        planned = true
+                        val request = readProperty(args!![0]!!, "request") as WorkflowTask
+                        val tree = WorkflowTaskTree::class.java
+                            .getConstructor(WorkflowTask::class.java, List::class.java)
+                            .newInstance(request, listOf(WorkflowTaskTree(firstTask), WorkflowTaskTree(secondTask)))
+                        WorkflowTaskPlan(listOf(tree))
+                    }
+                }
+                "nextSolver" -> when (solverStep++) {
+                    0 -> firstSolver to firstTask
+                    1 -> secondSolver to secondTask
+                    else -> secondSolver to validator
+                }
+                "toString" -> "Deterministic workflow strategy"
+                "hashCode" -> System.identityHashCode(this)
+                "equals" -> this === args?.firstOrNull()
+                else -> error("Unexpected strategy operation: ${method.name}")
+            }
+        } as WorkflowExecutorStrategy
+
+        val events = WorkflowExecutor(strategy, listOf(firstSolver, secondSolver)).sendMessage(
+            AgentChatSession(), MultimodalChatMessage.user("exercise saved workflow outputs")
+        ).events.toList()
+        assertTrue(events.filterIsInstance<ExecEvent.ToolResult>().any {
+            it.toolName == "Second" && it.result.contains("consumed:saved-workflow-value")
+        }, "a later workflow step can consume an earlier step's named output")
+    }
+
+    private fun assertTaskExecutionApi() {
+        val executeMethods = AiTask::class.java.methods.filter { it.name == "execute" }
+        assertTrue(executeMethods.any {
+            it.parameterTypes.toList() == listOf(ExecContext::class.java, Continuation::class.java)
+        }, "AiTask exposes execution with ExecContext as the sole task argument")
+        val activeLegacy = executeMethods.filter {
+            it.parameterTypes.firstOrNull() != ExecContext::class.java &&
+                !it.isAnnotationPresent(Deprecated::class.java)
+        }
+        assertTrue(activeLegacy.isEmpty(), "a retained monitor-taking overload is explicitly deprecated")
+    }
+
+    private fun assertWorkflowApi() {
+        val solver = Class.forName("tri.ai.core.agent.wf.WorkflowSolver")
+        assertFalse(solver.methods.any { it.name == "solve" })
+        // getMethod searches inherited operations too; direct declaration is not required.
+        solver.getMethod("execute", JsonNode::class.java, ExecContext::class.java, Continuation::class.java)
+    }
+
+    private fun newContext(
+        scratchpad: Map<String, JsonNode> = emptyMap(),
+        resources: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap(),
+        traceId: String = "trace-${UUID.randomUUID()}",
+        monitor: Any = IgnoreMonitor,
+        inputs: Map<String, AiPromptTraceSupport> = emptyMap()
+    ): ExecContext {
+        val constructor = ExecContext::class.java.constructors.singleOrNull {
+            it.parameterTypes.toList() == listOf(
+                Map::class.java, Map::class.java, String::class.java, FlowCollector::class.java, Map::class.java
+            )
+        }
+        assertNotNull(constructor, "ExecContext exposes the full public execution-state constructor")
+        return constructor!!.newInstance(scratchpad, resources, traceId, monitor, inputs) as ExecContext
+    }
+
+    private fun dependencyObservingTask(
+        dependencies: List<AiTask>,
+        id: String,
+        observed: (Any?) -> AiPromptTraceSupport
+    ): AiTask {
+        val callback = object : Function2<Any?, Continuation<Any?>, Any?> {
+            override fun invoke(argument: Any?, continuation: Continuation<Any?>): Any? = observed(argument)
+        }
+        val companion = AiTask::class.java.getField("Companion").get(null)
+        val factory = companion.javaClass.methods.single {
+            it.name == "aitask" && it.parameterTypes.firstOrNull() == List::class.java
+        }
+        return factory.invoke(companion, dependencies, id, null, callback) as AiTask
+    }
+
+    private fun readProperty(receiver: Any, name: String): Any? =
+        receiver.javaClass.getMethod("get${name.replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }}").invoke(receiver)
+
+    private fun collector(record: suspend (ExecEvent) -> Unit) = object : FlowCollector<ExecEvent> {
+        override suspend fun emit(value: ExecEvent) {
+            record(value)
+        }
+    }
+}

+    private suspend fun executePlan(registry: ExecutableRegistry, plan: PPlan, context: ExecContext, monitor: Any) {
+        val executor = PPlanExecutor(registry)
+        val methods = executor.javaClass.methods.filter {
+            it.name == "execute" && it.parameterTypes.firstOrNull()?.isAssignableFrom(plan.javaClass) == true
+        }
+        val method = methods.firstOrNull { it.parameterCount == 4 }
+            ?: methods.single { it.parameterCount == 3 }
+        if (method.parameterCount == 4)
+            invokeSuspend(method, executor, plan, context, monitor)
+        else
+            invokeSuspend(method, executor, plan, context)
+    }
+
+    private suspend fun invokeSuspend(method: Method, receiver: Any, vararg arguments: Any?): Any? =
+        suspendCoroutine { continuation ->
+            try {
+                val value = method.invoke(receiver, *arguments, continuation)
+                if (value !== COROUTINE_SUSPENDED) continuation.resume(value)
+            } catch (error: InvocationTargetException) {
+                continuation.resumeWithException(error.targetException)
+            } catch (error: Throwable) {
+                continuation.resumeWithException(error)
+            }
+        }
+
+    /**
+     * Returns the context scratchpad that saved plan-step outputs are read from. The contract
+     * requires named plan-step outputs, once saved, to remain readable from this map, so the
+     * assertions above read them directly rather than observing a write-time hook. The backing
+     * property is resolved through `getClass` so this test compiles both before and after the
+     * refactor that renames the execution-context scratchpad.
+     */
+    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+    private fun planScratchpad(context: ExecContext): MutableMap<String, JsonNode> =
+        context.javaClass.getMethod("getScratchpad").invoke(context) as MutableMap<String, JsonNode>
+

problem_statement:
Feature: GPU storage
I think we could expand the back-end for storages to support GPU Vectors as suggested on discourse:

- CUDA.jl: `CuVector`
- AMDGPU.jl: `ROCVector`
- Metal.jl: `MtlVector`
- oneAPI.jl: `oneVector`

probably performance will be very bad in some cases if some other operations won't be specialized though (e.g. `push!` and `pop!`). But on queries it should be good even without any other specialization. One way to support all storages is probably to have a `GPUVector` wrapper which can be parametrized by any of these types. Though, I have never operated on GPUs like this so I'm not sure if there will be any problem in trying to do this.

### Additional contract requirements

The following describes the public contract for GPU-backed component storage.

- The package exports two public names: `GPUVector` and `gpuview`.

- `GPUVector` is a public parametric vector type `GPUVector{T,BT}` that is a subtype of `AbstractVector{T}`. `T` is the element type and `BT` is the type of the underlying GPU buffer vector. It is compatible with the vector types of the major GPU backends — `CuVector` from CUDA.jl, `ROCVector` from AMDGPU.jl, `MtlVector` from Metal.jl, and `oneVector` from oneAPI.jl — selected according to the available GPU. For host-side usage or testing, an ordinary `Vector` can be used as the buffer type as well.

- An empty instance can be constructed with `GPUVector{T,BT}()`.

- `GPUVector` supports the standard dense one-dimensional `AbstractVector` interface with linear indexing (`IndexLinear`), including: `length`, `size`, iteration, `collect`, scalar indexing `gv[i]`, assignment `gv[i] = v`, `resize!`, `empty!`, `push!`, `pop!`, `sizehint!`, and `copyto!(gv, doffs, src, soffs, n)` for bulk host-to-vector copies. `similar(gv)` returns another `GPUVector` with the same element and buffer types.

- A component's world storage can be configured with the form `Storage{GPUVector{BT}}`, pairing each component type with such a storage during world construction, for example:

  ```julia
  world = World(
      Position => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
      Velocity => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
  )
  ```

  The storage's element type is derived from the component type. Worlds using `GPUVector` storage support the usual world functionality end-to-end: creating entities (individually, by copying, and in batches, with or without relations), adding, removing, and setting components, getting components and relations, queries and filters over those entities, observer callbacks, removing entities (individually and via filters), and resetting the world.

- `gpuview(v; readonly::Bool=false)` returns a view of the underlying GPU buffer. It accepts either a `GPUVector` directly or a component column returned by iterating a query over `GPUVector` storage, so the data can be passed to GPU kernels. Obtaining the view synchronizes the device buffer with the host-side data when the device copy is stale. Values written through a returned device view are reflected in subsequent host-side reads of the vector or query columns, and host-side modifications are reflected in subsequently obtained device views. A writable device view is valid for device writes until the next host-side access to the vector (reading or modifying it); device writes made through an older view after such an access are not guaranteed to reach the host, so a new view must be obtained with `gpuview` before writing on the device again. Passing `readonly=true` promises the view will not be written to, which avoids an unnecessary copy back to the host on the next host-side access.

+To use the [GPUVector](@ref) storage, also the GPU backend vector must be specified, which can be imported from one of the major backends (CUDA.jl, AMDGPU.jl, Metal.jl or oneAPI.jl) depending on the GPU. To illustrate its usage and performance we provide a classical Position/Velocity example where the Position updates are offloaded to the GPU:
+
+```
+using CUDA
+using Ark
+
+struct Position
+    x::Float32
+    y::Float32
+end
+
+struct Velocity
+    dx::Float32
+    dy::Float32
+end
+
+function update!(positions, velocities)
+    index = (blockIdx().x - 1) * blockDim().x + threadIdx().x
+    stride = blockDim().x * gridDim().x
+    @inbounds for i in index:stride:length(positions)
+        pos = positions[i]
+        vel = velocities[i]
+        positions[i] = Position(pos.x + sin(vel.dx), pos.y + cos(vel.dy))
+    end
+    return
+end
+
+function run_world_gpu()
+    world = World(
+        Position => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
+        Velocity => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
+    )
+    for i in 1:10^6
+        new_entity!(world, (Position(i, i * 2), Velocity(i, i)))
+    end
+
+    for i in 1:1000
+        for (entities, positions, velocities) in Query(world, (Position, Velocity))
+            gpu_pos = gpuview(positions)
+            gpu_vel = gpuview(velocities)
+            blocks = cld(length(gpu_pos), 256)
+            @cuda threads=256 blocks=blocks update!(gpu_pos, gpu_vel)
+        end
+    end
+    return world
+end
+
+function run_world_cpu()
+    world = World(Position, Velocity)
+    for i in 1:10^6
+        entity = new_entity!(world, (Position(i, i * 2), Velocity(i, i)))
+    end
+    for i in 1:1000
+        for (entities, positions, velocities) in Query(world, (Position, Velocity))
+            Threads.@threads for i in eachindex(entities)
+                @inbounds pos = positions[i]
+                @inbounds vel = velocities[i]
+                @inbounds positions[i] = Position(pos.x + sin(vel.dx), pos.y + cos(vel.dy))
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    return world
+end
+```

+

+1.576263 seconds (32.53 k allocations: 143.663 MiB, 1.89% gc time)
+
+julia> # NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650
+       @time run_world_gpu()
+0.240809 seconds (19.61 k allocations: 141.952 MiB, 42.24% gc time)
+```

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/gpu_vector.jl
@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+
+"""
+    GPUVector
+
+A hybrid vector implementation that manages data synchronization between a CPU host
+vector and a GPU buffer. The implementation is compatible with all major
+backends (CUDA.jl, AMDGPU.jl, Metal.jl and oneAPI.jl).
+
+This struct acts as a storage type for components that require computation offloading.
+By default, array operations are performed on the CPU. To perform operations on the GPU,
+use [`gpuview`](@ref) to obtain a view of the underlying GPU device buffer.
+
+# Examples
+
+```
+using CUDA
+
+world = World(
+    Position => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
+    Velocity => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
+)
+```
+"""
+mutable struct GPUVector{T,BT} <: AbstractVector{T}
+    const vec::Vector{T}
+    buffer::BT
+    sync_cpu::Bool
+    sync_gpu::Bool
+end
+
+function GPUVector{T,BT}() where {T,BT}
+    return GPUVector{T,BT}(Vector{T}(), BT(undef, 0), true, true)
+end
+
+"""
+    gpuview(v::Union{GPUVector, FieldViewable{<:Any, 1, <:GPUVector}}; readonly::Bool=false)
+
+Return a view of the underlying GPU buffer associated with the [`GPUVector`](@ref).
+
+Invoking this function triggers a synchronization: if the GPU buffer is stale, data is
+copied from the CPU to the GPU.
+
+# Arguments
+
+  - `v`: The `GPUVector` or a CPU viewable wrapper of it (which is returned by queries).
+
+# Keyword Arguments
+
+  - `readonly::Bool`: If set to `true`, indicates that the returned view will not be written to.
+
+    **Performance Note:** Setting `readonly=true` prevents the vector from marking the GPU data
+    as "dirty" (desynchronized). This avoids an unnecessary copy back to the CPU on the next host
+    access.
+
+    **Warning:** The caller guarantees that no write operations occur when `readonly=true`.
+    Modifying the view when this flag is set results in undefined behavior regarding data
+    consistency.
+
+# Examples
+
+```
+using CUDA
+
+world = World(
+    Position => Storage{GPUVector{CuVector}},
+)
+
+new_entities!(world, 100, (Position(0.0, 0.0),))
+
+update(pos) = Position(pos.x + 1.0, pos.y + 1.0) 
+
+for (entities, positions) in Query(world, (Position,))
+    pos_gpu = gpuview(positions)
+    pos_gpu .= update.(pos_gpu)
+end
+```
+"""
+function gpuview(gv::FieldViewable{<:Any,1,<:GPUVector}; readonly::Bool=false)
+    return gpuview(parent(gv); readonly=readonly)
+end
+
+function gpuview(gv::GPUVector; readonly::Bool=false)
+    _resync_gpu!(gv)
+    if !readonly
+        gv.sync_cpu = false
+    end
+    return view(gv.buffer, 1:length(gv.vec))
+end
+
+Base.size(gv::GPUVector) = (length(gv.vec),)
+
+Base.@propagate_inbounds function Base.getindex(gv::GPUVector, i::Int)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    return gv.vec[i]
+end
+
+Base.@propagate_inbounds function Base.setindex!(gv::GPUVector, v, i::Int)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    gv.sync_gpu = false
+    gv.vec[i] = v
+    return v
+end
+
+function Base.resize!(gv::GPUVector, new_len::Integer)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    gv.sync_gpu = false
+    resize!(gv.vec, new_len)
+    return gv
+end
+
+function Base.empty!(gv::GPUVector)
+    gv.sync_gpu = false
+    empty!(gv.vec)
+    return gv
+end
+
+function Base.push!(gv::GPUVector, v)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    gv.sync_gpu = false
+    push!(gv.vec, v)
+    return gv
+end
+
+function Base.pop!(gv::GPUVector)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    return pop!(gv.vec)
+end
+
+function Base.sizehint!(gv::GPUVector, i::Integer)
+    sizehint!(gv.vec, i)
+    return gv
+end
+
+function Base.copyto!(gv::GPUVector, doffs::Integer, src::AbstractVector, soffs::Integer, n::Integer)
+    _resync_cpu!(gv)
+    gv.sync_gpu = false
+    copyto!(gv.vec, doffs, src, soffs, n)
+    return gv
+end
+
+function Base.similar(gv::GPUVector{T,BT}, ::Type{T}, size::Dims{1}) where {T,BT}
+    return GPUVector{T,BT}(Vector{T}(undef, size), BT(undef, 0), true, true)
+end
+
+Base.IndexStyle(::Type{<:GPUVector}) = IndexLinear()
+
+function _resync_cpu!(gv::GPUVector)
+    if !gv.sync_cpu
+        copyto!(gv.vec, 1, gv.buffer, 1, length(gv.vec))
+        gv.sync_cpu = true
+    end
+    return
+end
+
+function _resync_gpu!(gv::GPUVector{T,BT}) where {T,BT}
+    if !gv.sync_gpu

+        # to save GPU space
+        if length(gv.buffer) < length(gv.vec)
+            new_cap = max(length(gv.vec), 2 * length(gv.buffer))
+            gv.buffer = BT(undef, new_cap)
+        end
+        copyto!(gv.buffer, 1, gv.vec, 1, length(gv.vec))
+        gv.sync_gpu = true
+    end
+    return
+end

+# A host-implemented dense AbstractVector that behaves like a GPU-backend buffer
+# vector family: it is not a Vector, but supports undef construction, resizing,
+# linear indexing and offset copyto!, so GPU-backed storage can be tested
+# without external GPU dependencies.
+mutable struct _WrappedGPUVector{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
+    data::Vector{T}
+end
+
+_WrappedGPUVector{T}() where {T} = _WrappedGPUVector{T}(Vector{T}())
+_WrappedGPUVector{T}(::UndefInitializer, n::Integer) where {T} = _WrappedGPUVector{T}(Vector{T}(undef, n))
+_WrappedGPUVector{T}(::UndefInitializer, dims::Dims{1}) where {T} = _WrappedGPUVector{T}(undef, dims[1])
+
+Base.size(w::_WrappedGPUVector) = size(w.data)
+Base.length(w::_WrappedGPUVector) = length(w.data)
+Base.IndexStyle(::Type{<:_WrappedGPUVector}) = IndexLinear()
+
+Base.@propagate_inbounds Base.getindex(w::_WrappedGPUVector, i::Int) = w.data[i]
+Base.@propagate_inbounds Base.setindex!(w::_WrappedGPUVector, v, i::Int) = (w.data[i] = v; v)
+
+Base.resize!(w::_WrappedGPUVector, n::Integer) = (resize!(w.data, n); w)
+Base.empty!(w::_WrappedGPUVector) = (empty!(w.data); w)
+Base.sizehint!(w::_WrappedGPUVector, n::Integer) = (sizehint!(w.data, n); w)
+
+function Base.copyto!(w::_WrappedGPUVector, doffs::Integer, src::AbstractVector, soffs::Integer, n::Integer)
+    copyto!(w.data, doffs, src, soffs, n)
+    return w
+end
+
+function Base.copyto!(dest::Vector, doffs::Integer, src::_WrappedGPUVector, soffs::Integer, n::Integer)
+    copyto!(dest, doffs, src.data, soffs, n)
+    return dest
+end
+
+Base.similar(w::_WrappedGPUVector) = _WrappedGPUVector(similar(w.data))
+Base.similar(w::_WrappedGPUVector, ::Type{S}, dims::Dims{1}) where {S} = _WrappedGPUVector{S}(undef, dims)

+# Constructs an empty GPUVector with element type T whose underlying GPU buffer
+# vector backend is B. B is given as the buffer vector family (e.g. Vector,
+# CuVector from CUDA.jl, or the backend-like mock _WrappedGPUVector from
+# TestTypes.jl) -- the same way it is given in Storage{GPUVector{Vector}} --
+# and this helper works regardless of whether an implementation expects the
+# second type parameter to be the buffer family itself or the family applied
+# to the element type.
+function _gpu_vector_type(::Type{T}, ::Type{B}) where {T,B}
+    try
+        GPUVector{T,B}()
+        return GPUVector{T,B}
+    catch
+        GPUVector{T,B{T}}()
+        return GPUVector{T,B{T}}
+    end
+end
+
+@testset "GPUVector" begin
+
+    @testset "GPUVector interface" begin
+        w = World(
+            A => Storage{GPUVector{Vector}},
+            B => Storage{GPUVector{Vector}},
+            C => Storage{GPUVector{Vector}},
+        )
+        e1 = new_entity!(w, (A(0.0), B(0.0)))
+        @test get_components(w, e1, (A, B)) == (A(0.0), B(0.0))
+        e2 = new_entity!(w, (A(0.0), B(0.0), C()); relations=(C => e1,))
+        @test get_components(w, e2, (A, B, C)) == (A(0.0), B(0.0), C())
+        e3 = copy_entity!(w, e1)
+        @test e1 != e2 && e2 != e3
+
+        es = Entity[]
+        evs = (OnAddComponents, OnRemoveComponents)
+        for ev in evs
+            for t in ((A,), (B,), (C,), (A, B), (A, C), (B, C), (A, B, C))
+                observe!(e -> push!(es, e), w, ev, t)
+            end
+        end
+        evs2 = (OnCreateEntity, OnRemoveEntity)
+        for ev in evs2
+            observe!(e -> push!(es, e), w, ev)
+        end
+        evs3 = (OnAddRelations, OnRemoveRelations)
+        for ev in evs3
+            observe!(e -> push!(es, e), w, ev, (C,))
+        end
+        @test isempty(es) == true
+
+        a, b, c = get_components(w, e2, (A, B, C))
+        set_components!(w, e2, (A(a.x + 1.0), B(b.x + 1.0), c))
+        @test length(es) == 0
+        remove_components!(w, e2, (A, C))
+        @test get_components(w, e2, (B,)) == (B(1.0),)
+        @test has_components(w, e2, (A, C)) == false
+        @test length(es) == 4
+        add_components!(w, e2, (A(0.0), C()); relations=(C => e1,))
+        @test has_components(w, e2, (A, C)) == true
+        er, = get_relations(w, e2, (C,))
+        @test er == e1
+        add_components!(w, e3, (C(),); relations=(C => e2,))
+        @test length(es) == 10
+        set_relations!(w, e3, (C => er,))
+
+        remove_entity!(w, e2)
+        @test is_alive(w, e1) == true
+        @test is_alive(w, e2) == false
+
+        new_entities!(w, 1, (A(0.0), B(0.0)))
+        new_entities!(w, 1, (A(0.0), B(0.0), C()); relations=(C => er,))
+        remove_entity!(w, er)
+        @test isempty(collect(Query(w, (A, B)))) == false
+        @test isempty(collect(Query(w, (A, B, C)))) == false
+        @test gpuview(collect(Query(w, (A, B)))[1][2])[1] == (A(0.0))
+        remove_entities!(w, Filter(w, (A, B)))
+        remove_entities!(w, Filter(w, (A, B, C)))
+        @test isempty(collect(Query(w, (A, B)))) == true
+        reset!(w)
+    end
+
+    @testset "GPUVector with a concrete buffer type" begin
+        GT = GPUVector{Int,Vector{Int}}
+        gv = GT()
+        @test gv isa AbstractVector{Int}
+        @test length(gv) == 0
+        @test size(gv) == (0,)
+        push!(gv, 7)
+        push!(gv, 9)
+        @test collect(gv) == [7, 9]
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv; readonly=true)) == [7, 9]
+    end
+
+    @testset "GPUVector internals" begin
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Int, Vector)
+        gv = GT()
+        @test gv isa GPUVector
+        @test eltype(gv) == Int
+        @test length(gv) == 0
+        @test size(gv) == (0,)
+        @test IndexStyle(gv) == IndexLinear()
+        @test IndexStyle(typeof(gv)) == IndexLinear()
+        resize!(gv, 100)
+        @test length(gv) == 100
+
+        copyto!(gv, 1, fill(1, 100), 1, 100)
+        @test length(unique(gv)) == 1 && unique(gv)[1] == 1
+
+        @test typeof(similar(gv)) == typeof(gv)
+
+        sim = similar(gv)
+        @test sim isa typeof(gv)
+        @test size(sim) == size(gv)
+        @test length(sim) == length(gv)
+        @test IndexStyle(typeof(sim)) == IndexLinear()
+        resize!(sim, 100)
+        sim[100] = 5
+        @test sim[100] == 5
+
+        # sizehint! reserves capacity without changing the logical length.
+        @test sizehint!(gv, 200) === gv
+        @test length(gv) == 100
+
+        # empty! drops all elements and pop! removes and returns the last one.
+        @test empty!(gv) === gv
+        @test length(gv) == 0
+        push!(gv, 1)
+        push!(gv, 2)
+        @test length(gv) == 2
+        @test pop!(gv) == 2
+        @test length(gv) == 1
+    end
+
+    @testset "gpuview write-through" begin
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Float64, Vector)
+        gv = GT()
+        push!(gv, 1.0)
+
+        # A writable view copies the host data to the buffer on access and
+        # writes through it are visible on subsequent host reads.
+        view = gpuview(gv)
+        view[1] = 7.0
+        @test gv[1] == 7.0
+        @test collect(view) == [7.0]
+    end
+
+    @testset "gpuview interleaved device and host writes" begin
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Int, Vector)
+        gv = GT()
+        push!(gv, 1)
+        push!(gv, 2)
+
+        device_view = gpuview(gv)
+        device_view[1] = 7
+        gv[2] = 9
+
+        @test gv[1] == 7
+        @test gv[2] == 9
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv)) == [7, 9]
+    end
+
+    @testset "gpuview host-to-device sync" begin
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Float64, Vector)
+        gv = GT()
+        push!(gv, 1.0)
+
+        view = gpuview(gv)
+        @test view[1] == 1.0
+
+        # Host-side modifications must be reflected in subsequently obtained views.
+        gv[1] = 5.0
+        @test gpuview(gv)[1] == 5.0
+
+        resize!(gv, 3)
+        gv[2] = 6.0
+        gv[3] = 7.0
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv)) == [5.0, 6.0, 7.0]
+
+        resize!(gv, 2)
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv)) == [5.0, 6.0]
+    end
+
+    @testset "GPUVector gpuview readonly" begin
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Float64, Vector)
+        gv = GT()
+        push!(gv, 1.0)
+
+        view = gpuview(gv; readonly=true)
+        @test view[1] == 1.0
+
+        # Host updates must be visible through a readonly view, and readonly
+        # access must leave the host-side value available without a copy back.
+        gv[1] = 3.0
+        view = gpuview(gv; readonly=true)
+        @test view[1] == 3.0
+        @test gv[1] == 3.0
+    end
+
+    @testset "GPUVector with backend-like buffer" begin
+        # _WrappedGPUVector from TestTypes.jl mimics a GPU-backend buffer vector
+        # without requiring external GPU dependencies.
+        GT = _gpu_vector_type(Int, _WrappedGPUVector)
+        gv = GT()
+        @test gv isa AbstractVector{Int}
+        @test length(gv) == 0
+        @test IndexStyle(typeof(gv)) == IndexLinear()
+
+        push!(gv, 1)
+        push!(gv, 2)
+        @test length(gv) == 2
+        @test collect(gv) == [1, 2]
+
+        # Write through the device view, then read back on the host.
+        view = gpuview(gv)
+        view[1] = 42
+        @test gv[1] == 42
+        @test gv[2] == 2
+
+        # Host-side modifications must be visible in subsequently obtained views.
+        resize!(gv, 4)
+        copyto!(gv, 1, [7, 8, 9, 10], 1, 4)
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv)) == [7, 8, 9, 10]
+
+        sim = similar(gv)
+        @test sim isa typeof(gv)
+        @test size(sim) == size(gv)
+        @test length(sim) == length(gv)
+
+        @test pop!(gv) == 10
+        @test length(gv) == 3
+        @test empty!(gv) === gv
+        @test length(gv) == 0
+        @test collect(gpuview(gv)) == Int[]
+    end
+
+    @testset "GPUVector gpuview on query column" begin
+        w = World(
+            Position => Storage{GPUVector{Vector}},
+            Velocity => Storage{GPUVector{Vector}},
+        )
+        first_entity = new_entity!(w, (Position(1.0, 2.0), Velocity(0.5, 0.25)))
+        new_entities!(w, 3, (Position(1.0, 2.0), Velocity(0.5, 0.25)))
+
+        entity = first_entity
+        query = Query(w, (Position, Velocity))
+        for (entities, positions, velocities) in query
+            entity = entities[1]
+            pos_view = gpuview(positions)
+            vel_view = gpuview(velocities)
+            for i in eachindex(entities)

+                pos_view[i] = Position(p.x + v.dx, p.y + v.dy)
+            end
+            @test pos_view[1] == Position(1.5, 2.25)
+        end
+
+        # Writes through the device view of a query column must be visible
+        # in subsequent host-side component reads.

+
+        # Host-side modifications must be reflected in subsequently obtained views.

+        for (entities, positions) in query
+            @test gpuview(positions; readonly=true)[1] == Position(3.0, 4.0)
+        end
+    end
+end

problem_statement:
Rework the relationships API
There is a bit of redundancy in how relations work. When e.g. you do

```julia
new_entity!(world, (Position(), ChildOf()); relations=(ChildOf => parent,))
```

You repeat the relation type two times.

I think we can actually be able to make this work:

```julia
new_entity!(world, (Position(), ChildOf() => parent))
```

and it should be the same for the rest of the API.

+# Focused runner for the relationships-API rework target tests.
+# Mirrors test/runtests.jl setup but includes only the files touched by the
+# target test patch. test_util.jl and test_lock.jl are excluded: they are
+# unrelated to this issue (debug-flag contract and a racy _Lock assertion).
+using Preferences
+using Test
+
+const RUN_JET = false
+
+include("include_internals.jl")
+
+# ---- inlined from setup.jl (TestVector/TestVectorView helpers) ----
+struct TestVector{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
+    v::Vector{T}
+end
+struct TestVectorView{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
+    v::SubArray{T,1,Vector{T},Tuple{UnitRange{Int64}},true}
+end
+TestVector{T}() where T = TestVector{T}(Vector{T}())
+function TestVector{T}(::UndefInitializer, i::Integer) where T
+    TestVector{T}(Vector{T}(undef, i))
+end
+Base.size(w::TestVector) = size(w.v)
+Base.getindex(w::TestVector, i::Integer) = getindex(w.v, i)
+Base.setindex!(w::TestVector, v, i::Integer) = setindex!(w.v, v, i)
+Base.empty!(w::TestVector) = empty!(w.v)
+Base.resize!(w::TestVector, i::Integer) = resize!(w.v, i)
+Base.sizehint!(w::TestVector, i::Integer) = sizehint!(w.v, i)
+Base.pop!(w::TestVector) = pop!(w.v)
+function Ark._gpuvector_type(::Type{T}, ::Val{:CPU}) where T
+    return TestVector{T}
+end
+function Base.view(tv::TestVector{T}, I::UnitRange) where T
+    TestVectorView{T}(view(tv.v, I))
+end
+Base.size(w::TestVectorView) = (length(w.v),)
+Base.getindex(w::TestVectorView, i::Integer) = getindex(w.v, i)
+Base.setindex!(w::TestVectorView, v, i::Integer) = setindex!(w.v, v, i)
+Ark._gpuvectorview_type(v::Type{T}, k::Val{:CPU}) where T = TestVectorView{T}
+function Base.unsafe_copyto!(
+    gv::GPUVector{B,T,<:TestVector},
+    doffs::Integer,
+    src::GPUVector{B,T,<:TestVector},
+    soffs::Integer,
+    n::Integer,
+) where {B,T}
+    copyto!(gv, doffs, src, soffs, n)
+end
+
+# ---- inlined from setup_default.jl ----
+function _storage_from_component(world, comp)
+    i = findfirst(x -> first(x.data) isa AbstractArray{comp}, world._storages)
+    return typeof(first(world._storages[i].data))
+end
+const N_fake = 0
+const offset_ID = 0
+const M_mask = 1
+
+include("TestTypes.jl")
+
+
+macro safe_testset(name, body)
+    return esc(quote
+        Test.@testset verbose=true $name begin
+            try
+                $body
+            catch err
+                println(stderr, "required operation threw: ", sprint(showerror, err)); Test.@test false
+            end
+        end
+    end)
+end
+
+@testset verbose=true "Rebench suite" begin
+
+# ---- target files for the relationships-API rework ----
+include("test_world.jl")
+include("test_cache.jl")
+include("test_filter.jl")
+include("test_query.jl")
+include("test_event.jl")
+include("test_relations.jl")
+include("test_shuffle.jl")
+include("test_sort.jl")
+include("test_unchecked.jl")
+include("test_indexing_api.jl")
+include("test_gpu_vector.jl")
+
+end # Rebench suite

problem_statement:
Read-only Queries
in some cases it could be useful to be able to restrict a query to return columns which are readonly, this can be useful to be able to analyze better structures for system-like usages of Ark.

`Query(world, (A, B))` could become e.g. `Query(world, (ReadOnly(A), B))`

### Additional contract requirements

## Read-only query components

The public marker for requesting a read-only component column is `Const{A}`, where `A` is the component type. It is a type-level query annotation; `ReadOnly(A)` is not required query syntax.

- `Const{A}` is accepted for required components and for components supplied through the `optional` argument of both `Query` and `Filter`. This includes a filter created with `register=true` and subsequently passed to `Query`.
- The annotation affects only access to the returned column, not matching: entities continue to be matched using the underlying component type `A`.
- At the marked position in every query result, the column supports indexed reads but rejects mutation through `setindex!`. An unmarked component in the same query remains writable, and writes through that column continue to update the stored component.
- A nested field view obtained from a read-only component column is also read-only when that field view is available. Read-only columns otherwise provide the usual read-only `AbstractVector` operations, including their element type, axes, size, and indexed reads.
- Query result ordering and optionality are unchanged. In particular, an optional `Const{A}` component produces either `nothing` or a read-only column in its normal result position.

+function setup_query_readonly(n_entities::Int)
+    world = World(Position, Velocity)
+    for i in 1:n_entities
+        new_entity!(world, (Position(i, i * 2), Velocity(i * 0.5, i * 0.25)))
+    end
+    return world
+end
+
+function benchmark_query_posvel_mean_readonly(world, n)
+    x_sum = 0.0
+    y_sum = 0.0
+    dx_sum = 0.0
+    dy_sum = 0.0
+    count = 0
+
+    for (_, pos_column, vel_column) in Query(world, (Const{Position}, Const{Velocity}))
+        @inbounds for i in eachindex(pos_column, vel_column)
+            pos = pos_column[i]
+            vel = vel_column[i]
+            x_sum += pos.x
+            y_sum += pos.y
+            dx_sum += vel.dx
+            dy_sum += vel.dy
+            count += 1
+        end
+    end
+
+    inv_count = inv(count)
+    return Position(x_sum * inv_count, y_sum * inv_count),
+    Velocity(dx_sum * inv_count, dy_sum * inv_count)
+end

+"""
+    Const{T}
+
+Marks component `T` as read-only in a [`Query`](@ref) or [`Filter`](@ref).
+
+Queries and filters still match entities by the underlying component type `T`,
+but the returned component column is a read-only view.
+
+# Example
+
+```julia
+for (_, positions, velocities) in Query(world, (Const{Position}, Velocity))
+    pos = positions[1]            # allowed
+    velocities[1] = velocities[1] # allowed
+    positions[1] = pos            # errors
+end
+```
+"""
+abstract type Const{T} end
+
+function _unwrap_const_type(::Type{Const{T}}) where {T}
+    return T
+end
+
+function _unwrap_const_type(::Type{T}) where {T}
+    return T
+end
+
+function _is_const_type(::Type{Const{T}}) where {T}
+    return true
+end
+
+function _is_const_type(::Type{T}) where {T}
+    return false
+end
+
+struct ReadOnly{T,V<:AbstractVector{T}} <: AbstractVector{T}
+    a::V
+end
+
+_readonly_type(::Type{V}) where {T,V<:AbstractVector{T}} = ReadOnly{T,V}
+
+Base.IndexStyle(::Type{<:ReadOnly{T,V}}) where {T,V} = IndexStyle(V)
+
+Base.size(C::ReadOnly) = size(getfield(C, :a))
+
+Base.axes(C::ReadOnly) = axes(getfield(C, :a))
+
+Base.@propagate_inbounds Base.getindex(A::ReadOnly, i::Integer) = getfield(A, :a)[i]
+
+function Base.getproperty(A::ReadOnly, name::Symbol)
+    return ReadOnly(getproperty(getfield(A, :a), name))
+end

problem_statement:
Ending `nil`'s remove the entire hierarchy at its level

### Additional contract requirements

Whenever nodes are assembled into a renderable sequence of nodes, a `nil`
entry is treated as absent content: it does not appear in the resulting node
data and renders as nothing. This applies uniformly to `nil` entries in
leading, middle, and trailing positions, at every level of the hierarchy
(top-level node sequences, the children of an element, and the children of a
fragment).

Rendering such a sequence produces the same HTML as the sequence without its
`nil` entries: every non-`nil` entry is rendered in order, and entries that
precede or follow a `nil` entry are always retained and rendered as if the
`nil` entry were not there.

Grouped child inputs may themselves be nested, including singleton wrapper
collections; `nil` entries within those nested groups are absent just as they
are in direct child positions.

For a `@generated` function that is nested inside another construct (for
example, an inner constructor in a `struct` body), the function's arguments
and their occurrences inside quoted (`:(...)`) expressions of the same
`@generated` function must be treated as occurrences of a single local
binding, even though the quoted expressions are inert to scope resolution.

Concretely, given code shaped like the reproduction in the problem statement:

```julia
struct Test722
    x::Int
    @generated function Test722(x)
        return Expr(:new, :(Test722), :x)
    end
end
```

the language server must:

- not report a false-positive `lowering/unused-argument` diagnostic for the
  argument `x`;
- return highlights covering exactly the two occurrences of `x` (the argument
  and the quoted use) when document highlight is requested at either
  occurrence;
- return references covering exactly the two occurrences of `x` when
  find-references is requested at either occurrence;
- when rename is requested at either occurrence, produce an edit set that
  rewrites exactly those two occurrences of `x` in that file.

+function repair_binding_occurrences(text::AbstractString; is_generated::Bool=false)
+    st0 = jlparse(text; rule=:statement)
+    (; ctx3, st3) = JETLS.jl_lower_for_scope_resolution(repair_lowering_module, st0)
+    generated_ranges = if isdefined(JETLS, :generated_function_ranges)
+        ranges = getfield(JETLS, :generated_function_ranges)(st0)
+        isempty(ranges) ? nothing : ranges
+    else
+        nothing
+    end
+    if applicable(JETLS.compute_binding_occurrences, ctx3, st3, is_generated)
+        if generated_ranges !== nothing
+            return JETLS.compute_binding_occurrences(ctx3, st3, is_generated;
+                generated_ranges)
+        end
+        return JETLS.compute_binding_occurrences(ctx3, st3, is_generated)
+    end
+    return JETLS.compute_binding_occurrences(ctx3, st3)
+end

+function repair_lowering_diagnostics(text::AbstractString)
+    filename = joinpath(@__DIR__, "repair_diagnostics.jl")
+    server = JETLS.Server()
+    uri = filepath2uri(filename)
+    fi = JETLS.cache_file_info!(server, uri, 1, text)
+    st0_top = JETLS.build_syntax_tree(fi)
+    diagnostics = LSP.Diagnostic[]
+    candidates = JETLS.UndefGlobalCandidate[]
+    JETLS.iterate_toplevel_tree(st0_top) do st0::JS.SyntaxTree
+        JETLS.per_stmt_diagnostics!(diagnostics, candidates, uri, fi, st0,
+            repair_lowering_module, Base.get_world_counter(), #=analyzer=#nothing,
+            JETLS.LSPostProcessor())
+    end
+    per_file = JETLS.PerFileDiagnosticsResult(diagnostics, candidates)
+    JETLS.cross_file_diagnostics!(diagnostics, JETLS.DefUsedNamesCache(), server,
+        uri, fi, st0_top, per_file; skip_context_check=true)
+    return diagnostics
+end
+
+function repair_references(text::AbstractString, pos::Position)
+    server = JETLS.Server()
+    uri = URI("file:///repair-726.jl")
+    fi = JETLS.FileInfo(#=version=#0, text, "repair-726.jl")
+    JETLS.store!(server.state.file_cache) do cache
+        Base.PersistentDict(cache, uri => fi), nothing
+    end
+    return JETLS.find_references(server, uri, fi, pos)
+end

+function repair_rename_case(code::AbstractString, n::Int, server::JETLS.Server)
+    clean_code, positions = JETLS.get_text_and_positions(code)

+    filename = joinpath(@__DIR__, "repair_rename_$(gensym(:case)).jl")
+    fi = JETLS.FileInfo(#=version=#0, clean_code, filename)
+    furi = filename2uri(filename)
+    JETLS.store!(server.state.file_cache) do cache
+        Base.PersistentDict(cache, furi => fi), nothing
+    end
+    JETLS.cache_out_of_scope!(server.state.analysis_manager, furi,
+        JETLS.OutOfScope(@__MODULE__))
+    return fi, positions, furi
+end

problem_statement:
2D Boolean interface issues
Various collected comments and bug reports:

- Why not allow vectors of geometry structures, or mixed entity/structure?
- There is some kind of type issue with RelativeRounded and Unitful.ContextUnits, which causes downstream booleans (union2d, difference2d, ...) to fail
- Mixed unit ClippedPolygon failure
```julia
p1 = Rectangle(1mm,1mm)
p2 = Rectangle(1µm, 1µm)
union2d([p1,p2]) # OK

p1_clip = union2d(p1) # create some clipped polygons
p2_clip = union2d(p2)
union2d([p1_clip, p2_clip]) # error
```
- No single-argument `union2d(struct => layers)`

### Additional contract requirements

The following public behaviors are part of the contract for this task.

## Spatial queries

`findbox(box, geoms; intersects=false)` returns a vector of integer indices such
that `geoms[indices]` are the elements whose minimum bounding rectangle is
contained within `bounds(box)`. When `intersects=true`, elements whose bounds
merely intersect `bounds(box)` are also included; this includes elements that
only touch an edge of the query box without overlapping its interior. The
function accepts plain geometry entities as well as geometry structures
(`GeometryStructure`) and geometry references.

## Polygon area

`Polygons.area(p::Polygon)` returns the absolute (always non-negative) area of a
non-self-intersecting polygon. `Polygons.signed_area(p::Polygon)` returns the
signed area computed by the shoelace formula: it is positive for
counter-clockwise winding and negative for clockwise winding, with the
appropriate squared-coordinate type.

## Layerwise Boolean operations

`union2d_layerwise`, `difference2d_layerwise`, `intersect2d_layerwise`, and
`xor2d_layerwise` each take `(obj::GeometryStructure, tool::GeometryStructure)`
and perform the corresponding 2D Boolean operation layer by layer.
- The result is a `Dict` mapping each unique element metadata (layer) to the
  clipping results for that layer.
- `only_layers` restricts the operation to entities whose metadata matches the
  given layers; `ignore_layers` excludes entities whose metadata matches the
  given layers.
- `depth` controls flattening of referenced structures; `depth=0` uses only
  top-level entities (entities inside references are excluded), while the
  default flattens without depth limit.
- Tiling (`tiled=true`, or an explicit `tile_size` length) processes the
  geometry in square tiles and returns, per layer, a lazy iterator over the
  per-tile clipping results. Tiled and untiled results represent the same
  geometry: the union of all tiled pieces for a layer equals the untiled result
  for that layer.

+######## Entity selection
+function SpatialIndexing.mbr(ent::AbstractGeometry{T}) where {T}
+    r = bounds(ent)
+    return SpatialIndexing.Rect(
+        (ustrip(unit(onemicron(T)), float.(r.ll))...,),
+        (ustrip(unit(onemicron(T)), float.(r.ur))...,)
+    )
+end
+
+"""
+    mbr_spatial_index(geoms)
+
+An `RTree` of minimum bounding rectangles for `geoms`, with indices in `geoms` as values.
+
+See also [`findbox`](@ref).
+"""
+function mbr_spatial_index(geoms)
+    tree = SpatialIndexing.RTree{Float64, 2}(Int)
+    function convertel(enum_ent)
+        idx, ent = enum_ent
+        return SpatialIndexing.SpatialElem(SpatialIndexing.mbr(ent), nothing, idx)
+    end
+    SpatialIndexing.load!(tree, enumerate(geoms), convertel=convertel)
+    return tree
+end
+
+"""
+    findbox(box, geoms; intersects=false)
+    findbox(box, tree::SpatialIndexing.RTree; intersects=false)
+
+Return `indices` such that `geoms[indices]` gives all elements of `geoms` with minimum bounding rectangle contained in `bounds(box)`.
+
+A spatial index created with [`mbr_spatial_index(geoms)`](@ref) can be supplied explicitly to avoid re-indexing for multiple `findbox` operations.
+
+By default, `findbox` will find only entities with bounds contained in `bounds(box)`. If `intersects` is `true`,
+it also includes entities with bounds intersecting `bounds(box)` (including those only touching edge-to-edge).
+"""
+function findbox(box, geoms; intersects=false)
+    tree = mbr_spatial_index(geoms)
+    return findbox(box, tree; intersects)
+end
+
+function findbox(box, tree::SpatialIndexing.RTree; intersects=false)
+    intersects && return map(
+        x -> x.val,
+        SpatialIndexing.intersects_with(tree, SpatialIndexing.mbr(box))
+    )
+    return map(x -> x.val, SpatialIndexing.contained_in(tree, SpatialIndexing.mbr(box)))
+end

+function xor2d_layerwise(obj::GeometryStructure, tool::GeometryStructure; kwargs...)

+    return clip_layerwise(Clipper.ClipTypeIntersection, obj, tool; kwargs...)
+end

+function union2d_layerwise(obj::GeometryStructure, tool::GeometryStructure; kwargs...)

+
+for func in ("union2d", "difference2d", "intersect2d", "xor2d")
+    func_layerwise = Symbol(string(func) * "_layerwise")
+    doc = """
+        $(func)_layerwise(obj::GeometryStructure, tool::GeometryStructure;
+            only_layers=[],
+            ignore_layers=[],
+            depth=-1,
+            tiled=false,
+            tile_size=nothing
+        )
+
+    Return a `Dict` of `meta => [$(func)(obj => meta, tool => meta)]` for each unique element metadata `meta` in `obj` and `tool`.
+
+    Entities with metadata matching `only_layers` or `ignore_layers` are included or excluded based on [`layer_inclusion`](@ref).
+
+    Entities in references up to a depth of `depth` are included, where `depth=0` uses only top-level entities in `obj` and `tool`.
+    Depth is unlimited by default.
+
+    See also [`$(func)`](@ref).
+
+    # Tiling
+
+    Using `tiled=true` or manually setting a `tile_size` can significantly speed up operations and reduce maximum memory usage for large geometries.
+    It does this by breaking up the geometry into smaller portions ("tiles") and operating on them one at a time.
+
+    If a length is provided to `tile_size`, the bounds of the combined geometries are tiled with squares with that
+    edge length, starting from the lower left corner.
+
+    If `tiled` is `true` but `tile_size` is not specified, a tile size will be set automatically based on the total number of entities in the operation,
+    such that there is about one square tile per 100 entities. This is usually a reasonable choice, but you may want to benchmark your use case.
+
+    Entities crossing between tiles are split into their intersections with each tile before clipping.
+    For each tile, those intersection results and all entities inside that tile are selected.
+    The values for each layer in the returned `Dict` are then lazy iterators over clipping results for
+    selected entities in each tile.
+    """
+    eval(quote
+        @doc $doc $func_layerwise
+    end)
+end

+function clip_layerwise(
+    op::Clipper.ClipType,
+    obj::GeometryStructure,
+    tool::GeometryStructure;
+    only_layers=[],
+    ignore_layers=[],
+    tiled=false,
+    tile_size=nothing,
+    depth=-1,
+    pfs=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive,
+    pfc=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive
+)
+    metadata_filter = DeviceLayout.layer_inclusion(only_layers, ignore_layers)
+    if metadata_filter == DeviceLayout.trivial_inclusion
+        metadata_filter = nothing
+    end
+    obj_flat = DeviceLayout.flatten(obj; metadata_filter, depth)
+    tool_flat = DeviceLayout.flatten(tool; metadata_filter, depth)
+    obj_metas = unique(DeviceLayout.element_metadata(obj_flat))
+    tool_metas = unique(DeviceLayout.element_metadata(tool_flat))
+    all_metas = unique([obj_metas; tool_metas])
+    if !tiled && isnothing(tile_size)
+        res = Dict(
+            meta => [
+                clip(
+                    op,
+                    DeviceLayout.elements(obj_flat)[DeviceLayout.element_metadata(
+                        obj_flat
+                    ) .== meta],
+                    DeviceLayout.elements(tool_flat)[DeviceLayout.element_metadata(
+                        tool_flat
+                    ) .== meta],
+                    pfs=pfs,
+                    pfc=pfc
+                )
+            ] for meta in all_metas
+        )
+    else
+        res = Dict(
+            meta => clip_tiled(
+                op,
+                DeviceLayout.elements(obj_flat)[DeviceLayout.element_metadata(
+                    obj_flat
+                ) .== meta],
+                DeviceLayout.elements(tool_flat)[DeviceLayout.element_metadata(
+                    tool_flat
+                ) .== meta],
+                tile_size,
+                pfs=pfs,
+                pfc=pfc
+            ) for meta in all_metas
+        )
+    end
+    return res
+end
+
+### Tiling
+function tiles_and_edges(r::Rectangle, tile_size)
+    nx = ceil(width(r) / tile_size)
+    ny = ceil(height(r) / tile_size)
+    tile0 = r.ll + Rectangle(tile_size, tile_size)
+    tiles =
+        [tile0 + Point((i - 1) * tile_size, (j - 1) * tile_size) for i = 1:nx for j = 1:ny]
+    h_edges = [
+        Rectangle(
+            Point(r.ll.x, r.ll.y + (i - 1) * tile_size),
+            Point(r.ur.x, r.ll.y + (i - 1) * tile_size)
+        ) for i = 2:ny
+    ]
+    v_edges = [
+        Rectangle(
+            Point(r.ll.x + (i - 1) * tile_size, r.ll.y),
+            Point(r.ll.x + (i - 1) * tile_size, r.ur.y)
+        ) for i = 2:nx
+    ]
+    return tiles, vcat(h_edges, v_edges) # Edges could be used for healing
+end
+
+function _auto_tile_size(bnds::Rectangle, num_ents)
+    target_ents_per_tile = 100
+    target_num_tiles = max(1.0, round(num_ents / target_ents_per_tile))
+    target_size = sqrt(width(bnds) * height(bnds) / target_num_tiles)
+    # Return the closest tile size that evenly divides width
+    return width(bnds) / max(1.0, round(width(bnds) / target_size))
+end
+
+"""
+    function clip_tiled(
+        op,
+        ents1::AbstractArray{<:GeometryEntity{T}},
+        ents2::AbstractArray{<:GeometryEntity{T}},
+        tile_size=nothing;
+        pfs=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive,
+        pfc=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive
+    )
+
+Return a lazy iterator that applies `op(ents1, ents2)` tile by tile.
+
+The bounds of the combined geometries are tiled with squares with edge length `tile_size`, starting at the bottom left
+corner. Entities crossing between tiles are split into their intersections with each tile before clipping.
+For each tile, those intersection results and all entities inside that tile are selected.
+The return value is a lazy iterator over clipping results for selected entities per tile.
+
+A rough guideline for choosing tile size is to aim for 100 polygons per tile, but you may want to
+benchmark your use case. If an explicit tile size is not provided, then tile size will be set automatically
+based on the total number of entities in the operation, such that there is about one square tile per 100 entities.
+"""
+function clip_tiled(
+    op,
+    ents1::AbstractArray{<:GeometryEntity{T}},
+    ents2::AbstractArray{<:GeometryEntity{T}},
+    tile_size=nothing;
+    pfs=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive,
+    pfc=Clipper.PolyFillTypePositive
+) where {T}
+    (isempty(ents1) && isempty(ents2)) &&
+        return Iterators.map(identity, ClippedPolygon{T}[])
+    # Create spatial index for each set of polygons
+    if isempty(ents2)
+        tree1 = DeviceLayout.mbr_spatial_index(ents1)
+        bnds = mbr(tree1)
+    elseif isempty(ents1)
+        tree2 = DeviceLayout.mbr_spatial_index(ents2)
+        bnds = mbr(tree2)
+    else
+        tree1 = DeviceLayout.mbr_spatial_index(ents1)
+        tree2 = DeviceLayout.mbr_spatial_index(ents2)
+        bnds = SpatialIndexing.combine(mbr(tree1), mbr(tree2))
+    end
+
+    # Get tiles and indices of polygons intersecting tiles
+    bnds_dl = Rectangle(
+        Point(bnds.low...) * DeviceLayout.onemicron(T),
+        Point(bnds.high...) * DeviceLayout.onemicron(T)
+    )
+
+    if isnothing(tile_size)
+        tile_size = _auto_tile_size(bnds_dl, length(ents1) + length(ents2))
+    end
+
+    tiles, edges = tiles_and_edges(bnds_dl, tile_size) # DeviceLayout Rectangles
+    # Get single vector of all entity indices touching any edge
+    edge_touching_idx1 = Set( # Use Set because we'll be testing membership
+        mapreduce(vcat, edges, init=Int[]) do edge
+            return isempty(ents1) ? Int[] : DeviceLayout.findbox(edge, tree1; intersects=true)
+        end
+    )
+    # Same for ents2
+    edge_touching_idx2 = Set(
+        mapreduce(vcat, edges, init=Int[]) do edge
+            return isempty(ents2) ? Int[] : DeviceLayout.findbox(edge, tree2; intersects=true)
+        end
+    )
+    # Get vector of (ents1 indices, ents2 indices) for each tile
+    tile_poly_indices = map(tiles) do tile
+        idx1 = isempty(ents1) ? Int[] : DeviceLayout.findbox(tile, tree1; intersects=true)
+        idx2 =
+            isempty(ents2) ? Int[] : DeviceLayout.findbox(tile, tree2; intersects=true)
+        return (idx1, idx2)
+    end
+    # Clip within each tile
+    res = Iterators.map(enumerate(tile_poly_indices)) do (tile_idx, poly_idxs)
+        idx1, idx2 = poly_idxs
+        # If an entity is touching a tile edge, clip it to the tile with intersect2d
+        idx1_on_edge = in.(idx1, Ref(edge_touching_idx1))
+        idx2_on_edge = in.(idx2, Ref(edge_touching_idx2))
+        edge_idx1 = idx1[idx1_on_edge]
+        bulk_idx1 = idx1[(!).(idx1_on_edge)]
+        edge_idx2 = idx2[idx2_on_edge]
+        bulk_idx2 = idx2[(!).(idx2_on_edge)]
+        tile = tiles[tile_idx]
+        ents1_clipped_to_tile =
+            vcat(ents1[bulk_idx1], intersect2d(tile, ents1[edge_idx1]))
+        ents2_clipped_to_tile =
+            vcat(ents2[bulk_idx2], intersect2d(tile, ents2[edge_idx2]))
+        return clip(op, ents1_clipped_to_tile, ents2_clipped_to_tile; pfs, pfc)
+    end
+    return res
+end
+
 end # module
