+# SWE-rebench target test runner for the 2D Boolean interface issue.
+# Runs each target test file in its own Julia process (fresh, hermetic) to avoid
+# cross-file Unitful ContextUnits promotion contamination. Each per-file script
+# is in test/rebench_targets/ and uses the documented @run_package_tests filter.
+const SCRIPTS = [
+    "run_clipping.jl",
+    "run_bspline.jl",
+    "run_render.jl",
+    "run_shapes.jl",
+    "run_tests.jl",
+]
+const DIR = @__DIR__
+const PROJ = dirname(DIR)
+# The task image may start with only production dependencies instantiated.
+# Install the test runner and test-only packages before launching child scripts.
+using Pkg
+Pkg.activate(PROJ; io=devnull)
+Pkg.add(["TestItemRunner", "Aqua", "Test"]; io=devnull)
+# Keep each hermetic child process from monopolizing too much time: kill the
+# child (and report the failure) once its timeout expires.
+const CHILD_TIMEOUT = get(ENV, "REBENCH_CHILD_TIMEOUT", "1800") # seconds
+failed = String[]
+for s in SCRIPTS
+    script = joinpath(DIR, "rebench_targets", s)
+    println("="^72)
+    println("### $s")
+    println("="^72)
+    cmd = `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=60 $CHILD_TIMEOUT $(Base.julia_cmd()) --project=$PROJ $script`
+    p = run(ignorestatus(cmd))
+    success(p) || push!(failed, s)
+end
+println()
+println("="^72)
+if isempty(failed)
+    println("ALL TARGET TEST ITEMS PASSED")
+else
+    println("FAILED: ", join(failed, ", "))
+    error("rebench target tests failed: $(join(failed, ", "))")
+end

+@testitem "Layerwise clipping" setup = [CommonTestSetup] begin
+    c1 = CoordinateSystem("test1")
+    c2 = CoordinateSystem("test2")
+    r1 = Rectangle(10μm, 10μm)
+    r2 = r1 + Point(5μm, 5μm)
+    overlap = intersect2d(r1, r2)
+    x = xor2d(r1, r2)
+    d1 = difference2d(r1, r2)
+    d2 = difference2d(r2, r1)
+    uni = union2d(r1, r2)
+    lyr_a = SemanticMeta(:a)
+    lyr_b = SemanticMeta(:b)
+    place!(c1, r1, lyr_a)
+    place!(c1, r2, lyr_b)
+    place!(c2, r1, lyr_b)
+    place!(c2, r2, lyr_a)
+
+    # The per-layer value is "the clipping results for that layer"; its container
+    # type, length, and element types are not part of the contract, so compare
+    # only the geometry it represents. `_per_layer_results` and
+    # `_tiled_layer_results` (defined in `CommonTestSetup`) adapt any valid
+    # per-layer clipping-results container into a vector of first-class clipping
+    # results, which can then be compared geometrically via `xor2d` +
+    # `to_polygons`.
+    same_result = safe_layerwise(Symbol("xor2d_layerwise"), c1, c1)
+    same = isnothing(same_result) ? nothing : _per_layer_results(same_result[lyr_a])
+    @test !isnothing(same) && geometrically_equal(same, same) # self-xor is empty
+    for lyr in (lyr_a, lyr_b)
+        xor_result = safe_layerwise(Symbol("xor2d_layerwise"), c1, c2)
+        diff_result = safe_layerwise(Symbol("difference2d_layerwise"), c1, c2)
+        @test !isnothing(xor_result) && geometrically_equal(xor_result[lyr], x)
+        @test !isnothing(diff_result) && geometrically_equal(diff_result[lyr], lyr == lyr_a ? d1 : d2)
+    end
+    union_result = safe_layerwise(Symbol("union2d_layerwise"), c1, c2)
+    intersect_result = safe_layerwise(Symbol("intersect2d_layerwise"), c1, c2)
+    @test !isnothing(union_result) && geometrically_equal(union_result[lyr_a], uni)
+    @test !isnothing(intersect_result) && geometrically_equal(intersect_result[lyr_b], overlap)
+
+    # Every layerwise entry point returns a Dict with every participating layer,
+    # and each operation is checked independently on both layers.
+    layerwise_ops = (
+        (:union2d_layerwise, uni),
+        (:difference2d_layerwise, nothing),
+        (:intersect2d_layerwise, overlap),
+        (:xor2d_layerwise, x),
+    )
+    for (layerwise_name, symmetric_expected) in layerwise_ops
+        layerwise_op = try_call(() -> getproperty(DeviceLayout, layerwise_name))
+        result = safe_layerwise(layerwise_op, c1, c2)
+        @test result isa Dict
+        if result isa Dict
+            @test Set(keys(result)) == Set([lyr_a, lyr_b])
+            if layerwise_name === :difference2d_layerwise
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_a], d1)
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_b], d2)
+            elseif layerwise_name === :intersect2d_layerwise
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_a], overlap)
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_b], overlap)
+            else
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_a], symmetric_expected)
+                @test geometrically_equal(result[lyr_b], symmetric_expected)
+            end
+        end
+    end
+
+    # Also cover the required complete key set when a layer occurs on only one

+    place!(one_sided_tool, r2, lyr_b)

+    cs2 = CoordinateSystem("test2m")

+@testitem "Spatial queries with structures and references" setup = [CommonTestSetup] begin
+    using DeviceLayout.PreferredUnits: μm as pμm
+    lyr_a = SemanticMeta(:a)
+    qbig = Rectangle(100pμm, 100pμm)
+    qsmall = Rectangle(20pμm, 20pμm)
+
+    # Structures are accepted as query elements, using their bounds: a contained
+    # structure matches by default and with intersects; a non-contained structure
+    # that overlaps the query interior matches only with intersects=true.
+    s_inner = CoordinateSystem("inner_struct")
+    place!(s_inner, Rectangle(10pμm, 10pμm) + Point(2pμm, 2pμm), lyr_a)
+    s_inner2 = CoordinateSystem("inner_struct2")
+    place!(s_inner2, Rectangle(14pμm, 14pμm) + Point(3pμm, 3pμm), lyr_a)
+    s_part = CoordinateSystem("partial_struct")
+    place!(s_part, Rectangle(30pμm, 10pμm) + Point(10pμm, 20pμm), lyr_a)
+    @test checked_findbox(qsmall, [s_inner, s_part]) == [1]
+    @test sort(checked_findbox(qsmall, [s_inner, s_part]; intersects=true)) == [1, 2]
+
+    # References are also accepted as query elements; their (transformed) bounds
+    # are used for containment and intersection.
+    r_inner1 = sref(s_inner)
+    r_inner2 = sref(s_inner2)
+    # This reference begins exactly at the query boundary, so it touches but
+    # does not overlap the query box.
+    r_touch_big = sref(s_inner, Point(98pμm, 0pμm))
+    @test sort(checked_findbox(qbig, [r_inner1, r_inner2, r_touch_big])) == [1, 2]
+    @test sort(checked_findbox(qbig, [r_inner1, r_inner2, r_touch_big]; intersects=true)) ==
+          [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # A geometry entity can serve as the query; its bounds determine the same
+    # containment and edge-touching selections as the equivalent rectangle.
+    qpoly = convert(Polygon, qbig)
+    @test checked_findbox(qpoly, [r_inner1, r_inner2, r_touch_big]) == [1, 2]
+    @test sort(checked_findbox(qpoly, [r_inner1, r_inner2, r_touch_big]; intersects=true)) ==
+          [1, 2, 3]
+
+    r_touch_small = sref(s_inner, Point(18pμm, 0pμm))
+    @test isempty(checked_findbox(qsmall, [r_touch_small]))
+    @test checked_findbox(qsmall, [r_touch_small]; intersects=true) == [1]
+
+    # Structures and references can be queried together with plain entities.
+    ent = Rectangle(10pμm, 10pμm) + Point(1pμm, 1pμm)
+    @test sort(checked_findbox(qsmall, [s_inner, ent, r_inner1])) == [1, 2, 3]
 end

problem_statement:
generate shell completion from specs
I'm curious how hard this would be.
Maybe have a special flag --complete that takes a partial command line and returns the list of completions to the shell.

### Additional contract requirements

# Shell completions for `dispatch` CLIs

## Completion command protocol

When the first argument to `babashka.cli/dispatch` is the command name
`org.babashka.cli/completions`, the dispatch request is handled as a
completion request instead of the normal command dispatch: no command handler
is invoked and the application's own arguments are not validated. The second
argument selects the action:

- `complete --shell <shell> [--fresh <true|false>] -- <words...>`: prints one
  completion candidate per line for the word list after `--`. The shell name
  selects shell-specific formatting concerns (for example, a PowerShell
  completion request cannot pass a trailing empty word and uses `--fresh true`
  to signal that the cursor sits on a fresh word, and a bash word list may
  arrive with an option's `--opt=val` token split by the shell into separate
  `--opt`, `=` and `val` words). The final word after `--` is the partial word
  being completed; an empty final word asks for candidates at a fresh
  position. Each non-empty line is the candidate value, and, when the
  candidate has a description, a tab character followed by the description.
  Candidates without a description are printed as the bare value with no
  trailing tab. Descriptions of subcommand candidates come from the table
  entry's `:doc`; descriptions of option candidates come from the spec
  entry's `:desc`, and a short alias carries the description of its option.
  Descriptions cannot make a line ambiguous: values and descriptions have
  tabs and newlines removed or folded to spaces (a multi-line description is
  reduced to its first line) before printing.
- `snippet --shell <shell> [--prog <name>]`: prints to stdout a ready-to-use
  registration snippet for that shell, one of `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`,
  `powershell` or `nushell`. The snippet registers completion for the
  `dispatch` `:prog` name (or the `--prog` override, e.g. for a renamed
  binary) and wires the shell's TAB key to the `complete` action above. An
  unrecognized shell name, or a program name that is not a plain command
  name (only alphanumeric characters, `.`, `_` and `-`), yields no snippet
  on stdout.

## Completion candidates

Completion knows subcommand names, option names (long forms and short
aliases), and option values:

- Subcommands and options complete by prefix at the position where they
  occur, including nested subcommand levels. Options declared at dispatch
  level, and spec options flagged `:inherit true`, are offered at subcommand
  levels as well.
- An option that has been used is not suggested again, unless it takes
  multiple values (`:coerce [<type>]` or `:collect`), and a `:default` value
  does not count as a use. Negated forms (`--no-foo`) and boolean options
  (`:coerce :boolean`, `:bool` or `[:boolean]`) take no following value, so
  after typing one the next position completes options again.
- An option's value completes from, in order of precedence: a `:complete`
  collection of candidate strings (or `{:value <s> :description <s>}` maps,
  whose descriptions are surfaced like option descriptions); a set-valued
  `:validate`, whose members double as value candidates (keyword members
  complete by their namespaced name); a `:complete-fn` callback, which is
  invoked with the partial value in `:to-complete` and the options parsed so
  far in `:opts` and returns candidate values (or value/description maps).
  All sources are prefix-filtered against the partial value. Candidates for
  an `--opt=val` word are printed as full `--opt=val` words.
- A value position without any of the above emits the line
  `org.babashka.cli/file-completion`, which instructs the shell snippet to
  fall back to the shell's own file completion. `:complete false` on a spec
  entry opts a value out of that file fallback, producing no candidates.
- Positional arguments declared with `:args->opts` complete like the
  corresponding option: with the option's value candidates, or file
  completion / an opted-out empty result otherwise. After a literal `--`
  word, only positional candidates complete.

Completion never fails the request on unparseable or unknown input: partial
words are not coerced or validated, and unknown options simply yield no (or
file) candidates. Option visibility follows the same rule as `--help`:
spec options and subcommands marked `:no-doc` are not suggested.

## Auto-generated help

In the help printed for a command, an option with `:no-doc true` is hidden,
like a `:no-doc` subcommand, while still parsing normally. When a command has
no visible options, its help output does not contain a dangling, empty
`Options:` section.

## Long options carrying a value

A long option word may carry its value as `--opt=value`: the word is split
at its first `=`, and the remainder of the word is the option's value, even
when that remainder is empty or itself contains `=`. A word in this form is
self-contained: it does not consume the following command-line word.

test_patch:
diff --git a/test/babashka/cli/completion_test.cljc b/test/babashka/cli/completion_test.cljc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2527b8d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/babashka/cli/completion_test.cljc
@@ -0,0 +1,661 @@
+(ns babashka.cli.completion-test
+  (:require
+   [babashka.cli :as cli]
+   [clojure.string :as str]
+   [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]))
+
+;; The public, user-facing completion interface is the hidden
+;; `org.babashka.cli/completions complete` subcommand that `cli/dispatch`
+;; installs: it prints one candidate per line as `value<TAB>description`, or
+;; the literal sentinel `org.babashka.cli/file-completion` to defer to the
+;; shell's own file completion. These helpers drive that public command with
+;; shell-tokenized words (the tokens a shell stub would pass after `--`) and
+;; return the candidate value strings, so the tests exercise only public API.
+;;
+;; NOTE: the evaluation harness selects individual test vars
+;; (babashka.cli.completion-test/inherit-completion-test,
+;; babashka.cli.completion-test/all-no-doc-help-test and
+;; babashka.cli-test/equals-value-test), so the completion regression suite
+;; below lives under `testing` blocks inside those selected vars to guarantee
+;; the harness actually executes every assertion.
+
+(defn- completion-lines
+  ([table args] (completion-lines table args nil))
+  ([table args dispatch-opts]
+   (->> (with-out-str
+          (cli/dispatch table
+                        (into ["org.babashka.cli/completions" "complete" "--shell" "zsh" "--"] args)
+                        (merge {:prog "myprogram"} dispatch-opts)))
+        str/split-lines
+        (remove str/blank?))))
+
+;; complete the words `args` against a dispatch `table`
+(defn complete
+  ([table args] (complete table args nil))
+  ([table args dispatch-opts]
+   (mapv #(first (str/split % #"\t" 2)) (completion-lines table args dispatch-opts))))
+
+;; complete against a single option-map (a command with no subcommands)
+(defn complete-options [opts args]
+  (complete [(assoc opts :cmds [])] args))
+
+;; an unconfigured value position defers to the shell's own file completion,
+;; signaled by the public `org.babashka.cli/file-completion` sentinel line
+(defn- files? [table args]
+  (some #{"org.babashka.cli/file-completion"} (completion-lines table args)))
+
+(defn- files-options? [opts args]
+  (files? [(assoc opts :cmds [])] args))
+
+;; drive the hidden `org.babashka.cli/completions` group: `snippet` prints the
+;; install snippet, `complete` completes the shell-tokenized words after `--`. The
+;; stub passes tokens; here we stand in for the shell by splitting the test line
+;; (dropping the program name, keeping a trailing empty for a fresh word).
+(defn- line->tokens [line]
+  (vec (rest (str/split (str/triml line) #" +" -1))))
+
+(defn- complete-via-cmd [table opts line]
+  (with-out-str
+    (cli/dispatch table (into ["org.babashka.cli/completions" "complete" "--shell" "zsh" "--"]
+                              (line->tokens line))
+                  opts)))
+
+(defn- snippet-via-cmd [table opts shell & extra]
+  (with-out-str
+    (cli/dispatch table (into ["org.babashka.cli/completions" "snippet" "--shell" shell] extra) opts)))
+
+(def cmd-table
+  [{:cmds ["foo"] :spec {:foo-opt {:coerce :string
+                                   :alias :f
+                                   :desc "The foo option"}
+                         :foo-opt2 {:coerce :string}
+                         :foo-flag {:coerce :bool ; :bool and :boolean both accepted
+                                    :alias :l
+                                    :desc "Enable foo"}}}
+   {:cmds ["foo" "bar"] :spec {:bar-opt {:coerce :keyword}
+                               :bar-flag {:coerce :boolean}}}
+   {:cmds ["bar"] :doc "The bar command"}
+   {:cmds ["bar-baz"]}])
+
+(def opts {:spec {:aopt {:alias :a
+                         :coerce :string}
+                  :aopt2 {:coerce :string
+                          :validate #{"aval2"}}
+                  :bflag {:alias :b
+                          :coerce :boolean}}})
+
+(defn- complete-out
+  "Run the completion handler for `cmdline` and return its emitted
+  `value\\tdescription` lines as a set of strings."
+  [cmdline]
+  (->> (complete-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "myprogram"} cmdline)
+       str/split-lines
+       (remove str/blank?)
+       set))
+
+(deftest inherit-completion-test
+  (let [t [{:cmds [] :fn identity :spec {:verbose {:coerce :boolean :inherit true}}}
+           {:cmds ["sub"] :fn identity :spec {:opt {}}}]]
+    (testing "inherited options are offered at subcommand levels"
+      (is (= #{"--opt" "--verbose"} (set (complete t ["sub" "--"])))))
+    (testing "a typed inherited flag is recognized as a flag"
+      (is (= #{"--opt"} (set (complete t ["sub" "--verbose" "--"]))))))
+  (testing "dispatch-level :inherit true"
+    (is (= #{"--env"}
+           (set (complete [{:cmds [] :spec {:env {}}}
+                           {:cmds ["sub"] :fn identity}]
+                          ["sub" "--"]
+                          {:inherit true})))))
+
+  (testing "complete-options-test"
+    ;; candidates completing a word match it by prefix; whether the matched
+    ;; word is offered again when the word equals it exactly (inclusive) or
+    ;; counts as already typed (strict) is an implementation choice, so the
+    ;; exact-full-word assertions below accept both candidate sets
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--aopt2" "--bflag" "-b" "-a"} (set (complete-options opts [""]))))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--aopt2" "--bflag" "-b" "-a"} (set (complete-options opts ["-"]))))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--aopt2" "--bflag"} (set (complete-options opts ["--"]))))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--aopt2"} (set (complete-options opts ["--a"]))))
+    (is (= #{"--bflag"} (set (complete-options opts ["--b"]))))
+    (is (#{#{} #{"--bflag"}} (set (complete-options opts ["--bflag"]))))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--aopt2" "-a"} (set (complete-options opts ["--bflag" ""]))))
+    (testing "an unconfigured option value defaults to file completion"
+      (is (files-options? opts ["--aopt" ""]))
+      (is (files-options? opts ["--aopt" "aval"])))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt2" "--bflag" "-b"} (set (complete-options opts ["--aopt" "aval" ""]))))
+    (is (= #{"--aopt" "--bflag" "-b" "-a"} (set (complete-options opts ["--aopt2" "aval2" ""]))))
+    (testing "an option-looking word while a value position is open never fails the request"
+      ;; No candidate shape is specified for an option-looking partial value,
+      ;; but the completion request must still be handled without an error.
+      (is (try
+            (completion-lines [(assoc opts :cmds [])] ["--aopt" "-"])
+            true
+            (catch #?(:clj Exception :cljs :default) _ false))))
+    (testing "completing a prefix that is itself a full option still offers the longer one"
+      (is (#{#{"--aopt2"} #{"--aopt" "--aopt2"}} (set (complete-options opts ["--aopt"])))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "completion-test"
+    (testing "complete commands"
+      (is (= #{"foo" "bar" "bar-baz"} (set (complete cmd-table [""]))))
+      (is (= #{"bar" "bar-baz"} (set (complete cmd-table ["ba"]))))
+      (is (#{#{"bar-baz"} #{"bar" "bar-baz"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["bar"]))))
+      (is (= #{"foo"} (set (complete cmd-table ["f"])))))
+
+    (testing "no completions for full command"
+      (is (#{#{} #{"foo"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo"])))))
+
+    (testing "complete subcommands and options"
+      (is (= #{"bar" "-f" "--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2" "-l" "--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" ""])))))
+
+    (testing "complete suboption"
+      (is (= #{"-f" "--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2" "-l" "--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "-"])))))
+
+    (testing "completing an option's value: files without :complete, and the partial is not mis-read as an option/number/keyword/boolean"
+      (is (#{#{} #{"-f"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "-f"]))))
+      (is (files? cmd-table ["foo" "-f" "123"]))
+      (is (let [ls (completion-lines cmd-table ["foo" "-f" ":foo"])]
+             (or (some #{"org.babashka.cli/file-completion"} ls)
+                 (every? #(str/starts-with? % ":") ls))))
+      (is (files? cmd-table ["foo" "-f" "true"]))
+      (testing "value consumed, the next token completes options again"
+        (is (= #{"bar" "--foo-opt2" "-l" "--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "-f" "foo-val" ""]))))))
+
+    (testing "complete option with same prefix"
+      (is (= #{"--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2" "--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo"]))))
+      (is (#{#{"--foo-opt2"} #{"--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-opt"])))))
+
+    (testing "the long --opt form awaits a value the same way (shares the option-key path)"
+      (is (files? cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-opt" ""]))
+      (is (= #{"bar" "--foo-opt2" "-l" "--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-opt" "foo-val" ""])))))
+
+    (is (= #{"--foo-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-f"]))))
+
+    (testing "complete short flag"
+      (is (#{#{} #{"-l"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "-l"]))))
+      (is (= #{"bar" "-f" "--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "-l" ""])))))
+
+    (testing "complete long flag"
+      (is (#{#{} #{"--foo-flag"}} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag"]))))
+      (is (= #{"bar" "-f" "--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" ""])))))
+
+    (is (= #{"-f" "--foo-opt" "--foo-opt2"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "-"]))))
+    (is (= #{"bar"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "b"]))))
+
+    (testing "complete subcommand"
+      (is (= #{"--bar-opt" "--bar-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" ""]))))
+      (is (= #{"--bar-opt" "--bar-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "-"]))))
+      (is (= #{"--bar-opt" "--bar-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "--"]))))
+      (is (= #{"--bar-opt" "--bar-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "--bar-"]))))
+      (is (= #{"--bar-opt"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "--bar-o"]))))
+      (is (files? cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "--bar-opt" "a"]))
+      (is (= #{"--bar-flag"} (set (complete cmd-table ["foo" "--foo-flag" "bar" "--bar-opt" "bar-val" ""])))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "dispatch-completion-test"
+    (testing "output is shell-agnostic value<TAB>description data"
+      (is (= #{"foo"} (complete-out "myprogram f"))))
+    (testing "descriptions: subcommand :doc and option :desc are surfaced"
+      (is (= #{"bar\tThe bar command" "bar-baz"} (complete-out "myprogram ba")))
+      (is (= #{"--foo-opt\tThe foo option" "--foo-opt2" "--foo-flag\tEnable foo"}
+             (complete-out "myprogram foo --foo")))
+      (testing "short-option aliases carry the long option's description"
+        (is (= #{"--foo-opt\tThe foo option" "--foo-opt2" "--foo-flag\tEnable foo"
+                 "-f\tThe foo option" "-l\tEnable foo"}
+               (complete-out "myprogram foo -"))))
+      (testing "options with no :desc come out as a bare value (no trailing tab)"
+        ;; --foo-opt2 above appears as bare \"--foo-opt2\", proving the no-desc case
+        (is (contains? (complete-out "myprogram foo --foo") "--foo-opt2"))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "value-completion-test"
+    (testing ":complete as a static coll of strings"
+      (let [o {:spec {:env {:coerce :string :complete ["dev" "prod"]}}}]
+        (is (= #{"dev" "prod"} (set (complete-options o ["--env" ""]))))
+        (testing "prefix-filtered against the partial value"
+          (is (= #{"prod"} (set (complete-options o ["--env" "pr"])))))))
+    (testing ":complete coll of {:value :description} maps surfaces descriptions"
+      (let [t [{:cmds []
+                :spec {:env {:coerce :string
+                             :complete [{:value "dev" :description "Development"}
+                                        {:value "prod" :description "Production"}]}}}]]
+        (is (= #{"dev\tDevelopment" "prod\tProduction"}
+               (->> (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "deploy"} "deploy --env ")
+                    str/split-lines (remove str/blank?) set)))))
+    (testing "set-valued :validate auto-completes its values (keywords -> names)"
+      (is (= #{"a" "b"}
+             (set (complete-options {:spec {:mode {:coerce :keyword :validate #{:a :b}}}}
+                                    ["--mode" ""])))))
+    (testing ":complete-fn receives :to-complete and parsed :opts (dependent completion)"
+      (let [spec {:from {:coerce :string :complete ["x" "y"]}
+                  :to {:coerce :string
+                       :complete-fn (fn [{:keys [opts]}]
+                                      (when (= "x" (:from opts)) ["x1" "x2"]))}}]
+        (is (= #{"x1" "x2"} (set (complete-options {:spec spec} ["--from" "x" "--to" ""]))))
+        (testing "fn returns nothing when its dependency is absent"
+          ;; a nil-returning :complete-fn is ambiguous between "no candidates"
+          ;; and "no configured source"; both empty output and the documented
+          ;; file-completion fallback are contract-valid
+          (let [lines (complete-options {:spec spec} ["--to" ""])]
+            (is (or (empty? lines)
+                    (= ["org.babashka.cli/file-completion"] lines)))))))
+    (testing ":complete-fn output is prefix-filtered by the lib (powershell has no shell-side filter)"
+      ;; the fn returns an UNFILTERED list; the lib must filter it against the partial
+      (let [o {:spec {:env {:coerce :string
+                            :complete-fn (constantly ["dev" "staging" "prod"])}}}]
+        (is (= #{"dev" "staging" "prod"} (set (complete-options o ["--env" ""]))))
+        (is (= #{"staging"} (set (complete-options o ["--env" "st"]))))))
+    (testing "no :complete/:complete-fn/:validate -> the shell's file completion"
+      (is (files-options? {:spec {:env {:coerce :string}}} ["--env" ""])))
+    (testing ":complete false opts out of the file default"
+      (is (empty? (completion-lines [{:cmds [] :spec {:msg {:complete false}}}]
+                                    ["--msg" ""]))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "repeatable-option-test"
+    (testing "a single-value option drops out once used"
+      (let [o {:spec {:env {:coerce :string} :verbose {:coerce :boolean}}}]
+        (is (= #{"--verbose"} (set (complete-options o ["--env" "x" ""]))))))
+    (testing "a list option (:coerce [...]) stays suggestable after use"
+      (let [o {:spec {:file {:coerce [:string]} :verbose {:coerce :boolean}}}]
+        (is (= #{"--file" "--verbose"} (set (complete-options o ["--file" "a" ""]))))))
+    (testing "a :collect option stays suggestable after use"
+      (let [o {:spec {:tag {:collect [] :coerce :string} :x {:coerce :boolean}}}]
+        (is (= #{"--tag" "--x"} (set (complete-options o ["--tag" "a" ""]))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "restrict-completion-test"
+    ;; completion works under :restrict: it is env-driven and ignores args, and the
+    ;; internal completion parse does not inherit :restrict, so partial/in-progress
+    ;; input never throws on "unknown option"
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+              :spec {:env {:coerce :string} :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]
+          vals (fn [cmdline]
+                 (->> (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "p" :restrict true} cmdline)
+                      str/split-lines
+                      (remove str/blank?)
+                      (map #(first (str/split % #"\t")))
+                      set))]
+      (is (= #{"deploy"} (vals "p de")))
+      (is (= #{"--env" "--force"} (vals "p deploy --")))
+      (testing "a consumed option drops out, no throw despite :restrict"
+        (is (= #{"--force"} (vals "p deploy --env x --")))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "namespaced-keyword-value-test"
+    ;; kw->str keeps the namespace; name would drop it
+    (let [o {:spec {:k {:coerce :keyword :validate #{:a.b/local :a.b/global}}}}]
+      (is (= #{"a.b/local" "a.b/global"} (set (complete-options o ["--k" ""]))))
+      (is (= #{"a.b/local"} (set (complete-options o ["--k" "a.b/lo"])))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "completion-robustness-test"
+    (testing "unknown --shell for the snippet: no crash, nothing on stdout"
+      (is (= "" (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "p"} "bogus"))))
+    (testing "an empty line completes the top level, no NPE"
+      (is (= #{"foo" "bar" "bar-baz"}
+             (->> (complete-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "p"} "")
+                  str/split-lines (remove str/blank?)
+                  (map #(first (str/split % #"\t"))) set))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "completion-prog-override-test"
+    ;; :prog selects the command the snippet registers completion up for, and
+    ;; --prog overrides it (e.g. for a renamed binary); the registered name is
+    ;; all the snippet may assume
+    (testing ":prog is the default registered name"
+      (is (str/includes? (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "squint"} "bash") "squint")))
+    (testing "--prog overrides :prog (renamed binary)"
+      (let [s (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "squint"} "bash" "--prog" "sq")]
+        (is (re-find #"(?m)\bsq\b" s))))
+    (testing "a dotted/hyphenated command name still registers"
+      (is (str/includes? (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "x"} "bash" "--prog" "node_cli.js")
+                         "node_cli.js")))
+  )
+
+  (testing "snippet-behavior-test"
+    (testing "the bash snippet registers the program name for TAB completion"
+      ;; any registration shape is fine (a helper function or an inline command);
+      ;; what the contract promises is a ready-to-use snippet that wires TAB for
+      ;; the program name to the complete action
+      (let [snippet (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "myprogram"} "bash")]
+        (testing "is non-empty and mentions the program name"
+          (is (not (str/blank? snippet)))
+          (is (str/includes? snippet "myprogram")))
+        (testing "invokes the completion protocol with the words on the command line"
+          (is (re-find #"org\.babashka\.cli/completions\s+complete\b" snippet)))
+        (testing "routes the file-completion sentinel to file completion"
+          (is (str/includes? snippet "file-completion"))
+          (is (re-find #"compgen|-o\s+filenames|__files|_files" snippet)))
+        (testing "registers completion for the program name"
+          ;; any command shape is fine (the bash `complete` builtin, an alias
+          ;; such as `compdef`, ...) as long as the registration is for the
+          ;; program name
+          (is (re-find #"(?m)(^|[\s'\"])myprogram([\s'\"]|$)" snippet)))))
+    ;; every advertised shell registers completion for the requested program,
+    ;; drives the completion protocol command, and passes candidates and the
+    ;; file-completion sentinel through to the shell
+    (doseq [shell ["bash" "zsh" "fish" "powershell" "nushell"]]
+      (testing shell
+        (let [s (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "myprogram"} shell)]
+          (testing "is non-empty"
+            (is (not (str/blank? s))))
+          (testing "registers completion for the :prog name"
+            (is (str/includes? s "myprogram")))
+          (testing "invokes the completion protocol"
+            ;; whitespace- and quoting-tolerant: a snippet may pass the
+            ;; command as one quoted argument, e.g. powershell's
+            ;; `'org.babashka.cli/completions' 'complete'`
+            (is (re-find #"org\.babashka\.cli/completions[\s,'\"]+complete\b" s)))
+          (testing "passes its shell to the complete action"
+            (is (re-find (re-pattern (str "--shell[\\s,'\"]+" shell "\\b")) s)))
+          (testing "handles the file-completion sentinel"
+            (is (str/includes? s "file-completion"))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "nushell-context-forwarding-test"
+    ;; At a nested command and a partial option value, Nushell must send the
+    ;; words preceding the cursor to the completion protocol, not just ask for
+    ;; top-level candidates. The snippet may name its words however it likes
+    ;; (a spread of $spans, a derived list, a named completer); the protocol
+    ;; call must be followed by `--` and then the words after it.
+    (let [snippet (snippet-via-cmd
+                   [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+                     :spec {:region {:complete ["us-east" "us-west"]}}}]
+                   {:prog "myprogram"} "nushell")]
+      (is (re-find #"(?s)org\.babashka\.cli/completions[\s'\"]+complete[^\n]*--[ \t]+[^\s)\"']" snippet))))
+
+  (testing "positional-after-literal-dash-dash-test"
+    ;; after a literal `--` every word is positional, so an option-looking word
+    ;; such as `--env=us` is a value for the positional, not an attached option
+    ;; value; with no positional value matching it, nothing `--env=...` is offered
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :args->opts [:env]
+              :spec {:env {:complete ["us-east" "us-west"]}}}]]
+      (is (not-any? #(str/starts-with? % "--env=")
+                    (complete t ["deploy" "--" "--env=us"])))
+      (is (not-any? #(str/starts-with? % "--env=")
+                    (complete t ["deploy" "--" "--env="])))
+      (testing "the positional still completes plain values after --"
+        (is (= #{"us-east"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--" "us-e"]))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "nushell-tab-split-test"
+    ;; the protocol separates a candidate's value from its description with a
+    ;; TAB character, so the ready-to-use Nushell snippet must split each line at
+    ;; an actual TAB. Accepted spellings of a TAB in Nushell: a double-quoted
+    ;; string with the \t escape, the \u{9} escape, a (char ...) call that
+    ;; yields TAB, or a literal TAB. A backtick string such as `char tab` is a
+    ;; plain word in Nushell, not a TAB.
+    (let [snippet (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "myprogram"} "nushell")]
+      (is (re-find #"\"[^\"\n]*\\t[^\"\n]*\"|\\u\{0*9\}|\(\s*char\s+(?:tab\b|-u\s+['\"]?0*9\b|--unicode\s+['\"]?0*9\b|-i\s+9\b|--integer\s+9\b)|\t" snippet))))
+
+  (testing "positional-completion-test"
+    ;; :args->opts maps positionals to spec keys, so a positional completes that
+    ;; key's values (the same :complete / :validate the option form uses)
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :args->opts [:env :region]
+              :spec {:env {:complete ["dev" "prod"]}
+                     :region {:validate #{:us :eu}}
+                     :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]]
+      (testing "first positional completes its :complete values"
+        (is (= #{"prod"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "pr"])))))
+      (testing "second positional completes the next key's set :validate"
+        (is (= #{"eu"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "dev" "e"])))))
+      (testing "a flag among the args does not count as a positional (index unshifted)"
+        (is (= #{"prod"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--force" "pr"])))))
+      (testing "after a literal -- the positional still completes its values"
+        (is (= #{"prod"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--" "pr"])))))
+      (testing "no positional candidates past the :args->opts mapping"
+        (is (= #{} (set (complete t ["deploy" "dev" "us" "x"]))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "positional-file-completion-test"
+    ;; a declared positional with no value completion -> file-completion marker line,
+    ;; which the stub turns into the shell's own file completer
+    (let [marker "org.babashka.cli/file-completion"
+          t [{:cmds ["cat"] :args->opts [:file] :spec {:v {:coerce :boolean}}}]
+          lines (fn [line] (set (str/split-lines (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "p"} line))))]
+      (testing "positional with no value-config emits the marker"
+        (is (contains? (lines "p cat ") marker)))
+      (testing "completing an option does not emit the marker"
+        (is (not (contains? (lines "p cat --") marker))))
+      (testing "a positional with value-config completes values, not files"
+        (let [v [{:cmds ["deploy"] :args->opts [:env] :spec {:env {:complete ["dev"]}}}]]
+          (is (not (contains? (set (str/split-lines (complete-via-cmd v {:prog "p"} "p deploy ")))
+                              marker)))))
+      (testing ":complete false opts a positional out of the file default"
+        (let [v [{:cmds ["run"] :args->opts [:name] :spec {:name {:complete false}}}]]
+          (is (not (contains? (set (str/split-lines (complete-via-cmd v {:prog "p"} "p run ")))
+                              marker)))))
+      (testing "variadic :args->opts does not hang and emits the marker"
+        (let [v [{:cmds ["x"] :args->opts (cons :a (repeat :b))}]]
+          (is (contains? (set (str/split-lines (complete-via-cmd v {:prog "p"} "p x one two ")))
+                         marker))))
+      (testing "after a literal -- only positionals complete (no options, no commands)"
+        (is (= #{marker} (lines "p cat -- ")))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "no-doc-option-test"
+    ;; a :no-doc option still parses but is hidden from completion and --help, like a
+    ;; :no-doc subcommand is hidden from the command list
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+              :spec {:env {:coerce :string} :secret {:coerce :string :no-doc true :alias :s}}}]]
+      (testing "hidden from completion (long form and alias)"
+        (is (= #{"--env"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "-"])))))
+      (testing "hidden from --help"
+        (is (not (str/includes?
+                  (with-out-str (cli/dispatch t ["deploy" "--help"] {:prog "p" :help true}))
+                  "secret"))))
+      (testing "still parses"
+        (is (= {:secret "x"} (cli/parse-opts ["--secret" "x"] {:spec {:secret {:no-doc true}}})))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "description-sanitize-test"
+    ;; a newline/tab in a description must not break the value<TAB>desc wire protocol
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+              :doc "First line\nsecond line dropped"
+              :spec {:env {:coerce :string :desc "Tab\there" :complete ["dev"]}}}]]
+      (testing "newline in :doc is reduced to the first line"
+        (is (= #{"deploy\tFirst line"}
+               (->> (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "p"} "p dep") str/split-lines (remove str/blank?) set))))
+      (testing "tab in :desc is replaced with a space"
+        (is (contains? #{#{"--env\tTab here"} #{"--env\tTabhere"}}
+                       (->> (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "p"} "p deploy --e") str/split-lines (remove str/blank?) set)))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "equals-form-test"
+    ;; babashka.cli parses --opt=val, so completion handles it too. Candidates are
+    ;; emitted as full --opt=val words; shells then match and replace the whole
+    ;; current word or a wordbreak-split prefix of it
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"]
+              :spec {:env   {:coerce :string :complete ["dev" "prod"]}
+                     :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]]
+      (testing "value completion within the = token"
+        (is (= #{"--env=dev"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env=d"]))))
+        (is (= #{"--env=dev" "--env=prod"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env="])))))
+      (testing "a completed --opt=val does not consume the next token"
+        (is (= #{"--force"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env=dev" ""]))))
+        (testing "even when the value itself contains = (split happens at the first =)"
+          (is (= #{"--force"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env=dev=x" ""]))))))
+      (testing "the file fallback applies inside --opt= too (bare or wrapped sentinel)"
+        ;; empty is accepted as well: nothing valid completes this position
+        (let [u [{:cmds ["deploy"] :spec {:out {:coerce :string}}}]]
+          (is (#{#{}
+                 #{"org.babashka.cli/file-completion"}
+                 #{"--out=org.babashka.cli/file-completion"}}
+               (set (completion-lines u ["deploy" "--out="]))))))
+      (testing "bash wordbreak splitting (--opt = val may arrive as three words)"
+        ;; the snippet side of this contract is asserted for the golden bash
+        ;; snippet in snippet-behavior-test (COMP_WORDBREAKS stripping); on the
+        ;; protocol side, candidates for the value that follows the lone "="
+        ;; are printed as
+        ;; full --opt=val words; whether the lone "=" is collapsed back into
+        ;; the option word first or the split words are completed as-is is an
+        ;; implementation choice
+        (let [out (fn [& toks]
+                    (set (str/split-lines
+                          (with-out-str
+                            (cli/dispatch t (into ["org.babashka.cli/completions" "complete"
+                                                   "--shell" "bash" "--" "deploy"] toks)
+                                          {:prog "p"})))))]
+          ;; candidates for the value after the lone "=" may be printed either
+          ;; as full --opt=val words (the stub matches the wordbreak-split
+          ;; suffix) or -- like the --opt=val-token collapse -- as bare value
+          ;; candidates; both satisfy the emission rule for the value that
+          ;; follows the lone "="
+          (is (#{#{"--env=dev"} #{"dev"}} (out "--env" "=" "d")))
+          ;; with no partial value yet all values are candidates, emitted per
+          ;; the same word-style choice; completing the lone "=" as-is instead
+          ;; matches no candidate or, with inclusive prefix matching, itself
+          (is (#{#{"--env=dev" "--env=prod"}
+                 #{"dev" "prod"}
+                 #{}
+                 #{"="}}
+               (set (mapv #(first (str/split % #"\t" 2)) (out "--env" "="))))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "completion-bypass-test"
+    ;; completion of a request runs independently of the target command: no
+    ;; command handler is run, and neither the dispatch-level validation nor
+    ;; the application's own spec validation is applied to the partial words
+    ;; or to values the user already typed
+    (testing "the command handler is never invoked"
+      (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn (fn [_] (throw (ex-info "handler must not run" {})))
+                :spec {:env {:coerce :string}}}]]
+        (is (= #{"--env"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--"]))))))
+    (testing "the partial word being completed is not validated"
+      (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+                :spec {:env {:coerce :string
+                             :validate (fn [_] (throw (ex-info "validation must not run" {})))}
+                       :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]]
+        (is (files? t ["deploy" "--env" "prod"]))))
+    (testing "a typed value failing validation does not fail the request"
+      (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+                :spec {:env {:coerce :string :validate (constantly false)}
+                       :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]]
+        (is (= #{"--force"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env" "bad" ""]))))))
+    (testing "dispatch-level validators do not apply to the completion words"
+      (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+                :spec {:env {:coerce :string} :force {:coerce :boolean}}}]]
+        (is (= #{"--force"}
+               (set (complete t ["deploy" "--env" "bad" ""]
+                              {:validate {:env #{"dev"}}}))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "default-option-test"
+    ;; a :default value must not mark the option as already used
+    (let [o {:spec {:port {:default 8080} :host {}}}]
+      (is (= #{"--port" "--host"} (set (complete-options o ["--"])))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "require-completion-test"
+    (testing "a :require'd option does not disable used-option filtering"
+      (let [o {:spec {:level {:require true} :host {}}}]
+        (is (= #{"--level"} (set (complete-options o ["--host" "h" "--"]))))))
+    (testing "dispatch-level :require does not kill the completion callback"
+      (is (= #{"sub" "--env"}
+             (->> (complete-via-cmd [{:cmds ["sub"] :fn identity}]
+                                    {:require [:env] :spec {:env {}}}
+                                    "p ")
+                  str/split-lines (remove str/blank?) set))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "negation-completion-test"
+    ;; the parser accepts --no-foo as {:foo false}, consuming no value; completion
+    ;; must not treat it as an option awaiting a value
+    (let [o {:spec {:verbose {:coerce :boolean} :host {}}}]
+      (is (= #{"--host"} (set (complete-options o ["--no-verbose" ""])))))
+    (testing "typing the negated --no- form itself"
+      ;; negated forms take no following value (the contract groups --no-foo
+      ;; with boolean options), so "--no-verbose" is an option-like word and
+      ;; never opens :verbose's value position. The contracted candidates after
+      ;; a consumed negated form are the still-open options ("--host"); whether
+      ;; the negated form itself is re-offered as a partial word is an
+      ;; implementation choice.
+      (let [o {:spec {:verbose {:coerce :boolean} :host {}}}]
+        (is (not (files-options? o ["--no-verbose"])))
+        (is (#{#{} #{"--no-verbose"} #{"--host"} #{"--host" "--no-verbose"}}
+             (set (complete-options o ["--no-verbose"]))))
+      (testing "a bare --no prefix is not a recognized option word"
+        ;; "--no" is not spelled out as an option in the spec, so per the
+        ;; contract it yields no (or file) candidates; an implementation may
+        ;; also treat it as a partial option word, but it must never throw
+        (is (or (files-options? o ["--no"])
+                (contains? #{#{} #{"--host"}}
+                           (set (complete-options o ["--no"]))))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "coerce-vector-boolean-test"
+    ;; :coerce [:boolean] is a (repeatable) flag for the parser, so for completion too
+    (let [o {:spec {:verbose {:coerce [:boolean] :alias :v} :host {}}}]
+      (is (= #{"--verbose" "-v" "--host"} (set (complete-options o ["--verbose" ""])))))
+  )
+
+)
+
+(deftest all-no-doc-help-test
+  ;; Every advertised shell snippet registers completion for the requested
+  ;; program, drives the completion protocol command, and handles candidates
+  ;; and the file-completion sentinel (see snippet-behavior-test).
+  ;; a command whose spec options are all :no-doc prints its usage line and no
+  ;; dangling, empty Options: section
+  (let [help (cli/format-command-help {:table [{:cmds [] :fn identity :spec {:secret {:no-doc true}}}]
+                                       :prog "x"})]
+    (is (str/includes? help "Usage: x"))
+    (is (not (str/includes? help "Options:"))))
+
+  (testing "spec-shapes-test"
+    (testing "vec-of-pairs spec: options without :coerce/:alias still complete"
+      (let [o {:spec [[:plain {:desc "No coerce"}] [:other {:coerce :string}]]}]
+        (is (= #{"--plain" "--other"} (set (complete-options o ["--"]))))))
+    (testing "entry-level :coerce/:alias (no :spec): a previously typed flag does not open a value position"
+      (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity
+                :coerce {:force :boolean :env :string} :alias {:f :force}}]]
+        ;; The contract defines option candidates in terms of :spec entries, so
+        ;; options declared only via entry-level :coerce/:alias may or may not
+        ;; be offered as candidates at all; what the contract does rule out for
+        ;; either reading is a hang, a throw, or an invented value for the
+        ;; already-typed boolean --force (a flag takes no following value, so
+        ;; its "value candidates" -- the option names themselves -- are
+        ;; implausible)
+        (is (not= #{"--force" "-f"} (set (complete t ["deploy" "--force" ""]))))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "dispatch-level-spec-test"
+    ;; dispatch-level :spec options parse at every level, so they complete there too
+    (is (= #{"--local" "--glob"}
+           (set (complete [{:cmds ["sub"] :fn identity :spec {:local {}}}]
+                          ["sub" "--"]
+                          {:spec {:glob {}}}))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "fresh-word-flag-test"
+    ;; powershell signals a fresh word via --fresh true (it cannot pass an empty
+    ;; token: PS 5.1 / legacy argument passing drops empty-string args)
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity :spec {:env {}}}]
+          out (fn [fresh]
+                (with-out-str
+                  (cli/dispatch t ["org.babashka.cli/completions" "complete"
+                                   "--shell" "powershell" "--fresh" fresh "--" "deploy"]
+                                {:prog "p"})))]
+      (is (= ["--env"] (str/split-lines (out "true"))))
+      (testing "without a fresh word, deploy itself is the token being completed"
+        (is (or (= "" (out "false"))
+                (= ["deploy"] (str/split-lines (out "false"))))))))
+
+  (testing "value-sanitize-test"
+    ;; tabs/newlines in a candidate value would corrupt the line/field wire protocol
+    (let [t [{:cmds ["deploy"] :fn identity :spec {:env {:complete ["a\tb\nc"]}}}]]
+      (let [values (->> (complete-via-cmd t {:prog "p"} "p deploy --env ")
+                        str/split-lines (remove str/blank?) set)]
+        ;; Each tab/newline may either be removed or folded to a space.
+        (is (contains? #{#{"abc"} #{"a bc"} #{"ab c"} #{"a b c"}} values))))
+  )
+
+  (testing "prog-validation-test"
+    ;; :prog is embedded in the snippet's registration lines; a multi-word or
+    ;; metachar name would register completions for the wrong command (or inject)
+    (is (= "" (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "bb tasks"} "bash")))
+    (is (= "" (snippet-via-cmd cmd-table {:prog "x$(rm -rf .)"} "bash")))
+  )
+
+)

+(deftest equals-value-test
+  ;; `parse-opts` supports the documented long-option form `--foo=bar`: the
+  ;; word is split on its first `=`, and whatever text follows the `=` (even
+  ;; none) is the option's value, so such a word is fully self-contained
+  (is (= {:foo "bar"} (cli/parse-opts ["--foo=bar"])))
+  (is (= {:header "k=v"} (cli/parse-opts ["--header=k=v"])))
+  (is (= {:foo ""} (cli/parse-opts ["--foo="])))
+  (testing "a following word is not consumed by the self-contained --opt=value word"
+    (is (= {:header "k=v", :flag true}
+           (cli/parse-opts ["--header=k=v" "--flag"] {:coerce {:flag :boolean}})))
+    (is (= {:args ["pos"], :opts {:header "k=v"}}
+           (cli/parse-args ["--header=k=v" "pos"])))))
+
 (deftest parse-opts-keywords-test
   (is (= {:version "2021a4", :no-git-tag-version true, :deps-file "foo.edn"}
          (cli/parse-opts ["2021a4" ":no-git-tag-version" ":deps-file" "foo.edn"] {:args->opts [:version] :spec {:no-git-tag-version {:coerce :boolean}}}))))

install_config.test_cmd: clojure -M:test --nses babashka.cli-test babashka.cli.completion-test --vars babashka.cli-test/equals-value-test babashka.cli.completion-test/all-no-doc-help-test babashka.cli.completion-test/inherit-completion-test

problem_statement:
Client-side error handling
Support Elixir's `try` special form and related error-handling constructs in the client runtime.

## Scope

- `try` with `rescue`, `catch`, `after`, and `else` clauses
- `raise`, `reraise`, and `throw`
- Exception structs and `__STRUCT__`/`__exception__` semantics

## References

- https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/try-catch-and-rescue.html
- https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/main/Kernel.SpecialForms.html#try/1

### Additional contract requirements

The client runtime exposes `__STACKTRACE__` only as a compile-time placeholder that
always evaluates to the empty list `[]`. It is valid syntax inside `try`
`rescue`/`catch` clauses and in `reraise/2`, but the client does not capture or
propagate real stacktrace frames. Code passed to the client must therefore not rely
on stacktrace contents.

The `after` block of a `try` expression always executes after the `do` body has
completed, on every path: when the body succeeds, when a failure is handled by a
`rescue` or `catch` clause, when an `else` clause either matches or raises
`TryClauseError`, and when a failure propagates without being handled. Its result
is discarded and the try expression's value remains the value determined by its
body/clauses. If the `after` block itself raises, that error replaces any result or
in-flight error on every path, in both the synchronous and the asynchronous
runtime.

A `catch :exit` clause handles `exit/1` signals in the same way that catch clauses handle other matching signals.

An `else` clause is evaluated only when the `do` body completes normally. A value returned by a matching `rescue` or `catch` clause is the try expression's result and is not passed to `else` clauses.

A matching `rescue` or `catch` clause returns its body value even when that value is `false` or `nil`.

Raw Erlang error reasons are normalized to exception structs before rescue matching. In particular, `:erlang.error(:badarg)` is rescuable as `ArgumentError`, and `:erlang.error({:badmap, term})` is rescuable as `BadMapError`.
problem_statement_base:
Client-side error handling
Support Elixir's `try` special form and related error-handling constructs in the client runtime.

## Scope

- `try` with `rescue`, `catch`, `after`, and `else` clauses
- `raise`, `reraise`, and `throw`
- Exception structs and `__STRUCT__`/`__exception__` semantics

## References

- https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/try-catch-and-rescue.html
- https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/main/Kernel.SpecialForms.html#try/1
contract_addendum:
The client runtime exposes `__STACKTRACE__` only as a compile-time placeholder that
always evaluates to the empty list `[]`. It is valid syntax inside `try`
`rescue`/`catch` clauses and in `reraise/2`, but the client does not capture or
propagate real stacktrace frames. Code passed to the client must therefore not rely
on stacktrace contents.

The `after` block of a `try` expression always executes after the `do` body has
completed, on every path: when the body succeeds, when a failure is handled by a
`rescue` or `catch` clause, when an `else` clause either matches or raises
`TryClauseError`, and when a failure propagates without being handled. Its result
is discarded and the try expression's value remains the value determined by its
body/clauses. If the `after` block itself raises, that error replaces any result or
in-flight error on every path, in both the synchronous and the asynchronous
runtime.

A `catch :exit` clause handles `exit/1` signals in the same way that catch clauses handle other matching signals.

An `else` clause is evaluated only when the `do` body completes normally. A value returned by a matching `rescue` or `catch` clause is the try expression's result and is not passed to `else` clauses.

A matching `rescue` or `catch` clause returns its body value even when that value is `false` or `nil`.

Raw Erlang error reasons are normalized to exception structs before rescue matching. In particular, `:erlang.error(:badarg)` is rescuable as `ArgumentError`, and `:erlang.error({:badmap, term})` is rescuable as `BadMapError`.

+defmodule Hologram.ExJsConsistency.TryTest do
+  use Hologram.Test.BasicCase, async: false
+
+  alias Hologram.Compiler.Context
+  alias Hologram.Compiler.Encoder
+  alias Hologram.Compiler.IR
+  alias Hologram.Test.Fixtures.ExJsConsistency.ClientErrorHandling
+
+  @runner Path.join([
+            File.cwd!(),
+            "test",
+            "javascript",
+            "support",
+            "client_error_handling_contract.mjs"
+          ])
+
+  @async_functions [
+    :after_normal_success,
+    :after_handled_catch,
+    :after_handled_rescue,
+    :after_propagating_error,
+    :async_rescue_raw_badarg,
+    :async_rescue_raw_badmap,
+    :async_else_after_rescue,
+    :async_else_after_catch
+  ]
+
+  for {scenario, description} <- [
+        {"catch-signals", "compiled throw and exit are dispatched by catch clauses"},
+        {"raise-rescue", "compiled raise is rescued and exposes exception struct semantics"},
+        {"normalize-struct", "compiled errors preserve normalized exception structs"},
+        {"raw-error-normalization", "raw Erlang errors normalize to rescuable exception structs"},
+        {"else-after-handler", "else clauses only match normal body results"},
+        {"falsy-catch-values", "matched catch clauses preserve false and nil values"},
+        {"reraise", "compiled reraise preserves the exception and empty client stacktrace"},
+        {"after-success", "after executes on normal success and its result is discarded"},
+        {"else-after", "unmatched else raises TryClauseError and still executes after"},
+        {"after-handled", "after executes following handled rescue and catch clauses"},
+        {"after-propagation", "an after failure replaces a propagating body failure"},
+        {"async-paths", "async try handles and replaces failures while awaiting after"}
+      ] do
+    test description do
+      assert_runtime_scenario(unquote(scenario), build_encoded_javascript())
+    end
+  end
+
+  test "valid variable catch kinds compile in a try clause" do
+    javascript = compile_module(Hologram.Test.Fixtures.ExJsConsistency.VariableCatchKind)
+    assert is_binary(javascript)
+  end
+
+  defp build_encoded_javascript do
+    module = ClientErrorHandling
+
+    async_mfas =
+      @async_functions
+      |> Enum.map(&{module, &1, 0})
+      |> MapSet.new()
+
+    [
+      compile_module(Exception),
+      compile_module(ErlangError),
+      compile_module(ArgumentError),
+      compile_module(BadMapError),
+      compile_module(Enum),
+      compile_module(Map),
+      compile_module(Kernel.Utils),
+      compile_module(module),
+      compile_module(module, async_mfas)
+    ]
+    |> Enum.with_index()
+    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {module_javascript, index} ->
+      chunks =
+        module_javascript
+        |> :binary.bin_to_list()
+        |> Enum.chunk_every(60_000)
+        |> Enum.map(&:erlang.list_to_binary/1)
+        |> Enum.map(&Base.url_encode64(&1, padding: false))
+
+      if index == 0, do: chunks, else: ["!" | chunks]
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp compile_module(module, async_mfas \\ MapSet.new()) do
+    context = %Context{module: module, async_mfas: async_mfas}
+
+    module
+    |> IR.for_module()
+    |> Encoder.encode_ir(context)
+  end
+
+  defp assert_runtime_scenario(scenario, encoded_javascript) do
+    {output, exit_status} =
+      System.cmd("node", [@runner, scenario | encoded_javascript],
+        cd: File.cwd!(),
+        stderr_to_stdout: true
+      )
+
+    assert exit_status == 0,
+           "compiled client error-handling scenario #{inspect(scenario)} failed (#{exit_status}):\n#{output}"
+  end
+end

@@ -0,0 +1,256 @@
+defmodule Hologram.Test.Fixtures.ExJsConsistency.ClientErrorHandling do
+  def identity(value), do: value
+
+  def catch_throw_and_exit do
+    thrown =
+      try do
+        throw(:payload)
+      catch
+        :throw, value -> {:caught, value}
+      end
+
+    exited =
+      try do
+        exit(:shutdown)
+      catch
+        :exit, value -> {:caught, value}
+      end
+
+    {thrown, exited}
+  end
+
+  def rescue_raise do
+    try do
+      raise %{__struct__: RuntimeError, __exception__: true, message: "boom"}
+    rescue
+      error in RuntimeError ->
+        {:rescued, error.__struct__, error.__exception__, error.message}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def normalize_exception_struct do
+    try do
+      :erlang.error(%{__struct__: ArgumentError, __exception__: true, message: "argument error"})
+    rescue
+      error in ArgumentError ->
+        {:normalized, error.__struct__, error.__exception__, error.message}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def rescue_raw_badarg do
+    try do
+      :erlang.error(:badarg)
+    rescue
+      error in ArgumentError -> {error.__struct__, error.__exception__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def rescue_raw_badmap do
+    try do
+      :erlang.error({:badmap, 123})
+    rescue
+      error in BadMapError -> {error.__struct__, error.__exception__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def else_after_rescue do
+    try do
+      if identity(:body) == :body do
+        raise %{__struct__: RuntimeError, __exception__: true, message: "body"}
+      else
+        :normal
+      end
+    rescue
+      RuntimeError -> :handled
+    else
+      _value -> :else_ran_after_rescue
+    end
+  end
+
+  def else_after_catch do
+    try do
+      if identity(:body) == :body do
+        throw(:body)
+      else
+        :normal
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, :body -> :handled
+    else
+      _value -> :else_ran_after_catch
+    end
+  end
+
+  def falsy_catch_values do
+    false_value =
+      try do
+        throw(false)
+      catch
+        :throw, false -> false
+      end
+
+    nil_value =
+      try do
+        throw(nil)
+      catch
+        :throw, nil -> nil
+      end
+
+    {false_value, nil_value}
+  end
+
+  def async_rescue_raw_badarg do
+    try do
+      :erlang.error(:badarg)
+    rescue
+      error in ArgumentError -> {error.__struct__, error.__exception__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def async_rescue_raw_badmap do
+    try do
+      :erlang.error({:badmap, 123})
+    rescue
+      error in BadMapError -> {error.__struct__, error.__exception__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def async_else_after_rescue do
+    try do
+      if identity(:body) == :body do
+        raise %{__struct__: RuntimeError, __exception__: true, message: "body"}
+      else
+        :normal
+      end
+    rescue
+      RuntimeError -> :handled
+    else
+      _value -> :else_ran_after_rescue
+    end
+  end
+
+  def async_else_after_catch do
+    try do
+      if identity(:body) == :body do
+        throw(:body)
+      else
+        :normal
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, :body -> :handled
+    else
+      _value -> :else_ran_after_catch
+    end
+  end
+
+  def reraise_error do
+    try do
+      try do
+        raise %{__struct__: ArgumentError, __exception__: true, message: "original"}
+      rescue
+        error -> reraise error, __STACKTRACE__
+      end
+    rescue
+      error in ArgumentError -> {:reraised, error.message, __STACKTRACE__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_normal_success do
+    try do
+      try do
+        :body_result
+      after
+        throw(:after_normal)
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, value -> value
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_result_is_ignored do
+    try do
+      :body_result
+    after
+      :after_result
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_unmatched_else do
+    try do
+      try do
+        identity(:body_result)
+      else
+        :other -> :unreachable
+      after
+        throw(:after_else)
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, value -> value
+    end
+  end
+
+  def unmatched_else do
+    try do
+      try do
+        identity(:body_result)
+      else
+        :other -> :unreachable
+      after
+        :cleanup
+      end
+    rescue
+      error in TryClauseError -> {:try_clause_error, error.__struct__}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_handled_catch do
+    try do
+      try do
+        throw(:body)
+      catch
+        :throw, :body -> :handled
+      after
+        throw(:after_handled)
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, value -> value
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_handled_rescue do
+    try do
+      try do
+        raise %{__struct__: RuntimeError, __exception__: true, message: "body"}
+      rescue
+        RuntimeError -> :handled
+      after
+        throw(:after_rescue)
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, value -> value
+    end
+  end
+
+  def after_propagating_error do
+    try do
+      try do
+        raise %{__struct__: RuntimeError, __exception__: true, message: "body"}
+      after
+        throw(:after_propagating)
+      end
+    catch
+      :throw, value -> value
+    end
+  end
+end
+
+
+defmodule Hologram.Test.Fixtures.ExJsConsistency.VariableCatchKind do
+  def catch_kind do
+    try do
+      throw(:payload)
+    catch
+      kind, value -> {kind, value}
+    end
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
Many tests fail with insert-ordered-containers-0.3
The package seems to be relying on the broken instances in prior versions of this dependency:

```
/tmp/openapi3-3.2.4
 % cabal test --allow-newer=openapi3:insert-ordered-containers -c 'insert-ordered-containers^>=0.3
375 examples, 73 failures
Test suite spec: FAIL
```

### Additional contract requirements

The library must build and its public data-model behavior must work correctly
with both the `insert-ordered-containers` 0.3 series and the previously
supported 0.2 series of that dependency. A correct solution must not regress
in either dependency configuration.

Observable requirements, in both dependency configurations:

- Public OpenAPI schema values must encode map-like fields, including schema
  properties and named schema definitions, as JSON objects and must decode the
  corresponding JSON object representation.
- The observable entries in those fields are their key-value mappings; no
  insertion order or byte-level JSON ordering is required.
- The public schema test suite is exercised under the standard supported
  dependency configuration and under a legacy configuration that pins the
  dependency to the 0.2 series. It must pass in both configurations.

These requirements concern only behavior observable through the library's
public API and test-suite results. They impose no internal representation,
module, wrapper, instance placement, or other implementation design.
