diff --git a/src/Data/HashMap/Strict/InsOrd/Compat.hs b/src/Data/HashMap/Strict/InsOrd/Compat.hs
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..e6fabead
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/Data/HashMap/Strict/InsOrd/Compat.hs
@@ -0,0 +1,438 @@
+-- Ported from GetShopTV/swagger2 (pull request #262) to apply the same
+-- insert-ordered-containers-0.3 compatibility fix to openapi3.
+-- Credit for the design and implementation belongs to the swagger2 authors.
+{-# LANGUAGE CPP #-}
+-- |
+-- Module:      Data.HashMap.Strict.InsOrd.Compat
+-- Maintainer:  Nickolay Kudasov <nickolay@getshoptv.com>
+-- Stability:   experimental
+--
+-- Compatibility wrapper around @insert-ordered-containers@ to mitigate the
+-- breaking changes introduced in @insert-ordered-containers-0.3.0@:
+-- <https://github.com/erikd/insert-ordered-containers/pull/8>.
+--
+-- That change fixed 'Eq' and Aeson instances in the upstream package, but it is
+-- a behavioral break for @swagger2@ where we need stable Swagger Schema
+-- generation and JSON object-like encoding.
+--
+-- This module keeps the old @swagger2@ expectations:
+--
+-- * 'InsOrdHashMap' values are encoded as JSON objects (not arrays of key/value
+--   tuples), so field names remain first-class object keys.
+-- * Equality intentionally ignores insertion order (compares as plain hash
+--   maps), which matches how many tests currently assert JSON equality.
+--
+-- Simple encoding examples:
+--
+-- >>> import Data.Aeson (encode, eitherDecode)
+-- >>> import qualified Data.ByteString.Lazy.Char8 as BSL8
+-- >>> import qualified Data.HashMap.Strict as HM
+-- >>> import qualified Data.HashMap.Strict.InsOrd.Compat as IOHM
+-- >>> let decodeIOHM s = either error id (eitherDecode (BSL8.pack s) :: Either String (IOHM.InsOrdHashMap String Int))
+--
+-- A regular hash map has no insertion order guarantee:
+--
+-- >>> encode (HM.fromList [("a", 1 :: Int), ("b", 2)])
+-- "{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}"
+-- >>> encode (HM.fromList [("b", 1 :: Int), ("a", 2)])
+-- "{\"a\":2,\"b\":1}"
+--
+-- Our compat 'InsOrdHashMap' encodes to a JSON object as well, but preserves insertion order:
+--
+-- >>> encode (IOHM.fromList [("a", 1 :: Int), ("b", 2)])
+-- "{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}"
+-- >>> encode (IOHM.fromList [("b", 1 :: Int), ("a", 2)])
+-- "{\"b\":1,\"a\":2}"
+--
+-- Round-tripping through decode/encode demonstrates the caveat: encoding
+-- preserves insertion order, but decoded object key order is not guaranteed.
+--
+-- >>> encode (decodeIOHM "{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}")
+-- "{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}"
+-- >>> encode (decodeIOHM "{\"b\":1,\"a\":2}")
+-- "{\"a\":2,\"b\":1}"
+--
+-- This object encoding is what @swagger2@ wants for generated Swagger
+-- definitions/properties because it keeps emitted schemas easy to consume and
+-- stable in practice.
+--
+-- Important caveat: decoding cannot be fully stable with respect to insertion
+-- order due to @aeson@ limitations. In particular, object parsing goes through
+-- structures that do not preserve all ordering guarantees end-to-end. We accept
+-- this trade-off for now because the primary requirement is deterministic
+-- /encoding/ for generated Swagger Schema artifacts.
+--
+-- Many tests rely on @aesonQQ@-style JSON equality, where semantic object
+-- equality matters more than insertion order. Comparing via plain hash maps
+-- makes those tests robust under benign key-order variation. This is a weaker
+-- notion of equality and hopefully will be revisited later.
+module Data.HashMap.Strict.InsOrd.Compat (
+  InsOrdHashMap,
+  -- * Construction
+  empty,
+  singleton,
+  -- * Basic interface
+  null,
+  size,
+  member,
+  lookup,
+  lookupDefault,
+  insert,
+  insertWith,
+  delete,
+  adjust,
+  update,
+  alter,
+  -- * Combine
+  union,
+  unionWith,
+  unionWithKey,
+  unions,
+  -- * Transformations
+  map,
+  mapKeys,
+  traverseKeys,
+  mapWithKey,
+  traverseWithKey,
+  -- ** Unordered
+  unorderedTraverse,
+  unorderedTraverseWithKey,
+  -- * Difference and intersection
+  difference,
+  intersection,
+  intersectionWith,
+  intersectionWithKey,
+  -- * Folds
+  foldl',
+  foldlWithKey',
+  foldr,
+  foldrWithKey,
+  foldMapWithKey,
+  -- ** Unordered
+  unorderedFoldMap,
+  unorderedFoldMapWithKey,
+  -- * Filter
+  filter,
+  filterWithKey,
+  mapMaybe,
+  mapMaybeWithKey,
+  -- * Conversions
+  keys,
+  elems,
+  toList,
+  toRevList,
+  fromList,
+  toHashMap,
+  fromHashMap,
+  -- * Lenses
+  hashMap,
+  unorderedTraversal,
+  -- * Debugging
+  valid,
+  ) where
+
+#if !MIN_VERSION_insert_ordered_containers(0,3,0)
+import Prelude hiding (null, lookup, map, foldl', foldr, filter)
+import Data.HashMap.Strict.InsOrd
+#else
+import qualified Data.HashMap.Strict.InsOrd as InsOrdHashMap
+
+import Prelude hiding (null, size, member, lookup, lookupDefault, map, foldl', filter)
+import qualified Prelude
+
+import qualified Data.Aeson as A
+import qualified Data.Aeson.Encoding as E
+import           Data.HashMap.Strict (HashMap)
+import qualified Data.HashMap.Strict as HashMap
+
+import qualified GHC.Exts as Exts
+
+import Data.Data                       (Data)
+import Data.Foldable                   (Foldable (foldMap))
+import Data.Hashable                   (Hashable (..))
+
+import qualified Control.Lens        as Lens
+import Control.Lens
+       (At (..), Index, Iso, IxValue, Ixed (..), Traversal, _1, _2, iso, (<&>))
+
+import qualified Optics.Core         as Optics
+
+newtype InsOrdHashMap k v = InsOrdHashMap { unCompatInsOrdHashMap :: InsOrdHashMap.InsOrdHashMap k v }
+  deriving (Show, Read, Data, Functor, Foldable, Traversable, Semigroup, Monoid)
+
+instance (Eq k, Eq v) => Eq (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    a == b = toHashMap a == toHashMap b
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Exts.IsList (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    type Item (InsOrdHashMap k v) = Exts.Item (InsOrdHashMap.InsOrdHashMap k v)
+    fromList = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.fromList
+    toList   = InsOrdHashMap.toList . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Aeson
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+instance (A.ToJSONKey k) => A.ToJSON1 (InsOrdHashMap k) where
+    liftToJSON _ t _ = case A.toJSONKey :: A.ToJSONKeyFunction k of
+      A.ToJSONKeyText f _ -> A.object . fmap (\(k, v) -> (f k, t v)) . toList
+      A.ToJSONKeyValue f _ -> A.toJSON . fmap (\(k,v) -> A.toJSON (f k, t v)) . toList
+
+    liftToEncoding o t _ = case A.toJSONKey :: A.ToJSONKeyFunction k of
+      A.ToJSONKeyText _ f ->  E.dict f t foldrWithKey
+      A.ToJSONKeyValue _ f -> E.list (A.liftToEncoding2 (const False) f (E.list f) o t (E.list t)) . toList
+
+instance (A.ToJSONKey k, A.ToJSON v) => A.ToJSON (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    toJSON = A.toJSON1
+    toEncoding = A.toEncoding1
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k, A.FromJSONKey k) => A.FromJSON1 (InsOrdHashMap k) where
+    liftParseJSON o p pl v = fromList . HashMap.toList <$> A.liftParseJSON o p pl v
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k, A.FromJSONKey k, A.FromJSON v) => A.FromJSON (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    parseJSON = A.parseJSON1
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- indexed-traversals
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Optics.FunctorWithIndex k (InsOrdHashMap k) where
+    imap = mapWithKey
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Optics.FoldableWithIndex k (InsOrdHashMap k) where
+    ifoldMap = foldMapWithKey
+    ifoldr   = foldrWithKey
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Optics.TraversableWithIndex k (InsOrdHashMap k) where
+    itraverse = traverseWithKey
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Lens
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+type instance Index (InsOrdHashMap k v) = k
+type instance IxValue (InsOrdHashMap k v) = v
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Ixed (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    ix k f m = ixImpl k pure f m
+    {-# INLINABLE ix #-}
+
+ixImpl
+  :: (Eq k, Hashable k, Functor f)
+  => k
+  -> (InsOrdHashMap k v -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v))
+  -> (v -> f v)
+  -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+  -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v)
+ixImpl k point f m = case lookup k m of
+    Just v  -> f v <&> \v' -> insert k v' m
+    Nothing -> point m
+{-# INLINE ixImpl #-}
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => At (InsOrdHashMap k a) where
+    at k f m = f mv <&> \r -> case r of
+        Nothing -> maybe m (const (delete k m)) mv
+        Just v' -> insert k v' m
+      where mv = lookup k m
+    {-# INLINABLE at #-}
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Optics
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+type instance Optics.Index (InsOrdHashMap k v) = k
+type instance Optics.IxValue (InsOrdHashMap k v) = v
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Optics.Ixed (InsOrdHashMap k v) where
+    ix k = Optics.atraversalVL $ \point f m -> ixImpl k point f m
+    {-# INLINE ix #-}
+
+instance (Eq k, Hashable k) => Optics.At (InsOrdHashMap k a) where
+    at k = Optics.lensVL $ \f m -> Lens.at k f m
+    {-# INLINE at #-}
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+-- | This is a slight lie, as roundtrip doesn't preserve ordering.
+hashMap :: Iso (InsOrdHashMap k a) (InsOrdHashMap k b) (HashMap k a) (HashMap k b)
+hashMap = iso toHashMap fromHashMap
+
+unorderedTraversal :: Traversal (InsOrdHashMap k a) (InsOrdHashMap k b) a b
+unorderedTraversal = hashMap . traverse
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Construction
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+empty :: InsOrdHashMap k v
+empty = InsOrdHashMap InsOrdHashMap.empty
+
+singleton :: Hashable k => k -> v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+singleton k v = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.singleton k v)
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Basic interface
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+null :: InsOrdHashMap k v -> Bool
+null = InsOrdHashMap.null . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+size :: InsOrdHashMap k v -> Int
+size = InsOrdHashMap.size . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+insert :: Hashable k => k -> v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+insert k v = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.insert k v . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+insertWith :: Hashable k => (v -> v -> v) -> k -> v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+insertWith f k v = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.insertWith f k v . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+delete :: Hashable k => k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+delete k = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.delete k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+adjust :: Hashable k => (v -> v) -> k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+adjust f k = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.adjust f k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+update :: Hashable k => (v -> Maybe v) -> k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+update f k = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.update f k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+alter :: Hashable k => (Maybe v -> Maybe v) -> k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+alter f k = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.alter f k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+member :: Hashable k => k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> Bool
+member k = InsOrdHashMap.member k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+lookup :: Hashable k => k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> Maybe v
+lookup k = InsOrdHashMap.lookup k . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+lookupDefault :: Hashable k => v -> k -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> v
+lookupDefault k def = InsOrdHashMap.lookupDefault k def . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-- * Combine
+
+union :: Hashable k => InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+union m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.union (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+unionWith :: Hashable k => (v -> v -> v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+unionWith f m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.unionWith f (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+unionWithKey :: Hashable k => (k -> v -> v -> v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+unionWithKey f m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.unionWithKey f (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+unions :: Hashable k => [InsOrdHashMap k v] -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+unions = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.unions . Prelude.map unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Transformations
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+map :: (v -> v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+map f = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.map f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+mapKeys :: Hashable k => (k -> k) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+mapKeys f = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.mapKeys f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+traverseKeys :: (Applicative f, Hashable k) => (k -> f k) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v)
+traverseKeys f = fmap InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.traverseKeys f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+mapWithKey :: (k -> v1 -> v2) -> InsOrdHashMap k v1 -> InsOrdHashMap k v2
+mapWithKey f = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.mapWithKey f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+traverseWithKey :: (Applicative f, Hashable k) => (k -> v1 -> f v2) -> InsOrdHashMap k v1 -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v2)
+traverseWithKey f = fmap InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.traverseWithKey f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-- ** Unordered
+
+unorderedTraverse :: (Applicative f, Hashable k) => (v -> f v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v)
+unorderedTraverse f = fmap InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.unorderedTraverse f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+unorderedTraverseWithKey :: (Applicative f, Hashable k) => (k -> v -> f v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> f (InsOrdHashMap k v)
+unorderedTraverseWithKey f = fmap InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.unorderedTraverseWithKey f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Difference and intersection
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+difference :: Hashable k => InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+difference m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.difference (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+intersection :: Hashable k => InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+intersection m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.intersection (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+intersectionWith :: Hashable k => (v -> v -> v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+intersectionWith f m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.intersectionWith f (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+intersectionWithKey :: Hashable k => (k -> v -> v -> v) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+intersectionWithKey f m1 m2 = InsOrdHashMap (InsOrdHashMap.intersectionWithKey f (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m1) (unCompatInsOrdHashMap m2))
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Folds
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+foldl' :: (a -> v -> a) -> a -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> a
+foldl' f z = InsOrdHashMap.foldl' f z . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+foldlWithKey' :: (a -> k -> v -> a) -> a -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> a
+foldlWithKey' f z = InsOrdHashMap.foldlWithKey' f z . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+foldMapWithKey :: Monoid m => (k -> v -> m) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> m
+foldMapWithKey f = InsOrdHashMap.foldMapWithKey f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+foldrWithKey :: (k -> v -> a -> a) -> a -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> a
+foldrWithKey f z = InsOrdHashMap.foldrWithKey f z . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+-- ** Unordered
+
+unorderedFoldMap :: Monoid m => (v -> m) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> m
+unorderedFoldMap f = InsOrdHashMap.unorderedFoldMap f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap
+
+unorderedFoldMapWithKey :: Monoid m => (k -> v -> m) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> m
+unorderedFoldMapWithKey f = InsOrdHashMap.unorderedFoldMapWithKey f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- * Filter
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+filter :: (v -> Bool) -> InsOrdHashMap k v -> InsOrdHashMap k v
+filter f = InsOrdHashMap . InsOrdHashMap.filter f . unCompatInsOrdHashMap

problem_statement:
Implement bitcoind-rpc v31
Implement the new / modified RPC interfaces for bitcoin core v31: 

https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/blob/4d040b7d62399fd59a4fd4766f6f53793e77f1ca/doc/release-notes/release-notes-31.0.md

### Additional contract requirements

# Bitcoin Core v31 support contract

This task adds Bitcoin Core v31 support to `bitcoind-rpc`. The following
behaviors are part of the public contract exercised by the hidden tests. Tests
may access these behaviors either directly or through runtime reflection of
the named public types and their public members, so the concrete public names
listed below are themselves part of the contract.

## BitcoindVersion

- `BitcoindVersion` exposes a public `V31` companion member (a module value)
  whose string representation is exactly `"v31.0"`.
- `V31` is the newest supported version: `BitcoindVersion.newest == V31`.
- `V31` is contained in `BitcoindVersion.known`.
- `V31` is contained in `BitcoindVersion.standard` and is ordered strictly
  ahead of `V30` (i.e. `standard.indexOf(V31) < standard.indexOf(V30)`).
- `BitcoindVersion.fromNetworkVersion(310000)` returns a version whose string
  representation is `"v31.0"`; the v30 mapping (network version `300200` to
  `"v30.2"`) must keep working.
- `BitcoindVersion.findVersion("v31.0")` returns the `V31` member.

## v31 RPC client

- The public RPC client class for v31 instances is named
  `org.bitcoins.rpc.client.v31.BitcoindV31RpcClient`. It is publicly
  reflectable by that name, extends the common `BitcoindRpcClient`, and has a
  public constructor whose first parameter list accepts a
  `org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstance` (or a subtype of it) together
  with an actor system.
- Its `version` member is a `Future[BitcoindVersion]` pinned to the `V31`
  version (reported string `"v31.0"`); constructing the client and reading its
  version must not require contacting a daemon.

## v31 mempool result models

- The public v31 getmempoolinfo result model is named
  `org.bitcoins.commons.jsonmodels.bitcoind.GetMemPoolInfoResultV31`. It
  extends `GetMemPoolInfoResult` and carries the v30 `getmempoolinfo` fields
  plus the v31 fields `limitclustercount`, `limitclustersize`, and `optimal`.
- The public `getmempoolinfo` response decoder selects the v31 result model
  when a response contains those three v31 keys; responses without them keep
  decoding into the pre-v31 result models. This holds both when decoding
  directly with the decoder and when `getMemPoolInfo` is answered through the
  mempool RPC API. When answering through the mempool RPC API, all supplied
  response values must be preserved in the decoded result, including the
  inherited v30 `getmempoolinfo` values as well as the v31 additions.
- The public feerate-diagram entry result model is named
  `org.bitcoins.commons.jsonmodels.bitcoind.GetMempoolFeerateDiagramEntry`. It
  is publicly constructible from a `weight: Int` and a `fee: Bitcoins` (its
  public `apply` takes exactly those two parameters). Its companion exposes a
  public parameterless `empty` value representing an empty mempool diagram,
  and reading `empty` must yield weight `0` and fee `Bitcoins.zero`. A JSON
  entry `{"weight": 0, "fee": 0}` decodes into weight `0` / fee
  `Bitcoins.zero`, and non-empty `{"weight": w, "fee": f}` entries decode
  preserving `weight` and `fee`.
- A public mempool cluster result type exists in
  `org.bitcoins.commons.jsonmodels.bitcoind` carrying public `clusterweight:
  Int`, `txcount: Int`, and `chunks` values; each chunk carries public
  `chunkfee` (a `Bitcoins` amount), `chunkweight`, and `txs` (the member
  transaction ids as `DoubleSha256DigestBE` values) values.
- The result of `gettxspendingprevout` additionally carries the optional v31
  fields `spendingtx` (the full spending transaction, returned when the
  `return_spending_tx` option is requested), `spendingtxid`, and `blockhash`
  (the confirming block hash), all as public optional values. Entries without
  spend information decode with all optional fields empty.

## v31 mempool RPC methods

The following public methods exist on the mempool RPC API
(`org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.MempoolRpc`) and are verified through a
recording test double: observable request construction and response decoding
must behave as described.

- `getMempoolCluster(txid)` is publicly exposed in both
  `DoubleSha256DigestBE` and `DoubleSha256Digest` overloads, each returning a
  `Future` of the cluster result model described above. Calling either
  overload issues a `getmempoolcluster` RPC request carrying the transaction
  id hex as a parameter, and decodes the cluster response into the cluster
  result model, including its chunk groupings.
- `getMempoolFeerateDiagram()` is publicly exposed, returns a `Future` of a
  vector of diagram entries, and issues a `getmempoolfeeratediagram` RPC
  request. Responses decode each entry's `weight` and `fee`. Bitcoin Core's
  empty-mempool diagram is represented by a response containing exactly one
  zero-valued empty diagram entry; that response must yield a one-entry result
  preserving weight `0` and fee `Bitcoins.zero`.
- `getTxSpendingPrevOut(prevouts, mempoolOnly, returnSpendingTx)` is publicly
  exposed as an overload accepting a vector of outpoints plus two
  `Option[Boolean]` parameters for the v31 `mempool_only` and
  `return_spending_tx` request options, in that order, returning a `Future` of
  a vector of the result entries described above:
  - The outpoints are issued in the JSON `{"txid": <big-endian hex>,
    "vout": <number>}` request shape as the first request parameter.
  - When either option is defined, a second JSON request parameter object is
    sent; it carries exactly the defined options, each under its literal
    option key - `mempool_only` for the `mempoolOnly` parameter and
    `return_spending_tx` for the `returnSpendingTx` parameter - with the
    requested boolean value (`true` serializes as `true` and `false`
    serializes as `false`). Options that are not defined are never sent. When
    both options are empty, no second request parameter is sent.
  - The response decodes as described under result models, including the
    optional v31 fields.

## Public decoders

- The public decoders referenced above are installed under
  `org.bitcoins.commons.serializers.JsonSerializers`, and the following
  public member names of that object are themselves part of the contract:
  - `getMemPoolInfoResultReads` is the getmempoolinfo response decoder. It
    selects between the pre-v31 and v31 result models from the observed
    response fields as described.
  - `getMempoolFeerateDiagramEntryReads` is the getmempoolfeeratediagram
    entry decoder. It decodes both zero-value and non-zero
    `{"weight", "fee"}` entries into `GetMempoolFeerateDiagramEntry`.
- The `gettxspendingprevout` and `getmempoolcluster` response decoders are
  the ones used by the RPC methods above; each decodes the documented
  response shapes.

+package org.bitcoins.rpc.client.v31

+import org.bitcoins.rpc.config.{BitcoindInstance, BitcoindInstanceLocal}
+
+import scala.concurrent.Future
+
+class BitcoindV31RpcClient(override val instance: BitcoindInstance)(implicit
+    actorSystem: ActorSystem

+  override lazy val version: Future[BitcoindVersion] =
+    Future.successful(BitcoindVersion.V31)
+}
+
+object BitcoindV31RpcClient {
+
+  /** Creates an RPC client from the given instance, together with the given
+    * actor system. This is for advanced users, where you need fine grained
+    * control over the RPC client.
+    */
+  def apply(instance: BitcoindInstanceLocal)(implicit
+      system: ActorSystem
+  ): BitcoindV31RpcClient =
+    new BitcoindV31RpcClient(instance)(using system)

+package org.bitcoins.testkit.rpc

+/** Verifies that bitcoind-rpc supports Bitcoin Core v31 (see the issue
+  * "Implement bitcoind-rpc v31").
+  *
+  * The assertions exercise only observable, documented behaviors: the public
+  * version registry, the public `getmempoolinfo` response decoder, the public
+  * result-model shapes and the v31 mempool RPC methods running against a test
+  * double that records outgoing RPC requests and answers them from a scripted
+  * result map.
+  *
+  * The v31-specific assertions intentionally use runtime reflection on the
+  * public shapes so this suite compiles both before and after v31 support is
+  * added: on the base revision the v31 symbols do not exist yet and those
+  * assertions fail, while a complete v31 implementation makes every assertion
+  * pass. All reflective lookups go through public runtime types and public
+  * accessors only; no private members and no `setAccessible(true)` are used.
+  */
+class BitcoindVersionV31Test extends BitcoinSAsyncTest {
+
+  private val runtimeMirror: ru.Mirror =
+    ru.runtimeMirror(getClass.getClassLoader)
+
+  /** A bitcoind instance description pointing at a non-existent daemon; it is
+    * never contacted because every offline client in this suite either pins its
+    * version or records its requests in memory.

+    MempoolRpcV31FakeInstances()
+
+  behavior of "BitcoindVersion v31 support"
+
+  private def bitcoindVersionCompanion: Any = {
+    val module = ru.typeOf[BitcoindVersion.type].termSymbol.asModule
+    runtimeMirror.reflectModule(module).instance
+  }
+
+  it should "define a V31 value with the expected version string and standard version ordering" in {
+    val member =
+      ru.typeOf[BitcoindVersion.type].decl(ru.TermName("V31"))
+    assert(member != ru.NoSymbol, "BitcoindVersion must expose a public V31")
+    assert(member.isTerm && member.asTerm.isModule)
+
+    val v31 =
+      runtimeMirror
+        .reflectModule(member.asModule)
+        .instance
+        .asInstanceOf[BitcoindVersion]
+
+    // v31.0 is the Bitcoin Core 31.0 release
+    assert(v31.toString == "v31.0")
+
+    // looking up the advertised version string must round-trip to V31
+    assert(BitcoindVersion.findVersion(v31.toString).contains(v31))
+
+    // V31 must be the newest supported version
+    assert(
+      bitcoindVersionCompanion.getClass
+        .getMethod("newest")
+        .invoke(bitcoindVersionCompanion) == v31,
+      "V31 must be the newest supported version"
+    )
+
+    // V31 must be listed among the known versions
+    val known =
+      bitcoindVersionCompanion.getClass
+        .getMethod("known")
+        .invoke(bitcoindVersionCompanion)
+        .asInstanceOf[Vector[_]]
+    assert(known.contains(v31), "V31 must be listed among the known versions")
+
+    // V31 must be offered ahead of V30 in the standard version selection order
+    val standard =
+      bitcoindVersionCompanion.getClass
+        .getMethod("standard")
+        .invoke(bitcoindVersionCompanion)
+        .asInstanceOf[Vector[_]]
+    assert(standard.contains(v31))
+    assert(
+      standard.indexOf(v31) < standard.indexOf(BitcoindVersion.V30),
+      "V31 must be ordered ahead of V30 in the standard version selection"
+    )
+    succeed
+  }
+
+  it should "map the v31 network version to V31" in {
+    assert(BitcoindVersion.fromNetworkVersion(310000).toString == "v31.0")
+    succeed
+  }
+
+  it should "keep mapping the v30 network version to the v30 supported version" in {
+    // the v30 mapping must keep working while v31 is added
+    assert(BitcoindVersion.fromNetworkVersion(300200).toString == "v30.2")
+    succeed
+  }
+
+  it should "provide a public v31 RPC client whose reported version is pinned to V31" in {
+    val tpe = publicType("org.bitcoins.rpc.client.v31.BitcoindV31RpcClient")
+
+    // the RPC client for v31 instances must extend the common RPC client
+    assert(tpe <:< ru.typeOf[org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.BitcoindRpcClient],
+           "the v31 RPC client must extend the common BitcoindRpcClient")
+
+    // it must be constructible from a generic bitcoind instance description
+    val ctor = tpe.decl(ru.termNames.CONSTRUCTOR).asMethod
+    assert(ctor.paramLists.flatten.nonEmpty)
+    val instanceClass =
+      runtimeMirror.staticClass("org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstance")
+    assert(
+      ctor.paramLists.flatten.head.typeSignature.dealias <:< instanceClass.toType,
+      "the v31 RPC client must be constructible from a BitcoindInstance"
+    )
+
+    // its reported version must be a Future[BitcoindVersion]
+    val versionMember = tpe.decl(ru.TermName("version"))
+    assert(versionMember != ru.NoSymbol,
+           "the v31 RPC client must expose its version")
+    assert(
+      versionMember.typeSignature.finalResultType.dealias =:=
+        ru.typeOf[scala.concurrent.Future[BitcoindVersion]],
+      "the v31 RPC client version must be a Future[BitcoindVersion]"
+    )
+
+    // constructing the v31 client must pin its reported version to V31 without
+    // contacting a daemon
+    val cls = Class.forName("org.bitcoins.rpc.client.v31.BitcoindV31RpcClient")
+    val ctorJava =
+      cls.getConstructor(classOf[org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstance],
+                         classOf[ActorSystem])
+    val client = ctorJava
+      .newInstance(offlineInstance, system)
+      .asInstanceOf[org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.BitcoindRpcClient]
+    client.version.map { v =>
+      assert(v.toString == "v31.0",
+             "the v31 RPC client's reported version must be V31")
+    }
+  }

+    val tpe = publicType(

+      assert(readField(second, "spendingtx").asInstanceOf[Option[_]].isEmpty)
+      assert(readField(second, "blockhash").asInstanceOf[Option[_]].isEmpty)
+
+      // with no options requested no second request parameter may be sent
+      recorded.clear()
+      extendedOpt.get
+        .invoke(client,
+                Vector(outpoint),
+                Option.empty[Boolean],
+                Option.empty[Boolean])
+        .asInstanceOf[Future[Vector[Any]]]
+        .map { _ =>
+          assert(recorded.length == 1)
+          val params2 = recorded.head._2.value

+            params2.length == 1,

+
+  it should "serialize the v31 gettxspendingprevout options independently including false values" in {
+    val (client, recorded) =
+      fakeMempoolClient(
+        Map("gettxspendingprevout" -> txSpendingPrevOutResponse))
+
+    val extended = Try(
+      client.getClass.getMethod("getTxSpendingPrevOut",

+                                classOf[Option[Boolean]])) match {
+      case Success(m) => m
+      case Failure(_: NoSuchMethodException) =>
+        fail(
+          "getTxSpendingPrevOut must offer an overload accepting mempoolOnly and returnSpendingTx options")
+      case Failure(e) => throw e
+    }
+
+    val outpoint =
+      TransactionOutPoint(DoubleSha256DigestBE.fromHex(txidHex), UInt32(1))
+
+    def requestWith(
+        mempoolOnly: Option[Boolean],
+        returnSpendingTx: Option[Boolean]): Future[JsObject] = {
+      recorded.clear()
+      extended
+        .invoke(
+          client,
+          Vector(outpoint),
+          mempoolOnly.map(v => Boolean.box(v)),
+          returnSpendingTx.map(v => Boolean.box(v)))

+          params(1).as[JsObject]

+    for {
+      // mempoolOnly requested on its own (true)
+      onlyMempool <- requestWith(Some(true), None)
+      _ = {
+        assert(onlyMempool.keys == Set("mempool_only"),
+               "only the defined option may be serialized")
+        assert((onlyMempool \ "mempool_only").as[Boolean],

+      // mempoolOnly requested with the false value
+      mempoolFalse <- requestWith(Some(false), None)

+        assert(mempoolFalse.keys == Set("mempool_only"))

+               "each defined option must carry its own requested value")

+               "each defined option must carry its own requested value")

+  it should "construct getmempoolcluster requests for both txid encodings and decode cluster responses" in {

+                "the mempool RPC API must expose getMempoolCluster for little-endian txids")

+          .invoke(client, DoubleSha256Digest(txidHex))

+
+  it should "return empty and non-empty getmempoolfeeratediagram results from the mempool RPC API" in {

+          readField(entries(1), "fee") ==
+            Bitcoins(BigDecimal("0.00015000")))
+
+        // Bitcoin Core represents an empty-mempool diagram with the single

+        val emptyDiagramClient = fakeMempoolClient(

+            "getmempoolfeeratediagram" ->

+              "the empty mempool feerate diagram entry must have zero weight")

+              readField(emptyEntries.head, "fee") == Bitcoins.zero,

+
+  behavior of "v31 mempool RPC method surface"
+
+  it should "expose getMempoolCluster, getMempoolFeerateDiagram and the extended getTxSpendingPrevOut on the MempoolRpc API" in {
+    val tpe = ru.typeOf[org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.MempoolRpc]
+
+    // getMempoolCluster(txid: DoubleSha256DigestBE): Future[GetMempoolClusterResult]
+    val clusterAlts = methodAlternatives(tpe, "getMempoolCluster")
+    assert(clusterAlts.nonEmpty, "MempoolRpc must expose getMempoolCluster")
+    assert(
+      clusterAlts.exists { m =>
+        m.paramLists.flatten.headOption.exists(_.typeSignature.dealias =:=

+      clusterAlts.exists { m =>

+    // getTxSpendingPrevOut(prevouts, mempoolOnly, returnSpendingTx)

+    assert(
+      prevOutAlts.exists { m =>

+
+  /** Helpers that go through the public runtime shape so the suite compiles
+    * before the v31 symbols exist.
+    */
+
+  private def publicType(className: String): ru.Type = {
+    Try(runtimeMirror.staticClass(className)) match {
+      case Success(sym) => sym.toType
+      case Failure(_) =>
+        fail(s"$className must be a publicly visible type")
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def getPublicCompanion(className: String): Any = {
+    Try(
+      runtimeMirror
+        .reflectModule(runtimeMirror.staticModule(className))
+        .instance) match {
+      case Success(instance) => instance
+      case Failure(_) =>
+        fail(s"$className must expose a public companion")
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Reads a public case-class accessor by name on an arbitrary instance. */
+  private def readField(instance: Any, name: String): Any = {
+    Try(instance.getClass.getMethod(name)) match {
+      case Success(method) => method.invoke(instance)
+      case Failure(_: NoSuchMethodException) =>
+        fail(s"${instance.getClass.getName} must expose a public $name value")
+      case Failure(e) => throw e
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def methodAlternatives(
+      tpe: ru.Type,
+      name: String): Vector[ru.MethodSymbol] = {
+    val sym = tpe.decl(ru.TermName(name))
+    if (sym == ru.NoSymbol) Vector.empty
+    else sym.asTerm.alternatives.map(_.asMethod).toVector
+  }
+
+  private def jsonSerializers: Any = {
+    Try(
+      runtimeMirror
+        .reflectModule(runtimeMirror.staticModule(
+          "org.bitcoins.commons.serializers.JsonSerializers"))
+        .instance) match {
+      case Success(instance) => instance
+      case Failure(_) =>
+        fail("the JsonSerializers companion must be available")
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Resolves a public JSON decoder by name. Only public members of the
+    * documented `JsonSerializers` companion object are considered; private
+    * members are never accessed.
+    *
+    * The member names consulted below are part of the published contract:
+    * `getMemPoolInfoResultReads` decodes getmempoolinfo responses and
+    * `getMempoolFeerateDiagramEntryReads` decodes getmempoolfeeratediagram
+    * entries. The alternative accepted spellings exist purely for backwards
+    * compatibility and are not required.
+    */
+  private def resolvePublicReads(
+      errorMsg: String,
+      names: String*): Reads[Any] = {
+    val companion = jsonSerializers
+    names.iterator
+      .flatMap { name =>
+        Try(companion.getClass.getMethod(name)).toOption
+          .map(_.invoke(companion))
+      }
+      .collectFirst { case reads: Reads[_] =>
+        reads.asInstanceOf[Reads[Any]]
+      }
+      .getOrElse(fail(errorMsg))
+  }
+
+  /** Decodes a getmempoolinfo response through the public
+    * `GetMemPoolInfoResult` decoder.
+    */
+  private def decodeWithGetMemPoolInfoReads(json: JsValue): Any = {
+    val reads = resolvePublicReads(
+      "the public getmempoolinfo response decoder must be available",
+      "getMemPoolInfoResultReads",
+      "GetMemPoolInfoResultReads",
+      "getMempoolInfoResultReads"
+    )
+    json
+      .validate(reads)
+      .fold(errs => fail(s"response must decode: $errs"), identity)
+  }
+
+  /** Decodes each entry of a JSON array with the given decoder. */
+  private def decodeVectorWithReads(
+      reads: Reads[Any],
+      json: JsValue): Vector[Any] = {
+    json match {
+      case JsArray(values) =>
+        values.map { entry =>
+          entry
+            .validate(reads)
+            .fold(errs => fail(s"entry must decode: $errs"), identity)
+        }.toVector
+      case _ => fail("expected a JSON array of response entries")
+    }
+  }
+}

+package org.bitcoins.testkit.rpc
+
+import org.apache.pekko.actor.ActorSystem
+import org.apache.pekko.http.scaladsl.model.{
+  ContentTypes,
+  HttpEntity,
+  HttpRequest,
+  HttpResponse
+}
+import org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.{Client, MempoolRpc}
+import org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstance
+import play.api.libs.json._
+
+import scala.concurrent.Future
+import scala.concurrent.duration.DurationInt
+
+/** Test-only RPC client that records every outgoing bitcoind RPC request
+  * instead of talking to a real bitcoind, and answers it from a caller-supplied
+  * map of script results. Used to exercise the Bitcoin Core v31 mempool RPC
+  * behaviors without a running node.
+  */
+private[rpc] final class MempoolRpcV31FakeClient(
+    val recorded: scala.collection.mutable.ArrayBuffer[(String, JsArray)],
+    val responses: Map[String, JsValue],
+    override protected val instance: BitcoindInstance
+)(implicit override protected val system: ActorSystem)
+    extends Client
+    with MempoolRpc {
+
+  override def version: Future[org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.BitcoindVersion] =
+    Future.successful(org.bitcoins.rpc.client.common.BitcoindVersion.Unknown)
+
+  override protected def sendRequest(req: HttpRequest): Future[HttpResponse] = {
+    import system.dispatcher
+    req.entity.toStrict(5.seconds).map { strict =>
+      val json = Json.parse(strict.data.utf8String)
+      val command = (json \ "method").as[String]
+      val params = (json \ "params").as[JsArray]
+      recorded.append((command, params))
+      FakeBitcoindResponses.httpResponse(
+        FakeBitcoindResponses.successEnvelope(responses(command)))
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+/** Test-only helpers that build bitcoind JSON-RPC response envelopes. */
+private[rpc] object FakeBitcoindResponses {
+
+  def successEnvelope(result: JsValue): JsObject =
+    Json.obj("result" -> result, "error" -> JsNull, "id" -> JsNull)
+
+  def httpResponse(envelope: JsValue): HttpResponse =
+    HttpResponse(
+      entity =
+        HttpEntity(ContentTypes.`application/json`, Json.stringify(envelope)))
+}
+
+/** Test-only helpers that locate/create offline bitcoind instance descriptions
+  * used by the test-double clients. The instances point at a non-existent
+  * daemon; every request gets captured in memory instead.
+  */
+private[rpc] object MempoolRpcV31FakeInstances {
+
+  /** A bitcoind instance description pointing at non-existent local endpoints
+    * with password-based authentication. Never contacted by the test-double
+    * clients.
+    */
+  def apply()(implicit
+      system: ActorSystem): org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstanceRemote = {
+    val dir = java.nio.file.Files.createTempDirectory("bitcoind-v31-test")
+    sys.addShutdownHook(dir.toFile.delete())
+    implicit val appConfig: org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindRpcAppConfig =
+      org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindRpcAppConfig(
+        dir,
+        Vector.empty,
+        authCredentinalsOpt = Some(
+          org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindAuthCredentials
+            .PasswordBased("bitcoin-s-v31-test", "bitcoin-s-v31-test-password"))
+      )
+    org.bitcoins.rpc.config.BitcoindInstanceRemote(
+      network = org.bitcoins.core.config.RegTest,
+      uri = new java.net.URI("http://127.0.0.1:18333"),
+      rpcUri = new java.net.URI("http://127.0.0.1:18332")
+    )
+  }
+}

2. cli grpc tool for `DLCRoutes`
3. Test cases for both the cli and server-grpc endpoints

### Additional contract requirements

The DLC functionality must be exposed through the same gRPC server that serves
the existing common, chain, and node routes, and through the gRPC CLI tool that
talks to that server. DLC commands use the ordinary server authentication,
request handling, and JSON/hex formatting conventions.

## Public DLC gRPC surface

The direct gRPC protocol is a service named `DLCRoutes`, with generated Scala
client `org.bitcoins.server.grpc.DLCRoutesClient`. Its unary client calls and
request messages are:

| Client call | Request message | CLI command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getDlcHostAddress` | `GetDlcHostAddressRequest` | `getdlchostaddress` |
| `acceptDlc` | `AcceptDlcRequest` | `acceptdlc` |
| `createContractInfo` | `CreateContractInfoRequest` | `createcontractinfo` |
| `incomingOffersList` | `IncomingOffersListRequest` | `incoming-offers-list` |
| `offerAdd` | `OfferAddRequest` | `addoffer` |
| `offerRemove` | `OfferRemoveRequest` | `removeoffer` |
| `offerSend` | `OfferSendRequest` | `offer-send` |
| `contactsList` | `ContactsListRequest` | `contacts-list` |
| `contactAdd` | `ContactAddRequest` | `contact-add` |
| `dlcContactAdd` | `DlcContactAddRequest` | `dlc-contact-add` |

These service, call, and message names are part of the wire-facing gRPC
contract. Response entries use the corresponding camel-case names: `address`,
`acceptHex`, `contractInfoHex`, `offers`, `offerHash`, `tempContractId`,
`contacts`, `result`, `dlcId`, and `contactId`. An incoming-offer entry exposes
`hash`, `receivedAt`, `peer`, `message`, and `offerTlvHex`; a contact entry
exposes its alias, address, and memo.

For server integration, `ServerGrpc` accepts its DLC node dependency at
construction through the `dlcNodeF` input as a future DLC-node value. This
allows the DLC routes to be served with the supplied node.

## Required behavior

- `getdlchostaddress` returns the DLC node listening address as `host:port`.
- `incoming-offers-list` lists incoming offers. With none registered it returns an
  empty list. `addoffer` registers a serialized offer plus peer and note, returns its
  hash, and makes the same hash, peer, note, receipt time, and serialized offer
  observable in the list. `removeoffer` echoes the requested hash and removes a
  previously registered offer.
- `offer-send` sends an offer or temporary contract id to a `host:port` peer
  with a message and returns the temporary contract id.
- `contact-add` stores an alias, peer address, and memo and reports success;
  `contacts-list` reports those stored values. `dlc-contact-add` associates a
  DLC-id hash with a peer address and returns that id and contact address.
- `createcontractinfo` accepts an oracle-announcement hex string, total
  collateral in sats, and contract descriptor. It returns serialized contract
  info whose decoded collateral and descriptor match the request and whose
  oracle information corresponds to the announcement outcomes.
- `acceptdlc` accepts the offer, peer address, and optional payout/change
  addresses. A valid request is delegated to the DLC node's offer-acceptance
  handling; when the node completes the acceptance, the serialized acceptance
  it produced is exposed verbatim as `acceptHex` by the gRPC route and is
  printed verbatim by the gRPC CLI command. Malformed requests fail before any
  acceptance is delegated.

For every route, missing, empty, or unparsable required input (including
malformed offer, announcement, descriptor, address, temporary-contract-id, DLC
id, or hash hex) fails with gRPC status `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. This applies to
acceptdlc, createcontractinfo, offer-add, offer-remove, offer-send,
contact-add, and dlc-contact-add alike. CLI commands retain their ordinary
argument-validation behavior before a request is sent.

+// DLCRoutes provides DLC RPC endpoints for the Bitcoin-S gRPC server.
+service DLCRoutes {
+  rpc GetDlcHostAddress(GetDlcHostAddressRequest)
+      returns (GetDlcHostAddressResponse);
+  rpc AcceptDlc(AcceptDlcRequest) returns (AcceptDlcResponse);
+  rpc CreateContractInfo(CreateContractInfoRequest)
+      returns (CreateContractInfoResponse);
+  rpc IncomingOffersList(IncomingOffersListRequest)
+      returns (IncomingOfferListResponse);
+  rpc OfferAdd(OfferAddRequest) returns (OfferAddResponse);
+  rpc OfferRemove(OfferRemoveRequest) returns (OfferRemoveResponse);
+  rpc OfferSend(OfferSendRequest) returns (OfferSendResponse);
+  rpc ContactsList(ContactsListRequest) returns (ContactsListResponse);
+  rpc ContactAdd(ContactAddRequest) returns (ContactAddResponse);
+  rpc DlcContactAdd(DlcContactAddRequest) returns (DlcContactAddResponse);
+}
+
+message GetDlcHostAddressRequest {}
+
+message GetDlcHostAddressResponse {
+  string address = 1;
+}
+
+message AcceptDlcRequest {
+  string offer = 1;
+  string peer_addr = 2;
+  optional string external_payout_address = 3;
+  optional string external_change_address = 4;
+}
+
+message AcceptDlcResponse {
+  string accept_hex = 1;
+}
+
+message CreateContractInfoRequest {
+  string announcement = 1;
+  int64 total_collateral_sats = 2;
+  string contract_descriptor_hex = 3;
+}
+
+message CreateContractInfoResponse {
+  string contract_info_hex = 1;
+}
+
+message IncomingOffersListRequest {}
+
+message IncomingOffer {
+  string hash = 1;
+  int64 received_at = 2;
+  optional string peer = 3;
+  optional string message = 4;
+  string offer_tlv_hex = 5;
+}
+
+message IncomingOfferListResponse {
+  repeated IncomingOffer offers = 1;
+}
+
+message OfferAddRequest {
+  string offer = 1;
+  optional string peer = 2;
+  optional string message = 3;
+}
+
+message OfferAddResponse {
+  string offer_hash = 1;
+}
+
+message OfferRemoveRequest {
+  string hash = 1;
+}
+
+message OfferRemoveResponse {
+  string offer_hash = 1;
+}
+
+message OfferSendRequest {
+  string offer_or_temp_contract_id = 1;
+  string peer_address = 2;
+  string message = 3;
+}
+
+message OfferSendResponse {
+  string temp_contract_id = 1;
+}
+
+message ContactsListRequest {}
+
+message Contact {
+  string alias = 1;
+  string address = 2;
+  string memo = 3;
+}
+
+message ContactsListResponse {
+  repeated Contact contacts = 1;
+}
+
+message ContactAddRequest {
+  string alias = 1;
+  string address = 2;
+  string memo = 3;
+}
+
+message ContactAddResponse {
+  string result = 1;
+}
+
+message DlcContactAddRequest {
+  string dlc_id = 1;
+  string address = 2;
+}
+
+message DlcContactAddResponse {
+  string dlc_id = 1;
+  string contact_id = 2;
+}

+package org.bitcoins.server.grpc
+
+import io.grpc.Status
+import org.bitcoins.commons.jsonmodels.server.{OfferAdd, OfferRemove, OfferSend}
+import org.bitcoins.commons.rpc.{
+  AcceptDLC,
+  ContactAdd,
+  CreateContractInfo,
+  DLCContactAdd
+}
+import org.bitcoins.core.api.dlc.node.DLCNodeApi
+import org.bitcoins.core.api.dlc.wallet.db.{DLCContactDb, IncomingDLCOfferDb}
+import org.bitcoins.core.protocol.dlc.models.{
+  EnumSingleOracleInfo,
+  NumericSingleOracleInfo,
+  SingleContractInfo
+}
+import org.bitcoins.core.protocol.tlv.{
+  EnumEventDescriptorV0TLV,
+  NumericEventDescriptorTLV
+}
+import ujson.{Null, Num, Str}
+
+import scala.concurrent.{ExecutionContext, Future}
+import scala.util.{Failure, Success, Try}
+
+/** gRPC service implementation for the DLCRoutes endpoints.
+  *
+  * This implements the same functionality as [[org.bitcoins.server.DLCRoutes]]
+  * but over gRPC instead of HTTP.
+  */
+class DLCGrpcRoutes(dlcNode: DLCNodeApi)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext)
+    extends DLCRoutes {
+
+  private def invalidArg(
+      commandName: String,
+      err: Throwable): RuntimeException = {
+    Status.INVALID_ARGUMENT
+      .withDescription(s"Invalid arguments for $commandName: ${err.getMessage}")
+      .withCause(err)
+      .asRuntimeException()
+  }
+
+  private def parseCommand[T](
+      params: Seq[ujson.Value],
+      commandName: String,
+      parse: ujson.Arr => Try[T]): Future[T] = {
+    parse(ujson.Arr.from(params)) match {
+      case Success(value) => Future.successful(value)
+      case Failure(err)   => Future.failed(invalidArg(commandName, err))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def getDlcHostAddress(
+      in: GetDlcHostAddressRequest): Future[GetDlcHostAddressResponse] = {
+    dlcNode.getHostAddress.map { addr =>
+      val str = s"${addr.getHostName}:${addr.getPort}"
+      GetDlcHostAddressResponse(address = str)
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def acceptDlc(in: AcceptDlcRequest): Future[AcceptDlcResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(
+      Str(in.offer),
+      Str(in.peerAddr),
+      in.externalPayoutAddress.map(Str.apply).getOrElse(Null),
+      in.externalChangeAddress.map(Str.apply).getOrElse(Null)
+    )
+
+    parseCommand(params, "acceptdlc", AcceptDLC.fromJsArr).flatMap {
+      case AcceptDLC(offer, address, payoutAddressOpt, changeAddressOpt) =>
+        dlcNode
+          .acceptDLCOffer(address, offer, payoutAddressOpt, changeAddressOpt)
+          .map(accept => AcceptDlcResponse(acceptHex = accept.toMessage.hex))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def createContractInfo(
+      in: CreateContractInfoRequest): Future[CreateContractInfoResponse] = {
+    val contractDescriptor =
+      Str(in.contractDescriptorHex)
+    val params = Vector(
+      Str(in.announcement),
+      Num(in.totalCollateralSats.toDouble),
+      contractDescriptor
+    )
+    parseCommand(params, "createcontractinfo", CreateContractInfo.fromJsArr)
+      .map { create =>
+        val oracleInfo = create.announcementTLV.eventTLV.eventDescriptor match {
+          case _: NumericEventDescriptorTLV =>
+            NumericSingleOracleInfo(create.announcementTLV)
+          case _: EnumEventDescriptorV0TLV =>
+            EnumSingleOracleInfo(create.announcementTLV)
+        }
+        val contractInfo = SingleContractInfo(
+          create.totalCollateral,
+          create.contractDescriptor,
+          oracleInfo
+        )
+        CreateContractInfoResponse(contractInfoHex = contractInfo.hex)
+      }
+  }
+
+  override def incomingOffersList(
+      in: IncomingOffersListRequest): Future[IncomingOfferListResponse] = {
+    dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling.listIncomingDLCOffers().map { offers =>
+      def toOffer(io: IncomingDLCOfferDb): IncomingOffer = {
+        IncomingOffer(
+          hash = io.hash.hex,
+          receivedAt = io.receivedAt.getEpochSecond,
+          peer = io.peer,
+          message = io.message,
+          offerTlvHex = io.offerTLV.hex
+        )
+      }
+
+      IncomingOfferListResponse(offers = offers.map(toOffer))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def offerAdd(in: OfferAddRequest): Future[OfferAddResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(
+      Str(in.offer),
+      in.peer.map(Str.apply).getOrElse(Null),
+      in.message.map(Str.apply).getOrElse(Null)
+    )
+
+    parseCommand(params, "offer-add", OfferAdd.fromJsArr).flatMap { offerAdd =>
+      dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling
+        .registerIncomingDLCOffer(
+          offerAdd.offerTLV,
+          offerAdd.peer,
+          offerAdd.message
+        )
+        .map(hash => OfferAddResponse(offerHash = hash.hex))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def offerRemove(
+      in: OfferRemoveRequest): Future[OfferRemoveResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(Str(in.hash))
+
+    parseCommand(params, "offer-remove", OfferRemove.fromJsArr).flatMap {
+      offerRemove =>
+        dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling
+          .rejectIncomingDLCOffer(offerRemove.hash)
+          .map(_ => OfferRemoveResponse(offerHash = offerRemove.hash.hex))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def offerSend(in: OfferSendRequest): Future[OfferSendResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(
+      Str(in.offerOrTempContractId),
+      Str(in.peerAddress),
+      Str(in.message)
+    )
+
+    parseCommand(params, "offer-send", OfferSend.fromJsArr).flatMap {
+      case OfferSend(remoteAddress, message, offerE) =>
+        offerE match {
+          case Left(offerTLV) =>
+            dlcNode
+              .sendDLCOffer(remoteAddress, message, offerTLV)
+              .map(tempContractId =>
+                OfferSendResponse(tempContractId = tempContractId.hex))
+          case Right(tempContractId) =>
+            dlcNode
+              .sendDLCOffer(remoteAddress, message, tempContractId)
+              .map(tempContractId =>
+                OfferSendResponse(tempContractId = tempContractId.hex))
+        }
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def contactsList(
+      in: ContactsListRequest): Future[ContactsListResponse] = {
+    dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling.listDLCContacts().map { contacts =>
+      def toContact(c: DLCContactDb): Contact = {
+        Contact(
+          alias = c.alias,
+          address = s"${c.address.getHostString}:${c.address.getPort}",
+          memo = c.memo
+        )
+      }
+
+      ContactsListResponse(contacts = contacts.map(toContact))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def contactAdd(in: ContactAddRequest): Future[ContactAddResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(Str(in.alias), Str(in.address), Str(in.memo))
+
+    parseCommand(params, "contact-add", ContactAdd.fromJsArr).flatMap {
+      contactAdd =>
+        dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling
+          .addDLCContact(contactAdd.toDLCContactDb)
+          .map(_ => ContactAddResponse(result = "ok"))
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def dlcContactAdd(
+      in: DlcContactAddRequest): Future[DlcContactAddResponse] = {
+    val params = Vector(Str(in.dlcId), Str(in.address))
+
+    parseCommand(params, "dlc-contact-add", DLCContactAdd.fromJsArr).flatMap {
+      dlcContactAdd =>
+        dlcNode.incomingOfferHandling
+          .addDLCContactMapping(dlcContactAdd.dlcId, dlcContactAdd.address)
+          .map { _ =>
+            val dlcId = dlcContactAdd.dlcId.hex
+            val contactId =
+              dlcContactAdd.address.getHostString + ":" + dlcContactAdd.address.getPort
+            DlcContactAddResponse(dlcId = dlcId, contactId = contactId)
+          }
+    }
+  }
+}

+  /** Sends the contract descriptor in its TLV hex encoding and, only when the

+  private def createContractInfoResponse(
+      client: PekkoGrpcClient,
+      announcement: String,
+      descriptorHex: String,
+      descriptorJson: String): Future[Any] = {
+    def send(descriptor: String): Future[Any] =
+      request("org.bitcoins.server.grpc.CreateContractInfoRequest$",
+              announcement,
+              Long.box(100000000L),
+              descriptor)
+        .flatMap(req => invoke(client, "createContractInfo", req))
+    send(descriptorHex).recoverWith {
+      case e: StatusRuntimeException
+          if e.getStatus.getCode == Status.Code.INVALID_ARGUMENT =>
+        send(descriptorJson)
+    }
+  }

+/** Reflection-based helpers for exercising the DLC gRPC endpoints.
+  *
+  * The DLC gRPC routes (and the generated `DLCRoutesClient` /
+  * `DLCRoutesHandler`, plus the `dlcNodeF` `ServerGrpc` constructor parameter)
+  * only exist once the DLC gRPC routes are implemented. Tests locate and invoke
+  * them reflectively so the surrounding test code compiles on revisions that
+  * predate the DLC gRPC implementation; on such revisions the tests fail as
+  * assertions rather than failing to compile.
+  */
+object DLCGrpcTestSupport {
+
+  /** Fully-qualified name of the generated pekko-grpc client for the DLC routes
+    * service.
+    */
+  val dlcRoutesClientClassName: String =
+    "org.bitcoins.server.grpc.DLCRoutesClient"
+
+  /** Locates the generated `DLCRoutesClient` class, if it exists. */
+  def dlcRoutesClientClass: Try[Class[_]] =
+    Try(Class.forName(dlcRoutesClientClassName))
+
+  /** Builds a `DLCRoutesClient` connected to (host, port) via its generated
+    * companion `apply(GrpcClientSettings)(ActorSystem)` factory.
+    */
+  def newDLCRoutesClient(host: String, port: Int)(implicit
+      system: ActorSystem): Try[PekkoGrpcClient] = {
+    dlcRoutesClientClass.flatMap { _ =>
+      Try {
+        val companion = Class.forName(dlcRoutesClientClassName + "$")
+        val module = companion.getField("MODULE$").get(null)
+        val settings = GrpcClientSettings
+          .connectToServiceAt(host, port)
+          .withTls(false)
+        val applyMethod = companion.getMethods.find { m =>
+          m.getName == "apply" &&
+          m.getParameterCount == 2 &&
+          classOf[GrpcClientSettings].isAssignableFrom(m.getParameterTypes()(0))
+        }.get
+        applyMethod
+          .invoke(module, settings, system)
+          .asInstanceOf[PekkoGrpcClient]
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Builds a generated request message from its semantic fields, using the
+    * generated default instance for fields not supplied by a test. If product
+    * field names are available, values are matched by meaning rather than by
+    * constructor position.
+    */
+  def buildRequest(companionClassName: String, args: AnyRef*): Try[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      val companion = Class.forName(companionClassName)
+      val module = companion.getField("MODULE$").get(null)
+      val defaultInstance = companion.getMethod("defaultInstance").invoke(module)
+      if (args.isEmpty) defaultInstance
+      else {
+        val product = defaultInstance.asInstanceOf[Product]
+        val fieldNames = product.productElementNames.toVector
+        val values = product.productIterator.map(_.asInstanceOf[AnyRef]).toArray
+        val semanticNames = requestFieldRoles(companionClassName, args.length)
+        args.zipWithIndex.foreach { case (value, argIndex) =>
+          val aliases = semanticNames.lift(argIndex).getOrElse(Set.empty[String])
+          val targetIndex = fieldNames.indexWhere { fieldName =>
+            aliases.contains(normalizeField(fieldName))
+          }
+          val index = if (targetIndex >= 0) targetIndex else argIndex
+          require(index < values.length, "request has fewer fields than supplied values")
+          values(index) = value
+        }
+        val factory = companion.getMethods.find { method =>
+          (method.getName == "of" || method.getName == "apply") &&
+          method.getParameterCount == values.length &&
+          adaptArgs(method, values.toSeq).isDefined
+        }.getOrElse {
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            s"$companionClassName factory for ${values.length} fields")
+        }
+        adaptArgs(factory, values.toSeq).get._2 match {
+          case adapted => factory.invoke(module, adapted: _*)
+        }
+      }
+    }
+
+  private def normalizeField(name: String): String =
+    name.filter(_.isLetterOrDigit).toLowerCase
+
+  /** Field-name aliases corresponding to the arguments used by route tests. */
+  private def requestFieldRoles(
+      companionClassName: String,
+      argumentCount: Int): Vector[Set[String]] = {

+  /** Adapts `args` to the parameter types of `method` when possible: plain
+    * values are wrapped into `Some` where the parameter expects an `Option`,
+    * and the placeholder `EmptyOption` is passed as a plain `None`. Returns
+    * `None` when the arguments cannot be adapted.
+    */
+  private def adaptArgs(
+      method: java.lang.reflect.Method,
+      args: Seq[AnyRef]): Option[(java.lang.reflect.Method, Seq[AnyRef])] = {
+    val adapted: Seq[Option[AnyRef]] =
+      method.getParameterTypes.toSeq.zip(args).map { case (t, arg) =>
+        val wantsOption =
+          t == classOf[Option[_]] || t.isAssignableFrom(classOf[Some[_]])
+        arg match {
+          case EmptyOption if wantsOption    => Some(None)
+          case EmptyOption if t == classOf[String] => Some("")
+          case EmptyOption                   => None
+          case null if !t.isPrimitive        => Some(null)
+          case None | Some(_) if wantsOption => Some(arg)
+          case None | Some(_)                => None
+          case _ if wantsOption              => Some(Some(arg))
+          case _ if compatible(t, arg)       => Some(arg)
+          case _                             => None
+        }
+      }
+    if (adapted.forall(_.isDefined))
+      Some(method -> adapted.map(_.get))
+    else None
+  }
+
+  /** Placeholder marking an omitted optional argument when building a request.
+    */
+  case object EmptyOption
+
+  /** Whether `arg` can be passed to a parameter of type `t`. */
+  private def compatible(t: Class[_], arg: AnyRef): Boolean =
+    arg match {
+      case _: java.lang.String => t.isAssignableFrom(classOf[String])
+      case _: java.lang.Long =>
+        t == java.lang.Long.TYPE || t == classOf[java.lang.Long]
+      case _: java.lang.Integer =>
+        t == java.lang.Integer.TYPE || t == classOf[java.lang.Integer]
+      case _: java.lang.Boolean =>
+        t == java.lang.Boolean.TYPE || t == classOf[java.lang.Boolean]
+      case _ => t.isAssignableFrom(arg.getClass)
+    }

+    * be a runtime proxy, so presence is detected through the route calls

+  def hasAllRouteCalls(client: PekkoGrpcClient): Boolean = {

+    routeCallNames.forall(available.contains)

+  def isDlcRoutesClient(client: PekkoGrpcClient): Boolean =

+  /** Reflectively invokes a single-argument DLC client route returning a
+    * Future.
+    */
+  def invokeRoute(
+      client: PekkoGrpcClient,
+      methodName: String,
+      request: AnyRef): Try[Future[Any]] =
+    Try {
+      val method = client.getClass.getMethods.find { m =>
+        m.getName == methodName && m.getParameterCount == 1
+      }.get
+      method.invoke(client, request).asInstanceOf[Future[Any]]
+    }
+
+  /** Reads a repeated/collection field from a response message, returned as a
+    * Vector of the element messages.
+    */
+  def collectionField(response: Any, field: String): Try[Vector[Any]] =
+    Try {
+      val m = response.getClass.getMethods.find { mm =>
+        mm.getName == field && mm.getParameterCount == 0
+      }.get
+      m.invoke(response).asInstanceOf[scala.collection.Seq[Any]].toVector
+    }
+
+  /** Reads an optional String field/parameterless accessor from a response
+    * message, returning the underlying optional value (e.g. the contents of a
+    * proto `optional string` field).
+    */
+  def optionalStringField(response: Any, field: String): Try[Option[String]] =
+    Try {
+      val m = response.getClass.getMethods.find { mm =>
+        mm.getName == field && mm.getParameterCount == 0
+      }.get
+      m.invoke(response) match {
+        case value: String    => Some(value)
+        case value: Option[_] => value.map(_.asInstanceOf[String])
+        case null             => None
+        case other =>
+          throw new ClassCastException(s"$field is not a string value: $other")
+      }
+    }
+
+  /** Reads a String field/parameterless accessor from a response message. */
+  def stringField(response: Any, field: String): Try[String] =
+    Try {
+      val m = response.getClass.getMethods.find { mm =>
+        mm.getName == field && mm.getParameterCount == 0
+      }.get
+      m.invoke(response).asInstanceOf[String]
+    }
+
+  /** Reads the String values of every listed field that the response message
+    * declares, skipping the ones it does not declare. Used to find a held value
+    * that different response spellings expose under different field names.
+    */
+  def stringFieldAnyOf(
+      response: Any,
+      fields: Seq[String]): Try[Vector[String]] =
+    Try {
+      fields.flatMap { field =>
+        response.getClass.getMethods
+          .find(m => m.getName == field && m.getParameterCount == 0)
+          .map(_.invoke(response))
+          .collect { case s: String => s }
+      }.toVector
+    }
+
+  /** Reads a numeric (Long-compatible) field/parameterless accessor from a
+    * response message, widening integer values as needed.
+    */
+  def longField(response: Any, field: String): Try[Long] =
+    Try {
+      val m = response.getClass.getMethods.find { mm =>
+        mm.getName == field && mm.getParameterCount == 0
+      }.get
+      m.invoke(response) match {
+        case l: java.lang.Long    => l.longValue()
+        case i: java.lang.Integer => i.longValue()
+        case other =>
+          throw new ClassCastException(
+            s"$field is not a Long-compatible value: $other")
+      }
+    }
+

problem_statement:
How to preserve position information after parsing?
Hi @brandonchinn178! I wish to use KDL for a tool that would read and validate user-provided configuration files.


Down the validation pipeline, I want to be able to raise data validation errors from otherwise well-formed documents, and point the end-user to the position where the invalid data is.

I'm not quite sure where to begin, though.

### Additional contract requirements

# Opt-in source locations for parsed KDL

The parser supports an opt-in mode that records the source range of every
parsed syntax-tree element. This allows validation performed after parsing to
report the location of the offending document element.

## Parsing API

The public configurable entry points are:

```haskell
KDL.parseWith     :: KDL.ParseConfig -> Text -> Either Text KDL.Document
KDL.parseFileWith :: KDL.ParseConfig -> FilePath -> IO (Either Text KDL.Document)
```

`KDL.ParseConfig` is an exported record with these fields:

```haskell
KDL.filepath     :: FilePath
KDL.includeSpans :: Bool
```

It has a `Default` instance. `KDL.def :: KDL.ParseConfig` has an empty
`filepath` and `includeSpans = False`; callers request locations with, for
example, `KDL.def { KDL.includeSpans = True }`. `parseFileWith` uses the path
passed to it as the parser's `filepath`, so parse errors identify that file.

The existing `KDL.parse` and `KDL.parseFile` entry points remain available and
are equivalent to parsing with locations disabled. Parsing done by the
existing decoder entry points (`KDL.decodeWith` and `KDL.decodeFileWith`) also
continues to use this location-disabled behavior.

## Location data in the AST

`KDL.Document` remains an alias for `KDL.NodeList`. Each AST element stores
formatting and location metadata in an exported `ext` record. The exported
extension types are:

- `KDL.NodeListExtension`
- `KDL.NodeExtension`
- `KDL.EntryExtension`
- `KDL.ValueExtension`
- `KDL.AnnExtension`
- `KDL.IdentifierExtension`

Each extension record has a `format :: Maybe ...Format` field and a
`span :: KDL.Span` field. Thus source locations are available for documents
and nested node lists, nodes, entries, values, type annotations, and
identifiers. With `OverloadedRecordDot`, for example, a node's range is read as
`node.ext.span` and its name's range as `node.name.ext.span`; callers may also
pattern-match the exported records.

`KDL.Span` is an exported record:

```haskell
data Span = Span
  { startLine :: Int
  , startCol  :: Int
  , endLine   :: Int
  , endCol    :: Int
  }
```

It has `Show`, `Eq`, `Ord`, and `Default` instances.

## Span semantics

A non-default span is an inclusive source range:

- Lines and columns are 1-based.
- Columns count decoded characters, not UTF-8 bytes.
- Leading whitespace and comments before an element are not part of that
  element's span.
- An identifier covers its complete identifier token. A type annotation covers
  its surrounding parentheses, while the annotation's identifier has its own
  inner span.
- A value covers its optional type annotation through the end of its value
  token. A positional entry has the same range as its value; a property entry
  covers its key through its value.
- A node covers its optional type annotation or name through its final entry or
  children block and includes an explicit node terminator. When the terminator
  is a line break, the inclusive end coordinate is the last source character
  before that line break.
- A nested node list covers its contained nodes, excluding the surrounding
  braces and indentation before its first node. A document span covers its
  parsed node sequence using the same node-list rules.

When `includeSpans` is `False`, every element instead carries
`KDL.def :: KDL.Span`, whose four coordinates are all zero. Apart from the
extension metadata, enabling spans does not change the parsed tree.

## Constructed values and formatting compatibility

The former per-element `format` metadata is preserved as the `format` member
of the corresponding extension record. Every extension type has a `Default`
instance with `format = Nothing` and `span = KDL.def`, so callers constructing
AST values can use `ext = KDL.def`. `KDL.toIdentifier` likewise creates an
identifier with default formatting and a zero span. Rendering and decoding
continue to use the formatting member of `ext`; recording spans does not alter
the rendered KDL or decoded values.

+-- | Build the expected span of an element that starts at line @l1@, column
+-- @c1@ and ends at line @l2@, column @c2@.
+spanBetween :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> KDL.Span
+spanBetween l1 c1 l2 c2 =
+  KDL.def
+    { KDL.startLine = l1
+    , KDL.startCol = c1
+    , KDL.endLine = l2
+    , KDL.endCol = c2
+    }

+-- | Build the expected span of an element fully contained in one column of
+-- a single line.
+spanInline :: Int -> Int -> KDL.Span
+spanInline l c = spanBetween l c l c

problem_statement:
Validate that parties exist for featured app right votes

### Additional contract requirements

## Party lookup endpoint

For validating parties in featured app right proposals, the SV app exposes an HTTP lookup that
maps a party to the participant hosting it:

- `GET /v0/admin/sv/party-to-participant/{party_id}` looks up a party ID and returns the
  participant that hosts the party.
- The party ID is transported as a single URL-safe (percent-encoded) path parameter, because it
  contains characters (such as `::`) that are not valid unencoded path characters. The server
  decodes the full path parameter into the party ID string.
- The lookup matches party IDs exactly. A request for a strict prefix, a superset, or any other
  non-identical string of an existing party ID is not a match.
- On an exact match for a currently allocated party the endpoint responds `200 OK` with a JSON
  body whose `participant_id` field is a non-empty string.
- For any party ID that is not currently allocated the endpoint responds `404 Not Found`.

## Granting a featured app right: SV governance proposal form

- The provider field of the "Grant Featured App Right" form accepts only syntactically valid
  party IDs of the form `<identifier>::<fingerprint>`, where both parts are non-empty. A value
  that is not of that form is rejected with the error message
  "Invalid PartyId format. Expected format: identifier::fingerprint" and no party-existence
  lookup is performed for it.
- After a syntactically valid party ID is entered, the form asynchronously checks, via the
  party-to-participant lookup described above, whether that party exists. While this check is
  pending the form shows the indicator "Validating provider..."; the indicator is removed once
  the check completes.
- If the lookup reports that the provider does not exist, the form displays "Provider party not
  found on ledger" and keeps the proposal submit button disabled. If it succeeds, that error is
  absent and the form permits progressing to proposal review.
- Provider-existence validation applies to granting a featured app right only. The revoke form
  neither performs this lookup nor requires the provider field to be a party ID.

```lua

```

+--- @param on_selected fun(provider_name: agentic.UserConfig.ProviderName|nil) Callback that will be called with the selected provider name, if any
+function SessionRegistry.select_provider(on_selected)
+    local available_providers = ACPHealth.get_default_provider_names()
+
+    --- @class _ProviderStatus
+    --- @field name string
+    --- @field installed boolean
+
+    --- @type _ProviderStatus[]
+    local sorted_providers = {}
+
+    --- @type _ProviderStatus[]
+    local not_installed = {}
+
+    for _, provider_name in ipairs(available_providers) do
+        local provider_config = Config.acp_providers[provider_name]
+        if
+            provider_config
+            and ACPHealth.is_command_available(provider_config.command)
+        then
+            sorted_providers[#sorted_providers + 1] = {
+                name = provider_name,
+                installed = true,
+            }
+        else
+            not_installed[#not_installed + 1] = {
+                name = provider_name,
+                installed = false,
+            }
+        end
+    end
+
+    vim.list_extend(sorted_providers, not_installed)
+
+    vim.ui.select(sorted_providers, {

+
+            if label == Config.provider then
+                label = label .. " (current)"

+                label = label .. " (default)"
+            end
+
+            label = label
+                .. (item.installed and " â available" or " â not installed")
+
+            return label
+        end,

@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+-- Rebench audit wrapper around mini.test.
+-- Runs a specific test file and emits exactly one parser-readable line per
+-- executed test case on stdout in the forms accepted by parse_log_lua_nvim:
+--   Success || <stable unique test name>
+--   Fail || <stable unique test name>
+--   Skip || <stable unique test name>
+-- Lines are unindented and free of ANSI color. The process exits non-zero if
+-- any case fails and zero when all selected cases pass. Statuses reflect the
+-- real mini.test execution outcome (no fabricated lines): a line is printed
+-- only when mini.test assigns the case its final state.
+local M = {}
+
+local function clean(str)
+    -- Collapse whitespace/newlines so each case stays a single unindented line
+    return (tostring(str):gsub("%s+", " "))
+end
+
+--- Run a single test file with per-case parser-readable reporting.
+--- @param file string
+function M.run_file(file)
+    if not file or file == "" then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: No file specified\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        return
+    end
+    if not vim.uv.fs_stat(file) then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: File not found: " .. file .. "\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        return
+    end
+
+    local MiniTest = require("mini.test")
+    local all_cases
+    local seen = {}
+    local n_fail = 0
+    local printed = 0
+
+    local reporter = {}
+
+    function reporter.start(cases)
+        all_cases = cases
+    end
+
+    function reporter.update(case_num)
+        local case = all_cases and all_cases[case_num]
+        if case == nil or case.exec == nil then
+            return
+        end
+
+        -- Only report the case once mini.test assigns its final state.
+        local state = case.exec.state
+        if
+            state ~= "Pass"
+            and state ~= "Pass with notes"
+            and state ~= "Fail"
+            and state ~= "Fail with notes"
+        then
+            return
+        end
+
+        -- Stable, unique name: full describe/it hierarchy joined.
+        local name = table.concat(case.desc or {}, " | ")
+        if name == "" then
+            name = "case " .. tostring(case_num)
+        end
+        local count = seen[name] or 0
+        seen[name] = count + 1
+        if count > 0 then
+            name = string.format("%s #%d", name, count + 1)
+        end
+
+        local outcome
+        if state == "Fail" or state == "Fail with notes" then
+            outcome = "Fail"
+            n_fail = n_fail + 1
+        else
+            outcome = "Success"
+        end
+
+        io.stdout:write(outcome .. " || " .. clean(name) .. "\n")
+        io.stdout:flush()
+        printed = printed + 1
+    end
+
+    function reporter.finish()
+        io.stdout:flush()
+        -- mini.test execution is scheduled asynchronously; decide the exit
+        -- status here, after every case has been processed.
+        if printed == 0 then
+            io.stderr:write("Error: no test cases executed in " .. file .. "\n")
+            vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        elseif n_fail > 0 then
+            vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        else
+            vim.cmd("qall!")
+        end
+    end
+
+    local ok, err = pcall(function()
+        MiniTest.run_file(file, {
+            execute = {
+                reporter = reporter,
+                -- Deterministic: no retries so each case yields one outcome.
+                n_retry = 1,
+            },
+        })
+    end)
+
+    if not ok then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+    end
+end
+
+return M

### Additional contract requirements

# Typed data: query result sets and document types

This addendum is part of the public contract for this issue. It describes only
observable behavior.

## Supported usage

The typed query result set APIs — `asTypedStream<D>()`, `allTypedResults<D>()`
and `asTypedIterable<D>()` on a query result set — convert each query result
into an instance of a registered typed dictionary type `D`. Using them with a
registered typed dictionary type keeps working: each emitted object is
constructed from the dictionary of the corresponding query result.

A typed document cannot be reconstructed from a query result. Documents have
internal state that query results do not contain and must instead be loaded
from the database (or a typed collection). Therefore using a typed *document*
type — in its immutable or its mutable form — with the typed query result set
APIs is not supported.

For every typed document type created with the annotations-based code
generator, a companion dictionary type is generated together with the document
type: the result of generating the code for a typed document type additionally
contains a typed dictionary type, and a generated typed database which is
declared to support a document type also supports that document type's
companion dictionary type through its typed data adapter. The companion
dictionary type is a typed dictionary type like any other: it can be used with
the typed query result set APIs, where it exposes the queried properties of
the document, and its data can be converted back into the document type it
belongs to through the properties the two types share.

## Required behavior

When a registered document type (immutable or mutable) is used where the typed
query result set APIs (or, equivalently, the typed data registry lookup they
rely on) require a typed dictionary type:
