contract_addendum:
# Typed data: query result sets and document types

This addendum is part of the public contract for this issue. It describes only
observable behavior.

## Supported usage

The typed query result set APIs — `asTypedStream<D>()`, `allTypedResults<D>()`
and `asTypedIterable<D>()` on a query result set — convert each query result
into an instance of a registered typed dictionary type `D`. Using them with a
registered typed dictionary type keeps working: each emitted object is
constructed from the dictionary of the corresponding query result.

A typed document cannot be reconstructed from a query result. Documents have
internal state that query results do not contain and must instead be loaded
from the database (or a typed collection). Therefore using a typed *document*
type — in its immutable or its mutable form — with the typed query result set
APIs is not supported.

For every typed document type created with the annotations-based code
generator, a companion dictionary type is generated together with the document
type: the result of generating the code for a typed document type additionally
contains a typed dictionary type, and a generated typed database which is
declared to support a document type also supports that document type's
companion dictionary type through its typed data adapter. The companion
dictionary type is a typed dictionary type like any other: it can be used with
the typed query result set APIs, where it exposes the queried properties of
the document, and its data can be converted back into the document type it
belongs to through the properties the two types share.

## Required behavior

When a registered document type (immutable or mutable) is used where the typed
query result set APIs (or, equivalently, the typed data registry lookup they
rely on) require a typed dictionary type:

1. A `TypedDataException` must be signalled. For `asTypedStream`, it is
   delivered either by throwing from the API call or as an error of the
   returned stream; for `allTypedResults` either by throwing or through the
   returned future; and for `asTypedIterable` either by throwing or while
   consuming the returned iterable.
2. The exception must not behave as if the type were unregistered: its error
   code must not be `TypedDataErrorCode.unknownType` and its message must not
   claim that the type "is not a known typed data type".
3. The exception message must name the offending document type and must
   contain the word "dictionary" (any capitalization), pointing the user to
   the companion dictionary type alternative as an actionable remedy.

This requirement applies equally to the immutable and to the mutable form of
a registered document type.

Types that are registered as typed dictionary types must continue to be
resolved normally by the typed query result set APIs, and types that are
registered neither as dictionary types nor as document types must continue to
throw the `unknownType` error as before.

nil} ``` ### Additional contract requirements When cleaning or organizing the `:require` and `:import` sections of an `ns` form — the behavior triggered by `lsp-organize-imports` and the ns clean-up refactorings — comments and reader-discard forms interleaved among the entries must not be silently dropped or detached from the entry they annotate. The ownership rules below are semantic: they constrain whether such context survives cleaning and which entry it stays adjacent to, not the exact whitespace, line layout, or resulting order of the entries. - An unqualified reader discard of the `#_` form (in particular `#_:clj-kondo/ignore`) immediately preceding an entry that survives cleaning — including an entry kept only for side effects, or one whose discard suppresses its unused-entry warning — must be retained and must stay directly in front of that following entry. When the entry is removed, the discard marker is removed together with it. - A standalone comment on its own line(s) directly between two entries belongs to the entry that follows it. When that entry survives cleaning the comment must remain directly before it, wherever the pair is sorted; when the entry is removed the comment is removed together with it. - A standalone comment immediately before a reader-discard group belongs to that discard group: it must travel with the marker and its entry whenever the entry survives, and it is removed together with the group when the entry is removed. - Inside a reader-discard group, a comment between the `#_` marker and the discarded form belongs to the group: it must stay inside the group when the group's entry survives, and it is removed together with the group when the entry is removed. - A comment on the same source line as an entry, to its right, belongs to that entry. It must survive whenever the entry survives, staying attached so that the entry and its comment can always be read off a single source line; it must be removed whenever its entry is removed, and must never be inherited by a different entry's line. The retained ordering of surviving entries is otherwise governed by the existing sort settings. contract_addendum:
When cleaning or organizing the `:require` and `:import` sections of an `ns` form — the
behavior triggered by `lsp-organize-imports` and the ns clean-up refactorings — comments
and reader-discard forms interleaved among the entries must not be silently dropped or
detached from the entry they annotate. The ownership rules below are semantic: they
constrain whether such context survives cleaning and which entry it stays adjacent to,
not the exact whitespace, line layout, or resulting order of the entries.

- An unqualified reader discard of the `#_` form (in particular `#_:clj-kondo/ignore`)
  immediately preceding an entry that survives cleaning — including an entry kept only
  for side effects, or one whose discard suppresses its unused-entry warning — must be
  retained and must stay directly in front of that following entry. When the entry is
  removed, the discard marker is removed together with it.
- A standalone comment on its own line(s) directly between two entries belongs to the
  entry that follows it. When that entry survives cleaning the comment must remain
  directly before it, wherever the pair is sorted; when the entry is removed the
  comment is removed together with it.
- A standalone comment immediately before a reader-discard group belongs to that
  discard group: it must travel with the marker and its entry whenever the entry
  survives, and it is removed together with the group when the entry is removed.
- Inside a reader-discard group, a comment between the `#_` marker and the discarded
  form belongs to the group: it must stay inside the group when the group's entry
  survives, and it is removed together with the group when the entry is removed.
- A comment on the same source line as an entry, to its right, belongs to that entry.
  It must survive whenever the entry survives, staying attached so that the entry and
  its comment can always be read off a single source line; it must be removed whenever
  its entry is removed, and must never be inherited by a different entry's line.

The retained ordering of surviving entries is otherwise governed by the existing sort
settings. Within the presence and adjacency rules above, implementations may place a
preserved group on a different line than it occupied originally; callers must not rely
on exact line breaks, indentation, or trailing-newline layout beyond the stated
presence and association of the preserved context.

+(defn ^:private find-after-libspec-comment
+  "look for comment to the right of the libspec 'node' on the same line"
+  [require-nodes idx libspec-node]
+  (when-let [right-node (nth require-nodes (inc idx) nil)]
+    (when (and (n/comment? right-node)
+               (= (:row (meta right-node)) (:end-row (meta libspec-node))))
+      right-node)))
+
+(defn ^:private comment-or-discard? [node]
+  (or (n/comment? node) (fast= :uneval (n/tag node))))
+
+(defn ^:private find-interstitial-nodes
+  "find any interstitial nodes (comments or discard macros) that are between current libspec idx 
+   and the previous libspec (or top of vector)"
+  [require-nodes libspec-idx]
+
+  ;; find previous node (or top) 
+  (let [prev-node-idx (first (filter #(n/sexpr-able? (nth require-nodes %)) (range (dec libspec-idx) -1 -1)))
+        prev-node-row (if prev-node-idx (:end-row (meta (nth require-nodes prev-node-idx))) -1)]
+
+    ;; loop backward until we hit the previous require or top
+    (loop [n (dec libspec-idx)
+           found-comments []]
+
+      ;; gather comments while between libspecs (or hit top)
+      (if (and (not (neg? n))
+               (comment-or-discard? (nth require-nodes n))
+               (> (some-> (nth require-nodes n) meta :row) prev-node-row))
+        (recur (dec n) (concat [(nth require-nodes n)] found-comments))
+        found-comments))))
+
+(defn ^:private build-vector-of-associated-nodes
+  "returns a vector of a node and associated interstitial nodes (comments and reader discard macros) for temporary
+   grouping during sort.  If no associations, just return the node."
+  [require-nodes idx node]
+  (let [after-node-comment (some-> (find-after-libspec-comment require-nodes idx node)
+                                   (vary-meta assoc :associated-node node))
+        before-node-comments (find-interstitial-nodes require-nodes idx)]
+    (cond
+      (and after-node-comment (seq before-node-comments))
+      (vary-meta (n/vector-node [node after-node-comment before-node-comments]) assoc :association-types :before-and-after)
+
+      after-node-comment
+      (vary-meta (n/vector-node [node after-node-comment]) assoc :association-types :after-only)
+
+      (seq before-node-comments)
+      (vary-meta (n/vector-node [node before-node-comments]) assoc :association-types :before-only)
+
+      :else
+      node)))
+
+(defn ^:private has-association-vector?
+  "if node is a :vector inside a :vector [[]] or a :list inside a :vector [()]
+   then this is a comment grouping we created before the sort"
+  [node]
+  (and (fast= :vector (n/tag node))
+       (or (fast= :vector (some-> node n/children first n/tag))
+           (fast= :list (some-> node n/children first n/tag)))))
+
+(defn ^:private expand-comment-associations
+  "if this node is a vector with associated comments or discard macros, return them as a 
+   vector along with the node.  If not, just return the node."
+  [node]
+  (case (some-> node meta :association-types)
+    :before-only (let [[n before-comments] (n/children node)]
+                   (concat before-comments [n]))
+    :after-only (let [[n comment] (n/children node)]
+                  [n comment])
+    :before-and-after (let [[n comment before-comments] (n/children node)]
+                        (concat before-comments [n comment]))
+    [node]))

problem_statement:
Gate swift-nio behind a package trait so the SwiftMCP core stays cross-platform
## Motivation

The `SwiftMCP` library target links swift-nio (`NIOCore`, `NIOHTTP1`, `NIOPosix`, `NIOFoundationCompat`) plus swift-crypto / swift-certificates — but those are used **only by the HTTP/SSE server transport**. Every consumer of `SwiftMCP`, even one that uses only `JSONValue`, `JSONSchema`, `MCPToolProviding`, the `@MCPTool`/`@MCPServer` macros, or the **client** (`MCPServerProxy`), is forced to compile swift-nio.

- **Windows is blocked entirely** — `NIOPosix` doesn't compile on Windows on current toolchains (`System.swift` `IPPROTO`/`BinaryFloatingPoint`; `Thread.swift` non-`Sendable` `NIOLockedValueBox`; `ThreadWindows.swift` `UnsafeMutableRawPointer` `Sendable`). Any downstream package that just wants the tool/schema/client layer can't build for Windows, even though its own code is portable.
- Heavier graph + slower builds for client/tools-only consumers everywhere.

_Found making SwiftAgents cross-platform (Cocoanetics/SwiftAgents#17): against 1.4.7 it builds on macOS / iOS / Linux / **Android**; Windows is the only gap and swift-nio is the sole blocker._

## NIO is already quarantined

| Area | swift-nio | Crypto/X509 |
|---|---|---|
| `Transport/` (HTTP/SSE server) | 10 files | 3 files |
| `Extensions/JSONRPCMessage+Batch.swift` | 1 file (`ByteBuffer`) | – |
| `Models/`, `Protocols/`, `Client/`, `Errors/`, `Naming/`, `AppIntents/`, `OpenAPI/`, macros | **0** | **0** |

The client (`MCPServerProxy`) has been NIO-free since the SwiftCross adoption (#126) — it uses `URLSession.bytes(for:)` everywhere — and the core does not reference any `Transport/` type.

## Proposal: package traits (keep the single `SwiftMCP` umbrella)

Use [SwiftPM package traits](https://docs.swift.org/swiftpm/documentation/packagemanagerdocs/packagetraits/) (the package is already `swift-tools-version: 6.1`) to make the optional feature areas — and the heavy deps they pull — opt-in, **without splitting products**. `import SwiftMCP` stays unchanged.

Define feature traits, **all enabled by default** (so existing consumers are unaffected):

- **`Server`** — the HTTP/SSE transport (`Transport/`). The *only* thing that needs swift-nio + swift-crypto + swift-certificates.
- **`Client`** — the MCP client (`Client/`, `MCPServerProxy`).
- plus any other optional surfaces worth gating (`OpenAPI`, `AppIntents`, tracing/observability, …).

The tool/schema foundation — `JSONValue`, `JSONSchema`, `MCPToolProviding`, the `@MCPTool`/`@MCPServer` **macros**, errors — stays **always-on core** (no trait); everyone needs it. (Note: the `@MCPServer` *macro* is core — it generates tool metadata; the `Server` *trait* is the NIO HTTP transport. Distinct things.)

[HIDDEN]

[HIDDEN]

## Consumer usage

A client-only consumer enables just what it needs and drops `Server` → no swift-nio → **builds on Windows**. e.g. SwiftAgents (tool/schema core + client, never runs a server):

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/Cocoanetics/SwiftMCP", from: "1.5.0", traits: ["Client"])
```

Consumer manifests must be `swift-tools-version: 6.1+` to select traits (SwiftAgents would bump from 5.10).

## Benefits

- One umbrella `SwiftMCP` module; `import SwiftMCP` unchanged.
- Client/tools-only consumers drop swift-nio + crypto → **Windows builds**, lighter graph, faster builds.
- Default = all traits on → fully backward-compatible for existing server users.
- Granular: enable `Client`-only, `Server`-only, etc.

## Open questions / work

- [HIDDEN]
- CI: add a trait-matrix build (e.g. `Client`-only on Linux + Windows) so the NIO-free config stays green.

## Alternative considered: product split

Splitting `Transport/` into a separate `SwiftMCPServer` product reaches the same goal without traits, but adds a second product/import and gives no per-feature granularity. Traits keep the single umbrella and let consumers link exactly the features they want, which is preferable here.

### Additional contract requirements

# SwiftMCP package traits

SwiftMCP exposes three named package traits: `Server`, `Client`, and `OpenAPI`. All three are enabled by default, preserving the existing full-feature configuration.

`Server` enables the HTTP/SSE and TCP server transport surface and its server-only dependency graph. `Client` enables the MCP client surface. `OpenAPI` enables the OpenAPI and AI-plugin surface. The tool and schema foundation remains available without selecting a feature trait.

index dacb59c4..fdf37ca3 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/swift.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/swift.yml
@@ -77,6 +77,52 @@ jobs:
         run: swift test -v --skip-build
         continue-on-error: true
 
+  # Trait matrix: the tool/schema core and the `Client` feature must build
+  # WITHOUT the `Server` trait, i.e. without swift-nio / swift-crypto /
+  # swift-certificates. This keeps the NIO-free configuration green so a
+  # client/tools-only consumer (and Windows, below) never regresses. The whole
+  # package builds NIO-free too — the server demo CLIs are gated `#if Server`
+  # and compile to a no-op stub — so a plain `swift build`/`swift test` with
+  # `Server` disabled works, not just `--target SwiftMCP`.
+  build-traits:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 25
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - name: Verify Swift version
+        run: swift --version
+      - name: Build SwiftMCP library — core only (all traits disabled)
+        run: swift build --target SwiftMCP --disable-default-traits
+      - name: Build SwiftMCP library — Client trait only (no swift-nio)
+        run: swift build --target SwiftMCP --traits Client
+      - name: Build whole package — Client + OpenAPI (no swift-nio)
+        run: swift build --traits "Client,OpenAPI"
+      - name: Test — non-server suite (Client + OpenAPI, no swift-nio)
+        run: swift test --traits "Client,OpenAPI"
+
+  # Windows DOES build AND test the NIO-free configuration. With the `Server`
+  # trait disabled there is no swift-nio in the graph (the server demo CLIs are
+  # gated `#if Server` and compile to a no-op stub), so `swift test` builds the
+  # library plus the non-server test suite. These are real (non continue-on-error)
+  # checks: if swift-nio ever leaks back into the core/client, or a non-server
+  # test regresses, this job goes red. The full `build-windows` job above stays
+  # aspirational until swift-nio itself builds on Windows.
+  windows-client:

+      - name: Setup Swift

+      - name: Verify Swift version
+        run: swift --version
+      - name: Build SwiftMCP library — Client trait only (no swift-nio)
+        run: swift build --target SwiftMCP --traits Client
+      - name: Test — non-server suite (Client + OpenAPI, no swift-nio)
+        run: swift test --traits "Client,OpenAPI"

 ```
 
+### Package traits
+
+SwiftMCP exposes its optional feature areas as [SwiftPM package traits](https://docs.swift.org/swiftpm/documentation/packagemanagerdocs/packagetraits/), **all enabled by default** — existing consumers and a plain `swift build` are unaffected. The single `import SwiftMCP` module is unchanged.
+
+| Trait | Enables | Extra dependencies |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `Server` | HTTP/SSE + TCP server transports | swift-nio, swift-crypto, swift-certificates |
+| `Client` | The MCP client (`MCPServerProxy`) | — |
+| `OpenAPI` | OpenAPI / AI-plugin manifest models and routes | — |
+
+The tool/schema foundation — `JSONValue`, `JSONSchema`, `MCPToolProviding`, the `@MCPTool` / `@MCPServer` macros, errors — is always-on core and needs no trait.
+
+Disabling `Server` drops swift-nio (and swift-crypto/swift-certificates) entirely, which makes the package **build on Windows** and gives client/tools-only consumers a lighter graph. A consumer that only talks to remote MCP servers selects just what it needs (your manifest must be `swift-tools-version: 6.1` or newer to choose traits):
+
+```swift
+.package(
+    url: "https://github.com/Cocoanetics/SwiftMCP.git",
+    branch: "main",
+    traits: ["Client"]   // tool/schema core + client, no swift-nio
+)
+```
+
+> AppIntents bridging (`@MCPAppIntentTool`, AppShortcuts discovery) is not a trait: it is already gated by `#if canImport(AppIntents)`, so it is automatically excluded on platforms without AppIntents (Linux, Windows, Android).
+

+//  DNS-SD / Bonjour service-type naming for MCP over TCP. These helpers live in
+//  the always-on core (not behind the `Server` trait) so the client-side
+//  `MCPServerTcpConfig` can derive default service types without linking the
+//  `TCPBonjourTransport` server transport.
+//
+
+import Foundation
+
+/// DNS-SD service-type naming for MCP over TCP.
+public enum MCPBonjourServiceType {
+    /// Base DNS-SD service type for MCP over TCP.
+    public static let base = "_mcp._tcp"
+
+    /// Returns a server-specific service type derived from the server name,
+    /// e.g. `"Post"` → `"_post-mcp._tcp"`. This prevents Bonjour collisions
+    /// between unrelated MCP servers on the same network.
+    public static func forServer(_ serverName: String) -> String {
+        "_\(serverName.lowercased())-mcp._tcp"
+    }
+}

+//

+//
+//  The MCP protocol versions understood by this package. These constants live
+//  in the always-on core (not behind the `Server` trait) because both the
+//  server-runtime initialize handshake and the client (`MCPServerProxy`) need
+//  to negotiate the protocol version without linking the HTTP transport.
+//
+
+import Foundation
+
+/// Model Context Protocol revisions supported by SwiftMCP.
+public enum MCPProtocolVersion {
+    /// The most recent protocol revision advertised during initialization.
+    public static let latest = "2025-11-25"
+
+    /// Intermediate revision still accepted over the HTTP transport.
+    public static let intermediateHTTP = "2025-06-18"
+
+    /// Oldest revision still accepted over the HTTP transport.
+    public static let fallbackHTTP = "2025-03-26"
+
+    /// The full set of protocol revisions this package can negotiate.
+    public static let supported: Set<String> = [
+        latest,
+        intermediateHTTP,
+        fallbackHTTP
+    ]
+}

diff --git a/Tests/SwiftMCPTests/PackageTraitContractTests.swift b/Tests/SwiftMCPTests/PackageTraitContractTests.swift
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9928f2a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Tests/SwiftMCPTests/PackageTraitContractTests.swift
@@ -0,0 +1,851 @@
+// Tests for the package-trait feature-selection contract. These checks are
+// behavior-based: they run the package in supported trait configurations and
+// consume it as a client-only dependency, rather than matching Package.swift
+// source text, so any semantically equivalent manifest satisfies them.
+
+import Foundation
+import Testing
+@testable import SwiftMCP
+
+@Suite("Package trait contract")
+struct PackageTraitContractTests {
+
+    /// A minimal tool/schema probe proves the always-on core remains usable
+    /// no matter which optional feature traits are selected.
+    @MCPServer
+    fileprivate final class TraitProbeService: Sendable {
+        /// Returns a fixed greeting.
+        @MCPTool
+        func noServerPing() -> String {
+            "pong"
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("Core tool layer is available regardless of the selected traits")
+    func coreToolLayerAvailable() async {
+        let metadata = await TraitProbeService().mcpToolMetadata.map(\.name)
+        #expect(metadata.contains("noServerPing"))
+    }
+
+    // The client surface is exercised through the in-process stdio bridge
+    // here. The trait contract promises the `Client` trait as the outbound
+    // client surface only, so an implementation may require the `Server`
+    // trait for the in-process bridge (the bridge is backed by the server
+    // runtime). This test therefore requires both surfaces in the test
+    // module, exactly like the Server+OpenAPI combination below.
+    #if Client && Server
+    @Test("Client layer can drive an in-process server without the server transport")
+    func clientLayerAvailable() async throws {
+        let proxy = MCPServerProxy(config: .stdioHandles(server: TraitProbeService()))
+        try await proxy.connect()
+        defer { Task { await proxy.disconnect() } }
+
+        let tools = try await proxy.listTools().map(\.name)
+        let result = try await proxy.callTool("noServerPing")
+
+        #expect(tools.contains("noServerPing"))
+        #expect(result.contains("pong"))
+    }
+    #endif
+
+    #if OpenAPI
+    @MCPServer(name: "trait_contract_probe")
+    fileprivate final class TraitProbeOpenAPIService: Sendable {
+        /// Returns a fixed greeting.
+        @MCPTool
+        func openapiPing() -> String {
+            "pong"
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("OpenAPI surface generates a spec and AI-plugin manifest")
+    func openAPISurfaceAvailable() async throws {
+        let service = TraitProbeOpenAPIService()
+        let spec = await OpenAPISpec(server: service, scheme: "http", host: "localhost:8080")
+
+        // The OpenAPI feature is actually functional: it exposes a path for
+        // the probe tool and produces a non-empty specification and manifest.
+        #expect(spec.paths.keys.contains("/trait_contract_probe/openapiPing"))
+        let encodedSpec = try JSONEncoder().encode(spec)
+        #expect(encodedSpec.isEmpty == false)
+
+        let manifest = AIPluginManifest(
+            nameForHuman: "TraitContractProbe",
+            nameForModel: "trait_contract_probe",
+            descriptionForHuman: "Probe",
+            descriptionForModel: "Probe",
+            auth: .none,
+            api: AIPluginManifest.API(type: "openapi", url: "http://localhost:8080/openapi.json")
+        )
+        let encodedManifest = try JSONEncoder().encode(manifest)
+        #expect(encodedManifest.isEmpty == false)
+    }
+    #endif
+
+    // MARK: - Behavioral trait-matrix probes
+
+    private enum FeatureSurface: String, CaseIterable {
+        case server = "Server"
+        case client = "Client"
+        case openAPI = "OpenAPI"
+
+        /// A marker name for a generated consumer variable.
+        var probeMarker: String {
+            switch self {
+            case .server: return "serverSurface"
+            case .client: return "clientSurface"
+            case .openAPI: return "openAPISurface"
+            }
+        }
+
+        /// Swift source lines appended to the generated consumer that reference
+        /// public types from this trait's promised feature surface, so that
+        /// merely declaring a trait without compiling its public API cannot
+        /// satisfy the corresponding matrix entry. The placeholder `MARKER` is
+        /// replaced with this trait's variable name. `canImport` fallbacks keep
+        /// the consumer compilable when a surface type lives in an optional
+        /// module on some platforms.
+        var generatedProbe: [String] {
+            switch self {
+            case .server:
+                return [
+                    "// `Session` belongs to the server runtime surface: the trait",
+                    "// contract allows implementations that only expose it when the",
+                    "// `Server` trait is selected (the existing Session-based test",
+                    "// suites are gated the same way), so the Server matrix entries",
+                    "// must reference it.",
+                    "#if canImport(Network)",
+                    "let MARKER: [String] = [String(describing: HTTPSSETransport.self), String(describing: TCPBonjourTransport.self), String(describing: Session.self)]",
+                    "#else",
+                    "let MARKER: [String] = [String(describing: HTTPSSETransport.self), String(describing: Session.self)]",
+                    "#endif",
+                    "print(MARKER)",
+                ]
+            case .client:
+                return [
+                    "let MARKER = MCPServerProxy(config: .sse(config: MCPServerSseConfig(url: URL(string: \"http://127.0.0.1\")!)))",
+                    "print(String(describing: MARKER))",
+                ]
+            case .openAPI:
+                return [
+                    "let MARKER: [String] = [String(describing: FileContent.self), String(describing: OpenAIFileResponse.self)]",
+                    "print(MARKER)",
+                ]
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    private struct MatrixConfiguration {
+        let label: String
+        /// `nil` means use the dependency's defaults. An empty array selects
+        /// no named traits; a non-empty array selects exactly those traits.
+        let traits: [FeatureSurface]?
+    }
+
+    /// Every subset of the three named traits, plus a separate default-traits
+    /// probe. Non-server selections come first so their build manifests cannot
+    /// be confused with outputs left by a preceding server build.
+    private static let supportedConfigurations: [MatrixConfiguration] = [
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "core only (no named traits)", traits: []),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "OpenAPI", traits: [.openAPI]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Client", traits: [.client]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Client,OpenAPI", traits: [.client, .openAPI]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Server", traits: [.server]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Server,OpenAPI", traits: [.server, .openAPI]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Server,Client", traits: [.server, .client]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "Server,Client,OpenAPI", traits: [.server, .client, .openAPI]),
+        MatrixConfiguration(label: "default traits", traits: nil)
+    ]
+
+    #if Server && OpenAPI
+    /// A probe server type that exercises the combined Server+OpenAPI
+    /// surface: the OpenAPI spec must expose the natural HTTP route that the
+    /// server transport serves for every tool.
+    @MCPServer(name: "trait_route_probe")
+    fileprivate final class TraitProbeRouteOpenAPIService: Sendable {
+        /// Adds two numbers.
+        @MCPTool
+        func routeProbeAdd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int {
+            a + b
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("OpenAPI surface exposes the routes the server transport serves")
+    func openAPISurfaceServedByServer() async throws {
+        let spec = await OpenAPISpec(
+            server: TraitProbeRouteOpenAPIService(),
+            scheme: "http",
+            host: "localhost:8080"
+        )
+
+        // The server transport POSTs tool calls at /<server-name>/<tool>;
+        // the combined Server+OpenAPI surface must describe that route as a
+        // POST operation. The operation metadata is a presentation detail
+        // (implementations may prefix, slugify, or annotate differently), so
+        // only the route and its POST method are asserted.
+        let path = try #require(spec.paths["/trait_route_probe/routeProbeAdd"])
+        #expect(path.post != nil)
+        let encoded = try JSONEncoder().encode(spec)
+        #expect(encoded.isEmpty == false)
+    }
+    #endif
+
+    @Test("Every supported trait configuration builds the SwiftMCP library surface")
+    func supportedTraitMatrixBuilds() throws {
+        let root = try packageRoot()
+        let workspace = try scratchWorkspace()
+        defer { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: workspace.root) }
+
+        let consumer = workspace.subdirectory("TraitMatrixConsumer")
+        let sources = consumer.appendingPathComponent("Sources", isDirectory: true)
+        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: sources, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
+        let scratch = consumer.appendingPathComponent(".build", isDirectory: true)
+
+        var failures: [String] = []
+        for configuration in Self.supportedConfigurations {
+            let dependencyTraits: String
+            if let traits = configuration.traits {
+                let names = traits.map { "\"\($0.rawValue)\"" }.joined(separator: ", ")
+                dependencyTraits = ", traits: [\(names)]"
+            } else {
+                dependencyTraits = ""
+            }
+
+            // A downstream package product-scopes the build to the SwiftMCP
+            // library. This deliberately avoids compiling demo executables,
+            // which are not part of the contract for core-only or OpenAPI-only
+            // consumers. Supplying `traits: []` disables dependency defaults;
+            // omitting the argument exercises the documented default traits.
+            let manifest = """
+            // swift-tools-version: 6.1
+            import PackageDescription
+
+            let package = Package(
+                name: "TraitMatrixConsumer",
+                dependencies: [
+                    .package(name: "SwiftMCP", path: "\(root.path)"\(dependencyTraits))
+                ],
+                targets: [
+                    .executableTarget(
+                        name: "TraitMatrixConsumer",
+                        dependencies: [
+                            .product(name: "SwiftMCP", package: "SwiftMCP")
+                        ]
+                    )
+                ]
+            )
+            """
+            try manifest.write(
+                to: consumer.appendingPathComponent("Package.swift"),
+                atomically: true,
+                encoding: .utf8
+            )
+
+            // All selections must expose the always-on tool/schema foundation.
+            // Client and Server selections additionally reference a public type
+            // from their promised surface, so merely declaring a trait without
+            // compiling its API cannot satisfy the corresponding matrix entry.
+            var source = """
+            import Foundation
+            #if canImport(FoundationNetworking)
+            import FoundationNetworking
+            #endif
+            import SwiftMCP
+
+            // A regular import checks always-on core values and protocols even when
+            // this dependency explicitly selects no optional traits. The independently
+            // implemented provider lets server-only
+            // integration modes exercise tool dispatch without making the
+            // core @MCPServer expansion depend on the Client feature.
+            final class HTTPProbeServer: MCPServer, MCPToolProviding, Sendable {
+                var serverName: String { "trait_matrix_probe" }
+                var serverVersion: String { "1.0" }
+                var serverDescription: String? { nil }
+                var mcpToolMetadata: [MCPToolMetadata] { get async {
+                    [MCPToolMetadata(name: "coreMacroProbe", parameters: [], returnType: String.self)]
+                } }
+                func callTool(_ name: String, arguments: JSONDictionary) async throws -> any Encodable & Sendable {
+                    guard name == "coreMacroProbe" else { throw MCPToolError.unknownTool(name: name) }
+                    return "core"
+                }
+                func handleMessage(_ message: JSONRPCMessage) async -> JSONRPCMessage? { nil }
+            }
+
+            func compileCoreSurface() async {
+                let coreValue: JSONValue = .string("core")
+                let coreSchema: JSONSchema = .string(description: "trait matrix core probe")
+                let coreHints: MCPToolHints = []
+                let coreError = JSONValueError.expectedObject
+                let toolError = MCPToolError.unknownTool(name: "missing")
+                let provider: any MCPToolProviding = HTTPProbeServer()
+                let metadata = await provider.mcpToolMetadata
+                guard metadata.contains(where: { $0.name == "coreMacroProbe" }) else {
+                    fatalError("Core MCPToolProviding metadata was unavailable")
+                }
+                print(coreValue, coreSchema, coreHints, coreError, toolError, metadata.map(\\.name))
+            }
+            """
+            let activeTraits = configuration.traits ?? [.server, .client, .openAPI]
+            if activeTraits.contains(.client) {
+                source += """
+
+                // The reference @MCPServer macro also generates outbound Client
+                // proxy APIs. Exercise its tool metadata expansion in Client
+                // configurations, where those generated symbols are selected.
+                @MCPServer(generateClient: false)
+                final class ClientTraitMacroProbe: Sendable {
+                    @MCPTool
+                    func corePing() -> String { "pong" }
+                }
+                func compileClientMacroSurface() async {
+                    let provider: any MCPToolProviding = ClientTraitMacroProbe()
+                    let names = await provider.mcpToolMetadata.map(\\.name)
+                    guard names.contains("corePing") else { fatalError("tool metadata missing") }
+                    print(names)
+                }
+                """
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "OpenAPI" {
+                source += """
+
+                // Public OpenAPI model types must be importable by an ordinary
+                // downstream package with OpenAPI selected and no other trait.
+                func compileOpenAPIOnlySurface() throws {
+                    let file = FileContent(name: "probe.txt", mimeType: "text/plain", content: Data("probe".utf8))
+                    let response = OpenAIFileResponse(files: [file])
+                    let encoded = try JSONEncoder().encode(response)
+                    guard !encoded.isEmpty else { fatalError("OpenAPI model encoded no data") }
+                }
+                """
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "Server" {
+                source += """
+
+                // A Server-only downstream consumer starts the real transport
+                // and reaches its MCP HTTP endpoint without Client/OpenAPI.
+                func runServerOnlyHTTPProbe() async throws {
+                    let transport = HTTPSSETransport(server: HTTPProbeServer(), host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0)
+                    try await transport.start()
+                    defer { Task { try? await transport.stop() } }
+                    var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1:\\(transport.port)/mcp")!)
+                    request.httpMethod = "POST"
+                    request.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
+                    request.setValue("application/json, text/event-stream", forHTTPHeaderField: "Accept")
+                    let (_, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
+                    guard (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode == 400 else {
+                        fatalError("Server-only MCP endpoint did not handle the request")
+                    }
+                }
+                """
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "Server,OpenAPI" {
+                source += """
+
+                // Exercise the combined route surface from an ordinary
+                // downstream Server+OpenAPI package with Client omitted.
+                func runServerOpenAPIHTTPProbe() async throws {
+                    let transport = HTTPSSETransport(server: HTTPProbeServer(), host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0)
+                    transport.serveOpenAPI = true
+                    try await transport.start()
+                    defer { Task { try? await transport.stop() } }
+                    let base = URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1:\\(transport.port)")!
+                    for path in ["/openapi.json", "/.well-known/ai-plugin.json"] {
+                        let (data, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(from: base.appending(path: path))
+                        guard (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode == 200, !data.isEmpty else {
+                            fatalError("OpenAPI endpoint did not return a document: \\(path)")
+                        }
+                    }
+                    var request = URLRequest(url: base.appending(path: "/trait_matrix_probe/coreMacroProbe"))
+                    request.httpMethod = "POST"
+                    request.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
+                    request.httpBody = Data("{}".utf8)
+                    let (data, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
+                    guard (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode == 200,
+                          String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self).contains("core") else {
+                        fatalError("OpenAPI tool route did not dispatch the downstream tool")
+                    }
+                }
+                """
+            }
+            for trait in FeatureSurface.allCases where activeTraits.contains(trait) {
+                for probeLine in trait.generatedProbe {
+                    source += "\n" + probeLine.replacingOccurrences(of: "MARKER", with: trait.probeMarker) + "\n"
+                }
+            }
+            source += "\nawait compileCoreSurface()\n"
+            if activeTraits.contains(.client) {
+                source += "await compileClientMacroSurface()\n"
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "OpenAPI" {
+                source += "try compileOpenAPIOnlySurface()\n"
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "Server" {
+                source += "try await runServerOnlyHTTPProbe()\n"
+            }
+            if configuration.label == "Server,OpenAPI" {
+                source += "try await runServerOpenAPIHTTPProbe()\n"
+            }
+            try source.write(
+                to: sources.appendingPathComponent("main.swift"),
+                atomically: true,
+                encoding: .utf8
+            )
+
+            var buildArguments = [
+                "build",
+                "--package-path", consumer.path,
+                "--scratch-path", scratch.path,
+                "--cache-path", workspace.cache.path,
+                "-Xswiftc", "-DSWIFTMCP_TRAIT_MATRIX_PROBE",
+            ]
+            let checksNoServerGraph = configuration.label == "Client" || configuration.label == "Client,OpenAPI"
+            if checksNoServerGraph {
+                buildArguments.append("-v")
+            }
+            let result = runProcess(
+                launchPath: try swiftToolchainExecutable("swift"),
+                arguments: buildArguments
+            )
+            if result.status != 0 {
+                failures.append(configuration.label)
+                Issue.record(
+                    "Configuration '\(configuration.label)' must build the SwiftMCP library surface: \(result.output.suffix(1200))"
+                )
+                continue
+            }
+
+            // Look at the effective build plan, not just successful imports:
+            // a Linux build can succeed even when server-only products remain
+            // linked into a no-Server consumer's graph.
+            if checksNoServerGraph {
+                let forbiddenModuleNames = [
+                    "NIOCore", "NIOHTTP1", "NIOPosix", "NIOFoundationCompat",
+                    "Crypto", "_CryptoExtras", "X509"

+                let selectedModules = forbiddenModuleNames.filter { module in
+                    result.output.contains("-module-name \(module) ") ||

+                if !selectedModules.isEmpty {

+                    )

+            }
+
+            // Execute the downstream probes as well as compiling them: this
+            // confirms generated metadata and OpenAPI model serialization.
+            let executable = scratch.appendingPathComponent("debug/TraitMatrixConsumer").path
+            let probeRun = runProcess(launchPath: executable, arguments: [])
+            if probeRun.status != 0 {
+                failures.append("\(configuration.label) consumer probe")
+                Issue.record("Configuration '\(configuration.label)' consumer probe failed: \(probeRun.output.suffix(1200))")
+            }
+
+            // Expand @MCPServer in an ordinary downstream package with no
+            // named traits. Inspect the generated core metadata independently
+            // from the optional nested client companion: the core macro must
+            // remain available when Client is not selected.
+            if configuration.label == "core only (no named traits)" {
+                let macroSource = """
+                import SwiftMCP
+                @MCPServer
+                final class CoreOnlyMacroProbe: Sendable {
+                    @MCPTool
+                    func coreOnlyPing() -> String { "pong" }
+                }
+                """
+                try macroSource.write(
+                    to: sources.appendingPathComponent("main.swift"),
+                    atomically: true,
+                    encoding: .utf8
+                )
+                let expansionArguments = [
+                    "build",
+                    "--package-path", consumer.path,
+                    "--scratch-path", scratch.path,
+                    "--cache-path", workspace.cache.path,
+                    "-Xswiftc", "-Xfrontend",
+                    "-Xswiftc", "-dump-macro-expansions",
+                ]
+                let expansion = runProcess(
+                    launchPath: try swiftToolchainExecutable("swift"),
+                    arguments: expansionArguments
+                )
+                let containsGeneratedCoreMetadata =
+                    expansion.output.contains("mcpToolMetadata") &&
+                    expansion.output.contains("MCPToolMetadata") &&
+                    expansion.output.contains("name: \"coreOnlyPing\"")
+                if !containsGeneratedCoreMetadata {
+                    failures.append("core-only @MCPServer metadata expansion")
+                    Issue.record(
+                        "The downstream no-trait @MCPServer expansion must emit tool metadata: \(expansion.output.suffix(1200))"
+                    )
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        #expect(
+            failures.isEmpty,
+            "Unsupported trait configurations: \(failures.joined(separator: ", "))"
+        )
+    }

+    @Test("CI client-only build accepts equivalent guarded workflow layouts")

+        #expect(workflowCoversClientOnlyBuild(localActionWorkflow, platform: .windows, root: root))

+            platform: .windows, root: root

+        #expect(!workflowCoversClientOnlyBuild(

+        ))
+        #expect(!workflowCoversClientOnlyBuild(
+            matrixWorkflow.replacingOccurrences(of: "swift build --target SwiftMCP --traits 'Client'", with: "swift build --target SwiftMCP --traits 'Client' || true"),

+
+    private enum CIPlatform { case linux, windows }
+
+    private func workflowCoversClientOnlyBuild(_ workflow: String, platform: CIPlatform, root: URL) -> Bool {
+        workflowJobBlocks(workflow).contains { _, job in
+            jobRunsOn(job, platform: platform) && !jobIsDisabled(job) && !jobHasFailureSuppression(job) &&
+                jobSteps(job).contains { stepIndexAndText in
+                    let (index, step) = stepIndexAndText
+                    guard !conditionIsDisabled(step), hasClientOnlyBuild(step, root: root) else { return false }
+                    return buildFailureIsPropagated(step, laterSteps: Array(jobSteps(job).dropFirst(index + 1)), job: job)
+                }
+        }
+    }
+
+    private func workflowJobBlocks(_ workflow: String) -> [(name: String, body: String)] {
+        var result: [(String, String)] = []
+        var currentName: String?
+        var currentLines: [String] = []
+        var insideJobs = false
+        for line in workflow.components(separatedBy: .newlines) {
+            if line == "jobs:" { insideJobs = true; continue }
+            if insideJobs && !line.isEmpty && !line.hasPrefix(" ") { break }
+            if insideJobs && line.hasPrefix("  ") && !line.hasPrefix("    ") && line.hasSuffix(":") && !line.hasPrefix("  - ") {
+                if let currentName { result.append((currentName, currentLines.joined(separator: "\n"))) }
+                currentName = String(line.dropFirst(2).dropLast())
+                currentLines = []
+            } else if currentName != nil {
+                currentLines.append(line)
+            }
+        }
+        if let currentName { result.append((currentName, currentLines.joined(separator: "\n"))) }
+        return result
+    }
+
+    private func jobRunsOn(_ job: String, platform: CIPlatform) -> Bool {
+        let runnerLines = job.components(separatedBy: .newlines).filter { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).hasPrefix("runs-on:") }
+        let runnerText = runnerLines.joined(separator: " ").lowercased()
+        switch platform {
+        case .linux:
+            if runnerText.contains("ubuntu") || runnerText.contains("linux") { return true }
+            return runnerText.contains("matrix.") && matrixMentionsPlatform(job, words: ["ubuntu", "linux"])
+        case .windows:
+            if runnerText.contains("windows") || runnerText.contains("win-") { return true }
+            return runnerText.contains("matrix.") && matrixMentionsPlatform(job, words: ["windows", "win-"])
+        }
+    }
+
+    private func matrixMentionsPlatform(_ job: String, words: [String]) -> Bool {
+        let lines = job.components(separatedBy: .newlines)
+        guard let runnerLine = lines.first(where: { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).hasPrefix("runs-on:") }),
+              let variable = runnerLine.components(separatedBy: "matrix.").dropFirst().first?.split(whereSeparator: { !$0.isLetter && !$0.isNumber && $0 != "_" }).first else { return false }
+        let key = String(variable) + ":"
+        guard let matrixLine = lines.first(where: { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).hasPrefix(key) }) else { return false }
+        let value = matrixLine.lowercased()
+        return words.contains(where: { value.contains($0) })
+    }
+
+    private func jobIsDisabled(_ job: String) -> Bool {
+        let jobFields = job.components(separatedBy: .newlines).filter {
+            $0.prefix(while: { $0 == " " }).count <= 4
+        }.joined(separator: "\n")
+        return conditionIsDisabled(jobFields)
+    }
+
+    private func conditionIsDisabled(_ block: String) -> Bool {
+        for line in block.components(separatedBy: .newlines) {
+            let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+            guard trimmed.hasPrefix("if:") else { continue }
+            let expression = trimmed.dropFirst(3).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
+                .replacingOccurrences(of: "${{", with: "").replacingOccurrences(of: "}}", with: "")
+                .trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet.whitespacesAndNewlines.union(CharacterSet(charactersIn: "'\"")))
+                .lowercased()
+            if ["false", "0", "null", "never()"].contains(expression) { return true }
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    private func jobHasFailureSuppression(_ job: String) -> Bool {
+        let lines = job.components(separatedBy: .newlines)
+        for line in lines {
+            let indentation = line.prefix(while: { $0 == " " }).count
+            let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased()
+            if indentation <= 4 && trimmed.hasPrefix("continue-on-error:") && trimmed.contains("true") { return true }
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    private func jobSteps(_ job: String) -> [(Int, String)] {
+        var steps: [String] = []
+        var current: [String] = []
+        for line in job.components(separatedBy: .newlines) {
+            if line.range(of: "^\\s{6}- ", options: .regularExpression) != nil {
+                if !current.isEmpty { steps.append(current.joined(separator: "\n")) }
+                current = [line]
+            } else if !current.isEmpty {
+                current.append(line)
+            }
+        }
+        if !current.isEmpty { steps.append(current.joined(separator: "\n")) }
+        return Array(steps.enumerated())
+    }
+
+    private func buildFailureIsPropagated(_ step: String, laterSteps: [(Int, String)], job: String) -> Bool {
+        let lowerStep = step.lowercased()
+        let continueOnError = lowerStep.components(separatedBy: .newlines).contains {
+            let line = $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+            return line.hasPrefix("continue-on-error:") && line.contains("true")
+        }
+        if hasBuildSuppression(step) { return false }
+        guard continueOnError else { return true }
+        guard let idLine = step.components(separatedBy: .newlines).first(where: { $0.contains("id:") }) else { return false }
+        guard let idRange = idLine.range(of: "id:") else { return false }
+        let id = idLine[idRange.upperBound...].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        return laterSteps.contains { _, later in
+            let body = later.lowercased()
+            let checksOutcome = body.contains("steps.\(id.lowercased()).outcome") || body.contains("steps.\(id.lowercased()).conclusion")
+            let exitsOnFailure = body.contains("exit 1") || body.contains("exit /b 1") || body.contains("throw ") || body.contains("fail ")
+            return !conditionIsDisabled(later) && checksOutcome && exitsOnFailure
+        }
+    }
+
+    private func hasBuildSuppression(_ step: String) -> Bool {
+        let normalized = step.lowercased().replacingOccurrences(of: "\\\n", with: " ")
+        return normalized.range(
+            of: "swift\\s+build[\\s\\S]*\\|\\|\\s*(?:true|exit\\s+0)",
+            options: .regularExpression
+        ) != nil
+    }
+
+    private func hasClientOnlyBuild(_ step: String, root: URL) -> Bool {
+        if hasClientOnlyCommand(step) { return !hasBuildSuppression(step) }
+        for line in step.components(separatedBy: .newlines) {
+            let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+            if trimmed.hasPrefix("run:") || trimmed.hasPrefix("- run:") {
+                let command = trimmed.replacingOccurrences(of: "^-?\\s*run:", with: "", options: .regularExpression)
+                    .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+                for token in command.split(whereSeparator: { $0.isWhitespace }) {
+                    let path = String(token).trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "'\""))
+                    guard path.hasSuffix(".sh") || path.hasPrefix("./") else { continue }
+                    let relative = path.hasPrefix("./") ? String(path.dropFirst(2)) : path
+                    if let contents = try? String(contentsOf: root.appendingPathComponent(relative), encoding: .utf8),
+                       hasClientOnlyCommand(contents) {
+                        return !hasBuildSuppression(contents)
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            if trimmed.hasPrefix("uses:") || trimmed.hasPrefix("- uses:") {
+                let action = trimmed.replacingOccurrences(of: "^-?\\s*uses:", with: "", options: .regularExpression)
+                    .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+                if action.hasPrefix("./") {
+                    let dir = root.appendingPathComponent(String(action.dropFirst(2)), isDirectory: true)
+                    for filename in ["action.yml", "action.yaml"] {
+                        if let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dir.appendingPathComponent(filename), encoding: .utf8),
+                           hasClientOnlyCommand(contents) {
+                            return !hasBuildSuppression(contents)
+                        }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    private func hasClientOnlyCommand(_ text: String) -> Bool {
+        let normalized = text.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\\n", with: " ")
+        guard normalized.range(of: "swift\\s+build", options: .regularExpression) != nil,
+              let option = normalized.range(of: "--traits") else { return false }
+        var valueText = normalized[option.upperBound...].drop(while: { $0.isWhitespace })
+        guard let first = valueText.first else { return false }
+        let value: String
+        if first == "'" || first == "\"" {
+            valueText = valueText.dropFirst()
+            guard let end = valueText.firstIndex(of: first) else { return false }
+            value = String(valueText[..<end])
+        } else {
+            value = String(valueText.prefix(while: { !$0.isWhitespace && $0 != ";" && $0 != "&" && $0 != "|" }))
+        }
+        let traits = value.split(separator: ",").map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }
+        return traits == ["Client"]
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - Process / path helpers
+
+    private struct ProcessResult {
+        let status: Int32
+        let output: String
+    }
+
+    private func packageRoot() throws -> URL {
+        URL(fileURLWithPath: #filePath)
+            .deletingLastPathComponent()   // SwiftMCPTests
+            .deletingLastPathComponent()   // Tests
+            .deletingLastPathComponent()   // package root
+    }
+
+    private final class ScratchWorkspace {
+        let root: URL
+        let cache: URL
+
+        init() throws {
+            let root = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
+                .appendingPathComponent("SwiftMCPTraitContract-\(UUID().uuidString)", isDirectory: true)
+            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: root, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
+            self.root = root
+            // A single network cache shared by every spawned build in this
+            // process prevents repeated remote-dependency fetches, while each
+            // build keeps its own isolated scratch directory.
+            self.cache = root.appendingPathComponent("shared-cache", isDirectory: true)
+        }
+
+        func subdirectory(_ name: String, isDirectory: Bool = true) -> URL {
+            root.appendingPathComponent(name, isDirectory: isDirectory)
+        }
+    }
+
+    private func scratchWorkspace() throws -> ScratchWorkspace {
+        try ScratchWorkspace()
+    }
+
+    private func swiftToolchainExecutable(_ name: String) throws -> String {
+        // Resolve the active toolchain from the running test process so the
+        // spawned build uses the same Swift that built the tests.
+        let swiftc = URL(fileURLWithPath: CommandLine.arguments[0])
+        // CommandLine.arguments[0] is the test runner, not swiftc. Fall back
+        // to /usr/bin when we cannot resolve from the environment.
+        _ = swiftc
+        if let swift = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["SWIFT_EXEC"] { return swift }
+        for candidate in ["/usr/bin/\(name)", "/usr/local/bin/\(name)"] where FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: candidate) {
+            return candidate
+        }
+        return "/usr/bin/\(name)"
+    }
+
+    private func runProcess(launchPath: String, arguments: [String]) -> ProcessResult {
+        let process = Process()
+        process.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: launchPath)
+        process.arguments = arguments
+        process.currentDirectoryURL = nil
+        var environment = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
+        environment.removeValue(forKey: "LD_LIBRARY_PATH")
+        process.environment = environment
+
+        let pipe = Pipe()
+        process.standardOutput = pipe
+        process.standardError = pipe
+        do {
+            try process.run()
+        } catch {
+            return ProcessResult(status: -1, output: "failed to launch: \(error)")
+        }
+        let data = pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
+        process.waitUntilExit()
+        return ProcessResult(status: process.terminationStatus, output: String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self))
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Decouple transports from the server: JSON-RPC connection channels + server.serve(over:) + shutdown() hook
Surfaced while building a session daemon (`acpxd`) on SwiftMCP (in [Cocoanetics/SwiftACP](https://github.com/Cocoanetics/SwiftACP)). Three recurring friction points motivate a small restructuring of the transport ↔ server boundary.

## Pain points today

1. **Every consumer hand-wires a `ServiceGroup`** around the transport(s) and must get the graceful-shutdown details right themselves — including `failureTerminationBehavior`. The default `cancelGroup` cancels every service concurrently on a transport failure, which broke an *ordered* lock-release in our daemon (a successor could grab the lock mid-drain). It was only caught in code review — exactly the kind of thing a framework should own once.
2. **`MCPServer` has no shutdown hook.** Our server has lifetime resources to release on shutdown (live agent subprocesses, a singleton lock). With no hook, we had to conform the server to `Service` ourselves and hand-roll `gracefulShutdown()` + registration ordering.
3. **`@MCPServer` requires `class`/`actor`** even for stateless servers — partly because the transport stores a reference to the server.

## Proposal

### 1. Transports speak JSON-RPC at the boundary and don't know about the server

A transport is a *source of connections*; each connection is a JSON-RPC duplex. Wire specifics (Bonjour, HTTP POST+SSE, stdio framing) stay inside the transport.

```swift
public protocol MCPTransport: Service {
    var connections: AsyncStream<MCPConnection> { get }
}
public protocol MCPConnection: Sendable {
    var inbound: AsyncStream<JSONRPCMessage> { get }     // JSON-RPC in
    func send(_ message: JSONRPCMessage) async throws    // JSON-RPC out
}
```

The transport no longer takes `server:` and never calls `handleMessage`. This is largely *surfacing* today's `Session`/`SessionManager` as the public boundary instead of hiding them behind `transport(server:)`.

### 2. `serve(over:)` does the routing + lifecycle

```swift
extension MCPServer {
    func serve(over transports: [any MCPTransport],
               gracefulShutdownSignals: [UnixSignal] = [.sigterm, .sigint],
               logger: Logger) async throws {
        // run() each transport; per connection, route inbound -> handleMessage -> send;
        // build the ServiceGroup with correct reverse-order graceful shutdown AND
        // failureTerminationBehavior: .gracefullyShutdownGroup; then call shutdown()
        // once the transport group has stopped (ordered on every path).
    }
    func shutdown() async {}   // default no-op hook
}
```

Consumer code collapses from a hand-built `ServiceGroup` to:

```swift
let t = TCPBonjourTransport(serviceName: "acpx")   // no server ref
try await server.serve(over: [t], logger: log)
```

`serve` is a method on the server, so it already has `self` — it's the bridge that pulls each connection's `inbound` and calls `self.handleMessage(...)`, then writes replies via `conn.send`.

### 3. Outbound / notifications via the connection

Server→client pushes (e.g. streaming log notifications mid-tool-call) go through the connection's `send` (or the existing `Session.current`, now backed by it). No server ↔ transport reference in either direction.

### 4. Value-type (`struct`) servers

With the transport no longer holding the server, and per-connection state living in the connection layer, a server's only remaining state is its own *domain* state:

- **No domain state → `struct` works** (trivially `Sendable`; concurrent calls on an immutable value are safe).
- **Shared mutable domain state → `class`/`actor`** (inherent, not a framework limit).

So `@MCPServer` would stop *forcing* a reference type for plumbing reasons; you'd choose based on whether your server actually has state.

## Benefits

- **No retain cycle** — transport and server hold nothing of each other; `serve` owns both for the call's duration.
- **Centralized shutdown correctness** — the reverse-order + `failureTerminationBehavior` ordering is owned and tested once, instead of each consumer re-deriving it (see pain point #1).
- **Testable transports** — feed a canned `inbound` stream, assert `send` output, no server needed.
- **Far less boilerplate** — ~15 lines of `ServiceGroup` wiring → one `serve(over:)` call.
- **`struct` servers** for the broad population of small/stateless tool servers.

## Compatibility

Additive: keep `transport(server:)` + the manual `ServiceGroup` pattern working, and add the connection-based transport + `serve(over:)` + `shutdown()` alongside; extend the `@MCPServer` macro to allow `struct`.

---

Context: SwiftACP currently works around #1/#2 by conforming its `@MCPServer` actor to `Service` and wiring the group by hand (Cocoanetics/SwiftACP#5). This issue captures the cleaner framework-side shape so consumers don't have to.

🤖 Filed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Additional contract requirements

Test-contract clarifications for this task:

- At the transport boundary, a connection is a stream of single JSON-RPC messages: it exposes an inbound `AsyncStream<JSONRPCMessage>` and accepts one message at a time for outbound delivery. Tests exercise only this single-message interface; no batch-frame or protocol-version batch-gating behavior is required by the tests.
- Both server-less and server-coupled construction of the stdio and Bonjour TCP transports must remain available: constructing a transport without a server yields no server reference and still exposes its connections stream, while the existing `server:`-taking initializer keeps working and keeps its server reference.
- A server-less Bonjour TCP transport derives its service name from the name it was constructed with.
- Routing over a connection only responds to `initialize` and subsequent requests from a connection once the session is initialized; a request that arrives before any `initialize` is answered with an error response carrying that request's id, and a request pipelined immediately after `initialize` is dispatched normally rather than rejected.
- While a tool call is in flight, the server can send its own request over the same connection and consume the client's reply without deadlock.
- `serve(over:)` stops the transports before the server's shutdown hook runs, and the shutdown hook still runs when a transport run fails.
- A stateless value-type server annotated with the server macro carries its declared identity and tool metadata, can run its tools, is `Sendable`, and can be served over a transport.

@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+# Connection-Based Transports
+
+Decouple transports from the server and let `serve(over:)` own the run loop, signal handling, and ordered shutdown.
+
+## Overview
+
+A transport is fundamentally a *source of connections*, and each connection is a
+JSON-RPC duplex. SwiftMCP makes that boundary explicit with two small protocols
+and a single entry point on the server:
+
+- ``MCPConnection`` — one full-duplex JSON-RPC channel to a client, carrying
+  **single messages**.
+- ``MCPBatchConnection`` — an opt-in refinement for transports that also carry
+  JSON-RPC *batches*.
+- ``MCPTransport`` — a `Service` that yields connections.
+- ``MCPServer/serve(over:gracefulShutdownSignals:logger:)`` — runs the
+  transports, routes every message (or batch) through the server, and shuts
+  everything down in order.
+- ``MCPServer/shutdown()`` — a lifecycle hook for releasing server-lifetime
+  resources, called last.
+
+The transport never sees the server, and the server never sees the transport.
+`serve` owns both for the duration of the call.
+
+## The boundary
+
+The base connection deals in **single messages** — the common case, and the only
+shape MCP `2025-06-18` and later use (that revision removed JSON-RPC batching):
+
+```swift
+public protocol MCPConnection: Sendable {
+    var inbound: AsyncStream<JSONRPCMessage> { get }     // JSON-RPC in
+    func send(_ message: JSONRPCMessage) async throws    // JSON-RPC out
+}
+
+public protocol MCPTransport: Service {
+    var connections: AsyncStream<MCPConnection> { get }
+}
+```
+
+A transport that must still carry batches — a top-level JSON array that has to
+round-trip as one payload — conforms to ``MCPBatchConnection`` instead, which
+adds a whole-frame interface. Conformers implement only the batch members; the
+single-message requirements are derived for free:
+
+```swift
+public protocol MCPBatchConnection: MCPConnection {
+    var inboundBatches: AsyncStream<[JSONRPCMessage]> { get }
+    func send(_ batch: [JSONRPCMessage]) async throws
+}
+```
+
+`serve` routes a plain ``MCPConnection`` one message at a time through
+``MCPServer/handleMessage(_:)``, and a ``MCPBatchConnection`` whole-frame through
+``MCPServer/processBatch(_:ignoringEmptyResponses:)`` — applying the same
+version-gated batch reject the byte-stream transports use, so a client on a
+no-batching revision that sends a batch gets a `-32600` error. The bundled
+``StdioTransport`` and ``TCPBonjourTransport`` are batch-capable, because a stdin
+line or TCP frame may be a JSON array.
+
+Wire specifics — stdio framing, a TCP listener with Bonjour advertising, HTTP
+POST + SSE — stay inside the transport. Dispatch (initialize, tools, resources,
+notifications, sampling) stays inside the server.
+
+## Serving
+
+Hand the server one or more transports and let it run:
+
+```swift
+let transport = TCPBonjourTransport(serviceName: "acpx")   // no server reference
+try await server.serve(over: [transport], logger: log)
+```
+
+That single call replaces the hand-built `ServiceGroup` consumers used to write:
+
+```swift
+// Before — every consumer re-derived this, including the shutdown details.
+let transport = TCPBonjourTransport(server: server, serviceName: "acpx")
+let group = ServiceGroup(configuration: .init(
+    services: [.init(service: transport,
+                     successTerminationBehavior: .gracefullyShutdownGroup,
+                     failureTerminationBehavior: .gracefullyShutdownGroup)],
+    gracefulShutdownSignals: [.sigterm, .sigint],
+    logger: log))
+try await group.run()
+```
+
+### Shutdown correctness, owned once
+
+`serve` registers every transport with both `successTerminationBehavior` and
+`failureTerminationBehavior` set to `.gracefullyShutdownGroup`. The default
+failure behavior (`.cancelGroup`) cancels every service *concurrently* when one
+transport fails, which can race ordered teardown — a successor grabbing a lock
+while the previous owner is still draining. Graceful failure handling instead
+unwinds the group in reverse-registration order.
+
+``MCPServer/shutdown()`` runs **after** the transport group has fully stopped, so
+your teardown is always the last step — on a graceful signal, on a transport
+finishing, and on a transport throwing alike:
+
+```swift
+@MCPServer(name: "acpx")
+actor Daemon {
+    func shutdown() async {
+        await closeLiveAgents()   // no orphaned subprocesses
+        releaseSingletonLock()    // safe: transports already drained
+    }
+}
+```
+
+## Value-type servers
+
+With the transport no longer holding the server, and per-connection state living
+in the connection layer, a server's only remaining state is its own *domain*
+state. Choose the type by whether that state is shared and mutable:
+
+- **No domain state → `struct`.** Trivially `Sendable`; concurrent calls on an
+  immutable value are safe.
+- **Shared mutable state → `actor`** (or a thread-safe `class`).
+
+```swift
+@MCPServer(name: "calc")
+struct Calculator {
+    @MCPTool func add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int { a + b }
+}
+```
+
+## Writing a transport
+
+Conform to ``MCPTransport``: accept connections however the wire dictates, wrap
+each as an ``MCPConnection``, and yield it to ``MCPTransport/connections``. Run
+until graceful shutdown in `Service.run()`, then finish the connections stream
+(and each connection's `inbound`) so routing unwinds.
+
+The bundled ``StdioTransport`` and ``TCPBonjourTransport`` support both modes:
+construct them with a server (`init(server:)`) to run them yourself, or
+server-less (`StdioTransport()` / `TCPBonjourTransport(serviceName:)`) to hand
+them to `serve`.
+
+## Testability
+
+Because a connection is just two JSON-RPC streams and a transport is just a
+source of them, both can be exercised with no sockets and no server: feed a
+canned ``MCPConnection/inbound`` stream and assert on what
+`send(_:)` receives. That is exactly how SwiftMCP tests
+`serve(over:)` itself.
+
+## Topics
+
+### Protocols
+
+- ``MCPConnection``
+- ``MCPBatchConnection``
+- ``MCPTransport``
+
+### Serving
+
+- ``MCPServer/serve(over:gracefulShutdownSignals:logger:)``
+- ``MCPServer/shutdown()``
+
+### Bundled transports
+
+- ``StdioTransport``
+- ``TCPBonjourTransport``
+- ``HTTPSSETransport``

+//
+//  JSONRPCFrame.swift
+//  SwiftMCP
+//
+//  Wire encoding for a JSON-RPC frame shared by the connection-based transports.
+//
+
+import Foundation
+
+/// Wire-format helpers for a JSON-RPC *frame* (an array of ``JSONRPCMessage``).
+///
+/// Connection-based transports that speak a byte stream (stdio, TCP) use this to
+/// turn an outbound frame into a single JSON payload, matching the historical
+/// encoding: a one-element frame is written as a single message object, a
+/// multi-element frame as a JSON array (a batch). Keys are sorted and dates use
+/// ISO-8601 with a time zone, identical to the legacy `Transport.send` path.
+enum JSONRPCFrame {
+    /// Encodes a frame to a single JSON payload.
+    ///
+    /// - Parameter frame: One or more JSON-RPC messages.
+    /// - Returns: JSON data — a bare object for a single message, an array for a
+    ///   batch.
+    static func encode(_ frame: [JSONRPCMessage]) throws -> Data {
+        let encoder = JSONEncoder()
+        encoder.dateEncodingStrategy = .iso8601WithTimeZone
+        encoder.outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys]
+        if frame.count == 1 {
+            return try encoder.encode(frame[0])
+        }
+        return try encoder.encode(frame)
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+//
+//  MCPConnection.swift
+//  SwiftMCP
+//
+//  The JSON-RPC duplex at the transport ↔ server boundary. See the
+//  <doc:Connection-Based-Transports> article for the full picture.
+//
+
+import Foundation
+
+/// A single, full-duplex JSON-RPC channel to one client.
+///
+/// A ``MCPTransport`` is a *source* of connections; each connection is one
+/// JSON-RPC conversation. The connection knows nothing about the MCP server —
+/// it only moves JSON-RPC messages in and out.
+/// ``MCPServer/serve(over:gracefulShutdownSignals:logger:)`` is the bridge that
+/// pulls each connection's ``inbound`` messages, routes them through the server,
+/// and writes replies back with `send(_:)`.
+///
+/// The base protocol deals in **single messages** — the common case, and the
+/// only shape MCP `2025-06-18` and later use (that revision removed JSON-RPC
+/// batching). A transport that needs to carry batches conforms to
+/// ``MCPBatchConnection`` instead, which adds a whole-frame interface.
+///
+/// ## Testability
+///
+/// Because a connection is just two JSON-RPC streams, it can be exercised
+/// without any networking: feed a canned ``inbound`` stream and assert on what
+/// `send(_:)` receives. No server, sockets, or `ServiceGroup` required.
+public protocol MCPConnection: Sendable {
+    /// JSON-RPC messages arriving from the client.
+    ///
+    /// The stream finishes when the client disconnects or the underlying
+    /// transport stops, which lets the per-connection routing loop in
+    /// `serve(over:)` end cleanly.
+    var inbound: AsyncStream<JSONRPCMessage> { get }
+
+    /// Sends a JSON-RPC message to the client.
+    ///
+    /// Server→client pushes — responses, progress and log notifications emitted
+    /// mid–tool-call, or `sampling`/`elicitation`/`roots` requests — all travel
+    /// through this method.
+    ///
+    /// - Parameter message: The message to deliver.
+    /// - Throws: A transport-specific error if the message cannot be written
+    ///   (for example, the connection has already closed).
+    func send(_ message: JSONRPCMessage) async throws
+}
+
+/// A connection that can also carry JSON-RPC *batches* — a top-level array of
+/// messages that must round-trip as one wire payload.
+///
+/// Batching was removed in MCP `2025-06-18`, so this is an opt-in refinement for
+/// transports that still need to interoperate with older clients. A batch-capable
+/// transport (stdio, TCP) conforms to `MCPBatchConnection`;
+/// ``MCPServer/serve(over:gracefulShutdownSignals:logger:)`` then routes whole
+/// frames through ``MCPServer/processBatch(_:ignoringEmptyResponses:)`` (and
+/// applies the version-gated batch reject), instead of the per-message path it
+/// uses for a plain ``MCPConnection``.
+///
+/// Conformers implement only the batch members; the single-message
+/// ``MCPConnection`` requirements are derived for free (a message is sent as a
+/// one-element frame, and ``MCPConnection/inbound`` flattens
+/// ``inboundBatches``).
+public protocol MCPBatchConnection: MCPConnection {
+    /// Inbound JSON-RPC frames. A single message arrives as a one-element frame;
+    /// a JSON-RPC batch arrives as a multi-element frame.
+    var inboundBatches: AsyncStream<[JSONRPCMessage]> { get }
+
+    /// Sends a whole JSON-RPC frame as one wire payload, preserving batch
+    /// semantics.
+    /// - Parameter batch: One or more JSON-RPC messages to deliver together.
+    /// - Throws: A transport-specific error if the frame cannot be written.
+    func send(_ batch: [JSONRPCMessage]) async throws
+}
+
+public extension MCPBatchConnection {
+    /// Derives the single-message inbound stream by flattening ``inboundBatches``.
+    /// `serve` consumes ``inboundBatches`` directly for batch connections, so
+    /// this exists only to satisfy ``MCPConnection`` conformance.
+    var inbound: AsyncStream<JSONRPCMessage> {
+        let batches = inboundBatches
+        return AsyncStream { continuation in
+            let task = Task {
+                for await frame in batches {
+                    for message in frame {
+                        continuation.yield(message)
+                    }
+                }
+                continuation.finish()
+            }
+            continuation.onTermination = { _ in task.cancel() }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Sends a single message as a one-element frame.
+    func send(_ message: JSONRPCMessage) async throws {
+        try await send([message])
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+//
+//  MCPConnectionTransport.swift
+//  SwiftMCP
+//
+//  Internal glue: lets a connection-backed `Session` push outbound bytes
+//  through an `MCPConnection`. Gated behind `Server` alongside the rest of the
+//  connection-based serving stack.
+//
+
+#if Server
+import Foundation
+import Logging
+
+/// A minimal ``Transport`` adapter that forwards a ``Session``'s outbound bytes
+/// to an ``MCPConnection``.
+///
+/// ``Session`` writes every server→client message (responses, progress and log
+/// notifications, `sampling`/`roots` requests) through its weakly-held
+/// ``Transport``. When ``MCPServer/serve(over:gracefulShutdownSignals:logger:)``
+/// routes a connection it binds one of these as the session's transport, so all
+/// of the server's existing outbound paths flow over the connection unchanged —
+/// no modification to ``Session`` or the request handlers required.
+///
+/// The adapter only implements outbound (`send`); inbound is driven by the
+/// connection's ``MCPConnection/inbound`` stream, and the run-loop/lifecycle is
+/// owned by the real ``MCPTransport``. Its lifecycle methods are therefore
+/// no-ops.
+final class MCPConnectionTransport: Transport, @unchecked Sendable {
+    /// The connection outbound bytes are forwarded to.
+    let connection: any MCPConnection
+
+    /// Logger inherited from `serve(over:)`.
+    let logger: Logger
+
+    init(connection: any MCPConnection, logger: Logger) {
+        self.connection = connection
+        self.logger = logger
+    }
+
+    func start() async throws {}
+    func run() async throws {}
+    func stop() async throws {}
+
+    /// Decodes the JSON-RPC payload `Session` produced and forwards it on the
+    /// connection.
+    ///
+    /// `Session` always hands us a single encoded message (responses,
+    /// notifications, `sampling`/`roots` requests), so we decode and forward it
+    /// via the single-message ``MCPConnection/send(_:)``. A batch connection turns
+    /// that into a one-element frame.
+    func send(_ data: Data) async throws {
+        let messages = try JSONRPCMessage.decodeMessages(from: data)
+        for message in messages {
+            try await connection.send(message)
+        }
+    }
+}
+#endif
