``` clojure
       com.cognitect.aws/endpoints {:mvn/version "1.1.12.504"}
       com.cognitect.aws/s3 {:mvn/version "848.2.1413.0"}}}
```

## Description with failing test case

In this scenario any valid request fails with the stack trace below.

The cause turned out to be due to a dependency conflict, so there's nothing to fix per se in this library. Maintainers could close this issue directly. However it was tedious to debug, so I'm documenting it in hopes of saving someone else the difficulty.

The issue turns out to be that if your project includes an older version of `clojure.data.xml` (in my case `0.0.8`, the last stable version) then `cognitect.aws.util/xml-read` will throw due to the keyword arguments to `clojure.data.xml/parse` being invalid. This isn't immediately obvious from the error about nulls. It was necessary to use `clojure.data.xml` version `0.2.0-alpha8`.

contract_addendum: # Clarification: XML response parsing must not depend on the consuming application's `clojure.data.xml` version The failure described in the issue occurs when an application using this library resolves an older version of `clojure.data.xml` (for example the last stable release, `0.0.8`) onto its classpath, instead of the `0.2.0` alpha line this library was developed against. In that situation, processing any otherwise valid XML response fails while parsing (with an `IllegalArgumentException` such as "Property null is not supported"), even though the response document itself is well formed. ## Expected library behavior The XML parsing this library performs for response bodies must be self contained. Applications may have any version of `clojure.data.xml`, or none, on their classpath, so parsing and handling valid XML response and error documents must not depend on which version of `clojure.data.xml` (if any) the consuming application resolves, or on whether `clojure.data.xml` has been loaded in the runtime at all. Specifically: - Parsing and handling well formed UTF-8 XML documents, as the library does for response bodies, must complete without throwing for valid response and error documents (for example typical AWS service responses and `......` error documents), for response elements that are empty or carry attributes, and for documents containing a DOCTYPE, comments, processing instructions, CDATA sections, repeated sibling elements, or whitespace between elements. - These outcomes must be identical whether the runtime resolves the older stable `clojure.data.xml` release, the `0.2.0` alpha line, or no `clojure.data.xml` at all, must not change by loading a version of `clojure.data.xml` in the runtime, and must hold on the classpath an application using this library would resolve with any of those `clojure.data.xml` versions. - Applications must be able to log, print or serialize the results of response handling as usual, so those results must be printable values. ## Out of scope - No new public API is required. How the library realizes this outcome, including the concrete representation it parses response bodies into and the shape of its ingested response maps, is an implementation detail. - Full behavioral or output equivalence with `clojure.data.xml` is not required, and no `clojure.data.xml` namespace may appear in any observable result or printed representation. - The library may keep, change, extend or remove its own declared dependencies, including `clojure.data.xml`, to realize this outcome. - Parsing behavior for malformed XML documents is not specified by this contract.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/cognitect/aws/util/xml.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+(ns cognitect.aws.util.xml
+  "For internal use. Do not call directly.
+
+  Parse XML strings into Clojure maps. Simplified version of clojure.data.xml/parse,
+  expected to be backwards compatible.
+
+  Authors: Ghadi Shayban, Marco Biscaro"
+  (:require [clojure.string :as str])
+  (:import (java.net URLEncoder)
+           (javax.xml.stream XMLInputFactory
+                             XMLStreamConstants
+                             XMLStreamReader)))
+
+(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)
+
+(def ^:private factory
+  (delay (doto (XMLInputFactory/newInstance)
+           (.setProperty XMLInputFactory/IS_NAMESPACE_AWARE false)
+           (.setProperty XMLInputFactory/IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES false)
+           (.setProperty XMLInputFactory/IS_COALESCING true))))
+
+(def ^:private consts
+  {XMLStreamConstants/END_DOCUMENT  :doc/end
+   XMLStreamConstants/START_ELEMENT :el/start
+   XMLStreamConstants/END_ELEMENT   :el/end
+   XMLStreamConstants/CHARACTERS    :chars})
+
+(defn- attr-key
+  [^XMLStreamReader rdr i]
+  (let [attr-ns (.getAttributeNamespace rdr i)
+        attr-local-name (.getAttributeLocalName rdr i)]
+    (keyword (when-not (str/blank? attr-ns)
+               ; For compatibility with clojure.data.xml
+               (URLEncoder/encode (str "xmlns." attr-ns) "UTF-8"))
+             attr-local-name)))
+
+(defn- read-element
+  [^XMLStreamReader rdr]
+  (let [name (.getLocalName rdr)
+        nattrs (.getAttributeCount rdr)]
+    {:tag   (keyword name)
+     :attrs (loop [i 0 attrs {}]
+              (if (< i nattrs)
+                (recur (inc i)
+                       (assoc attrs
+                         (attr-key rdr i)
+                         (.getAttributeValue rdr i)))
+                attrs))}))
+
+(defn- xml->map
+  [^XMLStreamReader rdr]
+  ;; stack is interleaved: coll, element-info, coll, element-info...
+  (loop [stack nil content []]
+    (if (.hasNext rdr)
+      (let [tok (.next rdr)
+            tok (consts tok tok)]
+        (case tok
+          ;; when an element nests, push current coll and nested element info
+          :el/start (recur (conj stack content (read-element rdr)) [])
+          ;; pop element info and parent coll, add element to parent coll
+          :el/end (let [[el pcontent & stack] stack]
+                    (recur stack (conj pcontent (assoc el :content content))))
+          :chars (recur stack (cond-> content (not (.isWhiteSpace rdr)) (conj (.getText rdr))))
+          :doc/end (nth content 0)
+          ;; skip other types (e.g. comment, ignorable space, dtd, cdata)
+          (recur stack content)))
+      (throw (IllegalStateException. "unreachable")))))
+
+(defn parse
+  [^java.io.Reader rdr]
+  (let [^XMLInputFactory factory @factory]
+    (xml->map (.createXMLStreamReader factory rdr))))

problem_statement:
Swap the Atlassian MCP for the working jira MCP (sooperset/mcp-atlassian) across setup.sh, skills, and app
## Summary

Replace the **Atlassian remote MCP** (`mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp`, server name `atlassian`) — added in #522/#524 but **not working** — with the **`jira` MCP** that is confirmed working (`ghcr.io/sooperset/mcp-atlassian`, stdio via Docker). Everything that currently uses the Atlassian MCP for Jira fetch / create / assign / transition should switch to the `jira` MCP.

## Why

The Atlassian remote MCP server doesn't work in our setup. A self-hosted `jira` MCP (sooperset/mcp-atlassian) is already configured globally and works. Migrate all Crow Jira tooling to it and remove the Atlassian one.

## The two servers

**Old — remove (`atlassian`):**
```json
{ "atlassian": {
    "type": "http",
    "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "${ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION}" } } }
```
- Cloud-hosted; requires a `cloudId` resolution step (`getAccessibleAtlassianResources`).
- Tools: `getJiraIssue`, `createJiraIssue`, `editJiraIssue`, `transitionJiraIssue`, `getTransitionsForJiraIssue`, `lookupJiraAccountId`, `atlassianUserInfo`.

**New — adopt (`jira`, already in `~/.claude.json`):**
```json
{ "jira": {
    "type": "stdio",
    "command": "docker",
    "args": ["run","-i","--rm","-e","JIRA_URL","-e","JIRA_USERNAME","-e","JIRA_API_TOKEN",
             "ghcr.io/sooperset/mcp-atlassian:latest","--transport","stdio"] } }
```
- Self-hosted bridge; **no `cloudId` concept.**
- Auth via env: `JIRA_URL`, `JIRA_USERNAME`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (Docker `-e`).
- Tools (different names — note the `jira_` prefix): `jira_get_issue`, `jira_create_issue`, `jira_update_issue`, `jira_transition_issue`, `jira_get_transitions`, `jira_search`, `jira_add_comment`, `jira_get_user_profile` / current-user lookup. (Confirm exact tool names against the running server.)

## What uses the Atlassian MCP today (all must switch)

1. **Skill `setup.sh`** (`.claude/skills/crow-workspace/setup.sh`) — `resolve_atlassian_mcp_env()` reads `atlassianMCP` from `config.json` (`.endpoint`, email, `op://` token ref), and the `.mcp.json` writer injects the `atlassian` HTTP server + `ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION` into the worktree `settings.local.json` env + `enabledMcpjsonServers`. Switch to provisioning/trusting the `jira` stdio server instead.
2. **Skill docs** — the `### Jira (Atlassian MCP)` sections + tool references in `crow-workspace/SKILL.md`, `crow-batch-workspace/SKILL.md`, and `crow-create-ticket/SKILL.md`. Rewrite to the `jira_*` tool names and drop the `cloudId` / `getAccessibleAtlassianResources` step.
3. **Crow app (#522/#524)** — any Settings → Automation surface for the Atlassian MCP token / endpoint, and any app-side `.mcp.json` / session injection. Repoint at the `jira` server (Docker stdio + `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USERNAME`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN`), or rely on the user's global `jira` server and just auto-trust it.
4. **devRoot `.mcp.json`** — currently pins the `atlassian` server; replace with `jira` (or stop managing it if the global config is authoritative).

## Decision to make (call out in the PR)

- **Injection vs. global:** the `jira` server already lives in the user's global `~/.claude.json`. Either (a) have `setup.sh` inject the `jira` stdio config into each worktree `.mcp.json` (self-contained), or (b) stop injecting and just auto-trust the pre-existing global `jira` server (`enabledMcpjsonServers`). Pick one; (b) is simpler if the global server is reliably present.
- **Secret handling:** `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USERNAME`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` (Docker `-e`) replace the single `ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION` header. If Crow injects, route these through the existing `op://` secret mechanism (don't commit the API token).

## Acceptance criteria

- No remaining references to `mcp.atlassian.com` / the `atlassian` MCP server / `ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION` in `setup.sh`, the skills, the app, or `.mcp.json`.
- A Crow-launched Jira-workspace session can **fetch, create, assign, and transition** a `MAXX` work item via the `jira` MCP (`jira_*` tools) — including the create-with-assignee flow that motivated #522.
- The skills' Jira sections document the `jira_*` tool names (no `cloudId` step).
- Manager + cron headless paths still work with the `jira` server.

## Notes

- Related/depends: #522 / PR #524 (introduced the Atlassian MCP), #523 (jiraStatusMap — its `transitionJiraIssue` consumer becomes `jira_transition_issue`), #526 (mark-done context menu — same transition path).
- Keep `gh`/`glab` GitHub/GitLab paths untouched — Jira-only swap.

### Additional contract requirements

The task's solutions are evaluated only on the externally observable migration
outcomes stated in the task description. The following clarifications apply:

- Session behavior for Jira-backed workspaces must use the `jira` MCP server's
  documented `jira_*` tools (fetch, create with assignee, update/assign, and
  transition by workflow status), and the checked-in skill documents must
  describe that `jira_*` tool surface without the retired cloudId resource
  resolution step. The skills' documented `jira_*` flow must keep the full
  fetch / create-with-assignee / assign / transition path reachable, and it is
  used by interactive and Manager/cron (headless) sessions alike.
- The retired cloud-hosted Atlassian remote MCP server
  (`mcp.atlassian.com`/`v1/mcp`), an MCP server registered under the retired
  `atlassian` server name, and the `ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION` secret must
  not remain an ACTIVE reference in any user-facing surface: the workspace
  setup script, the skills, the app's session launch / automation-settings /
  configuration surfaces, and the engineering documentation must not register,
  trust, authenticate, or steer sessions at that hosted server. References
  that exist solely to delete or clear that previously persisted state (for
  example a script line or helper call whose effect is only to remove the
  retired server key, its trust entry, or its secret from a stale settings
  file) are allowed; they are not active retired-server references. Historical
  mentions (release notes, migration explanations, and comments explaining
  removed behavior) are likewise not active references. And unrelated uses of
  the vendor name — Jira ticket URLs and site hosts such as `*.atlassian.net`,
  and plain Jira account or authentication settings — are not retired-server
  references at all.
- Either provisioning approach explicitly offered in the task description is
  equally acceptable: the checked-in setup surface may inject the `jira` stdio
  (Docker, env-flag authenticated) server into each worktree, or the app may
  inject nothing and rely on the user's pre-existing global `jira` server.
  In either case there must be a launch/configuration path by which both
  interactive and Manager/cron (headless) sessions reach the `jira` MCP
  server, and any injected registration must be a registration FOR the server
  named `jira` (by server key, container image, or explicit naming) using the
  Docker stdio bridge authenticated through all three of the `JIRA_URL`,
  `JIRA_USERNAME`, and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` environment flags rather than a hosted
  HTTP endpoint.
- The required call-out of the chosen provisioning approach may live in any
  checked-in surface — an engineering document under `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
  `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or a comment in the provisioning script or
  configuration itself. It must state that launched sessions work against the
  `jira` MCP server.
- Where the repository ships a checked-in file together with the checked-in
  template the app generates that file from (the workspace skills and the
  provisioning script), the two must stay consistent on their Jira MCP
  behavior so a freshly generated workspace gets the migrated behavior.
- No particular Swift type, property, resolver function, view, configuration
  key, documentation file location, or migration of previously persisted
  configuration is required; solutions may use any internal naming and
  structure that delivers the behaviors above.

+import Foundation
+import Testing
+
+// Externally observable contract for migrating Crow's Jira tooling off the
+// retired hosted remote MCP server and onto the `jira` MCP server (a
+// Docker-launched stdio bridge authenticated through the `JIRA_URL` /
+// `JIRA_USERNAME` / `JIRA_API_TOKEN` environment flags). These suite-level
+// tests assert only the user-facing outcomes the requirements state, so no
+// Swift type, property, resolver, view, or configuration-key name is pinned,
+// and both expressly permitted provisioning choices pass:
+//
+//   (a) a checked-in provisioning surface injects the `jira` stdio server
+//       into each worktree, or
+//   (b) the app injects nothing and relies on the user's pre-existing global
+//       `jira` server registration, documenting / trusting it.
+//
+// What "not an active retired-server reference" means here (mirroring the
+// public contract): references whose effect is solely to delete or clear
+// previously persisted retired state are permitted, and historical mentions
+// (release notes, migration explanations, doc/code comments that explain
+// removed behavior) are likewise permitted. Unrelated uses of the vendor
+// name — Jira site hosts such as `acme.atlassian.net`, plain Atlassian
+// account or CLI settings — are never retired-server references. Scans are
+// context-aware rather than raw-token bans: retired markers are accepted
+// inside fenced code blocks and inline code spans (`.md`), in `#`/`//`/doc
+// comments, and in migration / legacy-decode code lines carrying an explicit
+// cleanup or historical framing — while any line that still teaches,
+// registers, authenticates, or steers sessions at the retired hosted server
+// or its retired tool names fails wherever it is checked in, including
+// inside heredoc-generated configuration bodies. Discovery is repo-wide: the
+// retired-flow retirement scan does not rely on a fixed file list, so moving
+// the retired flow to an unlisted file cannot evade it.
+
+// MARK: - Repository file access
+
+// Anchors on a directory that is stable across checkouts: the checked-in
+// skills tree always lives at <repo>/skills/crow-workspace.
+private func jiraSwapRepoRoot() throws -> URL {
+    let probe = URL(fileURLWithPath: FileManager.default.currentDirectoryPath)
+    let anchor = probe.appendingPathComponent("skills/crow-workspace")
+    #expect(FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: anchor.path),
+            "repo root not found at \(probe.path) — run the tests from a repository checkout")
+    return probe
+}
+
+private func jiraSwapRepoFileText(_ relativePath: String) throws -> String {
+    let url = try jiraSwapRepoRoot().appendingPathComponent(relativePath)
+    return try String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8)
+}
+
+private func jiraSwapRepoFileExists(_ relativePath: String) throws -> Bool {
+    FileManager.default.fileExists(
+        atPath: try jiraSwapRepoRoot().appendingPathComponent(relativePath).path)
+}
+
+// MARK: - Retired-surface markers
+
+// The retired hosted remote server: its endpoint, its `mcp__atlassian` tool
+// namespace, the eight retired tool names, its `atlassian` server-name key,
+// and the retired authorization setting. Plain Jira site hosts
+// (`*.atlassian.net`) and unquoted uses of the vendor name in REST/auth
+// contexts are NOT retired-server references and never appear here.
+private let jiraSwapRetiredTools = [
+    "getJiraIssue", "createJiraIssue", "editJiraIssue", "transitionJiraIssue",
+    "getTransitionsForJiraIssue", "lookupJiraAccountId", "atlassianUserInfo",
+    "getAccessibleAtlassianResources",
+]
+
+private let jiraSwapServerMarkers = ["mcp.atlassian.com", "mcp__atlassian"] + jiraSwapRetiredTools
+
+private let jiraSwapToolNamespaces = jiraSwapRetiredTools.map { "mcp__atlassian__" + $0 }
+
+private let jiraSwapRetiredKeys = [
+    #""atlassian""#, "'atlassian'", "$atlassian", ".atlassianMCP",
+    #""atlassianMCP""#, "ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION",
+]
+
+// Markers that steer a session when they appear in Swift CODE — including
+// a string literal that restores the retired vendor MCP label (a UI section
+// or prompt restored to the retired "Atlassian MCP" flow re-teaches the
+// retired surface).
+private let jiraSwapSwiftCodeMarkers = jiraSwapServerMarkers + jiraSwapToolNamespaces
+    + jiraSwapRetiredKeys + ["Atlassian MCP", "atlassian MCP"]
+
+// Markers whose appearance in a Swift COMMENT counts as teaching the retired
+// tooling unless the line carries explicit historical framing. Quoted
+// vendor-name mentions inside historical comments are permitted — a comment
+// explaining removed behavior may name what was removed.
+private let jiraSwapSwiftCommentMarkers = jiraSwapServerMarkers + jiraSwapToolNamespaces
+    + jiraSwapRetiredKeys + ["`atlassian`", "`atlassianMCP`", "`AtlassianMCP`"]
+
+// Words that mark a line or a small surrounding block of lines as cleanup /
+// migration / historical CONTEXT: the retired mention exists only to delete
+// or clear stale state, or to explain removed behavior. CONTEXT words may sit
+// on the same line as the mention or anywhere in the small surrounding unit
+// the scans consider (a short code block, a comment directly above or below,
+// or a heredoc body); they NEVER reach across a string-literal boundary, so
+// the code that hosts a generated configuration payload and the payload
+// itself are framed separately. Only the retired mention itself is excused —
+// the scans keep the code half and comment half of each line distinct.
+private let jiraSwapPurposeWords = [
+    "migrat", "legacy", "tolerate", "clean", "delete", "remove", "histor",
+    "backward", "stale", "pre-crow", "previously", "deprecat", "no longer",
+    "formerly", "used to", "pulled from", "moved off", "replace", "retire",
+    "compat", "fallback", "backfill", "shim", "obsolete", "old", "strip",
+    "gone", "dropped", "never written", "never used", "no longer used",
+    "toggling off", "toggling", "turned off", "dangling", "previous version",
+    "used a cloud", "leftover", "leftovers", "scrub",
+]
+
+// Words that mean RETIRED STATE IS REMOVED HERE: unlike the context words
+// above, a removal word only excuses a retired mention on its OWN physical
+// line, so a line cannot borrow a removal comment that belongs to other
+// cleanup code around it. Matching is by whole word, so `cleanup`
+// qualifies, while a call name merely containing it does not by itself
+// frame a sibling line.
+private let jiraSwapRemovalWords: Set<String> = [
+    "clean", "delete", "remove", "unset", "strip",
+]
+
+// MARK: - Lexical helpers
+
+// Blanks the interior of single-backtick code spans (`...`), so historical
+// `code` mentions such as `getJiraIssue` do not count as operational prose.
+private func jiraSwapBlankingInlineCode(_ text: String) -> String {
+    var result = ""
+    for rawLine in text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) {
+        var line = ""
+        var inSpan = false
+        for ch in rawLine {
+            if ch == "`" {
+                inSpan.toggle()
+                line.append(ch)
+            } else if inSpan {
+                line.append(" ")
+            } else {
+                line.append(ch)
+            }
+        }
+        result += line + "\n"
+    }
+    return result
+}
+
+// Removes fenced code blocks (``` / ~~~) from a markdown-ish text so JSON
+// snippets, historical examples, and command listings inside fences do not
+// trip the operational-prose scans. A file with unbalanced fences yields no
+// prose (nothing is asserted for it).
+private func jiraSwapMarkdownProse(_ text: String) -> String {
+    let fenceCount = text.components(separatedBy: "```").count - 1
+    guard fenceCount % 2 == 0 else { return "" }
+    var out: [String] = []
+    var inFence = false
+    for rawLine in text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) {
+        let line = String(rawLine)
+        let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        if trimmed.hasPrefix("```") || trimmed.hasPrefix("~~~") {
+            inFence.toggle()
+            continue
+        }
+        if !inFence { out.append(line) }
+    }
+    return out.joined(separator: "\n")
+}
+
+private func jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(_ line: String) -> Bool {
+    let lower = line.lowercased()
+    return jiraSwapPurposeWords.contains { lower.contains($0) }
+}
+
+// True when the line itself states a removal of the retired surface: a whole
+// word like `remove` / `delete` / `unset` / `cleanup` appears on THIS line
+// (not merely somewhere nearby).
+private func jiraSwapLineHasRemovalWord(_ line: String) -> Bool {
+    let lower = line.lowercased()
+    for word in jiraSwapRemovalWords {
+        if lower.range(of: "\\b" + word + "\\b", options: .regularExpression) != nil {
+            return true
+        }
+    }
+    return false
+}
+
+// True when a mention of the retired authorization secret exists only to
+// delete, clear, or guard the cleanup of that previously persisted state:
+// a `del(...)` excision, a `select(. != ...)` removal filter, a `grep -q`
+// stale-state detection gate, a cleanup/removed flag assignment, a
+// legacy-config decoder, or an explicit migration / cleanup / historical
+// framing word anywhere on the line. A line that still WRITES or EXPORTS
+// the secret settles none of these shapes.
+private func jiraSwapRetiredSecretLineIsCleanup(_ line: String) -> Bool {
+    let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+    if trimmed.hasPrefix("#") || trimmed.hasPrefix("//") || trimmed.hasPrefix("*") { return true }
+    if line.contains("del(") { return true }
+    if line.contains("select(. !=") { return true }
+    let lower = line.lowercased()
+    if lower.contains("grep -q") || lower.contains("grep -qe") { return true }
+    if lower.contains("cleanup=") || lower.contains("removed_") { return true }
+    if lower.contains("decodeifpresent(") && lower.contains("forkey") { return true }
+    if lower.contains("unset") { return true }
+    if lower.contains("atlassian_mcp_authorization")
+        && (lower.contains("= null") || lower.contains(": null")) { return true }
+    return jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(line)
+}
+
+// Splits one physical line into its code half, its RAW string-literal half
+// (the full text sitting between the literal's delimiters), and its comment
+// half, tracking """ ... """ multi-line string literals, "..." string
+// literals, and /* ... */ block comments across lines. Comment markers
+// inside string literals are not comment structure, and everything between
+// an opening """ and the next """ belongs to the literal, not to code — a
+// heredoc or settings payload generated into a worktree is configuration
+// DATA, framed by the code that hosts it, not Swift code itself.
+private func jiraSwapSplitCodeComment(
+    _ raw: String,
+    inBlockCommentAtStart: Bool,
+    inMultiLineLiteralAtStart: Bool
+) -> (code: String, literal: String, comment: String,
+      nextInBlockComment: Bool, nextInMultiLineLiteral: Bool) {
+    var code = ""
+    var literal = ""
+    var comment = ""
+    var inBlock = inBlockCommentAtStart
+    var inTriple = inMultiLineLiteralAtStart
+    var inDouble = false
+    var escaped = false
+    let chars = Array(raw)
+    var idx = 0
+    while idx < chars.count {
+        let ch = chars[idx]
+        if escaped {
+            if inBlock { comment.append(ch) } else { code.append(ch) }
+            escaped = false
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+        }
+        if inBlock {
+            comment.append(ch)
+            if ch == "*" && idx + 1 < chars.count && chars[idx + 1] == "/" {
+                comment.append(chars[idx + 1])
+                inBlock = false
+                idx += 2
+                continue
+            }
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+        }
+        if ch == "\\" && inDouble {
+            escaped = true
+            code.append(ch)
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+        }
+        if inDouble {
+            // Interior of a "...": raw literal text, never code structure.
+            literal.append(ch)
+            if ch == "\"" { inDouble = false }
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+        }
+        if inTriple {
+            // Interior of a """ ... """ payload: raw literal text until the
+            // closing triple-quote; /* */ or // inside is payload data.
+            literal.append(ch)
+            if ch == "\"" && idx + 2 < chars.count
+                && chars[idx + 1] == "\"" && chars[idx + 2] == "\"" {
+                code.append(contentsOf: chars[idx..<(idx + 3)])
+                inTriple = false
+                idx += 3
+                continue
+            }
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+        }
+        if ch == "\"" && idx + 2 < chars.count
+            && chars[idx + 1] == "\"" && chars[idx + 2] == "\"" {
+            code.append(contentsOf: chars[idx..<(idx + 3)])
+            inTriple = true
+            idx += 3
+            continue
+        }
+        if ch == "\"" { inDouble = true; code.append(ch); idx += 1; continue }
+        if ch == "/" && idx + 1 < chars.count && chars[idx + 1] == "/" {
+            comment.append(contentsOf: chars[idx...])
+            idx = chars.count
+            continue
+        }
+        if ch == "/" && idx + 1 < chars.count && chars[idx + 1] == "*" {
+            comment.append(ch)
+            comment.append(chars[idx + 1])
+            inBlock = true
+            idx += 2
+            continue
+        }
+        code.append(ch)
+        idx += 1
+        escaped = false
+    }
+    return (code, literal, comment, inBlock, inTriple)
+}
+
+// MARK: - Shared scans
+
+// Recognize a retired key inside a multi-line expression whose observable
+// effect is to detect or remove old persisted state. JQ commonly formats
+// `del`, subtraction and `select` filters across several physical lines.
+private func jiraSwapIsCleanupExpression(_ lines: [String], at index: Int) -> Bool {
+    let start = max(0, index - 8)
+    let end = min(lines.count - 1, index + 8)
+    let window = lines[start...end].joined(separator: " ").lowercased()
+    guard window.contains("jq") || window.contains("del(") || window.contains("select(")
+            || window.contains(" - [") || window.contains("grep -q")
+            || window.contains("needs_cleanup") || window.contains("remove_retired") else { return false }
+    return window.contains("del(") || window.contains("select(")
+        || window.contains(" - [") || window.contains("!= null")
+        || window.contains("= null") || window.contains("has(")
+        || window.contains("grep -q") || window.contains("grep -qe")
+        || window.contains("needs_cleanup") || window.contains("remove_retired")
+}
+
+// Purpose-aware scan of provisioning and documentation text (.md prose,
+// .sh, .template): any shell segment (split at `;`, `&`, `|`) mentioning a
+// retired marker fails unless the whole physical line is a comment
+// (`#`/`//`/`*`), a deletion-only expression (`del(`), a removal filter
+// (`select(. != <retired key>)` / `map(select(...))` — removing the retired
+// server from a trust or env list is deletion by filtering), a stale-state
+// DETECTION gate (`grep -q` / `grep -qE` matching a marker merely guards a
+// needs-cleanup branch), a cleanup-flag assignment (`needs_cleanup=true`,
+// `removed_...=...`), a legacy-config decoder
+// (`decodeIfPresent(... forKey:`), or carries an explicit
+// migration / cleanup / historical framing word. The scan sees raw file
+// text, so a retired registration inside a heredoc-generated configuration
+// body is still caught.
+private func jiraSwapSegmentScan(_ relativePath: String, _ text: String,
+                                 markers: [String], scanLabel: String) {
+    let lines = text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
+    for (lineIndex, lineText) in lines.enumerated() {
+        let trimmed = lineText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        if trimmed.isEmpty { continue }
+        if trimmed.hasPrefix("#") || trimmed.hasPrefix("//") || trimmed.hasPrefix("*") { continue }
+        if jiraSwapIsCleanupExpression(lines, at: lineIndex) { continue }
+        // Removal-by-filtering IS deletion: `select(. != "atlassian")` and
+        // wrappers like `map(select(...))` exclude the retired server from a
+        // trust/env list instead of keeping or adding it.
+        if lineText.contains("select(. !=") { continue }
+        let lower = lineText.lowercased()
+        // Detecting stale persisted state is not using it: a `grep -q`-style
+        // match for a retired marker merely guards a cleanup branch, and
+        // assigning or consuming a needs-cleanup flag likewise only frames
+        // the cleanup path — neither registers the retired server.
+        if lower.contains("grep -q") || lower.contains("grep -qe") { continue }
+        if lower.contains("cleanup=") || lower.contains("removed_") { continue }
+        if lower.contains("decodeifpresent(") && lower.contains("forkey") { continue }
+        if lower.contains("atlassian_mcp_authorization")
+            && (lower.contains("= null") || lower.contains(": null")) { continue }
+        if jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(lineText) { continue }
+        for segment in lineText.components(separatedBy: CharacterSet(charactersIn: ";&|")) {
+            for marker in markers where segment.contains(marker) {
+                Issue.record(Comment(rawValue: "\(relativePath) (\(scanLabel)) actively references the retired Jira-MCP surface `\(marker)`: \(segment.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces))"))
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private func jiraSwapCommentContext(_ lines: [String], at index: Int) -> String {
+    func isComment(_ line: String) -> Bool {
+        let value = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        return value.hasPrefix("//") || value.hasPrefix("/*") || value.hasPrefix("*")
+    }
+    var first = index
+    while first > 0 && index - first < 5 && isComment(lines[first - 1]) { first -= 1 }
+    var last = index
+    while last + 1 < lines.count && last - index < 5 && isComment(lines[last + 1]) { last += 1 }
+    return lines[first...last].joined(separator: " ")
+}
+
+// Swift-source scan. Splits each physical line into a code half, a raw
+// string-literal half, and a comment half (`""" ... """` multi-line literals
+// tracked across lines — generated configuration payloads are literal DATA,
+// not Swift code, mirrored by the data-literal checks further below). A
+// retired marker in CODE is an active retired reference unless its small
+// surrounding unit (a short trailing run of comment-free lines, or the
+// leading comment of the NEXT line) carries an explicit migration / cleanup
+// / cleanup framing word — with removal words such as `remove` required
+// on the line itself — or the line is a legacy-config decoder
+// (`...decodeIfPresent(... forKey:`), a removal filter (`select(. != ...)` on
+// the same line only), or a bare enum-case naming declaration (`case
+// atlassianMCP` — a declaration binds a name only). A retired marker in
+// COMMENT text is permitted historical material when the line carries
+// explicit framing; an unframed comment that still points at the retired
+// endpoint, tool names, server keys, or the retired secret fails.
+@discardableResult
+private func jiraSwapSwiftScan(_ relativePath: String, _ text: String) -> [String] {
+    var inBlock = false
+    var inTriple = false
+    var inPayload = false
+    var dataLines: [String] = []
+    var trailingCommentFreeRun = 0
+    var scannedLines: [String] = []
+    let sourceLines = text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
+    for (lineIndex, lineText) in sourceLines.enumerated() {
+        let wasInPayload = inPayload
+        let parts = jiraSwapSplitCodeComment(lineText,
+                                             inBlockCommentAtStart: inBlock,
+                                             inMultiLineLiteralAtStart: inTriple)
+        // A strictly interior literal line (the """ opener owns only its own
+        // line): its raw text is generated configuration data, and a line
+        // the """ opener leaves open becomes payload until a line closes it.
+        let isPayloadInteriorLine = wasInPayload
+        let trimmedScannedCode = parts.code.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        inPayload = (isPayloadInteriorLine && parts.nextInMultiLineLiteral)
+            || (!isPayloadInteriorLine && trimmedScannedCode.hasSuffix("\"\"\""))
+        inBlock = parts.nextInBlockComment
+        inTriple = parts.nextInMultiLineLiteral
+        if isPayloadInteriorLine { dataLines.append(lineText) }
+        let code = parts.code
+        let trimmedCode = code.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        // Framing is recognized at the level of the small visible source
+        // unit: a short run of comment-free code lines just behind the line,
+        // or the comment introducing the next line (doc comments and block
+        // comments introduce or close out what follows them).
+        let commentFree = parts.comment.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty
+        if !commentFree { trailingCommentFreeRun = 0 } else { trailingCommentFreeRun += 1 }
+        var blockLines: [String] = []
+        if trailingCommentFreeRun > 0 && trailingCommentFreeRun <= 4 {
+            let take = jiraSwapFramingLookbehind + min(trailingCommentFreeRun - 1, jiraSwapFramingLookahead)
+            let start = max(0, scannedLines.count - take)
+            blockLines = Array(scannedLines[start...])
+        } else {
+            blockLines = [lineText]
+        }
+        scannedLines.append(lineText)
+        if scannedLines.count > 24 { scannedLines.removeFirst(scannedLines.count - 24) }
+        var blockFrame = blockLines.joined(separator: "\n")
+        // LATER lines cannot frame an earlier one; the enclosing leading
+        // comment of a short comment-free block (already inside blockLines)
+        // carries the context.
+        let blockHasPurpose = jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(blockFrame)
+        let hasPurpose = blockHasPurpose
+            && (jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(lineText) || !jiraSwapLineHasRemovalWord(blockFrame))
+        let codeMarkers = jiraSwapSwiftCodeMarkers.filter { code.contains($0) }
+        if !codeMarkers.isEmpty {
+            if isPayloadInteriorLine || hasPurpose
+                || (code.lowercased().contains("decodeifpresent(")
+                    && code.lowercased().contains("forkey"))
+                || trimmedCode.hasPrefix("case ")
+                || code.contains("select(. !=")
+                || jiraSwapLooksLikeLegacyDecoder(code) {
+                // A purpose-framed line migrates, decodes, filters out, or
+                // clears retired state; a case naming declaration binds a
+                // name only; a legacy decoder names the retired shape solely
+                // to read previously persisted state.
+            } else {
+                for marker in codeMarkers {
+                    Issue.record(Comment(rawValue: "\(relativePath) still contains an active retired Jira-MCP surface `\(marker)` in code: \(trimmedCode)"))
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        // A pure document/comment line that teaches the retired tooling with no
+        // historical framing fails; a code line's trailing comment is exempt —
+        // the CODE half of that line is what's enforced above.
+        let commentIsWholeLine = !isPayloadInteriorLine
+            && parts.code.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty
+            && parts.literal.isEmpty
+        if commentIsWholeLine && !parts.comment.isEmpty
+            && !jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(blockFrame)
+            && !jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(parts.comment)
+            && !jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(jiraSwapCommentContext(sourceLines, at: lineIndex)) {
+            for marker in jiraSwapSwiftCommentMarkers where parts.comment.contains(marker) {
+                Issue.record(Comment(rawValue: "\(relativePath) comment still teaches the retired Jira-MCP surface `\(marker)` without historical framing: \(lineText.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces))"))
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    // Lines that sat strictly BETWEEN a """ opener and its closer: raw
+    // string-literal data, not Swift code. Trimmed entries only; a closer
+    // line that opened its own literal adds a bare """ sentinel that is not
+    // payload content.
+    return dataLines
+        .map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }
+        .filter { !$0.isEmpty && $0 != "\"\"\"" }
+}
+
+// How many lines behind a code line its framing unit may extend: a compact
+// migration / cleanup comment plus one or two adjacent code lines — never
+// far enough for a generally documented file to frame an unrelated
+// registration further below.
+private let jiraSwapFramingLookbehind = 4
+// Of a comment-free code line's run, only this many lines BEFORE the line
+// itself may contribute framing; the rest of the run follows it and cannot
+// frame it.
+private let jiraSwapFramingLookahead = 2
+
+// App scaffolding host sources: files whose multi-line string literals hold
+// full configuration payload bodies generated into scaffolded worktrees.
+// The consistency of a host literal with the checked-in file it duplicates
+// is asserted by the generated-payload contract below.
+private let jiraSwapScaffoldingHostFiles: Set<String> = [
+    "Sources/Crow/App/Scaffolder.swift",
+    "Sources/Crow/App/CrowScaffolder.swift",
+]
+
+// Markers retired in a configuration PAYLOAD body: the retired hosted
+// endpoint, its `mcp__atlassian` tool namespace, the eight retired tool
+// names, and its `atlassian` server-name key. The retired authorization
+// SECRET — a bare environment-variable token, not a substring of vendor
+// tooling names — is validated line-by-line below, the same as in the
+// .sh / .template surfaces. A non-MCP REST/auth mention such as
+// `acme.atlassian.net` or `ATLASSIAN_EMAIL` is never retired-server
+// content.
+private let jiraSwapRetiredConfigMarkers = jiraSwapServerMarkers
+    + [#""atlassian""#, "'atlassian'", #""atlassianMCP""#]
+
+// Two configuration texts "echo" each other on the retired surface when
+// every retired marker appears in both or in neither: a fallback literal
+// that still grants exactly what the checked-in permissions copy still
+// grants is a faithful mirror of that copy, while a literal whose retired
+// content drifts ahead of or behind the copy no longer is.
+private func jiraSwapPayloadEchoes(_ checkedIn: String, _ payload: String) -> Bool {
+    for marker in jiraSwapRetiredConfigMarkers
+        where checkedIn.contains(marker) != payload.contains(marker) {
+        return false
+    }
+    return checkedIn.contains("ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION")
+        == payload.contains("ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION")
+}
+
+// The generated-payload contract, checked token-aware on the
+// string-literal half of the scan: a multi-line string literal that a
+// scaffolding host embeds as a configuration body must not teach, register,
+// pre-trust, or authenticate the retired hosted server beyond what a
+// checked-in copy of that same payload still does; a stale mention that a
+// checked-in copy still carries stays answerable to that copy's own scans,
+// while a payload line whose retired mention exists solely to remove the
+// retired state — a whole removal word on the same line — is the sanctioned
+// deletion-only behavior, not the active record.
+private func jiraSwapCheckScaffoldingHostPayloads(_ relativePath: String,
+                                                       _ text: String) {
+    let payloadLines = jiraSwapSwiftScan(relativePath, text)
+    guard !payloadLines.isEmpty else { return }
+    let payloadText = payloadLines.joined(separator: "\n")
+    let checkedInCopies: [String] = ["settings.json"].compactMap {
+        try? jiraSwapRepoFileText($0)
+    }
+    for payloadLine in payloadLines {
+        for marker in jiraSwapRetiredConfigMarkers where payloadLine.contains(marker) {
+            // A payload line that frames its own retired mention as cleanup
+            // (a whole removal word or a migration / compatibility framing
+            // word on the same line) is the sanctioned deletion-only
+            // behavior, not the active record.
+            if jiraSwapLineHasRemovalWord(payloadLine)
+                || jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(payloadLine) { continue }
+            // A payload that merely mirrors the cleanup of the checked-in
+            // copy it scaffolds from adds no rule of its own: whenever the
+            // copy it ships alongside is equally retired in this marker, the
+            // provisioning scans already hold the copy to account; the
+            // payload becomes answerable only once it drifts past the copy
+            // it was generated from.
+            if checkedInCopies.contains(where: {
+                $0.contains(marker) }) { continue }
+            if checkedInCopies.contains(where: {
+                jiraSwapPayloadEchoes($0, payloadText) }) { continue }
+            Issue.record(Comment(rawValue: "\(relativePath) still contains an active retired Jira-MCP surface `\(marker)` inside a generated configuration payload: \(payloadLine)"))
+        }
+        if payloadLine.contains("ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION")
+            && !jiraSwapRetiredSecretLineIsCleanup(payloadLine)
+            && !checkedInCopies.contains(where: { $0.contains("ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION") }) {
+            Issue.record(Comment(rawValue: "\(relativePath) still writes or exports the retired authorization setting inside a generated configuration payload: \(payloadLine)"))
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// A code line that decodes a legacy-named Codable shape: the retired server
+// name appears only in the type name of a migration/deprovisioning decoder
+// (e.g. `struct LegacyAtlassianMCP: Decodable` or
+// `let legacy = try LegacyAtlassianMCP(from: decoder)`), never as a live
+// registration the app persists for new sessions.
+private func jiraSwapLooksLikeLegacyDecoder(_ code: String) -> Bool {
+    let lower = code.lowercased()
+    guard lower.contains("legacy") || lower.contains("decodable") || lower.contains("decoder") else {
+        return false
+    }
+    // Only naming markers (the retired type/binding names) may remain — an
+    // endpoint, tool name, or secret is never migration scaffolding.
+    for marker in jiraSwapSwiftCodeMarkers where code.contains(marker) {
+        let isTypeName = marker == "Atlassian MCP" || marker == "atlassian MCP"
+            || marker == ".atlassianMCP" || marker == "$atlassian"
+            || marker == #""atlassian""# || marker == #""atlassianMCP""#
+        if !isTypeName { return false }
+    }
+    return true
+}
+
+// Every quoted `atlassian`-family server key in a provisioning text must sit
+// inside a deletion/cleanup context: the six lines above it, its own line,
+// or the line just after it carry a deletion word. The window spans a
+// multi-line jq pipeline or case branch, so a framing cleanup comment
+// separated from the retired key by unrelated `del()`/filter lines still
+// counts. An active registration adds the key with no such framing anywhere
+// in its enclosing expression — including when the registration is the body
+// of a heredoc that generates a config file.
+private func jiraSwapRetiredKeysAreDeletionsOnly(_ text: String) -> (ok: Bool, suspicious: String?) {
+    let lines = text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
+    let keyMarkers = [#""atlassian""#, "'atlassian'", #""atlassianMCP""#]
+    for (index, line) in lines.enumerated() {
+        let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        if trimmed.hasPrefix("#") || trimmed.hasPrefix("//") || trimmed.hasPrefix("*") { continue }
+        guard keyMarkers.contains(where: { line.contains($0) }) else { continue }
+        let lower = line.lowercased()
+        if jiraSwapIsCleanupExpression(lines, at: index)
+            || jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(line)
+            || lower.contains("decodeifpresent(")
+            || lower.contains("cleanup=") || lower.contains("removed_") { continue }
+        return (false, line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces))
+    }
+    return (true, nil)
+}

+// Enumerates checked-in text files, skipping repository metadata, build
+// products, symlinks, and the test suite itself (test code is not a
+// user-facing surface).
+private func jiraSwapTextFiles(extensions: Set<String>) throws -> [(path: String, text: String)] {
+    let fm = FileManager.default
+    let root = try jiraSwapRepoRoot()
+    guard let enumerator = fm.enumerator(at: root, includingPropertiesForKeys: []) else {
+        Issue.record("cannot enumerate the checkout")
+        return []
+    }
+    var files: [(String, String)] = []
+    for case let url as URL in enumerator {
+        let absolutePath = url.path
+        // Skip symlinks (they may point outside the checkout).
+        if (try? fm.destinationOfSymbolicLink(atPath: absolutePath)) != nil { continue }
+        let relative: String
+        if absolutePath.hasPrefix(root.path + "/") {
+            relative = String(absolutePath.dropFirst(root.path.count + 1))
+        } else { continue }
+        if relative.hasPrefix(".git/") || relative.hasPrefix(".build/") || relative.contains("/.build/")
+            || relative.hasPrefix(".rebench_contract/") { continue }
+        if relative.hasPrefix("Tests/") || relative.contains("/Tests/") { continue }
+        guard !relative.hasSuffix("/") else { continue }
+        let ext = url.pathExtension.isEmpty ? "" : "." + url.pathExtension.lowercased()
+        guard extensions.contains(ext) else { continue }
+        guard let values = try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey, .isRegularFileKey]),
+              values.isRegularFile == true,
+              let size = values.fileSize, size < 1_000_000 else { continue }
+        guard let text = try? String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8) else { continue }
+        files.append((relative, text))
+    }
+    return files
+}

+// The retired-hook suites (AtlassianMCPResolverTests.swift and
+// ClaudeHookConfigWriterMCPTests.swift) are deleted or rewritten by the
+// migration's test patch, so their source type names are not asserted here —

+@Test func jiraSwapHookWriterDropsRetiredRegistrationSurface() throws {
+    let path = "Packages/CrowClaude/Sources/CrowClaude/ClaudeHookConfigWriter.swift"
+    guard try jiraSwapRepoFileExists(path) else {
+        Issue.record("\(path) is missing — the launch-side configuration writer should exist")
+        return
+    }
+    // Before the migration, this writer actively registered the retired
+    // hosted server into launched worktrees; afterwards it must not
+    // register, trust, authenticate, or point launched sessions at the
+    // retired server. Because the migration itself deletes the exact
+    // retired strings, the scan first exempts every COMMENT, every line
+    // whose code carries an explicit cleanup / migration / removal framing
+    // word, and every deletion / clearing / stale-state-detection shape —
+    // exactly the lines the contract allows (`removeValue(forKey:
+    // "atlassian")`, `removeAll { $0 == "atlassian" }`,
+    // `env.removeValue(forKey: "ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION")`, a
+    // `select(. != ...)` exclusion, an `unset`/`del(` shell excision, a
+    // `grep -q` stale-state gate). A bare, unframed line that still
+    // REGISTERS, TRUSTS, AUTHENTICATES, or teaches the retired surface
+    // fails wherever it is written.
+    let text = try jiraSwapRepoFileText(path)
+    for rawLine in text.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) {
+        let line = String(rawLine)
+        // Comments, doc lines, and cleanup/detection shapes never register.
+        guard !jiraSwapRetiredSecretLineIsCleanup(line) else { continue }
+        let parts = jiraSwapSplitCodeComment(line, inBlockCommentAtStart: false,
+                                             inMultiLineLiteralAtStart: false)
+        let code = parts.code
+        var working = code
+        if working.lowercased().contains("decodeifpresent(") {
+            working.removeAll { $0 == "\"" }
+        }
+        let hasFramingHere = !parts.comment.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty
+            || jiraSwapLineHasPurpose(code)
+        guard !hasFramingHere else { continue }
+        let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        #expect(!working.contains("mcp.atlassian.com"),
+                Comment(rawValue: "\(path) still points launched sessions at the retired hosted endpoint: \(trimmed)"))
+        #expect(!working.contains("mcp__atlassian"),
+                Comment(rawValue: "\(path) still pre-trusts the retired server's tool namespace: \(trimmed)"))
+        #expect(!working.contains("ATLASSIAN_MCP_AUTHORIZATION"),
+                Comment(rawValue: "\(path) still provisions the retired authorization setting as a live credential: \(trimmed)"))
+        // The retired server-NAME key is an active reference only as a
+        // word-leading occurrence — a registration, assignment, trust-list
+        // append, or declaration such as `servers["atlassian"]`,
+        // `static let ... = "atlassian"`, or `enabled.append("atlassian")`;
+        // removal-closure and exclusion-comparison shapes carry a removal
+        // word and were exempted above.
+        let nameIsActive = working.range(
+            of: #"(:?=|\[)"atlassian""#, options: .regularExpression) != nil
+            || working.range(of: #"(^|[\s(\[{,;])"atlassian""#, options: .regularExpression) != nil
+            || (working.contains("'atlassian'") && !jiraSwapLineHasRemovalWord(code))
+        #expect(!nameIsActive,
+                Comment(rawValue: "\(path) still embeds the retired server's registration name as active code: \(trimmed)"))
+    }
+}

+    let aboutJira = text.contains("`jira`") || text.contains("jira MCP")
+        || text.contains("mcp__jira") || text.contains(#""jira""#)

+}
+
+/// Whether any checked-in surface GENUINELY satisfies provisioning
+/// CHOICE (a) — the provisioning script or its template intrinsically
+/// registers a `jira`-named MCP server over the Docker stdio bridge
+/// authenticated by all three JIRA_URL / JIRA_USERNAME / JIRA_API_TOKEN
+/// environment flags.
+private func jiraSwapStdioInjectionPresent() -> Bool {
+    for path in [jiraSwapSetupScript, jiraSwapSetupTemplate] {
+        guard let text = try? jiraSwapRepoFileText(path) else { continue }
+        if jiraSwapRegistersStdioJiraServer(text) { return true }
+    }
+    return false
+}
+
+/// Whether any checked-in surface GENUINELY satisfies provisioning
+/// CHOICE (b) — documented reliance on the user's pre-existing global
+/// `jira` server (or an explicit statement that the app injects nothing
+/// and sessions use that global registration).
+private func jiraSwapGlobalJiraRelianceDocumented() -> Bool {
+    for path in ["docs/automation.md", "docs/configuration.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "README.md",
+                 "CLAUDE.md", jiraSwapSetupScript, jiraSwapSetupTemplate] {
+        guard let text = try? jiraSwapRepoFileText(path) else { continue }
+        if jiraSwapDocumentsGlobalJiraTrust(text) || text.contains("injects nothing") { return true }
+    }
+    return false
+}
+
+@Test func jiraSwapRegistersStdioJiraServerForPerWorktreeInjection() throws {
+    // Provisioning CHOICE (a), per-worktree injection. Whether this specific
+    // path is taken or deliberately waived is recorded so the evaluation
+    // shows which of the two permitted provisioning paths an attempt took.
+    // The contract explicitly permits EITHER choice — the checked-in setup
+    // surface may inject the stdio/Docker `jira` server per worktree, or the
+    // app may inject nothing and rely on the user's pre-existing global
+    // `jira` server — so waiving a path is only sanctioned alongside its
+    // documented counterpart; NEITHER choice being satisfied fails here.
+    let injectionSurface: String? = [jiraSwapSetupScript, jiraSwapSetupTemplate].first { path in
+        guard let text = try? jiraSwapRepoFileText(path) else { return false }
+        return jiraSwapRegistersStdioJiraServer(text)
+    }
+    let relianceDocumented = jiraSwapGlobalJiraRelianceDocumented()
+    let waived = relianceDocumented && injectionSurface == nil
+    if !waived && injectionSurface == nil {
+        Issue.record("no checked-in provisioning surface injects the stdio/Docker `jira` server authenticated by JIRA_URL / JIRA_USERNAME / JIRA_API_TOKEN into each worktree (provisioning choice (a)), and no checked-in surface documents reliance on the user's pre-existing global `jira` server (provisioning choice (b)) — the task permits either, but at least one path must be taken")
+    }
+    if let surface = injectionSurface, let text = try? jiraSwapRepoFileText(surface) {
+        #expect(!text.contains("https://mcp."),
+                "\(surface) must not register a hosted HTTP MCP endpoint")
+        #expect(!text.contains(#""type": "http""#),
+                "\(surface) must not register a hosted HTTP MCP server")
+        let envAuth = text.contains("JIRA_URL") && text.contains("JIRA_USERNAME")
+            && text.contains("JIRA_API_TOKEN")
+        #expect(envAuth, "\(surface) registers `jira` without the full JIRA_URL / JIRA_USERNAME / JIRA_API_TOKEN env-flag authentication")
+    }
+}
+
+@Test func jiraSwapDocumentsGlobalJiraServerReliance() {
+    // Provisioning CHOICE (b), documented reliance on the user's
+    // pre-existing global `jira` server. Whether this specific path is taken
+    // or deliberately waived is recorded so the evaluation shows which of
+    // the two permitted provisioning paths an attempt took. The contract
+    // explicitly permits EITHER choice, so waiving a path is only sanctioned
+    // alongside its genuine counterpart; NEITHER choice being satisfied
+    // fails here.
+    let relianceDocumented = jiraSwapGlobalJiraRelianceDocumented()

+    }

+@Test func jiraSwapLaunchPathReachesJiraServerForInteractiveAndHeadless() throws {

+    // the two permitted provisioning choices the migration took. Each choice

#endif

  -module-name CrowCoreTests -parse-as-library -o "$B/core/coretest.o" 2>&1 | grep -E "error:"
[ -f "$B/core/coretest.o" ] || { echo "CrowCore TEST COMPILE FAILED (target symbols JiraCredential/JiraCredentialResolver/AppConfig.jiraCredential missing at base)"; exit 92; }

[ -f "$B/claude/claudetest.o" ] || { echo "CrowClaude TEST COMPILE FAILED"; exit 93; }
swiftc -I "$B/core" -I "$B/claude" -c "$B/gen/Runner.swift" -module-name RunMain -parse-as-library -o "$B/runner.o" 2>&1 | grep -E "error:"

[ -f "$B/runtests" ] || { echo "LINK FAILED"; exit 94; }
"$B/runtests" --event-stream-output-path /tmp/rebench-test-results.jsonl
st=$?
echo "--- machine-readable results: /tmp/rebench-test-results.jsonl ---"
cat /tmp/rebench-test-results.jsonl 2>/dev/null
exit $st

problem_statement:
crow hook-event blocks on the daemon RPC reply it never uses — busy MainActor stalls every hook to the 5s hook timeout (should be fire-and-forget)
## Summary

`crow hook-event` performs a **blocking** JSON-RPC round-trip and waits for the daemon's reply — but the reply is never used for anything except printing an error. Because the daemon serializes every RPC on the `@MainActor` (`EngineRouter`), any busy window (board poll, git/worktree op, whole-`store.json` write, or a burst of concurrent hook-events) stalls the hook-event RPC until Claude Code's 5s hook timeout kills it. The hook is meant to be fire-and-forget (the code comment says so) — the wait-for-response is accidental and should be removed.

## Evidence (measured from Claude Code transcripts, ~50 sessions / 2 days on the Manager host)

PreToolUse:Bash hook durations are **bimodal** — fast or timeout, nothing between:
- 0–200ms: 232 runs (88%)
- ~5s timeout: 31 runs (11%)
- 200ms–4.9s: 0 runs

A slow-but-completing op would smear across 200ms–3s. A clean fast-or-5s split is the signature of a **block**, not slow code.

The timeouts **cluster in busy windows** and concentrate in a few sessions (not spread across the 263 calls):
- 2026-07-27 17:55–17:56 — ~16 timeouts in a ~90s burst
- 2026-07-28 19:14–19:50 — steady ~1/20–60s for 36 min, almost all from one session (24 of ~50 timeouts came from a single session; two others contributed 12 and 9)

Other per-call/per-prompt hooks show the same tail: UserPromptSubmit (32 runs, 6 timeouts), PreToolUse:Edit (68, 6), PreToolUse:Read (27, 3), Stop (29, 3). All hooks are the same `crow hook-event … --event X` call, so they share the one bottleneck.

Cost: each timeout is a ~5s stall before the tool runs (hook cancelled, Claude proceeds). ~49 stalls ≈ ~4 min of dead wait, concentrated in the busy sessions. Annoying, not corrupting — but it makes heavy Manager/batch periods drag.

## Root cause (pinned to source)

`Packages/CrowCLI/Sources/CrowCLILib/Commands/HookEventCommand.swift:61` — `forwardHookEvent`:

[HIDDEN]

Daemon handler `Packages/CrowEngine/Sources/CrowEngine/EngineRouter.swift:1208` runs on the `@MainActor` router (line 15; nearly every handler does `await MainActor.run { … }`) and does a whole-store `mutate`. So hook-event must acquire the MainActor, contending with board polls, git ops, and every other terminal's hook-events (each rewriting the full store — the single-writer design). During busy windows it queues; the CLI blocks on a reply it doesn't use; the 5s hook timeout fires. The doc comment above the code already states "Hooks are fire-and-forget" — the blocking wait contradicts the intended design.

## Proposed fix

1. **Primary (client-side, ~one function):** make `hook-event` a genuine fire-and-forget notification — send it as a JSON-RPC notification (no `id`) or write the payload to the socket and return without awaiting the response. Keep the existing `SocketError.connectionFailed` silent no-op (missing daemon is expected). The daemon still processes the event when the MainActor frees; Claude Code never waits. This removes the stall outright and matches the code's stated intent. Verify no hook consumes the hook-event *output* to gate a tool (PreToolUse here is a pure notification — nothing does).
2. **Structural (daemon-side, follow-up):** ensure board polling / long git ops don't hold the MainActor across their network/subprocess `await` — hop to MainActor only for the final state mutation, so hook-events aren't starved during polls. Consider not doing a synchronous whole-store write on every hook-event notification (coalesce), which would also cut the per-event MainActor pressure.

## Non-fix

Raising the 5s hook `timeout` in the scaffolded settings is the wrong lever — it makes each stall *longer* before giving up, not rarer. Don't.

## Related

- #874 (CLOSED) — "Blocking NSLog on the MainActor can wedge the daemon's RPC surface." Same MainActor-serialization failure class, but scoped to an NSLog on `reload-tmux-config`'s success path. Its fix does NOT cover this: hook-event still blocks whenever the MainActor is *legitimately* busy (polls, store writes, bursts) — which is what the 07-27/07-28 windows above show.
- #728 (CLOSED), #304/#404/#250 (CLOSED) — adjacent MainActor-contention symptoms (store-write race; UI freeze under concurrent reviews).

Refactor: reduce per-layer boilerplate and duplicated math in src/layers/ (~250–350 lines)
Full-repo review found that `src/layers/` (~1324 lines) carries **~250–350 lines** of per-layer boilerplate and duplicated math that could be generated or shared, a 25–30% reduction of the directory.

## 1. Struct/constructor/getproperty boilerplate repeated 10× (~200 net lines)

Every layer repeats the same five-part pattern: inner constructor asserting `size(par, 1) == nparams` and `ndims(par) == N + 1`; `Layer(par)` outer constructor; kwarg constructor via `vstack`; `Layer(::Type{T}, sz)` with per-parameter defaults; `Layer(sz) = Layer(Float64, sz)`; then `Base.propertynames` + a `Base.getproperty` if-chain of views into `par`.

Locations: `binary.jl:6–23`, `spin.jl:13–30`, `potts.jl:12–29`, `pottsgumbel.jl:6–23`, `gaussian.jl:6–39`, `relu.jl:6–39`, `drelu.jl:6–49`, `prelu.jl:8–49`, `xrelu.jl:6–45`, `nsReLU.jl:7–33`, plus `common.jl:1–2` (per-layer `Union` for `size`/`length`) and `common.jl:6–15` (`_FieldLayers` getproperty). Total ≈ 300 lines whose only variable content is the layer name, the parameter-name tuple, and the per-parameter default initializer (`zeros` vs `ones`).

Proposed refactor: [HIDDEN]

```julia
[HIDDEN]
```

(~50–60 lines, defined once near `abstractlayer.jl`), [HIDDEN] Ten invocations plus retained docstrings ≈ 100 lines total. The inner constructor should always call `_validate_layer_parameters` (default no-op, `abstractlayer.jl:3`), which absorbs pReLU's special validation hook (`prelu.jl:13–15`) with no per-layer escape hatch.

Constraints for the macro to be zero-behavioral-risk:

- [HIDDEN]
- [HIDDEN]
- `Adapt.@adapt_structure` (`src/adapt.jl`) and `ext/HDF5Ext.jl:114–123` only depend on the single `par` field and the `Layer(par)` constructor — both preserved.
- Cost: macros hurt greppability; mitigate by keeping the docstrings at call sites.

Independent micro-win even without the macro: replace `common.jl:1–2` and the redundant `drelu.jl:31–33` overrides with generic `Base.size(l::AbstractLayer) = [HIDDEN]` and `Base.length(l::AbstractLayer) = [HIDDEN]` in abstractlayer.jl — type-stable, works for all layers, and removes the `Union` that must be extended for every new layer.

## 2. dReLU two-sided-mixture preamble copy-pasted 7× (~85–140 lines)

The ~12-line block building the two-sided ReLU mixture (construct `lp`/`ln`, compute `Γp`/`Γn`/`Γ = logaddexp`, weights `pp`/`pn`, truncated-normal moments `μp, νp`/`μn, νn`) appears essentially verbatim in:

- `drelu.jl:76–89` (`mean_from_inputs`), `91–105` (`var_from_inputs`), `107–122` (`meanvar_from_inputs`), `124–138` (`mean_abs_from_inputs`), `140–160` (`∂cgfs`)
- `prelu.jl:75–101` (`∂cgfs`), `xrelu.jl:57–87` (`∂cgfs`)

Proposed refactor, two independent steps:

1. A private helper in drelu.jl [HIDDEN]; each call site keeps only its final 2–6 lines of layer-specific algebra (~65 lines saved). `mean_from_inputs` and `var_from_inputs` of dReLU can additionally become one-liners over `meanvar_from_inputs` (~25 more). Essentially risk-free.
2. Deeper option: `∂cgfs(::pReLU)` and `∂cgfs(::xReLU)` are the dReLU gradient pushed through the reparameterization Jacobian of `dReLU(layer)` (the maps at `common.jl:89–96` and `106–114`). Computing `∂ = ∂cgfs(dReLU(layer), inputs)` and contracting with the analytic Jacobian would collapse `prelu.jl:75–101` and `xrelu.jl:57–87` (~55 lines) to ~20, and eliminate the risk of the hand-expanded formulas drifting from the parameter maps. Same idea applies to `∂energy_from_moments` (`prelu.jl:103–121` vs `xrelu.jl:89–108`, near-identical modulo `η = ξ/(1+|ξ|)`). The existing Zygote/FiniteDifferences gradient checks in `test/layers.jl` are exactly the safety net needed; note the Jacobian-contraction form changes floating-point association slightly.

(The family layering is otherwise already clean — pReLU/xReLU/nsReLU delegate `energies`/`cgfs`/`sample`/`mean`/`var`/`mode` through `dReLU(layer)` / `xReLU(layer)` one-liners, and the conversion math lives once in `common.jl:81–129`. Only `∂cgfs`/`∂energy_from_moments` escape that scheme.)

## 3. Generic `anneal` via `par` interpolation (~50 lines)

`src/ais.jl:114–170` defines 9 per-layer `anneal` methods, plus a 10th at `pottsgumbel.jl:51–54`; every one is exactly `(1 - β) * init.par + β * final.par` spelled out parameter-by-parameter (every named parameter is a row of `par`). One generic method suffices:

```julia
[HIDDEN]
```

`anneal_zero` (`ais.jl:174–182`) is **not** pure par-scaling (zeroes fields, keeps scales) — leave it per-layer. pReLU validation still runs via its constructor; interpolating η within (−1, 1) stays in (−1, 1).

## 4. Safe quick wins (~60 lines, near-zero risk)

- `drelu.jl:162–170` (`moments_from_samples`) is character-for-character identical to `common.jl:149–157` (the `Union{pReLU, xReLU, nsReLU}` method). Widen the Union to include `dReLU` and delete the copy.
- `common.jl:131–147`: 17 lines of commented-out ReLU→dReLU/pReLU/xReLU conversions — delete (git history keeps them).
- `std_from_inputs(l, inputs) = sqrt.(var_from_inputs(l, inputs))` is written 8 times (`spin.jl:36`, `potts.jl:34`, `gaussian.jl:56`, `relu.jl:50`, `drelu.jl:74`, `prelu.jl:73`, `xrelu.jl:54`, `nsReLU.jl:42`). One `AbstractLayer` fallback replaces all; only Binary keeps its numerically nicer `binary_std` specialization.
- A generic fallback `meanvar_from_inputs(l, inputs) = (mean_from_inputs(l, inputs), var_from_inputs(l, inputs))` deletes `gaussian.jl:59–61`. Keep the Spin/Potts versions (they avoid recomputing `tanh`/`softmax`) and the genuinely fused Binary/ReLU/dReLU ones.
- `pottsgumbel.jl:28–34,42–46` are 12 one-line delegations through `Potts(layer.par)`, and `pottsgumbel.jl:47–49` duplicates `colors`/`sitedims`/`sitesize` that `common.jl:61,70,79` define for `Potts`. Defining the shared statistics on `Union{Potts, PottsGumbel}` removes the delegation layer except `sample_from_inputs` (the Gumbel trick — the one genuine difference).

## Related placement cleanup

`anneal`/`anneal_zero`/`initialize!` for PottsGumbel live in `pottsgumbel.jl:51–60` while every other layer's live in `ais.jl`/`initialization.jl`; same for nsReLU's `initialize!`, `∂regularize_fields`, `shift_fields` at `nsReLU.jl:60–80`, whose siblings live in `src/train/initialization.jl`, `src/regularize.jl`, `src/gauge/shift_fields.jl`. Worth normalizing one way or the other regardless of the refactors above.

### Additional contract requirements

# Layer refactor contract

The layer refactor preserves the public behavior of all existing layer types, including
constructors, named parameter accessors, dimensions, statistics, sampling, gradients,
and conversions.

- `anneal(init, final; β)` has common layer-level dispatch for every matching concrete
  `AbstractLayer` type.  It returns that layer type with its stored parameter array
  equal to the elementwise affine interpolation `(1 - β) * init.par + β * final.par`.
  Existing RBM annealing continues to interpolate its visible layer, hidden layer, and
  weights.
- `PottsGumbel` retains the Potts statistical operations while retaining its own
  sampling behavior.  Its initialization from one-hot data agrees with `Potts`, and
  its zero annealing result has zero fields.
- `nsReLU` initialization from data sets its field row to the batch mean and clears
  its auxiliary rows; no-argument initialization clears all of its parameters.
  Field shifts change only its field row, and field regularization applies only to
  that row.
- Field shifting, field regularization, and initialization remain available for the
  affected layer types after the refactor.

# Layer refactor contract

The layer refactor preserves the public behavior of all existing layer types, including
constructors, named parameter accessors, dimensions, statistics, sampling, gradients,
and conversions.

- `anneal(init, final; β)` has common layer-level dispatch for every matching concrete
  `AbstractLayer` type.  It returns that layer type with its stored parameter array
  equal to the elementwise affine interpolation `(1 - β) * init.par + β * final.par`.
  Existing RBM annealing continues to interpolate its visible layer, hidden layer, and
  weights.
- `PottsGumbel` retains the Potts statistical operations while retaining its own
  sampling behavior.  Its initialization from one-hot data agrees with `Potts`, and
  its zero annealing result has zero fields.
- `nsReLU` initialization from data sets its field row to the batch mean and clears
  its auxiliary rows; no-argument initialization clears all of its parameters.
  Field shifts change only its field row, and field regularization applies only to
  that row.
- Field shifting, field regularization, and initialization remain available for the
  affected layer types after the refactor.

+    # so dispatch must not depend on the specific layer type. Locate the method

+    # non-parametric generic signatures, unlike `which` on abstract tuples).

+    @test all(m -> m === first(layer_anneal_methods), layer_anneal_methods)

+    @test (@which anneal(rbm, rbm)) !== first(layer_anneal_methods)
+end

+    final = Layer(sz)

+    randn!(final.par)
