problem_statement:
Add versioned dynamic graph mutations and reconciliation
## Problem

Squidie can preview, record, and schedule bounded dynamic work, but current dynamic edges are inspection metadata rather than execution dependencies. Hosts cannot safely apply concurrent graph changes, remove unstarted dynamic work, or distinguish a committed mutation from incomplete dispatch scheduling.

This follows the broader graph-expansion direction completed in #141 and tightens it around the current journal runtime.

Reference: https://hexdocs.pm/jido/pods.html

## Proposed solution

Add opt-in versioned graph mutation APIs:

```elixir
Squidie.preview_graph_mutation(run_id, mutation,
  expected_version: 4,
  action_registry: registry
)

Squidie.apply_graph_mutation(run_id, mutation,
  expected_version: 4,
  action_registry: registry,
  queue: "default"
)

Squidie.reconcile_dynamic_graph(run_id,
  action_registry: registry,
  queue: "default"
)
```

A mutation is an atomic batch with a stable `mutation_id`, expected semantic graph version, origin, added nodes/edges, and optional removed node/edge IDs.

Reports expose base/result versions, duplicate state, applied operations, planned/ready/blocked/scheduled nodes, reconciliation status, and warnings. If the run-thread append committed but dispatch scheduling failed, return `status: :committed_needs_reconciliation` rather than an ambiguous rollback-style error.

## V1 semantics

- Support add node, add edge, remove edge, and constrained remove node.
- Resolve all executable nodes through the host action registry before append.
- Node and edge IDs are permanent; removed IDs are tombstoned and cannot be reused.
- The final active graph must be acyclic and reachable from an applied declared origin.
- Persist runnable intents for blocked nodes, but dispatch only when all active predecessors are durably applied.
- Reject new dependencies for nodes already ready, dispatched, claimed, completed, or failed.
- Exact retries of one mutation ID return duplicate success; different content with the same ID fails.
- Duplicate detection wins over a stale expected version.

A node may be removed only when it is blocked by an unsatisfied dependency, has no dispatch attempt, has not applied, has no retry/compensation work, and all incident edges are removed in the same batch. V1 never revokes already scheduled work.

## Persistence and recovery

- Append a `:dynamic_graph_mutated` fact and every planned runnable in one run-thread append using the current revision.
- Write dispatch-thread facts only after the run append commits.
- Schedule newly ready successors after each durable dynamic application.
- Include active dynamic nodes in terminal-state decisions; ignore tombstoned runnables.
- Reconciliation rebuilds projections and repairs missing queue markers or ready attempts, but never invents graph facts.
- Add a semantic `graph_version` independent from journal revision.

## Backward compatibility

- Preserve `preview_dynamic_work/3`, `record_dynamic_work/3`, and `schedule_dynamic_work/3` signatures and return contracts.
- Preserve legacy eager scheduling: existing dynamic edges remain inspection-only after rebuild.
- Record provenance distinguishing legacy eager work from dependency-ordered mutations.
- Deterministically derive graph versions from legacy records during checkpoint upgrade/rebuild.

## Implementation plan

- [ ] Define mutation, preview, report, and serialization contracts.
- [ ] Add graph version, mutation, and tombstone state to the workflow projection.
- [ ] Add the new journal fact and checkpoint upgrade behavior.
- [ ] Implement DAG, reachability, identity, version, and removal validation.
- [ ] Atomically append mutation facts and runnable intents before dispatch writes.
- [ ] Make pending dispatch and terminal calculations dependency/tombstone-aware.
- [ ] Implement explicit reconciliation and committed-needs-reconciliation reporting.
- [ ] Surface versions, readiness, active state, and mutation history through inspection.
- [ ] Enforce host-owned per-mutation and per-run graph limits.
- [ ] Update usage rules, docs, and the minimal-host example.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two writers at one graph version cannot both commit different mutations.
- [ ] Exact retry is idempotent and conflicting reuse is rejected.
- [ ] Mutation fact and runnable intents are all-or-nothing on the run thread.
- [ ] Run append failure creates no dispatch facts.
- [ ] Post-commit scheduling failure is visible and repairable.
- [ ] Chains and fan-in dispatch only after durable predecessor application.
- [ ] Only blocked, never-dispatched nodes can be removed.
- [ ] Removing an edge may make a target ready and schedules it after commit.
- [ ] Restarts/checkpoint loss rebuild identical versions, topology, and readiness.
- [ ] Legacy dynamic work retains eager behavior after upgrade.
- [ ] Terminal fencing, action allowlisting, retry persistence, and redaction remain intact.

## Verification

- Projection, validator, executor, fault-injection, Ecto atomic-append, graph inspection, and visibility tests.
- `mix precommit`
- Minimal host-app smoke path.

## Out of scope

- Replacing declared steps or revoking dispatched work.
- Updating an existing node's action, input, retry policy, or metadata.
- Cycles, loops, conditional/quorum edges, or reused tombstoned IDs.
- Automatic background reconciliation.
- Making dynamic actions replay-safe without a separate recovery contract.

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum defines observable requirements for the versioned graph mutation,
graph inspection, and dynamic-work compatibility surfaces that the acceptance
criteria and mutation APIs rely on. It refines the base statement for cases it
does not spell out and does not replace it.

## Inspection and snapshot state

`Squidie.inspect_run/2` returns a run snapshot and `Squidie.inspect_run_graph/2`
returns an inspection graph whose public map form exposes the following
versioned-mutation fields:

- `graph_version`: a non-negative integer semantic graph version, independent
  from per-thread journal revisions. It starts at 0 for a run with no graph
  records and increments deterministically on each committed versioned mutation
  and on each legacy dynamic-work record. A checkpoint rebuild derives the same
  version from persisted records.
- `graph_provenance`: a map of the shape
  `%{nodes: [%{id: string_id, provenance: provenance}], edges: [...]}` where
  `provenance` is either `:legacy_eager` or `:dependency_ordered`. It contains
  only public identity and provenance; node inputs, action options, errors,
  metadata, credentials, and trace state are never exposed.
- `active_node_ids`, `active_edge_ids`, `ready_node_ids`, `blocked_node_ids`,
  `tombstoned_node_ids`, `tombstoned_edge_ids`: lists of string IDs.
- `mutation_history`: a list of redacted mutation records. Each record contains
  only `mutation_id`, `origin`, `expected_version`, `result_version`, and the
  added/removed node and edge ID lists when present. Inputs, action options,
  errors, metadata, credentials, and trace data are never exposed.
- `reconciliation_status`: one of `:not_required`, `:required`, `:completed`,
  or `:unknown` (when queue state could not be read reliably).

These fields are redacted operator evidence. Their inspected representation must
not contain runnable input values or credential secrets.

## Legacy stored data normalization

Inspection survives legacy or partially corrupted persisted state deterministically:

- String-keyed legacy maps in graph provenance and mutation history are
  normalized to the public atom-keyed shapes above.
- Recognized string provenance values (for example `"dependency_ordered"` or
  `"legacy_eager"`) are normalized to the corresponding atoms.
- Recognized string reconciliation statuses (for example `"required"` or
  `"completed"`) are normalized to the corresponding atoms.
- Entries that are not maps with a string `id` are dropped. Non-string node or
  edge IDs (such as integers) are dropped. Non-list identity collections are
  treated as empty. Invalid versions normalize to 0 and invalid reconciliation
  statuses normalize to `:unknown`.
- Normalization removes extra payload fields that inspection does not publish;
  inputs and other sensitive values present on stored legacy records are not
  surfaced.

## Mutation validation and identity

Versioned mutations are validated before any durable commit:

- The final active graph after a mutation must be acyclic; any cycle (including
  a self-loop) is rejected.
- Every added executable node must be reachable from an applied declared origin;
  unreachable additions are rejected.
- Node and edge IDs are permanent. Removed IDs are tombstoned and may never be
  re-added. Declared workflow node and edge IDs and legacy eager dynamic
  identities may not be consumed or re-added either.
- Only a dynamic node that is blocked on an unsatisfied dependency, has never
  been dispatched or applied, has no pending retry or compensation work, and has
  all incident edges removed in the same mutation may be removed. Ready,
  dispatched, claimed, completed, failed, retried, or compensating nodes may not
  be removed.
- A mutation may not add a new dependency edge whose target node is already
  ready, dispatched, claimed, completed, or failed.
- Retry of the same `mutation_id` with identical normalized content returns a
  duplicate success regardless of the current graph version; duplicate detection
  wins over a stale `expected_version`. Reuse of the same `mutation_id` with
  different content is rejected, and a different mutation is rejected with a
  stale-version error whenever `expected_version` differs from the current graph
  version.
- Applying a mutation commits its intent on the run thread atomically; dispatch
  threads are written only after the run commit. If dispatch scheduling cannot
  be written after a commit, the mutation stays committed, exposed through
  inspection as `reconciliation_status: :required`, and the report carries
  `status: :committed_needs_reconciliation`. Reconciliation is idempotent:
  repairing it marks inspection `:completed` and scheduling nothing new.

## Dependency readiness

Dependency-ordered dynamic nodes remain pending until every active predecessor
has been durably applied; only then are they scheduled. Nodes are never exposed
as ready until their predecessors are durable. Inspection and dispatch stay
consistent after each durable mutation.

## Legacy eager behavior and rebuild compatibility

- `Squidie.preview_dynamic_work/3`, `Squidie.record_dynamic_work/3`, and
  `Squidie.schedule_dynamic_work/3` keep their existing signatures and return
  contracts, and legacy eager dynamic work remains inspection-only and eagerly
  dispatched; it is not gated by dependency readiness.
- Legacy eager dynamic work recorded before this feature coexists with versioned
  mutations in the same run and is exposed through inspection and graph
  provenance as `:legacy_eager`.
- After checkpoint loss or rebuild, inspection and graph views expose identical
  graph versions, provenance, readiness, active IDs, tombstones, and mutation
  history, and legacy eager attempts remain visible. Redaction, terminal
  fencing, action allowlisting, and retry persistence remain intact.
problem_statement_base:
Add versioned dynamic graph mutations and reconciliation
## Problem

Squidie can preview, record, and schedule bounded dynamic work, but current dynamic edges are inspection metadata rather than execution dependencies. Hosts cannot safely apply concurrent graph changes, remove unstarted dynamic work, or distinguish a committed mutation from incomplete dispatch scheduling.

This follows the broader graph-expansion direction completed in #141 and tightens it around the current journal runtime.

Reference: https://hexdocs.pm/jido/pods.html

## Proposed solution

Add opt-in versioned graph mutation APIs:

```elixir
Squidie.preview_graph_mutation(run_id, mutation,
  expected_version: 4,
  action_registry: registry
)

Squidie.apply_graph_mutation(run_id, mutation,
  expected_version: 4,
  action_registry: registry,
  queue: "default"
)

Squidie.reconcile_dynamic_graph(run_id,
  action_registry: registry,
  queue: "default"
)
```

A mutation is an atomic batch with a stable `mutation_id`, expected semantic graph version, origin, added nodes/edges, and optional removed node/edge IDs.

Reports expose base/result versions, duplicate state, applied operations, planned/ready/blocked/scheduled nodes, reconciliation status, and warnings. If the run-thread append committed but dispatch scheduling failed, return `status: :committed_needs_reconciliation` rather than an ambiguous rollback-style error.

## V1 semantics

- Support add node, add edge, remove edge, and constrained remove node.
- Resolve all executable nodes through the host action registry before append.
- Node and edge IDs are permanent; removed IDs are tombstoned and cannot be reused.
- The final active graph must be acyclic and reachable from an applied declared origin.
- Persist runnable intents for blocked nodes, but dispatch only when all active predecessors are durably applied.
- Reject new dependencies for nodes already ready, dispatched, claimed, completed, or failed.
- Exact retries of one mutation ID return duplicate success; different content with the same ID fails.
- Duplicate detection wins over a stale expected version.

A node may be removed only when it is blocked by an unsatisfied dependency, has no dispatch attempt, has not applied, has no retry/compensation work, and all incident edges are removed in the same batch. V1 never revokes already scheduled work.

## Persistence and recovery

- Append a `:dynamic_graph_mutated` fact and every planned runnable in one run-thread append using the current revision.
- Write dispatch-thread facts only after the run append commits.
- Schedule newly ready successors after each durable dynamic application.
- Include active dynamic nodes in terminal-state decisions; ignore tombstoned runnables.
- Reconciliation rebuilds projections and repairs missing queue markers or ready attempts, but never invents graph facts.
- Add a semantic `graph_version` independent from journal revision.

## Backward compatibility

- Preserve `preview_dynamic_work/3`, `record_dynamic_work/3`, and `schedule_dynamic_work/3` signatures and return contracts.
- Preserve legacy eager scheduling: existing dynamic edges remain inspection-only after rebuild.
- Record provenance distinguishing legacy eager work from dependency-ordered mutations.
- Deterministically derive graph versions from legacy records during checkpoint upgrade/rebuild.

## Implementation plan

- [ ] Define mutation, preview, report, and serialization contracts.
- [ ] Add graph version, mutation, and tombstone state to the workflow projection.
- [ ] Add the new journal fact and checkpoint upgrade behavior.
- [ ] Implement DAG, reachability, identity, version, and removal validation.
- [ ] Atomically append mutation facts and runnable intents before dispatch writes.
- [ ] Make pending dispatch and terminal calculations dependency/tombstone-aware.
- [ ] Implement explicit reconciliation and committed-needs-reconciliation reporting.
- [ ] Surface versions, readiness, active state, and mutation history through inspection.
- [ ] Enforce host-owned per-mutation and per-run graph limits.
- [ ] Update usage rules, docs, and the minimal-host example.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two writers at one graph version cannot both commit different mutations.
- [ ] Exact retry is idempotent and conflicting reuse is rejected.
- [ ] Mutation fact and runnable intents are all-or-nothing on the run thread.
- [ ] Run append failure creates no dispatch facts.
- [ ] Post-commit scheduling failure is visible and repairable.
- [ ] Chains and fan-in dispatch only after durable predecessor application.
- [ ] Only blocked, never-dispatched nodes can be removed.
- [ ] Removing an edge may make a target ready and schedules it after commit.
- [ ] Restarts/checkpoint loss rebuild identical versions, topology, and readiness.
- [ ] Legacy dynamic work retains eager behavior after upgrade.
- [ ] Terminal fencing, action allowlisting, retry persistence, and redaction remain intact.

## Verification

- Projection, validator, executor, fault-injection, Ecto atomic-append, graph inspection, and visibility tests.
- `mix precommit`
- Minimal host-app smoke path.

## Out of scope

- Replacing declared steps or revoking dispatched work.
- Updating an existing node's action, input, retry policy, or metadata.
- Cycles, loops, conditional/quorum edges, or reused tombstoned IDs.
- Automatic background reconciliation.
- Making dynamic actions replay-safe without a separate recovery contract.
contract_addendum:
This addendum defines observable requirements for the versioned graph mutation,
graph inspection, and dynamic-work compatibility surfaces that the acceptance
criteria and mutation APIs rely on. It refines the base statement for cases it
does not spell out and does not replace it.

## Inspection and snapshot state

`Squidie.inspect_run/2` returns a run snapshot and `Squidie.inspect_run_graph/2`
returns an inspection graph whose public map form exposes the following
versioned-mutation fields:

- `graph_version`: a non-negative integer semantic graph version, independent
  from per-thread journal revisions. It starts at 0 for a run with no graph
  records and increments deterministically on each committed versioned mutation
  and on each legacy dynamic-work record. A checkpoint rebuild derives the same
  version from persisted records.
- `graph_provenance`: a map of the shape
  `%{nodes: [%{id: string_id, provenance: provenance}], edges: [...]}` where
  `provenance` is either `:legacy_eager` or `:dependency_ordered`. It contains
  only public identity and provenance; node inputs, action options, errors,
  metadata, credentials, and trace state are never exposed.
- `active_node_ids`, `active_edge_ids`, `ready_node_ids`, `blocked_node_ids`,
  `tombstoned_node_ids`, `tombstoned_edge_ids`: lists of string IDs.
- `mutation_history`: a list of redacted mutation records. Each record contains
  only `mutation_id`, `origin`, `expected_version`, `result_version`, and the
  added/removed node and edge ID lists when present. Inputs, action options,
  errors, metadata, credentials, and trace data are never exposed.
- `reconciliation_status`: one of `:not_required`, `:required`, `:completed`,
  or `:unknown` (when queue state could not be read reliably).

These fields are redacted operator evidence. Their inspected representation must
not contain runnable input values or credential secrets.

## Legacy stored data normalization

Inspection survives legacy or partially corrupted persisted state deterministically:

- String-keyed legacy maps in graph provenance and mutation history are
  normalized to the public atom-keyed shapes above.
- Recognized string provenance values (for example `"dependency_ordered"` or
  `"legacy_eager"`) are normalized to the corresponding atoms.
- Recognized string reconciliation statuses (for example `"required"` or
  `"completed"`) are normalized to the corresponding atoms.
- Entries that are not maps with a string `id` are dropped. Non-string node or
  edge IDs (such as integers) are dropped. Non-list identity collections are
  treated as empty. Invalid versions normalize to 0 and invalid reconciliation
  statuses normalize to `:unknown`.
- Normalization removes extra payload fields that inspection does not publish;
  inputs and other sensitive values present on stored legacy records are not
  surfaced.

## Mutation validation and identity

Versioned mutations are validated before any durable commit:

- The final active graph after a mutation must be acyclic; any cycle (including
  a self-loop) is rejected.
- Every added executable node must be reachable from an applied declared origin;
  unreachable additions are rejected.
- Node and edge IDs are permanent. Removed IDs are tombstoned and may never be
  re-added. Declared workflow node and edge IDs and legacy eager dynamic
  identities may not be consumed or re-added either.
- Only a dynamic node that is blocked on an unsatisfied dependency, has never
  been dispatched or applied, has no pending retry or compensation work, and has
  all incident edges removed in the same mutation may be removed. Ready,
  dispatched, claimed, completed, failed, retried, or compensating nodes may not
  be removed.
- A mutation may not add a new dependency edge whose target node is already
  ready, dispatched, claimed, completed, or failed.
- Retry of the same `mutation_id` with identical normalized content returns a
  duplicate success regardless of the current graph version; duplicate detection
  wins over a stale `expected_version`. Reuse of the same `mutation_id` with
  different content is rejected, and a different mutation is rejected with a
  stale-version error whenever `expected_version` differs from the current graph
  version.
- Applying a mutation commits its intent on the run thread atomically; dispatch
  threads are written only after the run commit. If dispatch scheduling cannot
  be written after a commit, the mutation stays committed, exposed through
  inspection as `reconciliation_status: :required`, and the report carries
  `status: :committed_needs_reconciliation`. Reconciliation is idempotent:
  repairing it marks inspection `:completed` and scheduling nothing new.

## Dependency readiness

Dependency-ordered dynamic nodes remain pending until every active predecessor
has been durably applied; only then are they scheduled. Nodes are never exposed
as ready until their predecessors are durable. Inspection and dispatch stay
consistent after each durable mutation.

## Legacy eager behavior and rebuild compatibility

- `Squidie.preview_dynamic_work/3`, `Squidie.record_dynamic_work/3`, and
  `Squidie.schedule_dynamic_work/3` keep their existing signatures and return
  contracts, and legacy eager dynamic work remains inspection-only and eagerly
  dispatched; it is not gated by dependency readiness.
- Legacy eager dynamic work recorded before this feature coexists with versioned
  mutations in the same run and is exposed through inspection and graph
  provenance as `:legacy_eager`.
- After checkpoint loss or rebuild, inspection and graph views expose identical
  graph versions, provenance, readiness, active IDs, tombstones, and mutation
  history, and legacy eager attempts remain visible. Redaction, terminal
  fencing, action allowlisting, and retry persistence remain intact.

+  defp ensure_graph_reconciliation(reconciliation, dynamic_queue) do
+    if reconciliation.status == :reconciled and
+         reconciliation.repaired_queue_ids == [dynamic_queue] and
+         reconciliation.scheduled_node_ids == ["dynamic-chain", "dynamic-parallel"] do
+      :ok
+    else
+      {:error, :unexpected_graph_reconciliation}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp drain_graph_mutation_run(_run_id, _queues, 0) do
+    {:error, :timeout}
+  end
+
+  defp drain_graph_mutation_run(run_id, queues, attempts_remaining) do
+    case Squidie.inspect_run(run_id) do
+      {:ok, %Squidie.ReadModel.Inspection.Snapshot{terminal?: true} = run} ->
+        {:ok, run}
+
+      {:ok, %Squidie.ReadModel.Inspection.Snapshot{}} ->
+        Enum.each(queues, fn queue ->
+          _result =
+            Squidie.execute_next(
+              owner_id: "minimal-host-app-graph-mutation-smoke",
+              queue: queue
+            )
+        end)
+
+        drain_graph_mutation_run(run_id, queues, attempts_remaining - 1)
+
+      {:error, reason} ->
+        {:error, reason}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp ensure_completed_graph_mutation(graph) do
+    payload = Squidie.Runs.GraphInspection.to_map(graph)
+
+    if payload.terminal? and payload.graph_version == 1 and
+         payload.active_node_ids == ["dynamic-chain", "dynamic-join", "dynamic-parallel"] and
+         payload.ready_node_ids == [] and payload.blocked_node_ids == [] and
+         payload.reconciliation_status == :completed and
+         Enum.map(payload.mutation_history, & &1.mutation_id) == [
+           "minimal-host-graph-mutation"
+         ] do
+      :ok
+    else
+      {:error, :unexpected_completed_graph_mutation}
+    end
+  end
+
   defp journal_run_queue do
     "#{@journal_run_queue_prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
   end

diff --git a/lib/squidie/read_model/inspection/graph_state.ex b/lib/squidie/read_model/inspection/graph_state.ex
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b7094fe
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/squidie/read_model/inspection/graph_state.ex
@@ -0,0 +1,376 @@
+defmodule Squidie.ReadModel.Inspection.GraphState do
+  @moduledoc false
+
+  alias Squidie.MapField
+  alias Squidie.Runtime.DispatchAgent
+  alias Squidie.Runtime.WorkflowAgent.Projection
+
+  @identity_limit 500
+  @history_limit 100
+  @provenance_values [:legacy_eager, :dependency_ordered]
+  @reconciliation_statuses [:not_required, :required, :completed, :unknown]
+
+  @doc """
+  Builds a bounded public graph-state summary from a rebuilt workflow agent.
+  """
+  @spec from_agent(term(), Jido.Agent.t(), String.t()) :: map()
+  def from_agent(storage, workflow_agent, default_queue) when is_binary(default_queue) do
+    projection = workflow_agent.state.projection
+    graph = projection.graph
+    {ready_node_ids, blocked_node_ids} = readiness(projection)
+
+    %{
+      graph_version: valid_version(graph.version),
+      graph_provenance: provenance(graph.provenance),
+      active_node_ids: identities(graph.active_node_ids),
+      active_edge_ids: identities(graph.active_edge_ids),
+      ready_node_ids: identities(ready_node_ids),
+      blocked_node_ids: identities(blocked_node_ids),
+      tombstoned_node_ids: identities(graph.tombstoned_node_ids),
+      tombstoned_edge_ids: identities(graph.tombstoned_edge_ids),
+      mutation_history: mutation_history(graph.mutation_history),
+      reconciliation_status: reconciliation_status(storage, projection, graph, default_queue)
+    }
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Normalizes graph-state fields from current or legacy inspection data.
+  """
+  @spec sanitize(map()) :: map()
+  def sanitize(state) when is_map(state) do
+    %{
+      graph_version: valid_version(MapField.get(state, :graph_version)),
+      graph_provenance: provenance(MapField.get(state, :graph_provenance, %{})),
+      active_node_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :active_node_ids, [])),
+      active_edge_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :active_edge_ids, [])),
+      ready_node_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :ready_node_ids, [])),
+      blocked_node_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :blocked_node_ids, [])),
+      tombstoned_node_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :tombstoned_node_ids, [])),
+      tombstoned_edge_ids: identities(MapField.get(state, :tombstoned_edge_ids, [])),
+      mutation_history: mutation_history(MapField.get(state, :mutation_history, [])),
+      reconciliation_status:
+        normalize_reconciliation_status(MapField.get(state, :reconciliation_status))
+    }
+  end
+
+  defp readiness(%Projection{} = projection) do
+    graph = projection.graph
+    applied_node_ids = applied_node_ids(projection)
+    predecessors = active_predecessors(graph)
+
+    Enum.reduce(graph.active_node_ids, {MapSet.new(), MapSet.new()}, fn node_id,
+                                                                        {ready, blocked} ->
+      dependency_ordered? = Map.get(graph.provenance.nodes, node_id) == :dependency_ordered
+
+      cond do
+        not dependency_ordered? or MapSet.member?(applied_node_ids, node_id) ->
+          {ready, blocked}
+
+        MapSet.subset?(Map.get(predecessors, node_id, MapSet.new()), applied_node_ids) ->
+          {MapSet.put(ready, node_id), blocked}
+
+        true ->
+          {ready, MapSet.put(blocked, node_id)}
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp applied_node_ids(%Projection{} = projection) do
+    projection
+    |> Projection.planned_runnables()
+    |> Enum.reduce(MapSet.new(), fn runnable, node_ids ->
+      runnable_key = MapField.get(runnable, :runnable_key)
+      node_id = MapField.get(runnable, :step)
+
+      if is_binary(node_id) and
+           MapSet.member?(projection.applied_runnable_keys, runnable_key) do
+        MapSet.put(node_ids, node_id)
+      else
+        node_ids
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp active_predecessors(graph) do
+    Enum.reduce(graph.active_edge_ids, %{}, fn edge_id, predecessors ->
+      edge = Map.get(graph.topology.edges, edge_id, %{})
+      source = MapField.get(edge, :from)
+      target = MapField.get(edge, :to)
+
+      if is_binary(source) and is_binary(target) do
+        Map.update(predecessors, target, MapSet.new([source]), &MapSet.put(&1, source))
+      else
+        predecessors
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp reconciliation_status(_storage, _projection, graph, _default_queue)
+       when map_size(graph.mutation_history) == 0 do
+    :not_required
+  end
+
+  defp reconciliation_status(storage, projection, graph, default_queue) do
+    runnables = dependency_runnables(projection, graph)
+    dispatchable_keys = Projection.dispatchable_runnable_keys(projection)
+
+    runnables
+    |> Enum.filter(&MapSet.member?(dispatchable_keys, MapField.get(&1, :runnable_key)))
+    |> Enum.group_by(&(MapField.get(&1, :queue) || default_queue))
+    |> missing_dispatch_status(storage)
+  end
+
+  defp dependency_runnables(projection, graph) do
+    projection
+    |> Projection.planned_runnables()
+    |> Enum.filter(fn runnable ->
+      Map.get(graph.provenance.nodes, MapField.get(runnable, :step)) == :dependency_ordered
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp missing_dispatch_status(queues, storage) do
+    Enum.reduce_while(queues, :completed, fn {queue, runnables}, _status ->
+      case DispatchAgent.rebuild(storage, queue) do
+        {:ok, dispatch_agent} ->
+          queue_dispatch_status(dispatch_agent, runnables)
+
+        {:error, _reason} ->
+          {:halt, :unknown}
+      end
+    end)
+  end
+
+  defp queue_dispatch_status(dispatch_agent, runnables) do
+    attempts = dispatch_agent.state.projection.attempts
+
+    if Enum.any?(runnables, &missing_attempt?(&1, attempts)) do
+      {:halt, :required}
+    else
+      {:cont, :completed}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp missing_attempt?(runnable, attempts) do
+    runnable_key = MapField.get(runnable, :runnable_key)
+    not is_binary(runnable_key) or not Map.has_key?(attempts, runnable_key)
+  end
+
+  defp provenance(provenance) when is_map(provenance) do
+    %{
+      nodes: provenance_entries(MapField.get(provenance, :nodes, %{})),
+      edges: provenance_entries(MapField.get(provenance, :edges, %{}))
+    }
+  end
+
+  defp provenance(_provenance) do
+    %{nodes: [], edges: []}
+  end
+
+  defp provenance_entries(entries) when is_map(entries) do
+    entries
+    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {id, value} ->
+      case {id, normalize_provenance(value)} do
+        {id, provenance} when is_binary(id) and not is_nil(provenance) ->
+          [%{id: id, provenance: provenance}]
+
+        _invalid ->
+          []
+      end
+    end)
+    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.id)
+    |> Enum.take(@identity_limit)
+  end
+
+  defp provenance_entries(entries) when is_list(entries) do
+    entries
+    |> Enum.flat_map(fn entry ->
+      id = MapField.get(entry, :id)
+      value = normalize_provenance(MapField.get(entry, :provenance))
+
+      if is_binary(id) and not is_nil(value) do
+        [%{id: id, provenance: value}]
+      else
+        []
+      end
+    end)
+    |> Enum.uniq_by(& &1.id)
+    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.id)
+    |> Enum.take(@identity_limit)
+  end
+
+  defp provenance_entries(_entries) do
+    []
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provenance(value) when value in @provenance_values do
+    value
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provenance("legacy_eager") do
+    :legacy_eager
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provenance("dependency_ordered") do
+    :dependency_ordered
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_provenance(_value) do
+    nil
+  end
+
+  defp identities(%MapSet{} = values) do
+    values
+    |> MapSet.to_list()
+    |> identities()
+  end
+
+  defp identities(values) when is_list(values) do
+    values
+    |> Enum.filter(&is_binary/1)
+    |> Enum.uniq()
+    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1)
+    |> Enum.take(@identity_limit)
+  end
+
+  defp identities(_values) do
+    []
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_history(history) when is_map(history) do
+    history
+    |> Enum.map(fn {mutation_id, entry} ->
+      if is_map(entry), do: Map.put_new(entry, :mutation_id, mutation_id), else: entry
+    end)
+    |> mutation_history()
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_history(history) when is_list(history) do
+    history
+    |> Enum.flat_map(&mutation_summary/1)
+    |> Enum.sort_by(&{Map.get(&1, :result_version, -1), Map.get(&1, :mutation_id, "")})
+    |> Enum.take(-@history_limit)
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_history(_history) do
+    []
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_summary(entry) when is_map(entry) do
+    mutation_id = MapField.get(entry, :mutation_id)
+
+    if is_binary(mutation_id) do
+      [
+        compact(%{
+          mutation_id: mutation_id,
+          origin: binary_value(entry, :origin),
+          expected_version: version_value(entry, :expected_version),
+          result_version: version_value(entry, :result_version),
+          occurred_at: datetime_value(entry, :occurred_at),
+          added_node_ids: mutation_ids(entry, :added_node_ids, :additions, :node),
+          added_edge_ids: mutation_ids(entry, :added_edge_ids, :additions, :edge),
+          removed_node_ids: mutation_ids(entry, :removed_node_ids, :removals, :node),
+          removed_edge_ids: mutation_ids(entry, :removed_edge_ids, :removals, :edge)
+        })
+      ]
+    else
+      []
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_summary(_entry) do
+    []
+  end
+
+  defp mutation_ids(entry, summary_field, operations_field, kind) do
+    case MapField.get(entry, summary_field) do
+      values when is_list(values) -> identities(values)
+      _missing -> operation_ids(entry, operations_field, kind)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp operation_ids(entry, field, kind) do
+    case MapField.get(entry, field) do
+      operations when is_list(operations) ->
+        operations
+        |> Enum.filter(&(normalize_kind(MapField.get(&1, :kind)) == kind))
+        |> Enum.map(&MapField.get(&1, :id))
+        |> identities()
+
+      _invalid ->
+        nil
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_kind(kind) when kind in [:node, :edge] do
+    kind
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_kind("node") do
+    :node
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_kind("edge") do
+    :edge
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_kind(_kind) do
+    nil
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status(status) when status in @reconciliation_statuses do
+    status
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status("not_required") do
+    :not_required
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status("required") do
+    :required
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status("completed") do
+    :completed
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status("unknown") do
+    :unknown
+  end
+
+  defp normalize_reconciliation_status(_status) do
+    :unknown
+  end
+
+  defp valid_version(value) when is_integer(value) and value >= 0 do
+    value
+  end
+
+  defp valid_version(_value) do
+    0
+  end
+
+  defp version_value(entry, field) do
+    case MapField.get(entry, field) do
+      value when is_integer(value) and value >= 0 -> value
+      _invalid -> nil
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp binary_value(entry, field) do
+    case MapField.get(entry, field) do
+      value when is_binary(value) -> value
+      _invalid -> nil
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp datetime_value(entry, field) do
+    case MapField.get(entry, field) do
+      %DateTime{} = value -> value
+      _invalid -> nil
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp compact(map) do
+    Map.reject(map, fn {_key, value} -> is_nil(value) end)
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
[swift2objc] Generate implicit ctor for structs
This swift struct has an implicit constructor that takes a `name` and `age`:

```swift
public struct Person {
    public var name: String
    public var age: Int
}
```

The implicit constructor is only generated if there are no explicit constructors. The implicit constructor doesn't show up in the symbolgraph, so we'll need to manually create an implicit constructor for the wrapper class.

### Additional contract requirements

When generating the wrapper class for a Swift struct that declares at least
one stored instance property and no explicit initializers, the generated
wrapper must offer an initializer that corresponds to the struct's implicit
memberwise initializer. This initializer never appears in the symbolgraph, so
it must be synthesized for the wrapper.

- Only stored instance properties of the struct participate in the synthesized
  initializer's parameter list. Static properties and computed properties
  (properties declared with only a getter and no stored value) are excluded.
  Each participating property contributes one parameter named after that
  property.
- When the source provides enough information to recover the properties'
  declaration order, the parameters must appear in that declaration order,
  regardless of the order in which the properties happen to be listed in the
  parsed input.
- When the declaration order cannot be recovered from the input, the
  synthesized initializer must still include exactly one parameter for every
  stored instance property, in some deterministic order.
- If the struct declares any explicit initializer, no implicit memberwise
  initializer is synthesized; only the explicitly declared initializers are
  reflected in the wrapper.

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,458 @@
+// Copyright (c) 2026, the Dart project authors. Please see the AUTHORS file
+// for details. All rights reserved. Use of this source code is governed by a
+// BSD-style license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+// Tests that a Swift struct with no explicit initializers receives a
+// synthesized wrapper initializer in its generated wrapper class, matching
+// the implicit memberwise initializer that Swift generates for such structs
+// (the implicit initializer never appears in the symbolgraph, so the wrapper
+// must supply it). The tests are driven by symbolgraph JSON fixtures instead
+// of invoking the Swift compiler, so they can run in any environment.
+
+import 'dart:convert';
+
+import 'package:logging/logging.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/ast/declarations/compounds/class_declaration.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/config.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/context.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/parser/_core/json.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/parser/parser.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/parser/parsers/parse_relations_map.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/parser/parsers/parse_symbols_map.dart';
+import 'package:swift2objc/src/transformer/transform.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Symbolgraph fixture builders.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/// A single token in a symbolgraph fragment list. `preciseId` is only
+/// present on type references.
+typedef Token = ({String kind, String spelling, String? preciseId});
+
+Token token(String kind, String spelling, [String? preciseId]) =>
+    (kind: kind, spelling: spelling, preciseId: preciseId);
+
+Map<String, dynamic> encodeToken(Token t) => {
+  'kind': t.kind,
+  'spelling': t.spelling,
+  if (t.preciseId != null) 'preciseIdentifier': t.preciseId,
+};
+
+List<Map<String, dynamic>> encodeTokens(List<Token> tokens) =>
+    tokens.map(encodeToken).toList();
+
+Map<String, dynamic> location(int line) => {
+  'uri': 'file:///tmp/input.swift',
+  'position': {'line': line, 'character': 0},
+};
+
+Map<String, dynamic> structSymbol(String id, String name) => {
+  'kind': {'identifier': 'swift.struct', 'displayName': 'Structure'},
+  'identifier': {'precise': id, 'interfaceLanguage': 'swift'},
+  'pathComponents': [name],
+  'names': {
+    'title': name,
+    'subHeading': encodeTokens([
+      token('keyword', 'struct'),
+      token('text', ' '),
+      token('identifier', name),
+    ]),
+  },
+  'declarationFragments': encodeTokens([
+    token('keyword', 'struct'),
+    token('text', ' '),
+    token('identifier', name),
+  ]),
+};
+
+/// A `var` property of the struct. Set [isStatic] for a static property and
+/// [isComputed] for a computed property (getter only), or
+/// [isComputedWithSetter] for a computed get/set property.
+Map<String, dynamic> propertySymbol(
+  String id,
+  String structName,
+  String name, {
+  required Token typeToken,
+  bool isStatic = false,
+  bool isComputed = false,
+  bool isComputedWithSetter = false,
+  int? line,
+}) => {
+  'kind': {
+    'identifier': isStatic ? 'swift.type.property' : 'swift.property',
+    'displayName': isStatic ? 'Type Property' : 'Instance Property',
+  },
+  'identifier': {'precise': id, 'interfaceLanguage': 'swift'},
+  'pathComponents': [structName, name],
+  'names': {
+    'title': name,
+    'subHeading': encodeTokens([
+      token('keyword', 'var'),
+      token('text', ' '),
+      token('identifier', name),
+      token('text', ': '),
+      typeToken,
+    ]),
+  },
+  'declarationFragments': encodeTokens([
+    if (isStatic) ...[token('keyword', 'static'), token('text', ' ')],
+    token('keyword', 'var'),
+    token('text', ' '),
+    token('identifier', name),
+    token('text', ': '),
+    typeToken,
+    if (isComputed) token('text', ' { get }'),
+    if (isComputedWithSetter) ...[
+      token('text', ' { '),
+      token('keyword', 'get'),
+      token('text', ' '),
+      token('keyword', 'set'),
+      token('text', ' }'),
+    ],
+  ]),
+  if (line != null) 'location': location(line),
+};
+
+/// An explicit `init` of the struct taking the given parameter token
+/// lists.
+Map<String, dynamic> initializerSymbol(
+  String id,
+  String structName,
+  List<Token> params,
+) => {
+  'kind': {'identifier': 'swift.init', 'displayName': 'Initializer'},
+  'identifier': {'precise': id, 'interfaceLanguage': 'swift'},
+  'pathComponents': [structName, 'init(...)'],
+  'names': {'title': 'init(...)'},
+  'declarationFragments': encodeTokens([
+    token('keyword', 'init'),
+    token('text', '('),
+    for (var i = 0; i < params.length; i++) ...[
+      if (i > 0) token('text', ', '),
+      params[i],
+    ],
+    token('text', ')'),
+  ]),
+};
+
+/// A parameter fragment list for an initializer, with a Swift-like id.
+List<Token> param(String name, String typeName, String typeId) => [
+  token('externalParam', name),
+  token('text', ': '),
+  token('typeIdentifier', typeName, typeId),
+];
+
+Map<String, dynamic> memberOf(String memberId, String structId) => {
+  'kind': 'memberOf',
+  'source': memberId,
+  'target': structId,
+};
+
+void main() {
+  final context = Context(Logger.detached('implicitInitializerTest'));
+
+  /// Parses a symbolgraph JSON document containing a single struct and
+  /// returns the transformed wrapper class for it.
+  ClassDeclaration transformStruct({
+    required String module,
+    required String structName,
+    required String structId,
+    required List<Map<String, dynamic>> memberSymbols,
+    required List<String> memberIds,
+    InputConfig? inputConfig,
+  }) {
+    final input =
+        inputConfig ??
+        JsonFileInputConfig(jsonFile: Uri.file('/tmp/input.json'));
+    final document = Json(
+      jsonDecode(
+        jsonEncode({
+          'metadata': {
+            'formatVersion': {'major': 1, 'minor': 0, 'patch': 0},
+            'generator': 'test',
+          },
+          'module': {'name': module},
+          'symbols': [structSymbol(structId, structName), ...memberSymbols],
+          'relationships': [
+            for (final memberId in memberIds) memberOf(memberId, structId),
+          ],
+        }),
+      ),
+    );
+    final symbolgraph = ParsedSymbolgraph(
+      symbols: {
+        ...ParsedSymbolgraph.builtInSymbolsMap(),
+        ...parseSymbolsMap(input, document),
+      },
+      relations: parseRelationsMap(input, document),
+    );
+
+    final declarations = parseDeclarations(context, symbolgraph);
+    expect(
+      declarations.length,
+      equals(1),
+      reason: 'fixture should parse to exactly the struct declaration',
+    );
+
+    final transformed = transform(context, declarations, filter: (_) => true);
+    return transformed.whereType<ClassDeclaration>().firstWhere(
+      (decl) => decl.name == '${structName}Wrapper',
+      orElse: () => fail('no wrapper class was generated for $structName'),
+    );
+  }
+
+  /// The full names of [wrapper]'s initializers, e.g. `init:name:age`.
+  List<String> initializerFullNames(ClassDeclaration wrapper) => [
+    for (final init in wrapper.initializers) init.fullName,
+  ];
+
+  /// Parameter names in each initializer, retaining duplicates and order.
+  List<List<String>> initializerParameterNames(ClassDeclaration wrapper) => [
+    for (final init in wrapper.initializers)
+      [for (final parameter in init.params) parameter.name],
+  ];
+
+  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Shared fixture data.
+  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+  const module = 'TestModule';
+  const structName = 'Person';
+  const structId = 's:$module${structName.length}PersonV';
+  const nameId = '${structId}4nameSSvp';
+  const ageId = '${structId}3ageSivp';
+
+  final stringRef = token('typeIdentifier', 'String', 's:SS');
+  final intRef = token('typeIdentifier', 'Int', 's:Si');
+
+  Map<String, dynamic> nameProperty({int? line}) => propertySymbol(
+    nameId,
+    structName,
+    'name',
+    typeToken: stringRef,
+    line: line,
+  );
+
+  Map<String, dynamic> ageProperty({int? line}) =>
+      propertySymbol(ageId, structName, 'age', typeToken: intRef, line: line);
+
+  /// Parses the `Person` struct from the problem statement example and
+  /// returns its transformed wrapper.
+  ClassDeclaration transformedPerson({
+    bool nameBeforeAge = true,
+    int? nameLine,
+    int? ageLine,
+  }) {
+    // Both the symbol list and the membership relations follow the same
+    // order, controlled by [nameBeforeAge]. The parser visits members in
+    // membership-relation order, so flipping both orders means a transform
+    // that preserves parsed-input order yields `init:age:name`, while only
+    // recovering the declaration order from the source locations yields
+    // `init:name:age`.
+    final memberIds = nameBeforeAge ? [nameId, ageId] : [ageId, nameId];
+    final members = nameBeforeAge
+        ? [nameProperty(line: nameLine), ageProperty(line: ageLine)]
+        : [ageProperty(line: ageLine), nameProperty(line: nameLine)];
+    return transformStruct(
+      module: module,
+      structName: structName,
+      structId: structId,
+      memberSymbols: members,
+      memberIds: memberIds,
+    );
+  }
+
+  group('Implicit Initializer Generation', () {
+    test('generates implicit init for struct with stored properties', () {
+      // The symbolgraph lists `name` before `age`, matching the declaration
+      // order established by their source locations. The synthesized
+      // wrapper initializer must take `name` first and `age` second.
+      final wrapper = transformedPerson(nameLine: 2, ageLine: 3);
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:name:age']));
+    });
+
+    test('orders params in declaration order regardless of symbol order', () {
+      // The declaration order of the properties is recoverable from the
+      // source locations, even though the symbolgraph lists `age` before
+      // `name` (in both the symbol list and the membership relations, so
+      // the parsed-input order is `age`, `name`). The parameters must
+      // follow declaration order, not the parsed-input order.
+      final wrapper = transformedPerson(
+        nameBeforeAge: false,
+        nameLine: 2,
+        ageLine: 3,
+      );
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:name:age']));
+    });
+
+    test(
+      'includes all stored properties when declaration order is unknown',
+      () {
+        // The fixture provides no source locations, so declaration order cannot
+        // be recovered. The synthesized wrapper initializer must still accept
+        // every stored property, in some deterministic order; only the set of
+        // parameters is observable here.
+        final wrapper = transformedPerson(nameLine: null, ageLine: null);
+        final params = initializerParameterNames(wrapper);
+        expect(
+          wrapper.initializers,
+          isNot(isEmpty),
+          reason: 'a synthesized wrapper initializer must exist',
+        );
+        expect(params, hasLength(1));
+        expect(params.single, hasLength(2));
+        expect(params.single.toSet(), equals({'name', 'age'}));
+        final repeated = transformedPerson(nameLine: null, ageLine: null);
+        expect(
+          initializerParameterNames(repeated),
+          equals(initializerParameterNames(wrapper)),
+        );
+      },
+    );
+
+    test('does not generate implicit init when explicit init exists', () {
+      final initId = '${structId}ACSS_tcfc';
+      final wrapper = transformStruct(
+        module: module,
+        structName: structName,
+        structId: structId,
+        memberSymbols: [
+          nameProperty(line: 2),
+          initializerSymbol(initId, structName, [
+            ...param('label', 'String', 's:SS'),
+          ]),
+        ],
+        memberIds: [nameId, initId],
+      );
+      // Only the explicit `init(name:)` is wrapped; no synthesized
+      // memberwise initializer is added alongside it.
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:name']));
+      expect(
+        initializerParameterNames(wrapper),
+        equals([
+          ['name'],
+        ]),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('excludes static properties from implicit init', () {
+      const defaultNameId = '${structId}11defaultNameSSvpZ';
+      final wrapper = transformStruct(
+        module: module,
+        structName: structName,
+        structId: structId,
+        memberSymbols: [
+          nameProperty(line: 2),
+          propertySymbol(
+            defaultNameId,
+            structName,
+            'defaultName',
+            typeToken: stringRef,
+            isStatic: true,
+            line: 3,
+          ),
+        ],
+        memberIds: [nameId, defaultNameId],
+      );
+      // Static properties are not settable through an instance, so the
+      // synthesized wrapper initializer only takes `name`.
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:name']));
+      expect(
+        initializerParameterNames(wrapper),
+        equals([
+          ['name'],
+        ]),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('excludes computed properties from implicit init', () {
+      const fullNameId = '${structId}8fullNameSSvp';
+      final wrapper = transformStruct(
+        module: module,
+        structName: structName,
+        structId: structId,
+        memberSymbols: [
+          propertySymbol(
+            '${structId}9firstNameSSvp',
+            structName,
+            'firstName',
+            typeToken: stringRef,
+            line: 2,
+          ),
+          propertySymbol(
+            fullNameId,
+            structName,
+            'fullName',
+            typeToken: stringRef,
+            isComputed: true,
+            line: 3,
+          ),
+        ],
+        memberIds: ['${structId}9firstNameSSvp', fullNameId],
+      );
+      // A computed property is not a stored property and is never a
+      // parameter of the implicit memberwise initializer.
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:firstName']));
+      expect(
+        initializerParameterNames(wrapper),
+        equals([
+          ['firstName'],
+        ]),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('excludes computed get/set properties from implicit init', () {
+      const storedId = '${structId}6storedSSvp';
+      const computedId = '${structId}8computedSSvp';
+      final wrapper = transformStruct(
+        module: module,
+        structName: structName,
+        structId: structId,
+        memberSymbols: [
+          propertySymbol(
+            storedId,
+            structName,
+            'stored',
+            typeToken: stringRef,
+            line: 2,
+          ),
+          propertySymbol(
+            computedId,
+            structName,
+            'computed',
+            typeToken: stringRef,
+            isComputedWithSetter: true,
+            line: 3,
+          ),
+        ],
+        memberIds: [storedId, computedId],
+      );
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:stored']));
+      expect(
+        initializerParameterNames(wrapper),
+        equals([
+          ['stored'],
+        ]),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('synthesizes initializer for module-configured symbolgraph input', () {
+      final wrapper = transformStruct(
+        module: module,
+        structName: structName,
+        structId: structId,
+        memberSymbols: [nameProperty(line: 2)],
+        memberIds: [nameId],
+        inputConfig: const ModuleInputConfig(module: module),
+      );
+      expect(initializerFullNames(wrapper), equals(['init:name']));
+      expect(
+        initializerParameterNames(wrapper),
+        equals([
+          ['name'],
+        ]),
+      );
+    });
+  });
+}

[record_use] Implementation: JSON: use `snake_case` for tagged unions
  `pkgs/record_use/doc/schema/record_use.schema.json`

  In this file, there is an inconsistency in the Constant definition. The type property uses a mix of PascalCase and snake_case for its enum values.

   * `Call.type`: snake_case ("tearoff", "with_arguments")
   * `Constant.type`: Mixed case.
       * PascalCase: "Instance", "Null", "String"
       * snake_case: "bool", "int", "list", "map"


  `pkgs/hooks/doc/schema/shared/shared_definitions.schema.json`

  This file is consistent. All tagged unions use snake_case.

   * `Asset.type`: snake_case ("hooks/metadata")
   * `FailureType`: snake_case ("build", "infra", "uncategorized")
   * `OutputStatus`: snake_case ("failure", "success")


We should clean this up.

(Split from https://github.com/dart-lang/native/issues/1093)

### Additional contract requirements

In `pkgs/record_use`, constant entries exchanged on the JSON wire format
described by `doc/schema/record_use.schema.json` use `snake_case` type tags
only. This is an end-to-end requirement covering both production of the JSON
(serialization of recorded usages and of individual constants through the
public API) and consumption of it (deserialization of the same structures
through the public API and validation of documents against the JSON schema):

- The `type` tag of every constant variant is one of `bool`, `instance`,
  `int`, `list`, `map`, `null`, and `string`. The tags `instance`, `null`,
  and `string` are the lower-case forms that replace the previously used
  spellings `Instance`, `Null`, and `String`. Every public serialization
  path (whole recordings as well as individual constants) emits the
  `snake_case` tags, and the corresponding deserialization paths accept
  them.
- The value shape and optionality enforced by the schema for each variant
  stays as defined per tag: a `value` is required and typed for `bool`
  (boolean), `int` (integer), `list` (array), `map` (object), and `string`
  (string); `value` is optional for `instance` and is omitted when the
  instance has no fields; and `value` must be absent for `null`. A constant
  entry carrying one of the seven tags with a missing or wrongly shaped
  `value` is invalid according to the schema.
- The constant JSON decoding API does not interpret any of the retired
  spellings `Instance`, `Null`, or `String` as a known constant variant:
  decoding a constant entry whose `type` tag is one of those retired
  spellings fails. No particular error class or message content is
  required.
- The tagged-union `type` property in the schema tolerates tag spellings
  outside the seven known ones (forward compatibility with future
  variants), so schema validation is not required to reject a constant
  entry that carries a retired or otherwise unknown spelling.
- No checked-in JSON sample or test document continues to use the retired
  spellings; documents exercising this wire format use only the
  `snake_case` tags, and tests that deserialize or validate them continue
  to succeed against the updated documents. No particular checked-in
  document is required (or relied upon) to contain any specific set of
  constant variants; schema and API behavior is specified independently of
  any document's contents.

described by `doc/schema/record_use.schema.json` use `snake_case` type tags
only. This is an end-to-end requirement covering both production of the JSON
(serialization of recorded usages and of individual constants through the
public API) and consumption of it (deserialization of the same structures
through the public API and validation of documents against the JSON schema):

- The `type` tag of every constant variant is one of `bool`, `instance`,
  `int`, `list`, `map`, `null`, and `string`. The tags `instance`, `null`,
  and `string` are the lower-case forms that replace the previously used
  spellings `Instance`, `Null`, and `String`. Every public serialization
  path (whole recordings as well as individual constants) emits the
  `snake_case` tags, and the corresponding deserialization paths accept
  them.
- The value shape and optionality enforced by the schema for each variant
  stays as defined per tag: a `value` is required and typed for `bool`
  (boolean), `int` (integer), `list` (array), `map` (object), and `string`
  (string); `value` is optional for `instance` and is omitted when the
  instance has no fields; and `value` must be absent for `null`. A constant
  entry carrying one of the seven tags with a missing or wrongly shaped
  `value` is invalid according to the schema.
- The constant JSON decoding API does not interpret any of the retired
  spellings `Instance`, `Null`, or `String` as a known constant variant:
  decoding a constant entry whose `type` tag is one of those retired
  spellings fails. No particular error class or message content is
  required.
- The tagged-union `type` property in the schema tolerates tag spellings
  outside the seven known ones (forward compatibility with future
  variants), so schema validation is not required to reject a constant
  entry that carries a retired or otherwise unknown spelling.
- No checked-in JSON sample or test document continues to use the retired
  spellings; documents exercising this wire format use only the
  `snake_case` tags, and tests that deserialize or validate them continue
  to succeed against the updated documents. No particular checked-in
  document is required (or relied upon) to contain any specific set of
  constant variants; schema and API behavior is specified independently of
  any document's contents.

problem_statement:
tbl() -> collect() workflow does not work in networks where `blob.core.windows.net` is blocked
## Issue

In `dbSendQuery` the disposition parameter is hardcoded and set to `EXTERNAL_LINKS` (for `dbGetQuery` on the other hand we can set the disposition ourselves). That is, in an environment where `blob.core.windows.net` is blocked by teh firewall, we cannot use `dbSendQuery`.

The problem becomes apparent if we want to use `tbl`, because under the hood it will eventually call `dbSendQuery`.

## Call Chain: `tbl()` Ã¢ÂÂ `dbSendQuery()`
 
 ```
 tbl(con, "table")
   Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ dbplyr::tbl.DBIConnection()
        Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ dbplyr::tbl_sql()
             Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ builds a lazy "tbl_lazy" object
                  Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ NO SQL executed yet Ã¢ÂÂ only triggered by collect()!
 
 collect(lazy_tbl)
   Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ dbplyr::collect.tbl_sql()
        Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ dbplyr::db_collect()
             Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ DBI::dbFetch()
                  Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ DBI::dbSendQuery()
                       Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ brickster:::dbSendQuery,DatabricksConnection
                            Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂ db_sql_exec_query(disposition = "EXTERNAL_LINKS") Ã¢ÂÂ Ã°ÂÂÂ¥
 ```
 
 | Step | Package | What happens |
 |---|---|---|
 | `tbl()` | dbplyr | Builds a query plan only, no SQL sent |
 | `collect()` | dbplyr | Triggers actual execution |
 | `dbFetch()` | DBI | Fetches the results |
 | `dbSendQuery()` | DBI Ã¢ÂÂ brickster | Sends SQL to Databricks Ã¢ÂÂ this is where the hardcoded `disposition = "EXTERNAL_LINKS"` is applied, with no way to override it |
 
 `tbl()` itself does not interact with the database at all. The critical point is `collect()`, which triggers the full dbplyr Ã¢ÂÂ DBI Ã¢ÂÂ brickster chain Ã¢ÂÂ and there is no way to pass `disposition = "INLINE"`  through this path.

## Desired Behaviour

Ideally there would be an option, with which we could override the hard coded `disposition` to allow for using `tbl` also on systems with no connection to `blob.core.windows.net`.

[HIDDEN]

## Error Message

```r
library(DBI)
library(brickster)
library(dbplyr)
library(dplyr)

warehouse_id <- 12345
con <- dbConnect(
  DatabricksSQL(),
  warehouse_id = warehouse_id
)

con %>% 
  tbl(I("my_catalog.my_schema.my_table")) %>% 
  head(5L)

## Error in `collect()`:
## ! Failed to collect lazy table.
## Caused by error in `httr2::req_perform()`:
## ! Failed to perform HTTP request.
## Caused by error in `curl::curl_fetch_memory()`:
## ! SSL connect error [dbstoragejcmu2vp2x6lnw.blob.core.windows.net]:
## Recv failure: Connection was reset
```

### Additional contract requirements

## Query result disposition

`dbConnect()` accepts a `disposition` option for a Databricks SQL connection.
The supported values are `"EXTERNAL_LINKS"` and `"INLINE"`; the default is
`"EXTERNAL_LINKS"`. Invalid disposition values are rejected with an error when
creating the connection.

The selected value is retained by the connection and is used for query results
when no per-query disposition is supplied. In particular, `dbSendQuery()` and
the default behavior of `dbGetQuery()` use the connection setting, so dbplyr
`tbl()`/`collect()` workflows use it as well. A per-query disposition supplied
to `dbGetQuery()` continues to take precedence over the connection default.

`EXTERNAL_LINKS` remains the backwards-compatible default. Use `"INLINE"` for
queries whose results must be returned without direct cloud-storage result
downloads; fetching results from a statement executed with `"INLINE"`
disposition never downloads result data from external cloud-storage URLs.

set +e
(
R CMD INSTALL . --no-multiarch >/tmp/rebench-install.log 2>&1 && Rscript - <<'RS_EOF'
suppressMessages({
  library(testthat)
  library(brickster)
})
target_descs <- c(
  "dbConnect validates tuning inputs and persists connection settings",
  "query execution DBI methods dispatch expected options",
  "dbFetch processes inline results from dbSendQuery",
  "db_collect uses connection query disposition"
)
files <- c(
  "tests/testthat/test-databricks-dbi-offline-helpers.R",
  "tests/testthat/test-databricks-dbplyr-offline-helpers.R"
)
res <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(files, function(f) as.data.frame(testthat::test_file(f, reporter = "silent")))
)
saveRDS(res, "/tmp/rebench-test-results.rds")
feat <- res[res$test %in% target_descs, , drop = FALSE]
cat("\n==== TARGET TESTS (disposition feature) ====\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(feat))) {
  ok <- feat$failed[i] == 0 && !isTRUE(feat$error[i])
  cat(sprintf("[%s] %s | %s (passed=%d failed=%d error=%s)\n", if (ok) "PASS" else "FAIL", basename(feat$file[i]), feat$test[i], feat$passed[i], feat$failed[i], isTRUE(feat$error[i])))
}
feat_fail <- sum(feat$failed) + sum(feat$error)
cat(sprintf("TARGET: %d tests | passed=%d failed=%d errors=%d\n", nrow(feat), sum(feat$passed), sum(feat$failed), sum(feat$error)))
cat(sprintf("ALL-FILES: %d tests | passed=%d failed=%d errors=%d skipped=%d\n", nrow(res), sum(res$passed), sum(res$failed), sum(res$error), sum(res$skipped)))
quit(status = if (feat_fail == 0 && nrow(feat) == length(target_descs)) 0 else 1)
RS_EOF
)
swan_rebench_status=$?
if [ "$swan_rebench_status" -eq 0 ]; then

fi
exit "$swan_rebench_status"

problem_statement:
Allow output to standard stream
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, only the console ouput can be written to standard stream. There should be an option to ouput to standard stream for all formats.

### Additional contract requirements

# Report output to the CLI standard output

The report destination option accepts the special value `-`, which selects the
CLI standard output stream instead of a file:

- `-o -` or `--output -` writes the generated report to the CLI standard
  output as seen by a command-line user, rather than to any report file.
- This applies when the requested output is a single report in one of the
  supported file formats: HTML, Markdown, or JSON. The full generated report
  content appears on the standard output.
- When `-` is used as the report destination, no report file is created; in
  particular, no file literally named `-` is created.
- Using a file path as the report destination behaves as before: the report is
  written to that file for a single selected output type.

+@file:Suppress("UnusedImport")
+
+package com.deezer.caupain.cli.internal
+
+import com.deezer.caupain.internal.systemSink
+import com.github.ajalt.clikt.completion.CompletionCandidates
+import com.github.ajalt.clikt.core.Context
+import com.github.ajalt.clikt.parameters.options.NullableOption
+import com.github.ajalt.clikt.parameters.options.RawOption
+import com.github.ajalt.clikt.parameters.options.convert
+import okio.Buffer
+import okio.FileSystem
+import okio.IOException
+import okio.Path
+import okio.SYSTEM
+import okio.Sink
+import okio.Timeout
+
+fun RawOption.sink(
+    createIfNotExist: Boolean = true,
+    truncateExisting: Boolean = false,
+    createDirectories: Boolean = createIfNotExist,
+    fileSystem: FileSystem = FileSystem.SYSTEM,
+): NullableOption<OutputSink, OutputSink> {
+    return convert({ localization.fileMetavar() }, CompletionCandidates.Path) { s ->
+        convertToSink(
+            s = s,
+            createIfNotExists = createIfNotExist,
+            createDirectories = createDirectories,
+            truncateExisting = truncateExisting,
+            fileSystem = fileSystem,
+            context = context
+        ) { fail(it) }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun convertToSink(
+    s: String,
+    createIfNotExists: Boolean,
+    truncateExisting: Boolean,
+    createDirectories: Boolean,
+    fileSystem: FileSystem,
+    context: Context,
+    fail: (String) -> Unit,
+): OutputSink {
+    return if (s == "-") {
+        OutputSink.System
+    } else {
+        val path = convertToPath(
+            stringPath = s,
+            mustExist = !createIfNotExists,
+            canBeFile = true,
+            canBeFolder = false,
+            canBeSymlink = true,
+            fileSystem = fileSystem,
+            context = context,
+            fail = fail,
+        )
+        if (createDirectories) {
+            path.parent?.let(fileSystem::createDirectories)
+        }
+        if (!createIfNotExists && !fileSystem.exists(path)) {
+            throw IOException("File does not exist: $path")
+        }
+        OutputSink.File(
+            delegate = if (truncateExisting) {
+                fileSystem.sink(path)
+            } else {
+                fileSystem.appendingSink(path)
+            },
+            path = path,
+        )
+    }
+}
+
+sealed interface OutputSink : Sink {
+
+    data object System : OutputSink {
+        private val delegate by lazy { systemSink() }
+
+        override fun write(source: Buffer, byteCount: Long) {
+            delegate.write(source, byteCount)
+        }
+
+        override fun flush() {
+            delegate.flush()
+        }
+
+        override fun timeout(): Timeout = delegate.timeout()
+
+        override fun close() {
+            flush()
+        }
+    }
+
+    class File(delegate: Sink, val path: Path) : OutputSink, Sink by delegate {
+        override fun toString(): String {
+            return "File(path=$path)"
+        }
+    }
+}

+@file:OptIn(ExperimentalForeignApi::class)
+
+package com.deezer.caupain.internal
+
+import kotlinx.cinterop.ByteVarOf
+import kotlinx.cinterop.CPointer
+import kotlinx.cinterop.ExperimentalForeignApi
+import kotlinx.cinterop.addressOf
+import kotlinx.cinterop.convert
+import kotlinx.cinterop.get
+import kotlinx.cinterop.usePinned
+import okio.Buffer
+import okio.Buffer.UnsafeCursor
+import okio.FileNotFoundException
+import okio.IOException
+import okio.Sink
+import okio.Timeout
+import platform.posix.ENOENT
+import platform.posix.errno
+import platform.posix.fflush
+import platform.posix.fwrite
+import platform.posix.stdout
+import platform.posix.strerror
+
+private object SystemOutputSink : Sink {
+
+    private val unsafeCursor = UnsafeCursor()
+
+    override fun write(source: Buffer, byteCount: Long) {
+        require(byteCount >= 0L) { "byteCount < 0: $byteCount" }
+        require(source.size >= byteCount) { "source.size=${source.size} < byteCount=$byteCount" }
+
+        var byteCount = byteCount
+        while (byteCount > 0) {
+            // Get the first segment, which we will read a contiguous range of bytes from.
+            val cursor = source.readUnsafe(unsafeCursor)
+            val segmentReadableByteCount = cursor.next()
+            val attemptCount = minOf(byteCount, segmentReadableByteCount.toLong()).toInt()
+
+            // Copy bytes from that segment into the file.
+            val bytesWritten = cursor.data!!.usePinned { pinned ->
+                fwrite(
+                    pinned.addressOf(cursor.start),
+                    1u,
+                    attemptCount.toUInt().convert(),
+                    stdout
+                ).toLong()
+            }
+
+            // Consume the bytes from the segment.
+            cursor.close()
+            source.skip(bytesWritten)
+            byteCount -= bytesWritten
+
+            // If the write was shorter than expected, some I/O failed.
+            if (bytesWritten < attemptCount) {
+                throw errnoToIOException(errno)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    override fun flush() {
+        if (fflush(stdout) != 0) throw errnoToIOException(errno)
+    }
+
+    override fun timeout(): Timeout = Timeout.NONE
+
+    override fun close() {
+        flush()
+    }
+
+    private fun errnoToIOException(errno: Int): IOException {
+        val message = strerror(errno)
+        val messageString = if (message != null) {
+            Buffer().writeNullTerminated(message).readUtf8()
+        } else {
+            "errno: $errno"
+        }
+        return if (errno == ENOENT) {
+            FileNotFoundException(messageString)
+        } else {
+            IOException(messageString)
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun Buffer.writeNullTerminated(bytes: CPointer<ByteVarOf<Byte>>): Buffer = apply {
+    var pos = 0
+    while (true) {
+        val byte = bytes[pos++].toInt()
+        if (byte == 0) {
+            break
+        } else {
+            writeByte(byte)
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/**
+ * A platform-specific sink writing to the system standard output. This uses [stdout].
+ */
+public actual fun systemSink(): Sink = SystemOutputSink

problem_statement:
IAsyncEnumerable
I noticed `FSharp.Control.TaskSeq` isn't supported with computation expressions like `taskResult`, any plans?

### Additional contract requirements

The `taskResult`, `taskOption`, `taskValidation`, and `taskValueOption` computation expressions, together with their `backgroundTaskResult`, `backgroundTaskOption`, `backgroundTaskValidation`, and `backgroundTaskValueOption` counterparts, support `for ... in` over `IAsyncEnumerable<'T>` sources.

Each iteration awaits asynchronous source progression, including sources whose `MoveNextAsync` completes asynchronously, and runs the loop body in source order. When the source completes normally, the computation continues with the code following the loop.

If any loop iteration fails (short-circuits), iteration stops immediately for every supported builder: the source enumerator is not advanced past the element whose iteration failed, later source elements and subsequent loop effects are not evaluated, and the failure is returned according to the builder's existing result, option, value-option, or validation semantics.

The source's enumerator is asynchronously disposed after iteration ends, whether it ends by normal completion or by an early loop-body failure.

problem_statement:
Terms in languages without word delimiters (CJK, Thai, etc.) are not detected
### Problem

Contextive currently relies on delimiter-based tokenisation (spaces, parentheses, etc.) and regex-based splitting (camelCase, snake_case) to identify candidate terms. This works well for languages that use spaces between words, but languages that don't use spaces to delimit words — such as Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai, Lao, and Khmer — cannot match glossary terms at all.

### Reproduction

1. Create a glossary file:

```yaml
contexts:
  - terms:
    - name: 注文
      definition: An order placed by a customer
```

2. Open a file containing the text `注文が届く`
3. Hover over `注文` — no hover result is shown

### Why this happens

The Tokeniser extracts the entire `注文が届く` as a single token (no delimiters within it). The CandidateTerms regex then attempts to split it by camelCase/snake_case patterns, but since CJK characters are not in the `\p{Lu}` / `\p{Ll}` ranges used by the regex, no splitting occurs. The full string `注文が届く` is looked up as-is in the index, which only contains `注文`, so no match is found.

### Affected languages

Any language that does not use spaces between words:

| Language | Script | Example |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Japanese | Kanji / Kana | 注文が届く |
| Chinese | Hanzi | 购物车管理 |
| Korean | Hangul | 주문을처리 |
| Thai | Thai script | สวัสดีครับ |
| Lao | Lao script | ພາສາລາວ |
| Khmer | Khmer script | ភាសាខ្មែរ |
| Myanmar | Myanmar script | မြန်မာဘာသာ |

### Additional contract requirements

For Japanese, Chinese, and Korean text that has no word delimiters, when a
document token contains a glossary term or alias, hovering anywhere in that
token must return hover information containing every matching glossary entry.
A matching entry may occur at any position within the token. Text containing
no glossary term or alias must continue to produce no hover result.

This is an observable requirement on the hover result. The mechanism used to
identify matching glossary entries is unspecified.

@@ -28,9 +28,18 @@ let private Default: CandidateTerms = Seq.empty<CandidateTerm>
 let private TokenSplitterRegex =
     "([A-Z\\p{Lu}]+(?![a-z\\p{Ll}])|[A-Z\\p{Lu}][a-z\\p{Ll}]+|[0-9]+|[a-z\\p{Ll}]+)"
 
+let containsCJK (token: string) =
+    token |> Seq.exists (fun c ->
+        let cp = int c
+        (cp >= 0x3000 && cp <= 0x9FFF)    // CJK main ranges (kana, CJK unified ideographs, etc.)
+        || (cp >= 0xAC00 && cp <= 0xD7AF) // Hangul syllables
+        || (cp >= 0xF900 && cp <= 0xFAFF) // CJK compatibility ideographs
+    )
+
 let candidateTermsFromToken =
     function
     | None -> Default
+    | Some(token) when containsCJK token -> seq { token }
     | Some(Regex TokenSplitterRegex tokens) -> tokens
     | Some(token) -> seq { token }
