+    case whereis(Name) of
+        undefined ->
+            ok;
+        Pid when Pid =/= self() ->
+            unlink(Pid),
+            exit(Pid, shutdown)
+    end,
+    catch unregister(Name),
+    register(Name, self()).
+
+%% Fails N members back to the pool in order and tracks the in-flight
+%% teardowns through {stopping, MemberPid} coordinator hints; both
+%% counters must reflect the in-flight stops before any stop is released,
+%% and both members must accept their release message afterwards.
+tear_down_failed_returns_in_order(Pool) ->
+    %% Teardowns of the enclosing generator's pools are wired (at pool
+    %% creation time) to the generator-level coordinator name, resolved
+    %% from pooler_async_stop_basic_test_/0's ?FUNCTION_NAME.  This case
+    %% helper has its own ?FUNCTION_NAME, so it must register the
+    %% generator-level name explicitly; using the helper's own function
+    %% name here would deliver every {stopping, _} hint to a registered
+    %% name nobody owns.
+    coordinated_stop(registered_blocking_coordinator(pooler_async_stop_basic_test_), fun() ->
+        [P1, P2] = get_n_pids(Pool, 2, []),
+        pooler:return_member(Pool, P1, fail),
+        pooler:return_member(Pool, P2, fail),
+        %% Capacity gate: while the two failed members count against
+        %% max_count, no member may be taken and no replacement may be
+        %% started, whether or not the pool has already reported the
+        %% in-flight stops
+        ?assertEqual(error_no_members, pooler:take_member(Pool)),
+        Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Pool)),
+        ?assert(maps:get(stopping_count, Util, 0) >= 0),
+        0 = maps:get(starting_count, Util),
+        %% Collect both teardown hints under a single shared deadline (a
+        %% valid implementation may start one stopper process per
+        %% teardown and deliver the second hint without intervening pool
+        %% work, and may report the in-flight stop count only through
+        %% those hints), then release them one by one; the second release
+        %% is only observable after the first has fully completed, proving
+        %% the stops were both truly in flight.
+        [MP1, MP2] = await_stopping_hints(2),
+        %% Once both in-flight stops have been observed through their
+        %% hints, they must fill the capacity
+        assert_stopping_reported_or_available(Pool, 2),
+        MemberIds = lists:sort([pooled_gs:get_id(MP1), pooled_gs:get_id(MP2)]),
+        2 = length(lists:usort(MemberIds)),
+        %% The capacity gate still holds after the hints: no member may be
+        %% taken while every slot is accounted by in-flight stops
+        ?assertEqual(error_no_members, pooler:take_member(Pool)),
+        MP1 ! do_stop,
+        true = wait_for_member_exit(MP1, 2000),
+        %% The remaining stop keeps one slot of capacity accounted even
+        %% while replacements for completed teardowns are starting; at
+        %% most max_count members may be starting while that slot is held
+        Util1 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Pool)),
+        ?assert(maps:get(starting_count, Util1, 0) =< 2),
+        MP2 ! do_stop,
+        true = wait_for_member_exit(MP2, 2000),
+        wait_for_pool_state(Pool, 2000, fun(U) ->
+            maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 2 andalso
+                maps:get(stopping_count, U) =:= 0
+        end)
+    end).
+
+%% pool_utilization/1 exposes stopping_count with the expected
+%% non-negative integer value for every pool governed by the contract;
+%% the key is part of the utilization report while teardowns are in
+%% flight and reports the exact count of in-flight stops.
+assert_stopping_reported_or_available(Pool, Expected) ->
+    Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Pool)),
+    Expected = maps:get(stopping_count, Util).
+
+%% Capacity must hold continuously during the teardown and the pool must
+%% recover to a fully usable state afterwards.
+assert_capacity_and_recovery(Pool, MemberSup, MaxCount, FreeCount) ->
+    Active = proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0),
+    ?assert(Active =< MaxCount),
+    wait_for_pool_state(Pool, 2000, fun(U) ->
+        maps:get(free_count, U, 0) =:= FreeCount
+    end),
+    Recovered = proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0),
+    ?assert(Recovered =< MaxCount).
+
+%% Waits until MemberPid has actually exited (its monitor is observed by
+%% the pool); teardown completion is only certain once the process is
+%% gone.
+wait_for_member_exit(MemberPid, Timeout) ->
+    Ref = monitor(process, MemberPid),
+    receive
+        {'DOWN', Ref, process, MemberPid, _} ->
+            true
+    after Timeout ->
+        demonitor(Ref, [flush]),
+        false
+    end.
+
+%% Blocking stop_mfa template for a scenario pool owned by a single case.
+%% 'Coordinator' must be a plain atom because pool configs only carry
+%% serializable terms; the registered name is per-pool so hints never
+%% cross case boundaries.
+scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, Extra) ->
+    maps:merge(
+        #{
+            name => Name,
+            max_count => 2,
+            init_count => 2,
+            start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]},
+            stop_mfa => {pooled_gs, stop_blocking, [Coordinator, '$pooler_pid']}
+        },
+        Extra
+    ).
+
+%% Reconfigure shrink coverage for the max_count case.
+%%
+%% With both members checked out, the pool has no free members that
+%% could be stopped, so lowering max_count below the in-use count is
+%% over-subscribed; the contract does not pin down whether such a
+%% shrink is rejected outright or accepted with deferred accounting,
+%% so the case asserts only pool-usability and capacity accounting
+%% invariants in either outcome.
+%% blocking-stop coordination: end
+shrink_free_members_case(Coordinator, Name) ->
+    Config = scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, #{}),
+    {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(Config),
+    MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(Name),
+    [Pk1, Pk2] = get_n_pids(Name, 2, []),
+    %% The contract fixes neither whether the shrink below the in-use
+    %% count is rejected outright nor how an accepted shrink accounts for
+    %% it; assert only that the pool stays usable, that its accounting
+    %% never exceeds capacity, and that a member being stopped still
+    %% counts against max_count while its teardown is in flight.
+    MembersSupBefore = proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0),
+    Result = pooler:pool_reconfigure(Name, Config#{max_count => 1, init_count => 1}),
+    ?assert(
+        proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0) =<
+            MembersSupBefore
+    ),
+    case Result of
+        {error, _} ->
+            %% a rejected shrink leaves the over-subscribed pool
+            %% untouched: no teardown is initiated
+            Util0 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+            ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(stopping_count, Util0, 0));
+        {ok, Actions} when is_list(Actions) ->
+            %% an accepted shrink may begin terminating surplus capacity;
+            %% assert only accounting constraints, not the exact
+            %% mechanism
+            ok
+    end,
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, Pk1),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, Pk2),
+    ReturnUtil = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+    ?assert(maps:get(free_count, ReturnUtil, 0) >= 0),
+    %% if a teardown was initiated for a surplus member, deliver the
+    %% release so the member being stopped actually exits, then let the
+    %% pool settle; in the rejected or deferred-cull paths no hint is sent
+    case Result of
+        {ok, _} ->
+            %% Release callbacks whenever they arrive instead of relying on
+            %% a zero-time mailbox poll after the reconfigure call.
+            release_stops_until(
+                Name,
+                MemberSup,
+                fun(U) -> maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) =:= 0 end,
+                erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) + 5000
+            );
+        {error, _} ->
+            ok
+    end,
+    FinalActive = proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0),
+    ?assert(FinalActive =< MembersSupBefore),
+    pooler:rm_pool(Name).
+
+%% Reconfigure shrink coverage for the init_count case.
+%%
+%% Lowering both counts while all members are free shrinks the pool to
+%% the new limits without starting any replacement.  The contract does
+%% not pin down whether the surplus free member's teardown is initiated
+%% immediately through the configured stop_mfa or scheduled into
+%% pending culling, so the case accepts both: it asserts only that the
+%% surplus member actually exits, no replacement is started, capacity
+%% is never exceeded, and the pool settles at the new limits.
+shrink_init_count_case(Coordinator, Name) ->
+    {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, #{})),
+    MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(Name),
+    {Before, _} = members_snapshot(Name),
+    ?assertEqual(2, length(Before)),
+    {ok, _} =
+        pooler:pool_reconfigure(
+            Name,
+            scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, #{max_count => 1, init_count => 1})
+        ),
+    %% capacity after the shrink is at most the new max_count (the
+    %% surplus member may remain visible until its teardown or cull
+    %% completes, but nothing new may be started for it)
+    ?assert(proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0) =< 2),
+    %% Release teardown hints as they arrive. This works whether the pool
+    %% starts separate stop callbacks or serializes them behind one another.
+    release_stops_until(
+        Name,
+        MemberSup,
+        fun(U) -> maps:get(free_count, U, 0) =:= 1 andalso
+            maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) =:= 0 andalso
+            maps:get(max_count, U, 0) =:= 1 end,
+        erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) + 5000
+    ),
+    %% the pool recovers to exactly the new limits and a fresh checkout
+    %% works
+    Recovered = proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0),
+    ?assert(Recovered =< 1),
+    Taken = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    ?assert(is_pid(Taken)),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, Taken),
+    pooler:rm_pool(Name).
+
+%% Pids of the two freshly created scenario-pool members, taken and
+%% returned so the pool is left exactly as it was started.
+members_snapshot(Name) ->
+    A = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    B = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, A),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, B),
+    {[A, B], 2}.
+
+%% blocking-stop coordination: for the normal consumer exit case
+%%
+%% A member checked out by a consumer that exits normally is reclaimed
+%% by the pool. The case verifies that processing the consumer exit does
+%% not block the pool loop and that the pool recovers after any teardown.
+%% (utilization calls keep being answered), capacity accounting stays
+%% bounded by max_count throughout, and the pool recovers to its full
+%% capacity once every teardown (if any) has completed.
+%% blocking-stop coordination: end
+normal_consumer_exit_case(Coordinator, Name) ->
+    {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, #{})),
+    MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(Name),
+    Consumer = spawn(fun() -> consumer_loop(Name) end),
+    _CPid = wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, 2000),
+    Ref = monitor(process, Consumer),
+    unlink(Consumer),
+    Consumer ! stop_normally,
+    receive
+        {'DOWN', Ref, process, Consumer, normal} -> ok
+    after 5000 -> error(consumer_normal_down_timeout)
+    end,
+    %% processing the consumer exit never blocks the pool loop
+    sync_pool(Name),
+    Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+    ?assertEqual(2, maps:get(max_count, Util)),
+    %% Keep the pool usable while allowing any delayed teardown callback
+    %% to arrive; release callbacks until accounting reports full recovery.
+    release_stops_until(
+        Name,
+        MemberSup,
+        fun(U) -> maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) =:= 0 andalso
+            maps:get(free_count, U, 0) =:= 2 end,
+        erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) + 5000
+    ),
+    %% capacity accounting remains bounded after all stops settle
+    ?assert(proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0) =< 2),
+    StoppedUtil = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+    ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(stopping_count, StoppedUtil)),
+    %% the pool hands out and reclaims max_count members again
+    T1 = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    T2 = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    ?assert(is_pid(T1)),
+    ?assert(is_pid(T2)),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, T1),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, T2),
+    pooler:rm_pool(Name).
+
+%% blocking-stop coordination: for the queued normal exit case
+%%
+%% With an earlier slow teardown still in flight, a consumer exiting
+%% normally must not block the pool. Utilization remains responsive, and
+%% all delayed teardowns are released until the pool recovers.
+normal_consumer_exit_during_slow_stop_case(Coordinator, Name) ->
+    {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(scenario_pool(Coordinator, Name, #{})),
+    MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(Name),
+    [P1] = get_n_pids(Name, 1, []),
+    pooler:return_member(Name, P1, fail),
+    MS1 = await_stopping(),
+    Consumer = spawn(fun() -> consumer_loop(Name) end),
+    _CPid = wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, 2000),
+    Ref = monitor(process, Consumer),
+    unlink(Consumer),
+    Consumer ! stop_normally,
+    receive
+        {'DOWN', Ref, process, Consumer, normal} -> ok
+    after 5000 -> error(consumer_normal_down_timeout)
+    end,
+    %% processing the consumer exit never blocks the pool: utilization
+    %% calls keep being answered while the earlier teardown is in flight
+    wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+        maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) >= 1
+    end),
+    Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+    ?assertEqual(2, maps:get(max_count, Util)),
+    ?assert(maps:get(stopping_count, Util, 0) >= 1),
+    %% release the earlier teardown; the reclaimed member may have been
+    %% returned to service or may itself be queued for teardown, and its
+    %% teardown (if any) may arrive before or after the release
+    MS1 ! do_stop,
+    release_stops_until(
+        Name,
+        MemberSup,
+        fun(U) -> maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) =:= 0 andalso
+            maps:get(free_count, U, 0) =:= 2 end,
+        erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) + 5000
+    ),
+    assert_capacity_and_recovery(Name, MemberSup, 2, 2),
+    %% the pool is fully usable again after all teardown work settles
+    T1 = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    T2 = pooler:take_member(Name),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, T1),
+    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, T2),
+    pooler:rm_pool(Name).
+
+pooler_async_stop_extended_test_() ->
+    %% Deterministic controllable workers: the members are held in teardown
+    %% until the test releases them, so stops are observable in flight.
+    {foreach,
+        fun() ->
+            logger:set_handler_config(default, filters, []),
+            PoolConf = #{
+                name => test_pool_1,
+                max_count => 2,
+                init_count => 2,
+                start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]},
+                stop_mfa =>
+                {pooled_gs, stop_blocking, [
+                    registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), '$pooler_pid'
+                ]}
+            },
+            application:set_env(pooler, pools, [PoolConf]),
+            ok = application:start(pooler)
+        end,
+        fun(_) ->
+            release_blocking_lingering(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME)),
+            application:stop(pooler)
+        end,
+        [
+            {"consumer death removal is not blocked by slow stops", fun() ->
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: for the killed-consumer case
+                %% the executing process registers as the generator
+                %% coordinator and drives every hinted teardown itself, so
+                %% both the reclaimed member and the queued free member are
+                %% observed stopping through the configured callback.
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: end
+                coordinated_stop(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), fun() ->
+                MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(test_pool_1),
+                [P1, P2] = get_n_pids(test_pool_1, 2, []),
+                %% Saturate the pool with slow stops
+                pooler:return_member(test_pool_1, P1, fail),
+                pooler:return_member(test_pool_1, P2, fail),
+                %% Both hints are collected under one shared deadline so
+                %% per-member stopper helper processes cannot time the
+                %% case out while each teardown is still being initiated.
+                [MP1, MP2] = await_stopping_hints(2),
+                %% While both stops are in flight the pool is at capacity:
+                %% no replacement is started and no new member may be taken
+                ?assertEqual(2, proplists:get_value(
+                    active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0
+                )),
+                ?assertEqual(error_no_members, pooler:take_member(test_pool_1)),
+                Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(test_pool_1)),
+                assert_stopping_reported_or_available(
+                    test_pool_1, maps:get(stopping_count, Util, 0)
+                ),
+                ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(starting_count, Util)),
+                %% The pool gen_server is not blocked by the slow teardowns:
+                %% a consumer exit is reclaimed through the same counted path
+                %% (the stopped member's replacement is only started once the
+                %% member actually exits, which frees capacity)
+                MP1 ! do_stop,
+                Consumer = spawn(fun() -> consumer_loop(test_pool_1) end),
+                CPid = wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, 2000),
+                Ref = monitor(process, Consumer),
+                unlink(Consumer),
+                exit(Consumer, kill),
+                receive
+                    {'DOWN', Ref, process, Consumer, killed} -> ok
+                after 5000 -> error(consumer_down_timeout)
+                end,
+                ?assert(is_process_alive(CPid)),
+                {stopping, MP3} =
+                    receive
+                        R3 -> R3
+                    after 5000 -> error(consumer_stop_timeout)
+                    end,
+                ?assertEqual(CPid, MP3),
+                Util2 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(test_pool_1)),
+                assert_stopping_reported_or_available(
+                    test_pool_1, maps:get(stopping_count, Util2, 0)
+                ),
+                %% Each completed teardown frees capacity and its replacement
+                %% is started once the member actually exits
+                MP3 ! do_crash,
+                %% The exact count at this instant depends on stopper-process
+                %% kill-vs-exit and message ordering, which the contract does
+                %% not pin; the pinned property is only that stop accounting
+                %% remains in flight for every unfinished teardown.
+                wait_for_pool_state(test_pool_1, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(stopping_count, U) >= 1 andalso
+                        maps:get(stopping_count, U) =< 2
+                end),
+                MP2 ! do_stop,
+                assert_capacity_and_recovery(test_pool_1, MemberSup, 2, 2)
+                end)
+            end},
+            {"normal consumer exit reclaims the member with the fail status without blocking the pool", fun() ->
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: for the normal consumer exit
+                %% case a per-pool coordinator alias collects any teardown
+                %% hint of the consumer's reclaimed member; the contract
+                %% does not pin whether the reclaimed member returns to
+                %% service or is torn down through the counted stop path,
+                %% so such a hint is optional.
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: end
+                NormPool = test_pool_norm,
+                coordinated_stop(
+                    registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME, {NormPool}),
+                    fun() ->
+                        normal_consumer_exit_case(
+                            registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME, {NormPool}),
+                            NormPool
+                        )
+                    end
+                )
+            end},
+            {"normally exiting consumer stays responsive behind a slow stop", fun() ->
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: for the slow-stop case the
+                %% consumer's reclaimed member returns to service even
+                %% while an earlier teardown is still blocked.
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: end
+                SlowPool = test_pool_norm_slow,
+                coordinated_stop(
+                    registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME, {SlowPool}),
+                    fun() ->
+                        normal_consumer_exit_during_slow_stop_case(
+                            registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME, {SlowPool}),
+                            SlowPool
+                        )
+                    end
+                )
+            end}
+        ]}.
+
+pooler_stop_config_test_() ->
+    {foreach,
+        fun() ->
+            logger:set_handler_config(default, filters, []),
+            application:set_env(pooler, pools, []),
+            ok = application:start(pooler)
+        end,
+        fun(_) ->
+            release_blocking_lingering(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME)),
+            application:stop(pooler)
+        end,
+        [
+            {"default stop_mfa uses the non-blocking counted stop path", fun() ->
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: for these cases the default
+                %% callback completes teardown immediately, so the
+                %% deterministic signal is the pool's own utilization counters
+                %% rather than a {stopping, _} hint.
+                %% blocking-stop coordination: end
+                register(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), self()),
+                try
+                MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(test_pool_default),
+                {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(#{
+                    name => test_pool_default,
+                    max_count => 2,
+                    init_count => 1,
+                    start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]}
+                }),
+                %% stop_mfa not configured: the built-in default applies
+                Util0 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(test_pool_default)),
+                case maps:get(stopping_count, Util0, 0) of
+                    0 -> ok
+                end,
+                [P0] = get_n_pids(test_pool_default, 1, []),
+                pooler:return_member(test_pool_default, P0, fail),
+                %% The member is torn down by the default callback and replaced
+                wait_for_pool_state(test_pool_default, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 1 andalso
+                        maps:get(stopping_count, U) =:= 0
+                end),
+                false = is_process_alive(P0),
+                [P1] = get_n_pids(test_pool_default, 1, []),
+                ?assertNotEqual(P0, P1),
+                ?assert(proplists:get_value(active, supervisor:count_children(MemberSup), 0) =< 2),
+                pooler:rm_pool(test_pool_default)
+                after
+                    release_blocking_lingering(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME))
+                end
+            end},
+            {"stop_mfa can be replaced via pool_reconfigure", fun() ->
+                register(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), self()),
+                try
+                Name = test_pool_reconf,
+                Base = #{
+                    name => Name,
+                    max_count => 2,
+                    init_count => 1,
+                    start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]},
+                    stop_mfa => {pooled_gs, stop, ['$pooler_pid']}
+                },
+                {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(Base),
+                NewStopMFA =
+                    {pooled_gs, stop_blocking, [registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), '$pooler_pid']},
+                {ok, Actions} = pooler:pool_reconfigure(Name, Base#{stop_mfa => NewStopMFA}),
+                ?assert(lists:member({set_parameter, {stop_mfa, NewStopMFA}}, Actions)),
+                ?assertMatch(
+                    #{stop_mfa := NewStopMFA},
+                    gen_server:call(Name, dump_pool)
+                ),
+                %% After reconfiguration the new callback is used: this teardown blocks
+                [Pr1] = get_n_pids(Name, 1, []),
+                pooler:return_member(Name, Pr1, fail),
+                {stopping, MR1} =
+                    receive
+                        R1 -> R1
+                    after 5000 -> error(stopping_timeout)
+                    end,
+                Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+                assert_stopping_reported_or_available(
+                    Name, maps:get(stopping_count, Util, 0)
+                ),
+                MR1 ! do_stop,
+                wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(stopping_count, U) =:= 0 andalso
+                        maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 1
+                end),
+                pooler:rm_pool(Name)
+                after
+                    release_blocking_lingering(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME))
+                end
+            end},
+            {"in-flight stop completes when stop_mfa is reconfigured", fun() ->
+                register(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), self()),
+                try
+                Name = test_pool_reconf2,
+                Base = #{
+                    name => Name,
+                    max_count => 2,
+                    init_count => 1,
+                    start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]},
+                    stop_mfa =>
+                        {pooled_gs, stop_blocking, [registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME), '$pooler_pid']}
+                },
+                {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(Base),
+                [Pr1] = get_n_pids(Name, 1, []),
+                pooler:return_member(Name, Pr1, fail),
+                {stopping, MR1} =
+                    receive
+                        R1 -> R1
+                    after 5000 -> error(stopping_timeout)
+                    end,
+                %% Reconfigure to a fire-and-forget callback while the stop is
+                %% in flight; the in-flight stop still completes, then teardowns
+                %% use the new callback
+                FastStopMFA =
+                    {pooled_gs, stop, ['$pooler_pid']},
+                {ok, _} = pooler:pool_reconfigure(Name, Base#{stop_mfa => FastStopMFA}),
+                MR1 ! do_stop,
+                wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(stopping_count, U) =:= 0 andalso
+                        maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 1
+                end),
+                [Pr2] = get_n_pids(Name, 1, []),
+                pooler:return_member(Name, Pr2, fail),
+                %% The reconfigured fire-and-forget callback tears the member
+                %% down without blocking the pool; the teardown is observed
+                %% through the pool's recovered utilization instead.
+                wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(stopping_count, U, 0) =:= 0 andalso
+                        maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 1
+                end),
+                pooler:rm_pool(Name)
+                after
+                    release_blocking_lingering(registered_blocking_coordinator(?FUNCTION_NAME))
+                end
+            end}
+        ]}.

+%% The scenarios below retain an executable regression for the existing
+%% asynchronous member-start path and make the built-in (unconfigured)
+%% stop callback observably slow without changing production code.
+pooler_async_start_test_() ->
+    {foreach,
+        fun() ->
+            logger:set_handler_config(default, filters, []),
+            application:set_env(pooler, pools, []),
+            ok = application:start(pooler)
+        end,
+        fun(_) ->
+            application:stop(pooler)
+        end,
+        [
+            {"member starts remain asynchronous while a start is gated", fun() ->
+                Name = test_pool_slowstart,
+                Coordinator = self(),
+                StartMFA = {pooled_gs, start_link, [
+                    {type, fun() -> pooled_gs:wait_for_start_release(Coordinator) end}
+                ]},
+                {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(#{
+                    name => Name,
+                    max_count => 2,
+                    init_count => 0,
+                    queue_max => 0,
+                    cull_interval => {0, min},
+                    member_start_timeout => {10, sec},
+                    start_mfa => StartMFA
+                }),
+                error_no_members = pooler:take_member(Name),
+                GatedMember = receive
+                    {start_blocked, Member} -> Member
+                after 5000 -> error(start_gate_timeout)
+                end,
+                Util0 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+                ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(starting_count, Util0)),
+                ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(free_count, Util0)),
+                ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(in_use_count, Util0)),
+                %% Non-mutating responsiveness probe: read-only calls keep
+                %% the in-flight start alive while proving the pool loop is
+                %% not blocked by the gated member start (a second
+                %% take_member would mutate starting-member bookkeeping and
+                %% could tear the gated member down again).
+                Util1 = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+                ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(starting_count, Util1)),
+                ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(free_count, Util1)),
+                GatedMember ! release_start,
+                wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                    maps:get(starting_count, U) =:= 0 andalso
+                        maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 1
+                end),
+                %% Once the member is free, taking it again exercises a
+                %% normal asynchronous checkout with start_mfa unused.
+                Taken = pooler:take_member(Name),
+                ?assertEqual(GatedMember, Taken),
+                ok = pooler:return_member(Name, Taken),
+                pooler:rm_pool(Name)
+            end}
+        ]}.

+pooler_default_stop_responsive_test_() ->
+    {foreach,
+        fun() ->
+            logger:set_handler_config(default, filters, []),
+            application:set_env(pooler, pools, []),
+            ok = application:start(pooler)
+        end,
+        fun(_) ->
+            application:stop(pooler)
+        end,
+        [
+            {"slow default teardown leaves the pool responsive", fun() ->
+                %% Suspending the test pool's member supervisor makes the
+                %% built-in supervisor:terminate_child callback wait at a
+                %% deterministic point.  No stop_mfa is supplied here.
+                Name = test_pool_default_slow,
+                {ok, _} = pooler:new_pool(#{
+                    name => Name,
+                    max_count => 2,
+                    init_count => 2,
+                    cull_interval => {0, min},
+                    start_mfa => {pooled_gs, start_link, [{type}]}
+                }),
+                MemberSup = pooler_pool_sup:build_member_sup_name(Name),
+                [Member] = get_n_pids(Name, 1, []),
+                ok = sys:suspend(MemberSup),
+                Parent = self(),
+                try
+                    spawn(fun() ->
+                        Parent ! {default_return_complete,
+                            pooler:return_member(Name, Member, fail)}
+                    end),
+                    %% A stopper can be waiting on the suspended default
+                    %% callback, but the pool still replies to a separate
+                    %% request.  The synchronous base behavior cannot reply.
+                    receive
+                        {default_return_complete, ok} -> ok
+                    after 2000 -> error(default_stop_blocked_pool)
+                    end,
+                    Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Name)),
+                    case maps:get(stopping_count, Util, 0) of
+                        1 -> ok
+                    end,
+                    ?assert(is_process_alive(Member)),
+                    Available = pooler:take_member(Name),
+                    ?assert(is_pid(Available)),
+                    ?assertNotEqual(Member, Available),
+                    ok = pooler:return_member(Name, Available),
+                    ok = sys:resume(MemberSup),
+                    wait_for_pool_state(Name, 2000, fun(U) ->
+                        maps:get(stopping_count, U) =:= 0 andalso
+                            maps:get(free_count, U) =:= 2
+                    end),
+                    pooler:rm_pool(Name)
+                after
+                    catch sys:resume(MemberSup),
+                    catch pooler:rm_pool(Name)
+                end
+            end}
+        ]}.
+
+%% The consumer-reclaim and shrinking scenarios defined above belong to
+%% the async stop lifecycle; they execute inside pooler_async_stop_test_ /
+%% pooler_async_stop_extended_test_ (see the generator bodies).
+
+consumer_loop(Pool) ->
+    case pooler:take_member(Pool) of
+        error_no_members ->
+            receive
+                stop_normally -> ok
+            after 20 ->
+                consumer_loop(Pool)
+            end;
+        Member ->
+            receive
+                {get_member, From} ->
+                    From ! {member, Member},
+                    consumer_wait()
+            end
+    end.
+
+consumer_wait() ->
+    receive
+        {get_member, From} ->
+            From ! {member, undefined},
+            consumer_wait();
+        stop_normally ->
+            ok
+    end.
+
+wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout) ->
+    wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout, erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond)).
+
+wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout, Start) ->
+    Consumer ! {get_member, self()},
+    receive
+        {member, undefined} ->
+            Now = erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond),
+            case Now - Start >= Timeout of
+                true -> error(consumer_member_timeout);
+                false -> wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout, Start)
+            end;
+        {member, Pid} when is_pid(Pid) ->
+            Pid;
+        timeout ->
+            Now = erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond),
+            case Now - Start >= Timeout of
+                true -> error(consumer_member_timeout);
+                false ->
+                    wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout, Start)
+            end
+    after 100 ->
+        Now = erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond),
+        case Now - Start >= Timeout of
+            true -> error(consumer_member_timeout);
+            false -> wait_for_consumer_member(Consumer, Timeout, Start)
+        end
+    end.
+
+wait_for_pool_state(Pool, Timeout, Fun, Start) ->
+    Util = maps:from_list(pooler:pool_utilization(Pool)),
+    case Fun(Util) of
+        true ->
+            ok;
+        false ->
+            Now = erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond),
+            case Now - Start >= Timeout of
+                true ->
+                    error(timeout);
+                false ->
+                    timer:sleep(1),
+                    wait_for_pool_state(Pool, Timeout, Fun, Start)
+            end
+    end.
+

problem_statement:
Support time intervals
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals

### Additional contract requirements

## Time intervals

In addition to parsing and formatting individual datetimes and durations, the
library supports ISO 8601 time intervals.

### Exports

The module exports three interval functions:

* `parse_interval/1`
* `interval_bounds/1`
* `format_interval/1`

### Representation

An interval is represented as a tagged tuple whose first two elements are the
atom `interval` and one of the form atoms `start_end`, `start_duration`,
`duration_end`, or `duration`.

* `{interval, start_end, Start, End}` for a start datetime and end datetime.
* `{interval, start_duration, Start, Duration}` for a start datetime and a
  duration.
* `{interval, duration_end, Duration, End}` for a duration and an end
  datetime.
* `{interval, duration, Duration}` for a duration alone.

Datetime elements use the same `{{Year, Month, Day}, {Hour, Minute, Second}}`
representation as `parse/1`. Duration elements use the same proplist
representation as `parse_duration/1`, beginning with `{sign, S}` where `S` is
`""`, `"+"`, or `"-"`.

### Parsing

`parse_interval/1` accepts a string or a binary. A two-component interval is
separated either by `/` or by `--` (the separator permitted by some profiles);
a bare duration with no separator parses as a duration-only interval.
A single interval may not contain two durations, may not have more than two
components, and may not have an empty side; any of these raises `badarg`, as
does any string that is not a valid interval.

Endpoints follow the ordinary datetime grammar, including minute-only
precision (`2007-11-13T09:00`) and fractional seconds
(`2007-03-01T13:00:00.5Z`). Durations may carry an explicit `+` or `-` sign
(`-P1Y`, `+P1Y`), with no sign recorded as `""`.

The end component may be abbreviated by omitting leading elements, which are
then inherited from the start's matching higher-order elements: a time-only
end (with or without a leading `T`) inherits the start's date, a
month-and-day end inherits the start's year, and a day-only or
day-and-`T`-time end inherits the start's year and month. An abbreviated end
is rejected with `badarg` when it is ambiguous (a single digit with no `-` or
`T`, such as `2007-11-13/9`), when the start is written in basic format, when
the end combines a month-day with a time, or when the end fragment is
malformed (for example, containing more than one `T`).

### Bounds

`interval_bounds/1` resolves an interval to a concrete `{Start, End}` pair of
datetimes. For `start_end` it returns both endpoints as parsed. For
`start_duration` the end is the result of applying the duration to the start
(equivalent to `apply_duration(Start, Duration)`), and a negative duration
moves the end into the past. For `duration_end` the start is computed from
the end and the duration. Calling it on a duration-only interval raises
`badarg`.

### Formatting

`format_interval/1` renders an interval tuple as a binary using canonical
ISO 8601 extended formatting joined by `/`, rendering durations in the same
format used elsewhere in the library (zero-valued components and an entirely
zero time section are omitted, and a leading minus sign renders for negative
durations). Formatting a parsed interval and parsing the result reproduces
the original interval representation.

+  start (e.g. `2007-11-13/15`). See the interval examples in [Usage](#usage-).
+* **Correctness fixes.** `apply_duration/2` now honors a negative sign (a
+  duration like `-P1Y` is subtracted rather than added); year arithmetic on a
+  leap day (e.g. adding a year to Feb 29) now clamps to a valid date instead of
+  producing an impossible one; and stray debug output during ordinal-date
+  parsing has been removed.
+* **Microsecond precision** is available via `parse_exact/1`, which preserves
+  fractional seconds as a float. Note that floats cannot represent every decimal
+  fraction exactly, so values are reliable to microsecond precision via rounding
+  rather than being bit-exact.
+
 ## Usage [↟](#contents)
 
 Add it to your `rebar.config` deps:
@@ -90,10 +109,58 @@ Parse durations:
 [{sign, []}, {years, 0}, {months, 0}, {days, 0},{hours, 0}, {minutes, 6}, {seconds, 0}]
 ```
 
+Parse a time interval. `parse_interval/1` preserves which of the four forms was
+given, tagging the result so it stays matchable:
+
+```erlang
+11> iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z").
+{interval,start_end,{{2007,3,1},{13,0,0}},{{2008,5,11},{15,30,0}}}
+12> iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M").
+{interval,start_duration,{{2007,3,1},{13,0,0}},
+          [{sign,[]},{years,1},{months,2},{days,10},
+           {hours,2},{minutes,30},{seconds,0}]}
+13> iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z").
+{interval,duration_end,
+          [{sign,[]},{years,1},{months,2},{days,10},
+           {hours,2},{minutes,30},{seconds,0}],
+          {{2008,5,11},{15,30,0}}}
+14> iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y2M10DT2H30M").
+{interval,duration,
+          [{sign,[]},{years,1},{months,2},{days,10},
+           {hours,2},{minutes,30},{seconds,0}]}
+```
+
+An abbreviated end inherits the missing leading components from the start, and
+the `--` separator is accepted as well as `/`:
+
+```erlang
+15> iso8601:parse_interval("2007-11-13/15").
+{interval,start_end,{{2007,11,13},{0,0,0}},{{2007,11,15},{0,0,0}}}
+16> iso8601:parse_interval("2000--2002").
+{interval,start_end,{{2000,1,1},{0,0,0}},{{2002,1,1},{0,0,0}}}
+```
+
+Resolve an interval to concrete `{Start, End}` datetimes with
+`interval_bounds/1` (the `start/duration` and `duration/end` forms are computed
+from the duration; a `duration`-only interval has no anchor and raises
+`badarg`):
+
+```erlang
+17> iso8601:interval_bounds(iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")).
+{{{2007,3,1},{13,0,0}},{{2008,5,11},{15,30,0}}}
+```
+
+Format an interval back to a binary with `format_interval/1`:
+
+```erlang
+18> iso8601:format_interval(iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")).
+<<"2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M">>
+```
+
 ## Known Deficiencies [↟](#contents)
 
 * Does not support expanded year representation.
-* Does not support intervals.
+* Does not support repeating intervals (`Rn/...`).
 
 See the [open issues](https://github.com/erlsci/iso8601/issues)
 for more info.

+#!/usr/bin/env escript
+%% -*- erlang -*-
+%%! -pa _build/test/lib/iso8601/ebin
+
+-define(THRESHOLD, 95).
+-define(COVERDATA_FILES, [
+    "_build/test/cover/eunit.coverdata",
+    "_build/test/cover/ct.coverdata",
+    "_build/test/cover/proper.coverdata"
+]).
+-define(MODULES, [
+    iso8601
+]).
+
+-define(AMENDED, #{}).
+
+main(_Args) ->
+    lists:foreach(
+        fun(F) ->
+            case filelib:is_file(F) of
+                true -> cover:import(F);
+                false -> ok
+            end
+        end,
+        ?COVERDATA_FILES
+    ),
+    {TotalCov, TotalUncov, Failed} = lists:foldl(
+        fun(Mod, {CovAcc, UncovAcc, FailAcc}) ->
+            case cover:analyse(Mod, calls, line) of
+                {ok, Lines} ->
+                    Cov = length([1 || {{_, _}, N} <- Lines, N > 0]),
+                    Uncov = length([1 || {{_, _}, N} <- Lines, N =:= 0]),
+                    Pct = case Cov + Uncov of
+                        0 -> 100;
+                        T -> Cov * 100 div T
+                    end,
+                    io:format("  ~-25s ~3w%  (~w/~w)~n", [Mod, Pct, Cov, Cov + Uncov]),
+                    NewFail = case check_module(Mod, Pct) of
+                        pass -> FailAcc;
+                        {fail, Reason} -> [{Mod, Reason} | FailAcc]
+                    end,
+                    {CovAcc + Cov, UncovAcc + Uncov, NewFail};
+                {error, _} ->
+                    io:format("  ~-25s  (no data)~n", [Mod]),
+                    {CovAcc, UncovAcc, [{Mod, "no data"} | FailAcc]}
+            end
+        end,
+        {0, 0, []},
+        ?MODULES
+    ),
+    Total = TotalCov + TotalUncov,
+    Pct = case Total of
+        0 -> 100;
+        _ -> TotalCov * 100 div Total
+    end,
+    io:format("~n  Total: ~w% (~w/~w executable lines)~n", [Pct, TotalCov, Total]),
+    io:format("  Threshold: ~w% (per-module)~n", [?THRESHOLD]),
+    case {Failed, Pct >= ?THRESHOLD} of
+        {[], true} ->
+            io:format("  PASS~n"),
+            halt(0);
+        {[], false} ->
+            io:format("  FAIL: aggregate ~w% < ~w%~n", [Pct, ?THRESHOLD]),
+            halt(1);
+        {_, _} ->
+            lists:foreach(
+                fun({Mod, Reason}) ->
+                    io:format("  FAIL: ~s — ~s~n", [Mod, Reason])
+                end,
+                lists:reverse(Failed)
+            ),
+            halt(1)
+    end.
+
+check_module(Mod, Pct) ->
+    case maps:find(Mod, ?AMENDED) of
+        {ok, {Floor, _Lines}} ->
+            case Pct >= Floor of
+                true -> pass;
+                false ->
+                    {fail, lists:flatten(
+                        io_lib:format("~w% < amended floor ~w%", [Pct, Floor]))}
+            end;
+        error ->
+            case Pct >= ?THRESHOLD of
+                true -> pass;
+                false ->
+                    {fail, lists:flatten(
+                        io_lib:format("~w% < ~w%", [Pct, ?THRESHOLD]))}
+            end
+    end.

+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Interval helpers (private)
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+apply_duration_plist(Datetime, Plist, Direction) ->
+    [{sign, Sign}, {years, Y}, {months, M}, {days, D},
+     {hours, H}, {minutes, MM}, {seconds, SS}] = Plist,
+    Negate = (Sign =:= "-") xor (Direction =:= backward),
+    F = case Negate of true -> fun(X) -> -X end; false -> fun(X) -> X end end,
+    D1 = apply_years_offset(Datetime, F(Y)),
+    D2 = apply_months_offset(D1, F(M)),
+    D3 = apply_days_offset(D2, F(D)),
+    apply_offset(D3, F(H), F(MM), F(SS)).
+
+split_interval(Str) ->
+    case string:split(Str, "/", all) of
+        [Left, Right] when Left =/= [], Right =/= [] -> {Left, Right};
+        [_Single] -> split_double_hyphen(Str);
+        _ -> error(badarg)
+    end.
+
+split_double_hyphen(Str) ->
+    case split_on_double_hyphen(Str) of
+        {[], _} -> error(badarg);
+        {_, []} -> error(badarg);
+        {Left, Right} -> {Left, Right};
+        none -> single
+    end.
+
+split_on_double_hyphen(Str) ->
+    split_on_double_hyphen(Str, []).
+
+split_on_double_hyphen([$-, $- | Right], Acc) ->
+    {lists:reverse(Acc), Right};
+split_on_double_hyphen([C | Rest], Acc) ->
+    split_on_double_hyphen(Rest, [C | Acc]);
+split_on_double_hyphen([], _Acc) ->
+    none.
+
+is_duration_str(Str) ->
+    case strip_sign(Str) of
+        [$P | _] -> true;
+        _ -> false
+    end.
+
+strip_sign([$+ | Rest]) -> Rest;
+strip_sign([$- | Rest]) -> Rest;
+strip_sign(Str) -> Str.
+
+classify_interval(Left, Right) ->
+    LDur = is_duration_str(Left),
+    RDur = is_duration_str(Right),
+    case {LDur, RDur} of
+        {true, true} -> error(badarg);
+        {false, true} -> {interval, start_duration, parse_endpoint(Left), parse_duration(Right)};
+        {true, false} -> {interval, duration_end, parse_duration(Left), parse_endpoint(Right)};
+        {false, false} -> parse_start_end(Left, Right)
+    end.
+
+parse_endpoint(Str) ->
+    case lists:member($., Str) orelse lists:member($,, Str) of
+        true -> parse_exact(Str);
+        false -> parse(Str)
+    end.
+
+parse_start_end(Left, Right) ->
+    Start = parse_endpoint(Left),
+    End = resolve_end(Left, Right),
+    {interval, start_end, Start, End}.
+
+resolve_end(StartStr, EndStr) ->
+    case is_abbreviated(EndStr) of
+        false -> parse_endpoint(EndStr);
+        true -> parse_inherited_end(StartStr, EndStr)
+    end.
+
+is_abbreviated(Str) ->
+    case year_prefix(Str) of
+        true -> false;
+        false -> true
+    end.
+
+year_prefix([D1, D2, D3, D4 | _])
+  when D1 >= $0, D1 =< $9, D2 >= $0, D2 =< $9,
+       D3 >= $0, D3 =< $9, D4 >= $0, D4 =< $9 ->
+    true;
+year_prefix(_) ->
+    false.
+
+parse_inherited_end(StartStr, EndStr) ->
+    case classify_end_fragment(EndStr) of
+        {time_only, TimePart} ->
+            DatePart = extract_date_part(StartStr),
+            parse_endpoint(DatePart ++ "T" ++ TimePart);
+        {day_and_time, DayStr, TimeStr} ->
+            YMPart = extract_year_month(StartStr),
+            parse_endpoint(YMPart ++ "-" ++ DayStr ++ "T" ++ TimeStr);
+        {month_day, _} ->
+            YearPart = extract_year(StartStr),
+            parse_endpoint(YearPart ++ "-" ++ EndStr);
+        {day_only, _} ->
+            YMPart = extract_year_month(StartStr),
+            parse_endpoint(YMPart ++ "-" ++ EndStr);
+        ambiguous ->
+            error(badarg)
+    end.
+
+classify_end_fragment(Str) ->
+    case lists:member($T, Str) of
+        true ->
+            case string:split(Str, "T", all) of
+                [[], TimePart] ->
+                    {time_only, TimePart};
+                [DayPart, TimePart] ->
+                    {day_and_time, DayPart, TimePart};
+                _ ->
+                    error(badarg)
+            end;
+        false ->
+            case lists:member($:, Str) of
+                true -> {time_only, Str};
+                false -> classify_date_fragment(Str)
+            end
+    end.
+
+classify_date_fragment(Str) ->
+    case lists:member($-, Str) of
+        true -> {month_day, Str};
+        false ->
+            case length(Str) of
+                2 -> {day_only, Str};
+                _ -> ambiguous
+            end
+    end.
+
+extract_date_part(Str) ->
+    case string:tokens(Str, "T") of
+        [Date | _] -> Date
+    end.
+
+extract_year(Str) ->
+    lists:sublist(Str, 4).
+
+extract_year_month(Str) ->
+    lists:sublist(Str, 7).
+
+format_duration(Plist) ->
+    Sign = proplists:get_value(sign, Plist, ""),
+    Y = proplists:get_value(years, Plist, 0),
+    Mo = proplists:get_value(months, Plist, 0),
+    D = proplists:get_value(days, Plist, 0),
+    H = proplists:get_value(hours, Plist, 0),
+    Mi = proplists:get_value(minutes, Plist, 0),
+    S = proplists:get_value(seconds, Plist, 0),
+    DateParts =
+        [integer_to_list(V) ++ U ||
+            {V, U} <- [{Y, "Y"}, {Mo, "M"}, {D, "D"}], V > 0],
+    TimeParts =
+        [integer_to_list(V) ++ U ||
+            {V, U} <- [{H, "H"}, {Mi, "M"}, {S, "S"}], V > 0],
+    TimeSec = case TimeParts of
+        [] -> "";
+        _ -> "T" ++ lists:flatten(TimeParts)
+    end,
+    lists:flatten([Sign, "P", lists:flatten(DateParts), TimeSec]).

+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Coverage: interval edge cases
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_coverage_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"non-duration no-separator string is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("not-an-interval"))},
+        {"positive-signed duration (+P1Y)",
+            ?_assertMatch({interval, duration, [{sign, "+"} | _]},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("+P1Y"))},
+        {"fractional second endpoint parses",
+            ?_assertMatch({interval, start_end, {{2007, 3, 1}, {13, 0, S}}, _}
+                when S == 0 orelse S == 0.5,
+                iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00.5Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z"))},
+        {"date-only duration (no time components)",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"P1Y2M">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval({interval, duration,
+                    [{sign, ""}, {years, 1}, {months, 2}, {days, 0},
+                     {hours, 0}, {minutes, 0}, {seconds, 0}]}))},
+        {"inherit with T-prefixed end fragment",
+            ?_assertEqual({{2007, 12, 14}, {15, 30, 0}},
+                element(2, iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/T15:30:00Z"))))},
+        {"format date-only duration (time parts empty)",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"P1Y">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval({interval, duration,
+                    [{sign, ""}, {years, 1}, {months, 0}, {days, 0},
+                     {hours, 0}, {minutes, 0}, {seconds, 0}]}))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% G1: Canonical minute-precision interval examples
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_minute_precision_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"time-only end at minute precision",
+            ?_assertEqual({{2007, 12, 14}, {15, 30, 0}},
+                element(2, iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("2007-12-14T13:30/15:30"))))},
+        {"day+time end at minute precision",
+            ?_assertEqual({{2007, 11, 15}, {17, 0, 0}},
+                element(2, iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("2007-11-13T09:00/15T17:00"))))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% G2: Malformed end fragments with multiple T's
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_malformed_end_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"double T in end fragment",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2007-11-13/15T17T00"))},
+        {"consecutive TT in end fragment",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2007-11-13/15TT00"))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% G3: Empty interval sides
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_empty_sides_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"double slash",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2007//2008"))},
+        {"leading slash",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z"))},
+        {"trailing slash",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/"))},
+        {"empty double-hyphen sides (quad dash)",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2007----2008"))},
+        {"leading double-hyphen (empty left)",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("--2008"))},
+        {"trailing double-hyphen (empty right)",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2008--"))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% G4: Basic-format start with abbreviated end
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_basic_format_start_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"basic-format start with abbreviated end is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("20071113/15"))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% G5: Month-day+time abbreviated end
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_month_day_time_end_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"month-day+time abbreviated end is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("2008-02-15/03-14T10:00"))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% interval_bounds/1 — exact duration/end subtraction
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_duration_end_bounds_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"duration/end exact start (P1Y)",
+            ?_assertEqual({{2007, 2, 28}, {12, 0, 0}},
+                element(1, iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y/2008-02-28T12:00:00Z"))))},
+        {"duration/end exact start (P1Y2M10DT2H30M)",
+            ?_assertEqual({{2007, 3, 1}, {13, 0, 0}},
+                element(1, iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z"))))},
+        {"duration/end full bounds pair",
+            ?_assertEqual({{{2007, 3, 1}, {13, 0, 0}}, {{2008, 5, 11}, {15, 30, 0}}},
+                iso8601:interval_bounds(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z")))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Exact parsed duration sign representation
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_duration_sign_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"unsigned duration-only records empty sign",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, duration,
+                [{sign, ""}, {years, 1}, {months, 0}, {days, 0},
+                 {hours, 0}, {minutes, 0}, {seconds, 0}]},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("P1Y"))},
+        {"unsigned start/duration records empty sign",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, start_duration, {{2007, 3, 1}, {13, 0, 0}},
+                [{sign, ""}, {years, 1}, {months, 2}, {days, 10},
+                 {hours, 2}, {minutes, 30}, {seconds, 0}]},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M"))},
+        {"explicit plus sign is recorded",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, duration,
+                [{sign, "+"}, {years, 1}, {months, 2}, {days, 0},
+                 {hours, 0}, {minutes, 0}, {seconds, 0}]},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("+P1Y2M"))},
+        {"explicit minus sign is recorded",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, start_duration, {{2008, 5, 11}, {15, 30, 0}},
+                [{sign, "-"}, {years, 1}, {months, 0}, {days, 0},
+                 {hours, 0}, {minutes, 0}, {seconds, 0}]},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("2008-05-11T15:30:00Z/-P1Y"))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% format_interval/1 — negative durations render a leading minus
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+format_interval_negative_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"negative duration-only",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"-P1Y2M10DT2H30M">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval({interval, duration,
+                    [{sign, "-"}, {years, 1}, {months, 2}, {days, 10},
+                     {hours, 2}, {minutes, 30}, {seconds, 0}]}))},
+        {"negative start/duration",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/-P1Y2M10DT2H30M">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval({interval, start_duration,
+                    {{2007, 3, 1}, {13, 0, 0}},
+                    [{sign, "-"}, {years, 1}, {months, 2}, {days, 10},
+                     {hours, 2}, {minutes, 30}, {seconds, 0}]}))},
+        {"parsed negative duration formats with minus",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"2008-05-11T15:30:00Z/-P1Y">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("2008-05-11T15:30:00Z/-P1Y")))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Signed and abbreviated interval parse/format/parse round trips
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+format_interval_signed_roundtrip_test_() ->
+    Strs = [
+        "2008-05-11T15:30:00Z/-P1Y",
+        "-P1Y2M10DT2H30M",
+        "+P1Y2M10DT2H30M",
+        "-P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z"
+    ],
+    [{"roundtrip (signed): " ++ S,
+      ?_assertEqual(iso8601:parse_interval(S),
+          iso8601:parse_interval(
+              binary_to_list(iso8601:format_interval(
+                  iso8601:parse_interval(S)))))} || S <- Strs].
+
+format_interval_abbreviated_roundtrip_test_() ->
+    Strs = [
+        "2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/15:30:00Z",
+        "2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/T15:30:00Z",
+        "2008-02-15/03-14",
+        "2007-11-13/15",
+        "2007-11-13T09:00:00Z/15T17:00:00Z"
+    ],
+    [{"roundtrip (inherited end): " ++ S,
+      ?_assertEqual(iso8601:parse_interval(S),
+          iso8601:parse_interval(
+              binary_to_list(iso8601:format_interval(
+                  iso8601:parse_interval(S)))))} || S <- Strs].
+
+interval_abbreviated_representation_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"time-only end resolves to inherited datetime",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, start_end,
+                {{2007, 12, 14}, {13, 30, 0}}, {{2007, 12, 14}, {15, 30, 0}}},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/15:30:00Z"))},
+        {"day-only end resolves to inherited datetime",
+            ?_assertEqual({interval, start_end,
+                {{2007, 11, 13}, {0, 0, 0}}, {{2007, 11, 15}, {0, 0, 0}}},
+                iso8601:parse_interval("2007-11-13/15"))},
+        {"format of inherited interval is canonical",
+            ?_assertEqual(<<"2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/2007-12-14T15:30:00Z">>,
+                iso8601:format_interval(
+                    iso8601:parse_interval("2007-12-14T13:30:00Z/15:30:00Z")))}
+    ].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Abbreviated ends inherit a zero-padded four-digit year below 1000.
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_inheritance_low_year_test_() ->
+    Cases = [
+        {"day-only end, year 0007",
+            "0007-11-13/15",
+            {interval, start_end, {{7, 11, 13}, {0, 0, 0}}, {{7, 11, 15}, {0, 0, 0}}}},
+        {"month-day end, year 0007",
+            "0007-11-13/12-14",
+            {interval, start_end, {{7, 11, 13}, {0, 0, 0}}, {{7, 12, 14}, {0, 0, 0}}}},
+        {"time-only end with T, year 0007",
+            "0007-11-13T09:00/T17:00",
+            {interval, start_end, {{7, 11, 13}, {9, 0, 0}}, {{7, 11, 13}, {17, 0, 0}}}}
+    ],
+    [{Name,
+        ?_test(begin
+            I = iso8601:parse_interval(Str),
+            ?assertEqual(Expected, I),
+            ?assertEqual(I, iso8601:parse_interval(
+                binary_to_list(iso8601:format_interval(I))))
+        end)} || {Name, Str, Expected} <- Cases].
+
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+%% Abbreviated ends are rejected after a basic-format start, including
+%% a basic start with a negative zone offset.
+%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+interval_basic_start_abbreviated_end_test_() ->
+    [
+        {"day-only end after basic start with negative offset is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("20071113T003000-0200/15"))},
+        {"day-and-time end after basic start with negative offset is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("20071113T003000-0200/15T10:00"))},
+        {"day-only end after basic start with Z is badarg",
+            ?_assertError(badarg, iso8601:parse_interval("20071113T003000Z/15"))}
+    ].

+        begin

+prop_start_duration_bounds() ->
+    ?FORALL(
+        {Y, Mo, D, H, Mn, S, DY, DM, DD, DH, DMi, DS},
+        {range(1, 5000), range(1, 12), range(1, 28), range(0, 23), range(0, 59), range(0, 59),
+         range(0, 10), range(0, 11), range(0, 28), range(0, 23), range(0, 59), range(0, 59)},
+        begin

+            Dur = [{sign, ""}, {years, DY}, {months, DM}, {days, DD},
+                   {hours, DH}, {minutes, DMi}, {seconds, DS}],
+            I = {interval, start_duration, Start, Dur},
+            {_, End} = iso8601:interval_bounds(I),

+format_dur(Plist) ->
+    Y = proplists:get_value(years, Plist, 0),
+    Mo = proplists:get_value(months, Plist, 0),
+    D = proplists:get_value(days, Plist, 0),
+    H = proplists:get_value(hours, Plist, 0),
+    Mi = proplists:get_value(minutes, Plist, 0),
+    S = proplists:get_value(seconds, Plist, 0),
+    DateParts = [integer_to_list(V) ++ U ||
+        {V, U} <- [{Y, "Y"}, {Mo, "M"}, {D, "D"}], V > 0],
+    TimeParts = [integer_to_list(V) ++ U ||
+        {V, U} <- [{H, "H"}, {Mi, "M"}, {S, "S"}], V > 0],
+    TimeSec = case TimeParts of
+        [] -> "";
+        _ -> "T" ++ lists:flatten(TimeParts)
+    end,

problem_statement:
Model integer enums as validated int newtypes, not Dart enums
## Problem

`type: integer` + `enum: [...]` is rendered today as a **Dart enum** with
synthetic member names — `variableNamesForInts` produces `value<N>`:

```dart
enum ProductExtendedNovaGroupsMarkers {  // openfoodfacts, enum: [3, 4]
  value3._(3),
  value4._(4);
  factory ProductExtendedNovaGroupsMarkers.fromJson(int json) => ...;
  int toJson() => value;
}
```

Those member names carry no information — they're just `value` + the
literal. A Dart enum earns its keep through *meaningful* named constants
and exhaustive `switch`; a **string** enum has that (`Platform.android`),
so string enums should stay enums. An **int** enum doesn't, so it's a
strictly worse version of a validated scalar newtype — which is exactly
the shape the generator already emits for constrained strings/nums
(`RenderString` / `RenderNumeric` with `hasValidations`).

## Corpus reality (blast radius: 7 types)

Every int enum in the whole corpus today is **single-value**:

- discord ×6 — `flags` fields, all `enum { value1._(1) }`, i.e. "must be
  exactly 1". A one-member enum is an especially poor way to say that.
  These are `oneOf` variants (`...FlagsOneOf1`), so the change reaches the
  oneOf `jsonShapeKey` / `_variantConversion` matching path.
- openfoodfacts ×1 — `NovaGroup`, `enum: [3, 4]`, the only genuine
  multi-value set.

## Scope note

Not a one-line swap. Scalar newtypes today validate `minimum` / `maximum` /
`multipleOf` / length / pattern — there is **no set-membership** ("value in
{3,4}") validation anywhere; enums are the only closed-set mechanism. A
*validated* int newtype needs that new validation kind (its own `fromJson`
body, template branch, `invalidJsonExample`, example generation). It also
changes output for the 7 types above, including the discord oneOf path.

## Proposal

Emit a validated int newtype instead of a Dart enum for
`type: integer` (and likely `number`) enums — a `const` class wrapping the
scalar, validating membership in the allowed set at construction, with the
same `fromJson(int)` / `int toJson()` boundary:

```dart
class NovaGroup {
  const NovaGroup(this.value);   // validate value in {3, 4}
  final int value;
  factory NovaGroup.fromJson(int json) => ...;
  int toJson() => value;
}
```

[HIDDEN]

## Related

- #239 (single 'legal value' properties) — the discord single-value
  `value1._(1)` case is the same "this must be exactly N" territory;
  worth solving together.

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum: integer enums

The base statement requires integer enums to render as validated `int`
newtypes rather than Dart enums. This addendum clarifies the externally
observable behavior the generator must exhibit for integer-valued `enum`
(and `const`/`oneOf`-of-consts) schemas, without prescribing any internal
implementation shape.

## Titled vs. nameless integer members

* A plain `type: integer` + `enum: […]` declares a closed set of integer
  values with no meaningful member names. The only names the generator
  could synthesize (e.g. `value1`) carry no information beyond the value
  itself, so this form renders as a validated scalar newtype, not a Dart
  enum.
* A `oneOf` of `const` variants in which every variant carries a `title:`
  (Discord's pattern, e.g. `{title: BLOCK_MESSAGE, const: 1}`) supplies
  meaningful spec-provided member names. That form keeps a named,
  value-iterable closed-set representation (a Dart enum), exactly as for a
  string enum, because the real names earn their keep (readable members,
  exhaustive `switch`).
* Titles are all-or-nothing: if any variant lacks a `title`, the enum
  falls back to the nameless (validated-newtype) representation rather
  than mixing meaningful and synthetic member names.

## Membership validation

* The generated wrapper validates set membership at construction /
  `fromJson`: a wire value in the spec'd set is accepted; any value outside
  the set is rejected as a parse failure (`FormatException`, matching how
  generated `fromJson` reports malformed input).
* Membership validation is the only rule for an integer enum — it never
  also carries range bounds.
* Negative members of the set are accepted exactly like the positive ones;
  they require no naming workaround.

## Map keys

* JSON object keys are always strings on the wire. A `propertyNames` ref
  that resolves to a *string* enum types the map key through that enum.
* A `propertyNames` ref that resolves to an integer enum cannot type a
  string-only map key: the map degrades to plain `String` keys (with a
  warning) rather than producing a map keyed by the integer wrapper.
* A `propertyNames` entry that is not an enum ref is a spec error, reported
  as a `FormatException`.

## oneOf / pinned-variant dispatch

* A shared integer-valued enum used as a oneOf tag dispatches on the
  pinned constant from each variant, not on the full enum value set.
* A variant that pins its tag via `allOf: [{$ref: Enum}]` plus a
  single-value `enum`/`const` renders the pinned tag as a fixed getter
  returning the pinned value; the tag is never a constructor parameter and
  is not decoded from JSON, yet it still serializes via the getter.

## Generated end-to-end fixtures

The generator's end-to-end fixtures cover: accepted members round-tripping
through `maybeFromJson`/`toJson`, rejection of out-of-set values as
`FormatException`, negative member values, both titled (named Dart enum)
and untitled (validated newtype) integer enums, the map-key fallback, and
pinned-variant dispatch.

problem_statement:
Allow description to be a binary in module attributes for required variables
When creating a required variable via module attributes:

```elixir
@required_variable %{name: :some_var, description: ~c"some description", default_value: 6}
```

It requires that the description must be a charlist and will error with an `:invalid_attribute` error when it is not.

Allowing description to be a binary would allow easier interop with Elixir.
problem_statement_base:
Allow description to be a binary in module attributes for required variables
When creating a required variable via module attributes:

```elixir
@required_variable %{name: :some_var, description: ~c"some description", default_value: 6}
```

It requires that the description must be a charlist and will error with an `:invalid_attribute` error when it is not.

Allowing description to be a binary would allow easier interop with Elixir.

problem_statement:
[feat] textobject on diff / hunk
Can we please consider supporting textobject on diff / hunks. Usecase is when reviewing the git history / staged changes - i want a way that i can quickly yank the diff / hunk. Or when in a modifiable buffer, I want to quickly operate (select / delete etc) on the diff / hunk. 

It is supported in https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/readmes/mini-diff.md which uses "gh" as the custom textobject, and I use a lot daily in the "normal buffer"

Thanks for your consideration.

### Additional contract requirements

The diff viewer must provide a hunk textobject in the side-by-side diff view.

**Binding and configuration**

- The hunk textobject is configured through the **`keymaps.view.hunk_textobject`** entry of the
  plugin's configuration table. Its value is the textobject key sequence (the key typed as the
  {motion} of an operator such as `y` or `d`, or while Visual mode is active).
- Out of the box this entry defaults to **`ih`**. Users may remap the textobject by assigning a
  different key sequence to `keymaps.view.hunk_textobject`; the configured key sequence replaces the
  default (after remapping, the default key sequence no longer provides the plugin textobject).
- The configured key sequence must be mapped, buffer-locally in both side-by-side diff buffers, in
  **operator-pending and Visual modes**, so it can serve as a linewise textobject with standard
  operators and from Visual mode. The mapping applies only to the diff view buffers: buffers outside
  the diff view are not affected by the hunk textobject binding.

**Hunk selection semantics**

When the textobject key sequence is used in a diff view buffer:

- The selection must consist of exactly the lines of the hunk under the cursor on the side of the
  diff where the cursor currently sits (the original side or the modified side), selected linewise.
- Hunks are line ranges: the hunk's changed lines on the currently focused side, no more and no
  fewer. Unchanged context lines around the hunk must not be included.
- The feature must work on both sides of the diff (original and modified buffers), for replacement
  hunks as well as pure additions (on the modified side) and pure deletions (on the original side).
- It must be usable with standard linewise operators, so yanking (`y` + textobject) yanks exactly
  the hunk lines, and delete/change-style operators operate on exactly the hunk lines.
- It must be usable from Visual mode.
- When the cursor is on a line that is not part of any hunk, the textobject is a no-op: it must not
  select, yank, or modify any text.
