test_patch:
diff --git a/tests/ui/view/hunk_textobject_spec.lua b/tests/ui/view/hunk_textobject_spec.lua
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bb1bd4e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/ui/view/hunk_textobject_spec.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,489 @@
+-- Tests for the hunk textobject in the side-by-side diff view.
+--
+-- The public contract designates the `keymaps.view.hunk_textobject`
+-- configuration entry as the hunk textobject binding, shipping an `ih`
+-- default: the plugin installs a buffer-local mapping for the configured key
+-- in operator-pending and Visual modes in both side-by-side diff buffers (and
+-- in no other buffer), so `yih`, `dih`, `vih ...` operate on the hunk under
+-- the cursor, and remapping the entry replaces the default. This spec presses
+-- the literal default sequence, inspects the installed mappings, and repeats
+-- the mapping-scope checks for a user remap of the documented entry.
+
+local view = require("codediff.ui.view")
+local config = require("codediff.config")
+local highlights = require("codediff.ui.highlights")
+local lifecycle = require("codediff.ui.lifecycle")
+
+describe("Hunk Textobject", function()
+  local left_path, right_path, outside_bufnr
+  local user_ih_mapping_installed = false
+
+  local function open_default_view()
+    view.create({
+      mode = "standalone",
+      git_root = nil,
+      original_path = left_path,
+      modified_path = right_path,
+      original_revision = nil,
+      modified_revision = nil,
+    })
+  end
+
+  -- Look up a buffer-local mapping for lhs in the given mode.
+  local function buffer_mapping(bufnr, mode, lhs)
+    for _, map in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_keymap(bufnr, mode)) do
+      if map.lhs == lhs then
+        return map
+      end
+    end
+    return nil
+  end
+
+  -- Look up a global (non buffer-local) mapping for lhs in the given mode.
+  local function global_mapping(mode, lhs)
+    for _, map in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_get_keymap(mode)) do
+      if map.lhs == lhs then
+        return map
+      end
+    end
+    return nil
+  end
+
+  -- The configured textobject key must be mapped buffer-locally in both
+  -- side-by-side diff buffers, in operator-pending and Visual modes, so it can
+  -- serve as a textobject (typed as an operator motion or from Visual mode),
+  -- and the binding must not leak into other buffers or a global mapping.
+  local function assert_textobject_scope(session, lhs)
+    local original_bufnr = vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(session.original_win)
+    local modified_bufnr = vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(session.modified_win)
+    assert.are_not.equal(original_bufnr, modified_bufnr, "The diff view should use two distinct buffers")
+
+    for _, bufnr in ipairs({ original_bufnr, modified_bufnr }) do
+      for _, mode in ipairs({ "o", "x" }) do
+        assert.is_not_nil(
+          buffer_mapping(bufnr, mode, lhs),
+          ("%s should be mapped in %s mode in diff buffer %d"):format(lhs, mode, bufnr)
+        )
+      end
+    end
+
+    for _, mode in ipairs({ "o", "x" }) do
+      assert.is_nil(
+        global_mapping(mode, lhs),
+        ("%s must be buffer-local, not a global %s-mode mapping"):format(lhs, mode)
+      )
+    end
+
+    -- Use a buffer that was created before the diff view. This catches
+    -- implementations that accidentally install the mapping on all existing
+    -- buffers when setting up the view.
+    assert.is_not_nil(outside_bufnr, "An outside buffer should exist before view setup")
+    for _, mode in ipairs({ "o", "x", "n" }) do
+      assert.is_nil(
+        buffer_mapping(outside_bufnr, mode, lhs),
+        ("%s must not leak into buffers outside the diff view"):format(lhs)
+      )
+    end
+  end
+
+  local function assert_no_textobject_behavior(bufnr, lhs)
+    local before = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false)
+    local sentinel = "outside buffer register"
+    vim.api.nvim_buf_call(bufnr, function()
+      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 1, 0 })
+      vim.fn.setreg("a", sentinel)
+      vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('"ay' .. lhs, "x!", false)
+    end)
+    assert.are.equal(sentinel, vim.fn.getreg("a"), "An outside buffer must not invoke the hunk textobject")
+    assert.are.same(before, vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false))
+  end
+
+  before_each(function()
+    highlights.setup()
+
+    -- Reset the configuration to the shipped defaults between cases so a
+    -- remap case cannot leak into the default-binding cases.
+    config.options = vim.deepcopy(config.defaults)
+
+    -- One replacement hunk, one deletion hunk, one insertion hunk.
+    -- original: line 1 / OLD 2 / OLD 3 / line 4 / line 5 / OLD 6 / line 7 / line 8
+    -- modified: line 1 / NEW 2 / NEW 3 / line 4 / line 5 / line 7 / NEW AFTER 7 / line 8
+    local original_lines = { "line 1", "OLD 2", "OLD 3", "line 4", "line 5", "OLD 6", "line 7", "line 8" }
+    local modified_lines = { "line 1", "NEW 2", "NEW 3", "line 4", "line 5", "line 7", "NEW AFTER 7", "line 8" }
+
+    left_path = vim.fn.tempname() .. "_left.txt"
+    right_path = vim.fn.tempname() .. "_right.txt"
+    vim.fn.writefile(original_lines, left_path)
+    vim.fn.writefile(modified_lines, right_path)
+
+    -- Create this buffer before the view so both binding and behavior checks
+    -- cover a pre-existing non-diff buffer.
+    outside_bufnr = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
+    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(outside_bufnr, 0, -1, false, { "outside line" })
+
+    -- No keymap option is touched here: the view must install the textobject
+    -- with its out-of-the-box default binding. The remap case below changes
+    -- the documented member before reopening the view.
+    open_default_view()
+  end)
+
+  after_each(function()
+    while vim.fn.tabpagenr("$") > 1 do
+      pcall(vim.cmd, "tabclose!")
+    end
+    if user_ih_mapping_installed then
+      pcall(vim.keymap.del, "o", "ih")
+      pcall(vim.keymap.del, "x", "ih")
+      user_ih_mapping_installed = false
+    end
+    if outside_bufnr and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(outside_bufnr) then
+      pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_delete, outside_bufnr, { force = true })
+    end
+    if left_path then
+      vim.fn.delete(left_path)
+    end
+    if right_path then
+      vim.fn.delete(right_path)
+    end
+    left_path, right_path, outside_bufnr = nil, nil, nil
+  end)
+
+  -- Helper: wait for the session and its stored diff result.
+  local function get_session()
+    local tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+    local session
+    vim.wait(3000, function()
+      session = lifecycle.get_session(tabpage)
+      return session
+        and session.stored_diff_result
+        and session.stored_diff_result.changes
+        and #session.stored_diff_result.changes > 0
+    end)
+    assert.is_not_nil(session, "Session should exist")
+    assert.is_not_nil(session.stored_diff_result, "Diff result should exist")
+    return session
+  end
+
+  local function focus_window(win)
+    assert.is_not_nil(win, "Window handle should exist")
+    assert.is_true(vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win), "Window should be valid")
+    vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(win)
+  end
+
+  local function yanked_lines(reg)
+    return vim.split(vim.fn.getreg(reg), "\n", { trimempty = true })
+  end
+
+  -- Check behavior rather than requiring that an old lhs be absent. A user
+  -- may legitimately keep unrelated mappings with the old lhs after the
+  -- plugin's configured textobject key is remapped.
+  local function assert_old_textobject_is_replaced(session, lhs)
+    -- Operator-pending invocation must not select the hunk on either side.
+    for _, win in ipairs({ session.original_win, session.modified_win }) do
+      focus_window(win)
+      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 2, 0 })
+      local sentinel = "user mapping was not replaced"
+      vim.fn.setreg("a", sentinel)
+      vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('"ay' .. lhs, "x!", false)
+      assert.are.equal(sentinel, vim.fn.getreg("a"), "The old key must not invoke the plugin textobject after remapping")
+      assert.are_not.same({ "NEW 2", "NEW 3" }, yanked_lines("a"), "The old key must not yank the hunk after remapping")
+    end
+
+    -- An unrelated user mapping may own the old Visual lhs. Either that user
+    -- action or an untouched Visual selection is permitted, but stale plugin
+    -- behavior must not select the hunk.
+    for _, win in ipairs({ session.original_win, session.modified_win }) do
+      focus_window(win)
+      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 2, 0 })
+      vim.api.nvim_feedkeys("v", "x!", false)
+      local visual_start = vim.fn.getpos("v")
+      local visual_cursor = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)
+      local sentinel = "user visual mapping was not replaced"
+      vim.fn.setreg("a", sentinel)
+      vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(lhs, "x!", false)
+      local mode = vim.fn.mode()
+      assert.is_true(mode == "n" or mode == "v", "The old Visual key must not enter a hunk selection")
+      assert.are.equal(sentinel, vim.fn.getreg("a"), "The old Visual key must not yank the hunk")
+      if mode == "v" then
+        assert.are.same(visual_start, vim.fn.getpos("v"), "The old Visual key must preserve the selection start")
+        assert.are.same(visual_cursor, vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0), "The old Visual key must preserve the selection cursor")
+        vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(vim.keycode("<Esc>"), "x!", false)
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  it("installs the default ih binding buffer-locally in both diff buffers", function()
+    -- The documented configuration entry ships with the ih default.
+    assert.are.equal(
+      "ih",
+      config.defaults.keymaps.view.hunk_textobject,
+      "keymaps.view.hunk_textobject should ship with the ih default"
+    )
+
+    local session = get_session()
+    assert_textobject_scope(session, "ih")
+    assert_no_textobject_behavior(outside_bufnr, "ih")
+
+    -- The default binding is reachable from Visual mode too.
+    focus_window(session.original_win)
+    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 6, 0 })
+    vim.fn.setreg("a", "")
+    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('vih"ay', "x!", false)
+    assert.are.same({ "OLD 6" }, yanked_lines("a"), "ih should select the hunk from Visual mode")
+    assert.are.equal("V", vim.fn.getregtype("a"), "Visual ih should yank the deleted hunk linewise")
+  end)
+
+  it("yih yanks a multi-line replacement hunk from its last changed line on both sides of the diff", function()
+    local session = get_session()
+
+    -- The cursor sits on the second (noninitial) changed line of the hunk:
+    -- the hunk under the cursor must still be the full line range.
+    focus_window(session.original_win)
+    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 3, 0 })
+    vim.fn.setreg("a", "")
+    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('"ayih', "x!", false)
+    assert.are.same(
+      { "OLD 2", "OLD 3" },
+      yanked_lines("a"),
+      "yih should yank the whole hunk from a noninitial changed line on the original side"
+    )
+    assert.are.equal("V", vim.fn.getregtype("a"), "Original-side yih should be linewise")
+
+    focus_window(session.modified_win)
+    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 3, 0 })
+    vim.fn.setreg("a", "")
+    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('"ayih', "x!", false)
+    assert.are.same(
+      { "NEW 2", "NEW 3" },
+      yanked_lines("a"),
+      "yih should yank the whole hunk from a noninitial changed line on the modified side"
+    )
+  end)
+
+  it("vih selects a replacement hunk linewise on the original side", function()
+    local session = get_session()
+    focus_window(session.original_win)
+    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 2, 0 })
+    vim.fn.setreg("a", "")
+    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('vih"ay', "x!", false)
+    assert.are.equal("V", vim.fn.getregtype("a"), "Visual ih should yank linewise on the original side")
+    assert.are.same({ "OLD 2", "OLD 3" }, yanked_lines("a"), "Visual ih should select exactly the original replacement hunk")
+  end)
+
+  it("yih yanks a deleted hunk on the original side", function()
+    local session = get_session()
+    focus_window(session.original_win)
+
+    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 6, 0 })
+    vim.fn.setreg("a", "")
+    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('"ayih', "x!", false)
+

problem_statement: Bug: 3-way merge fails to include non-conflicting adjacent insertions in Result buffer When performing a 3-way merge, codediff fails to correctly populate the Result buffer if both OURS and THEIRS have different but non-overlapping additions within the same code block (e.g., a list of require statements). Instead of merging them or marking specific lines, it often leaves the Result buffer with only the common base, effectively "dropping" the new code from both sides. Screenshots Problem in codediff Correct behavior in diffview: ### Additional contract requirements ## Scope This addendum clarifies the observable behavior of the merge **Result buffer** -- the buffer the merge UI populates as the editable result of a 3-way merge when a file is in the unmerged (conflicted) state, where OURS has one set of changes relative to BASE and THEIRS has another. ## Result-buffer requirements When both OURS and THEIRS add different content at different, non-overlapping positions relative to BASE (the scenario described in the bug report): 1. **No silently dropped additions.** The Result buffer must not be seeded with only the common BASE content. Every addition produced by either branch that does not overlap a change made by the other branch must be present in the Result buffer. 2. **Exact-once preservation.** Each such added line appears in the Result buffer exactly once, with its exact content. 3. **Base-relative ordering.** Each addition appears in the Result buffer between the same BASE lines that surrounded the position at which the branch added it. All BASE lines that neither branch changed (including BASE lines lying between two branches' additions) are preserved, in their original BASE order, at their original positions relative to the merged additions. 4. **Branch symmetry.** The merged result is independent of which branch (OURS or THEIRS) contributed a given addition and of where the additions are located within the file (adjacent positions inside one code block, reordered positions, or positions separated by unchanged BASE lines). ## Representation requirements - The Result buffer must never display raw on-disk conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`). - This addendum defines the observable Result-buffer outcome only for the non-overlapping additions scenario above. It specifies no required representation for regions where both branches changed the same BASE content differently (true overlapping conflicts), whose presentation is implementation-defined beyond the stated bug fix.

Instead of merging them or marking specific lines, it often leaves the Result buffer with only the common base, effectively "dropping" the new code from both sides. contract_addendum:
## Scope

This addendum clarifies the observable behavior of the merge **Result
buffer** -- the buffer the merge UI populates as the editable result of a
3-way merge when a file is in the unmerged (conflicted) state, where OURS has
one set of changes relative to BASE and THEIRS has another.

## Result-buffer requirements

When both OURS and THEIRS add different content at different, non-overlapping
positions relative to BASE (the scenario described in the bug report):

1. **No silently dropped additions.** The Result buffer must not be seeded
   with only the common BASE content. Every addition produced by either
   branch that does not overlap a change made by the other branch must be
   present in the Result buffer.

2. **Exact-once preservation.** Each such added line appears in the Result
   buffer exactly once, with its exact content.

3. **Base-relative ordering.** Each addition appears in the Result buffer
   between the same BASE lines that surrounded the position at which the
   branch added it. All BASE lines that neither branch changed (including
   BASE lines lying between two branches' additions) are preserved, in their
   original BASE order, at their original positions relative to the merged
   additions.

4. **Branch symmetry.** The merged result is independent of which branch
   (OURS or THEIRS) contributed a given addition and of where the additions
   are located within the file (adjacent positions inside one code block,
   reordered positions, or positions separated by unchanged BASE lines).

## Representation requirements

- The Result buffer must never display raw on-disk conflict markers
  (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`).

- This addendum defines the observable Result-buffer outcome only for the
  non-overlapping additions scenario above. It specifies no required
  representation for regions where both branches changed the same BASE
  content differently (true overlapping conflicts), whose presentation is
  implementation-defined beyond the stated bug fix.

+--- Compute the auto-merged Result buffer content.
+--- Ports VSCode's MergeEditorModel.computeAutoMergedResult().
+--- For each base-range group:
+---   * only input1 changed -> take input1 lines
+---   * only input2 changed -> take input2 lines
+---   * both changed identically -> take input1 lines
+---   * both changed differently (conflict) -> keep base lines (user resolves)
+--- Lines outside any group are copied straight from base.
+---
+--- Also returns conflict_blocks with `result_range` (1-based, inclusive start /
+--- exclusive end) marking where each unresolved conflict lives in the merged
+--- buffer, so extmark tracking can anchor to merged-content line numbers
+--- instead of pure-base line numbers.
+---
+--- @param base_to_input1_diff table { changes = {...} }
+--- @param base_to_input2_diff table { changes = {...} }
+--- @param base_lines string[]
+--- @param input1_lines string[]
+--- @param input2_lines string[]
+--- @return string[] merged_lines, table[] conflict_blocks
+function M.compute_auto_merged_result(base_to_input1_diff, base_to_input2_diff, base_lines, input1_lines, input2_lines)
+  local mapping_alignments = compute_mapping_alignments(base_to_input1_diff.changes, base_to_input2_diff.changes)
+
+  local result_lines = {}
+  local conflict_blocks = {}
+
+  local function append_range(source, start_line, end_line_exclusive)
+    for i = start_line, end_line_exclusive - 1 do
+      table.insert(result_lines, source[i] or "")
+    end
+  end
+
+  local function ranges_equal_content(s1, r1, s2, r2)
+    local len1 = r1.end_line - r1.start_line
+    local len2 = r2.end_line - r2.start_line
+    if len1 ~= len2 then
+      return false
+    end
+    for i = 0, len1 - 1 do
+      if (s1[r1.start_line + i] or "") ~= (s2[r2.start_line + i] or "") then
+        return false
+      end
+    end
+    return true
+  end
+
+  local base_cursor = 1 -- 1-based line index into base_lines, inclusive
+
+  for _, ma in ipairs(mapping_alignments) do
+    -- Copy unchanged base lines preceding this group.
+    append_range(base_lines, base_cursor, ma.base_range.start_line)
+    base_cursor = ma.base_range.end_line
+
+    local has1 = ma.has_input1
+    local has2 = ma.has_input2
+
+    if has1 and not has2 then
+      append_range(input1_lines, ma.output1_range.start_line, ma.output1_range.end_line)
+    elseif has2 and not has1 then
+      append_range(input2_lines, ma.output2_range.start_line, ma.output2_range.end_line)
+    elseif has1 and has2 and ranges_equal_content(input1_lines, ma.output1_range, input2_lines, ma.output2_range) then
+      -- Both sides made the identical change -> not a conflict, apply once.
+      append_range(input1_lines, ma.output1_range.start_line, ma.output1_range.end_line)
+    else
+      -- True conflict: keep base, leave for the user to resolve.
+      local conflict_start = #result_lines + 1
+      append_range(base_lines, ma.base_range.start_line, ma.base_range.end_line)
+      local conflict_end_exclusive = #result_lines + 1
+      table.insert(conflict_blocks, {
+        base_range = ma.base_range,
+        output1_range = ma.output1_range,
+        output2_range = ma.output2_range,
+        inner1 = ma.inner1,
+        inner2 = ma.inner2,
+        result_range = { start_line = conflict_start, end_line = conflict_end_exclusive },
+      })
+    end
+  end
+
+  -- Copy any remaining base lines after the last group.
+  append_range(base_lines, base_cursor, #base_lines + 1)
+
+  return result_lines, conflict_blocks
+end
+
 return M

diff --git a/tests/ui/conflict/issue_353_spec.lua b/tests/ui/conflict/issue_353_spec.lua
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..53ceba4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/ui/conflict/issue_353_spec.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,347 @@
+-- Regression test for https://github.com/esmuellert/codediff.nvim/issues/353
+-- "3-way merge fails to include non-conflicting adjacent insertions in Result buffer"
+--
+-- Integration-level: builds the on-disk state a conflicted merge leaves
+-- behind (three unmerged index stages plus a marker-bearing working-tree
+-- file -- the trigger the conflict view keys on), drives the public conflict
+-- Result-window setup, and asserts on the exact ordered lines the user is
+-- actually shown in the merge Result buffer (" Result" pane).
+
+local h = require('tests.helpers')
+local view = require('codediff.ui.view')
+local lifecycle = require('codediff.ui.lifecycle')
+local config = require('codediff.config')
+
+local assert = require('luassert')
+
+-- Open the merge Result view through the plugin's supported merge-view entry
+-- path: the same `view.create` call the `:CodeDiff merge <file>` command
+-- issues for a conflicted file (THEIRS in the left pane, OURS in the right
+-- pane, conflict mode on). Everything the spec asserts on -- the Result
+-- buffer the user is shown -- is produced by this flow.
+local function open_merge_result(repo, rel_path)
+  local ours_position = config.options.diff.conflict_ours_position or 'right'
+  local original_rev = ours_position == 'right' and ':3' or ':2'
+  local modified_rev = ours_position == 'right' and ':2' or ':3'
+
+  local ready = false
+  view.create({
+    mode = 'standalone',
+    git_root = repo.dir,
+    original_path = rel_path,
+    modified_path = rel_path,
+    original_revision = original_rev,
+    modified_revision = modified_rev,
+    conflict = true,
+  }, 'lua', function()
+    ready = true
+  end)
+
+  local ok = vim.wait(10000, function()
+    return ready
+  end, 50)
+  assert.is_true(ok, 'merge view must finish opening within the timeout')
+
+  local tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+  assert.is_not_nil(lifecycle.get_session(tabpage), 'a merge session must be registered')
+
+  local result_bufnr = lifecycle.get_result(tabpage)
+  assert.is_not_nil(result_bufnr, 'a Result buffer must exist')
+  local result_lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(result_bufnr, 0, -1, false)
+
+  return {
+    tabpage = tabpage,
+    result_bufnr = result_bufnr,
+    result_lines = result_lines,
+    result_text = table.concat(result_lines, '\n'),
+  }
+end
+
+local function cleanup_view(view)
+  pcall(vim.api.nvim_set_current_tabpage, view.tabpage)
+  local wins = vim.api.nvim_tabpage_list_wins(view.tabpage)
+  for i = 2, #wins do
+    pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, wins[i], true)
+  end
+  for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
+    if vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) and vim.fn.bufwinid(buf) == -1 then
+      pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_delete, buf, { force = true })
+    end
+  end
+end
+
+-- Put the repository into the on-disk state a conflicted merge produces for
+-- `rel_path`: the index carries the three unmerged stages (:1 base, :2 ours,
+-- :3 theirs) and the working-tree file contains `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>`
+-- conflict markers (supplied as `worktree_lines`). Returns the marker-bearing
+-- working-tree text.
+local function setup_merge_conflict(repo, rel_path, base_lines, ours_lines, theirs_lines, worktree_lines)
+  -- Sanity: the fixture really looks like a conflicted merge output.
+  local worktree_text = table.concat(worktree_lines, '\n')
+  local saw_start, saw_sep, saw_end = false, false, false
+  for _, line in ipairs(worktree_lines) do
+    saw_start = saw_start or line:match('^<<<<<<<') ~= nil
+    saw_sep = saw_sep or line:match('^=======') ~= nil
+    saw_end = saw_end or line:match('^>>>>>>>') ~= nil
+  end
+  assert.is_true(saw_start and saw_sep and saw_end,
+    'working-tree fixture must contain conflict markers:\n' .. worktree_text)
+
+  local tmp = h.create_temp_dir()
+  local function stage(content_lines)
+    local path = tmp .. '/stage.txt'
+    vim.fn.writefile(content_lines, path)
+    return vim.trim(repo.git('hash-object -w ' .. vim.fn.shellescape(path)))
+  end
+  local base_blob = stage(base_lines)
+  local ours_blob = stage(ours_lines)
+  local theirs_blob = stage(theirs_lines)
+  vim.fn.delete(tmp, 'rf')
+
+  local index_info = string.format(
+    '100644 %s 1\t%s\n100644 %s 2\t%s\n100644 %s 3\t%s\n',
+    base_blob, rel_path, ours_blob, rel_path, theirs_blob, rel_path
+  )
+  vim.fn.system({ 'git', '-C', repo.dir, 'update-index', '--index-info' }, index_info)
+  assert.equal(0, vim.v.shell_error, 'update-index must register the unmerged stages')
+  repo.write_file(rel_path, worktree_lines)
+
+  -- Sanity guards: the index really is the post-merge unmerged state.
+  for _, spec in ipairs({
+    { ':1:' .. rel_path, base_lines, 'BASE' },
+    { ':2:' .. rel_path, ours_lines, 'OURS' },
+    { ':3:' .. rel_path, theirs_lines, 'THEIRS' },
+  }) do
+    local content, rc = repo.git('show ' .. spec[1])
+    assert.equal(0, rc, 'stage ' .. spec[1] .. ' must exist in the index')
+    assert.equal(table.concat(spec[2], '\n'), vim.trim(content),
+      'stage ' .. spec[1] .. ' must hold ' .. spec[3])
+  end
+  return worktree_text
+end
+
+local function assert_no_raw_conflict_markers(text)
+  -- The merge tool's Result pane must never surface raw on-disk conflict markers.
+  for _, marker in ipairs({ '<<<<<<<', '=======', '>>>>>>>' }) do
+    assert.is_true(text:find(marker, 1, true) == nil,

problem_statement:
Add keymap to cycle through hunks across all files
Hey, great work on this plugin.

Just like you can do this in vim with the quickfix list, it would be awesome to be able to cycle through all hunks across all files when in diff mode.

If I'm not mistaken, currently available keymaps are:
- cycle through hunks in a given file
- cycle through files

This is a suggestion to add:
- cycle through hunks across all files

This would avoid users having to `]h` `]h` `]h` `]f` (switch file) `]h` `]h` `]f` (switch again) `]h` etc.

Keep up the great work,

Cheers

### Additional contract requirements

The built-in diff view provides hunk-navigation mappings: by default `]c`
moves to the next hunk and `[c` moves to the previous hunk (these keys are the
default values of the configurable hunk-navigation mappings and may be
rebound).

When the diff view shows multiple files (i.e. a file list is present), hunk
navigation continues across files:

- Cross-file cycling is enabled by default; no opt-in is required.
- Enabled (default): pressing the next-hunk key while on the last hunk of the
  current file switches the view to the next file in the list and places the
  cursor on that file's first hunk. Pressing the previous-hunk key while on
  the first hunk switches to the previous file in the list and places the
  cursor on that file's last hunk. The cursor is placed on the line the user
  sees in the focused pane (e.g. the modified-side line when the modified
  pane is focused).
- The feature can be disabled through the documented diff-view configuration
  (setting the cross-file hunk-cycling option to `false`, for example via
  `require("codediff").setup({ diff = { cycle_hunks_across_files = false } })`).
  When disabled, the hunk-navigation keys keep their previous behavior at the
  first/last hunk and operate only within the current file.
- This boundary behavior applies in each supported diff layout (side-by-side
  and inline).
- After a cross-file hop, ordinary hunk navigation continues normally from the
  landing hunk (for example, the next next-hunk press advances to the
  following hunk within the newly displayed file).

+local function hop_to_adjacent_file(direction)
+  local tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+  local panel_obj = lifecycle.get_explorer(tabpage)
+  if not panel_obj then
+    -- Cross-file cycling only makes sense in explorer/history mode.
+    return false
+  end
+
+  local session = lifecycle.get_session(tabpage)
+  if session then
+    -- "next" â land on first hunk of the next file (the natural forward walk)
+    -- "prev" â land on last hunk of the previous file (the natural backward walk)
+    session.pending_cursor_landing = direction == "next" and "first" or "last"
+  end
+
+  if direction == "next" then
+    return M.next_file()
+  else
+    return M.prev_file()
+  end

@@ -0,0 +1,670 @@
+-- Regression test for https://github.com/esmuellert/codediff.nvim/issues/161
+-- Cross-file hunk cycling: pressing the next-hunk key (]c by default) while
+-- on the last hunk of the current file jumps to the FIRST hunk of the next
+-- file in the explorer/history list; pressing the previous-hunk key ([c by
+-- default) on the first hunk jumps to the LAST hunk of the previous file.
+-- The feature is ON by default and can be turned off via
+-- `require("codediff").setup({ diff = { cycle_hunks_across_files = false } })`,
+-- in which case the hunk keys keep their legacy within-file behavior.
+-- These tests exercise the public contract only: the real keymaps, the
+-- documented configuration option, and observable explorer/cursor state.
+
+local h = require("tests.helpers")
+
+describe("cycle_hunks_across_files (#161)", function()
+  local repo
+  local lifecycle, config
+
+  before_each(function()
+    h.ensure_plugin_loaded()
+    -- setup() merges user config over the current options table, so reset to
+    -- pristine defaults first to undo any config set by earlier tests.
+    local cfg = require("codediff.config")
+    cfg.options = vim.deepcopy(cfg.defaults)
+

+      local win = session and session[pane .. "_win"]

problem_statement:
Tint added/deleted single-file views
When selecting an entirely added, untracked, or deleted file, CodeDiff shows it as a single-file view with no diff highlighting.

Iâd like the file contents to be visually marked as a change:
- added / untracked files: green line tint
- deleted files: red line tint

This would make it clearer that the whole file is new or deleted, rather than just an ordinary opened file.

### Additional contract requirements

Supplementary observable requirements for this task:

- Whole-file tinting of added, untracked, and deleted files is controlled by the boolean configuration option `diff.highlight_added_deleted_files`.
  - The option defaults to `false`. With the default configuration, no whole-file tinting occurs.
  - Setting the option to `true` enables whole-file tinting for added, untracked, and deleted single-file views.
- Tint mapping:
  - Added and untracked files use the same green insert tint used for inserted diff lines.
  - Deleted files use the same red delete tint used for deleted diff lines.
  - The tint covers every line of the file, including the end-of-line region.
- Regardless of file length, the whole-file tint is rendered as a single buffer-wide decoration (including for empty files and very large files, e.g. 10,000 lines).
- For virtual buffers that are populated asynchronously, the tint is applied before content arrives and must expand automatically to cover the content once it loads.
- When adding the whole-file tint, any previously applied diff decorations in the buffer's highlight and filler namespaces are cleared first; removing or re-applying the tint likewise leaves no stale decorations.
- Lifecycle behavior:
  - Suspending the diff removes the whole-file tint; resuming restores it.
  - The whole-file tint is re-applied after the displayed file is edited (auto-refresh).
  - A regular two-sided diff session carries no single-file tint state.
  - Switching from a single-file view back to a diff view removes the single-file tint and restores normal diff highlighting.
- With the option disabled, both single-file view styles (side-by-side and inline layouts) show added, untracked, and deleted files without any whole-file tint, while all other aspects of the single-file view (single-pane layout, file content, and empty diff state) remain unchanged. This remains true when a single-file view is suspended, its displayed content is edited, and the view is resumed: the edited content is preserved and the diff state remains empty.

+-- ============================================================================
+-- Whole File Rendering
+-- ============================================================================
+
+--- Render a one-sided file with highlighting across all logical lines.
+---@param bufnr number
+---@param side "original"|"modified"
+function M.render_whole_file(bufnr, side)
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(bufnr, ns_highlight, 0, -1)
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(bufnr, ns_filler, 0, -1)
+
+  if not config.options.diff.highlight_added_deleted_files then
+    return
+  end
+
+  local highlight_groups = {
+    original = "CodeDiffLineDelete",
+    modified = "CodeDiffLineInsert",
+  }
+  local hl_group = highlight_groups[side]
+  if not hl_group then
+    error("Invalid whole-file diff side: " .. tostring(side))
+  end
+
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(bufnr, ns_highlight, 0, 0, {
+    end_row = vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(bufnr),
+    end_col = 0,
+    hl_group = hl_group,
+    hl_eol = true,
+    priority = config.options.diff.highlight_priority,
+    right_gravity = false,
+    end_right_gravity = true,
+  })
+end

+    for _, mark in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_extmarks(bufnr, ns_id, 0, -1, { details = true })) do
+      local details = mark[4]
+      local insert_or_delete = details
+        and (details.hl_group == "CodeDiffLineInsert" or details.hl_group == "CodeDiffLineDelete")
+      local whole_file_range = mark[2] == 0 and details.hl_eol
+        and (details.end_row == line_count or details.end_row == 0)
+      if insert_or_delete and whole_file_range then
+        table.insert(marks, mark)
+      end
+    end
+  end
+  return marks
+end

+local function assert_pending_whole_file_highlight(bufnr, expected_group)
+  -- Before virtual contents arrive, only the presence and side/color of the

problem_statement:
Hook hints are mutable through the pipeline, violating spec 4.5.3 - migrate metrics hook to HookData and freeze hints before 1.0
## Summary
Hook hints are mutable through the pipeline: `before` returns `Option[(EvaluationContext, HookHints)]` and the returned hints are threaded into subsequent hooks and all later stages. Spec Â§4.5.3: "the hook MUST NOT alter the hook hints structure"; Â§4.2.2.1: hints must be immutable in languages that can express it. `HookData` (Â§4.6) is the designated channel for per-hook state.

## Evidence
- `core/src/main/scala/zio/openfeature/Hook.scala:130` â `before` signature returns updated hints.
- `Hook.scala:159-170` â `FeatureHook.compose` threads returned hints onward; `FeatureFlagsLive.scala:233-237` passes them to all later stages.
- `Hook.scala:344-347` â built-in `FeatureHook.metrics` writes its start-time into hints (while `structuredLogging`/`metricsDetailed` already use `HookData` correctly).
- `conformance-zio-bdd/.../ConformanceSpec.scala:32-33` excludes `@immutability` scenarios claiming immutability is "compile-time guaranteed" â not true for hints.

## Proposed fix
Change `before` to return `Option[EvaluationContext]`; migrate `FeatureHook.metrics` to `HookData` (mirroring `metricsDetailed`). Breaking API change â worth doing before a 1.0 final. Re-enable the `@immutability` conformance scenarios afterwards.

### Additional contract requirements

## Behavioral contract addendum

- `FeatureHook.before` returns `UIO[Option[EvaluationContext]]`: a `before` hook may modify the evaluation context, but it has no way to return or replace hook hints. Hook hints are the same value for every hook and for every subsequent stage of an evaluation (spec §4.5.3, §4.2.2.1).
- Per-hook mutable state must travel through `HookContext.hookData` (spec §4.6), scoped to the hook instance for that evaluation. The built-in `FeatureHook.metrics` hook stores its start time in its own `HookData` and never writes it into the hook hints; two co-installed `metrics` hook instances therefore measure independent durations for the same evaluation.
- A `before` hook's evaluation-context modification is still propagated to the provider evaluation and to all later hooks/stages.
- The change to `FeatureHook.before` is breaking: every pre-existing in-repo test source that declared a `before` override must continue to compile against the new signature (a stale override with the previous tuple-based return type must not compile).

+  * This spec never overrides `FeatureHook.before` with either signature: the hook signature differs between the two
+  * API revisions, so an anonymous `new FeatureHook { override def before ... }` literal would fail to compile on one
+  * of them. Instead it builds hooks reflectively through a `java.lang.reflect.Proxy` (which dispatches by parameter
+  * types, not by the differing return type) and drives a normal flag evaluation, asserting the observable pipeline
+  * behaviour. Every assertion is expressed against base-stable types and fails on the unfixed API.
+  */
+object HookHintsImmutabilitySpec extends ZIOSpecDefault {
+
+  /** True when the runtime `FeatureHook.before` still returns hints (the unfixed `Option[(ctx, hints)]` shape). */
+  private def beforeReturnsHints: Boolean =
+    classOf[FeatureHook].getMethod("before", classOf[HookContext], classOf[HookHints]).toGenericString.contains("Tuple2")
+
+  /** Builds a `before` result shaped for the runtime `before` signature: on the fixed API (`Option[ctx]`) the hint
+    * half is ignored and only `Some(ctx)` is returned; on the unfixed API (`Option[(ctx, hints)]`) the full
+    * `Some((ctx, hints))` is returned (and the unfixed pipeline threads those hints onward). This keeps the hook
+    * defect-free on either API while letting the observable hint behaviour diverge.
+    */
+  private def resultForShape(ctx: EvaluationContext, hints: => HookHints): AnyRef =
+    if (beforeReturnsHints) ZIO.succeed(Some((ctx, hints))) else ZIO.succeed(Some(ctx))
+
+  private def contextResult(ctx: EvaluationContext, hints: HookHints): AnyRef =
+    resultForShape(ctx, hints)
+
+  /** Builds a `FeatureHook` reflectively. `dispatch` maps a stage name to a base-stable effect; `Object` methods are
+    * handled here so `FeatureHook.compose`'s per-hook `HookData` map (keyed by hook identity) works on proxies. */
+  private def hook(name: String)(dispatch: PartialFunction[String, Array[AnyRef] => AnyRef]): FeatureHook = {
+    val fallback: String => Array[AnyRef] => AnyRef = {
+      case "supportedFlagTypes" => _ => FlagValueType.allTypes
+      case _                    => _ => ZIO.unit
+    }
+    val stage = dispatch
+    val handler = new InvocationHandler {
+      override def invoke(proxy: AnyRef, m: Method, args: Array[AnyRef]): AnyRef = {
+        val a = if (args == null) Array.empty[AnyRef] else args
+        m.getName match {
+          case "toString"   => name
+          case "hashCode"   => Int.box(java.lang.System.identityHashCode(proxy))
+          case "equals"     => Boolean.box(proxy.asInstanceOf[AnyRef] eq a(0))
+          case n if stage.isDefinedAt(n) => stage(n)(a)
+          case n            => fallback(n)(a)
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    Proxy.newProxyInstance(getClass.getClassLoader, Array(classOf[FeatureHook]), handler).asInstanceOf[FeatureHook]
+  }
+
+  /** A provider that always resolves the boolean `value` (after an optional delay used by the metrics test). */
+  private final class StaticBooleanProvider(value: Boolean, evalDelayMillis: Long = 0L) extends EventProvider {
+    @scala.annotation.nowarn("msg=deprecated")
+    override def getMetadata: Metadata                      = new Metadata { override def getName: String = "Static" }
+    override def getState: ProviderState                    = ProviderState.READY
+    override def initialize(ctx: OFEvaluationContext): Unit = ()
+    override def shutdown(): Unit                           = ()
+    override def getBooleanEvaluation(k: String, d: java.lang.Boolean, c: OFEvaluationContext)
+      : ProviderEvaluation[java.lang.Boolean] = {
+      if (evalDelayMillis > 0) Thread.sleep(evalDelayMillis)
+      ProviderEvaluations.of[java.lang.Boolean](value, "STATIC")
+    }
+    override def getStringEvaluation(k: String, d: String, c: OFEvaluationContext): ProviderEvaluation[String] =
+      ProviderEvaluations.of[String](d, "DEFAULT")
+    override def getIntegerEvaluation(k: String, d: java.lang.Integer, c: OFEvaluationContext)
+      : ProviderEvaluation[java.lang.Integer] =
+      ProviderEvaluations.of[java.lang.Integer](d, "DEFAULT")
+    override def getDoubleEvaluation(k: String, d: java.lang.Double, c: OFEvaluationContext)
+      : ProviderEvaluation[java.lang.Double] =
+      ProviderEvaluations.of[java.lang.Double](d, "DEFAULT")
+    override def getObjectEvaluation(k: String, d: Value, c: OFEvaluationContext): ProviderEvaluation[Value] =
+      ProviderEvaluations.of[Value](d, "DEFAULT")
+  }
+
+  private def buildFF(hooks: List[FeatureHook], evalDelayMillis: Long = 0L): ZIO[Scope, Throwable, FeatureFlags] = {
+    val api = OpenFeatureAPIFactory.create()
+    FeatureFlags.build(
+      new StaticBooleanProvider(true, evalDelayMillis),
+      domain = Some(s"hook-hints-${java.util.UUID.randomUUID()}"),
+      version = None,
+      initialHooks = hooks,
+      statusRef = None,
+      addShutdownFinalizer = true,
+      apiOverride = Some(api),
+      evaluationTimeout = Some(5.seconds)
+    )
+  }
+
+  def spec = suite("HookHintsImmutabilitySpec")(
+
+    test("a before hook cannot alter the hook hints observed by a later hook (spec Â§4.5.3)") {
+      // Reflect on the declared return type: this spec is compiled once and must run against both API revisions, and
+      // the difference between them is only visible in `before`'s generic signature.
+      val returnsTuple = beforeReturnsHints
+      for {
+        hintsFrozen <- ZIO.attempt(!returnsTuple).mapError(e => new RuntimeException("reflection failed", e))
+        behavioral <- ZIO.unless(returnsTuple) {
+                        // A first hook that (on the unfixed signature) rewrites the hints in `before`.
+                        val first = hook("first") { case "before" => a =>
+                          val ctx   = a(0).asInstanceOf[HookContext]
+                          val hints = a(1).asInstanceOf[HookHints]
+                          resultForShape(ctx.evaluationContext, hints + ("polluted" -> true))
+                        }
+                        val secondSawPolluted = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean(false)
+                        val second = hook("second") { case "before" => a =>
+                          val hints = a(1).asInstanceOf[HookHints]
+                          secondSawPolluted.set(hints.get[Boolean]("polluted").contains(true))
+                          ZIO.none
+                        }
+                        ZIO.scoped {
+                          for {
+                            ff <- buildFF(List(first, second))
+                            _  <- ff.boolean("flag", default = false)
+                          } yield assertTrue(!secondSawPolluted.get)
+                        }
+                      }
+      } yield
+        // unfixed API: `before` still returns hints, so the hints are not frozen - behavioural failure.
+        if (returnsTuple) assertTrue(hintsFrozen)
+        else behavioral.getOrElse(assertTrue(true))
+    },
+
+    test("every stage of an evaluation observes the identical hook hints value (spec Â§4.2.2.1)") {

+      // evaluation each keep `before` neutral here, so any implementation - old or new - must present the
+      // same hint value to the earlier hook's `before`, the later hook's `before`, and the `after` stage.
+      val beforeSeen = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference[Option[HookHints]](None)
+      val afterSeen  = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference[Option[HookHints]](None)
+      val first = hook("invariant-first") { case "before" => a =>
+        ZIO.succeed { beforeSeen.set(Some(a(1).asInstanceOf[HookHints])) }.as(None)
+      }
+      val second = hook("invariant-second") {
+        case "before" => a =>
+          ZIO.succeed {

+            if (Some(a(1).asInstanceOf[HookHints]) != beforeSeen.get()) beforeSeen.set(None)

+          ZIO.succeed { afterSeen.set(Some(a(2).asInstanceOf[HookHints])) }

+    },

+    test("the built-in metrics hook keeps its start time in HookData, leaving the hints untouched (spec Â§4.6)") {

+      val observer = hook("observer") {

+      }
+      ZIO.scoped {
+        for {
+          metrics <- ZIO.attempt(FeatureHook.metrics { (_, dur, _) =>
+                       ZIO.succeed(recordedDuration.set(Some(dur))).unit
+                     })
+          // 60 ms of provider latency between the metrics hook's `before` and `after`: a measured duration of at least
+          // 40 ms proves the start time was genuinely captured in this hook's own `HookData` (a broken capture falls
+          // back to `after`'s `end`, giving a ~zero duration).
+          ff <- buildFF(List(metrics, observer), evalDelayMillis = 60L)
+          _  <- ff.boolean("flag", default = false)
+        } yield {
+          // Structural evidence, not a timing window, that the start time lives in per-hook HookData and never
+          // leaks into the hints: a later hook must observe the exact invariant hint map, with no metric
+          // start-time key injected by the built-in metrics hook.
+          val observedBefore = hintsSeenByObserver.get()
+          assertTrue(
+            observedClean.get,                              // metrics left the hints untouched for the later hook
+            observedBefore != null && observedBefore.isEmpty, // the observer saw the exact pristine initial hints
+            recordedDuration.get().exists(_ >= 40.millis)   // and still measured a real duration via HookData
+          )
+        }
+      }
+    },
+
+    test("two concurrent metrics hooks keep independent HookData, so each observes its own start time") {
+      // Two distinct metrics hook instances stacked around a flagged provider evaluation. Each must
+      // record a distinct duration through its own per-hook HookData; a shared-state implementation
+      // either cross-writes the start time or leaves the outer hook with no start time at all.
+      val d1Set = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference[Option[Duration]](None)
+      val d2Set = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference[Option[Duration]](None)
+      ZIO.scoped {
+        for {
+          m1 <- ZIO.attempt(FeatureHook.metrics { (_, dur, _) =>
+                  ZIO.succeed(d1Set.set(Some(dur))).unit
+                })
+          m2 <- ZIO.attempt(FeatureHook.metrics { (_, dur, _) =>
+                  ZIO.succeed(d2Set.set(Some(dur))).unit
+                })
+          ff <- buildFF(List(m1, m2), evalDelayMillis = 60L)
+          _  <- ff.boolean("flag", default = false)
+        } yield {
+          val d1 = d1Set.get()
+          val d2 = d2Set.get()
+          // Both instances must have captured genuinely positive durations: a cross-written or missing
+          // per-hook start time makes one measurement collapse to ~zero.
+          assertTrue(
+            d1.exists(_.toNanos > 0L),
+            d2.exists(_.toNanos > 0L)
+          ) &&

+          // start time. A leaked/shared start time would let one hook overwrite the other's, making
+          // one measured duration collapse towards zero.
+          assertTrue(
+            d1.exists(_ >= 40.millis),
+            d2.exists(_ >= 40.millis)
+          )
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  ) @@ sequential @@ withLiveClock
+}

+++ b/project/test-support/run_hook_spec.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Runs the hidden-test gates through the normal sbt test task against the CURRENT checkout's `core` module:
+#
+#   * zio.openfeature.HookHintsImmutabilitySpec - the graded fix-detection suite (spec §4.5.3/§4.6).
+#   * zio.openfeature.HookContractAnchorSpec    - a broad, argument-independent regression anchor over the
+#     hook contract (hint/HookData data structures, no-op hook stages, compose ordering and flag-type
+#     filtering, full stage routing through a live evaluation, and the public FeatureFlags surface).
+#
+# The sbt test-configuration compile is itself part of the contract gate: any candidate that ships
+# the new `FeatureHook.before` API (returning `UIO[Option[EvaluationContext]]`) but leaves a
+# pre-existing core test source overriding `before` with the stale tuple-based return type fails to
+# compile here, so an incomplete migration cannot pass. On the pre-fix checkout the migrated sources
+# fail that same compile, so the pre-fix checkout reports a failing run with no named tests, while
+# HookHintsImmutabilitySpec's reflective API-shape assertions add named per-test failures whenever the
+# configuration does compile; any candidate that changes the new API but introduces an unrelated
+# hook-pipeline regression fails the argument-independent anchor suite.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+sbt -batch -no-colors "core / Test / testOnly zio.openfeature.HookHintsImmutabilitySpec zio.openfeature.HookContractAnchorSpec"
+STATUS=$?
+echo "REBENCH_TEST_EXIT=$STATUS"
+exit "$STATUS"

problem_statement:
Retry engine build if it fails with dependency error
## Description 

If the engine build is interrupted (or is a local release and the dependencies have been updated) the next time it builds/loads it will fail. 

At this point it requires manual intervention. 

Instead, we should run it again with force: true (MIX_INSTALL_FORCE=1).

### Additional contract requirements

When engine preparation fails with a recognized Mix dependency error (output containing "Unchecked dependencies" or "Can't continue due to errors on dependencies"), preparation is retried exactly once in forced mode; the initial attempt is not forced. Forced mode is observable either as a forced-install flag on the preparation command or as the forced-install environment variable MIX_INSTALL_FORCE=1 being set for the retried preparation process.

A successful forced retry continues normal engine initialization, proceeding to start the engine node. If the retried preparation fails again with a recognized dependency error, preparation stops after that single retry and reports an error. A preparation failure that is not a recognized dependency error is not retried.

diff --git a/apps/expert/lib/expert/engine_node/builder.ex b/apps/expert/lib/expert/engine_node/builder.ex
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..8e08d1a2c
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,221 @@
+defmodule Expert.EngineNode.Builder do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Builds the engine node for a project.
+  """
+  alias Forge.Project
+  require Logger
+
+  use GenServer
+
+  defmodule State do
+    defstruct [:project, :last_line, :from, :port, :mix_home, attempts: 0]
+  end
+
+  @max_attempts 1
+
+  def build_engine(project) do
+    with {:ok, pid} <- start_link(project) do
+      GenServer.call(pid, :build, :infinity)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def start_link(project) do
+    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, project)
+  end
+
+  @impl GenServer
+  def init(project) do
+    {:ok, %State{project: project, last_line: ""}}
+  end
+
+  @impl GenServer
+  def handle_call(:build, from, state) do
+    state =
+      case start_build(state.project, from) do
+        {:ok, port} ->
+          %State{state | port: port}
+
+        _ ->
+          state
+      end
+
+    {:noreply, %State{state | from: from}}
+  end
+
+  @impl GenServer
+  def handle_info({_port, {:data, "mix_home:" <> mix_home}}, state) do
+    mix_home = String.trim(mix_home)
+    {:noreply, %State{state | mix_home: mix_home}}
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({_port, {:data, "engine_path:" <> engine_path}}, state) do
+    engine_path = String.trim(engine_path)
+    Logger.info("Engine build available at: #{engine_path}", project: state.project)
+
+    Logger.info("ebin paths:\n#{inspect(ebin_paths(engine_path), pretty: true)}",
+      project: state.project
+    )
+
+    GenServer.reply(state.from, {:ok, {ebin_paths(engine_path), state.mix_home}})
+    {:stop, :normal, state}
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({_port, {:data, data}}, state) do
+    line = to_string(data)
+    Logger.debug("Engine build output: #{line}", project: state.project)
+
+    if detect_deps_error(line) do
+      if state.attempts < @max_attempts do
+        Logger.warning(
+          "Detected dependency errors during engine build, retrying... (attempt #{state.attempts + 1}/#{@max_attempts})",
+          project: state.project
+        )
+
+        close_port(state.port)
+
+        state =
+          case start_build(state.project, state.from, force: true) do
+            {:ok, port} ->
+              %State{state | port: port}
+
+            _ ->
+              state
+          end
+
+        {:noreply, %State{state | attempts: state.attempts + 1}}
+      else
+        Logger.error("Maximum build attempts reached. Failing the build.", project: state.project)
+
+        GenServer.reply(
+          state.from,
+          {:error, "Build failed due to dependency errors after #{@max_attempts} attempts", line}
+        )
+
+        {:stop, :normal, state}
+      end
+    else
+      {:noreply, %State{state | last_line: line}}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({_port, {:exit_status, 0}}, state) do
+    {:noreply, state}
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({_port, {:exit_status, status}}, state) do
+    Logger.error("Engine build script exited with status: #{status}", project: state.project)
+
+    GenServer.reply(
+      state.from,
+      {:error, "Build script exited with status: #{status}", state.last_line}
+    )
+
+    {:stop, :normal, state}
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({:EXIT, port, reason}, %State{port: port} = state) when reason != :normal do
+    Logger.error("Engine build script exited with reason: #{inspect(reason)}",
+      project: state.project
+    )
+
+    GenServer.reply(state.from, {:error, reason, state.last_line})
+    {:stop, :normal, state}
+  end
+
+  def handle_info({:EXIT, _port, _reason}, state) do
+    {:noreply, state}
+  end
+
+  if Mix.env() == :test do
+    # In test environment, Expert depends on the Engine app, so we look for it
+    # in the expert build path.
+    @excluded_apps [:patch, :nimble_parsec]
+    @allowed_apps [:engine | Mix.Project.deps_apps()] -- @excluded_apps
+
+    def start_build(_, from, _ \\ []) do
+      entries =
+        [Mix.Project.build_path(), "**/ebin"]
+        |> Forge.Path.glob()
+        |> Enum.filter(fn entry ->
+          Enum.any?(@allowed_apps, &String.contains?(entry, to_string(&1)))
+        end)
+
+      GenServer.reply(from, {:ok, {entries, nil}})
+    end
+
+    def close_port(_port), do: :ok
+  else
+    # In dev and prod environments, the engine source code is included in the
+    # Expert release, and we build it on the fly for the project elixir+opt
+    # versions if it was not built yet.
+    defp start_build(%Project{} = project, from, opts \\ []) do
+      with {:ok, elixir, env} <- Expert.Port.project_executable(project, "elixir"),
+           {:ok, erl, _env} <- Expert.Port.project_executable(project, "erl") do
+        Logger.info("Using path: #{System.get_env("PATH")}", project: project)
+        Logger.info("Found elixir executable at #{elixir}", project: project)
+        Logger.info("Found erl executable at #{erl}", project: project)
+
+        port = launch_engine_builder(project, elixir, env, opts)
+        {:ok, port}
+      else
+        {:error, name, message} = error ->
+          Logger.error(message, project: project)
+          GenServer.reply(from, {:error, message})
+          Expert.terminate("Failed to find an #{name} executable, shutting down", 1)
+          error
+      end
+    end
+
+    defp close_port(port), do: Port.close(port)
+  end
+
+  def launch_engine_builder(project, elixir, env, opts \\ []) do
+    expert_priv = :code.priv_dir(:expert)
+    packaged_engine_source = Path.join([expert_priv, "engine_source", "apps", "engine"])
+
+    engine_source =
+      "EXPERT_ENGINE_PATH"
+      |> System.get_env(packaged_engine_source)
+      |> Path.expand()
+
+    build_engine_script = Path.join(expert_priv, "build_engine.exs")
+
+    args = [
+      build_engine_script,
+      "--source-path",
+      engine_source,
+      "--vsn",
+      Expert.vsn()
+    ]
+
+    args =
+      if opts[:force] do
+        args ++ ["--force"]
+      else
+        args
+      end
+
+    Logger.info("Preparing engine", project: project)
+
+    Process.flag(:trap_exit, true)
+
+    env = [{"MIX_ENV", "dev"} | env]
+
+    Expert.Port.open_elixir_with_env(elixir, env,
+      args: args,
+      cd: Project.root_path(project)
+    )
+  end
+
+  defp ebin_paths(base_path) do
+    Forge.Path.glob([base_path, "lib/**/ebin"])
+  end
+
+  @deps_error_patterns [
+    "Can't continue due to errors on dependencies",
+    "Unchecked dependencies"
+  ]
+  defp detect_deps_error(message) when is_binary(message) do
+    Enum.any?(@deps_error_patterns, &String.contains?(message, &1))
+  end
+end

+defmodule Expert.EngineNode.BuilderTest do
+  alias Expert.EngineNode
+  alias Expert.EngineSupervisor
+
+  import Forge.Test.Fixtures
+
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  setup_all do
+    original_mix_env = Mix.env()
+
+    source_files = Path.wildcard("lib/**/*.ex") |> Enum.sort()
+
+    modules =
+      source_files
+      |> Enum.flat_map(fn source ->
+        source
+        |> File.read!()
+        |> Code.string_to_quoted!()
+        |> defined_modules()
+      end)
+      |> Enum.uniq()
+
+    original_code =
+      Map.new(modules, fn module ->
+        {module, :code.get_object_code(module)}
+      end)
+
+    Mix.env(:dev)
+    Enum.each(source_files, &Code.compile_file/1)
+    Mix.env(original_mix_env)
+
+    on_exit(fn ->
+      Mix.env(original_mix_env)
+
+      Enum.each(Enum.reverse(modules), fn module ->
+        :code.purge(module)
+        :code.delete(module)
+
+        case original_code[module] do
+          {^module, binary, filename} -> :code.load_binary(module, filename, binary)
+          :error -> :ok
+        end
+      end)
+    end)
+
+    :ok
+  end
+
+  setup do
+    project = project()
+    tmp_dir = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "expert-engine-build-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
+    bin_dir = Path.join(tmp_dir, "bin")
+    launch_log = Path.join(tmp_dir, "launch.log")
+    File.mkdir_p!(bin_dir)
+
+    fake_elixir = Path.expand("test/support/executables/fake_engine_elixir.sh")
+
+    for executable <- ["elixir", "erl"] do
+      destination = Path.join(bin_dir, executable)
+      File.cp!(fake_elixir, destination)
+      File.chmod!(destination, 0o755)
+    end
+
+    original_environment =
+      Map.new(["PATH", "SHELL", "FAKE_ENGINE_SCENARIO", "FAKE_ENGINE_LAUNCH_LOG"], fn key ->
+        {key, System.get_env(key)}
+      end)
+
+    System.put_env("PATH", bin_dir <> ":" <> original_environment["PATH"])
+    System.delete_env("SHELL")
+    System.put_env("FAKE_ENGINE_LAUNCH_LOG", launch_log)
+
+    start_supervised!(Expert.ActiveProjects)
+    start_supervised!({Forge.NodePortMapper, []})
+    start_supervised!({EngineSupervisor, project})
+
+    on_exit(fn ->
+      Enum.each(original_environment, fn
+        {key, nil} -> System.delete_env(key)
+        {key, value} -> System.put_env(key, value)
+      end)
+
+      File.rm_rf!(tmp_dir)
+    end)
+
+    {:ok, project: project, launch_log: launch_log}
+  end
+
+  test "retries engine preparation once in forced mode after a dependency error", context do
+    System.put_env("FAKE_ENGINE_SCENARIO", "retry_succeeds")
+
+    start_engine(context.project)
+
+    assert [initial, retry, startup] = launches(context.launch_log)
+    refute forced?(initial)
+    assert forced?(retry)
+    assert startup?(startup)
+  end
+
+  test "reports an engine preparation error after the forced retry also has dependency errors",
+       context do
+    System.put_env("FAKE_ENGINE_SCENARIO", "dependency_error")
+
+    result = start_engine(context.project)
+
+    assert error_result?(result)
+    assert [initial, retry] = launches(context.launch_log)
+    refute forced?(initial)
+    assert forced?(retry)
+  end
+
+  test "does not retry when preparation fails without a dependency error", context do
+    System.put_env("FAKE_ENGINE_SCENARIO", "ordinary_error")
+
+    result = start_engine(context.project)
+
+    assert error_result?(result)
+    assert [initial] = launches(context.launch_log)
+    refute forced?(initial)
+  end
+
+  defp start_engine(project) do
+    try do
+      EngineNode.start(project)
+    catch
+      :exit, reason -> {:exit, reason}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp error_result?(result) do
+    is_tuple(result) and tuple_size(result) > 1 and elem(result, 0) == :error
+  end
+
+  defp launches(log_path) do
+    log_path
+    |> File.read!()
+    |> String.split("\n", trim: true)
+  end
+
+  defp forced?(launch) do
+    String.contains?(launch, "--force") or String.contains?(launch, "MIX_INSTALL_FORCE=1")
+  end
+
+  defp startup?(launch), do: String.contains?(launch, "--cookie")
+
+  defp defined_modules({:defmodule, _, [{:__aliases__, _, parts}, [do: body]]}) do
+    module = Module.concat(parts)
+    [module | defined_modules(body, module)]
+  end
+
+  defp defined_modules(ast), do: defined_modules(ast, nil)
+
+  defp defined_modules({:defmodule, _, [{:__aliases__, _, parts}, [do: body]]}, parent) do
+    module = if parent, do: Module.concat([parent | parts]), else: Module.concat(parts)
+    [module | defined_modules(body, module)]
+  end
+
+  defp defined_modules({_, _, arguments}, parent) when is_list(arguments) do
+    Enum.flat_map(arguments, &defined_modules(&1, parent))
+  end
+
+  defp defined_modules(arguments, parent) when is_list(arguments) do
+    Enum.flat_map(arguments, &defined_modules(&1, parent))
+  end
+
+  defp defined_modules(_, _), do: []
+end

problem_statement:
[Bug] Auto-closures are not forwarded correctly
### Swift Version

6.0

### Package Version

0.2.2

### Bug Description

If a mocked protocol has a method with an auto-closure parameter, the compiler throws an error: `Add () to forward '@autoclosure' parameter`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```swift
@Mocked
protocol Playground {
    func method(closure: @escaping @autoclosure () -> Int)
}
```

### Expected Behavior

The mock should compile without any errors.

### Actual Behavior

The compiler throws an error: `Add () to forward '@autoclosure' parameter`.

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

### Additional contract requirements

## Autoclosure Parameter Support

Mocked methods with parameters whose types are `@autoclosure` closures must be
supported. For a protocol annotated with `@Mocked`, the generated mock must
compile without errors when any of the protocol's methods declares an
`@autoclosure` parameter. This must hold for all autoclosure effect
combinations, specifically:

- A synchronous, non-throwing autoclosure.
- An `async` autoclosure (including on `async` methods).
- A `throws` autoclosure (including on `throws` methods).
- An `async throws` autoclosure (including on `async throws` methods).

For each of these combinations, both autoclosure closures returning `Void` and
autoclosure closures returning a non-`Void` value must be supported.

When a method with an `@autoclosure` parameter is invoked on the generated mock:

- The invocation must be usable exactly as the protocol declares; callers pass
  an expression of the autoclosure's result type (for example, an `Int` literal
  for an `@autoclosure () -> Int` parameter).
- The invocation must be recorded: after one call, the method's backing
  invocation record must have a call count of one and exactly one recorded
  invocation, consistent with how other recorded mock invocations behave.
- For methods without a throwing signature, the call must complete normally.
  For `throws` and `async throws` methods, the call must not rethrow an error
  when no error is expected.

problem_statement:
refactor: remove HttpsError and migrate entirely to HttpResponseException
Removes custom `HttpsError` and `FunctionsErrorCode` hierarchy in `lib/src/https/error.dart`, migrating internal auth/validation errors and callable/HTTPS error handling completely to `HttpResponseException` (`badRequest`,
  `unauthorized`, `notFound`, etc.) from `package:google_cloud_shelf`.

### Additional contract requirements

This task removes the legacy custom error hierarchy (`HttpsError`, `FunctionsErrorCode`, and its per-code subclasses) in favor of `HttpResponseException` from `package:google_cloud_shelf`. The following observable behavior is required after the migration:

## Public API surface

- The legacy error types (`HttpsError`, `FunctionsErrorCode`, `InvalidArgumentError`, `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `UnauthenticatedError`, `FailedPreconditionError`, `AlreadyExistsError`, `InternalError`, `ResourceExhaustedError`, `UnimplementedError`, `UnavailableError`, `DeadlineExceededError`, `CancelledError`, and any other per-code error subclasses that were previously public) are no longer defined in or exported from the package's public libraries.
- The package's public `firebase_functions.dart` library re-exports the `HttpResponseException` symbol from `package:google_cloud_shelf` so that function authors can import and use it from the main library. This includes statuses that never had a legacy per-code subtype (for example 503 `serviceUnavailable` and 504 `gatewayTimeout`).
- All documentation, samples, and example servers shipped with the package remain buildable using only supported public symbols.

## Exception constructors and status tokens

When a handler throws an `HttpResponseException` (for example via its named constructors such as `badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, or `internalServerError`), the client receives a response whose HTTP status code equals the exception's status code.

The JSON error body (where produced) has the shape `{"error": {"code": <int>, "status": <string>, "message": <string>}}`. `code` equals the exception's integer HTTP status code, and `message` equals the exception message. The `status` value is the exception's attached status token (see below), or `INTERNAL` when a generic internal error is produced for an unexpected failure.

The shared named constructors accept an optional status token override so that function authors can attach the token their client contract requires (for example a 400 `badRequest` may carry `FAILED_PRECONDITION` instead of the 400 default). When no override is given, the default status token that the shared named constructors attach to an exception (and therefore the observable default association between an HTTP status code and its status token) is:

- 400 → `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (created by `badRequest`)
- 401 → `UNAUTHENTICATED` (created by `unauthorized`)
- 403 → `PERMISSION_DENIED` (created by `forbidden`)
- 404 → `NOT_FOUND` (created by `notFound`)
- 409 → `ALREADY_EXISTS` (created by `conflict`)
- 429 → `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (created by `tooManyRequests`)
- 500 → `INTERNAL` (created by `internalServerError`, and used whenever an unexpected non-HTTP exception is converted into an error response)
- 501 → `UNIMPLEMENTED` (created by `notImplemented`)
- 503 → `UNAVAILABLE` (created by `serviceUnavailable`)
- 504 → `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` (created by `gatewayTimeout`)

## Response content negotiation and message safety

When the incoming request accepts JSON (`Accept: application/json`), error responses for `HttpResponseException` failures carry the `application/json` media type and the JSON error body described above. When the request does not accept JSON, `HttpResponseException` failures surface as a plain-text response. That text body carries the same status code and the exception message, and — when the exception was created with an explicit status token — the same token that the JSON error body would report; no client information is dropped by falling back to plain text.

Unexpected, non-HTTP exceptions always surface as HTTP 500 with status `INTERNAL`. The generic message contract below is intentionally literal-agnostic: implementations may choose any wording, and conformance must never be judged against one specific message string (for example neither "Internal Server Error" nor "An unexpected error occurred." is required). Their response bodies use only a generic internal-server-error message: the message must be present and must be sanitized and non-leaking, so original exception text, stack traces, and other internal details are never exposed to the client. Handler code, including headless `onRequest` functions, must rely on the request-handling pipeline that is placed in front of registered handlers to convert thrown exceptions into the responses described above, so the same response shapes apply to every request handler.

- Non-streaming callable invocations that fail with an `HttpResponseException` return the exception's HTTP status code and the JSON error body (with `code`, `status`, and `message` fields) when the request accepts JSON.

Unexpected errors in streams are reported with code `500`, status `INTERNAL`, and a non-empty generic message that does not expose internal details; the exact message text is not fixed.
- Existing callable request validations are unchanged: requests must use the POST method and an `application/json` content type, otherwise they are rejected with HTTP 400. When the response is JSON, the status token is the default one associated with 400 above.

## Identity (auth-blocking) functions

- Identity blocking functions (before-create, before-sign-in, and related triggers) validate their own input and signal failures with an `HttpResponseException`. An unsupported HTTP method or a non-JSON content type, a body that is not decodable JSON, a body that does not carry the required token field, or a token value that is not structurally decodable as a blocking token is rejected as invalid input with an HTTP 400 response.
- When the request is accepted, the user handler runs through the same error pipeline described above, so throwing an `HttpResponseException` from a user handler yields the exception's status code and the `code`/`status`/`message` JSON error shape when the request accepts JSON.

[in_app_purchase] Update to Google Play Billing Library 8.x
### Use case

Hi,
I’m using the in_app_purchase Flutter plugin in my app "Helty Home", currently published on the Google Play Store.

Today I received a critical message from the Google Play Console informing me that my app is using a deprecated version of the Google Play Billing Library, and that I need to update to version 7.0.0 or later before August 31, 2025 to continue publishing updates.

"Your app is using a version of Google Play Billing Library that will be deprecated soon. Starting August 31, 2025, all apps must use version 7.0.0 or later."
"We recommend upgrading to version 8 to benefit from the latest monetization features."

Can you please confirm if the plugin is planning to support Billing Library v7 or v8 soon?
If there's an existing issue or plan to migrate, I’d appreciate a link or estimated timeline so we can plan accordingly.

Thanks a lot for your work!



### Proposal

Upgrade in android billing client to v8 (build.gradle) "implementation"

### Additional contract requirements

# Additional contract for the `in_app_purchase_android` migration to Google Play Billing Library 8

The Android implementation side of `in_app_purchase_android` must be upgraded to Google Play
Billing Library 8.0.0 and adapted to its API changes. In addition to upgrading the dependency,
an implementation must satisfy all of the following observable behaviors:

## Product details queries

- Queries for product details complete through Billing Library 8 result-based callback
  contract: native code must consume the product-details callback result object
  (`QueryProductDetailsResult`, providing `getProductDetailsList()` and
  `getUnfetchedProductList()`) instead of the removed raw product-details list form.
- Both the platform-level product-details response (the platform-channel/Pigeon message) and
  the public `ProductDetailsResponseWrapper` include a product-details list and an unfetched
  product list. When the query results contain products that could not be fetched, the
  unfetched product list carries one entry per unfetched product, preserving each entry's
  product ID, from the native callback through translation and the platform bridge up to the
  Dart wrapper exposed in `ProductDetailsResponseWrapper.unfetchedProductList` as a list of
  `UnfetchedProductWrapper` values. Each `UnfetchedProductWrapper` exposes the product ID of
  the product that could not be fetched.
- `ProductDetailsWrapper` exposes `oneTimePurchaseOfferDetailsList` (a list of
  `OneTimePurchaseOfferDetailsWrapper`, or `null`) with the full set of one-time purchase
  offers for in-app products that have multiple buy options, complementing the existing
  single `oneTimePurchaseOfferDetails`, and the data survives the native-to-Dart
  serialization (in the platform-level product details as
  a `List<PlatformOneTimePurchaseOfferDetails>`).
- `BillingResultWrapper` and the platform-level billing result include a `subResponseCode`
  field (an `int` in Dart) reporting the Billing Library 8 sub-response code returned with a
  billing result; it is available on billing results surfaced from billing calls and
  defaults to `0`, which indicates that no other sub-response code applies.

## Removal of purchase history querying

- Querying purchase history is removed along with the underlying Billing Library API that was
  removed in Billing Library 7.0.0: `BillingClientWrapper` no longer exposes
  `queryPurchaseHistory`, and the platform interface no longer supports querying purchase
  history. Users who previously relied on it are directed to use `queryPurchases` instead.

## Compatibility

- All previously existing in-app purchase and subscription functionality — connecting to the
  billing client, querying product details, querying purchases, launching the billing flow,
  consuming purchases, acknowledging purchases, and pending purchases support — continues to
  behave as before the upgrade.

problem_statement:
[pigeon] Add support for sharing constants across platforms
### Use case

Pigeon is great for generating type-safe enums and model classes, but when I tried using it, I found I wanted to also put constants in my pigeons to be shared with native code.

Example use case:
For android_hardware_smoke_test (root issue https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/182123 ), I have a suite of integration tests which I want to run as both flutter driver tests in dart, and as Android Instrumented tests in kotlin. There are a few strings and test timeout constants which I would like to share between the dart and kotlin test scripts.

### Proposal

 It would be nice if I could define constants in my pigeons/messages.dart file and have them appear in the files generated by `pub run pigeon`.

### Additional contract requirements

Top-level constants in a Pigeon input file are supported under the
following observable contract:

- A shareable constant is a top-level `const` variable declaration with
  an explicit type annotation of `String`, `int`,
  `double`, or `bool`, initialized by a literal of the matching type.
  Integer and double literals may be negative, and an integer literal
  may initialize a `double` constant. An adjacent string literal (for
  example `'hello ' 'world'`) is a valid string value with the
  concatenated contents.

- Any of the following top-level constant declarations are rejected:
  a declaration whose declared type is not one of the four supported
  types, a declaration whose initializer is not a plain literal of the
  declared type (including arbitrary expressions and string
  interpolations), and a declaration that lacks an explicit type
  annotation. Rejection is observable as a reported error in parsing or
  a failed code-generation run, or both.

- When a target language output is requested (`--dart_out`,
  `--java_out`, `--kotlin_out`, `--swift_out`,
  `--objc_header_out`/`--objc_source_out`,
  `--cpp_header_out`/`--cpp_source_out`, or
  `--gobject_header_out`/`--gobject_source_out`), the generated code
  declares each constant in a form that is valid source in the target
  language, under a name equivalent to the Dart declaration (camelCase
  converted to the target's naming convention, including any language-
  or option-specific prefixing), with a value equal to the Dart value.
  The declared boolean values `true` and `false` are distinct: a `false`
  constant must be emitted as a false boolean value in every target.

- Generated string literals preserve the logical contents of the Dart
  value, including quotes, backslashes, dollar signs, and newlines,
  escaped or delimited as required by the target language. The generated
  representation is otherwise unconstrained: either quoting style,
  string literal prefixes (such as raw or extended-delimiter strings),
  visibility and storage modifiers (including non-const or final
  declarations where the target language gives them constant value
  semantics), whitespace, declaration placement, header/source
  placement for the C-family targets, constant naming prefixes,
  numeric suffixes, and language-specific boolean spellings
  are all valid.
