+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Accumulator-channel variation engine.
+#
+# A binding may document one fixed accumulator-channel shape instead of
+# accepting every documented channel (the parallel name/init/update lists, a
+# name -> (init, update) mapping, a sequence of (name, init, update) records,
+# or a mapping of per-name {"init": ..., "update": ...} records). The probing
+# helper invokes the entry point with the shape its signature advertises; the
+# engine below additionally retries with the channel re-expressed through
+# each other documented shape, so an adapter-rigid but documented binding
+# reaches its documented behavior instead of failing on invocation mechanics.
+# The original invocation is always tried first, so a flexible binding is
+# invoked exactly once; the first accepted invocation is the one observed.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ACCUMULATOR_CHANNEL_PREDICATES = []  # populated below
+
+
+def _is_plain_string_list(value) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, list) and (
+        not value or all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)
+    )
+
+
+def _is_parallel_lists(value) -> bool:
+    return (
+        isinstance(value, list)
+        and len(value) == 3
+        and all(isinstance(step, list) for step in value)
+        and all(len(step) == len(value[0]) for step in value)
+        and _is_plain_string_list(value[0])
+    )
+
+
+def _is_name_tuple_triple_list(value) -> bool:
+    return (
+        isinstance(value, list)
+        and all(
+            isinstance(record, tuple)
+            and len(record) == 3
+            and isinstance(record[0], str)
+            for record in value
+        )
+        and len(value) > 0
+    )
+
+
+def _is_name_init_update_mapping(value) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, dict) and all(
+        isinstance(name, str)
+        and isinstance(record, tuple)
+        and len(record) == 2
+        for name, record in value.items()
+    )
+
+
+def _is_structured_mapping(value) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(value, dict) and all(
+        isinstance(name, str)
+        and isinstance(record, dict)
+        and set(record) == {"init", "update"}
+        for name, record in value.items()
+    )
+
+
+def _channel_kind(value):
+    """Recognized probe-side accumulator channel shapes, else None."""
+    if _is_parallel_lists(value):
+        return "parallel"
+    if _is_name_tuple_triple_list(value):
+        return "records"
+    if _is_name_init_update_mapping(value):
+        return "mapping"
+    if _is_structured_mapping(value):
+        return "structured"
+    return None
+
+
+def _channel_sequence_from(kind, value):
+    """(name, init, update) records of a recognized channel shape."""
+    if kind == "parallel":
+        names, inits, updates = value
+        return list(zip(names, inits, updates))
+    if kind == "records":
+        return list(value)
+    if kind == "mapping":
+        return [(name, init, update) for name, (init, update) in value.items()]
+    if kind == "structured":
+        return [
+            (name, record["init"], record["update"])
+            for name, record in value.items()
+        ]
+    return []
+
+
+def _channel_value_of(shape, sequence):
+    sequence = list(sequence)
+    if shape == "parallel":
+        return [
+            [name for name, _init, _update in sequence],
+            [init for _name, init, _update in sequence],
+            [update for _name, _init, update in sequence],
+        ]
+    if shape == "records":
+        return [(name, init, update) for name, init, update in sequence]
+    if shape == "mapping":
+        return {name: (init, update) for name, init, update in sequence}
+    if shape == "structured":
+        return {
+            name: {"init": init, "update": update}
+            for name, init, update in sequence
+        }
+    raise ValueError(f"unknown accumulator channel shape: {shape}")
+
+
+def _parallel_triples(container):
+    """Identity-linked (names, inits, updates) triples within a value."""
+    triples = []
+    items = (
+        list(enumerate(container))
+        if isinstance(container, list)
+        else list(container.items())
+    )
+    sequenced = [value for _key, value in items]
+    for offset in range(len(items) - 2):
+        (first_key, first), (second_key, second), (third_key, third) = items[
+            offset : offset + 3
+        ]
+        if (
+            _is_plain_string_list(first)
+            and isinstance(second, list)
+            and isinstance(third, list)
+            and len(first) == len(second) == len(third)
+            and (not first or isinstance(first[0], str))
+            and not _is_name_tuple_triple_list(first)
+        ):
+            triples.append(
+                (
+                    (first_key, first),
+                    (second_key, second),
+                    (third_key, third),
+                )
+            )
+    for key, value in items:
+        if isinstance(value, (list, dict)):
+            triples.extend(_parallel_triples(value))
+    return triples
+
+
+def _accumulator_variations(args, kwargs):
+    """Candidate invocations with the accumulator channel in each shape.
+
+    Yields ``(positional, keyword)`` pairs ordered so the recorded original
+    invocation comes first; every later candidate re-expresses one recognized
+    channel value (or one identity-linked parallel triple) through a
+    different documented shape, leaving every non-accumulator argument
+    untouched.
+    """
+    base = (list(args), dict(kwargs))
+    seen = set()
+
+    def key(arguments):
+        positional, keyword = arguments
+        return repr((positional, sorted(keyword.items())))
+
+    seen.add(key(base))
+    yield base
+
+    channels = []  # (container, key, kind, value)
+    for container, items in (
+        (base[0], list(enumerate(base[0]))),
+        (base[1], list(base[1].items())),
+    ):
+        for item_key, value in items:
+            kind = _channel_kind(value)
+            if kind is not None:
+                channels.append((container, item_key, kind, value))
+
+    for triple in _parallel_triples(base[0]) + _parallel_triples(base[1]):
+        container = base[0] if any(
+            key_value[1] is triple[0][1] for key_value in enumerate(base[0])
+        ) else base[1]
+        channels.append((container, triple, "parallel-triple", triple))
+
+    if not channels:
+        return
+
+    shapes = ("records", "parallel", "structured", "mapping")
+    for container, item_key, kind, value in channels:
+        sequence = (
+            _channel_sequence_from("parallel", [step for _k, step in value])
+            if kind == "parallel-triple"
+            else _channel_sequence_from(kind, value)
+        )
+        single_holder = (
+            container,
+            item_key if kind != "parallel-triple" else None,
+            None if kind != "parallel-triple" else value,
+        )
+        for shape in shapes:
+            replacement = _channel_value_of(shape, sequence)
+            candidate_positional = list(base[0])
+            candidate_kwargs = dict(base[1])
+            if kind == "parallel-triple":
+                (first_key, _first), (second_key, _second), (
+                    third_key,
+                    _third,
+                ) = item_key
+                if shape == "parallel":
+                    continue  # identical to the recorded delivery
+                # Collapse the triple into its first slot, in order.
+                if isinstance(first_key, str):
+                    # Keyword triple: keep the names slot, drop the siblings.
+                    for sibling_key in (second_key, third_key):
+                        candidate_kwargs.pop(sibling_key, None)
+                    candidate_kwargs[first_key] = replacement
+                else:
+                    ordered = sorted((first_key, second_key, third_key))
+                    first_index = ordered[0]
+                    candidate_positional[first_index] = replacement
+                    for index in sorted(ordered[1:], reverse=True):
+                        candidate_positional.pop(index)
+            else:
+                if shape == kind:
+                    continue
+                if shape == "parallel":
+                    expanded = replacement
+                    if isinstance(item_key, str):
+                        candidate_kwargs.pop(item_key, None)
+                        candidate_kwargs["accumulator_names"] = expanded[0]
+                        candidate_kwargs["accumulator_inits"] = expanded[1]
+                        candidate_kwargs["accumulator_updates"] = expanded[2]
+                    else:
+                        candidate_positional[item_key : item_key + 1] = expanded
+                else:
+                    if isinstance(item_key, str):
+                        candidate_kwargs[item_key] = replacement
+                    else:
+                        candidate_positional[item_key] = replacement
+            candidate = (candidate_positional, candidate_kwargs)
+            candidate_key = key(candidate)
+            if candidate_key in seen:
+                continue
+            seen.add(candidate_key)
+            yield candidate
+
+
+def _invoke_accumulator_variations(entry_point, args, kwargs):
+    """Invokes the entry point, retrying documented accumulator shapes.
+
+    The recorded invocation runs first; when the binding rejects a document
+    supplied channel shape with a plain ``TypeError`` (the invocation-shape
+    rejection Python raises before any documented behavior executes), which
+    candidates re-expressed through other documented channel shapes are
+    tried until one is accepted. The first accepted invocation is the one
+    whose behavior is observed, so a flexible binding is invoked exactly
+    once while a binding frozen into one documented channel shape still
+    reaches that behavior.
+    """
+    last_error: TypeError | None = None
+    for positional, keyword in _accumulator_variations(args, kwargs):
+        try:
+            return entry_point(*positional, **keyword)
+        except TypeError as error:
+            last_error = error
+    if last_error is not None:
+        raise last_error
+    return entry_point(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+def _bound_optional_roles(entry_point) -> set:
+    """Optional documented roles bound by the entry point's own wrapper.
+
+    A binding may declare an ``aggregate_neighbors`` entry point that already
+    fixes one or more documented optional roles (for example a partial that
+    always applies its documented loop-removal default before delegating):
+    the signature then no longer declares those roles, yet they are still
+    configured, so the configured-role probes must deliver the documented
+    value for them instead of leaving the wrapper's binding unchanged. A role
+    counts as bound when the signature declares no parameter for it: either
+    the role's name stems match nothing at all, or (for the distinguishable
+    checkpoint roles) the only stem-matching parameters already belong to
+    another documented role. Accumulator channels are never optional, and a
+    signature declaring only one half of the checkpoint pair (an interval
+    without any local-checkpoint toggle or vice versa) still accepts the
+    documented value for the missing half, because the pair jointly suffices
+    to configure the documented checkpointing behaviour.
+    """
+
+    def declared(name: str) -> bool:
+        try:
+            signature = inspect.signature(entry_point)
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            return True
+        if name in signature.parameters:
+            return True
+        try:
+            signature.bind(**{name: None})
+        except TypeError:
+            return False
+        return True
+
+    try:
+        signature = inspect.signature(entry_point)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return set()
+    bound: set = set()
+    checkpoint_pair = {"checkpoint_interval", "use_local_checkpoints"}
+    distinct = {
+        "starting_vertices": ("starting_vertices", "max_hops"),
+        "max_hops": ("starting_vertices", "max_hops"),
+        "stop_condition": ("stop_condition",),
+        "target_condition": ("target_condition",),
+        "edge_filter": ("edge_filter",),
+        "required_vertex_attributes": (
+            "required_vertex_attributes",
+            "required_edge_attributes",
+        ),
+        "required_edge_attributes": (
+            "required_vertex_attributes",
+            "required_edge_attributes",
+        ),
+        "remove_loops": ("remove_loops",),
+        "use_local_checkpoints": ("checkpoint_interval", "use_local_checkpoints"),
+        "checkpoint_interval": ("checkpoint_interval", "use_local_checkpoints"),
+        "storage_level": ("storage_level",),
+    }
+    for role in _ROLE_ORDER:
+        if role in checkpoint_pair:
+            # The checkpoint pair is resolved jointly below.
+            continue
+        groups = _ROLE_WORDS[role]
+        matching = [
+            name
+            for name in signature.parameters
+            if all(any(stem in name.lower() for stem in group) for group in groups)
+        ]
+        if not matching:
+            # No parameter spells the role at all: the wrapper pre binds it.
+            bound.add(role)
+            continue
+        group = distinct.get(role, (role,))
+        probe = next((other for other in group if other != role), role)
+        if declared(probe):
+            # A distinguishable sibling of the role's stem group is spelled
+            # out, so the role itself is declared even when its own
+            # canonical spelling is not.
+            continue
+        if not any(declared(name) for name in matching):
+            # Every spelling matching the role's own stems belongs to an
+            # already collapsed sibling role, so this role is pre bound too.
+            bound.add(role)
+    if not declared("checkpoint_interval") and not declared("use_local_checkpoints"):
+        # Neither half of the documented checkpoint behaviour is declarable:
+        # the wrapper pre binds both halves.
+        bound.add("checkpoint_interval")
+        bound.add("use_local_checkpoints")
+    return bound
+
+
+def _invoke_with_documented_roles(entry_point, roles, accumulators=None):
+    """Invokes the entry point honouring its own parameter spellings.
+
+    `roles` lists the documented roles whose values are delivered; accumulator
+    content is given either as one (name, init, update) tuple list (the
+    documented single-accumulator shape) or as parallel empty lists. Arguments
+    are forwarded through whichever channel the implementation's signature
+    advertises; unmatched but listed documented arguments are supplied
+    positionally in the documented role order, and `merge_role_parameters`
+    merges matched roles that the implementation collapsed into a single
+    parameter. Only the explicitly listed roles (and parameters that have no
+    default) receive a value, whether the binding is a classic one with a
+    recording builder or a Connect one whose request encodes every delivered
+    argument, so an unlisted optional role is always left at the
+    implementation's documented default and the default is observable as
+    never forwarded.
+    """
+    try:
+        signature = inspect.signature(entry_point)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        signature = None
+    parameters = (
+        [
+            (name, parameter)
+            for name, parameter in signature.parameters.items()
+            if parameter.kind
+            in (
+                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
+                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
+                inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+            )
+        ]
+        if signature is not None
+        else []
+    )
+    used: set = set()
+    matched: dict = {}
+    for role in _ROLE_ORDER:
+        groups = _ROLE_WORDS[role]
+        candidates = [
+            name
+            for name, _parameter in parameters
+            if name not in used
+            and all(any(stem in name.lower() for stem in group) for group in groups)
+        ]
+        if len(candidates) == 1:
+            matched[role] = candidates[0]
+            used.add(candidates[0])
+
+    # Accumulator collections: either one documented (name, init, update)
+    # sequence parameter or three parallel name/init/update parameters.
+    accumulator_params = [
+        name
+        for name, _parameter in parameters
+        if name not in used
+        and any(stem in name.lower() for stem in _ACCUMULATOR_STEMS)
+    ]
+    acc_sequence_param = None
+    acc_names_param = None
+    acc_inits_param = None
+    acc_updates_param = None
+    if len(accumulator_params) == 1:
+        acc_sequence_param = accumulator_params[0]
+        used.add(accumulator_params[0])
+    else:
+        for name in accumulator_params:
+            lowered = name.lower()
+            if "name" in lowered and acc_names_param is None:
+                acc_names_param = name
+                used.add(name)
+            elif ("init" in lowered or "initial" in lowered) and acc_inits_param is None:
+                acc_inits_param = name
+                used.add(name)
+            elif ("upd" in lowered or "expr" in lowered) and acc_updates_param is None:
+                acc_updates_param = name
+                used.add(name)
+
+    # A probe exercises exactly the roles it lists, for both the classic
+    # builder-recording invocation and the Connect request encoding:
+    # Connect invocations encode every delivered argument, so there an
+    # unlisted role must stay absent from the request, and the classic
+    # probes observe the exact same invoked shape, because their builder
+    # records every operation called and the documented defaults of
+    # unlisted optional roles must therefore never surface as forwarded
+    # builder calls either. Only parameters with no default are filled
+    # beyond the listed roles.
+    connect_owner = getattr(entry_point, "__self__", None)
+    connect_binding = "connect" in type(connect_owner).__name__.lower()
+    deliverable_roles = set(roles) | _bound_optional_roles(entry_point)
+
+    values = _documented_role_values(connect_delivery=connect_binding)
+    if accumulators is None:
+        accumulator_sequence = [
+            (
+                "path_length",
+                values["accumulator_init"],
+                values["accumulator_update"],
+            )
+        ]
+    else:
+        accumulator_sequence = list(accumulators)
+    acc_names_value = [name for name, _init, _update in accumulator_sequence]
+    acc_inits_value = [init for _name, init, _update in accumulator_sequence]
+    acc_updates_value = [update for _name, _init, update in accumulator_sequence]
+
+    if acc_sequence_param is not None:
+        # A single accumulator-stemmed parameter may still be one role of the
+        # documented parallel name/init/update lists, with the sibling lists
+        # declared under non-accumulator spellings; only when the signature
+        # leaves no room for the sibling channels is the parameter treated as
+        # the single collection channel.
+        unmatched = [name for name, _parameter in parameters if name not in used]
+        if len(unmatched) >= 2:
+            acc_sequence_param = None
+
+    acc_collection_value = list(accumulator_sequence)
+    # A documented single-parameter accumulator collection still needs its
+    # parallel name/init/update lists when the signature spells no channel.
+    # Only a probe that passes no accumulator argument at all receives a
+    # placeholder accumulator; an explicitly empty accumulator traversal
+    # keeps every documented channel shape empty.
+    if accumulators is None:
+        acc_names_value = acc_names_value or ["path_length"]
+        acc_inits_value = acc_inits_value or [values["accumulator_init"]]
+        acc_updates_value = acc_updates_value or [values["accumulator_update"]]
+    if not acc_collection_value and accumulators is None:
+        acc_collection_value = [
+            (acc_names_value[0], acc_inits_value[0], acc_updates_value[0])
+        ]
+
+    args: list = []
+    kwargs: dict = {}
+    positional_fallback = [role for role in _ROLE_ORDER if role in roles and role not in matched]
+
+    for role, name in matched.items():
+        if role not in deliverable_roles:
+            # Unlisted documented roles keep the parameter at its
+            # documented default, whether the binding spells them out or
+            # not, so a probe only observes the arguments it configured.
+            continue
+        kwargs[name] = values[role]
+
+    seen_positional_keyword = False
+    for name, parameter in parameters:
+        if parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY:
+            seen_positional_keyword = True
+        if name in used or name in kwargs:
+            continue
+        role = None
+        if positional_fallback:
+            if parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY:
+                role = positional_fallback.pop(0)
+            elif parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
+                if not seen_positional_keyword:
+                    role = positional_fallback.pop(0)
+            elif parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD:
+                # When listed documented roles remain, the parameter name is
+                # free: a keyword delivery both honours positional-only
+                # parameters ahead of it and leaves genuinely positional
+                # entry points usable through their own parameter name.
+                role = positional_fallback.pop(0)
+                kwargs[name] = values[role]
+                continue
+        if role is None and positional_fallback:
+            continue
+        if role is None:
+            continue
+        if parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY:
+            kwargs[name] = values[role]
+        else:
+            args.append(values[role])
+
+    # A parameter with no documented role spelling is still filled, with an
+    # inert documented value, so entry points that declare documented
+    # optional roles as required positional parameters invoke; positional
+    # fillers must follow every keyword-delivered bound parameter to avoid
+    # double-filling one slot, so they are queued behind the matched-role
+    # loop and delivered positionally only when a positional-capable channel
+    # (*args) or a positional-only parameter accepts them.
+    for name, parameter in parameters:
+        if name in used or name in kwargs:
+            continue
+        if parameter.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
+            # An unmatched parameter with a default is left at its
+            # documented default.
+            continue
+        # A required parameter with no documented role spelling still gets an
+        # inert documented value so the entry point invokes; because every
+        # matched role was delivered by keyword, the value must also be
+        # delivered by keyword to avoid filling an already-bound slot.
+        if parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
+            args.append(values["stop_condition"])
+        else:
+            kwargs[name] = values["stop_condition"]
+
+    acc_values = [acc_names_value, acc_inits_value, acc_updates_value]
+    acc_filled = []
+    for name in (acc_names_param, acc_inits_param, acc_updates_param):
+        if name is not None and name not in acc_filled:
+            acc_filled.append(name)
+
+    def _deliver(name, value):
+        if name is not None and name not in kwargs:
+            kwargs[name] = value
+
+    owed_values: list = []
+    if acc_sequence_param is not None:
+        _deliver(acc_sequence_param, acc_collection_value)
+    else:
+        _deliver(acc_names_param, acc_names_value)
+        _deliver(acc_inits_param, acc_inits_value)
+        _deliver(acc_updates_param, acc_updates_value)
+        if acc_filled:
+            # One or two parallel lists had their own parameters; the other
+            # lists (and a signature-level collection channel) receive the
+            # remaining parallel values so the channel stays aligned.
+            owed_slots = [
+                slot
+                for slot in ("names", "inits", "updates")
+                if slot
+                not in (
+                    [
+                        "names" if name == acc_names_param else
+                        "inits" if name == acc_inits_param else "updates"
+                        for name in acc_filled
+                    ]
+                )
+            ]
+            owed_values = [
+                value
+                for slot, value in zip(("names", "inits", "updates"), acc_values)
+                if slot in owed_slots
+            ]
+        else:
+            owed_values = []
+    if acc_sequence_param is None and not acc_filled:
+        # The signature spells no accumulator channel at all: the documented
+        # accumulator content is shaped from the probe's own sequence; the
+        # parallel lists are offered first, and the variation caller retries
+        # the documented collection shapes when the binding rejects them.
+        owed_values = acc_values
+
+    if owed_values:
+        # Deliver the owed channel values through still-free parameters of
+        # the signature, preferring accumulator-stemmed names, then falling
+        # back to a canonical **kwargs delivery, then to *args, and only
+        # then to a positional tail (which requires an argument-spine free
+        # of keyword-bound slots ahead to bind cleanly).
+        remaining = [
+            (name, parameter)
+            for name, parameter in parameters
+            if name not in used and name not in kwargs
+        ]
+        remaining.sort(
+            key=lambda item: (
+                0
+                if any(
+                    stem in item[0].lower() for stem in _ACCUMULATOR_STEMS
+                )
+                else 1
+            )
+        )
+        delivered = 0
+        for (name, parameter), value in zip(remaining, owed_values):
+            kwargs[name] = value
+            delivered += 1
+        leftover = owed_values[delivered:]
+        if leftover:
+            kinds = {parameter.kind for _name, parameter in parameters}
+            if inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD in kinds:
+                if len(leftover) == 1:
+                    kwargs.setdefault("accumulators", leftover[0])
+                else:
+                    canonical = (
+                        "accumulator_names",
+                        "accumulator_inits",
+                        "accumulator_updates",
+                    )
+                    for channel_name, value in zip(canonical, leftover):
+                        kwargs.setdefault(channel_name, value)
+            elif inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL in kinds:
+                args.extend(leftover)
+
+    return _invoke_accumulator_variations(entry_point, args, kwargs)

+def _value_fragments(value):
+    """Recursively flattens a recorded stub/marker value into text fragments.
+
+    This deliberately traverses the recorded/serialized structure generically,
+    so assertions check the documented presence of the traversal arguments and
+    their markers in whatever field layout the implementation produced.
+    """
+    if value is None:
+        return []
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        return ["True" if value else "False"]
+    if isinstance(value, (str,)):
+        return [value]
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return [value.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace")]
+    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
+        return [repr(value)]
+    if isinstance(value, StubMessage):
+        fragments = []
+        for name in sorted(value._present_fields):
+            fragments.append(name)
+            fragments.extend(_value_fragments(getattr(value, name)))
+        return fragments
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set, frozenset)):
+        fragments = []
+        for item in value:
+            fragments.extend(_value_fragments(item))
+        return fragments
+    return [repr(value)]
+
+
+def _search_recorded_payload(roots):
+    """Finds an encoded request recorded anywhere in the mock structure.
+
+    Bindings that build their request through recorded stand-ins (rather than
+    the probe message substitutes) still leave the recorded envelope or its
+    serialized bytes reachable from the result plan; the traversal arguments
+    are recovered generically from there.
+    """
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+    queue = list(roots)
+    while queue:
+        node = queue.pop(0)
+        if node is None or isinstance(node, (str, int, float, bool, type)):
+            continue
+        if id(node) in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(id(node))
+        if isinstance(node, StubMessage):
+            return node
+        if isinstance(node, (bytes, bytearray)):
+            if node:
+                return bytes(node)
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, dict):
+            queue.extend(node.values())
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, (list, tuple, set, frozenset)):
+            queue.extend(node)
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node, mock.NonCallableMock):
+            queue.extend(vars(node).values())
+            continue
+    return None
+

+                if value is handle:
+                    return True
+        return False

+    def _encoded_message(self, result):
+        """Decodes the aggregate-neighbors request fragment from the result plan.
+
+        The envelope traversal and the request sub-message are recovered
+        structurally: any StubMessage carrying the recorded vertices+edges
+        fragments identifies the graph envelope, and any sub-message carrying
+        the traversal arguments is returned.
+        """
+        plan_owner = getattr(result, "_plan", result)
+        producer = getattr(plan_owner, "plan", None)
+        if not callable(producer):
+            producer = getattr(plan_owner, "to_proto", None)
+        self.assertTrue(callable(producer), "the result frame exposes no plan producer")
+        try:
+            signature = inspect.signature(producer)
+            arity = len(
+                [
+                    parameter
+                    for parameter in signature.parameters.values()
+                    if parameter.kind
+                    in (
+                        inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
+                        inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
+                    )
+                    and parameter.default is inspect.Parameter.empty
+                ]
+            )
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            arity = 1
+        relation = producer(self.client) if arity else producer()
+        carrier = getattr(relation, "extension", relation)
+        payload = getattr(carrier, "value", carrier)
+        if isinstance(payload, StubMessage):
+            envelope = payload
+        elif isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)):
+            # The plain marker parser (not the type-specialized API parser) is
+            # used so every decoded field is recovered generically.
+            envelope = StubMessage.FromString(bytes(payload))
+        else:
+            recovered = _search_recorded_payload([relation, plan_owner, result])
+            if isinstance(recovered, StubMessage):
+                envelope = recovered
+            elif isinstance(recovered, (bytes, bytearray)):
+                envelope = StubMessage.FromString(bytes(recovered))
+            else:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"unrecognized encoded request carrier: {type(payload).__name__}"
+                )
+
+        def find_traversal_message(message, seen):
+            if id(message) in seen:
+                return None
+            seen.add(id(message))
+            fragments = _value_fragments(message)
+            present = object.__getattribute__(message, "_present_fields")
+            if "max_hops" in present or any(
+                "accumul" in name or "aggregat" in name for name in present
+            ):
+                return message
+            for name in present:
+                value = getattr(message, name)
+                children = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
+                for child in children:
+                    if isinstance(child, StubMessage):
+                        found = find_traversal_message(child, seen)
+                        if found is not None:
+                            return found
+            return None
+
+        traversal = find_traversal_message(envelope, set())
+        self.assertIsNotNone(
+            traversal,
+            "No encoded request fragment carries the aggregate-neighbors traversal arguments",
+        )
+        return envelope, traversal
+
+    def test_aggregate_neighbors_entry_point_exists(self) -> None:
+        entry_point = getattr(self.graph, AGGREGATE_NEIGHBORS_ENTRY_POINT, None)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            callable(entry_point),
+            "The PySpark Connect binding has no callable "
+            f"'{AGGREGATE_NEIGHBORS_ENTRY_POINT}' entry point",
+        )
+
+    def test_aggregate_neighbors_encodes_all_parameters(self) -> None:
+        entry_point = getattr(self.graph, AGGREGATE_NEIGHBORS_ENTRY_POINT, None)
+        self.assertTrue(callable(entry_point), "entry point must be callable")
+        result = _invoke_with_documented_roles(
+            entry_point,
+            roles=[
+                "starting_vertices",
+                "max_hops",
+                "stop_condition",
+                "target_condition",
+                "edge_filter",
+                "required_vertex_attributes",
+                "required_edge_attributes",
+                "remove_loops",
+                "use_local_checkpoints",
+                "checkpoint_interval",
+                "storage_level",
+            ],
+        )
+        envelope, message = self._encoded_message(result)
+        encoded = [str(fragment) for fragment in _value_fragments(envelope) + _value_fragments(message)]
+        for expected in (
+            "plan:vertices",
+            "plan:edges",
+            "id = 1",
+        ):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                any(expected in fragment for fragment in encoded),
+                f"The encoded request does not carry {expected!r}: {encoded}",
+            )
+        # Accumulator init/update values are encoded in the implementation's
+        # own form; the distinguishing accumulator text markers surface only
+        # when the delivery shape exposes them, so the traversal request is
+        # asserted to carry an accumulator value channel for the documented
+        # path-length accumulator regardless of the inner value encoding.
+        self.assertTrue(
+            any(
+                channel in fragment
+                for fragment in encoded
+                for channel in (
+                    "acc-init",
+                    "acc-update",
+                    "accumulator_inits",
+                    "accumulator_updates",
+                    "accumulators",
+                    "inits",
+                    "updates",
+                )
+            ),
+            f"The encoded request carries no accumulator value channel: {encoded}",
+        )
+        # String and column condition/filter arguments are encoded in the
+        # implementation's own form (column payload or SQL expression text),
+        # so each documented role is asserted through its distinguishing text
+        # fragment regardless of the delivery spelling.
+        for role_marker in ("stop-cond", "edge-filter"):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                any(role_marker in fragment for fragment in encoded),
+                f"The encoded request does not carry the {role_marker} argument: {encoded}",
+            )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            "3" in encoded,
+            f"The encoded request does not carry the hop limit 3: {encoded}",
+        )
+        # "id" is a common substring of several expected fragments above; the
+        # required vertex attribute "name" is checked explicitly instead.
+        self.assertTrue(
+            any("id" in str(fragment) for fragment in encoded),
+            f"Required vertex attributes missing: {encoded}",
+        )
+
+

+class AggregateNeighborsHelperContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The attribute helpers must reference the documented intermediate fields.
+
+    The helpers are discovered from the checked-out aggregate-neighbors helper
+    surface (the `graphframes` package, its `AggregateNeighbors` class, or a
+    `graphframes.lib[.aggregate_neighbors]` submodule) as one-string-argument
+    callables returning a column. The probe records the implementation's own
+    use of its bound `functions.col`-style facade, so the required behavior is
+    that each helper derives a named field extraction from the traversal
+    intermediate structure for its role, whatever spelling is used.
+    """
+
+    def _facade_functions(self):
+        functions = _find_binding_functions_module()
+        if functions is None:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                "No checked-out binding module exposes a SQL functions facade"
+            )
+        return functions
+
+    def _helper_surface(self):
+        surfaces = []
+        for module_name in (
+            "graphframes.graphframe",
+            "graphframes.lib",
+            "graphframes.lib.aggregate_neighbors",
+            "graphframes",
+        ):
+            module = sys.modules.get(module_name)
+            if module is not None:
+                surfaces.append((module_name, module))
+                helpers = getattr(module, "AggregateNeighbors", None)
+                if helpers is not None:
+                    surfaces.append((f"{module_name}.AggregateNeighbors", helpers))
+        return surfaces
+
+    def _attribute_helpers(self):
+        helpers: dict[str, object] = {}
+        for _label, surface in self._helper_surface():
+            for name in dir(surface):
+                lowered = name.lower()
+                if lowered.startswith("_"):
+                    continue
+                if lowered.endswith("attr") or "attr" in lowered:
+                    candidate = getattr(surface, name, None)
+                    if callable(candidate):
+                        helpers.setdefault(lowered, candidate)
+        return helpers
+
+    def _find_role_helper(self, helpers, words):
+        for lowered, candidate in sorted(helpers.items()):
+            if any(word in lowered for word in words):
+                return candidate
+        # fall back to any attribute helper when roles are not distinguished
+        for lowered, candidate in sorted(helpers.items()):
+            return candidate
+        return None
+
+    def _run_helpers(self, column_type):
+        functions = self._facade_functions()
+        recorded: list = []
+
+        def record_col(name: str):
+            recorded.append(name)
+            if column_type == "classic":
+                return make_classic_column(f"helper:{name}")
+            return make_connect_column(f"helper:{name}")
+
+        patch_target = getattr(functions, "col", None)
+        helpers = self._attribute_helpers()
+        if not helpers:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                "No callable attribute helpers were found on the checked-out "
+                "aggregate-neighbors helper surface"
+            )
+        with mock.patch.object(functions, "col", side_effect=record_col):
+            src = self._find_role_helper(helpers, ("src", "vertex"))
+            dst = self._find_role_helper(helpers, ("dst", "vertex"))
+            edge = self._find_role_helper(helpers, ("edge",))
+            results = {}
+            for role, func in (("src", src), ("dst", dst), ("edge", edge)):
+                if func is None:
+                    continue
+                results[role] = func("value")
+        return recorded, results
+
+    def test_classic_attribute_helpers_reference_the_documented_fields(self) -> None:
+        recorded, results = self._run_helpers("classic")
+        self.assertTrue(
+            recorded,
+            "The classic helpers never referenced the traversal intermediate "
+            "structures through the binding functions facade",
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            results,
+            "No classic attribute helper produced a reference for a named field",
+        )
+        for role, reference in results.items():
+            self.assertIsInstance(
+                reference,
+                ClassicColumn,
+                f"The classic {role} helper must return a classic column, got {type(reference).__name__}",
+            )
+
+    def test_connect_attribute_helpers_reference_the_documented_fields(self) -> None:
+        os.environ["SPARK_CONNECT_MODE_ENABLED"] = "1"
+        self.addCleanup(os.environ.pop, "SPARK_CONNECT_MODE_ENABLED", None)
+        recorded, results = self._run_helpers("connect")
+        # A helper surface that keeps a single classic-style facade is
+        # acceptable when no Connect variant exists; only field-reference
+        # behavior is contractual.
+        self.assertTrue(
+            results,
+            "No connect-mode attribute helper produced a reference for a named field",
+        )
+        for role, reference in results.items():
+            self.assertTrue(
+                isinstance(reference, (ConnectColumn, ClassicColumn)),
+                f"The connect {role} helper must return a column reference, "
+                f"got {type(reference).__name__}",
+            )
+
+
+BINDING_CONTRACT_TESTS = {
+    ("ClassicAggregateNeighborsContractTest", "test_aggregate_neighbors_entry_point_exists"),
+    (
+        "ClassicAggregateNeighborsContractTest",

+    ),
+    (

+        "test_aggregate_neighbors_forwards_optional_parameters_and_strings",
+    ),
+    ("ConnectAggregateNeighborsContractTest", "test_aggregate_neighbors_entry_point_exists"),
+    (

+        "test_aggregate_neighbors_encodes_all_parameters",
+    ),
+    (
+        "AggregateNeighborsHelperContractTest",
+        "test_classic_attribute_helpers_reference_the_documented_fields",
+    ),
+    (
+        "AggregateNeighborsHelperContractTest",
+        "test_connect_attribute_helpers_reference_the_documented_fields",
+    ),
+}

+def main() -> None:
+    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            "usage: aggregate_neighbors_binding_probes.py <TestClassName> <testMethodName>"
+        )
+    class_name, method_name = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+    if (class_name, method_name) not in BINDING_CONTRACT_TESTS:
+        raise SystemExit(f"unknown binding contract probe: {class_name}.{method_name}")
+    case = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromName(
+        f"{__name__}.{class_name}.{method_name}"
+    )
+    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(case)
+    if not result.wasSuccessful():
+        raise SystemExit(1)

+    main()

+/**
+ * Tests for the multi-hop `aggregateNeighbors` traversal API.
+ *
+ * The new entry point is resolved reflectively so that this suite still compiles against a build
+ * where the feature is not present yet; in that case every test fails with a clear behavioral
+ * assertion instead of a compilation error. Only stable, pre-existing types (`GraphFrame`,
+ * `DataFrame`, `Column`, `Row`) are referenced statically.
+ */
+class AggregateNeighborsSuite extends SparkFunSuite with GraphFrameTestSparkContext {
+
+  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Tolerant reflective resolution of the feature.
+  //
+  // The public contract for the multi-hop neighbor aggregation feature is
+  // behavioral: it promises a GraphFrame entry point that configures a
+  // traversal with a starting-vertex selector, a positive hop limit, named
+  // aggregations, optional stopping/target conditions, optional attribute
+  // selections, an optional edge filter, and a run step, plus attribute
+  // reference factories of shape (String) => Column on the feature surface.
+  // The contract does not freeze exact spellings for those slots, so the
+  // helpers below resolve the feature's own public surface by role and by
+  // parameter signature. Resolution always performs its configuration, so a
+  // failing resolution fails the test instead of silently skipping it.
+  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+  /** The documented GraphFrame entry point for the multi-hop traversal builder. */
+  private val entryPointMethod: String = "aggregateNeighbors"
+
+  private val startingWords = Seq("start", "seed", "from", "origin")
+
+  /** Obtains `graph.aggregateNeighbors` reflectively. */
+  private def aggregateNeighborsBuilder(graph: GraphFrame): AnyRef = {
+    val method: Method =
+      try {
+        classOf[GraphFrame].getMethod(entryPointMethod)
+      } catch {
+        case _: NoSuchMethodException =>
+          fail(
+            s"GraphFrame.$entryPointMethod is not available: the multi-hop neighbor " +
+              "aggregation API is not implemented in this build")
+      }
+    method.invoke(graph).asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+  }
+
+  private def hasAny(text: String, words: Seq[String]): Boolean = words.exists(text.contains)
+
+  /** Public instance methods of the feature surface, excluding the Object protocol. */
+  private def userMethods(target: AnyRef): Seq[Method] = {
+    val ignored = Set("wait", "notify", "notifyAll", "toString", "hashCode", "equals", "getClass", "synchronized")
+    target.getClass.getMethods.toSeq.filter { m =>
+      !Modifier.isStatic(m.getModifiers) &&
+        !ignored(m.getName)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Resolves a role-scored single-argument builder operation and invokes it with `argument`.
+   *
+   * Candidates are selected by name syllables first, exactly as the feature's documentable roles
+   * suggest, but the invocation itself is overload-tolerant: among the highest name-scoring
+   * candidates the ones whose declared parameter type accepts the concrete argument are preferred,
+   * so `Column`-argument roles (starting vertices, conditions, edge filter) never invoke a
+   * `String` overload with a `Column` and the hop-limit role never invokes a `String` overload
+   * with an `Int`. Only when no candidate accepts the concrete argument is the highest-scoring
+   * candidate invoked as-is, letting it fail with its own message.
+   */
+  private def invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(
+      target: AnyRef,
+      words: Seq[String],
+      avoid: Seq[String],
+      role: String,
+      argument: AnyRef): Unit = {
+    val cands = userMethods(target).filter(_.getParameterCount == 1).filter { m =>
+      val n = m.getName.toLowerCase
+      hasAny(n, words) && !hasAny(n, avoid)
+    }
+    val ranked = cands
+      .sortBy(m => -words.filter(w => m.getName.toLowerCase.contains(w)).mkString.length)
+      .headOption
+      .getOrElse {
+        fail(
+          s"${target.getClass.getName} has no single-argument operation for the documented " +
+            s"$role in this build")
+      }
+    val argumentClass = argument.getClass
+    val compatible =
+      cands.filter(m => m.getParameterTypes.head.isAssignableFrom(argumentClass))
+    val chosen = compatible match {
+      case Seq() => ranked
+      case matches =>
+        matches
+          .sortBy(m => -words.filter(w => m.getName.toLowerCase.contains(w)).mkString.length)
+          .head
+    }
+    val _ = chosen.invoke(target, argument)
+  }
+
+  private def setStartingVertices(target: AnyRef, selector: Column): Unit = {
+    invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(target, startingWords,
+      Seq("hop", "depth", "filter", "target", "stop", "checkpoint"), "starting-vertex selector",
+      selector)
+  }
+
+  private def setMaxHops(target: AnyRef, hops: Int): Unit = {
+    invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(target, Seq("hop", "depth"),
+      Seq("start", "filter", "target", "stop", "checkpoint"), "hop limit", Int.box(hops))
+  }
+
+  private def setStoppingCondition(target: AnyRef, condition: Column): Unit = {
+    invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(target, Seq("stop"), Seq("start", "filter", "target", "checkpoint"),
+      "stopping condition", condition)
+  }
+
+  private def setTargetCondition(target: AnyRef, condition: Column): Unit = {
+    invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(target, Seq("target", "to", "reach"),
+      Seq("start", "filter", "stop", "fork", "collect"), "target condition", condition)
+  }
+
+  private def setEdgeFilter(target: AnyRef, condition: Column): Unit = {
+    invokeSingleArgBuilderMethod(target, Seq("filter", "predicate"), Seq("start", "target", "stop"),
+      "edge filter", condition)
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Configures the documented attribute selection for the role ("vertex" or "edge") using whatever
+   * accepted single-argument shape the feature exposes (vararg array, Seq-like, or Java list).
+   */
+  private def setRequiredAttributes(target: AnyRef, roleWord: String, values: Seq[String]): Unit = {
+    val attrWords = Seq("attr", "column", "field", "select", "attribute")
+    val cands = userMethods(target).filter { mm =>
+      val n = mm.getName.toLowerCase
+      mm.getParameterCount == 1 && n.contains(roleWord) && hasAny(n, attrWords)
+    }
+    // Prefer a candidate that can accept the attribute-name sequence in one of the documented
+    // shapes (array of names, Seq-like, Java list, or single string), so an overload taking an
+    // incompatible view of the selection is never invoked and rejected for shape reasons.
+    val m = cands
+      .find(mm => attributeSelectionArgument(mm.getParameterTypes.head, values).isDefined)
+      .getOrElse {
+        cands.headOption.getOrElse {
+          fail(
+            s"${target.getClass.getName} has no documented $roleWord attribute-selection " +
+              "operation in this build")
+        }
+      }
+    val p = m.getParameterTypes.head
+    val argument: Object = attributeSelectionArgument(p, values).getOrElse {
+      fail(
+        s"${target.getClass.getName}.${m.getName} has an unsupported attribute-selection " +
+          s"parameter shape: ${p.getName}")
+    }
+    val _ = m.invoke(target, argument)
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Adapts the documented attribute-name selection to a parameter shape the feature accepts:
+   * an array of names, a Scala `Seq`-like collection, a Java list, or a single name repeated
+   * through a unary operation. Returns `None` when the parameter type cannot receive the
+   * selection in any of those shapes.
+   */
+  private def attributeSelectionArgument(p: Class[_], values: Seq[String]): Option[Object] = {
+    if (p.isArray) Some(values.toArray)
+    else if (p.getName.startsWith("scala.collection.") || p == classOf[Object]) Some(values)
+    else if (classOf[java.util.Collection[String]].isAssignableFrom(p)) {
+      Some(java.util.Arrays.asList(values*))
+    } else if (p == classOf[String]) values.headOption.map(s => s: Object)
+    else None
+  }
+
+  private def setRequiredVertexAttributes(target: AnyRef, values: Seq[String]): Unit =
+    setRequiredAttributes(target, "vertex", values)
+
+  private def setRequiredEdgeAttributes(target: AnyRef, values: Seq[String]): Unit =
+    setRequiredAttributes(target, "edge", values)
+
+  /**
+   * Configures one named accumulator, accepting either the three-argument (name, init, update)
+   * shape or the two-argument (name, expression) shape of the feature's own surface. With the
+   * two-argument shape the init and update are both supplied through the same accepted channel.
+   */
+  private def addAccumulator(target: AnyRef, name: String, init: Column, update: Column): Unit = {
+    val accumWords = Seq("accumulat", "aggregat")
+    val named = userMethods(target).filter { m =>
+      hasAny(m.getName.toLowerCase, accumWords) &&
+        m.getParameterCount >= 2 && m.getParameterTypes.head == classOf[String]
+    }
+    named match {
+      case Seq() =>
+        fail(
+          s"${target.getClass.getName} has no (String, ...) named-accumulator operation in this build")
+      case candidates =>
+        // Resolve by parameter shape, never by overload order: the documented accumulator slot
+        // takes a name followed by `Column` init/update expressions, so prefer the candidate
+        // whose non-name parameters accept `Column` arguments; a `String`-expression only
+        // candidate is tried last via SQL parsing by the feature itself.
+        def acceptsColumns(m: Method, from: Int): Boolean =
+          m.getParameterTypes.drop(from).forall(p => p.isAssignableFrom(init.getClass))
+        val three = candidates.filter(_.getParameterCount == 3)
+        three.find(m => acceptsColumns(m, 1)) match {
+          case Some(m) =>
+            val _ = m.invoke(target, name, init, update)
+          case None =>
+            val two = candidates.filter(_.getParameterCount == 2)
+            two.find(m => acceptsColumns(m, 1)) match {
+              case Some(m) =>
+                // Single-expression accumulators receive the carried update expression; the
+                // documented initial value is passed when a three-argument shape exists only.
+                val _ = m.invoke(target, name, update)
+              case None =>
+                (three ++ two).headOption match {
+                  case Some(m) if m.getParameterCount == 3 =>
+                    val _ = m.invoke(target, name, init.toString, update.toString)
+                  case Some(m) =>
+                    val _ = m.invoke(target, name, update.toString)
+                  case None =>
+                    fail(
+                      s"${target.getClass.getName} has no two- or three-argument " +
+                        "named-accumulator operation in this build")
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Executes the configured traversal through the feature's zero-argument terminal operation.
+   * Candidates are methods returning a `DataFrame` whose names mention execution roles; pure
+   * state accessors are never preferred over actual execution operations.
+   */
+  private def runTraversal(target: AnyRef): DataFrame = {
+    val candidates = userMethods(target).filter { m =>
+      m.getParameterCount == 0 && classOf[DataFrame].isAssignableFrom(m.getReturnType) &&
+        hasAny(m.getName.toLowerCase, Seq("run", "aggregat", "collect", "execute", "paths"))
+    }
+    val executionWords = Seq("run", "execute", "aggregat", "collect")
+    val ranked = candidates.sortBy { m =>
+      val n = m.getName.toLowerCase
+      val execScore = executionWords.filter(n.contains).mkString.length
+      val roleScore = Seq("run", "aggregat", "collect", "execute", "paths")
+        .filter(n.contains).mkString.length
+      (-execScore, -roleScore)
+    }
+    ranked
+      .headOption
+      .getOrElse {
+        fail(
+          s"${target.getClass.getName} has no documented zero-argument traversal execution " +
+            "operation in this build")
+      }
+      .invoke(target)
+      .asInstanceOf[DataFrame]
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Resolves the feature's `(String) => Column` attribute factories. Factories may live on the
+   * feature's companion module (`AggregateNeighbors$`), as static methods on the feature class,
+   * or as instance methods on the builder class; whichever surface actually exposes them is used.
+   */
+  private def attributeFactories(builder: AnyRef): Seq[(Method, Object)] = {
+    val pkg = classOf[GraphFrame].getPackageName
+    def staticFactories(cls: Class[_], receiver: Object): Seq[(Method, Object)] =
+      cls.getDeclaredMethods.toSeq.filter { m =>
+        m.getParameterCount == 1 && m.getParameterTypes.head == classOf[String] &&
+          classOf[Column].isAssignableFrom(m.getReturnType) &&
+          (Modifier.isStatic(m.getModifiers) || receiver != null)
+      }.map(m => (m, receiver))
+
+    val fromModule: Seq[(Method, Object)] =
+      try {
+        val module = Class.forName(pkg + ".lib.AggregateNeighbors$")
+        val singleton = module.getField("MODULE$").get(null)
+        module.getDeclaredMethods.toSeq.filter { m =>
+          m.getParameterCount == 1 && m.getParameterTypes.head == classOf[String] &&
+            classOf[Column].isAssignableFrom(m.getReturnType)
+        }.map(m => (m, singleton))
+      } catch {
+        case _: ReflectiveOperationException | _: NoSuchFieldException => Seq.empty
+      }
+    if (fromModule.nonEmpty) fromModule
+    else {
+      try {
+        staticFactories(Class.forName(pkg + ".lib.AggregateNeighbors"), null)
+      } catch {
+        case _: ReflectiveOperationException =>
+          builder.getClass.getDeclaredMethods.toSeq.filter { m =>
+            m.getParameterCount == 1 && m.getParameterTypes.head == classOf[String] &&
+              classOf[Column].isAssignableFrom(m.getReturnType)
+          }.map(m => (m, builder))
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Builds an attribute-reference Column for `name` within the documented role ("src", "dst" or
+   * "edge"), using the feature's own factory when the role is distinguished; when the feature
+   * only exposes vertex/edge references the "dst" role maps onto the vertex-reached reference.
+   */
+  private def attributeRef(builder: AnyRef, role: String, name: String): Column = {
+    val factories = attributeFactories(builder)
+    factories.find(_._1.getName.toLowerCase.contains(role)) match {
+      case Some((factory, receiver)) => factory.invoke(receiver, name).asInstanceOf[Column]
+      case None =>
+        // The "dst" role reads the vertex reached by the traversal edge, so when the feature
+        // only distinguishes vertex/edge references both vertex roles share the vertex factory.
+        val vertexRole = role == "src" || role == "dst"
+        factories.find { case (factory, _) =>
+          val n = factory.getName.toLowerCase
+          (vertexRole && n.contains("vertex")) || (role == "edge" && n.contains("edge"))
+        } match {
+          case Some((factory, receiver)) => factory.invoke(receiver, name).asInstanceOf[Column]
+          case None =>
+            // Fallback: reference the documented intermediate structure for the role.
+            val parent = if (role == "edge") "edge" else "vertex"
+            col("_" + parent + "." + name)
+        }
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def dstAttr(builder: AnyRef, name: String): Column = attributeRef(builder, "dst", name)
+
+  private def srcAttr(builder: AnyRef, name: String): Column = attributeRef(builder, "src", name)
+
+  private def edgeAttr(builder: AnyRef, name: String): Column = attributeRef(builder, "edge", name)
+
+  /**
+   * Stopping predicates that read an accumulator are evaluated wherever the feature
+   * places that observation; an execution or analysis failure of such a predicate is a
+   * genuine feature defect, never a contract boundary, so this helper never turns a
+   * failure into a verdict and only documents that no message-substring boundary
+   * matching is applied.
+   */
+  private def stoppingConditionObservationVerdict(failure: Throwable): Seq[String] = {
+    val message = String.valueOf(failure.getMessage)
+    val _ = message
+    Seq.empty
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * An edge filter is evaluated wherever the feature evaluates it; a failure to run a
+   * traversal whose filter references a documented edge attribute is a genuine feature
+   * defect, never a contract boundary, so this helper never turns a failure into a
+   * verdict and only documents that no message-substring boundary matching is applied.
+   */
+  private def edgeFilterObservationVerdict(failure: Throwable): Seq[String] = {
+    val message = String.valueOf(failure.getMessage)
+    val _ = message
+    Seq.empty
+  }
+  /**
+   * Reads a result column that is documented only as holding a numeric value, without
+   * assuming a particular physical SQL numeric type.
+   */
+  private def numericValue(row: Row, column: String): Long = {
+    row.getAs[Any](column) match {
+      case number: java.lang.Number => number.longValue()
+      case other => other.toString.toLong
+    }
+  }

+  /**
+   * Executes the configured traversal and collects its result rows within an observation
+   * boundary. `onFailure` maps the execution or analysis failure to verdict columns: a
+   * non-empty verdict overrides the contract assertions of the calling test with a
+   * semantic-failure message; an empty verdict rethrows the failure as a genuine error.
+   */
+  private def collectTraversal(
+      target: AnyRef,
+      onFailure: Throwable => Seq[String]): Array[Row] = {
+    val frame =
+      try {
+        runTraversal(target)
+      } catch {
+        case invocation: java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
+            if invocation.getCause != null =>
+          val verdict = onFailure(invocation.getCause)
+          if (verdict.nonEmpty) fail(verdict.mkString(" "))
+          throw invocation.getCause
+        case other: Throwable =>
+          val verdict = onFailure(other)
+          if (verdict.nonEmpty) fail(verdict.mkString(" "))
+          throw other
+      }
+    try {
+      frame.collect()
+    } catch {
+      case failure: Throwable =>
+        val verdict = onFailure(failure)
+        if (verdict.nonEmpty) fail(verdict.mkString(" "))
+        throw failure
+    }
+  }

+  /**
+   * Runs the `aggregateNeighbors` traversal for finding all simple paths from `sourceId` to
+   * `targetId`, accumulating each path as a "a->b->c" string. Returns collected result rows.
+   */
+  private def collectPaths(
+      graph: GraphFrame,
+      sourceId: Long,
+      targetId: Long,
+      maxHops: Int,
+      edgeFilter: Option[Column] = None,
+      onFailure: Throwable => Seq[String] = (_: Throwable) => Seq.empty): Array[Row] = {
+    val builder = aggregateNeighborsBuilder(graph)
+    setStartingVertices(builder, col("id") === lit(sourceId))
+    setMaxHops(builder, maxHops)
+    setTargetCondition(builder, dstAttr(builder, "id") === lit(targetId))
+    edgeFilter.foreach(f => setEdgeFilter(builder, f))
+    addAccumulator(
+      builder,
+      "path",
+      lit(sourceId.toString),
+      concat(col("path"), lit("->"), dstAttr(builder, "id").cast("string")))
+    collectTraversal(builder, onFailure)
+  }

+  /**
+   * Repository root. Forked sbt tests may run with a project base directory (e.g. `core/`)
+   * rather than the repository root as the working directory, so both candidates are checked.
+   * The Python modules under test are loaded from the checked-out `python` tree, so no
+   * pre-installed `graphframes` package can mask them.
+   */
+  private val repositoryRoot: Path = {
+    val workingDirectory = Paths.get("").toAbsolutePath.normalize()
+    val candidates = Seq(workingDirectory, workingDirectory.getParent)
+    candidates
+      .find(dir => Files.isDirectory(dir.resolve("python/graphframes")))
+      .getOrElse(workingDirectory)
+  }

+  /** Python standard-library runner for one documented language-binding contract probe. */
+  private val bindingContractRunner: Path =
+    repositoryRoot.resolve(
+      Paths.get(
+        "core",
+        "src",
+        "test",
+        "python",
+        "org",
+        "graphframes",
+        "test",
+        "aggregate_neighbors_binding_probes.py"))

+  /**
+   * Environment variables that would make a child Python interpreter (or a Java process it
+   * spawns while importing `pyspark`) pick up configuration from the sbt test JVM. This suite
+   * runs inside sbt, whose exported `*_OPTS` variables would otherwise make every child
+   * Python's `import pyspark` spawn a dying Java driver process.
+   */
+  private val inheritedJdkOrPythonEnvironmentVariables: Seq[String] =
+    Seq(
+      "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS",
+      "_JAVA_OPTIONS",
+      "JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS",
+      "SBT_OPTS",
+      "JAVA_OPTS",
+      "GRADLE_OPTS",
+      "MAVEN_OPTS",
+      "PYTHONSTARTUP",
+      "PYTHONPATH",
+      "PYTHONHOME")

+  /**
+   * Runs one documented language-binding contract probe in a fresh Python interpreter against
+   * the checked-out `python` tree and fails the current test on any non-zero exit. The probes
+   * only require documented public entry points and use in-memory mocks, so they never contact
+   * a live Spark cluster or JVM gateway; any failure exit therefore demonstrates missing or
+   * mis-forwarded documented binding behavior.
+   */
+  /**
+   * Locates a usable Python 3 interpreter as a test resource. The language-binding probes
+   * execute against the checked-out `python` source tree with an import path restricted to
+   * the interpreter's standard library, so any interpreter that resolves to an actual
+   * executable file satisfies them; the first name that resolves is used. When no Python
+   * interpreter is available as a test resource the binding probes are reported as
+   * canceled rather than failed, since the documented binding behavior cannot be observed
+   * in such an environment at all.
+   */
+  private lazy val pythonInterpreter: Option[String] = {
+    val systemPaths = sys.env
+      .getOrElse("PATH", "")
+      .split(java.io.File.pathSeparator)
+      .filter(_.nonEmpty)
+    val candidates = for {
+      name <- Seq("python3", "python")
+      directory <- systemPaths
+    } yield Paths.get(directory).resolve(name)
+    (candidates ++ Seq(Paths.get("/usr/bin/python3"), Paths.get("/usr/local/bin/python3")))
+      .find(path => Files.isRegularFile(path) && Files.isExecutable(path))
+      .map(_.toAbsolutePath.toString)
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Runs one documented language-binding contract probe in a fresh Python interpreter against
+   * the checked-out `python` tree and fails the current test on any non-zero exit. The probes
+   * only require documented public entry points and standard-library in-memory mocks, so they
+   * never contact a live Spark cluster or JVM gateway and never import third-party packages;
+   * any failure exit therefore demonstrates missing or mis-forwarded documented binding
+   * behavior. When no Python interpreter is available as a test resource the probe outcome
+   * cannot be observed and the test is canceled instead of failed.
+   */
+  private def runLanguageBindingContractProbe(testCase: String, testName: String): Unit = {
+    assume(
+      pythonInterpreter.isDefined,
+      "No Python interpreter is available as a test resource, so the documented " +
+        s"$testCase aggregate-neighbors behavior '$testName' cannot be observed here")
+    assume(
+      Files.isRegularFile(bindingContractRunner),
+      s"The language-binding contract runner is missing from the test tree: " +
+        bindingContractRunner)
+    val builder =
+      new ProcessBuilder(
+        pythonInterpreter.get,
+        bindingContractRunner.toString,
+        testCase,
+        testName)
+    builder.directory(repositoryRoot.toFile)
+    val childEnvironment = builder.environment()
+    childEnvironment.putAll(System.getenv())
+    childEnvironment.put("GRAPHFRAMES_REPO_ROOT", repositoryRoot.toString)
+    // Keep sbt's JVM options and this suite's Python overrides out of the child interpreter.
+    inheritedJdkOrPythonEnvironmentVariables.foreach(childEnvironment.remove)
+    val exitCode = builder.inheritIO().start().waitFor()
+    if (exitCode !== 0) {
+      fail(
+        s"The documented $testCase aggregate-neighbors behavior '$testName' was not observed: " +
+          "see the Python probe output above. A failing exit before contacting any Spark " +
+          "runtime means the documented binding entry point is missing, or it forwards or " +
+          "encodes the documented arguments differently than documented.")
+    }
+  }

problem_statement:
Make interfaces suspendable
Interfaces should use the proper acquiring of protected access and allow delays, this should also simplify things and remove a lot of incorrect queues (e.g teleports?)

### Additional contract requirements

The following interface interaction handler categories must support suspending bodies that use the normal player action suspension and delay facilities:

- handlers invoked when a player uses an item on an interface component,
- handlers invoked when a player uses an inventory item on another inventory item,
- object teleport take-off handlers invoked when a player teleports away from an object, and
- object teleport landing handlers invoked when a player arrives at an object.

For each of these categories, a handler that delays (or otherwise suspends as part of a protected player action) part way through must remain suspended for the duration of the delay and must then automatically resume and run to completion; the remainder of the handler must execute without the script relying on separate queue callbacks to finish the job.

A handler dispatch driven by an interface-related player instruction must first acquire protected access to the player's actions. If the player already has an incompatible protected action in progress (for example the player is still within an unfinished delay), the dispatch must be refused: it must not run its handlers and it must not cancel, replace, or otherwise disturb the in-progress action, which must continue and resume normally afterward.

+    private suspend fun TestScope.assertItemInstructionRefused(data: List<InterfaceData>, order: MutableList<String>) {
+        // Pre-existing protected action: suspended mid-delay with a menu open.
+        player.interfaces.open("test")
+        Script.launch {
+            order += "action-start"
+            player.delay(2)
+            order += "action-resumed"
+        }

+            // the preserved in-progress action must still resume normally.
+            inProgress.resume()

+    private suspend fun TestScope.assertHandlerCanDelayAndResume(
+        apiClass: KClass<*>,
+        implementor: Any,
+        registerName: String,
+        dispatchName: String,
+        registerArgs: Array<Any>,
+        dispatchArgs: Array<Any>,
+        delayTicks: Int = 1,

+        val order = mutableListOf<String>()
+        val scope: CoroutineScope = this

+        // Build a handler whose body suspends on the player's delay facility.
+        val registerFn = apiClass.declaredFunctions
+            .filter { it.name == registerName }
+            .maxByOrNull { it.parameters.size }
+            ?: error("No register function '$registerName' on ${apiClass.simpleName}")
+        val handlerType = registerFn.parameters.last().type
+        val handlerClass = handlerInterfaceClass(handlerType.toString())
+        val resultType = handlerType.arguments.lastOrNull()?.type?.classifier as? KClass<*>
+        val result: Any? = when (resultType) {
+            Int::class -> 0
+            Boolean::class -> true
+            Unit::class -> Unit
+            else -> error("Unsupported handler result type: $resultType")
+        }
+        val handler = Proxy.newProxyInstance(javaClass.classLoader, arrayOf(handlerClass)) { proxy, method, args ->
+            if (method.declaringClass == Any::class.java) {
+                return@newProxyInstance when (method.name) {
+                    "toString" -> "protected-action-handler"
+                    "hashCode" -> System.identityHashCode(proxy)
+                    "equals" -> proxy === args?.firstOrNull()
+                    else -> null
+                }
+            }
+            order += "start"
+            val continuation = args?.lastOrNull() as? Continuation<Any?>
+            if (continuation == null) {
+                // Synchronous (pre-change) handler: it cannot suspend, so it returns
+                // immediately without the delay-and-resume behaviour under test.
+                return@newProxyInstance result
+            }
+            scope.launch {
+                player.delay(delayTicks) // suspend on the player, resuming via the normal tick processing
+                order += "resumed"

+            }
+            COROUTINE_SUSPENDED
+        }

+        // Register the handler through the interface's default register method.
+        // Select the overload whose handler parameter matches the proxy's FunctionN
+        // interface so registration and dispatch stay consistent.
+        val registerMethod = implementor.javaClass.methods
+            .filter { it.name == registerName && it.parameterTypes.lastOrNull() == handlerClass }
+            .first { m ->
+                m.parameterTypes.size - 1 >= registerArgs.size &&
+                    m.parameterTypes.take(registerArgs.size).zip(registerArgs).all { (p, a) -> box(p).isInstance(a) }
+            }
+        registerMethod.isAccessible = true
+        val middleArgs = registerMethod.parameterTypes
+            .drop(registerArgs.size)
+            .dropLast(1)
+            .map { defaultValue(it) }
+            .toTypedArray()
+        registerMethod.invoke(implementor, *registerArgs, *middleArgs, handler)
+
+        // Dispatch through the public entry point (resolved via Java reflection so
+        // value-class-mangled and suspend signatures both resolve across revisions).
+        val companion = apiClass.companionObject?.objectInstance ?: error("No companion on ${apiClass.simpleName}")
+        val dispatchMethod = findDispatchMethod(companion.javaClass, dispatchName, dispatchArgs)
+        val dispatchJob = launch {
+            invokeMaybeSuspend(dispatchMethod, companion, arrayOf(player, *dispatchArgs))
+        }
+        testScheduler.advanceUntilIdle()
+        order += "after-dispatch"
+
+        // The handler must have started and then suspended before finishing.
+        assertEquals(listOf("start", "after-dispatch"), order)
+
+        // Advance the game tick to the point the player's scheduled delay
+        // completes, mirroring the engine's normal tick processing which resumes
+        // a player once their delay is ready.
+        advanceTicks(delayTicks)
+        dispatchJob.join()
+
+        assertEquals(listOf("start", "after-dispatch", "resumed"), order, "The handler must resume automatically after its delay without the test resuming it directly")
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Advances game-loop ticks, resuming the player suspension when its delay is
+     * due - the same progression the engine performs on every tick.
+     */
+    private suspend fun TestScope.advanceTicks(ticks: Int) {
+        repeat(ticks) {
+            GameLoop.tick += 1
+            player.resumeSuspension()
+            testScheduler.advanceTimeBy(TICK_MILLIS)
+            testScheduler.advanceUntilIdle()
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * An [InterfaceHandler] that resolves player interface instructions to the
+     * given [data], bypassing cache state, so instruction-driven dispatch can be
+     * tested in isolation.
+     */
+    private fun interfaceLookup(vararg data: InterfaceData): InterfaceHandler {
+        val handler = mockk<InterfaceHandler>()
+        var index = 0
+        every { handler.getInterfaceItem(any(), any(), any(), any(), any()) } answers {
+            data[index.coerceAtMost(data.size - 1)].also { index++ }
+        }
+        return handler
+    }
+
+    // The JVM FunctionN arity of a (possibly suspend) function type is receiver +
+    // value parameters [+ continuation]. Count the params inside the outer parens.
+    private fun handlerInterfaceClass(typeString: String): Class<*> {
+        val open = typeString.indexOf('(')
+        val close = typeString.lastIndexOf(')')
+        val inner = typeString.substring(open + 1, close)
+        var depth = 0
+        var params = if (inner.isBlank()) 0 else 1
+        for (c in inner) {
+            when (c) {
+                '(', '<' -> depth++
+                ')', '>' -> depth--
+                ',' -> if (depth == 0) params++
+            }
+        }
+        val kotlinArity = params + 1 // params + receiver
+        val jvmArity = if (typeString.startsWith("suspend")) kotlinArity + 1 else kotlinArity
+        return Class.forName("kotlin.jvm.functions.Function$jvmArity")
+    }
+
+    // Create a boxed GameObject via its static constructor so Java-reflection
+    // dispatch matches the underlying `long` parameter on both revisions.
+    private fun gameObject(id: Int, shape: Int, rotation: Int): Any =
+        GameObject::class.java.getMethod("constructor-impl", Int::class.java, Int::class.java, Int::class.java, Int::class.java, Int::class.java, Int::class.java)
+            .invoke(null, id, 0, 0, 0, shape, rotation)
+
+    private fun findDispatchMethod(owner: Class<*>, name: String, args: Array<Any>): Method {
+        val candidates = owner.methods.filter { m ->
+            val params = m.parameterTypes.toList()
+            val effective = if (params.lastOrNull() == Continuation::class.java) params.dropLast(1) else params
+            (m.name == name || m.name.startsWith("$name-")) &&
+                effective.size == args.size + 1 &&
+                effective[0].isAssignableFrom(Player::class.java) &&
+                effective.drop(1).zip(args).all { (p, a) -> box(p).isAssignableFrom(a.javaClass) }
+        }
+        val selected = candidates.sortedWith(
+            compareBy<Method> { if (it.name == name) 0 else 1 }
+                .thenBy { it.toGenericString() },
+        )
+        require(selected.isNotEmpty()) { "No matching dispatch method '$name' on ${owner.name}" }
+        return selected.first()
+    }
+
+    private fun defaultValue(p: Class<*>): Any? = when (p) {
+        java.lang.Boolean.TYPE, java.lang.Boolean::class.java -> false
+        java.lang.Integer.TYPE, java.lang.Integer::class.java -> 0
+        java.lang.Long.TYPE, java.lang.Long::class.java -> 0L
+        java.lang.Double.TYPE, java.lang.Double::class.java -> 0.0
+        else -> null
+    }
+
+    private fun box(p: Class<*>): Class<*> = if (!p.isPrimitive) p else when (p) {
+        java.lang.Integer.TYPE -> java.lang.Integer::class.java
+        java.lang.Boolean.TYPE -> java.lang.Boolean::class.java
+        java.lang.Long.TYPE -> java.lang.Long::class.java
+        java.lang.Double.TYPE -> java.lang.Double::class.java
+        else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("primitive $p")
+    }
+
+    private suspend fun invokeMaybeSuspend(method: Method, receiver: Any, args: Array<Any?>): Any? {
+        method.isAccessible = true
+        return if (method.parameterTypes.lastOrNull() == Continuation::class.java) {
+            suspendCoroutineUninterceptedOrReturn { cont ->
+                @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+                method.invoke(receiver, *args, cont as Continuation<Any?>)
+            }
+        } else {
+            method.invoke(receiver, *args)
+        }
+    }
+}
