problem_statement:
Bug on empty triangulations
This is documenting an error found by @zjwegert  while integrating multifield spaces on empty embedded triangulations in GridapEmbedded. This will get fixed by #1277 in the upcoming release.

The MWE: 

```julia
using Gridap, Gridap.TensorValues, Gridap.FESpaces, Gridap.Arrays
using GridapEmbedded, GridapEmbedded.LevelSetCutters

r = 1.5

model = CartesianDiscreteModel((0,1,0,1),(3,3))
V_φ = TestFESpace(model,ReferenceFE(lagrangian,Float64,1))
φh = interpolate(((x,y),)->sqrt((x-0.5)^2+(y-0.5)^2)-r,V_φ)
geo = DiscreteGeometry(φh,model)
cutgeo = cut(model,geo)
Γ = EmbeddedBoundary(cutgeo)
dΓ = Measure(Γ,2)

V1 = TestFESpace(model,ReferenceFE(lagrangian,Float64,1))
V = MultiFieldFESpace([V1,V1])

jump_u(u1,u2) = u1 - u2
a((u1,u2),(v1,v2)) = ∫(jump_u(u1,u2)*v2)dΓ
AffineFEOperator(a,v->0,V,V) # Fails in BroadcastingFieldOpMap

a((u1,u2),(v1,v2)) = ∫(u1*v1 + u1*v1)dΓ
AffineFEOperator(a,v->0,V,V) # Fails in IntegrationMap
```

diff --git a/test/GridapTests/issues/issue_1279.jl b/test/GridapTests/issues/issue_1279.jl

--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/GridapTests/issues/issue_1279.jl
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+module Issue1279
+
+using Test
+using Gridap
+using Gridap.ReferenceFEs, Gridap.Geometry, Gridap.Arrays
+using Gridap.Fields, Gridap.CellData, Gridap.FESpaces
+
+# Build a zero-length 1D-in-2D triangulation using only Gridap types, replicating
+# the internal structure of GridapEmbedded's SubFacetTriangulation. This reproduces
+# the bug reported in issue #1279: integrating multifield weak forms on an empty
+# embedded boundary used to fail in BroadcastingFieldOpMap / IntegrationMap.
+
+function empty_sub_facet_triangulation(model)
+  Dp = num_point_dims(model)
+
+  # Empty UnstructuredGrid: 1D segments embedded in 2D space
+  coords     = VectorValue{Dp,Float64}[]      # physical node coords (2D)
+  rcoords    = VectorValue{Dp,Float64}[]      # reference coords in background cell
+  node_ids   = Table(Int32[], Int32[1])       # 0-row face-to-node Table
+  cell_types = Int8[]
+  reffe      = LagrangianRefFE(Float64, SEGMENT, 1)
+  subgrid    = UnstructuredGrid(coords, node_ids, [reffe], cell_types)
+
+  # FaceToFaceGlue: maps 1D facet ref-coords to 2D background cell ref-coords
+  facet_to_rcoords   = lazy_map(Broadcasting(Reindex(rcoords)), node_ids)
+  facet_to_shapefuns = CompressedArray([get_shapefuns(reffe)], Int8[])
+  tface_to_mface_map = lazy_map(linear_combination, facet_to_rcoords, facet_to_shapefuns)
+  tface_to_mface     = Int32[]
+  cell_glue = FaceToFaceGlue(tface_to_mface, tface_to_mface_map, nothing)
+  return GenericTriangulation(subgrid, model, (nothing, nothing, cell_glue))
+end
+
+model = CartesianDiscreteModel((0,1,0,1),(3,3))
+
+# Empty (zero-length) embedded boundary triangulation and its measure.
+G  = empty_sub_facet_triangulation(model)
+dG = Measure(G, 2)
+
+V1 = TestFESpace(model, ReferenceFE(lagrangian, Float64, 1))
+V  = MultiFieldFESpace([V1, V1])
+u1, u2 = get_trial_fe_basis(V)
+v1, v2 = get_fe_basis(V)
+ndof = num_free_dofs(V)
+
+# Helper: assemble a multifield weak form and return its matrix.
+assemble_matrix(a) = get_matrix(AffineFEOperator(a, v->0, V, V))
+
+# Turn construction/integration exceptions into an explicit assertion failure,
+# while leaving any successfully assembled matrix available for the result checks.
+function try_assemble_matrix(a)
+  try
+    (true, assemble_matrix(a))
+  catch
+    (false, nothing)
+  end
+end
+
+@testset "empty boundary" begin
+  @test num_cells(G) == 0
+end
+
+@testset "jump-like multifield form" begin
+  a1((u1,u2),(v1,v2)) = ∫((u1 - u2)*v2)dG
+  assembled, M = try_assemble_matrix(a1)
+  @test assembled
+  if assembled
+    @test size(M) == (ndof, ndof)
+    @test iszero(M)
+  end
+end
+
+@testset "mass-like multifield form" begin
+  a2((u1,u2),(v1,v2)) = ∫(u1*v1 + u1*v1)dG
+  assembled, M = try_assemble_matrix(a2)
+  @test assembled
+  if assembled
+    @test size(M) == (ndof, ndof)
+    @test iszero(M)
+  end
+end
+
+end # module

problem_statement:
Dgt's ANSI styling doesn't match dgdebug's
[The codes that the Skein supports](https://github.com/hlship/dialog-tool/blob/master/src/dialog_tool/skein/ui/ansi.clj#L54):
- 0 disable all
- 1 bold
- 3 italic
- 4 underline
- 30-37 color

[The codes that dgdebug produces](https://github.com/Dialog-IF/dialog/blob/main/src/term_tty.c#L156):
- 0 disable all
- 1 bold
- 4 italic
- 7 reverse
- 36 debug output and logging
- 50 fixed-width
- 38 fg color
- 39 reset fg color
- 48 bg color
- 49 reset bg color

The skein doesn't necessarily need to support the full suite of foreground and background colors, but it would be nice if it supported the rest.

My recommendation:
- 0 disable all
- 1 bold [B]
- 4 italic [I]
- 7 underline [U]
- 36 cyan [CYAN]
- 50 fixed-width [TT]
- Leave all other color support for a future PR

This is not quite in accordance with the ANSI spec (which says 3 is italic and 4 is underline), but if the Skein is only going to get these codes from dgdebug, then what dgdebug does matters more than the spec. (And dgdebug does it this way because 4 usually produces better results than 3 on modern terminals.)

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

# ANSI SGR handling in the Skein UI

The Skein's ANSI SGR interpretation follows the escape codes actually emitted by
the Dialog debugger rather than the strict ANSI code assignments. This addendum
specifies the required behavior precisely and applies to both supported output
forms: styled markup (the styled span output) and the visible pseudo-marker
rendering used for diff output.

## Required SGR codes

- **SGR 0 (reset)** clears every required effect. In marker-form output, a reset
  emits the closing marker for every effect that is still open, in reverse of
  the order in which those effects were opened; any effect still open at the end
  of the text is closed there as well.
- **SGR 1** selects **bold**: styled markup presents the affected text in bold,
  and marker-form output wraps it with `[B] ... [/B]`.
- **SGR 4** requests **italic** text (the debugger uses the ANSI underline code
  for italics): styled markup presents the affected text in italic, and
  marker-form output wraps it with `[I] ... [/I]`.
- **SGR 7** requests **underlined** text (the debugger uses the ANSI
  reverse-video code for underline): styled markup presents the affected text
  underlined, and marker-form output wraps it with `[U] ... [/U]`.
- **SGR 36** selects **cyan**: styled markup visibly marks the affected text as
  cyan — the affected text must be wrapped in styled markup rather than emitted
  as plain text, but no particular selector or other specific representation is
  required. Marker-form output wraps the affected text with
  `[CYAN] ... [/CYAN]`.
- **SGR 50** selects **fixed-width** presentation: styled markup presents the
  affected text in a fixed-width (monospace) style in some way — the affected
  text must be wrapped in styled markup rather than emitted as plain text, but
  no particular selector or other specific representation is required.
  Marker-form output wraps the affected text with `[TT] ... [/TT]`.

## Pre-existing behavior that must be preserved

- The SGR 30–37 named foreground colors (black, red, green, yellow, blue,
  magenta, cyan, white) continue to be rendered as their named colors in both
  output forms, exactly as before this change: in styled markup, the affected
  text is visibly the named color; in marker-form output, the affected text is
  wrapped with the uppercase color-name marker (for example, `[GREEN] ...
  [/GREEN]`).
- A bare `ESC[m` (no parameters) is treated as a reset, as before.
- In the styled span output, each individual text run is rendered with only the
  effects active for that run. When one effect (for example a foreground color)
  is closed and a different effect of the same kind is selected later, the
  earlier effect does not accumulate into the later run. The transition itself
  is unspecified: close the earlier effect with a reset (or with the matching
  closing code, when one is supported) before selecting the new effect. Tests
  exercise such transitions only with the earlier effect of the same kind
  explicitly closed first.

## Unsupported codes

No behavior is required for any SGR code not listed above. In particular, the
extended and default color codes (38, 39, 48, 49) and any other unsupported
codes may be ignored or rendered in any reasonable way. The exact
representation chosen for unsupported codes is not part of the public contract;
hidden tests only check that unsupported codes do not break rendering of the
required codes and do not mandate any particular marker or styling for them.

+  (and (vector? node)

+           (and (string? (first node)) (map? (second node))))))

+(defn- hiccup-leaves
+  "Return text leaves and the Hiccup elements whose styles apply to each leaf."
+  ([node] (hiccup-leaves node []))
+  ([node ancestry]
+   (cond
+     (string? node) [{:text node :ancestry ancestry}]
+     (hiccup-element? node)
+     (let [attrs (when (map? (second node)) (second node))
+           children (drop (if attrs 2 1) node)
+           element {:tag (first node) :attrs attrs}]
+       (mapcat #(hiccup-leaves % (conj ancestry element)) children))
+     (coll? node) (mapcat #(hiccup-leaves % ancestry) node)
+     :else [])))

+                     (-> value (string/replace #"!important\s*$" "") string/lower-case string/trim)])))
+        (string/split (or declarations "") #";"))))

+(defn- inline-declarations [style]
+  (cond

+    (string? style) (declaration-map style)

problem_statement:
Remove context from getIcon and introduce FriendlyState
### Description

Simplify the EntityAPI by removing the need of a context on getIcom and friendlyState.

### Additional context

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

The entity display API must no longer require an Android `Context` where state or icon
display data is computed. The context-free callable surface is:

- a zero-argument `Entity.getIcon()` returning the resolved icon;
- a context-free `Entity.friendlyState(displayPrecision: Int?,
  appendUnitOfMeasurement: Boolean = false)` computing an entity's deferred display state
  as a `FriendlyState` value;
- `FriendlyState.resolve(context)` localizing that value into its final text at render
  time;
- a context-free `EntityDisplayItem.from(entity)` factory.

- **Context-free icon resolution**: `Entity`'s icon must be obtainable from the entity
  alone (its `entityId`, `state`, and `attributes`) without passing any `Context`. Valid
  `mdi:` icon attribute names (including names containing `-` segments) resolve to the
  matching mdi icon; an `mdi:` attribute with an empty or unknown icon name resolves to
  the bookmark fallback icon; a non-`mdi` icon attribute resolves to the domain default
  icon. Removing the `Context` parameter must not change which icon is resolved for any
  entity.

- **Context-free, deferred display state (`FriendlyState`)**: computing an entity's
  user-visible state must not require a `Context`. The entity alone (its domain, device
  class, state, and attributes — including its `unit_of_measurement`) is sufficient input;
  optionally, a registry-supplied display precision and a flag requesting the unit of
  measurement to be appended may refine the result, but no Android `Context` may be needed
  to produce the representation. The result is a `FriendlyState` value that defers all
  localization to a `resolve(context)` step performed at render time, so the final text
  always uses the configuration of the displaying context. For compatibility with existing
  callers, `Entity.friendlyState(context, options, appendUnitOfMeasurement = false)`
  remains available: it takes a `Context` plus optional entity-registry options and
  returns the final localized text directly, computing the `FriendlyState` representation
  and resolving it against the given context. When the registry options carry an explicit
  display precision and/or a suggested display precision for the sensor, the resolved text
  rounds a numeric sensor state using the explicit display precision when present,
  otherwise the suggested display precision. The supported public `FriendlyState` forms
  are:
  - `Literal` — raw text needing no localization (e.g. a precision-formatted number or a
    title-cased state); resolving returns it unchanged.
  - `Resource` — a reference to a translated state string resource (the `state_*` strings
    mapped from the entity's domain, device class, and state); resolving returns
    `context.getString(resId)`, localized with the given context.
  - `RelativeTime` — a timestamp state (e.g. an ISO timestamp) whose instant is captured
    and shown relative to *now*; it is formatted as an abbreviated relative time span
    only when resolved, so the displayed description stays current.
  - `WithUnit` — wraps another `FriendlyState` together with the entity's unit of
    measurement; resolving appends the unit after the resolved state, separated by a
    space.

- **Entity-side form selection**: the `FriendlyState` produced for an entity is chosen
  from its domain, device class, state, and attributes only:
  - a state with a known translation for its domain or device class produces a
    `Resource` carrying that translation (e.g. a locked lock, an open door binary sensor,
    or an `unavailable` state);
  - an ISO timestamp state produces `RelativeTime` capturing the parsed instant when the
    platform supports timestamp parsing (API 26+), and a `Literal` of the unchanged state
    below that platform level, relative formatting happens only at `resolve` time;
  - otherwise, a numeric sensor state with a supplied display precision produces a
    `Literal` of the value rounded to that precision; without a precision, or for a
    state with no translation, the `Literal` keeps the title-cased state unchanged;
  - `WithUnit` is produced only when unit appending is requested and the entity has a
    non-blank `unit_of_measurement` attribute, wrapping the otherwise-selected form.

- **Context-free display-item construction**: an `EntityDisplayItem` must be buildable
  from an `Entity` alone, without any `Context`. The displayed name and icon must be
  derived from the entity's own data (its `friendly_name` attribute, falling back to its
  `entityId`, and the icon-resolution rules above) and must not depend on resolving any
  string resource from a context.

  callers, `Entity.friendlyState(context, options, appendUnitOfMeasurement = false)`
  remains available: it takes a `Context` plus optional entity-registry options and
  returns the final localized text directly, computing the `FriendlyState` representation
  and resolving it against the given context. When the registry options carry an explicit
  display precision and/or a suggested display precision for the sensor, the resolved text
  rounds a numeric sensor state using the explicit display precision when present,
  otherwise the suggested display precision. The supported public `FriendlyState` forms
  are:
  - `Literal` — raw text needing no localization (e.g. a precision-formatted number or a
    title-cased state); resolving returns it unchanged.
  - `Resource` — a reference to a translated state string resource (the `state_*` strings
    mapped from the entity's domain, device class, and state); resolving returns
    `context.getString(resId)`, localized with the given context.
  - `RelativeTime` — a timestamp state (e.g. an ISO timestamp) whose instant is captured
    and shown relative to *now*; it is formatted as an abbreviated relative time span
    only when resolved, so the displayed description stays current.
  - `WithUnit` — wraps another `FriendlyState` together with the entity's unit of
    measurement; resolving appends the unit after the resolved state, separated by a
    space.

- **Entity-side form selection**: the `FriendlyState` produced for an entity is chosen
  from its domain, device class, state, and attributes only:
  - a state with a known translation for its domain or device class produces a
    `Resource` carrying that translation (e.g. a locked lock, an open door binary sensor,
    or an `unavailable` state);
  - an ISO timestamp state produces `RelativeTime` capturing the parsed instant when the
    platform supports timestamp parsing (API 26+), and a `Literal` of the unchanged state
    below that platform level, relative formatting happens only at `resolve` time;
  - otherwise, a numeric sensor state with a supplied display precision produces a
    `Literal` of the value rounded to that precision; without a precision, or for a
    state with no translation, the `Literal` keeps the title-cased state unchanged;
  - `WithUnit` is produced only when unit appending is requested and the entity has a
    non-blank `unit_of_measurement` attribute, wrapping the otherwise-selected form.

- **Context-free display-item construction**: an `EntityDisplayItem` must be buildable
  from an `Entity` alone, without any `Context`. The displayed name and icon must be
  derived from the entity's own data (its `friendly_name` attribute, falling back to its
  `entityId`, and the icon-resolution rules above) and must not depend on resolving any
  string resource from a context.

+/**
+ * Entity state prepared for display without a context: string resources and time-relative
+ * values are resolved to their final localized text with [resolve] at render time, so the
+ * translation always uses the configuration of the displaying context.
+ */
+@Immutable
+sealed interface FriendlyState {
+    /** Resolves the display text, localizing with [context]. */
+    fun resolve(context: Context): String
+
+    /** A translated state, see the `state_*` string resources. */
+    data class Resource(@StringRes val resId: Int) : FriendlyState {
+        override fun resolve(context: Context): String = context.getString(resId)
+    }
+
+    /** Text needing no localization, like a precision-formatted number. */
+    data class Literal(val value: String) : FriendlyState {
+        override fun resolve(context: Context): String = value
+    }
+
+    /** A timestamp state shown relative to now, resolved at render time so it stays current. */
+    data class RelativeTime(val epochMillis: Long) : FriendlyState {
+        override fun resolve(context: Context): String = DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(
+            epochMillis,
+            System.currentTimeMillis(),
+            0,
+            DateUtils.FORMAT_ABBREV_ALL,
+        ).toString()
+    }
+
+    /** A state with its unit of measurement appended. */
+    data class WithUnit(val state: FriendlyState, val unit: String) : FriendlyState {
+        override fun resolve(context: Context): String = "${state.resolve(context)} $unit"
+    }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Core [friendlyState] resolution, exposed to display consumers through `EntityDisplayItem.state`.
+ * Context-free: the returned [FriendlyState] localizes at render time.
+ */
+internal fun Entity.friendlyState(displayPrecision: Int?, appendUnitOfMeasurement: Boolean = false): FriendlyState {
+    val resource = stateResource()
+    val friendlyState = when {
+        resource != null -> FriendlyState.Resource(resource)
+        else -> relativeTimeState()
+            ?: precisionState(displayPrecision)
+            ?: FriendlyState.Literal(titleCasedState())
+    }
+
+    if (appendUnitOfMeasurement) {
+        val unit = attributes["unit_of_measurement"]?.toString()
+        if (unit?.isNotBlank() == true) {
+            return FriendlyState.WithUnit(friendlyState, unit)
+        }
+    }
+    return friendlyState
+}

+private fun Entity.relativeTimeState(): FriendlyState.RelativeTime? {
+    if (!SdkVersion.isAtLeast(Build.VERSION_CODES.O)) return null
+    return try {
+        val stateInMillis = ZonedDateTime.parse(state, DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME)
+            .toInstant()
+            .toEpochMilli()
+        FriendlyState.RelativeTime(stateInMillis)
+    } catch (e: DateTimeParseException) {
+        /* Not a timestamp */
+        null
+    }
+}

+private fun Entity.precisionState(displayPrecision: Int?): FriendlyState.Literal? {
+    if (displayPrecision == null || !canSupportPrecision()) return null
+    return FriendlyState.Literal(String.format(Locale.getDefault(), "%.${displayPrecision}f", state.toDouble()))
+}

+private fun Entity.titleCasedState(): String = state.split("_").joinToString(" ") { word ->
+    word.replaceFirstChar {
+        if (it.isLowerCase()) it.titlecase(Locale.getDefault()) else it.toString()
+    }
+}

+package io.homeassistant.companion.android.common.data.integration
+
+import android.content.Context

+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals

+/**
+ * Covers context-free icon and display-state behavior through the entity's public APIs.
+ */
+class EntityGetIconTest {
+
+    @AfterEach
+    fun tearDown() {
+        // A leftover static mock must not leak into (or out of) any test
+        clearStaticMockk(DateUtils::class)
+        unmockkAll()
+    }
+
+    private val baseDateTime = LocalDateTime.of(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
+
+    private fun createEntity(
+        entityId: String = "sensor.test",
+        state: String = "42",
+        attributes: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap(),
+    ) = Entity(
+        entityId = entityId,
+        state = state,
+        attributes = attributes,
+        lastChanged = baseDateTime,
+        lastUpdated = baseDateTime,
+    )
+
+    @Nested
+    inner class GetIcon {
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a valid mdi icon attribute with dashes when getting icon then returns the matching mdi icon`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(attributes = mapOf("icon" to "mdi:car-traction-control"))
+
+            assertEquals(Icon.cmd_car_traction_control, entity.getIcon())
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a mdi icon attribute with multiple dashes when getting icon then returns the matching mdi icon`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(attributes = mapOf("icon" to "mdi:ab-testing"))
+
+            assertEquals(Icon.cmd_ab_testing, entity.getIcon())
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a mdi icon attribute without a name when getting icon then returns the bookmark fallback`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(attributes = mapOf("icon" to "mdi:"))
+
+            assertEquals(Icon.cmd_bookmark, entity.getIcon())
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given an unknown mdi icon attribute when getting icon then returns the bookmark fallback`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(attributes = mapOf("icon" to "mdi:this-icon-does-not-exist"))
+
+            assertEquals(Icon.cmd_bookmark, entity.getIcon())
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Nested
+    inner class Resolve {
+
+        @BeforeEach
+        fun setUpResolve() {
+            // Entity display state reads the SDK level; pin a supported platform for these tests
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 26
+        }
+
+        @AfterEach
+        fun tearDownResolve() {
+            SdkVersion.resetSdkInt()
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a raw value state when resolving then returns the value unchanged`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.test", state = "20.13")
+            assertEquals("20.13", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a translated string resource state when resolving then localizes with the given context`() {
+            val context = mockk<Context>()
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "lock.test", state = "locked")
+            every { context.getString(commonR.string.state_locked) } returns "Vergrendeld"
+            val otherContext = mockk<Context>()
+            every { otherContext.getString(commonR.string.state_locked) } returns "Locked"
+            val displayState = entity.friendlyState(null)
+
+            assertEquals("Vergrendeld", displayState.resolve(context))
+            assertEquals("Locked", displayState.resolve(otherContext))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a timestamp state when resolving then formats the captured instant at resolution time`() {
+            val epochMillis = 1_700_000_000_000L
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 26
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.sun_next_rising", state = "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z")
+            mockkStatic(DateUtils::class)
+            try {
+                every { DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(any(), any(), any(), any()) } answers {
+                    firstArg<Long>().toString()
+                }
+
+                assertEquals(epochMillis.toString(), entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockk()))
+            } finally {
+                clearStaticMockk(DateUtils::class)
+                SdkVersion.resetSdkInt()
+            }
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a state with a unit of measurement when resolving then appends the unit after the resolved state`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "sensor.temperature",
+                state = "20.13",
+                attributes = mapOf("unit_of_measurement" to "°C"),
+            )
+            assertEquals("20.13 °C", entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Nested
+    inner class ContextFreeState {
+
+        private lateinit var initialLocale: Locale
+
+        @BeforeEach
+        fun setUpContextFreeState() {
+            initialLocale = Locale.getDefault()
+            // Precision formatting uses the default locale; pin it so assertions are stable
+            Locale.setDefault(Locale.US)
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 26
+        }
+
+        @AfterEach
+        fun tearDownContextFreeState() {
+            Locale.setDefault(initialLocale)
+            SdkVersion.resetSdkInt()
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a translated domain state when computing the display state then resolves with the supplied context`() {
+            val mockContext = mockk<Context>()
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "lock.front_door", state = "locked")
+
+            every { mockContext.getString(commonR.string.state_locked) } returns "Locked"
+            assertEquals("Locked", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockContext))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a binary sensor device class state when computing the display state then resource needs no context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "binary_sensor.front_door",
+                state = "on",
+                attributes = mapOf("device_class" to "door"),
+            )
+
+            val context = mockk<Context>()
+            every { context.getString(commonR.string.state_open) } returns "Open here"
+            assertEquals("Open here", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(context))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given an unavailable state when computing the display state then resource needs no context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.temperature", state = "unavailable")
+
+            val context = mockk<Context>()
+            every { context.getString(commonR.string.state_unavailable) } returns "Unavailable here"
+            assertEquals("Unavailable here", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(context))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a custom sensor state when computing the display state then literal is title cased without a context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.washing_machine", state = "running_cycle")
+
+            assertEquals("Running Cycle", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a timestamp state on api 26 when computing the display state then instant is held for relative resolution`() {
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 26
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.sun_next_rising", state = "2024-01-01T06:30:00+00:00")
+            val expectedMillis = ZonedDateTime.parse(entity.state).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
+
+            val displayState = entity.friendlyState(null)
+
+            mockkStatic(DateUtils::class)
+            try {
+                every { DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(any(), any(), any(), any()) } answers {
+                    firstArg<Long>().toString()
+                }
+                assertEquals(expectedMillis.toString(), displayState.resolve(mockk()))
+            } finally {
+                clearStaticMockk(DateUtils::class)
+            }
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a timestamp state below api 26 when computing the display state then instant is not derived`() {
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 25
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.sun_next_rising", state = "2024-01-01T06:30:00+00:00")
+
+            assertEquals("2024-01-01T06:30:00+00:00", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a numeric sensor state and precision when computing the display state then literal is rounded without a context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.temperature", state = "20.126456")
+
+            assertEquals("20.13", entity.friendlyState(2).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a numeric sensor state and null precision when computing the display state then literal is unchanged`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.temperature", state = "20.126456")
+
+            assertEquals("20.126456", entity.friendlyState(null).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a unit of measurement when appending to a custom state then unit wraps the literal without a context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "sensor.washing_machine",
+                state = "running_cycle",
+                attributes = mapOf("unit_of_measurement" to "cycles"),
+            )
+
+            assertEquals("Running Cycle cycles", entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a device class state when appending unit then unit wraps the resource without a context`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "binary_sensor.front_door",
+                state = "on",
+                attributes = mapOf("device_class" to "door", "unit_of_measurement" to "doors"),
+            )
+
+            val context = mockk<Context>()
+            every { context.getString(commonR.string.state_open) } returns "Open"
+            assertEquals("Open doors", entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true).resolve(context))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a blank unit of measurement when appending then the display state is not wrapped`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "sensor.washing_machine",
+                state = "running_cycle",
+                attributes = mapOf("unit_of_measurement" to "  "),
+            )
+
+            assertEquals("Running Cycle", entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given no unit of measurement when appending then the display state is not wrapped`() {
+            val entity = createEntity(entityId = "sensor.washing_machine", state = "running_cycle")
+
+            assertEquals("Running Cycle", entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true).resolve(mockk()))
+        }
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given a timestamp state and unit when computing the display state then instant formats only at resolve time`() {
+            SdkVersion.sdkInt = 26
+            val entity = createEntity(
+                entityId = "sensor.spare_next",
+                state = "2024-01-01T06:30:00+00:00",
+                attributes = mapOf("unit_of_measurement" to "occurrences"),
+            )
+            val expectedMillis = ZonedDateTime.parse(entity.state).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
+
+            val friendlyState = entity.friendlyState(null, appendUnitOfMeasurement = true)
+
+            mockkStatic(DateUtils::class)
+            try {
+                every { DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString(any(), any(), any(), any()) } answers {
+                    firstArg<Long>().toString()
+                }
+                assertEquals("$expectedMillis occurrences", friendlyState.resolve(mockk()))
+            } finally {
+                clearStaticMockk(DateUtils::class)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Nested
+    inner class ContextFreeDisplay {
+
+        @Test
+        fun `Given an entity when building its display item then name and icon are built without a context`() {
+            val entity = Entity(
+                entityId = "light.living_room",
+                state = "on",
+                attributes = mapOf("friendly_name" to "Living Room Light"),
+                lastChanged = baseDateTime,
+                lastUpdated = baseDateTime,
+            )
+
+            val item = EntityDisplayItem.from(entity)
+
+            assertEquals("light.living_room", item.entityId)
+            assertEquals("Living Room Light", item.name)
+            assertEquals(Icon2.cmd_lightbulb, item.icon)
+
+            // `Entity` is a data class, so an instance whose id cannot appear in
+            // `getString` is not `equals` to the displayed entity; asserting its name
+            // is displayed proves the name comes from the entity rather than from any
+            // `context.getString(entity.entityId)` lookup.
+            val unresolvableEntity = entity.copy(entityId = "switch.other_room")
+            assertTrue(unresolvableEntity != entity)
+            assertEquals("Living Room Light", EntityDisplayItem.from(unresolvableEntity).name)
+        }
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Rename `RewardAccount` to `Account`
With CIP-159 it will no longer be accurate to call it "reward account", since it is no longer just about rewards.
We will also need to rename `raCredential` to `aCredential` and `raNetwork` to `aNetwork`

As usual we should add `RewardAccount{raNetwork, raCredential}` pattern synonym with deprecation. This applies to all other helpers that will need to be renamed due to this rebranding.

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum clarifies the public naming and compatibility contract for the rebranding of the reward-account type. It refines the rename described in the base problem statement into the precise names and shapes that are required. Renaming any helper, accessor, record field, or serialized key affects only names, not behavior: serialization formats and ledger semantics remain unchanged.

## Core account-address type (`Cardano.Ledger.Address`, cardano-ledger-core)

- The existing type for stake/reward accounts is renamed from `RewardAccount` to `AccountAddress`. It is a record with exactly two fields:
  - `aaNetworkId :: Network`
  - `aaAccountId :: AccountId`
- `AccountId` is a newtype wrapper around `Credential Staking` with constructor `AccountId` and selector `unAccountId`.
- `AccountAddress` keeps all of the existing derived/existing class instances, and existing instance behavior is preserved. In particular:
  - Its binary serialization is unchanged: the CBOR/raw wire format (header byte with the `0xE0` prefix bits, network nibble and credential-kind bit, followed by the credential) is byte-for-byte identical to the previous `RewardAccount` encoding.
  - Its external (CBOR) round-trip is preserved.
  - Its JSON encoding is unchanged: an object with keys `network` and `credential`, i.e. the same shape as the previous `RewardAccount` JSON.

The following canonically named functions and lenses are provided:

- `serialiseAccountAddress :: AccountAddress -> ByteString`
- `deserialiseAccountAddress :: ByteString -> Maybe AccountAddress`
- `putAccountAddress :: AccountAddress -> Put`
- `decodeAccountAddress :: AddressBuffer b => b -> m AccountAddress`
- `fromCborAccountAddress :: Decoder s AccountAddress`
- `accountAddressAccountIdL :: Lens' AccountAddress AccountId`
- `accountAddressCredentialL :: Lens' AccountAddress (Credential Staking)`
- `accountAddressNetworkIdL :: Lens' AccountAddress Network`

### Backwards compatibility

Use of the old names continues to work with deprecation warnings, and each deprecated name behaves identically to its canonical replacement:

- A pattern synonym on `AccountAddress` is provided:
  `pattern RewardAccount :: Network -> Credential Staking -> AccountAddress`
  with record-pattern fields `raNetwork :: Network` and `raCredential :: Credential Staking`. Both construction via `RewardAccount n cred` and pattern matching via `RewardAccount {raNetwork, raCredential}` are supported (therefore `{-# LANGUAGE PatternSynonyms #-}` is used in declaring modules).
- The following are retained as deprecated aliases:
  - `serialiseRewardAccount` (alias of `serialiseAccountAddress`)
  - `deserialiseRewardAccount` (alias of `deserialiseAccountAddress`)
  - `putRewardAccount` (alias of `putAccountAddress`)
  - `decodeRewardAccount` (alias of `decodeAccountAddress`)
  - `fromCborRewardAccount` (alias of `fromCborAccountAddress`)
  - `rewardAccountCredentialL` (alias of `accountAddressCredentialL`)
  - `rewardAccountNetworkL` (alias of `accountAddressNetworkIdL`)
- The `RewardAccount` compatibility pattern is complete for `AccountAddress`, so an exhaustive match using it remains exhaustive under the project's warning discipline. Every pattern synonym definition must carry an explicit complete type signature.

## Stake pool state and pool parameters

- In `StakePoolParams` and `PoolParams`, the reward-account field is renamed from `sppRewardAccount :: RewardAccount` to `sppAccountAddress :: AccountAddress`, and the `PoolParams` pattern synonym field is renamed from `ppRewardAccount` to `ppAccountAddress`.
- In `StakePoolState`, the field `spsRewardAccount :: Credential Staking` is renamed to `spsAccountAddress :: Credential Staking` (its type is unchanged), and the lens `spsRewardAccountL` is renamed to `spsAccountAddressL`.
- `mkStakePoolState` and `stakePoolStateToStakePoolParams` keep their behavior, now using the renamed fields.
- The JSON encoding of `StakePoolParams` now uses the keys `poolId` (instead of `publicKey`) and `accountAddress` (instead of `rewardAccount`). For backwards compatibility, reading also accepts the previous keys `publicKey` and `rewardAccount`.

## Test-support and derived-consumer renames

Throughout test-support and Imp test infrastructure, corresponding helpers that mention reward accounts are renamed to the account-address vocabulary, for example: `registerAccount` to `registerAccountAddress`, `getRewardAccountFor` to `getAccountAddressFor`, and the pool/governance test helpers `registerPoolWithRewardAccount` to `registerPoolWithAccountAddress`, `expectRegisteredRewardAccount` to `expectRegisteredAccountAddress`, and `mkProposalWithRewardAccount` to `mkProposalWithAccountAddress`.

Downstream names that embed the old terminology are renamed according to the same scheme, for example the Plutus-translation helper `transRewardAccount` is provided canonically as `transAccountAddress` (with the old name retained as a deprecated alias), and the delegation predicate-failure constructor `StakeKeyHasNonZeroRewardAccountBalanceDELEG` is renamed to `StakeKeyHasNonZeroAccountBalanceDELEG`. In general, wherever public or test-support names use the `RewardAccount`/`rewardAccount` terminology or `ra`-prefixed account record accessors, they are renamed to the corresponding `AccountAddress`/`accountAddress` terminology or `aa`-prefixed accessors, while retaining their behavior and, where applicable, their serialized encodings.

+* Rename `RewardAccount` to `AccountAddress`.

+    + `decodeRewardAccount` → `decodeAccountAddress`

problem_statement:
Remove `NoThunks` instance for Predicate failures
There are some predicate failures that have `NoThunks` instances for some strange reasons. They need to go.
Same applies to all `ContextError`s for all eras

### Additional contract requirements

- The removal covers the predicate failure types of the Shelley-based ledger rules of the Shelley, Allegra, Alonzo, Babbage, Conway and Dijkstra eras, the chain-level `ChainPredicateFailure`, and the predicate failure types of the TPraos protocol rules (including `ChainTransitionError`).
- The removal covers the `ContextError` type of every era that defines one (Alonzo, Babbage, Conway and Dijkstra).
- Predicate failure types of the Byron executable-spec rules keep their `NoThunks` instances.
- The payload types `FailureDescription` and `TagMismatchDescription` of the Alonzo UTxOS rules keep their `NoThunks` instances.

problem_statement:
Fix classMethod-related problems
I've had this on my to-do list for a while, but haven't gotten around to creating an issue for it. In #4909, we realized that there are two issues with class methods. First, some of the renderers don't properly create them. E.g. the Python renderer just creates a normal instance method. Second, we don't actually have a way to call class methods. These should be fairly simple fixes, I'm hoping.

### Additional contract requirements

This task covers class-level (static) methods and class-qualified calls in the public OO code-generation interface in `Drasil.GOOL`.

- A class-level method declaration is made with the existing `method` operation: `method name visibility classLevel returnType parameters body`.  `classLevel` identifies the declaration as static; `instanceLevel` continues to identify an instance method.
- The interface must export class-qualified call operations with these argument forms:
  - `classMethodCall returnType classType name positionalArguments`
  - `classMethodCallNamedArgs returnType classType name namedArguments`
  - `classMethodCallMixedArgs returnType classType name positionalArguments namedArguments`
  - `classMethodCallNoParams returnType classType name`
  The `classType` is the class that qualifies the call.  These operations do not take, create, or use an implicit instance receiver.
- C++, C#, Java, Python, and Swift must render class-level declarations and class-qualified calls.  In particular, Python class-level methods use Python's static-method convention, and every target qualifies a class-method call with the containing class rather than an object receiver.
- A GOOL program that declares class-level methods and makes positional and zero-argument class-qualified calls renders correctly in C++, C#, Java, Python, and Swift. The named-argument and mixed-argument class-call constructors are exported and must type-check when used in a GOOL program. The C++ output includes the class declaration in a header and build support for it.

export PATH=/opt/ghc/9.8.4/bin:/usr/local/cargo/bin:/root/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH
set +e
(
set -e
cd /Drasil/code && stack build --no-terminal
cd /Drasil && owned=$(mktemp -d) && for f in cpp/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.cpp cpp/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.hpp cpp/HelloWorld/Makefile csharp/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.cs java/HelloWorld/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.java python/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.py swift/HelloWorld/main.swift; do mkdir -p "$owned/$(dirname code/stable/gooltest/$f)" && cp "code/stable/gooltest/$f" "$owned/code/stable/gooltest/$f"; done && for l in cpp csharp java python swift; do rm -rf "code/stable/gooltest/$l/HelloWorld" && git archive HEAD "code/stable/gooltest/$l/HelloWorld" | tar -x -C /Drasil; done && cp -r "$owned/code/stable/gooltest/." code/stable/gooltest/ && rm -rf "$owned"
cd /Drasil/code && rm -rf build/gooltest logs/gooltest_log.log && stack build --no-terminal "drasil-code:exe:codegenTest" && mkdir -p build/gooltest logs && (cd build/gooltest && stack exec --no-nix-pure -- codegenTest)
cd /Drasil/code && for f in build/gooltest/cpp/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.cpp build/gooltest/cpp/HelloWorld/HelloWorld.hpp; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then keep=1; case "$f" in *.hpp) keep=0;; esac; awk -v keep=$keep '/^#include "HelloWorld[.]hpp"$/ { if (keep && !seen) { seen=1; print; next } skip=1; next } skip && /^$/ { skip=0; next } { skip=0; print }' "$f" > "$f.norm" && mv "$f.norm" "$f"; fi; done
cd /Drasil/code && if diff --strip-trailing-cr -r -X ../.gitignore stable/gooltest/ build/gooltest/ > logs/gooltest_log.log 2>&1; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; echo "target: drasil-code:exe:codegenTest (GOOL codegen + stable-diff)"; echo "diff exit: $rc"; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ ! -s logs/gooltest_log.log ]; then echo "result: PASS (generated matches stable)"; else echo "result: FAIL (generated != stable)"; cat logs/gooltest_log.log; false; fi
)
_rebench_status=$?
if [ "$_rebench_status" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '\nRESULT: PASS (exit=0)\n'
else
  printf '\nRESULT: FAIL (exit=%s)\n' "$_rebench_status"
fi
exit "$_rebench_status"

problem_statement:
Fix `arrayDec` for Python, Julia, and Swift
In #5001 I "fixed" `arrayDec` for Python, Julia, and Swift. `arrayDec` takes an argument for the size of the array, and is supposed to use this argument to allocate the correct amount of space at declaration-time. These three renderers, however, would always assign the variable to `[]`, regardless of the size passed. This broke parity with the other renderers, making it so that writing to `arr[2]` after declaring `arr` as an array of at least size `3` works in C++, Java, and C#, but not the other three languages. [HIDDEN] It's not the most idiomatic, but it fixes the issue.

Then from talking with Daniel, I realized that sometimes, arrays hold things that aren't integers! And  we shouldn't try to put the integer `0` in an array of non-integers. Because of this, we should update these implementations to take note the type of the array and fill it with a suitable default value. This value should be obvious for most values, except for objects. The "default value" for an array of objects is not super clear, and `null` might be the best option. The user shouldn't write a program that reads from an array element before writing to it anyway, so it shouldn't matter too much what we choose as a default.

### Additional contract requirements

# Sized array declarations

`arrayDec` declares a sized array whose elements are writable immediately
after the declaration:

```haskell
arrayDec :: Integer -> SVariable r -> r ScopeData -> MS (r smt)
```

The caller supplies only the number of elements, the target array variable,
and its scope. Any initial element values are chosen by the implementation,
not passed by the caller.

For each of the Python, Julia, and Swift code generators, a sized array
declaration must allocate the requested number of writable elements at
declaration time. As a result, every index within the declared range can be
assigned immediately after the declaration, without any earlier append or
resize operation, and an indexing assignment to any element of the declared
range must be valid in the generated program for all three target languages.
This is a requirement on the observable behavior of the generated program,
not on any particular allocation strategy or syntax used to achieve it.

Any elements that are pre-filled at declaration time must be initialized with
values appropriate for the array's element type. In particular, an array whose
element type is not integer must not cause an integer (whole-number) literal to
be emitted as one of its initial elements. The choice of the specific default
element value is otherwise left to the implementation.

Then from talking with Daniel, I realized that sometimes, arrays hold things that aren't integers! And  we shouldn't try to put the integer `0` in an array of non-integers. Because of this, we should update these implementations to take note the type of the array and fill it with a suitable default value. This value should be obvious for most values, except for objects. The "default value" for an array of objects is not super clear, and `null` might be the best option. The user shouldn't write a program that reads from an array element before writing to it anyway, so it shouldn't matter too much what we choose as a default.

# Sized array declarations

`arrayDec` declares a sized array whose elements are writable immediately
after the declaration:

```haskell
arrayDec :: Integer -> SVariable r -> r ScopeData -> MS (r smt)
```

The caller supplies only the number of elements, the target array variable,
and its scope. Any initial element values are chosen by the implementation,
not passed by the caller.

For each of the Python, Julia, and Swift code generators, a sized array
declaration must allocate the requested number of writable elements at
declaration time. As a result, every index within the declared range can be
assigned immediately after the declaration, without any earlier append or
resize operation, and an indexing assignment to any element of the declared
range must be valid in the generated program for all three target languages.
This is a requirement on the observable behavior of the generated program,
not on any particular allocation strategy or syntax used to achieve it.

Any elements that are pre-filled at declaration time must be initialized with
values appropriate for the array's element type. In particular, an array whose
element type is not integer must not cause an integer (whole-number) literal to
be emitted as one of its initial elements. The choice of the specific default
element value is otherwise left to the implementation.

+-- representation-neutral structural guards always run; when a target
+-- toolchain is installed, the extracted program text additionally executes
+-- as a witness with per-marker size assertions, and otherwise the fallback
+-- checks that each declared array participates in an element write.
+sizedArrayContractTest :: TestName -> FilePath -> System.OsPath.OsPath ->
+  FilePath -> FileLayout -> String -> String ->
+  (DeclarationBundle -> String) -> (FilePath -> String) -> TestTree
+sizedArrayContractTest testName buildDir buildPath outputPath layout tool suffix
+    makeWitness commandFor = singleTest testName $ GeneratedProgramTest do
+  removePathForcibly buildDir
+  createDirectoryIfMissing True buildDir
+  writeFiles NeverOverwrite buildPath layout
+  output <- readFile outputPath
+  case isolateContract output of
+    Left problem -> pure $ Just problem
+    Right bundle -> case (markerGuards bundle, writesPresentCheck bundle) of
+      (Just problem, _) -> pure $ Just problem
+      (Nothing, Just problem) -> pure $ Just problem
+      (Nothing, Nothing) -> do
+        available <- (== 0) <$> runShell
+          ("command -v " ++ tool ++ " >/dev/null 2>&1")
+        if available
+          then do
+            let witnessPath = buildDir ++ "/sized_array_witness" ++ suffix
+                logPath = buildDir ++ "/sized_array_witness.log"
+            writeFile witnessPath (makeWitness bundle)
+            status <- runShell $ commandFor witnessPath ++
+              " >" ++ logPath ++ " 2>&1"
+            if status == 0
+              then pure Nothing
+              else do
+                details <- readFile logPath
+                pure $ Just $ "standalone sized-array declarations failed: "
+                  ++ details
+          else pure $ writesPresentCheck bundle
+
+-- | Extract the sections between the language-neutral marker pairs and parse
+-- the embedded marker specifications.
+isolateContract :: String -> Either String DeclarationBundle
+isolateContract source = do
+  declarations <- sectionBetween
+    "ARRAY_DEC begin sized array declarations"
+    "ARRAY_DEC end sized array declarations"
+  writes <- sectionBetween
+    "ARRAY_DEC use sized element writes"
+    "ARRAY_DEC end sized element writes"
+  specs <- parseSpecs declarations
+  pure (DeclarationBundle specs declarations writes)
+  where
+    sectionBetween beginMarker endMarker =
+      case dropWhile (not . isInfixOf beginMarker) (lines source) of
+        [] -> Left $ "start marker was not rendered: " ++ beginMarker
+        (_ : afterBegin) ->
+          let section = takeWhile (not . isInfixOf endMarker) afterBegin
+          in if not (any (isInfixOf endMarker) afterBegin)
+              then Left $ "end marker was not rendered: " ++ endMarker
+              else if null section
+                then Left $ "empty section after marker: " ++ beginMarker
+                else Right (unlines section)
+
+-- | Parse the typed, sized, named marker specifications from a declaration
+-- section.
+parseSpecs :: String -> Either String [MarkerSpec]
+parseSpecs section = traverse parse (mapMaybe markerLine (lines section))
+  where
+    markerLine line = stripPrefix "ARRAY_DEC" (dropCommentOpener line)
+    dropCommentOpener = dropWhile (`elem` "#/* ")
+    parse spec = case words spec of
+      [typeName, sizeText, variable]
+        | not (null sizeText) && all (`elem` ['0'..'9']) sizeText ->
+            Right (MarkerSpec typeName (read sizeText) variable)
+      _ -> Left $ "malformed sized-array marker: " ++ spec
+
+-- | Structural guards that rely only on the marker expectations.  These run
+-- regardless of whether a witness executed, because a failed parser here is
+-- evidence even when a toolchain was available: the declaration text is the
+-- only trace of the padding values.  Each guard rejects a whole-number
+-- literal being emitted directly as an initial element of a noninteger array
+-- (the contract explicitly forbids that), while staying silent for every
+-- other value, which may be as exotic as the implementation chooses.
+markerGuards :: DeclarationBundle -> Maybe String
+markerGuards bundle = firstJust (concatMap guardSpec (bundleSpecs bundle))
+  where
+    firstJust = foldr (\candidate found -> maybe found Just candidate) Nothing
+    sections = declarationSections (bundleDeclarations bundle)
+    codeLines = filter (\l -> isNothing (markerRef l))
+      (lines (bundleDeclarations bundle))
+    markerRef l = stripPrefix "ARRAY_DEC" (dropWhile (`elem` "#/* ") l)
+    isNothing Nothing = True
+    isNothing _ = False
+    guardSpec spec = doubleTypeEvidence ++ wholeNumberGuards
+      where
+        ownSection = maybe [] id (lookup (specName spec) sections)
+        doubleTypeEvidence
+          | specType spec == "double" =
+              [require (any (arrayTypeEvidence (specName spec)) ownSection)
+                ("double array " ++ specName spec ++
+                  " carried no element-type evidence in its declaration: " ++
+                  unlines ownSection)]
+          | otherwise = []
+        wholeNumberGuards
+          | specType spec == "int" = []
+          | otherwise =
+              [require (not (any (wholeNumberPadFor (specName spec)) ownSection))
+                ("whole-number literal was emitted as an initial element of "
+                  ++ specName spec ++ " (" ++ specType spec ++
+                  "): " ++ unlines ownSection)]
+    require condition message =
+      if condition then Nothing else Just message
+
+-- | Split the declaration section on the marker comment lines themselves, so
+-- each array's statement list is exactly the lines between its own marker and
+-- the next marker.
+declarationSections :: String -> [(String, [String])]
+declarationSections source = go Nothing [] (lines source)
+  where
+    go current acc [] = maybe acc (finish acc) current
+    go current acc (line : rest) =
+      case stripPrefix "ARRAY_DEC" (dropWhile (`elem` "#/* ") line) of
+        Just specText ->
+          let acc' = maybe acc (finish acc) current
+          in case words specText of
+            [_, _, variable] -> go (Just (variable, [])) acc' rest
+            _ -> go current acc' rest
+        Nothing -> go (fmap (\(name, ls) -> (name, ls ++ [line])) current)
+          acc rest
+    finish acc (name, ls) = acc ++ [(name, ls)]
+
+-- | A declaration line for the named array carries evidence that its element
+-- type is floating-point: an explicit floating type spelling attached to the
+-- array, or a decimal literal among the array's initial values.
+arrayTypeEvidence :: String -> String -> Bool
+arrayTypeEvidence variable line =
+  any (`isInfixOf` compact) (map (variable ++)
+    [": [Double", ": [Float", "[]float", "[]double"]) ||
+  any (`isInfixOf` compact)
+    ["[Double](", "[Float](", "fill(0f", "fill(0.", "fill(0F",
+      "repeat(0f", "repeat(0.", "Float64[", "Float32[",
+      variable ++ ":", "=" ++ variable] ||
+  hasDecimalLiteral compact
+  where
+    compact = filter (`notElem` " \t\r\n") line
+
+-- | Whether some decimal point sits between two digits.
+hasDecimalLiteral :: String -> Bool
+hasDecimalLiteral (a : '.' : b : rest) = digit a && digit b ||
+  hasDecimalLiteral ('.' : b : rest)
+hasDecimalLiteral (_ : rest) = hasDecimalLiteral rest
+hasDecimalLiteral [] = False
+
+digit :: Char -> Bool
+digit c = c `elem` ['0'..'9']
+
+-- | A line in the array's own section that emits a standalone whole-number
+-- literal into the array's initial contents.  Only bare whole-number literals
+-- are rejected, in the common element-producing positions (appended items,
+-- repeated fill arguments); decimals, typed literals, null-like placeholders,
+-- and every other value pass through untouched so the default choice stays
+-- with the implementation.
+wholeNumberPadFor :: String -> String -> Bool
+wholeNumberPadFor variable line = not typeAnchored &&
+  any (any startsWholeValue) probePositions
+  where
+    typeAnchored =
+      any (`isInfixOf` filter (/= ' ') line) [variable ++ ":", variable ++ "="]
+    text = filter (/= ' ') line
+    probePositions = map (suffixesAfter text) (probesFor variable)
+    suffixesAfter source probe = go source
+      where
+        go s = case stripPrefix probe s of
+          Just rest -> rest : go rest
+          Nothing -> case s of
+            [] -> []
+            (_ : more) -> go more
+
+-- | The positions where a value can flow straight into the contents of the
+-- named array.
+probesFor :: String -> [String]
+probesFor variable =
+  [ variable ++ ".append("
+  , "append!(" ++ variable ++ ","
+  , "push!(" ++ variable ++ ","
+  , "repeating:"
+  , "repeat("
+  , "fill("
+  , "=["
+  ]
+
+-- | Whether the text at an element-producing position starts with a
+-- standalone whole-number literal.
+startsWholeValue :: String -> Bool
+startsWholeValue text = case text of
+  '-' : more -> digitsCheck more
+  _ -> digitsCheck text
+  where
+    digitsCheck s =
+      let (digits, rest) = span (`elem` ['0'..'9']) s
+      in not (null digits) && case rest of
+        [] -> True
+        c : _ -> c `elem` "),];*"
+
+-- | Extra fallback for environments without a target toolchain: each
+-- marker-declared array must at least participate in one generated element
+-- write, since the witness would otherwise be the only evidence that the
+-- padded elements are writable.
+writesPresentCheck :: DeclarationBundle -> Maybe String
+writesPresentCheck bundle = firstJust (map perSpec (bundleSpecs bundle))
+  where
+    firstJust = foldr (\candidate found -> maybe found Just candidate) Nothing
+    writes = bundleWrites bundle
+    perSpec spec = require (specName spec `isInfixOf` writes)
+      ("sized array " ++ specName spec ++
+        " had no element write in the generated program: " ++ writes)
+    require condition message = if condition then Nothing else Just message
+
+-- | Per-marker size evidence for each witness language.  Python arrays are
+-- additionally checked for the explicit contract violation: a bare
+-- whole-number literal sitting in the padding of a noninteger array.  Every
+-- other padding value passes, so the default choice stays with the
+-- implementation.
+pythonAssertions, swiftAssertions :: [MarkerSpec] -> [String]
+pythonAssertions = concatMap (\spec ->
+  ("assert len(" ++ specName spec ++ ") == " ++ show (specSize spec)) :
+  case specType spec of
+    "int" -> []
+    _ -> ["assert not any(isinstance(value, int) and " ++
+      "not isinstance(value, bool) for value in " ++ specName spec ++ ")"])
+swiftAssertions = map (\spec ->
+  "precondition(" ++ specName spec ++ ".count == " ++ show (specSize spec) ++
+    ")")
+
+-- | Julia also lets the executed witness check the element type without
+-- pinning down the padding values: a container whose padding was a
+-- whole-number literal levelled to an integer element type cannot satisfy the
+-- floating-point or Boolean supertype checks.
+juliaAssertions :: [MarkerSpec] -> [String]
+juliaAssertions = concatMap perSpec
+  where
+    perSpec spec =
+      ("@assert length(" ++ specName spec ++ ") == " ++ show (specSize spec)) :
+      case specType spec of
+        "double" -> ["@assert eltype(" ++ specName spec ++
+          ") <: AbstractFloat"]
+        "bool" -> ["@assert eltype(" ++ specName spec ++ ") == Bool"]
+        _ -> []
+
+pythonWitness :: DeclarationBundle -> String
+pythonWitness bundle = unlines $
+  [ "# Sized-array contract witness: extracted declarations, then the",
+    "# generator's own element writes, then marker-derived length checks.",
+    bundleDeclarations bundle,
+    bundleWrites bundle ] ++ pythonAssertions (bundleSpecs bundle)
+
+juliaWitness :: DeclarationBundle -> String
+juliaWitness bundle = unlines $
+  [ "# Sized-array contract witness.  The generated module-level `global`",
+    "# prefixes declare module globals here too, so the extracted element",
+    "# writes can follow the extracted declarations directly.  Reading the",
+    "# first padded element keeps the padding inside the checked behavior.",
+    bundleDeclarations bundle,
+    "arrD_first = arrD[1]",
+    bundleWrites bundle ] ++ juliaAssertions (bundleSpecs bundle)
+
+swiftWitness :: DeclarationBundle -> String
+swiftWitness bundle = unlines $
+  [ "// Sized-array contract witness: extracted declarations, then the",
+    "// generator's own element writes, then marker-derived count checks.",
+    bundleDeclarations bundle,
+    bundleWrites bundle ] ++ swiftAssertions (bundleSpecs bundle)
+

   => (r ProgData -> ProgData)

problem_statement:
Incremental rendering: diff widget trees instead of full clear-and-rebuild
## Problem

Every UI event triggers a full destroy-and-rebuild of the entire native view hierarchy:

```haskell
renderWidget rs widget = do
  Bridge.clear            -- destroy ALL native views
  resetCallbacks rs       -- reset callback IDs to 0
  rootId <- renderNode rs widget  -- rebuild entire tree
  Bridge.setRoot rootId
```

This doesn't scale. A screen with 50 widgets where one counter changes still destroys and recreates all 50 native views, resets all callbacks, and re-issues ~150 FFI calls.

## Why the current architecture supports incremental rendering

The pieces are mostly in place:

1. **Widget ADT is diffable** -- it's a clean algebraic data type; structural equality is straightforward.
2. **Bridge already stores nodes by ID** -- both Android (`g_nodes[nodeId]`) and iOS (`g_nodes[nodeId]`) keep live native views indexed by ID. `setStrProp`/`setNumProp` already work as in-place updates on existing nodes.
3. **Callbacks are in an IntMap** -- supports incremental insert/delete; the current `resetCallbacks` wipe is a choice, not a constraint.
4. **watchOS already benefits from partial diffing** -- SwiftUI diffs when `@Published var rootNode` changes.

## What's needed

### Haskell side
- Derive `Eq` on `Widget` and all config types
- Retain previous `Widget` tree in an `IORef` alongside `RenderState`
- Diff algorithm: `diffWidget :: Widget -> Widget -> [Patch]` producing create/update/remove/reorder operations
- Apply patches via targeted bridge calls instead of clear+rebuild
- Stable node IDs that persist across renders (currently reset to 1)
- Stable callback IDs (currently reset to 0)

### C bridge -- 3 new operations
- `removeChild(parentId, childId)` -- currently no way to remove a single child
- `insertChildAt(parentId, childId, index)` -- current `addChild` only appends
- `removeNode(nodeId)` -- destroy a single node (currently only `clear` destroys all)

### Native side -- minor changes
- **Android**: stop using `setContentView` on every render. Keep root, apply mutations. `ViewGroup.addView(child, index)` and `ViewGroup.removeView(child)` already exist.
- **iOS**: stop clearing all subviews in `ios_set_root`. `UIStackView` already has `insertArrangedSubview:atIndex:` and `removeArrangedSubview:`.
- **watchOS**: likely no changes needed (SwiftUI already diffs the published node tree).

## Suggested incremental approach

**Phase 1 -- subtree-level diffing (simplest, biggest win):**
Walk old and new `Widget` trees in parallel. When a subtree is `==`, skip it entirely (don't touch the bridge). When different, clear and rebuild just that subtree. This avoids per-property patching but already avoids recreating static parts of the UI.

**Phase 2 -- node-level patching:**
When a node's type matches but properties differ, issue targeted `setStrProp`/`setNumProp` calls instead of destroying and recreating the node. Requires the 3 new bridge operations for child list mutations.

**Phase 3 -- keyed reconciliation:**
Add optional `key` support to widgets for stable identity in child lists, enabling efficient reordering (like React's key-based reconciliation).

### Additional contract requirements

The task replaces the render engine's full clear-and-rebuild strategy with
an incremental structural diff over the widget tree. The unit-test suite
exercises this through the library's public interfaces. Because an
incremental structural diff requires comparing old and new widget trees and
giving callbacks stable identity, the work necessarily introduces a small
public surface. The following are observable requirements of the task
contract and are named explicitly so a correct solution can be recognised;
they are the minimum needed for the requested "diff widget trees, keep
subtrees and callback IDs stable" goal.

Structural equality of the widget tree
- The `Widget` type and every widget config type it contains support
  structural equality (`Eq`). Two widget trees built from equal contents
  compare equal, and trees that differ in any label, hint, value, source,
  style, alignment, color, child list, or callback compare unequal.
- Equality is structural, not identity-based: two independently built but
  structurally identical trees compare equal. This comparability is what
  lets the renderer detect and skip an unchanged subtree.
- Child ordering is part of a container's identity: reordering, inserting,
  or removing a child changes the tree and must compare unequal, because
  it must produce a bridge mutation rather than a no-op.

Opaque, comparable callback handles
- Raw `IO` closures cannot be compared for equality, so embedding them in
  widget configs would defeat both structural equality and stable callback
  identity. Widget configs therefore carry opaque, comparable handle values
  instead of embedded `IO` actions. These handle types are exported with
  their constructors from the top-level `HaskellMobile` module:
  - `Action(..)` is the handle used for a tap (`ButtonConfig`'s action
    field) and for an optional page-load (`WebViewConfig`'s page-load
    field); it exposes `actionId`.
  - `OnChange(..)` is the handle used for a text edit
    (`TextInputConfig`'s on-change field); it exposes `onChangeId`.

Shared callback registry and registration interface
- The real `IO` callbacks are registered once at application setup with a
  shared callback registry. The following are exported from the top-level
  `HaskellMobile` module:
  - `newActionState` creates a fresh shared registry;
  - `createAction` registers an `IO ()` and returns its `Action` handle,
    and `createOnChange` registers a `Text -> IO ()` and returns its
    `OnChange` handle;
  - both registrations are sequenced through the `ActionM` monad and run
    against a registry with `runActionM`.
- Every registration yields a distinct handle identifier, and `Action` and
  `OnChange` handles share one identifier space with no collisions.
- The application record `MobileApp` exposes a `maActionState` field
  holding this shared registry, and `newRenderState` takes that registry
  as its argument so the renderer shares it.

Stability across re-renders
- Re-rendering never wipes or resets the shared callback registry: a
  handle registered before a re-render stays valid afterwards, and
  dispatching its identifier still fires the originally registered
  callback. Handle identifiers are stable across renders.
- Dispatching an unknown handle identifier does not crash; it is logged
  and ignored.

Incremental re-render guarantees (observable at the bridge boundary)
- Re-rendering a tree that is structurally equal to the previously
  rendered tree is a no-op at the bridge boundary: it produces no bridge
  calls at all, regardless of the tree's size or nesting depth.
- A re-render never discards the whole native view hierarchy: the bridge
  operation that resets the entire tree is never emitted by an
  incremental re-render.
- A change localized to one leaf is targeted: it does not (re)create or
  destroy the native views of unchanged widgets, however large or deeply
  nested the unchanged remainder of the tree is. Unchanged widgets keep
  their previously created native views from then on.
- A change to a container's child list is expressed through targeted
  child attach/detach operations and single-node destruction/creation,
  never through discarding or rebuilding the whole hierarchy. Unmoved
  and unchanged siblings keep their native views; detached children are
  destroyed or removed individually.

Bridge-boundary observation used by the suite
- The suite records calls at the bridge's supported platform-callback
  registration boundary. It records operation categories and counts only;
  it does not inspect renderer state, parse desktop diagnostics, or require
  a platform-specific callback implementation.
- The suite intentionally does not constrain any platform's native logic,
  any renderer-internal retained representation, logging or trace format,
  or which supported child-list operation a correct diff selects.

This contract does not pin down the renderer's internal snapshot of retained
native nodes, any per-platform native implementation detail, or the specific
error-dismiss handle used internally by the exception handler. Platform UI
integration is outside this portable unit-level contract. Dismissal of the
transient error view is therefore not asserted through an

problem_statement_base:
Incremental rendering: diff widget trees instead of full clear-and-rebuild
## Problem

Every UI event triggers a full destroy-and-rebuild of the entire native view hierarchy:

```haskell
renderWidget rs widget = do
  Bridge.clear            -- destroy ALL native views
  resetCallbacks rs       -- reset callback IDs to 0
  rootId <- renderNode rs widget  -- rebuild entire tree
  Bridge.setRoot rootId
```

This doesn't scale. A screen with 50 widgets where one counter changes still destroys and recreates all 50 native views, resets all callbacks, and re-issues ~150 FFI calls.

## Why the current architecture supports incremental rendering

The pieces are mostly in place:

1. **Widget ADT is diffable** -- it's a clean algebraic data type; structural equality is straightforward.
2. **Bridge already stores nodes by ID** -- both Android (`g_nodes[nodeId]`) and iOS (`g_nodes[nodeId]`) keep live native views indexed by ID. `setStrProp`/`setNumProp` already work as in-place updates on existing nodes.
3. **Callbacks are in an IntMap** -- supports incremental insert/delete; the current `resetCallbacks` wipe is a choice, not a constraint.
4. **watchOS already benefits from partial diffing** -- SwiftUI diffs when `@Published var rootNode` changes.

## What's needed

### Haskell side
- Derive `Eq` on `Widget` and all config types
- Retain previous `Widget` tree in an `IORef` alongside `RenderState`
- Diff algorithm: `diffWidget :: Widget -> Widget -> [Patch]` producing create/update/remove/reorder operations
- Apply patches via targeted bridge calls instead of clear+rebuild
- Stable node IDs that persist across renders (currently reset to 1)
- Stable callback IDs (currently reset to 0)

### C bridge -- 3 new operations
- `removeChild(parentId, childId)` -- currently no way to remove a single child
- `insertChildAt(parentId, childId, index)` -- current `addChild` only appends
- `removeNode(nodeId)` -- destroy a single node (currently only `clear` destroys all)

### Native side -- minor changes
- **Android**: stop using `setContentView` on every render. Keep root, apply mutations. `ViewGroup.addView(child, index)` and `ViewGroup.removeView(child)` already exist.
- **iOS**: stop clearing all subviews in `ios_set_root`. `UIStackView` already has `insertArrangedSubview:atIndex:` and `removeArrangedSubview:`.
- **watchOS**: likely no changes needed (SwiftUI already diffs the published node tree).

## Suggested incremental approach

**Phase 1 -- subtree-level diffing (simplest, biggest win):**
Walk old and new `Widget` trees in parallel. When a subtree is `==`, skip it entirely (don't touch the bridge). When different, clear and rebuild just that subtree. This avoids per-property patching but already avoids recreating static parts of the UI.

**Phase 2 -- node-level patching:**
When a node's type matches but properties differ, issue targeted `setStrProp`/`setNumProp` calls instead of destroying and recreating the node. Requires the 3 new bridge operations for child list mutations.

**Phase 3 -- keyed reconciliation:**
Add optional `key` support to widgets for stable identity in child lists, enabling efficient reordering (like React's key-based reconciliation).
contract_addendum:
The task replaces the render engine's full clear-and-rebuild strategy with
an incremental structural diff over the widget tree. The unit-test suite
exercises this through the library's public interfaces. Because an
incremental structural diff requires comparing old and new widget trees and
giving callbacks stable identity, the work necessarily introduces a small
public surface. The following are observable requirements of the task
contract and are named explicitly so a correct solution can be recognised;
they are the minimum needed for the requested "diff widget trees, keep
subtrees and callback IDs stable" goal.

Structural equality of the widget tree
- The `Widget` type and every widget config type it contains support
  structural equality (`Eq`). Two widget trees built from equal contents
  compare equal, and trees that differ in any label, hint, value, source,
  style, alignment, color, child list, or callback compare unequal.
- Equality is structural, not identity-based: two independently built but
  structurally identical trees compare equal. This comparability is what
  lets the renderer detect and skip an unchanged subtree.
- Child ordering is part of a container's identity: reordering, inserting,
  or removing a child changes the tree and must compare unequal, because
  it must produce a bridge mutation rather than a no-op.

Opaque, comparable callback handles
- Raw `IO` closures cannot be compared for equality, so embedding them in
  widget configs would defeat both structural equality and stable callback
  identity. Widget configs therefore carry opaque, comparable handle values
  instead of embedded `IO` actions. These handle types are exported with
  their constructors from the top-level `HaskellMobile` module:
  - `Action(..)` is the handle used for a tap (`ButtonConfig`'s action
    field) and for an optional page-load (`WebViewConfig`'s page-load
    field); it exposes `actionId`.
  - `OnChange(..)` is the handle used for a text edit
    (`TextInputConfig`'s on-change field); it exposes `onChangeId`.

Shared callback registry and registration interface
- The real `IO` callbacks are registered once at application setup with a
  shared callback registry. The following are exported from the top-level
  `HaskellMobile` module:
  - `newActionState` creates a fresh shared registry;
  - `createAction` registers an `IO ()` and returns its `Action` handle,
    and `createOnChange` registers a `Text -> IO ()` and returns its
    `OnChange` handle;
  - both registrations are sequenced through the `ActionM` monad and run
    against a registry with `runActionM`.
- Every registration yields a distinct handle identifier, and `Action` and
  `OnChange` handles share one identifier space with no collisions.
- The application record `MobileApp` exposes a `maActionState` field
  holding this shared registry, and `newRenderState` takes that registry
  as its argument so the renderer shares it.

Stability across re-renders
- Re-rendering never wipes or resets the shared callback registry: a
  handle registered before a re-render stays valid afterwards, and
  dispatching its identifier still fires the originally registered
  callback. Handle identifiers are stable across renders.
- Dispatching an unknown handle identifier does not crash; it is logged
  and ignored.

Incremental re-render guarantees (observable at the bridge boundary)
- Re-rendering a tree that is structurally equal to the previously
  rendered tree is a no-op at the bridge boundary: it produces no bridge
  calls at all, regardless of the tree's size or nesting depth.
- A re-render never discards the whole native view hierarchy: the bridge
  operation that resets the entire tree is never emitted by an
  incremental re-render.
- A change localized to one leaf is targeted: it does not (re)create or
  destroy the native views of unchanged widgets, however large or deeply
  nested the unchanged remainder of the tree is. Unchanged widgets keep
  their previously created native views from then on.
- A change to a container's child list is expressed through targeted
  child attach/detach operations and single-node destruction/creation,
  never through discarding or rebuilding the whole hierarchy. Unmoved
  and unchanged siblings keep their native views; detached children are
  destroyed or removed individually.

Bridge-boundary observation used by the suite
- The suite records calls at the bridge's supported platform-callback
  registration boundary. It records operation categories and counts only;
  it does not inspect renderer state, parse desktop diagnostics, or require
  a platform-specific callback implementation.
- The suite intentionally does not constrain any platform's native logic,
  any renderer-internal retained representation, logging or trace format,
  or which supported child-list operation a correct diff selects.

This contract does not pin down the renderer's internal snapshot of retained
native nodes, any per-platform native implementation detail, or the specific
error-dismiss handle used internally by the exception handler. Platform UI
integration is outside this portable unit-level contract. Dismissal of the
transient error view is therefore not asserted through an
implementation-internal field.
