+{-# LANGUAGE DerivingStrategies #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE DerivingVia #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE ImportQualifiedPost #-}
+-- | Opaque callback handles for the widget system.
+--
+-- Instead of embedding raw @IO ()@ closures inside widget configs,
+-- the framework uses typed handles ('Action', 'OnChange') that
+-- reference entries in a shared 'ActionState' registry.  Because
+-- the handles are plain 'Int32' newtypes they derive 'Eq', which
+-- lets 'Widget' derive 'Eq' naturally — enabling O(1) "skip if
+-- unchanged" diff in the render engine.
+--
+-- Users create handles once at init time via the restricted 'ActionM'
+-- monad, then embed them in widget configs.  The callback 'IntMap's
+-- are never cleared during rendering, eliminating the atomicity gap
+-- of the old clear-and-rebuild strategy.
+module HaskellMobile.Action
+  ( -- * Handles
+    Action(..)
+  , OnChange(..)
+    -- * Callback registry
+  , ActionState(..)
+    -- * Restricted construction monad
+  , ActionM
+  , createAction
+  , createOnChange
+  , liftIO
+    -- * Framework-internal
+  , newActionState
+  , runActionM
+  , lookupAction
+  , lookupTextAction
+  )
+where
+
+import Control.Monad.IO.Class (MonadIO, liftIO)
+import Control.Monad.Trans.Reader (ReaderT(..))
+import Data.IORef (IORef, newIORef, readIORef, modifyIORef')
+import Data.Int (Int32)
+import Data.IntMap.Strict (IntMap)
+import Data.IntMap.Strict qualified as IntMap
+import Data.Text (Text)
+
+-- | An opaque handle to a click / tap callback.
+-- Carries only an 'Int32' identifier, so it derives 'Eq' and 'Show'.
+newtype Action = Action { actionId :: Int32 }
+  deriving stock (Eq, Show)
+
+-- | An opaque handle to a text-change callback.
+-- Carries only an 'Int32' identifier, so it derives 'Eq' and 'Show'.
+newtype OnChange = OnChange { onChangeId :: Int32 }
+  deriving stock (Eq, Show)
+
+-- | Mutable callback storage shared between 'ActionM' (creation)
+-- and the render/dispatch engine (lookup).
+data ActionState = ActionState
+  { asCallbacks     :: IORef (IntMap (IO ()))
+    -- ^ Click/tap callbacks keyed by handle ID.
+  , asTextCallbacks :: IORef (IntMap (Text -> IO ()))
+    -- ^ Text-change callbacks keyed by handle ID.
+  , asNextId        :: IORef Int32
+    -- ^ Monotonically increasing counter for the next handle ID.
+  }
+
+-- | Create a fresh empty 'ActionState'.
+newActionState :: IO ActionState
+newActionState = do
+  callbacks     <- newIORef IntMap.empty
+  textCallbacks <- newIORef IntMap.empty
+  nextId        <- newIORef 0
+  pure ActionState
+    { asCallbacks     = callbacks
+    , asTextCallbacks = textCallbacks
+    , asNextId        = nextId
+    }
+
+-- | A restricted monad for creating callback handles.
+-- The constructor is hidden so that users cannot construct arbitrary
+-- 'ActionM' values — they must go through 'createAction' and
+-- 'createOnChange'.
+newtype ActionM a = ActionM (ActionState -> IO a)
+  deriving (Functor, Applicative, Monad, MonadIO)
+    via (ReaderT ActionState IO)
+
+-- | Register a click/tap callback and return its opaque handle.
+createAction :: IO () -> ActionM Action
+createAction callback = ActionM $ \state -> do
+  handleId <- readIORef (asNextId state)
+  modifyIORef' (asCallbacks state) (IntMap.insert (fromIntegral handleId) callback)
+  modifyIORef' (asNextId state) (+ 1)
+  pure (Action handleId)
+
+-- | Register a text-change callback and return its opaque handle.
+createOnChange :: (Text -> IO ()) -> ActionM OnChange
+createOnChange callback = ActionM $ \state -> do
+  handleId <- readIORef (asNextId state)
+  modifyIORef' (asTextCallbacks state) (IntMap.insert (fromIntegral handleId) callback)
+  modifyIORef' (asNextId state) (+ 1)
+  pure (OnChange handleId)
+
+-- | Run an 'ActionM' computation against a given 'ActionState'.
+runActionM :: ActionState -> ActionM a -> IO a
+runActionM state (ActionM f) = f state
+
+-- | Look up a click/tap callback by handle ID.
+-- Returns 'Nothing' if the ID is not registered.
+lookupAction :: ActionState -> Int32 -> IO (Maybe (IO ()))
+lookupAction state handleId = do
+  callbacks <- readIORef (asCallbacks state)
+  pure (IntMap.lookup (fromIntegral handleId) callbacks)
+
+-- | Look up a text-change callback by handle ID.
+-- Returns 'Nothing' if the ID is not registered.
+lookupTextAction :: ActionState -> Int32 -> IO (Maybe (Text -> IO ()))
+lookupTextAction state handleId = do
+  callbacks <- readIORef (asTextCallbacks state)
+  pure (IntMap.lookup (fromIntegral handleId) callbacks)

+      let widgetA = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "go", bcAction = handle, bcFontConfig = Just (FontConfig 12.0) }
+          widgetB = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "go", bcAction = handle, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different button fonts" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "InputType distinguishes text inputs" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      let widgetA = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputNumber, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different input types" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "TextInputConfig hint distinguishes widgets" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      let widgetA = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "one", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "two", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different input hints" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "TextInputConfig value distinguishes widgets" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      let widgetA = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "1", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "2", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different input values" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "distinct OnChange handles distinguish otherwise identical text inputs" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handleA <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      handleB <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      let widgetA = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handleA, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputText, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "", tiOnChange = handleB, tiFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different OnChange handles" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "ScaleType distinguishes images" $ do
+      let widgetA = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageResource (ResourceName "i"), icScaleType = ScaleFit }
+          widgetB = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageResource (ResourceName "i"), icScaleType = ScaleFill }
+      assertBool "different scale types" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "ImageSource resource name distinguishes images" $ do
+      let widgetA = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageResource (ResourceName "one"), icScaleType = ScaleFit }
+          widgetB = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageResource (ResourceName "two"), icScaleType = ScaleFit }
+      assertBool "different resource names" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "ImageSource raw data distinguishes images" $ do
+      let widgetA = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageData (BS.pack [1]), icScaleType = ScaleNone }
+          widgetB = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageData (BS.pack [2]), icScaleType = ScaleNone }
+      assertBool "different image bytes" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "ImageSource file path distinguishes images" $ do
+      let widgetA = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageFile "/a.png", icScaleType = ScaleNone }
+          widgetB = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageFile "/b.png", icScaleType = ScaleNone }
+      assertBool "different image files" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "WebViewConfig url distinguishes widgets" $ do
+      let widgetA = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://a.example", wvOnPageLoad = Nothing }
+          widgetB = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://b.example", wvOnPageLoad = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different webview urls" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "WebViewConfig page-load handle distinguishes widgets" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      (handleA, handleB) <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ do
+        hA <- createAction (pure ())
+        hB <- createAction (pure ())
+        pure (hA, hB)
+      let widgetA = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://a.example", wvOnPageLoad = Just handleA }
+          widgetB = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://a.example", wvOnPageLoad = Just handleB }
+      assertBool "different page-load handles" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "WidgetStyle padding distinguishes styled widgets" $ do
+      let child = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "s", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetA = Styled (WidgetStyle (Just 4.0) Nothing Nothing Nothing) child
+          widgetB = Styled (WidgetStyle (Just 8.0) Nothing Nothing Nothing) child
+      assertBool "different padding" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "TextAlignment distinguishes styled widgets" $ do
+      let child = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "s", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetA = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing (Just AlignStart) Nothing Nothing) child
+          widgetB = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing (Just AlignCenter) Nothing Nothing) child
+      assertBool "different text alignment" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "Color text color distinguishes styled widgets" $ do
+      let child = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "s", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetA = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing Nothing (Just (Color 255 0 0 255)) Nothing) child
+          widgetB = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing Nothing (Just (Color 0 255 0 255)) Nothing) child
+      assertBool "different text colors" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "WidgetStyle background color distinguishes styled widgets" $ do
+      let child = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "s", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetA = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing Nothing Nothing (Just (Color 0 0 0 255))) child
+          widgetB = Styled (WidgetStyle Nothing Nothing Nothing Nothing) child
+      assertBool "background presence" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+  ]
+
+-- | Ordering of children is part of the widget tree: reordering the
+-- children of a container changes the tree and must be observable
+-- through structural equality, since it must produce a bridge mutation.
+widgetOrderEqTests :: TestTree
+widgetOrderEqTests = testGroup "WidgetOrder"
+  [ testCase "Row child order matters" $ do
+      let widgetA = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                        , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+          widgetB = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                        , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      assertBool "reordered Row children differ" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "Column child order matters" $ do
+      let widgetA = Column [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                           , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+          widgetB = Column [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                           , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      assertBool "reordered Column children differ" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "ScrollView child insertion is observable" $ do
+      let widgetA = ScrollView [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+          widgetB = ScrollView [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                               , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      assertBool "inserted ScrollView child differs" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "Row child removal is observable" $ do
+      let widgetA = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                        , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+          widgetB = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      assertBool "removed Row child differs" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+  ]
+
+-- | Equality must hold for structurally identical trees built
+-- independently, confirming equality is structural rather than
+-- identity-based.  These exist so the diff can correctly skip an
+-- unchanged subtree.
+widgetIdenticalEqTests :: TestTree
+widgetIdenticalEqTests = testGroup "WidgetIdentical"
+  [ testCase "structurally identical Inputs are equal" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+      let widgetA = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputNumber, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "1", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Just (FontConfig 16.0) }
+          widgetB = TextInput TextInputConfig { tiInputType = InputNumber, tiHint = "h", tiValue = "1", tiOnChange = handle, tiFontConfig = Just (FontConfig 16.0) }
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "structurally identical Images are equal" $ do
+      let widgetA = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageData (BS.pack [1, 2]), icScaleType = ScaleFill }
+          widgetB = Image ImageConfig { icSource = ImageData (BS.pack [1, 2]), icScaleType = ScaleFill }
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "structurally identical WebViews are equal" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createAction (pure ())
+      let widgetA = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://x.example", wvOnPageLoad = Just handle }
+          widgetB = WebView WebViewConfig { wvUrl = "https://x.example", wvOnPageLoad = Just handle }
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "structurally identical Styled trees are equal" $ do
+      let style = WidgetStyle (Just 4.0) (Just AlignEnd) (Just (Color 1 2 3 4)) (Just (Color 5 6 7 8))
+          child = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "x", tcFontConfig = Just (FontConfig 18.0) }
+          widgetA = Styled style child
+          widgetB = Styled style child
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "structurally identical Rows are equal" $ do
+      let widgetA = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                        , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+          widgetB = Row [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                        , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+  ]
+
+-- | Tests for Action/OnChange handle equality and creation.
+actionTests :: TestTree
+actionTests = testGroup "Action"
+  [ testCase "createAction produces unique IDs" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      (handleA, handleB) <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ do
+        hA <- createAction (pure ())
+        hB <- createAction (pure ())
+        pure (hA, hB)
+      assertBool "different actions should have different IDs" (handleA /= handleB)
+
+  , testCase "createOnChange produces unique IDs" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      (handleA, handleB) <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ do
+        hA <- createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+        hB <- createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+        pure (hA, hB)
+      assertBool "different onChange handles should have different IDs" (handleA /= handleB)
+
+  , testCase "Action and OnChange share ID space" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      (actionHandle, changeHandle) <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ do
+        ah <- createAction (pure ())
+        ch <- createOnChange (\_ -> pure ())
+        pure (ah, ch)
+      assertBool "action and onChange should have different IDs"
+        (actionId actionHandle /= onChangeId changeHandle)
+
+  , testCase "same Action handle equals itself" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createAction (pure ())
+      handle @?= handle
+  ]
+
+-- | Tests for Widget Eq instance (enabled by opaque handles).
+widgetEqTests :: TestTree
+widgetEqTests = testGroup "WidgetEq"
+  [ testCase "same widget with same handle is equal" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      handle <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ createAction (pure ())
+      let widgetA = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "tap", bcAction = handle, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "tap", bcAction = handle, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "same widget with different handles is not equal" $ do
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      (handleA, handleB) <- runActionMEither runActionM actionState $ do
+        hA <- createAction (pure ())
+        hB <- createAction (pure ())
+        pure (hA, hB)
+      let widgetA = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "tap", bcAction = handleA, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "tap", bcAction = handleB, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different handles means different widgets" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "Text widgets with same content are equal" $ do
+      let widgetA = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "hello", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "hello", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+
+  , testCase "Text widgets with different content are not equal" $ do
+      let widgetA = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "hello", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          widgetB = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "world", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      assertBool "different labels means different widgets" (widgetA /= widgetB)
+
+  , testCase "Column equality is structural" $ do
+      let widgetA = Column [Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }]
+          widgetB = Column [Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "a", tcFontConfig = Nothing }]
+          widgetC = Column [Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "b", tcFontConfig = Nothing }]
+      widgetA @?= widgetB
+      assertBool "different children means different Column" (widgetA /= widgetC)
+  ]
+
+-- | Incremental-rendering behavior tests.
+--
+-- These cases observe the bridge calls the renderer makes through the
+-- test-only observation fixture registered at the bridge's exported ABI
+-- attachment point.  Assertions are expressed over whole-operation counts
+-- and operation categories (creation, full reset, child attachment and
+-- detach, destruction, property updates), and over per-widget operation
+-- budgets that distinguish an incremental update from a from-scratch
+-- rebuild.  They do not assume a renderer-internal retained representation,
+-- a platform's native logic, or a trace format.
+incrementalRenderTests :: TestTree
+incrementalRenderTests = sequentialTestGroup "IncrementalRender" AllFinish
+  [ testCase "re-rendering an identical tree issues no bridge operations" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let widget = Column
+            [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "title", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "body", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            ]
+      renderWidget rs widget
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs widget)
+      ops @?= []
+
+  , testCase "changing one leaf preserves an unchanged sibling subtree" $ do
+      (clickHandle, rs) <- withActions $ createAction (pure ())
+      let unchangedSibling = Row
+            [ Button ButtonConfig { bcLabel = "keep", bcAction = clickHandle, bcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "also kept", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            ]
+          mkWidget leafLabel = Column
+            [ unchangedSibling
+            , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = leafLabel, tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            ]
+      renderWidget rs (mkWidget "before")
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (mkWidget "after"))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- The unchanged sibling subtree of two widgets must not be
+      -- recreated: at most the single changed leaf may be recreated, and
+      -- any from-scratch rebuild of the four-widget tree exceeds that.
+      assertRetainedViews "unchanged sibling subtree was rebuilt" 4 ops
+      assertBool ("unchanged sibling subtree was recreated: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeCreateNode ops <= 1)
+
+  , testCase "changing a leaf label is targeted rather than a full rebuild" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let sibling = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "sibling", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          mkWidget caption = Column
+            [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = caption, tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            , sibling
+            ]
+      renderWidget rs (mkWidget "before")
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (mkWidget "after"))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- A one-label change inside a three-widget tree must not rebuild
+      -- the unaffected views: any from-scratch rebuild of the tree
+      -- exceeds one creation and one destruction.
+      assertRetainedViews "leaf change rebuilt unrelated widgets" 3 ops
+      assertBool ("leaf update recreated views of unrelated widgets: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeCreateNode ops <= 1)
+      assertBool ("leaf update destroyed views of unrelated widgets: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeDestroyNode ops <= 1)
+      -- A leaf whose label changes must be patched in place through a
+      -- targeted property update rather than only destroyed and
+      -- recreated: at least one property mutation is issued for it.
+      assertBool ("changed leaf received no targeted property update: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeSetStrProp ops + countOp BridgeSetNumProp ops >= 1)
+
+  , testCase "a small leaf change in a large tree touches few views" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let mkWidget caption = Column
+            ([ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = Text.pack ("row-" ++ show n), tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+             | n <- [1 .. 10 :: Int] ]
+              ++ [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = caption, tcFontConfig = Nothing } ])
+      renderWidget rs (mkWidget "before")
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (mkWidget "after"))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- In a twelve-widget tree with one changed label, recreating or
+      -- destroying more views than the changed leaf is a rebuild, not a
+      -- diff.
+      assertRetainedViews "small change in a twelve-widget tree" 12 ops
+
+  , testCase "removing a child uses a targeted mutation, in place" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let withChild = Column
+            [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "first", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "second", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+            ]
+          withoutChild = Column
+            [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "first", tcFontConfig = Nothing } ]
+      renderWidget rs withChild
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs withoutChild)
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- The surviving child must be kept: nothing may be (re)created,
+      -- and the removal itself must be a targeted detach/destroy pair
+      -- rather than detaching and re-attaching the whole child list.
+      countOp BridgeCreateNode ops @?= 0
+      assertBool ("removed child had no detach or destruction: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeRemoveChild ops + countOp BridgeDestroyNode ops >= 1)
+      assertBoundedChildListOps "child removal" ops
+
+  , testCase "reordering children mutates the child list without clearing" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let childA = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "aaa", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          childB = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "bbb", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          childC = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "ccc", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      renderWidget rs (Column [childA, childB, childC])
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (Column [childB, childA, childC]))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- The child list must actually change: at least one attach or
+      -- detach operation.  Unmoved children must not be needlessly
+      -- recreated, and any detach-everything-then-reattach-all strategy
+      -- exceeds these sequential caps.
+      assertBool ("reordering did not mutate the child list: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeAttachChild ops
+          + countOp BridgeRemoveChild ops >= 1)
+      assertBool ("unmoved children were needlessly recreated: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeCreateNode ops <= 2)
+      assertBoundedChildListOps "child reordering" ops
+
+  , testCase "appending a child creates and attaches only the new node" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let childA = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "aaa", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          childB = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "bbb", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      renderWidget rs (Column [childA, childB])
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (Column [childA, childB, childA]))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      countOp BridgeCreateNode ops @?= 1
+      -- The appended child must show up as exactly one new view; how it
+      -- is attached to its parent is left to the diff.  The rest of
+      -- the child list must not be detached or destroyed beyond bounds.
+      assertBoundedChildListOps "child append" ops
+
+  , testCase "a large flat re-render with one change stays incremental" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let mkLabels firstLabel = firstLabel : [ Text.pack ("static-" ++ show n) | n <- [1 .. 30 :: Int] ]
+          mkWidget labels = Column
+            [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = caption, tcFontConfig = Nothing } | caption <- labels ]
+      renderWidget rs (mkWidget (mkLabels "before"))
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (mkWidget (mkLabels "after")))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- One label change in a 31-widget tree must not recreate views:
+      -- a from-scratch rebuild needs at least one creation per widget.
+      assertRetainedViews "single change in a 31-widget tree" 31 ops
+
+  , testCase "a deep nested unchanged tree costs nothing to re-render" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let deepLeaf :: Int -> Widget
+          deepLeaf level = Text TextConfig
+            { tcLabel = Text.pack ("leaf-" ++ show level), tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          nested = Column
+            [ Column
+              [ Row [deepLeaf 1, Styled defaultStyle (deepLeaf 2)]
+              , deepLeaf 3
+              ]
+            , Styled defaultStyle (deepLeaf 4)
+            , Row [deepLeaf 5, deepLeaf 6]
+            ]
+      renderWidget rs nested
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs nested)
+      ops @?= []
+
+  , testCase "a large tree keeps its existing views on an append" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let leaf caption = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = caption, tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          wideTree extra = Column
+            ([ leaf (Text.pack ("wide-" ++ show n)) | n <- [1 .. 20 :: Int] ] ++ extra)
+      renderWidget rs (wideTree [])
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (wideTree [leaf "new-tail"]))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      -- Appending to a 20-widget tree creates exactly the one new view
+      -- and attaches it; existing views keep their identity because none
+      -- are destroyed and (at most) none besides the new one are created.
+      countOp BridgeCreateNode ops @?= 1
+      countOp BridgeDestroyNode ops @?= 0
+      -- The new tail view exists (one creation above); the suite does
+      -- not pin down which supported child-list operation attaches it.
+
+  , testCase "removal detaches before the surviving sibling is re-checked" $ do
+      ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+      let keep = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "keep", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          drop1 = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "drop1", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+          drop2 = Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "drop2", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+      renderWidget rs (Column [keep, drop1, drop2])
+      ((), ops) <- withObservation (renderWidget rs (Column [keep]))
+      assertNoFullClear ops
+      countOp BridgeCreateNode ops @?= 0
+      -- Two children left the tree: their views must be detached and/or
+      -- destroyed, in any order, but never rebuilt.
+      assertBool ("removed children had no detach or destruction: " ++ show ops)
+        (countOp BridgeRemoveChild ops + countOp BridgeDestroyNode ops >= 2)
+      assertBoundedChildListOps "two-child removal" ops
+  ]
+
+-- The bridge's native integration coverage for Android, iOS and watchOS
+-- stays in the platform-specific integration suites; the unit suite cannot
+-- execute native platform UI code, so it observes the bridge only through
+-- the registered test fixture.
FAIL_TO_PASS: rebench explicit result

install_config.test_cmd:
export PATH=/opt/ghc/9.8.4/bin:/usr/local/cargo/bin:/root/.nix-profile/bin:$PATH
set +e
(
cabal test unit --ghc-options=-O0 --ghc-options=-Wno-deprecations --test-options='--color=never'
)
_rebench_status=$?
if [ "$_rebench_status" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '\nRESULT: PASS (exit=0)\n'
else
  printf '\nRESULT: FAIL (exit=%s)\n' "$_rebench_status"
fi
exit "$_rebench_status"

problem_statement:
Numeric properties (font size, padding) have no effect on Android
## Problem

The Haskell API exposes `setNumProp` with `PropFontSize` and `PropPadding` properties, and the C bridge dispatches these through the `setNumProp` callback. However, on Android the implementation is a no-op — it only logs a message and discards the value.

This means consumers cannot control text size or spacing between widgets, even though the API surface suggests they can.

## Use case

prrrrrrrrr's "Enter PR" screen shows a history list directly below the Save/Back buttons with no visual separation, and all text renders at the default size. The app would benefit from larger text for history entries and padding/margins between sections to improve readability. Currently there is no way to achieve either through the widget API.

## Current behaviour

Calling `setNumProp` on any Android node logs:

```
setNumProp(node=N, prop=M, value=X.XX) — not yet implemented
```

The property value is silently ignored. The `TODO` comment in `cbits/ui_bridge_android.c:282` confirms this is known-unfinished.

On desktop (stub backend), the value is similarly logged but not applied (expected, since there's no real UI).

## Expected behaviour

Setting `PropFontSize` on a `Text` or `TextInput` node should change the rendered font size on Android. Setting `PropPadding` on any node should add spacing around it.

### Additional contract requirements

Numeric widget properties must have observable effects on Android:

- Calling the existing `setNumProp` numeric-property API with the font-size
  property changes the rendered text size of Android text-bearing views,
  including both text labels and text inputs.
- Calling the same existing API with the padding property adds spacing around
  the targeted Android native view, with the supplied padding applied on all

problem_statement_base:
Numeric properties (font size, padding) have no effect on Android
## Problem

The Haskell API exposes `setNumProp` with `PropFontSize` and `PropPadding` properties, and the C bridge dispatches these through the `setNumProp` callback. However, on Android the implementation is a no-op — it only logs a message and discards the value.

This means consumers cannot control text size or spacing between widgets, even though the API surface suggests they can.

## Use case

prrrrrrrrr's "Enter PR" screen shows a history list directly below the Save/Back buttons with no visual separation, and all text renders at the default size. The app would benefit from larger text for history entries and padding/margins between sections to improve readability. Currently there is no way to achieve either through the widget API.

## Current behaviour

Calling `setNumProp` on any Android node logs:

```
setNumProp(node=N, prop=M, value=X.XX) — not yet implemented
```

The property value is silently ignored. The `TODO` comment in `cbits/ui_bridge_android.c:282` confirms this is known-unfinished.

On desktop (stub backend), the value is similarly logged but not applied (expected, since there's no real UI).

## Expected behaviour

Setting `PropFontSize` on a `Text` or `TextInput` node should change the rendered font size on Android. Setting `PropPadding` on any node should add spacing around it.
contract_addendum:
Numeric widget properties must have observable effects on Android:

- Calling the existing `setNumProp` numeric-property API with the font-size
  property changes the rendered text size of Android text-bearing views,
  including both text labels and text inputs.
- Calling the same existing API with the padding property adds spacing around
  the targeted Android native view, with the supplied padding applied on all
  four sides. Padding applies to all node types, not only text-bearing views.
- On non-native or fallback platforms, numeric-property calls remain accepted
  without error; no particular diagnostic wording is required.

+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Android numeric-property contract tests
+--
+-- The existing 'setNumProp' numeric-property API must change the rendered
+-- font size of Android text-bearing views (both text labels and text
+-- inputs) and must add uniform spacing on all four sides of every
+-- targeted native view.  The desktop stub backend never applies native
+-- effects, so these scenarios check the real Android translation unit
+-- (@cbits/ui_bridge_android.c@) on the host: it is staged as a plain file
+-- copy, compiled against the fake JNI table in test/android/numericprops/,
+-- and executed in a separate child process per scenario so one failing
+-- scenario can never abort the rest silently.  The tasty report then
+-- names the exact contract point that holds or fails.
+
+-- | Scenarios of the Android numeric-property contract, in order.
+androidScenarioNames :: [String]
+androidScenarioNames =
+  [ "font-size-applied-to-text-label"
+  , "font-size-applied-to-text-input"
+  , "font-size-applied-to-button"
+  , "padding-applied-to-all-native-view-types"
+  ]
+
+-- | Contract tests for the Android numeric-property bridge.
+androidNumericPropsTests :: TestTree
+androidNumericPropsTests = testGroup "Android numeric properties"
+  [ testCase "numeric properties are accepted for every widget node type" $ do
+      state <- newRenderState
+      renderWidget state (compatText "numeric property target")
+      mapM_
+        (\prop -> setNumProp 1 (prop :: PropId) 12)
+        [PropFontSize, PropPadding, PropInputType]
+  , testCase "existing container widgets still render" $ do
+      state <- newRenderState
+      renderWidget state (Column [])
+  , testGroup "Android bridge scenarios" $ map androidBridgeScenario androidScenarioNames
+  ]
+
+-- | Run one named Android bridge scenario through the host fixture in its
+-- own child process; the captured output becomes the assertion diagnostic.
+androidBridgeScenario :: String -> TestTree
+androidBridgeScenario scenario = testCase ("Android bridge: " <> scenario) $ do
+  (status, captured) <- androidBridgeScenarioRun scenario
+  assertBool
+    ("Android bridge scenario " <> show scenario <> " did not pass:\n" <> captured)
+    (status == 0)
+
+-- | Build (or rebuild) the host fixture and run the named scenario in a
+-- subprocess, returning the exit status and captured output.  Every
+-- scenario gets its own working directory so concurrently running
+-- scenarios never share a binary while it is being relinked.
+androidBridgeScenarioRun :: String -> IO (Int, String)
+androidBridgeScenarioRun scenario = do
+  workDir <- androidNumericPropsWorkDirFor scenario
+  let stagedBridge = workDir <> "/ui_bridge_android.c"
+      stagedHeader = workDir <> "/UIBridge.h"
+      binary       = workDir <> "/bridge_numeric_properties"
+      source       = "test/android/numericprops/bridge_numeric_properties.c"
+  _ <- runShell ("cp include/UIBridge.h " <> quote stagedHeader)
+  _ <- runShell ("cp cbits/ui_bridge_android.c " <> quote stagedBridge)
+  compiler <- hostCompiler
+  (compileStatus, compileOut) <- runShellCapture $ unwords
+    [ compiler, "-o", quote binary
+    , "-DHATTER_UNDERSCORED_BRIDGE=" <> quotedDefine stagedBridge
+    , "-I", quote "test/android/include"
+    , "-I", quote workDir
+    , quote source
+    ]
+  if compileStatus /= 0
+    then pure (compileStatus
+      , "Android bridge fixture failed to compile with " <> show compiler
+        <> ":\n" <> compileOut)
+    else runShellCapture (quote binary <> " --scenario " <> quote scenario)
+  where _ = ()
+
+-- | Fresh per-process, per-scenario working directory below the system
+-- temp area.
+androidNumericPropsWorkDirFor :: String -> IO FilePath
+androidNumericPropsWorkDirFor scenario = do
+  (pidStatus, pidText) <- runShellCapture "echo $$"
+  let pid = filter (/= '\n') pidText
+      dir = "/tmp/hatter-numericprops-" <>
+            (if pidStatus == 0 && not (null pid) then pid else "run") <>
+            "-" <> scenario
+  _ <- runShell ("mkdir -p " <> quote dir)
+  pure dir
+
+-- | Quote a string as a single shell word.
+quote :: String -> String
+quote s = "'" <> concatMap escape s <> "'"
+  where
+    escape '\'' = "'\\''"
+    escape c    = [c]
+
+-- | Wrap a path as a C string literal for the -D define.
+quotedDefine :: FilePath -> String
+quotedDefine path = "\\\"" <> path <> "\\\""
+
+-- | The compiler for the host fixture: $CC when set, else cc.
+hostCompiler :: IO String
+hostCompiler = do
+  (status, captured) <- runShellCapture "printf '%s' \"${CC:-cc}\""
+  let name = filter (/= '\n') captured
+  pure (if status == 0 && not (null name) then name else "cc")
+
+-- | Run a command through the shell, capturing combined output and the
+-- numeric exit status.
+runShellCapture :: String -> IO (Int, String)
+runShellCapture command = do
+  (captureFile, handle) <- openTempFile "/tmp" "hatter-numericprops-capture"
+  hClose handle
+  let wrapped = command <> " > " <> quote captureFile <> " 2>&1"
+  status <- runShell wrapped
+  contents <- safeReadFile captureFile
+  pure (status, contents)
+
+-- | Run a shell command and return only its exit status.
+runShell :: String -> IO Int
+runShell command = hatterSystem command
+
+-- | Read a capture file; a missing file is reported as an empty capture.
+safeReadFile :: FilePath -> IO String
+safeReadFile path = do
+  exists <- fileExists path
+  if exists then readFile path else pure ""
+
+fileExists :: FilePath -> IO Bool
+fileExists path = do
+  status <- runShell ("test -f " <> quote path)
+  pure (status == 0)
+
+-- | FFI wrapper over the C library @system@ call; the raw wait status is
+-- normalised to the child exit code (high byte on POSIX).
+hatterSystem :: String -> IO Int
+hatterSystem command = do
+  raw <- withCString command c_system
+  pure (if raw < 0 then 127 else fromIntegral raw `div` 256)
+
+foreign import ccall unsafe "system"
+  c_system :: CString -> IO CInt

+/*
+ * Host-side contract fixture for the Android numeric-property bridge.
+ *
+ * The production Android translation unit (cbits/ui_bridge_android.c) is
+ * compiled on the host against the minimal fake JNI table below, then
+ * driven exactly the way the Android runtime drives it: a view is handed
+ * to the bridge through createNode, and the existing numeric property
+ * reaches it through setNumProp while the fake JNI table records which
+ * native view methods are invoked.
+ *
+ * Each named scenario runs in its own process (selected with
+ * --scenario <name>) so one failing scenario can never abort the others
+ * silently; every scenario failure leaves a diagnostic on stderr naming
+ * the contract point that did not hold.
+ *
+ * The bridge source is staged beside this binary as a plain
+ * "ui_bridge_android.c" copy, so no include path contains "cbits".
+ */
+#include <stdarg.h>
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+
+#include <jni.h>
+#include "UIBridge.h"
+
+
+#define TOKEN(value) ((void *)(uintptr_t)(value))
+#define CLASS_TEXT_VIEW TOKEN(0x101)
+#define CLASS_OTHER TOKEN(0x102)
+#define OBJECT_TEXT_VIEW TOKEN(0x201)
+#define OBJECT_EDIT_TEXT TOKEN(0x202)
+#define OBJECT_PLAIN_VIEW TOKEN(0x203)
+#define OBJECT_ANY_VIEW TOKEN(0x204)
+#define OBJECT_BUTTON TOKEN(0x205)
+#define OBJECT_COLUMN TOKEN(0x206)
+#define OBJECT_ROW TOKEN(0x207)
+#define OBJECT_SCROLL_VIEW TOKEN(0x208)
+#define METHOD_OTHER TOKEN(0x301)
+#define METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_FLOAT TOKEN(0x302)
+#define METHOD_SET_PADDING TOKEN(0x303)
+#define METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_UNIT TOKEN(0x304)
+#define FIELD_DENSITY TOKEN(0x401)
+
+static int font_calls;
+static int padding_calls;
+static jobject called_object;
+static double called_font_size;
+static jint called_padding[4];
+
+/* ---- Unused Haskell FFI exports referenced by the bridge ---- */
+
+static void haskellOnUIEvent(void *ctx, int callbackId)
+{
+    (void)ctx;
+    (void)callbackId;
+}
+
+static void haskellOnUITextChange(void *ctx, int callbackId, const char *text)
+{
+    (void)ctx;
+    (void)callbackId;
+    (void)text;
+}
+
+
+/* ---- Fake JNI environment ---- */
+
+static jclass fake_find_class(JNIEnv *env, const char *name)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    return strcmp(name, "android/widget/TextView") == 0
+        ? CLASS_TEXT_VIEW : CLASS_OTHER;
+}
+
+static jobject fake_global_ref(JNIEnv *env, jobject object)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    return object;
+}
+
+static void fake_delete_ref(JNIEnv *env, jobject object)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)object;
+}
+
+static jmethodID fake_get_method_id(
+    JNIEnv *env, jclass clazz, const char *name, const char *signature)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)clazz;
+    if (strcmp(name, "setTextSize") == 0) {
+        if (strcmp(signature, "(F)V") == 0) return METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_FLOAT;
+        if (strcmp(signature, "(IF)V") == 0) return METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_UNIT;
+    }
+    if (strcmp(name, "setPadding") == 0) return METHOD_SET_PADDING;
+    return METHOD_OTHER;
+}
+
+static jclass fake_get_object_class(JNIEnv *env, jobject object)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)object;
+    return CLASS_OTHER;
+}
+
+/* The view the fake runtime hands to the bridge at the next creation. */
+static jobject g_pending_view;
+
+static jobject fake_new_object(
+    JNIEnv *env, jclass clazz, jmethodID method, ...)
+{
+    jobject view = g_pending_view;
+
+    (void)env;
+    (void)clazz;
+    (void)method;
+    return view;
+}
+
+static jstring fake_new_string_utf(JNIEnv *env, const char *bytes)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    return (jstring)bytes;
+}
+
+static void fake_call_void_method(JNIEnv *env, jobject object, jmethodID method, ...)
+{
+    va_list args;
+
+    va_start(args, method);
+    if (method == METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_FLOAT
+            || method == METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_UNIT) {
+        double size;
+        if (method == METHOD_SET_TEXT_SIZE_UNIT) {
+            (void)va_arg(args, jint);
+        }
+        size = va_arg(args, double);
+        font_calls++;
+        called_object = object;
+        called_font_size = size;
+    } else if (method == METHOD_SET_PADDING) {
+        padding_calls++;
+        called_object = object;
+        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
+            called_padding[i] = va_arg(args, jint);
+        }
+    }
+    va_end(args);
+}
+
+static jobject fake_call_object_method(JNIEnv *env, jobject object, jmethodID method, ...)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)object;
+    (void)method;
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+static jint fake_call_int_method(JNIEnv *env, jobject object, jmethodID method, ...)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)object;
+    (void)method;
+    return 0;
+}
+

+{

+    (void)isCopy;
+    return (const char *)str;
+}
+
+static void fake_release_string_utf_chars(JNIEnv *env, jstring str, const char *chars)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)str;
+    (void)chars;
+}
+
+static jboolean fake_is_instance_of(JNIEnv *env, jobject object, jclass clazz)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)clazz;
+    return object == OBJECT_TEXT_VIEW || object == OBJECT_EDIT_TEXT
+            || object == OBJECT_BUTTON
+        ? JNI_TRUE : JNI_FALSE;
+}
+
+static jfieldID fake_get_field_id(
+    JNIEnv *env, jclass clazz, const char *name, const char *signature)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)clazz;
+    (void)signature;
+    return strcmp(name, "density") == 0 ? FIELD_DENSITY : NULL;
+}
+
+static jfloat fake_get_float_field(JNIEnv *env, jobject object, jfieldID field)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    (void)object;
+    (void)field;
+    return 1.0f;
+}
+
+static jboolean fake_exception_check(JNIEnv *env)
+{
+    (void)env;
+    return JNI_FALSE;
+}
+
+static void fake_exception_clear(JNIEnv *env)
+{
+    (void)env;
+}
+
+static const struct JNINativeInterface_ fake_functions = {
+    fake_find_class,
+    fake_global_ref,
+    fake_delete_ref,
+    fake_delete_ref,
+    fake_get_method_id,
+    fake_get_object_class,

+    fake_new_string_utf,

+    fake_call_object_method,

+    fake_release_string_utf_chars,
+    fake_is_instance_of,
+    fake_get_field_id,
+    fake_get_float_field,
+    fake_exception_check,
+    fake_exception_clear,
+};
+
+/* The registration hook stays unused: the scenarios call the platform
+ * callback table directly, exactly as the Android runtime does. */
+void ui_register_callbacks(UIBridgeCallbacks *callbacks)
+{
+    (void)callbacks;
+}
+
+int __android_log_print(int priority, const char *tag, const char *format, ...)
+{
+    (void)priority;
+    (void)tag;
+    (void)format;
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* ---- Compile the real Android bridge with the fakes ---- */
+
+#include HATTER_UNDERSCORED_BRIDGE
+
+/* ---- Scenario drivers ---- */
+
+static void reset_observation(void)
+{
+    font_calls = 0;
+    padding_calls = 0;
+    called_object = NULL;
+    called_font_size = 0.0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
+        called_padding[i] = 0;
+    }
+}
+
+/* Create a node through the bridge callback the Android runtime uses.
+ * Returns -1 (never aborts) when the bridge cannot create the node so
+ * the caller decides the scenario verdict. */
+static int32_t create_node(int32_t node_type, jobject view)
+{
+    int32_t node_id;
+
+    g_pending_view = view;
+    reset_observation();
+    node_id = g_android_callbacks.createNode(node_type);
+    if (node_id < 1) {
+        fprintf(stderr,
+            "the bridge could not create a view for node type %d\n",
+            node_type);
+        return -1;
+    }
+    return node_id;
+}
+
+static int expect_font_call(
+    int32_t node_type, jobject view, double size, const char *label)
+{
+    int32_t node_id = create_node(node_type, view);
+
+    if (node_id < 1) {
+        return 1;
+    }
+    reset_observation();
+    g_android_callbacks.setNumProp(node_id, UI_PROP_FONT_SIZE, size);
+    if (font_calls != 1 || padding_calls != 0 || called_object != view
+            || called_font_size != size) {
+        fprintf(stderr,
+            "font size %.2f was passed to setNumProp but no Android text-size"
+            " call reached the %s\n",
+            size, label);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static int expect_padding_call(
+    int32_t node_type, jobject view, jint padding, const char *label)
+{
+    int32_t node_id = create_node(node_type, view);
+
+    if (node_id < 1) {
+        return 1;
+    }
+    reset_observation();
+    g_android_callbacks.setNumProp(node_id, UI_PROP_PADDING, padding);
+    if (padding_calls != 1 || font_calls != 0 || called_object != view) {
+        fprintf(stderr,
+            "padding %d was passed to setNumProp but no Android padding"
+            " call reached the %s\n",
+            padding, label);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
+        if (called_padding[i] != padding) {
+            fprintf(stderr,
+                "padding was not applied uniformly on all four sides of the %s\n",
+                label);
+            return 1;
+        }
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+typedef int (*scenario_fn)(void);
+
+static int scenario_font_text_label(void)
+{
+    return expect_font_call(
+        UI_NODE_TEXT, OBJECT_TEXT_VIEW, 18.5, "text label view");
+}
+
+static int scenario_font_text_input(void)
+{
+    return expect_font_call(
+        UI_NODE_TEXT_INPUT, OBJECT_EDIT_TEXT, 23.25, "text input view");
+}
+
+static int scenario_font_button(void)
+{
+    return expect_font_call(
+        UI_NODE_BUTTON, OBJECT_BUTTON, 19.75, "button label view");
+}
+
+static int scenario_padding_all_native_views(void)
+{
+    return expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_TEXT, OBJECT_TEXT_VIEW, 7, "text view")
+        || expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_BUTTON, OBJECT_BUTTON, 7, "button view")
+        || expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_COLUMN, OBJECT_COLUMN, 7, "column view")
+        || expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_ROW, OBJECT_ROW, 7, "row view")
+        || expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_TEXT_INPUT, OBJECT_EDIT_TEXT, 7, "text input view")
+        || expect_padding_call(UI_NODE_SCROLL_VIEW, OBJECT_SCROLL_VIEW, 7, "scroll view");
+}
+
+int main(int argc, char **argv)
+{
+    JNIEnv env = &fake_functions;
+    int all = argc == 1 || strcmp(argv[1], "--scenario") != 0;
+    struct {
+        const char *name;
+        scenario_fn run;
+    } scenarios[] = {
+        { "font-size-applied-to-text-label", scenario_font_text_label },
+        { "font-size-applied-to-text-input", scenario_font_text_input },
+        { "font-size-applied-to-button", scenario_font_button },
+        { "padding-applied-to-all-native-view-types", scenario_padding_all_native_views },
+    };
+    int ran = 0;
+    int failed = 0;
+
+    g_env = &env;
+    g_activity = OBJECT_ANY_VIEW;
+    if (resolve_jni_ids(&env, g_activity) != 0) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "fake Android JNI setup failed\n");
+        return 1;
+    }
+
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(scenarios) / sizeof(scenarios[0]); i++) {
+        if (!all && strcmp(argv[2], scenarios[i].name) != 0) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        ran = 1;
+        if (scenarios[i].run() != 0) {
+            failed = 1;
+        }
+    }
+    if (!ran) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "unknown Android numeric-property scenario: %s\n",
+            argc > 2 ? argv[2] : "(none given)");
+        return 1;
+    }
+    return failed;
+}

problem_statement:
Keeper FSM stuck-turn livelock: 10 (keeper, turn) pairs retry 4-12× over 4+ hours, no max-attempts guard
## 증상

10 distinct (keeper, turn) 쌍이 같은 turn 번호로 4-12회 재시도. 일부는 4시간+ 동안 advance 못 함.

```
$ jq '.message' system_log_2026-04-25.jsonl | grep -oE 'agent=[^ ]+ turn=[0-9]+' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | awk '$1 >= 4'
12 agent=keeper-qa-king-agent turn=91
11 agent=keeper-taskmaster-agent turn=96
 8 agent=keeper-ramarama-agent turn=24
 8 agent=keeper-nick0cave-agent turn=70
 8 agent=keeper-analyst-agent turn=27
 6 agent=keeper-velvet-hammer-agent turn=19
 6 agent=keeper-ramarama-agent turn=25
 6 agent=keeper-qa-king-agent turn=92
 5 agent=keeper-verifier-agent turn=32
 5 agent=keeper-qa-king-agent turn=94
```

## qa-king turn=91 타임라인 (대표 사례)

```
2026-04-24T15:03:48 turn started turn=91
2026-04-24T15:14:30 turn completed turn=91  (model=qwen3.6, latency_ms=6)  ← 1차 OK
2026-04-24T15:20:52 turn started turn=91   ← 같은 turn 재시작
2026-04-24T15:23:16 keeper cycle FAILED  cascade=big_three latency=...
2026-04-24T15:33:52 turn started turn=91   ← 다시 같은 turn
2026-04-24T15:53:21 keeper cycle FAILED
2026-04-24T16:14:01 turn started turn=91
2026-04-24T16:33:31 keeper cycle FAILED
2026-04-24T17:07:00 turn started turn=91
2026-04-24T17:15:07 turn started turn=91
2026-04-24T17:23:04 turn completed turn=91  (model=qwen3.6, latency_ms=4)  ← 2차 OK
2026-04-24T17:32:11 turn started turn=91   ← 또 다시
2026-04-24T17:32:49 keeper cycle OK model=claude_code:auto latency=1062575ms  ← 17.7 분
2026-04-24T17:59:55 keeper cycle OK model=claude_code:auto latency=457093ms   ← 7.6 분
```

**같은 turn=91 이 6번 "completed", 사이사이 cascade 실패 누적**. 4시간+ 동안 turn counter 가 92로 advance 안 됨.

## Root cause (causal chain)

상위 layer 의 write_meta race (관련 #9733) 가 livelock 원인:

```
1. Turn N 시작 → cycle 완료 → turn_counter 를 N+1 로 in-memory update
2. write_meta 호출 → CAS conflict → ERROR log → in-memory increment 손실
3. (heartbeat 등 다른 fiber 가 disk 의 turn_counter 를 N 으로 유지)
4. 다음 cycle 시작 시 disk 에서 turn_counter=N 읽음
5. 같은 turn N 으로 재시작 → goto 1
```

증거: iter62 의 #9733 follow-up 에서 `write_meta failed after keeper_msg turn` 등 7+ 사이트가 bare `write_meta` (no retry) 사용 — turn-completion payload 손실 확인.

그러나 이는 **trigger** 일 뿐. Defense-in-depth 측면에서 **FSM 자체가 livelock detection 기제 부재**.

## FSM 의 누락된 guard

`Keeper_state_machine` 또는 keeper turn dispatcher 에 다음 guard 부재:

- **Per-turn retry budget**: 같은 turn_id 에 대해 N 회 (예: 3) 시도 후 더는 시작 안 함
- **Stuck-turn alert**: 같은 turn_id 가 X 분 (예: 30) 이상 advance 못 하면 operator 에게 alert
- **Poison turn marking**: N 회 실패 후 turn 을 "poison" 으로 마킹, skip 또는 외부 review 요청
- **Turn-counter divergence detection**: in-memory vs disk turn_counter 가 N 분 이상 불일치 시 강제 sync 또는 abort

현재 동작: keeper 가 `oas_timeout_budget` cascade exhaust → cycle FAILED → 다음 cycle 시 같은 turn 시작. 무한.

## 영향

1. **Resource burn**: qa-king turn=91 한 turn 에 6 successful cycles + 3 failed cascades = ~30+ 분 LLM time (claude_code:auto 17.7 분 × 1, 7.6 분 × 1, qwen3.6 × 2, big_three timeout × 3). 한 turn 에 30+ 분 = 14 keeper × stuck turn 평균 = 시간당 수 시간 LLM cost 낭비.
2. **Progress 정지**: 4시간+ 동안 keeper 가 다음 turn 으로 못 넘어감 → 실제 작업 진행 0.
3. **Telemetry 왜곡**: turn count = 91 이 6번 완료로 기록 → dashboard 가 turn velocity 과대평가, latency 통계 (turn 91 의 30+ 분) 가 정상 turn 으로 평균에 들어감.
4. **Fleet-wide effect**: 10 stuck turns × 14 keepers = significant portion of fleet 정체.

## 카테고리

- **FSM 오류**: ✓ primary — 무한 retry guard 부재
- **로직 문제**: ✓ secondary — write_meta race 가 trigger
- **로깅 및 텔레메트리**: ✓ — turn count 가 stuck 임을 surface 안 함

## 수정 제안

### Option A — Per-turn retry budget (권장)

`Keeper_state_machine` 또는 `keeper_agent_run` 에 turn_attempt counter:

[HIDDEN]

Poison turn 은 skip + WARN log + dashboard alert. 또는 turn descriptor 를 외부 review queue 로 이동.

### Option B — Boot-time stale-turn detection

서버 부팅 시 disk meta 에서 `last_completed_turn` 와 `last_started_turn` 비교. 차이가 N 이상이면 startup WARN + 자동 advance:

```
[livelock-detect] keeper qa-king: last_started=91 last_completed=90 (5+ start events).
Marking turn 91 as poison; advancing to 92.
```

### Option C — Causal fix: write_meta retry coverage

iter62 #9733 follow-up 의 migration 적용. write_meta race 가 사라지면 turn counter 손실 자체 발생 안 함. 그러나 이것만으로는 **다른 cause 의 livelock** 막지 못함.

권장: **A + C 동시**. A 가 defense-in-depth, C 가 root cause fix.

## 근거

- `~/me/.masc/logs/system_log_2026-04-25.jsonl`: 10 stuck-turn pairs, 5+ attempts each
- qa-king turn=91 4시간+ stuck (15:03 → 17:59)
- `Keeper_state_machine` 모듈에 retry/livelock guard 부재 (`rg -n 'max_attempts|poison_turn|stuck_turn' lib/keeper/`)

## 관련

- **#9733** (OPEN): write_meta CAS race — root cause trigger.
- **iter62 follow-up comment**: bare write_meta 7+ 사이트 migration 누락.
- #9943 (OPEN): claude_code:auto turn 20 분 burn — 본 이슈의 stuck-turn 이 정확히 이런 long-latency 를 누적.
- #9771 (OPEN): semaphore wait > 60s skip turn — 다른 turn-skip mechanism, 본 이슈와 별개.
- #7035 (CLOSED): cascade exhaustion blocker persists — 부분적으로 같은 영역.

### Additional contract requirements

The keeper dispatch behavior must prevent repeated work for a turn that is not advancing:

1. For the same keeper and turn id, dispatches within the configured attempt budget may proceed. The next dispatch must be blocked before model or prompt work, and the blocked cycle must complete without doing that work.
2. A keeper turn that remains at the same id longer than the configured stuck-age threshold must likewise be blocked before model or prompt work, independently of the attempt budget.
3. Configure the attempt budget with `MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, defaulting to 3. Configure the stuck-age threshold with `MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_STUCK_AFTER_SEC`, defaulting to 1800.0 seconds.
4. Failed or incomplete cycles at one turn id do not reset that id's attempt budget. When the turn completes and the turn counter advances, dispatch at the new id proceeds without being blocked by the previous id's budget.
5. Each blocked dispatch increments the Prometheus counter `masc_keeper_turn_livelock_blocks_total`, labeled by keeper and by a reason that identifies an exhausted attempt budget or exceeded stuck age (`attempts_exhausted` or `stuck_age_exceeded`). Each blocked dispatch also produces an error-level keeper log entry naming the keeper, turn id, and reason.
6. Preserve the existing reattempt/regression classifications and their counters.

+let expect_blocked ~msg ~keeper ~reason ~base_dir meta =
+  let classification, _res =
+    classify_cycle ~keeper ~reason ~label:msg (fun () ->
+        run_cycle ~base_dir meta)
+  in
+  match classification with
+  | Blocked -> Alcotest.(check pass) msg () ()
+  | Reached_dispatch -> Alcotest.fail msg
+
+let with_dispatch_env ~name f =
+  Eio_main.run @@ fun env ->
+  Fs_compat.set_fs (Eio.Stdenv.fs env);
+  let base_dir = temp_dir () in
+  let old_base = Sys.getenv_opt "MASC_BASE_PATH" in
+  Fun.protect
+    ~finally:(fun () ->
+      Unix.putenv "MASC_BASE_PATH" (Option.value ~default:"" old_base);
+      KR.clear ();
+      cleanup_dir base_dir)
+    (fun () ->
+      KR.clear ();
+      Unix.putenv "MASC_BASE_PATH" base_dir;
+      let meta = make_cycle_meta ~name in
+      ignore (KR.register ~base_path:base_dir name meta);
+      Alcotest.(check (option string))
+        "keeper registered in running phase"
+        (Some "running")
+        (Option.map KP.phase_to_string
+           (KR.get_phase ~base_path:base_dir name));
+      f ~base_dir meta)
+
+(* 7. Retry budget at the real dispatch boundary: with
+   [MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3], the first three cycles
+   at the same turn id reach model dispatch (and fail on the
+   unreachable local model), the fourth is blocked BEFORE any
+   model/prompt work and increments the
+   attempts_exhausted block counter. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_max_attempts_budget () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-max-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  List.iter
+    (fun attempt ->
+      expect_dispatched ~attempt ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+        ~base_dir meta)
+    [ 1; 2; 3 ];
+  expect_blocked ~msg:"attempt 4 blocked before model dispatch" ~keeper
+    ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~base_dir meta
+
+(* 8. Stuck-age guard at the dispatch boundary: a generous attempt
+   budget but a near-zero age threshold blocks the second cycle at the
+   same turn id before model dispatch and increments the
+   stuck_age_exceeded block counter. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_stuck_age_blocks () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-age-10121" in
+  (* The isolated process receives a 100-attempt budget and 1s age
+     threshold before the configuration snapshot is initialized. *)
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  expect_dispatched ~attempt:1 ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded"
+    ~base_dir meta;
+  (* Spend enough wall-clock that the same turn id is older than the
+     1s stuck threshold without completing a turn. *)
+  Unix.sleepf 1.1;
+  expect_blocked
+    ~msg:"second attempt past age threshold blocked before dispatch"
+    ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded" ~base_dir meta
+
+(* 9. Forward progress that never reaches model work (each cycle
+   fails during dispatch at the same turn id) does NOT restore
+   dispatch: attempts keep counting against the budget. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_failed_cycles_do_not_reset_budget () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-nofwd-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  List.iter
+    (fun attempt ->
+      expect_dispatched ~attempt ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+        ~base_dir meta)
+    [ 1; 2 ];
+  expect_blocked
+    ~msg:"third cycle blocked: failed attempts exhaust the budget"
+    ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~base_dir meta
+
+(* 11a. Defaults with unset configuration -- with the max-attempts
+   environment variable UNSET, the guard must behave as if the budget
+   were 3: dispatches 1..3 proceed into the dispatch path and the 4th
+   is blocked, all at the same turn id.  A fresh keeper name and
+   [reset_for_tests] give this case its own guard state. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_defaults_max_attempts () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-default-max-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  List.iter
+    (fun attempt ->
+      expect_dispatched ~attempt ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+        ~base_dir meta)
+    [ 1; 2; 3 ];
+  expect_blocked ~msg:"attempt 4 blocked: default budget is exactly 3"
+    ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~base_dir meta
+
+(* 11b. With the age setting unset, dispatch remains allowed for a
+   turn younger than the 1800-second default and is blocked once its
+   age exceeds that threshold. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_defaults_stuck_age () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-default-age-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  let before_age_blocks =
+    blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded"
+  in
+  expect_dispatched ~attempt:1 ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded"
+    ~base_dir meta;
+  (* A 61-second-old turn is still below the documented 1800-second
+     default, and rules out a materially smaller 60-second default. *)
+  Unix.sleepf 61.0;
+  expect_dispatched ~attempt:2 ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded"
+    ~base_dir meta;
+  Alcotest.(check (float 0.0001))
+    "a turn active for 61 seconds is not age-blocked under the 1800.0s default"
+    before_age_blocks
+    (blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded")
+
+(* 12. Block observability: a blocked dispatch must surface an
+   ERROR-level entry in the Keeper log ring naming the keeper, the
+   turn id that was blocked, and the block reason.  The assertion
+   filters the ring by keeper name, so pre-existing entries cannot
+   contaminate it. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_blocked_turn_logs_error () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-log-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  let turn_id = meta.KT.runtime.usage.total_turns in
+  List.iter
+    (fun attempt ->
+      expect_dispatched ~attempt ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+        ~base_dir meta)
+    [ 1; 2 ];
+  let log_cursor = Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1 ~order:`Newest_first () in
+  let blocked_classification, _blocked_res =
+    classify_cycle ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~label:"cycle 3"
+      (fun () -> run_cycle ~base_dir meta)
+  in
+  (match blocked_classification with
+   | Blocked ->
+     Alcotest.(check pass) "cycle 3 blocked before model dispatch" () ()
+   | Reached_dispatch ->
+     Alcotest.fail
+       "cycle 3 should be blocked by the retry budget, not dispatched");
+  let new_entries =
+    match log_cursor with
+    | [] -> Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1000 ~order:`Oldest_first ()
+    | (cursor_entry : Log.Ring.entry) :: _ ->
+      Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1000 ~order:`Oldest_first
+        ~since_seq:cursor_entry.seq ()
+  in
+  let keeper_error_entries =
+    List.filter
+      (fun (entry : Log.Ring.entry) ->
+        string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:keeper)
+      new_entries
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "blocked dispatch produced a Keeper log entry naming the keeper"
+    true
+    (keeper_error_entries <> []);
+  (* Accept equivalent human-readable reason wording while requiring
+     the log to name the actual blocked turn id. *)
+  let names_turn_id (entry : Log.Ring.entry) =
+    string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:(string_of_int turn_id)
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "the entry is error-level and names keeper, turn id, and reason"
+    true
+    (List.exists
+       (fun (entry : Log.Ring.entry) ->
+         string_contains ~haystack:entry.normalized_level
+           ~needle:"error"
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.module_name
+              ~needle:"keeper"
+         && names_turn_id entry
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"attempt"
+         && (string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"exhaust"
+             || string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"budget"
+             || string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"max"))
+       keeper_error_entries);
+  Alcotest.(check (float 0.0001))
+    "attempts_exhausted block counter incremented"
+    1.0
+    (blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted")
+
+
+let scenario_dispatch_stuck_age_logs_error () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-age-log-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  let turn_id = meta.KT.runtime.usage.total_turns in
+  expect_dispatched ~attempt:1 ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded"
+    ~base_dir meta;
+  Unix.sleepf 1.1;
+  let before_blocks = blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded" in
+  let log_cursor = Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1 ~order:`Newest_first () in
+  expect_blocked ~msg:"age-blocked dispatch" ~keeper
+    ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded" ~base_dir meta;
+  let new_entries =
+    match log_cursor with
+    | [] -> Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1000 ~order:`Oldest_first ()
+    | (cursor_entry : Log.Ring.entry) :: _ ->
+      Log.Ring.recent ~limit:1000 ~order:`Oldest_first
+        ~since_seq:cursor_entry.seq ()
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "age-blocked dispatch logs keeper, turn id, and stuck-age reason at error level"
+    true
+    (List.exists
+       (fun (entry : Log.Ring.entry) ->
+         string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:keeper
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.message
+              ~needle:(string_of_int turn_id)
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"stuck"
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.message ~needle:"age"
+         && string_contains ~haystack:entry.normalized_level ~needle:"error")
+       new_entries);
+  Alcotest.(check (float 0.0001))
+    "stuck-age block counter increments" (before_blocks +. 1.0)
+    (blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"stuck_age_exceeded")
+
+(* 10. Genuine forward progress restores dispatch: a completed turn
+   increments [total_turns], changing the id the guard sees, so the
+   budget for the new id starts fresh. *)
+let scenario_dispatch_completed_turn_restores_dispatch () =
+  L.reset_for_tests ();
+  let keeper = "test-keeper-dispatch-restore-10121" in
+  with_dispatch_env ~name:keeper @@ fun ~base_dir meta ->
+  let before_blocks =
+    blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+  in
+  let before_starts = starts_for ~keeper in
+  List.iter
+    (fun attempt ->
+      expect_dispatched ~attempt ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted"
+        ~base_dir meta)
+    [ 1; 2 ];
+  expect_blocked ~msg:"budget exhausted at turn id 0" ~keeper
+    ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~base_dir meta;
+  let starts_exhausted = starts_for ~keeper in
+  (* A completed turn advances the turn counter: the keeper moves to
+     the next turn id, and the guard must let it dispatch again.  The
+     advanced meta is built through the public
+     [Keeper_types.map_runtime]/[map_usage] surface -- the joints used
+     by production meta-update code -- rather than by round-tripping
+     the record's internal representation. *)
+  let advanced_meta =
+    KT.map_usage
+      (fun (u : KT.usage_metrics) ->
+        { u with KT.total_turns = u.KT.total_turns + 1 })
+      meta
+  in
+  expect_dispatched ~attempt:4 ~keeper
+    ~reason:"attempts_exhausted" ~base_dir advanced_meta;
+  Alcotest.(check (float 0.0001))
+    "exactly one block (the exhausted budget at turn id 0)"
+    (before_blocks +. 1.0)
+    (blocks_for ~keeper ~reason:"attempts_exhausted");
+  (* Turn starts at this turn id are bounded by the three same-id
+     runs above: the blocked run is not a new turn start under most
+     gate placements, and placements that record the same-id restart
+     before admitting or gating dispatch still stay within the
+     bound. *)
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "turn starts bounded by the three same-id runs"
+    true
+    (starts_exhausted <= before_starts +. 3.0 +. 0.0001)
+
+let run_isolated_dispatch scenario ?max_attempts ?stuck_after () =
+  let controlled =
+    [ "MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS";
+      "MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_STUCK_AFTER_SEC" ]
+  in
+  let inherited =
+    Array.to_list (Unix.environment ())
+    |> List.filter (fun item ->
+           not
+             (List.exists
+                (fun name ->
+                  String.length item > String.length name
+                  && String.sub item 0 (String.length name + 1) = name ^ "=")
+                controlled))
+  in
+  let configured =
+    inherited
+    @ (match max_attempts with
+       | None -> []
+       | Some value -> [ "MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS=" ^ value ])
+    @ (match stuck_after with
+       | None -> []
+       | Some value -> [ "MASC_KEEPER_TURN_LIVELOCK_STUCK_AFTER_SEC=" ^ value ])
+  in
+  let executable = Sys.executable_name in
+  let argv = [| executable; "--livelock-scenario"; scenario |] in
+  let pid =
+    Unix.create_process_env executable argv (Array.of_list configured)
+      Unix.stdin Unix.stdout Unix.stderr
+  in
+  match snd (Unix.waitpid [] pid) with
+  | Unix.WEXITED 0 -> ()
+  | Unix.WEXITED code -> Alcotest.failf "%s child failed with status %d" scenario code
+  | Unix.WSIGNALED signal -> Alcotest.failf "%s child killed by signal %d" scenario signal
+  | Unix.WSTOPPED signal -> Alcotest.failf "%s child stopped by signal %d" scenario signal
+
+let test_dispatch_max_attempts_budget () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "max" ~max_attempts:"3" ~stuck_after:"3600.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_stuck_age_blocks () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "age" ~max_attempts:"100" ~stuck_after:"1.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_failed_cycles_do_not_reset_budget () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "failed" ~max_attempts:"2" ~stuck_after:"3600.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_defaults_max_attempts () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "default-max" ~stuck_after:"7200.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_defaults_stuck_age () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "default-age" ~max_attempts:"100" ()
+let test_dispatch_blocked_turn_logs_error () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "attempt-log" ~max_attempts:"2" ~stuck_after:"3600.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_stuck_age_logs_error () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "age-log" ~max_attempts:"100" ~stuck_after:"1.0" ()
+let test_dispatch_completed_turn_restores_dispatch () =
+  run_isolated_dispatch "forward" ~max_attempts:"2" ~stuck_after:"3600.0" ()
+
+let isolated_case scenario fn =
+  Alcotest.run ~argv:[| Sys.argv.(0) |] "keeper_turn_livelock_scenario"
+    [ ("scenario", [ Alcotest.test_case scenario `Quick fn ]) ]
+
+let run_full_suite () =
+  Alcotest.run ~argv:Sys.argv "keeper_turn_livelock_10121"
     [
       ( "fresh",
         [
@@ -194,4 +721,37 @@ let () =
           Alcotest.test_case "seconds_since_first_attempt" `Quick
             test_seconds_since_first_attempt;
         ] );
+      ( "dispatch",
+        [
+          Alcotest.test_case "max attempts budget gates dispatch" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_max_attempts_budget;
+          Alcotest.test_case "stuck age gates dispatch" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_stuck_age_blocks;
+          Alcotest.test_case "failed cycles do not reset budget" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_failed_cycles_do_not_reset_budget;
+          Alcotest.test_case "completed turn restores dispatch" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_completed_turn_restores_dispatch;
+          Alcotest.test_case "unset env uses default max attempts" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_defaults_max_attempts;
+          Alcotest.test_case "unset env uses default stuck age" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_defaults_stuck_age;
+          Alcotest.test_case "blocked dispatch logs error entry" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_blocked_turn_logs_error;
+          Alcotest.test_case "stuck-age block logs error entry" `Quick
+            test_dispatch_stuck_age_logs_error;
+        ] );
     ]
+
+let () =
+  if Array.length Sys.argv > 2 && Sys.argv.(1) = "--livelock-scenario" then
+    (match Sys.argv.(2) with
+     | "max" -> isolated_case "max attempts" scenario_dispatch_max_attempts_budget
+     | "age" -> isolated_case "stuck age" scenario_dispatch_stuck_age_blocks
+     | "failed" -> isolated_case "failed cycles" scenario_dispatch_failed_cycles_do_not_reset_budget
+     | "default-max" -> isolated_case "default max attempts" scenario_dispatch_defaults_max_attempts
+     | "default-age" -> isolated_case "default stuck age" scenario_dispatch_defaults_stuck_age
+     | "attempt-log" -> isolated_case "attempt block log" scenario_dispatch_blocked_turn_logs_error
+     | "age-log" -> isolated_case "age block log" scenario_dispatch_stuck_age_logs_error
+     | "forward" -> isolated_case "forward progress" scenario_dispatch_completed_turn_restores_dispatch
+     | unknown -> Alcotest.failf "unknown isolated scenario %s" unknown)
+  else run_full_suite ()

dispatch 1 stuck age gates dispatch.

problem_statement:
refactor: remove hardcoded LLM model names, use provider-level defaults
## Problem

39 hardcoded model names across lib/ (e.g., `glm-4.7`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `gpt-5`). These break when models are deprecated or renamed.

## Current (broken)

```ocaml
[HIDDEN]
```

## Target

Default should be **provider** (e.g., `glm`, `gemini`, `claude`), not specific model versions. Provider resolves the current model at runtime.

## Affected files

| File | Count | Type |
|------|-------|------|
| `env_config_governance.ml` | 6 | Default values (highest risk) |
| `provider_adapter.ml` | 8 | Model spec construction |
| `lodge_cascade.ml` | 6 | Cascade chain building |
| `llm_types.ml` | 2 | Default model_spec records |
| `chain_stats.ml` | 5 | Price table |
| `council/router.ml` | 4 | Tier routing |
| Others | 8 | Various consumers |

## Approach

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

# Provider-level model defaults

Built-in cascade defaults select provider families rather than version-specific
model identifiers. In particular, the fallback safety net for an unknown
cascade and for every named built-in cascade must select the GLM provider and
defer its concrete model choice to runtime provider resolution.

A provider default may be represented by an empty configured model identifier
or by that provider's canonical name. Explicit provider/model configuration
continues to select the supplied model. Provider availability and pricing must
classify current or renamed models by provider family rather than require a
fixed list of versioned names.

Locally hosted models (llama, ollama) may appear in cascades with explicit
versioned identifiers; when no locally hosted model is configured, a cascade
that would lead with one degrades gracefully to its provider-only safety net.

+let fake_curl_script () =

+      "body=$(cat)";
+      "printf '%s\\t%s\\n' \"$6\" \"$body\" >> \"$" ^ recorded_requests_variable ^ "\"";

+                | None -> loop acc)
