problem_statement:
[P0] SafeAuto source-path discontinuation boundary is not implemented
## Problem

The P0 plan calls for fixing a SafeAuto/effect-handler source-path loss:

- effect handler discontinuation loses backtrace/source-path evidence
- source path should be attached to the effect payload before `discontinue`

During the current implementation pass, no direct `SafeAuto`, `safe_auto`,
`discontinue`, or `Effect.Deep.discontinue` code path was found in current
`masc-mcp` or `oas`. The nearest concrete fix is in OAS PR #1398, which adds
`Effect_evidence.source_path/source_line` and populates it at the
`Mode_enforcer` boundary.

## Evidence

- `rg "SafeAuto|safe_auto|discontinue|Effect\\.Deep\\.discontinue"` found no direct runtime effect-discontinue implementation.
- `safe-autonomy` hits are dashboard/read-model surfaces, not OCaml effect handlers.
- OAS PR: https://github.com/jeong-sik/oas/pull/1398

## Done Criteria

- Identify the actual SafeAuto/effect-handler discontinuation boundary, or explicitly remove/rename the stale SafeAuto requirement if it no longer exists.
- Attach source path/line to the payload before any continuation discontinuation.
- Add regression coverage that fails when source path is absent.
- Document the concrete source path propagation boundary in the PR body.

### Additional contract requirements

# Source-location evidence at the policy boundary

The stale “SafeAuto discontinuation” name is retired: this repository contains
no SafeAuto or continuation-discontinuation runtime boundary. For integrated
policy execution, the concrete producer boundary is the policy/effect mode
decision that can deny or otherwise block a tool attempt. That producer must
attach the call site's source path to the effect row before the decision can
terminate or short-circuit processing; it should also attach the source line
when one is available. The producer boundary lives in the agent SDK, which
this repository consumes only as an external dependency; the first producer
release whose effect rows carry the attached source-location fields is agent
SDK 0.190.10. Consequently, the repository must require the installed agent
SDK producer to be version 0.190.10 or newer, and that requirement must be
visible in the repository's own dependency and pin records (the canonical
executable pin record and the package manifest that mirrors it). The
repository must not depend on an older producer whose finalized effect rows
lack source-location evidence. The requirement name assignments,
quoting, and formatting used to express this minimum are unspecified,
but the requirement must be expressed in the shape of an effective
minimum-version assignment or comparison: a version string appearing
only in commentary or as bare unpaired text in those records does not
satisfy it.

MASC observes those rows through a referenced `evidence/effects.json` proof
artifact. The artifact is a JSON array. A row supplies usable source-location
evidence when `source_path` is a non-empty string after surrounding whitespace
is ignored. Consumers must tolerate an absent `source_line`.

Whenever a run records one or more blocked attempts, proof projection must
assess the referenced effect artifact for that run. The source-location
completeness requirement fails for the run when no referenced effect artifact
exists, when no readable referenced effect artifact can be interpreted as
effect rows, or when no row supplies usable source-location evidence.

A proof projection must still be produced for every run, including a blocked
run whose source-location completeness requirement fails. A projection's
public result exposes its negative outcomes through two observable
categories: evidence-completeness gap entries and review tripwire entries.
A failure of the source-location completeness requirement must be observable
in the projection's public result as a net-new negative outcome in one of
those categories for the affected run; when usable source-location evidence
is present for a blocked run, no negative outcome on source-location
completeness grounds may be reported for it. A run that records no blocked
attempts must not acquire any negative outcome on source-location
completeness grounds. The same assessment applies to multi-run projection,
independently for every blocked run in the window: usable evidence in one
run does not compensate for another blocked run that lacks it.

Diagnostic wording, internal module boundaries, data types, and presentation
grouping are not prescribed; only the presence or absence of negative
outcomes in the categories above is contractually observable.

contract_addendum:
# Source-location evidence at the policy boundary

The stale “SafeAuto discontinuation” name is retired: this repository contains
no SafeAuto or continuation-discontinuation runtime boundary. For integrated
policy execution, the concrete producer boundary is the policy/effect mode
decision that can deny or otherwise block a tool attempt. That producer must
attach the call site's source path to the effect row before the decision can
terminate or short-circuit processing; it should also attach the source line
when one is available. The producer boundary lives in the agent SDK, which
this repository consumes only as an external dependency; the first producer
release whose effect rows carry the attached source-location fields is agent
SDK 0.190.10. Consequently, the repository must require the installed agent
SDK producer to be version 0.190.10 or newer, and that requirement must be
visible in the repository's own dependency and pin records (the canonical
executable pin record and the package manifest that mirrors it). The
repository must not depend on an older producer whose finalized effect rows
lack source-location evidence. The requirement name assignments,
quoting, and formatting used to express this minimum are unspecified,
but the requirement must be expressed in the shape of an effective
minimum-version assignment or comparison: a version string appearing
only in commentary or as bare unpaired text in those records does not
satisfy it.

MASC observes those rows through a referenced `evidence/effects.json` proof
artifact. The artifact is a JSON array. A row supplies usable source-location
evidence when `source_path` is a non-empty string after surrounding whitespace
is ignored. Consumers must tolerate an absent `source_line`.

Whenever a run records one or more blocked attempts, proof projection must
assess the referenced effect artifact for that run. The source-location
completeness requirement fails for the run when no referenced effect artifact
exists, when no readable referenced effect artifact can be interpreted as
effect rows, or when no row supplies usable source-location evidence.

A proof projection must still be produced for every run, including a blocked
run whose source-location completeness requirement fails. A projection's
public result exposes its negative outcomes through two observable
categories: evidence-completeness gap entries and review tripwire entries.
A failure of the source-location completeness requirement must be observable
in the projection's public result as a net-new negative outcome in one of
those categories for the affected run; when usable source-location evidence
is present for a blocked run, no negative outcome on source-location
completeness grounds may be reported for it. A run that records no blocked
attempts must not acquire any negative outcome on source-location
completeness grounds. The same assessment applies to multi-run projection,
independently for every blocked run in the window: usable evidence in one
run does not compensate for another blocked run that lacks it.

Diagnostic wording, internal module boundaries, data types, and presentation
grouping are not prescribed; only the presence or absence of negative
outcomes in the categories above is contractually observable.

@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+(** Effect_evidence -- Source-path evidence at the Mode_enforcer boundary.
+
+    @since SafeAuto source-path boundary *)
+
+type t = {
+  source_path : string option;
+  source_line : int option;
+}
+
+let empty = { source_path = None; source_line = None }
+
+let source_path_is_populated = function
+  | Some path -> String.trim path <> ""
+  | None -> false
+
+let normalize_source_path = function
+  | "" -> None
+  | path -> Some path
+
+let is_populated (ev : t) = source_path_is_populated ev.source_path
+
+let of_json (json : Yojson.Safe.t) : t =
+  let open Yojson.Safe.Util in
+  try
+    let source_path =
+      match json |> member "source_path" with
+      | `String s -> normalize_source_path (String.trim s)
+      | _ -> None
+    in
+    let source_line =
+      match json |> member "source_line" with
+      | `Int n -> Some n
+      | _ -> None
+    in
+    { source_path; source_line }
+  with Eio.Cancel.Cancelled _ as e -> raise e
+     | _exn ->
+       (* JSON shape mismatch (e.g. wrong type for a field) -- treat as no
+          evidence rather than propagating a parse failure. Source-path fields
+          are optional enrichment on OAS effects evidence; callers decide
+          whether absence is a blocking gap for their proof surface. *)
+       empty
+
+let of_json_list (json : Yojson.Safe.t) : (t list, string) result =
+  match json with
+  | `List items -> Ok (List.map of_json items)
+  | _ -> Error "expected JSON array of effect evidence records"
+
+let any_source_path_present events =
+  List.exists is_populated events
+
+let check_any_source_path_present events =
+  if any_source_path_present events then Ok ()
+  else Error "effects evidence is missing source_path at Mode_enforcer boundary"
+
+let to_json_fields (ev : t) : (string * Yojson.Safe.t) list =
+  let fields = [] in
+  let fields =
+    match ev.source_path with
+    | Some p -> ("source_path", `String p) :: fields
+    | None -> fields
+  in
+  let fields =
+    match ev.source_line with
+    | Some n -> ("source_line", `Int n) :: fields
+    | None -> fields
+  in
+  List.sort (fun (a, _) (b, _) -> String.compare a b) fields

+(** Effect_evidence -- Source-path evidence at the Mode_enforcer boundary.
+
+    Captures [source_path] and [source_line] from the call site where a
+    mode-enforcement effect payload is produced. OAS writes these rows to
+    [evidence/effects.json]; [mode_violations.json] remains the older grouped
+    summary surface.
+
+    Both fields are optional for backward compatibility with existing
+    proof artifacts that pre-date this evidence layer.
+
+    @since SafeAuto source-path boundary *)
+
+(** Source-path evidence from the Mode_enforcer call site. *)
+type t = {
+  source_path : string option;  (** Path of the file that triggered the effect. *)
+  source_line : int option;     (** Line number within [source_path]. *)
+}
+
+(** The empty evidence record: both fields are [None]. *)
+val empty : t
+
+(** [is_populated ev] returns [true] when [ev.source_path] is non-empty
+    after trimming whitespace. *)
+val is_populated : t -> bool
+
+(** Parse evidence from a JSON object.  Returns [empty] when neither
+    [source_path] nor [source_line] is present.  Unknown fields are
+    ignored. *)
+val of_json : Yojson.Safe.t -> t
+
+(** Parse [evidence/effects.json], returning [Error] when the artifact is not
+    a JSON array. Individual rows are lenient because source-path evidence is
+    enrichment on top of OAS' effect schema. *)
+val of_json_list : Yojson.Safe.t -> (t list, string) result
+
+(** [any_source_path_present events] is true when at least one effects row
+    carries a non-empty [source_path]. *)
+val any_source_path_present : t list -> bool
+
+(** [check_any_source_path_present events] fails when the effects artifact
+    contains no [source_path]. Use this at proof-consumption boundaries that
+    must not silently lose Mode_enforcer call-site evidence. *)
+val check_any_source_path_present : t list -> (unit, string) result
+
+(** Serialize evidence to a JSON assoc list (sorted keys).
+    Omits fields that are [None]. *)
+val to_json_fields : t -> (string * Yojson.Safe.t) list

@@ -0,0 +1,665 @@
+(** Regression coverage for source-location evidence in blocked-run proof
+    projections, expressed purely through observable projection outcomes.
+
+    These tests deliberately avoid prescribing production internals:
+    no producer module, no internal helper, no record construction, no
+    literal diagnostic wording, artifact label, impact value, or
+    presentation grouping is asserted.  Every scenario is a black-box
+    observation of the public projection result for a blocked run:
+
+    - when no readable referenced [effects.json] row supplies usable
+      source-location evidence, the projection's public result must
+      carry a negative outcome for the affected run;
+    - when at least one referenced row supplies usable source-location
+      evidence for a blocked run, the projection's public result must
+      carry no outcome on source-location completeness grounds for that
+      run, even if every other row lacks one; and
+    - a run without blocked attempts never carries an outcome on
+      source-location completeness grounds.
+
+    The projection's public result exposes its negative outcomes through
+    two observable categories -- evidence-completeness gap entries and
+    review tripwire entries -- and these tests observe only whether such
+    entries are present, never what they say or how they are grouped. *)
+
+module CFP = Masc_mcp.Cdal_friction_projection
+
+let usable_path = "lib/policy_boundary.ml"
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Test prerequisites                                                *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+(* Regression fixtures are created in-process below; production file
+   helpers are never invoked from this suite. *)
+let in_process_mkdir = Unix.mkdir
+
+let () = ignore in_process_mkdir
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Proof and store fixtures                                          *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+(* [make_proof] materializes the public proof fields needed to locate
+   referenced evidence artifacts ([run_id], [raw_evidence_refs]) plus
+   generic placeholder metadata with no contract meaning. *)
+let make_proof ~run_id ~raw_evidence_refs : Agent_sdk.Cdal_proof.t =
+  {
+    schema_version = Agent_sdk.Cdal_proof.schema_version_current;
+    run_id;
+    contract_id = "md5:source-path-regression";
+    requested_execution_mode = Execute;
+    effective_execution_mode = Execute;
+    mode_decision_source = "passthrough";
+    risk_class = Agent_sdk.Risk_class.Low;
+    provider_snapshot = {
+      provider_name = "test";
+      model_id = "test-model";
+      api_version = None;
+    };
+    capability_snapshot = {
+      tools = ["read"; "write"];
+      mcp_servers = [];
+      max_turns = 10;
+      max_tokens = Some 4096;
+      thinking_enabled = None;
+    };
+    tool_trace_refs = [];
+    raw_evidence_refs;
+    checkpoint_ref = None;
+    result_status = Completed;
+    started_at = 1000.0;
+    ended_at = 1001.0;
+    scope = None;
+  }
+
+let make_proof_for_window ~run_id ~raw_evidence_refs ~ended_at
+    : Agent_sdk.Cdal_proof.t =
+  let proof = make_proof ~run_id ~raw_evidence_refs in
+  { proof with
+    Agent_sdk.Cdal_proof.started_at = ended_at -. 1.0;
+    ended_at;
+  }
+
+let setup_store () =

+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Observable outcome                                                *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+(** A public projection result carries an observable negative outcome
+    when it exposes any evidence-completeness gap entry or any review
+    tripwire entry.  Only presence is observed; entry wording, artifact
+    labels, impact values, and grouping are never inspected. *)
+let has_negative_outcome (projection : CFP.friction_projection) : bool =
+  projection.CFP.evidence_gap_groups <> []
+  || projection.CFP.review_tripwires <> []
+
+(** A projection must exist for every run: absent or unusable
+    source-location evidence changes the projection's reported
+    outcomes, never its existence. *)
+let require_projection = function
+  | Some projection -> projection
+  | None -> Alcotest.fail "a blocked run must still produce a projection"
+
+(** [projects_completeness_failure ~without ~with_] checks the full
+    observable contract for one failing scenario:
+
+    - the scenario with usable source-location evidence ([with_]) must
+      produce a projection carrying no negative outcome;
+    - the same run without usable source-location evidence ([without])
+      must produce a projection carrying a negative outcome.
+
+    Asserting both directions proves that the observed outcome is
+    net-new for the affected run rather than an unconditional
+    diagnostic emitted for every blocked run. *)
+let projects_completeness_failure ~without ~with_ : bool =
+  let with_projection = require_projection (with_ ()) in
+  if has_negative_outcome with_projection then
+    Alcotest.fail
+      "a blocked run with usable source-location evidence must carry \
+       no negative outcome"
+  ;
+  let without_projection = require_projection (without ()) in
+  has_negative_outcome without_projection
+
+let expect_completeness_failure name ~without ~with_ =
+  Alcotest.(check bool) name true
+    (projects_completeness_failure ~without ~with_)
+
+let project_single store ~run_id ~refs () =
+  CFP.project_single_run ~store (make_proof ~run_id ~raw_evidence_refs:refs)

+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Producer-version requirement records                              *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+(* The producer lives outside this repository, so its conformance is
+   represented here by two repository-owned requirements: the package
+   manifest and the canonical executable pin record.
+
+   The checks below recognise effective minimum-version semantics
+   wherever they appear in the record rather than prescribing a field
+   name, a quoting style, a comparison spelling, or a line layout.
+   Two equivalent forms are accepted in each record:
+
+   - [stipulates_min ~near_producer]: a version that is greater than or
+     equal to the floor and is preceded by a lower-bound operator
+     ([>=], [>], [=], or assignment through [=] or [:]); and
+   - [stipulates_pin]: a literal assignment or declaration of a version
+     greater than or equal to the floor with NO relational operator.
+
+   For the package manifest, which aggregates requirements for many
+   dependencies, the expression must additionally name the producer on
+   the same physical line, so an unrelated dependency's floor cannot
+   be mistaken for the producer floor.  Statements may span lines:
+   only individual line comments are removed, never whole statements. *)
+
+let producer_floor = (0, 190, 10)
+
+let floor_text () =
+  let major, minor, patch = producer_floor in
+  String.concat "."
+    (List.map string_of_int [major; minor; patch])
+
+let read_text path =
+  let ic = open_in_bin path in
+  let len = in_channel_length ic in
+  let text = really_input_string ic len in
+  close_in ic;
+  text
+
+let locate_project_root () =
+  let is_root dir =
+    Sys.file_exists (Filename.concat dir "dune-project")
+  in
+  let rec ascend dir =
+    if is_root dir then Some dir
+    else
+      let parent = Filename.dirname dir in
+      if String.equal parent dir then None else ascend parent
+  in
+  match ascend (Sys.getcwd ()) with
+  | Some root -> root
+  | None ->
+    Alcotest.fail
+      "cannot locate the project root above the test executable"
+
+let require_record root relative_path =
+  let path = Filename.concat root relative_path in
+  if not (Sys.file_exists path) then
+    Alcotest.failf "required producer requirement record is missing: %s" path;
+  (path, read_text path)
+
+let compare_version (a1, a2, a3) (b1, b2, b3) =
+  match Int.compare a1 b1 with
+  | 0 ->
+    (match Int.compare a2 b2 with
+     | 0 -> Int.compare a3 b3
+     | order -> order)
+  | order -> order
+
+let version_re =
+  Str.regexp "[vV]?\\([0-9]+\\)\\.\\([0-9]+\\)\\.\\([0-9]+\\)"
+
+let producer_name_re = Str.regexp_case_fold "agent[_-]*sdk"
+
+let token_names_producer token =
+  try
+    ignore (Str.search_forward producer_name_re token 0);
+    true
+  with Not_found -> false
+
+let is_trim_delimiter = function
+  | ' ' | '\t' | '\r' | '\n' | '"' | '\'' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' -> true
+  | _ -> false
+
+let trim_delimiters text =
+  let length = String.length text in
+  let rec first index =
+    if index >= length then index
+    else if is_trim_delimiter text.[index] then first (index + 1)
+    else index
+  in
+  let rec last index =
+    if index < 0 then index
+    else if is_trim_delimiter text.[index] then last (index - 1)
+    else index
+  in
+  let lo = first 0 in
+  let hi = last (length - 1) in
+  if hi < lo then "" else String.sub text lo (hi - lo + 1)
+
+let ends_with text suffix =
+  let text_len = String.length text in
+  let suffix_len = String.length suffix in
+  text_len >= suffix_len
+  && String.equal (String.sub text (text_len - suffix_len) suffix_len) suffix
+
+(** [has_lower_bound_operator prefix] recognises relational or
+    assignment spellings that make the immediately following version a
+    lower bound: [>=], [>], [=], or assignment through [=] or [:]. *)
+let has_lower_bound_operator prefix =
+  let prefix = trim_delimiters prefix in
+  ends_with prefix ">="
+  || (ends_with prefix ">" && not (ends_with prefix "<>"))
+  || (ends_with prefix "="
+      && not (ends_with prefix "<=")
+      && not (ends_with prefix "!=")
+      && not (ends_with prefix ">="))
+  || ends_with prefix ":"
+
+(** [has_assignment_operator prefix] strictly recognises a literal
+    assignment or declaration through [=] or [:] with NO relational
+    operator: the version is pinned rather than merely bounded. *)
+let has_assignment_operator prefix =
+  let prefix = trim_delimiters prefix in
+  (ends_with prefix ":"
+   || ends_with prefix "=")
+  && not (ends_with prefix "<=")
+  && not (ends_with prefix "!=")
+  && not (ends_with prefix ">=")
+  && not (ends_with prefix "<>")
+
+(** [version_contexts record] lists every version occurrence in
+    [record].  Each occurrence is described by the text fragment
+    immediately preceding it ([prefix]).  A version occurrence is
+    evidence independent of layout: the interpretation below only ever
+    reads the operator immediately before the version and any
+    producer-name token inside that same fragment, never a field name
+    or a quoting style.  Because an occurrence's fragment spans
+    physical lines, a wrapped operator or a producer name on a
+    preceding line is still honoured, while a statement terminator --
+    [] or [] closing a previous statement, or a full-line comment that
+    was reduced to whitespace -- clears the fragment so the previous
+    statement cannot stake a claim on this version. *)
+let version_contexts record =
+  let fragment_start pos =
+    (* The fragment is the text since the end of the previous complete
+       statement: a closing bracket, parenthesis, or semicolon clears
+       it so a finished statement cannot stake a claim on this version;
+       opening delimiters continue it.  Line comments were already
+       cleared to whitespace by the caller, so they only separate, they
+       never terminate. *)
+    let rec scan index =
+      if index < 0 then 0
+      else match record.[index] with
+        | ']' | ')' | ';' -> index + 1
+        | _ -> scan (index - 1)
+    in
+    scan (pos - 1)
+  in
+  let rec search offset acc =
+    try
+      let at = Str.search_forward version_re record offset in
+      let version =
+        ( int_of_string (Str.matched_group 1 record)
+        , int_of_string (Str.matched_group 2 record)
+        , int_of_string (Str.matched_group 3 record) )
+      in
+      let ls = fragment_start at in
+      let prefix = String.sub record ls (at - ls) in
+      search (Str.match_end ()) ((prefix, version) :: acc)
+    with Not_found -> List.rev acc
+  in
+  search 0 []
+
+(** [record_stipulates_floor ~same_line_producer record] accepts every
+    semantically effective minimum-version expression of the producer
+    floor.  A version occurrence no older than the floor qualifies
+    through either of two spellings:
+
+    - [has_lower_bound_operator]: a relational or assignment operator
+      immediately precedes the version; or
+    - [has_assignment_operator]: a plain assignment or declaration
+      operator (= or :) pins the version with no relational trappings.
+
+    A version appearing only as bare text -- no relational or
+    assignment operator before it anywhere in its fragment -- never
+    satisfies the requirement, matching the statement that commentary
+    alone cannot express a minimum.
+
+    With [same_line_producer], the version's physical line must also
+    carry a producer-name token, so an unrelated requirement's floor in
+    a multi-dependency manifest cannot impersonate the producer floor.
+    Otherwise the producer name is irrelevant: a record dedicated to
+    the producer (the canonical pin record) need not mention it, and a
+    version left alone by a wrapped assignment (an empty prefix) still
+    expresses the record's pinned version.  Statements may freely span
+    several physical lines. *)
+let record_stipulates_floor ?(same_line_producer = false) record =
+  let comment_free =
+    (* Remove comment text only; statements and identifiers survive,
+       even when they span several physical lines. *)
+    String.split_on_char '\n' record
+    |> List.map (fun row ->
+        match String.index_opt row '#' with
+        | None -> row
+        | Some index -> String.sub row 0 index)
+    |> String.concat "\n"
+  in
+  version_contexts comment_free
+  |> List.exists (fun (prefix, version) ->
+       compare_version version producer_floor >= 0
+       && (has_lower_bound_operator prefix
+           || has_assignment_operator prefix)
+       && (not same_line_producer
+           || token_names_producer prefix))
+
+let test_package_manifest_requires_producer_floor () =
+  let root = locate_project_root () in
+  let path, record = require_record root "masc_mcp.opam" in
+  if record_stipulates_floor ~same_line_producer:true record then ()
+  else
+    Alcotest.failf
+      "the package manifest (%s) must require agent_sdk %s or newer"
+      path (floor_text ())
+
+let test_canonical_pin_requires_producer_floor () =
+  let root = locate_project_root () in
+  let path, record =

+  in
+  if record_stipulates_floor record then ()
+  else
+    Alcotest.failf
+      "the canonical executable producer pin (%s) must enforce release %s or newer"
+      path (floor_text ())
+

problem_statement:
RFC: async_spawn mode for non-blocking subagent execution
## Context
Inspired by Deep Agents `AsyncSubAgentMiddleware` (`middleware/async_subagents.py`).

## Problem
`spawn_eio.ml` spawns subagents synchronously — the calling fiber blocks on `Eio.Process.await`. For long-running tasks, this ties up the caller. Deep Agents solves this with async subagents that return a job ID immediately.

## Proposed Architecture
Add `async_spawn` mode to `spawn_eio.ml`:
1. Spawn agent in background Eio fiber (not blocking the caller)
2. Return `job_id` immediately
3. New MCP tools: `masc_job_status(job_id)`, `masc_job_result(job_id)`, `masc_job_cancel(job_id)`
4. Job state persisted in `.masc/jobs/{job_id}.json`
5. Integrate with existing team_session async patterns

Key difference from Deep Agents: they use remote LangGraph servers. We use local Eio fibers — simpler but same lifecycle.

## Scope
RFC — architectural change. Needs design for:
- Job state persistence format
- Fiber lifecycle management (cancellation, timeout)
- Integration with team_session engine
- Dashboard visibility for running jobs

## Reference
- Deep Agents: `libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/async_subagents.py`
- Existing: `lib/spawn_eio.ml`, `lib/team_session_engine_eio.ml`

### Additional contract requirements

Async agent spawning is exposed through the public MCP tool-call surface.
A client submits background work with `masc_async_spawn`.  Its arguments are
`agent_name`, a string naming the local worker command, and `prompt`, the
required string task prompt.  A missing, empty, or non-string `prompt` is
rejected without registering work.  A valid submission is acknowledged
within ten seconds in the local MCP server execution environment; this is an
acknowledgement bound, not a worker-completion bound.

Successful responses from `masc_async_spawn`, `masc_job_status`, and
`masc_job_list` are JSON objects.  A successful submission has a nonempty
string `job_id`.  `masc_job_status` accepts that value in its string `job_id`
argument and returns that same value in `job_id`, together with a string
`status` equal to `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.  A
`completed` status includes boolean `success`.  `masc_job_list` returns a
`jobs` array whose job objects each have a nonempty string `job_id`.
Identifiers are otherwise opaque strings; no identifier spelling is implied.
The representation of errors, including an unknown job identifier, is not
specified.

A submitted job is observable in `masc_job_list` within fifteen seconds of
acknowledgement.  Status observation remains available while the job runs and
after its terminal outcome.  A worker command that does not exist reaches an
observable terminal failure within thirty seconds of acknowledgement: its
status is either `failed`, or `completed` with `success` false.  The
POSIX-controlled command `sh -c true` reaches `completed` with `success` true
within thirty seconds.  These thirty-second bounds apply only to those two
controlled worker cases in the local MCP server execution environment, not to
arbitrary worker commands.

Implementations may choose their storage, scheduling, retention, and internal
module design, provided the public tool behavior above is preserved.

diff --git a/lib/async_spawn.ml b/lib/async_spawn.ml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..e630a352206
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/async_spawn.ml
@@ -0,0 +1,162 @@
+(** Async_spawn — non-blocking agent execution with job tracking.
+
+    Wraps Spawn_eio.spawn in an Eio fiber so the caller gets a job_id
+    immediately and can poll for completion later. Inspired by Deep Agents
+    AsyncSubAgentMiddleware.
+
+    The registry is protected by Eio.Mutex (not Stdlib.Mutex) to avoid
+    EDEADLK under Eio cooperative scheduling.
+
+    @since 2.112.0 *)
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Types                                                            *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+type job_status =
+  | Running
+  | Completed of Spawn_eio.spawn_result
+  | Failed of string
+  | Cancelled
+
+type job = {
+  job_id : string;
+  agent_name : string;
+  prompt_preview : string;
+  started_at : float;
+  mutable status : job_status;
+  mutable finished_at : float option;
+}
+
+type registry = {
+  jobs : (string, job) Hashtbl.t;
+  mu : Eio.Mutex.t;
+}
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Registry lifecycle                                               *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+let create_registry () : registry =
+  { jobs = Hashtbl.create 16; mu = Eio.Mutex.create () }
+
+(** Generate a short unique job id: "job-<8-hex-chars>" *)
+let generate_job_id () =
+  let uuid = Uuidm.v4_gen (Random.State.make_self_init ()) () in
+  let hex = Uuidm.to_string uuid |> String.split_on_char '-' |> String.concat "" in
+  Printf.sprintf "job-%s" (String.sub hex 0 8)
+
+(** Truncate prompt to first [n] characters for preview. *)
+let truncate_prompt ?(n = 100) prompt =
+  if String.length prompt <= n then prompt
+  else String.sub prompt 0 n ^ "..."
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Core operations                                                  *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+(** Submit a job that runs [run_fn] in a background Eio fiber.
+
+    [run_fn] is the function that performs the actual work (typically
+    [Spawn_eio.spawn] partially applied with all spawn arguments).
+    This indirection enables mock injection in tests.
+
+    Returns the job record immediately. The fiber updates [job.status]
+    and [job.finished_at] when it completes, fails, or is cancelled. *)
+let submit_job (reg : registry) ~sw ~agent_name ~prompt
+    (run_fn : unit -> Spawn_eio.spawn_result) : job =
+  let job_id = generate_job_id () in
+  let job = {
+    job_id;
+    agent_name;
+    prompt_preview = truncate_prompt prompt;
+    started_at = Time_compat.now ();
+    status = Running;
+    finished_at = None;
+  } in
+  Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:true reg.mu (fun () ->
+    Hashtbl.replace reg.jobs job_id job);
+  (* Fork a fiber that runs the spawn function and records the result. *)
+  Eio.Fiber.fork ~sw (fun () ->
+    let finish status =
+      Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:true reg.mu (fun () ->
+        job.status <- status;
+        job.finished_at <- Some (Time_compat.now ()))
+    in
+    match run_fn () with
+    | result -> finish (Completed result)
+    | exception exn ->
+        let msg = Printexc.to_string exn in
+        finish (Failed msg));
+  job
+
+let get_job (reg : registry) job_id : job option =
+  Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:false reg.mu (fun () ->
+    Hashtbl.find_opt reg.jobs job_id)
+
+let cancel_job (reg : registry) job_id : bool =
+  Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:true reg.mu (fun () ->
+    match Hashtbl.find_opt reg.jobs job_id with
+    | Some job when (match job.status with Running -> true | _ -> false) ->
+        job.status <- Cancelled;
+        job.finished_at <- Some (Time_compat.now ());
+        true
+    | _ -> false)
+
+let list_jobs (reg : registry) : job list =
+  Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:false reg.mu (fun () ->
+    Hashtbl.fold (fun _k v acc -> v :: acc) reg.jobs [])
+
+(** Remove completed/failed/cancelled jobs older than [max_age_s] seconds.
+    Returns the number of removed entries. *)
+let cleanup_completed (reg : registry) ~max_age_s : int =
+  let now = Time_compat.now () in
+  Eio.Mutex.use_rw ~protect:true reg.mu (fun () ->
+    let to_remove = Hashtbl.fold (fun k (j : job) acc ->
+      match j.status with
+      | Running -> acc
+      | _ ->
+          let age = match j.finished_at with
+            | Some t -> now -. t
+            | None -> now -. j.started_at
+          in
+          if age > max_age_s then k :: acc else acc
+    ) reg.jobs [] in
+    List.iter (Hashtbl.remove reg.jobs) to_remove;
+    List.length to_remove)
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* JSON serialization helpers                                       *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+let status_to_string = function
+  | Running -> "running"
+  | Completed _ -> "completed"
+  | Failed _ -> "failed"
+  | Cancelled -> "cancelled"
+
+let job_to_json (j : job) : Yojson.Safe.t =
+  let base = [
+    ("job_id", `String j.job_id);
+    ("agent_name", `String j.agent_name);
+    ("prompt_preview", `String j.prompt_preview);
+    ("started_at", `Float j.started_at);
+    ("status", `String (status_to_string j.status));
+  ] in
+  let with_finished = match j.finished_at with
+    | Some t -> base @ [("finished_at", `Float t)]
+    | None -> base
+  in
+  let with_result = match j.status with
+    | Completed r ->
+        with_finished @ [
+          ("success", `Bool r.success);
+          ("exit_code", `Int r.exit_code);
+          ("elapsed_ms", `Int r.elapsed_ms);
+          ("output_preview", `String (truncate_prompt ~n:500 r.output));
+        ]
+    | Failed msg ->
+        with_finished @ [("error", `String msg)]
+    | _ -> with_finished
+  in
+  `Assoc with_result

+(** Async_spawn — non-blocking agent execution with job tracking.
+

+    immediately and can poll/cancel later.
+
+    @since 2.112.0 *)
+
+(** Job lifecycle status. *)
+type job_status =
+  | Running
+  | Completed of Spawn_eio.spawn_result

+  | Cancelled
+
+(** Immutable identification + mutable status for a background job. *)
+type job = {
+  job_id : string;
+  agent_name : string;
+  prompt_preview : string;
+  started_at : float;
+  mutable status : job_status;
+  mutable finished_at : float option;
+}

+type registry
+
+val create_registry : unit -> registry

+    Returns the job record immediately with status [Running]. *)
+val submit_job :
+  registry ->
+  sw:Eio.Switch.t ->
+  agent_name:string ->
+  prompt:string ->
+  (unit -> Spawn_eio.spawn_result) ->
+  job
+
+val get_job : registry -> string -> job option
+val cancel_job : registry -> string -> bool
+val list_jobs : registry -> job list
+
+(** Remove finished jobs older than [max_age_s]. Returns count removed. *)
+val cleanup_completed : registry -> max_age_s:float -> int
+
+(** Serialize status variant to string. *)
+val status_to_string : job_status -> string
+
+(** Serialize a job record to JSON. *)
+val job_to_json : job -> Yojson.Safe.t

diff --git a/lib/tool_async_spawn.ml b/lib/tool_async_spawn.ml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..db78010971d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/tool_async_spawn.ml
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+(** Tool_async_spawn — MCP tool schemas and dispatch for async agent spawning.
+
+    Provides 3 MCP tools:
+    - masc_async_spawn  — Start a background agent, return job_id immediately
+    - masc_job_status   — Query a job by id
+    - masc_job_list     — List all tracked jobs
+
+    @since 2.112.0 *)
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Global registry — single instance per server process             *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+let global_registry = Async_spawn.create_registry ()
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Tool Schemas                                                     *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+let schemas : Types.tool_schema list = [
+  {
+    name = "masc_async_spawn";
+    description = "Start an agent in the background and return a job_id immediately. \
+The agent runs as an Eio fiber; use masc_job_status to poll for completion. \
+Accepts the same agent_name and prompt as masc_spawn but does not block.";
+    input_schema = `Assoc [
+      ("type", `String "object");
+      ("properties", `Assoc [
+        ("agent_name", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "string");
+          ("description", `String "Agent CLI to run (claude, gemini, codex, llama, glm)");
+        ]);
+        ("prompt", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "string");
+          ("description", `String "Task prompt for the agent");
+        ]);
+        ("timeout_seconds", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "integer");
+          ("description", `String "Max execution time in seconds (default: from config)");
+        ]);
+        ("working_dir", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "string");
+          ("description", `String "Working directory for the agent (optional)");
+        ]);
+      ]);
+      ("required", `List [`String "agent_name"; `String "prompt"]);
+    ];
+  };
+
+  {
+    name = "masc_job_status";
+    description = "Get the current status of an async job by its job_id. \
+Returns running/completed/failed/cancelled with details.";
+    input_schema = `Assoc [
+      ("type", `String "object");
+      ("properties", `Assoc [
+        ("job_id", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "string");
+          ("description", `String "Job ID returned by masc_async_spawn");
+        ]);
+      ]);
+      ("required", `List [`String "job_id"]);
+    ];
+  };
+
+  {
+    name = "masc_job_list";
+    description = "List all tracked async jobs with their current status. \
+Optionally filter by status and clean up old completed jobs.";
+    input_schema = `Assoc [
+      ("type", `String "object");
+      ("properties", `Assoc [
+        ("status_filter", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "string");
+          ("description", `String "Filter by status: running, completed, failed, cancelled (optional, shows all if omitted)");
+        ]);
+        ("cleanup_age_seconds", `Assoc [
+          ("type", `String "number");
+          ("description", `String "Remove completed/failed/cancelled jobs older than this many seconds (optional)");
+        ]);
+      ]);
+    ];
+  };
+]
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Context                                                          *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+type context = {
+  config : Room_utils.config;
+  agent_name : string;
+  sw : Eio.Switch.t;
+  proc_mgr : Eio_unix.Process.mgr_ty Eio.Resource.t option;
+}
+
+(* ================================================================ *)
+(* Handlers                                                         *)
+(* ================================================================ *)
+
+let handle_async_spawn (ctx : context) args : bool * string =
+  let agent_target = Safe_ops.json_string ~default:"claude" "agent_name" args in
+  let prompt = Safe_ops.json_string ~default:"" "prompt" args in
+  if prompt = "" then
+    (false, "prompt is required")
+  else
+    match ctx.proc_mgr with
+    | None ->
+        (false, "proc_mgr unavailable (server not in Eio mode)")
+    | Some proc_mgr ->
+        let timeout_seconds = Safe_ops.json_int_opt "timeout_seconds" args in
+        let working_dir = Safe_ops.json_string_opt "working_dir" args in
+        let room_config = Some ctx.config in
+        let run_fn () =
+          Spawn_eio.spawn
+            ~sw:ctx.sw
+            ~proc_mgr
+            ~agent_name:agent_target
+            ~prompt
+            ?timeout_seconds
+            ?working_dir
+            ?room_config
+            ()
+        in
+        let job = Async_spawn.submit_job global_registry
+            ~sw:ctx.sw ~agent_name:agent_target ~prompt run_fn in
+        let response = `Assoc [
+          ("job_id", `String job.job_id);
+          ("agent_name", `String job.agent_name);
+          ("status", `String "running");
+          ("prompt_preview", `String job.prompt_preview);
+          ("started_at", `Float job.started_at);
+        ] in
+        (true, Yojson.Safe.to_string response)
+
+let handle_job_status _ctx args : bool * string =
+  let job_id = Safe_ops.json_string ~default:"" "job_id" args in
+  if job_id = "" then
+    (false, "job_id is required")
+  else
+    match Async_spawn.get_job global_registry job_id with
+    | None ->
+        (false, Printf.sprintf "Job not found: %s" job_id)
+    | Some job ->
+        (true, Yojson.Safe.to_string (Async_spawn.job_to_json job))
+
+let handle_job_list _ctx args : bool * string =
+  (* Optional cleanup *)
+  let cleanup_age = Safe_ops.json_float_opt "cleanup_age_seconds" args in
+  let cleaned = match cleanup_age with
+    | Some age when age > 0.0 ->
+        Async_spawn.cleanup_completed global_registry ~max_age_s:age
+    | _ -> 0
+  in
+  let status_filter = Safe_ops.json_string_opt "status_filter" args in
+  let all_jobs = Async_spawn.list_jobs global_registry in
+  let filtered = match status_filter with
+    | None -> all_jobs
+    | Some f ->
+        List.filter (fun (j : Async_spawn.job) ->
+          Async_spawn.status_to_string j.status = f
+        ) all_jobs
+  in
+  (* Sort by started_at descending *)
+  let sorted = List.sort (fun (a : Async_spawn.job) (b : Async_spawn.job) ->
+    compare b.started_at a.started_at
+  ) filtered in

@@ -0,0 +1,330 @@
+(** Black-box public-contract tests for asynchronous agent spawning.
+
+    The tests invoke only the normal MCP dispatcher.  The addendum defines
+    the JSON response fields used below; no internal registry, storage,
+    scheduler, identifier syntax, or error wording is assumed. *)
+
+module Mcp_eio = Masc_mcp.Mcp_server_eio
+
+type outcome = {
+  is_error : bool;
+  text : string;
+}
+
+type job_status = {
+  job_id : string;
+  lifecycle : string;
+  success : bool option;
+}
+
+let () = Random.self_init ()
+
+let temp_dir () =
+  let dir = Filename.temp_file "test_async_spawn_" "" in
+  Unix.unlink dir;
+  Unix.mkdir dir 0o755;
+  dir
+
+let cleanup_dir dir =
+  let rec rm path =
+    if Sys.is_directory path then begin
+      Array.iter (fun name -> rm (Filename.concat path name)) (Sys.readdir path);
+      Unix.rmdir path
+    end else
+      Unix.unlink path
+  in
+  try rm dir with _ -> ()
+
+let unavailable_worker () =
+  Printf.sprintf "async-spawn-fixture-%d-%d"
+    (Unix.getpid ()) (Random.int 1_000_000_000)
+
+let make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state =
+  fun name arguments ->
+    let success, text =
+      Mcp_eio.execute_tool_eio ~sw ~clock state ~name ~arguments
+    in
+    { is_error = not success; text }
+
+let with_server_state f =
+  Eio_main.run @@ fun env ->
+  let clock = Eio.Stdenv.clock env in
+  Eio.Switch.run @@ fun sw ->
+  let base_path = temp_dir () in
+  Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> cleanup_dir base_path) (fun () ->
+    let state =
+      Masc_mcp.Server_runtime_bootstrap.create_server_state ~sw ~base_path
+        ~clock ~mono_clock:(Eio.Stdenv.mono_clock env) ~net:(Eio.Stdenv.net env)
+        ~proc_mgr:(Eio.Stdenv.process_mgr env) ~fs:(Eio.Stdenv.fs env)
+    in
+    f ~sw ~clock state)
+
+let spawn_args ?(agent_name = unavailable_worker ()) prompt =
+  `Assoc [
+    ("agent_name", `String agent_name);
+    ("prompt", `String prompt);
+  ]
+
+let json_of_response label response =
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    (Printf.sprintf "%s succeeds (response: %s)" label response.text)
+    false response.is_error;
+  try Yojson.Safe.from_string response.text with
+  | Yojson.Json_error _ ->
+      Alcotest.failf "%s returns the contractual JSON object (response: %s)"
+        label response.text
+
+let object_fields label = function
+  | `Assoc fields -> fields
+  | json ->
+      Alcotest.failf "%s is a JSON object (response: %s)" label
+        (Yojson.Safe.to_string json)
+
+let required_string label field fields =
+  match List.assoc_opt field fields with
+  | Some (`String value) when String.length value > 0 -> value
+  | _ -> Alcotest.failf "%s has nonempty string field %S" label field
+
+let submitted_job_id response =
+  json_of_response "masc_async_spawn" response
+  |> object_fields "masc_async_spawn response"
+  |> required_string "masc_async_spawn response" "job_id"
+
+let status_of response =
+  let fields =
+    json_of_response "masc_job_status" response
+    |> object_fields "masc_job_status response"
+  in
+  let job_id = required_string "masc_job_status response" "job_id" fields in
+  let lifecycle = required_string "masc_job_status response" "status" fields in
+  let success =
+    if lifecycle = "completed" then
+      match List.assoc_opt "success" fields with
+      | Some (`Bool value) -> Some value
+      | _ -> Alcotest.fail "completed status includes a boolean success field"
+    else None
+  in
+  { job_id; lifecycle; success }
+
+let listed_job_ids response =
+  let fields =
+    json_of_response "masc_job_list" response
+    |> object_fields "masc_job_list response"
+  in
+  match List.assoc_opt "jobs" fields with
+  | Some (`List jobs) ->
+      List.map
+        (fun job ->
+          job |> object_fields "masc_job_list job"
+              |> required_string "masc_job_list job" "job_id")
+        jobs
+  | _ -> Alcotest.fail "masc_job_list response has a jobs array"
+
+let valid_lifecycle = function
+  | "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" -> true
+  | _ -> false
+
+let poll_within ~clock seconds f =
+  try
+    Eio.Time.with_timeout_exn clock seconds (fun () ->
+      let rec loop () =
+        if f () then true
+        else begin
+          Eio.Time.sleep clock 0.1;
+          loop ()
+        end
+      in
+      loop ())
+  with Eio.Time.Timeout -> false
+
+let status_call call_tool job_id =
+  call_tool "masc_job_status" (`Assoc [ ("job_id", `String job_id) ])
+
+let test_public_tools_are_routable () =
+  with_server_state (fun ~sw ~clock state ->
+    let call_tool = make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state in
+    let bogus = call_tool "masc_async_spawn_no_such_tool" (`Assoc []) in
+    Alcotest.(check bool) "undefined tool does not succeed" true bogus.is_error;
+
+    (* The controlled worker starts immediately because it does not depend on
+       a configured agent, so the acknowledgement elapsed time is measured
+       against the wall clock rather than the dispatcher's scheduler. *)
+    let started_at = Unix.gettimeofday () in
+    let submission =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn"
+        (spawn_args ~agent_name:"sh -c true" "routing check")
+    in
+    let elapsed = Unix.gettimeofday () -. started_at in
+    let job_id = submitted_job_id submission in
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      (Printf.sprintf
+         "valid submission of a controlled immediate worker is acknowledged \
+          within the contractual ten-second bound (elapsed %.2f s)"
+         elapsed)
+      true (elapsed <= 10.0);
+
+    let status = status_of (status_call call_tool job_id) in
+    Alcotest.(check string) "status identifies submitted job" job_id status.job_id;
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      "initial status is a documented lifecycle value"
+      true (valid_lifecycle status.lifecycle);
+
+    (* Unknown-job failures deliberately have no required representation. *)
+    ignore (listed_job_ids (call_tool "masc_job_list" (`Assoc []))))
+
+let test_failed_worker_lifecycle_and_listing () =
+  with_server_state (fun ~sw ~clock state ->
+    let call_tool = make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state in
+    let submission =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn" (spawn_args "unavailable worker lifecycle")
+    in
+    let job_id = submitted_job_id submission in
+
+    let visible =
+      poll_within ~clock 15.0 (fun () ->
+        List.mem job_id (listed_job_ids (call_tool "masc_job_list" (`Assoc []))))
+    in
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      "submitted job is listed within the contractual visibility window" true visible;
+
+    let last_status = ref "no status response" in
+    let terminal_failure =
+      poll_within ~clock 30.0 (fun () ->
+        let response = status_call call_tool job_id in
+        last_status := response.text;
+        let status = status_of response in
+        Alcotest.(check string) "polled status identifies submitted job"
+          job_id status.job_id;
+        Alcotest.(check bool) "polled status is a documented lifecycle value"
+          true (valid_lifecycle status.lifecycle);
+        status.lifecycle = "failed"
+        || (status.lifecycle = "completed" && status.success = Some false))
+    in
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      (Printf.sprintf "unavailable worker reaches terminal failure within 30 seconds (last response: %s)" !last_status)
+      true terminal_failure)
+
+let test_successful_worker_completion () =
+  with_server_state (fun ~sw ~clock state ->
+    let call_tool = make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state in
+    (* A POSIX shell is evaluator-provided test infrastructure.  This command
+       terminates successfully without depending on a configured agent. *)
+    let submission =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn"
+        (spawn_args ~agent_name:"sh -c true" "successful worker lifecycle")
+    in
+    let job_id = submitted_job_id submission in
+    let last_status = ref "no status response" in
+    let completed_successfully =
+      poll_within ~clock 30.0 (fun () ->
+        let response = status_call call_tool job_id in
+        last_status := response.text;
+        let status = status_of response in
+        status.job_id = job_id
+        && status.lifecycle = "completed"
+        && status.success = Some true)
+    in
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      (Printf.sprintf "controlled worker completes successfully within 30 seconds (last response: %s)" !last_status)
+      true completed_successfully)
+
+let test_submission_validates_prompt () =
+  with_server_state (fun ~sw ~clock state ->
+    let call_tool = make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state in
+    let jobs_before = List.sort String.compare
+        (listed_job_ids (call_tool "masc_job_list" (`Assoc []))) in
+    let missing =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn"
+        (`Assoc [ ("agent_name", `String (unavailable_worker ())) ])
+    in
+    Alcotest.(check bool) "missing prompt is rejected" true missing.is_error;
+
+    let empty = call_tool "masc_async_spawn" (spawn_args "") in
+    Alcotest.(check bool) "empty prompt is rejected" true empty.is_error;
+
+    let non_string =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn"
+        (`Assoc [ ("agent_name", `String (unavailable_worker ()));
+                  ("prompt", `Int 42) ])
+    in
+    Alcotest.(check bool) "non-string prompt is rejected" true non_string.is_error;
+
+    let jobs_after = List.sort String.compare
+        (listed_job_ids (call_tool "masc_job_list" (`Assoc []))) in
+    Alcotest.(check (list string))
+      "rejected prompts do not register jobs" jobs_before jobs_after)
+
+let test_status_success_field_by_lifecycle () =
+  let response status success_field =
+    let fields = [ ("job_id", `String "opaque-id"); ("status", `String status) ] in
+    let fields = match success_field with
+      | None -> fields
+      | Some value -> fields @ [ ("success", value) ]
+    in
+    { is_error = false; text = Yojson.Safe.to_string (`Assoc fields) }
+  in
+  let accepted status success_field expected =
+    let parsed = status_of (response status success_field) in
+    Alcotest.(check (option bool))
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s success representation is treated according to lifecycle" status)
+      expected parsed.success
+  in
+  accepted "running" None None;
+  accepted "running" (Some `Null) None;
+  accepted "running" (Some (`String "unknown")) None;
+  accepted "running" (Some (`Assoc [ ("future", `Bool true) ])) None;
+  accepted "failed" (Some `Null) None;
+  accepted "cancelled" (Some (`List [ `Int 1 ])) None;
+  accepted "completed" (Some (`Bool true)) (Some true);
+  accepted "completed" (Some (`Bool false)) (Some false);
+  let rejected success_field =
+    try
+      ignore (status_of (response "completed" success_field));
+      false
+    with _ -> true
+  in
+  List.iter
+    (fun (label, success_field) ->
+      Alcotest.(check bool)
+        ("completed status rejects " ^ label) true (rejected success_field))
+    [ "missing", None; "null", Some `Null; "string", Some (`String "true");
+      "number", Some (`Int 1); "array", Some (`List []);
+      "object", Some (`Assoc []) ]
+
+let test_long_worker_acknowledgement_and_running_status () =
+  with_server_state (fun ~sw ~clock state ->
+    let call_tool = make_call_tool ~clock ~sw ~state in
+    let started_at = Unix.gettimeofday () in
+    let submission =
+      call_tool "masc_async_spawn"
+        (spawn_args ~agent_name:"sleep 20" "check active worker")
+    in
+    let elapsed = Unix.gettimeofday () -. started_at in
+    let job_id = submitted_job_id submission in
+    Alcotest.(check bool)
+      (Printf.sprintf "long-running work is acknowledged within ten seconds (elapsed %.2f s)" elapsed)
+      true (elapsed <= 10.0);
+    let status = status_of (status_call call_tool job_id) in
+    Alcotest.(check string) "active worker status identifies submitted job" job_id status.job_id;
+    Alcotest.(check string) "status is available while controlled worker remains active"
+      "running" status.lifecycle)
+
+let () =
+  Alcotest.run "async_spawn" [
+    "public tool surface", [
+      Alcotest.test_case "async tools are routable" `Quick
+        test_public_tools_are_routable;
+    ];
+    "invocation", [
+      Alcotest.test_case "unavailable worker has observable terminal failure" `Slow
+        test_failed_worker_lifecycle_and_listing;
+      Alcotest.test_case "controlled worker completes with success" `Slow
+        test_successful_worker_completion;
+      Alcotest.test_case "submission requires a nonempty string prompt" `Quick
+        test_submission_validates_prompt;
+      Alcotest.test_case "status success field follows lifecycle" `Quick
+        test_status_success_field_by_lifecycle;
+      Alcotest.test_case "long worker is acknowledged and queryable while running" `Slow
+        test_long_worker_acknowledgement_and_running_status;
+    ];
+  ]

problem_statement:
Docker route fake-runner regression in keeper sandbox tests
Symptom:
- Current main Docker route regression test executable reports multiple failures in test_keeper_sandbox_docker_route.exe.
- Failures include generic typed Execute and typed push mounting repo CLI identity bundles when tests expect they should not, git -C/cwd expectation mismatches, git push unexpectedly succeeding without the expected write gate, rg no-match semantic success returning None, host-path rewrite fake Docker response returning None, and typed env wrapper validation not surfacing the expected validation error.

Reproduction:
- Repo: /Users/dancer/me/workspace/yousleepwhen/masc-mcp
- Commit under local checkout at check time: a7296801a7 on main...origin/main
- Command attempted: env -u MASC_BASE_PATH _build/default/test/test_keeper_sandbox_docker_route.exe
- The run was stopped after it hung waiting on Docker daemon availability, but Alcotest output files already contained the failures under _build/_tests/604H7CAP.
- Failure scan command: rg -n "^FAIL|FAIL |Expected:|Received:" _build/_tests/604H7CAP/*.output

Observed failing assertions:
- docker_route_fires.003: generic typed Execute does not mount repo CLI identity bundle, expected false received true.
- docker_route_fires.005: typed cwd error, expected true received false.
- docker_route_fires.006: git -C bare .worktrees succeeds, expected Some true received None.
- docker_route_fires.007: git push unexpectedly succeeded with ok=true via docker.
- docker_route_fires.008: generic typed push does not mount repo CLI identity bundle, expected false received true.
- docker_route_fires.012: rg no-match succeeds semantically, expected Some true received None.
- docker_route_fires.016: bash via fake docker is ok, expected Some true received None.
- docker_route_contract.004: validation error surfaced, expected true received false.

Estimated cause:
- Likely drift in typed Execute Docker dispatch, credential bundle mounting, or test fixture expectations around git command classification and fake Docker response parsing.
- Needs a focused source-level pass before treating the Docker route as green.

Tried:
- Verified OAS pin with scripts/check-oas-pin.sh --local-only.
- Tried focused Dune build of Docker/Playground targets in a dedicated DUNE_BUILD_DIR, but the machine was at 100 percent disk capacity and Dune failed with No space left on device.
- Ran already-built focused test executables for Local Playground and Docker route surfaces.
- Confirmed Local Playground path tests pass independently.
- Confirmed Docker daemon live smoke is currently blocked locally because docker info, docker ps, and image inspect time out against the server.

### Additional contract requirements

The affected contract is the observable keeper Docker-route sandbox behavior exercised through the existing typed tool and command-semantics interfaces. No new production interface is required.

For a typed Execute request and a typed git-push request that use the Docker route, the route must not mount a repository CLI identity bundle merely because the request is typed. A git push remains subject to the existing write permission gate before Docker execution; a request without that permission must not succeed through the Docker route.

Typed command validation is performed before dispatch. In particular, an invalid typed environment-wrapper target and an invalid typed working-directory request must return the established validation error rather than reaching Docker. A ripgrep command with no matches is a semantically successful no-result outcome, and a successful fake-Docker response (including one containing a rewritten sandbox host path) must be interpreted as a successful execution result.

Git working-directory handling is evaluated for commands issued from the sandbox playground root. A leading `git -C <path>` names a directory to validate before execution. Existing paths below the playground may be expressed either relative to that root or using the corresponding container playground path, since that mount is shared between host and container. The selected execution directory remains the sandbox playground root for this explicit form. A missing target is rejected with the established user-facing `git -C` directory error while retaining that root as the reported execution directory. Consecutive leading `-C` options are resolved in order, with each target relative to the previous target; a missing later target is rejected in the same way. A `-C` that occurs after the git subcommand is a subcommand argument, not a working-directory directive. In a sandbox containing exactly one repository, ordinary git commands, including such a subcommand argument, select that repository. Implicitly selected directories are normalized absolute paths.

The approval-count and trajectory serialization cases included in the test patch are pass-only registrations of already available test-suite behavior. They are retained as non-regression smoke checks and do not add approval metadata, runtime-contract projection, or other new keeper interface requirements. The fail-to-pass requirements of this task are confined to the Docker-route behavior above.

problem_statement:
Goal/task lifecycle allows unscoped done tasks and stale executing goals
Live symptom
- `masc_status` reports active tasks=0 while Goal Store still has 28 executing goals after operator-blocking three stale goals.
- `/Users/dancer/me/.masc/tasks/backlog.json` has 491 done tasks and 135 cancelled tasks, but 0 tasks with non-empty `goal_id`.
- Recent completed work is therefore invisible from goal rollups; dashboard shows goals with task count 0 even when related task records exist.

Evidence checked 2026-06-13 01:03 KST
- `jq -r "[.tasks[] | select((.goal_id // "") != "")] | length" /Users/dancer/me/.masc/tasks/backlog.json` => 0
- `jq "{executing:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="executing")]|length), blocked:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="blocked")]|length), awaiting_approval:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="awaiting_approval")]|length)}" /Users/dancer/me/.masc/goals.json` => executing=28, blocked=3, awaiting_approval=0
- Recent done tasks carry free-form `notes` evidence, not structured result/evidence refs. Examples: task-897 PR #20961, task-900 PR #20965, task-902 PR #20970, task-898 force done due offline assignee.

Why this is bad
- A goal can remain `executing` indefinitely with no active linked task, no owner, and no PR path.
- Agents can mark tasks `done` with text notes while the goal tree still sees no task evidence.
- This creates a false empty backlog and stale active goals consuming keeper attention/fibers.

Suggested fix
- Require `goal_id` for task creation when more than one active goal exists, or force explicit unscoped rationale.
- Disallow completing a task as `done` unless structured completion evidence satisfies the contract, not just free-form notes.
- Add a janitor/ratchet: executing goal with zero active/linked tasks beyond threshold moves to blocked or needs operator-visible rationale.
- Dashboard should surface unscoped done tasks separately so they cannot masquerade as goal progress.

### Additional contract requirements

# Public contract: goal-scoped task creation

## Task creation with a goal scope

When a task is created through the workspace task store with an explicit
goal identifier:

- The task creation succeeds and reports the created task identifier in
  its result, consistent with existing unscoped task creation.
- The goal-to-task association (which goal the created task belongs to)
  must be recorded durably inside the workspace storage, so that it can be
  recovered from the persisted workspace state alone, without access to
  the creating process's memory.
- The stored association uses the JSON field names `goal_id` for the goal
  identifier. Task identifiers are recorded either individually under the
  field name `task_id` or collectively under the field name `task_ids`
  (an array of task identifier strings). Beyond those field names, the
  storage layout is not prescribed: the association may live in any JSON
  document (or append-only sequence of JSON documents) stored under the
  workspace directory tree, in one file or several.
- Creating a new goal-scoped task must preserve goal-to-task associations
  that were recorded earlier: a new association adds to the stored set and
  must not drop, truncate, or overwrite associations for other goals or

problem_statement_base:
Goal/task lifecycle allows unscoped done tasks and stale executing goals
Live symptom
- `masc_status` reports active tasks=0 while Goal Store still has 28 executing goals after operator-blocking three stale goals.
- `/Users/dancer/me/.masc/tasks/backlog.json` has 491 done tasks and 135 cancelled tasks, but 0 tasks with non-empty `goal_id`.
- Recent completed work is therefore invisible from goal rollups; dashboard shows goals with task count 0 even when related task records exist.

Evidence checked 2026-06-13 01:03 KST
- `jq -r "[.tasks[] | select((.goal_id // "") != "")] | length" /Users/dancer/me/.masc/tasks/backlog.json` => 0
- `jq "{executing:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="executing")]|length), blocked:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="blocked")]|length), awaiting_approval:([.goals[]|select(.phase=="awaiting_approval")]|length)}" /Users/dancer/me/.masc/goals.json` => executing=28, blocked=3, awaiting_approval=0
- Recent done tasks carry free-form `notes` evidence, not structured result/evidence refs. Examples: task-897 PR #20961, task-900 PR #20965, task-902 PR #20970, task-898 force done due offline assignee.

Why this is bad
- A goal can remain `executing` indefinitely with no active linked task, no owner, and no PR path.
- Agents can mark tasks `done` with text notes while the goal tree still sees no task evidence.
- This creates a false empty backlog and stale active goals consuming keeper attention/fibers.

Suggested fix
- Require `goal_id` for task creation when more than one active goal exists, or force explicit unscoped rationale.
- Disallow completing a task as `done` unless structured completion evidence satisfies the contract, not just free-form notes.
- Add a janitor/ratchet: executing goal with zero active/linked tasks beyond threshold moves to blocked or needs operator-visible rationale.
- Dashboard should surface unscoped done tasks separately so they cannot masquerade as goal progress.
contract_addendum:
# Public contract: goal-scoped task creation

## Task creation with a goal scope

When a task is created through the workspace task store with an explicit
goal identifier:

- The task creation succeeds and reports the created task identifier in
  its result, consistent with existing unscoped task creation.
- The goal-to-task association (which goal the created task belongs to)
  must be recorded durably inside the workspace storage, so that it can be
  recovered from the persisted workspace state alone, without access to
  the creating process's memory.
- The stored association uses the JSON field names `goal_id` for the goal
  identifier. Task identifiers are recorded either individually under the
  field name `task_id` or collectively under the field name `task_ids`
  (an array of task identifier strings). Beyond those field names, the
  storage layout is not prescribed: the association may live in any JSON
  document (or append-only sequence of JSON documents) stored under the
  workspace directory tree, in one file or several.
- Creating a new goal-scoped task must preserve goal-to-task associations
  that were recorded earlier: a new association adds to the stored set and
  must not drop, truncate, or overwrite associations for other goals or
  for other tasks of the same goal.
- A task created with no goal identifier must not gain any goal-to-task
  association.

## Goal rollup visibility

- A goal rollup rebuilt from the persisted workspace state (for example
  after a process restart) must count and list every task whose goal-to
  task association is stored for that goal. In particular, a goal that has
  a stored linked task must never report a task count of 0 for that task.
- The rollup derived from the stored associations is scoped per goal:
  tasks associated with one goal are surfaced only under that goal's
  rollup, and each goal's rollup reflects only its own linked tasks.
- The in-memory goal-task index helpers may build their rollups from
  explicitly supplied goal-to-task associations; the requirement above is
  that the associations needed for a correct rollup are recoverable from
  the persisted workspace state.

+    let goal_id =
+      match List.assoc_opt "goal_id" fields with
+      | Some (`String value) -> String.trim value
+      | _ -> ""
+    in
+    let task_ids =
+      match List.assoc_opt "task_ids" fields with
+      | Some (`List values) ->
+        List.filter_map
+          (function
+            | `String value ->
+              let value = String.trim value in
+              if String.equal value "" then None else Some value
+            | _ -> None)
+          values

+    After the task<->goal boundary refactor, goal-task links are no longer
+    stored on task records.  The index is built from explicit
+    [goal_task_links] mappings.  The "persisted goal-task link" section
+    exercises the observable lifecycle contract through [Workspace.add_task]:
+    a task created with a goal scope must be recoverable as linked to that

 open Masc_domain
+open Masc
+
+(* ── temp workspace helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────── *)
+
+let temp_counter = ref 0
+
+let temp_dir () =
+  incr temp_counter;
+  let dir =

+      (Filename.get_temp_dir_name ())
+      (Printf.sprintf
+         "masc_goal_index_%d_%d_%d"
+         (Unix.getpid ())
+         (int_of_float (Unix.gettimeofday () *. 1_000_000.))
+         !temp_counter)
+  in
+  Unix.mkdir dir 0o755;
+  dir
+;;
+
+let rec rm_rf path =
+  if Sys.file_exists path
+  then
+    if Sys.is_directory path
+    then (
+      Sys.readdir path |> Array.iter (fun name -> rm_rf (Filename.concat path name));
+      Unix.rmdir path)

+  Eio_main.run
+  @@ fun env ->
+  Fs_compat.set_fs (Eio.Stdenv.fs env);
+  let dir = temp_dir () in
+  Fun.protect
+    ~finally:(fun () -> rm_rf dir)

+      (* The evaluator runs test executables with HOME pointing at its sandbox.

+let rec files_of dir =

+    Sys.readdir dir

+let task_ids_in_scope json =

+      let starts_new_scope =
+        not root

+            | Some (`String _) -> true
+            | _ -> false)
+      in
+      if starts_new_scope

+      else

+           | Some (`String id) -> [ id ]
+           | _ -> [])

+             | Some (`List ids) -> List.filter_map string_value ids
+             | _ -> [])

+        direct_ids

+           |> List.concat_map (fun (_, value) -> visit ~root:false value))
+    | `List values -> List.concat_map (visit ~root:false) values

+let rec associations_in_json = function

+                     |> List.map String.trim |> List.sort_uniq String.compare in

+let json_stream_documents content =
+  let length = String.length content in
+  let documents = ref [] in
+  let start = ref None in
+  let depth = ref 0 in
+  let in_string = ref false in
+  let escaped = ref false in
+  for index = 0 to length - 1 do
+    let character = content.[index] in
+    if !depth = 0
+    then
+      (match character with
+       | '{' | '[' ->
+         start := Some index;
+         depth := 1;
+         in_string := false;
+         escaped := false
+       | _ -> ())
+    else if !in_string
+    then
+      if !escaped then escaped := false
+      else if character = '\\' then escaped := true
+      else if character = '"' then in_string := false
+    else
+      match character with
+      | '"' -> in_string := true
+      | '{' | '[' -> incr depth
+      | '}' | ']' ->
+        decr depth;
+        if !depth = 0
+        then
+          (match !start with
+           | Some first ->
+             let document = String.sub content first (index - first + 1) in
+             (try documents := Yojson.Safe.from_string document :: !documents with _ -> ());
+             start := None
+           | None -> ())
+      | _ -> ()
+  done;
+  List.rev !documents
+;;

+let json_documents content =

problem_statement:
Track remaining MASC path SSOT fallback cleanup
## Symptom
PR #22439 fixes the init-command config root path, but the branch audit still finds 14 MASC lib call sites that use `Sys.getcwd ()` as an implicit fallback for relative paths or default base paths.

## Reproduction / evidence
See `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-06-26-sys-getcwd-audit.md` in PR #22439. The audit lists 36 total `Sys.getcwd ()` occurrences in `lib/`, with 14 categorized as `fallback-to-fix`.

## Suspected cause
Several modules still predate the `Config_dir_resolver` / explicit `base_path` path model and repair relative inputs locally instead of accepting a resolved workspace path from the caller.

## Tried in PR #22439
- Moved `bin/main_eio.ml init` to `Config_dir_resolver.base_path_config_root`.
- Left deeper call-site refactors out of scope to keep the bridge/path hardening PR reviewable.

## Next steps
Thread explicit `base_path` or `cwd` through the fallback-to-fix call sites from the audit note, [HIDDEN].

### Additional contract requirements

## Additional Contract Requirements

All requirements below concern how MASC resolves filesystem locations. They are
observable through resolved paths returned by MASC configuration, workspace,
route, and voice-config surfaces; they do not constrain internal module
organization.

### Current-working-directory recovery
- Any path-resolution operation that needs the process current working
  directory must still succeed when the process's current directory has been
  deleted: it must produce a usable absolute path instead of raising an
  error. When no more specific base path applies, the fallback anchor comes
  from the process environment (for example a configured base path or the
  home directory) or the system temporary directory.
- The resolved workspace base path and any config-file location derived from
  it (such as the voice configuration file) must therefore remain resolvable
  even when the current directory has been deleted and no explicit base path
  is configured.

### Workspace base path sourcing and precedence
- When a caller supplies an explicit base-path argument, that argument
  (trimmed of surrounding whitespace) always wins over any
  environment-derived value.
- When no explicit argument is supplied, the workspace base path can be
  sourced from the environment. Two environment variables participate:
  `MASC_BASE_PATH_INPUT` (the direct process input) and `MASC_BASE_PATH`
  (the state propagated from the parent shell). When both are set to
  nonblank values, `MASC_BASE_PATH_INPUT` takes precedence; when only one is
  set, that one applies. This precedence is part of the public contract.
- When neither an explicit argument nor a usable environment value exists,
  the base path default resolves to the absolute-path description above
  (the current working directory when available, otherwise the recovered
  fallback anchor).

### Base-path normalization
- A configured or requested base path is canonicalized lexically: directory
  separators are collapsed, `.` segments are removed, and trailing slashes
  are stripped.
- When the normalized value ends in the reserved `.masc` directory name,
  that final component is collapsed away so that the base path denotes the
  directory that contains `.masc` rather than `.masc` itself.

### Relative-path anchoring
- A relative environment-supplied workspace base path is anchored to the
  effective current working directory (with deleted-directory recovery as
  described above), yielding an absolute path.
- An explicit relative path argument supplied by a caller is anchored to the
  effective current working directory, not to an inherited environment base
  path. In particular, a test executable resolving an explicitly requested
  relative path must not retarget it under the parent shell's propagated
  `MASC_BASE_PATH`.

diff --git a/lib/config_dir_resolver/config_dir_resolver.ml b/lib/config_dir_resolver/config_dir_resolver.ml
index d339b20c4ba..d7cd2d11dbb 100644
--- a/lib/config_dir_resolver/config_dir_resolver.ml
+++ b/lib/config_dir_resolver/config_dir_resolver.ml
@@ -147,13 +147,19 @@ let current_working_dir () =
 
 let base_path_or_cwd () =
   match (Host_config.from_env ()).base_path with
+  | Some path when Filename.is_relative path ->
+    Filename.concat (current_working_dir ()) path
   | Some path -> path
   | None -> current_working_dir ()
 
+(** Prefer [absolute_path_from ~cwd] when the caller has an explicit anchor.
+    [absolute_path] falls back to the process cwd via [current_working_dir]. *)
 let absolute_path path =
   if Filename.is_relative path then Filename.concat (current_working_dir ()) path
   else path
 
+(** Resolve [path] relative to an explicit [cwd]. Absolute paths are returned
+    verbatim; this keeps the caller's anchor as the SSOT. *)
 let absolute_path_from ~cwd path =
   if Filename.is_relative path then Filename.concat cwd path else path

--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/rebench_run_target_tests.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Rebench target-test runner for the path-SSOT fallback cleanup tests.
+# Builds and runs the finalized target test executables from the current
+# checkout, emitting explicit per-case [PASS]/[FAIL] <exe> <case> records and a
+# machine-readable report at /tmp/rebench-test-results.txt.
+# Exit status is non-zero when any target case fails.
+set -u
+cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
+unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH
+eval "$(opam env 2>/dev/null)"
+
+EXE_DIR="_build/default/test"
+EXES="test_config_dir_resolver test_workspace_utils_coverage test_voice_config test_sidecar_lifecycle_routes"
+
+# Build the target test executables from the current checkout so a stale
+# installed artifact cannot shadow patched test code.
+for e in $EXES; do
+  MASC_DUNE_THROTTLE=0 MASC_SKIP_PIN_CHECK=1 scripts/dune-local.sh build "test/$e.exe" >/dev/null 2>&1
+done
+
+REPORT=/tmp/rebench-test-results.txt
+: > "$REPORT"
+overall=0
+for e in $EXES; do
+  bin="$EXE_DIR/$e.exe"
+  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then echo "[FAIL] $e <missing executable>" | tee -a "$REPORT"; overall=1; continue; fi
+  out="$("$bin" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
+  echo "$out" | grep -E '\[OK\]|\[FAIL\]' | sed -E 's/│//g' | \
+    awk -v exe="$e" '{ st=($1=="[OK]")?"[PASS]":"[FAIL]"; $1=""; sub(/^ +/,""); print st, exe, $0 }' | tee -a "$REPORT"
+  [ $rc -ne 0 ] && overall=1
+done
+echo "---- report: $REPORT ----"
+echo "RESULT_EXIT=$overall"
+exit $overall
