diff --git a/src/main/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes.clj b/src/main/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes.clj
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..1102898a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/main/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,264 @@
+(ns dk.cst.dannet.db.shapes
+  "SHACL validation of the DanNet graph.
+
+  Bundles structural shapes (resources/schemas/internal/shapes/) with helpers
+  to validate a graph — or a single focus node — and return violations as
+  Clojure data. The shapes are split by target:
+
+    * base.ttl      — invariants of the asserted (base) graph
+    * inferred.ttl  — relation completeness; INFERRED model only
+    * editorial.ttl — stricter rules gating newly edited data (validate-node)
+
+  Current uses:
+    * clojure.test assertions over small fixtures (see test ns),
+    * a non-fatal bootstrap/CI check that logs anomalies via Telemere,
+      comparing violation counts to a known baseline (shapes-baseline.edn), and
+    * a release gate aborting RDF exports on baseline regressions
+      (`validate-export!`, called from dk.cst.dannet.db.export.rdf)."
+  (:require [clojure.edn :as edn]
+            [clojure.java.io :as io]
+            ;; Required for its side effects: registers DanNet prefixes with
+            ;; ont-app/vocabulary so that `voc/keyword-for` works in fresh JVMs.
+            [dk.cst.dannet.prefix]
+            [ont-app.vocabulary.core :as voc]
+            [dk.cst.dannet.db.transaction :as txn]
+            [taoensso.telemere :as t])
+  (:import [org.apache.jena.shacl ShaclValidator Shapes]
+           [org.apache.jena.shacl.validation ReportEntry]
+           [org.apache.jena.graph Graph GraphUtil Node NodeFactory]
+           [org.apache.jena.riot RDFDataMgr]
+           [org.apache.jena.sparql.path Path P_Link]))
+
+;; TODO: shapes are kept internal for now, but since SHACL shapes are plain
+;; RDF, consider eventually publishing them as Linked Open Data under the dns:
+;; namespace (alongside dannet-schema.ttl, cf. prefix.cljc) once they have
+;; stabilised — e.g. letting the future editing UI derive required fields from
+;; the same shapes that gate writes.
+(def shapes-resources
+  "SHACL shape files by target; :inferred and :editorial extend :base."
+  {:base      "schemas/internal/shapes/base.ttl"
+   :inferred  "schemas/internal/shapes/inferred.ttl"
+   :editorial "schemas/internal/shapes/editorial.ttl"})
+
+(defn load-shapes
+  "Parse the SHACL shapes at one or more classpath `resources` into a single
+  Jena `Shapes`, merging the shape graphs."
+  [resource & resources]
+  (let [graph (RDFDataMgr/loadGraph resource)]
+    (doseq [r resources]
+      (GraphUtil/addInto graph (RDFDataMgr/loadGraph r)))
+    (Shapes/parse graph)))
+
+(def shapes
+  "The default shapes for the asserted (base) graph, parsed once."
+  (delay (load-shapes (:base shapes-resources))))
+
+;; NOTE: all shapes use SPARQL-based targets scoped to the dn: namespace --
+;; DanNet only validates the dataset it controls, so companion datasets (COR,
+;; OEWN) are deliberately not targeted. See the SCOPE note in base.ttl.
+(def inferred-shapes
+  "Base + relation-completeness shapes; only valid against the INFERRED model."
+  (delay (load-shapes (:base shapes-resources)
+                      (:inferred shapes-resources))))
+
+(def editorial-shapes
+  "Base + stricter editorial shapes; meant for gating newly edited data via
+  targeted `validate-node` calls, never for validating the full graph."
+  (delay (load-shapes (:base shapes-resources)
+                      (:editorial shapes-resources))))
+
+;; Everything below converts Jena's ValidationReport into plain Clojure data:
+;; IRIs become DanNet keywords (via ont-app/vocabulary) so that callers never
+;; touch Jena classes and results can be diffed against the EDN baseline.
+(defn- node->value
+  "A DanNet keyword for an IRI `node`, falling back to its string form."
+  [^Node node]
+  (when node
+    (if (.isURI node)
+      (try (voc/keyword-for (.getURI node))
+           (catch Exception _ (.getURI node)))
+      (str node))))
+
+(defn- path->value
+  "A DanNet keyword for a simple predicate `path`, falling back to its string
+  form for complex SHACL property paths."
+  [^Path path]
+  (when path
+    (if (instance? P_Link path)
+      (node->value (.getNode ^P_Link path))
+      (str path))))
+
+(defn- entry->map
+  [^ReportEntry e]
+  ;; :shape is the stable identity used for baselines and grouping -- the
+  ;; reason every property shape in the TTL has an explicit IRI instead of
+  ;; the usual blank node.
+  {:focus-node (node->value (.focusNode e))
+   :path       (path->value (.resultPath e))
+   :value      (node->value (.value e))
+   :shape      (node->value (.source e))
+   :constraint (node->value (.sourceConstraintComponent e))
+   :message    (.message e)
+   ;; :sh/Violation blocks a write; :sh/Warning only surfaces in the UI.
+   :severity   (some-> (.severity e) .level node->value)})
+
+(defn- report->result
+  "Convert a Jena `ValidationReport` into the standard result map."
+  [^org.apache.jena.shacl.ValidationReport report]
+  (let [entries (mapv entry->map (.getEntries report))]
+    {:conforms? (.conforms report)
+     :n         (count entries)
+     :entries   entries}))
+
+(defn validate
+  "Validate `graph` against `shapes` (a Jena `Shapes`), assuming a read
+  transaction is already open. Returns
+
+    {:conforms? boolean, :n long, :entries [{:focus-node ...} ...]}."
+  ([^Graph graph]
+   (validate graph @shapes))
+  ([^Graph graph ^Shapes shapes]
+   (report->result (.validate (ShaclValidator/get) shapes graph))))
+
+(defn- ->node
+  "Coerce `x` (a Jena Node, a prefixed keyword, or an IRI string) into a Node."
+  ^Node [x]
+  (cond
+    (instance? Node x) x
+    (keyword? x) (NodeFactory/createURI (voc/uri-for x))
+    (string? x) (NodeFactory/createURI x)
+    :else (throw (IllegalArgumentException.
+                   (str "Cannot coerce to Node: " (pr-str x))))))
+
+(defn validate-node
+  "Validate a single focus `node` of `graph` against `shapes`, assuming a read
+  transaction is already open. Only shapes targeting the node are checked,
+  making this cheap enough to gate individual writes (e.g. an RDF Patch).
+
+  The `node` may be a Jena Node, a prefixed keyword (e.g. :dn/synset-999), or
+  an IRI string. Returns the same result map as `validate`."
+  ([^Graph graph node]
+   (validate-node graph @shapes node))
+  ([^Graph graph ^Shapes shapes node]
+   (report->result (.validate (ShaclValidator/get) shapes graph (->node node)))))
+
+(defn by-severity
+  "Violation `entries` grouped by :severity, e.g. for separating blocking
+  violations (:sh/Violation) from surfaceable warnings (:sh/Warning)."
+  [entries]
+  (group-by :severity entries))
+
+(defn blocking?
+  "Does the validation `result` contain entries that should block a write?
+  Only :sh/Violation entries block; :sh/Warning and :sh/Info do not."
+  [result]
+  (boolean (some #(= :sh/Violation (:severity %)) (:entries result))))
+
+(def baseline-resource
+  "schemas/internal/shapes-baseline.edn")
+
+(def baseline
+  "Known violation counts per property shape, i.e. the accepted status quo.
+  Counts *exceeding* the baseline indicate a regression; counts below it mean
+  data was fixed (update the baseline file accordingly)."
+  (delay (some-> (io/resource baseline-resource) slurp edn/read-string)))
+
+(defn by-shape
+  "Frequencies of violation `entries` grouped by their source property shape."
+  [entries]
+  (frequencies (map :shape entries)))
+
+(defn exceeding-baseline
+  "The part of a `by-shape` frequency map exceeding the `baseline`, as a map of
+  shape to [baseline-count actual-count]. Empty when nothing regressed."
+  [by-shape baseline]
+  (into {}
+        (keep (fn [[shape n]]
+                (let [m (get baseline shape 0)]
+                  (when (> n m)
+                    [shape [m n]]))))
+        by-shape))
+
+(defn- against-baseline
+  "Add :exceeded to a validation `result` by comparing its :sh/Violation
+  entries to the known `baseline`; warnings never count against it.
+  Also adds :violations (the blocking entry count) for logging purposes."
+  [result]
+  (let [violations (:sh/Violation (by-severity (:entries result)))]
+    (assoc result
+      :violations (count violations)
+      :exceeded (exceeding-baseline (by-shape violations) @baseline))))
+
+(defn validate-db
+  "Validate the asserted (base) graph of `db` against the default shapes within a
+  read transaction, log a summary via Telemere, and return the result map with
+  added :violations and :exceeded keys comparing blocking violation counts to
+  the known baseline (warnings surface in the logged counts only).
+
+  Non-fatal by design: a bootstrap/CI check, not (yet) an acceptance gate.
+  Logs :error when the baseline is exceeded, :warn on known violations, and
+  :info when the graph conforms."
+  [db]
+  ;; Called async at boot from dk.cst.dannet.web.resources -- deliberately
+  ;; non-fatal so a validation problem can never take the service down.
+  (let [graph  (.getGraph ^org.apache.jena.rdf.model.Model (:base-model db))
+        {:keys [violations exceeded] :as result}
+        (against-baseline (txn/transact-read (:dataset db) (validate graph)))]
+    (t/log! {:level (cond (seq exceeded)            :error
+                          (not (:conforms? result)) :warn
+                          :else                     :info)
+             :id    :dannet.shapes/validate
+             :data  {:conforms?  (:conforms? result)
+                     :violations violations
+                     :by-shape   (by-shape (:entries result))
+                     :exceeded   exceeded}}
+            "SHACL validation of asserted graph")
+    result))
+
+(defn validate-inferred-db
+  "Validate the inference graph of `db` against the inferred shape set within a
+  read transaction, log a summary via Telemere, and return the result map.
+
+  EXPENSIVE and opt-in by design (never wired into boot): SHACL validation
+  traverses the entire inference graph, forcing materialization of inferred
+  triples. Expect this to take a long time on the full dataset."
+  [db]
+  (let [result (txn/transact-read (:dataset db)
+                 (validate (:graph db) @inferred-shapes))
+        counts (by-shape (:entries result))]
+    (t/log! {:level (if (:conforms? result) :info :warn)
+             :id    :dannet.shapes/validate-inferred
+             :data  {:conforms?  (:conforms? result)
+                     :violations (:n result)
+                     :by-shape   counts}}
+            "SHACL validation of inferred graph")
+    result))
+
+(defn validate-export!
+  "Validate the exported Turtle file at `path` (a plain .ttl on disk) against
+  the default base shapes, comparing :sh/Violation counts to the known
+  baseline. A release gate: throws ex-info when violations exceed the
+  baseline; warnings and baselined violations only log.
+
+  Returns the result map with added :violations and :exceeded keys when the
+  gate passes."
+  [path]
+  ;; Loads the artifact into a fresh in-memory graph so the gate validates
+  ;; exactly what ships, not the live TDB2 graph it was exported from.
+  (let [path (str path)
+        {:keys [violations exceeded] :as result}
+        (against-baseline (validate (RDFDataMgr/loadGraph path)))]
+    (t/log! {:level (cond (seq exceeded)            :error
+                          (not (:conforms? result)) :warn
+                          :else                     :info)
+             :id    :dannet.shapes/validate-export
+             :data  {:path       path
+                     :conforms?  (:conforms? result)
+                     :violations violations
+                     :exceeded   exceeded}}
+            "SHACL validation of exported artifact")
+    (when (seq exceeded)
+      (throw (ex-info (str "SHACL violations exceed baseline in " path)
+                      {:path     path
+                       :exceeded exceeded})))
+    result))

diff --git a/test/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes_test.clj b/test/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes_test.clj
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d68402e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/dk/cst/dannet/db/shapes_test.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,384 @@
+;; NB: `clojure.pprint` is required first as a workaround: loading the
+;; project's database namespaces with a plain `java` launcher under
+;; JDK 21+ lazily materialises the pprint class from within a custom
+;; classloader where it is not yet visible.
+(ns dk.cst.dannet.db.shapes-test
+  "Fixture-based tests for the SHACL validation of the DanNet graph. The
+  tests are self-contained: they validate small in-memory Turtle graphs,
+  temporary Turtle files, and small exported zip archives -- never a
+  running database.
+
+  Assertions only inspect violations whose focus node belongs to the fixture
+  graph; regardless of any pre-existing baseline of known violations in the
+  live dataset, every shape violation caused by a fixture must surface.
+
+  All assertions stick to the documented contract: the entry representation
+  of focus nodes, paths, and values is unspecified, so they are only ever
+  compared via their `str` form. The thrown type on gate failure is also
+  unspecified, so only `Throwable` is caught."
+  (:require [clojure.java.io :as io]
+            [clojure.pprint]
+            [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
+            [dk.cst.dannet.db.export.rdf :as export.rdf]
+            [dk.cst.dannet.db.shapes :as shapes]
+            [dk.cst.dannet.test-util :as util])
+  (:import [org.apache.jena.rdf.model ModelFactory]
+           [org.apache.jena.riot RDFFormat]))
+
+(def ^:private prefixes "
+@prefix ontolex: <http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#> .
+@prefix rdfs:    <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
+@prefix wn:      <https://globalwordnet.github.io/schemas/wn#> .
+@prefix dn:      <https://wordnet.dk/dannet/data/> .
+@prefix other:   <https://example.org/other/> .
+")
+
+(defn- validate-ttl
+  "Validate the graph parsed from `ttl` (with the shared prefixes prepended)
+  against the default shapes for the asserted graph."
+  [ttl]
+  (shapes/validate (util/ttl->graph (str prefixes ttl))))
+
+(defn- entry-value-mentions?
+  "Does `entry` report an entity whose textual form ends with the local
+  name `local-name`? Since the representation of reported focus nodes and
+  paths (keyword, string, IRI, ...) is unspecified by the contract, all
+  comparisons happen via `str` on both focus node and path."
+  [entry local-name]
+  (or (.endsWith (str (:focus-node entry)) local-name)
+      (.endsWith (str (:path entry)) local-name)))
+
+(defn- violation-entry?
+  "Is `entry` a blocking (sh:Violation) entry? Severity values are compared
+  by local name only, allowing both keyword and IRI-string representations."
+  [entry]
+  (.endsWith (str (:severity entry)) "Violation"))
+
+(defn- warning-entry?
+  "Is `entry` a non-blocking (sh:Warning) entry?"
+  [entry]
+  (.endsWith (str (:severity entry)) "Warning"))
+
+(defn- path-violation?
+  "Is there an :sh/Violation entry in `result` concerning the entity
+  `entity-iri` (a keyword or string), optionally on the state `path` (a
+  keyword or string, nil to ignore the path)?"
+  [result entity-iri path]
+  (let [entity-name (name entity-iri)
+        path-name (when path (name path))]
+    (boolean
+      (some (fn [entry]
+              (and (violation-entry? entry)
+                   (entry-value-mentions? entry entity-name)
+                   (or (nil? path)
+                       (.endsWith (str (:path entry)) path-name))))
+            (:entries result)))))
+
+(defn- entry-triple
+  "A minimal full entry (label, partOfSpeech, sense and canonicalForm)
+  used to keep words in a fixture otherwise well-formed."
+  [word sense form label]
+  (format "%s a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"%s\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense %s ; ontolex:canonicalForm %s ." word label sense form))
+
+(deftest basic-shapes
+  (testing "well-formed entry + sense + synset conforms"
+    (is (:conforms? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-1 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ;
+  rdfs:label \"hund\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-1 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-1 .
+dn:sense-1 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"hund\" .
+dn:synset-1 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{hund}\" ."))))
+  (testing "entities outside the dn: namespace are not validated"
+    (is (:conforms? (validate-ttl "
+other:entry-1 a ontolex:LexicalEntry .
+other:sense-1 a ontolex:LexicalSense .
+other:synset-1 a ontolex:LexicalConcept .")))))
+
+(deftest lexical-entry-shape
+  (testing "missing rdfs:label"
+    (let [result (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-2 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-2 .")]
+      (is (false? (:conforms? result)))
+      (is (path-violation? result :dn/entry-2 :rdfs/label))))
+  (testing "missing wn:partOfSpeech"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-2 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-2 .")
+                         :dn/entry-2 :wn/partOfSpeech)))
+  (testing "missing ontolex:sense"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ;
+  wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-2 .")
+                         :dn/entry-2 :ontolex/sense)))
+  (testing "missing ontolex:canonicalForm"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ;
+  wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ; ontolex:sense dn:sense-2 .")
+                         :dn/entry-2 :ontolex/canonicalForm)))
+  (testing "two canonical forms"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ;
+  wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ; ontolex:sense dn:sense-2 ;
+  ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-2 , dn:form-3 .")
+                         :dn/entry-2 :ontolex/canonicalForm)))
+  (testing "canonical form must not be a literal"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:entry-2 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ;
+  wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ; ontolex:sense dn:sense-2 ;
+  ontolex:canonicalForm \"hund\" .")
+                         :dn/entry-2 nil))))
+
+(deftest lexical-entry-subtypes
+  ;; The entry constraints apply identically to the DanNet entry subtypes
+  ;; used in exports: ontolex:Word and ontolex:MultiwordExpression.
+  (doseq [subtype ["ontolex:Word" "ontolex:MultiwordExpression"]]
+    (testing (str subtype " missing rdfs:label")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-1 a %s ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sub-sense-1 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:sub-form-1 ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-1 :rdfs/label)))
+    (testing (str subtype " missing wn:partOfSpeech")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-2 a %s ; rdfs:label \"ord\" ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sub-sense-2 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:sub-form-2 ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-2 :wn/partOfSpeech)))
+    (testing (str subtype " missing ontolex:sense")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-3 a %s ; rdfs:label \"ord\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:canonicalForm dn:sub-form-3 ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-3 :ontolex/sense)))
+    (testing (str subtype " missing ontolex:canonicalForm")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-4 a %s ; rdfs:label \"ord\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sub-sense-4 ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-4 :ontolex/canonicalForm)))
+    (testing (str subtype " two canonical forms")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-5 a %s ; rdfs:label \"ord\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sub-sense-5 ;
+  ontolex:canonicalForm dn:sub-form-5 , dn:sub-form-5b ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-5 :ontolex/canonicalForm)))
+    (testing (str subtype " literal canonical form")
+      (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl (format "
+dn:sub-6 a %s ; rdfs:label \"ord\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sub-sense-6 ; ontolex:canonicalForm \"ord\" ." subtype))
+                           :dn/sub-6 nil)))))
+
+(deftest lexical-sense-shape
+  (testing "missing rdfs:label"
+    (let [result (validate-ttl "
+dn:sense-3 a ontolex:LexicalSense .")]
+      (is (false? (:conforms? result)))
+      (is (path-violation? result :dn/sense-3 :rdfs/label)))))
+
+(deftest lexical-concept-shape
+  (testing "missing rdfs:label"
+    (let [result (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-10 a ontolex:LexicalConcept .")]
+      (is (false? (:conforms? result)))
+      (is (path-violation? result :dn/synset-10 :rdfs/label)))))
+
+(deftest hypernym-shapes
+  (testing "self-hypernymy is a violation"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-11 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  wn:hypernym dn:synset-11 .")
+                         :dn/synset-11 nil)))
+  (testing "mutual hypernymy is a violation"
+    (is (path-violation? (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-12 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  wn:hypernym dn:synset-13 .
+dn:synset-13 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  wn:hypernym dn:synset-12 .")
+                         :dn/synset-12 nil)))
+  (testing "cross-POS hypernymy is reported, but only as a warning"
+    (let [result (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-21 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-21 ; wn:hypernym dn:synset-23 .
+dn:synset-23 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-23 .
+dn:sense-21 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"a\" .
+dn:sense-23 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"b\" .
+dn:word-21 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"a\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-21 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-21 .
+dn:word-23 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"b\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:verb ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-23 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-23 .")]
+      ;; Reported as a warning entry concerning either synset...
+      (is (boolean (some (fn [entry]
+                         (and (warning-entry? entry)
+                              (or (entry-value-mentions? entry "synset-21")
+                                  (entry-value-mentions? entry "synset-23"))))
+                       (:entries result))))
+      ;; ...as the only report for this fixture...
+      (is (every? warning-entry? (:entries result)))
+      ;; ...which never blocks.
+      (is (not (shapes/blocking? result)))))
+  (testing "a foreign hypernym does not introduce a cross-POS warning"
+    (let [base (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-26 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-26 .
+dn:sense-26 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"a\" .
+dn:word-26 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"a\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-26 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-26 .")
+          with-foreign-parent (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-26 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-26 ; wn:hypernym other:synset-27 .
+other:synset-27 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-27 .
+dn:sense-26 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"a\" .
+dn:sense-27 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"b\" .
+dn:word-26 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"a\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-26 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-26 .
+dn:word-27 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"b\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:verb ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-27 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-27 .")]
+      (is (:conforms? base))
+      (is (:conforms? with-foreign-parent))))
+  (testing "hierarchy with agreeing POS conforms"
+    (is (:conforms? (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-24 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-24 ; wn:hypernym dn:synset-25 .
+dn:synset-25 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-25 .
+dn:sense-24 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"a\" .
+dn:sense-25 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"b\" .
+dn:word-24 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"a\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-24 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-24 .
+dn:word-25 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"b\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-25 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-25 .")))))
+
+(deftest blocking-severities
+  ;; Only :sh/Violation blocks; the presence of warnings never does.
+  (let [violating (validate-ttl "
+dn:sense-90 a ontolex:LexicalSense .")]
+    (is (boolean (shapes/blocking? violating))))
+  (let [warning-only (validate-ttl "
+dn:synset-91 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-91 ; wn:hypernym dn:synset-93 .
+dn:synset-93 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-93 .
+dn:sense-91 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"a\" .
+dn:sense-93 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"b\" .
+dn:word-91 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"a\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-91 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-91 .
+dn:word-93 a ontolex:Word ; rdfs:label \"b\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:verb ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-93 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-93 .")]
+    (is (false? (:conforms? warning-only)))
+    (is (not (shapes/blocking? warning-only)))))
+
+(deftest validate-node-targeting
+  (testing "targeted validation only checks the given focus node"
+    (let [g (util/ttl->graph (str prefixes "
+dn:entry-1 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ;
+  rdfs:label \"hund\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-1 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-1 .
+dn:sense-2 a ontolex:LexicalSense ."))]
+      ;; the graph as a whole has a violation...
+      (is (false? (:conforms? (shapes/validate g))))
+      ;; ...but the well-formed entry validates clean in isolation
+      (is (:conforms? (shapes/validate-node g :dn/entry-1)))
+      ;; ...while the problematic sense is still flagged when targeted,
+      ;; regardless of how the node is denoted
+      (is (not (:conforms? (shapes/validate-node g :dn/sense-2))))
+      (is (not (:conforms? (shapes/validate-node
+                             g "https://wordnet.dk/dannet/data/sense-2")))))))
+
+(defn- ->ttl-file
+  "Write `ttl` (with the shared prefixes prepended) to a temporary Turtle
+  file, returning the java.io.File."
+  [ttl]
+  (doto (java.io.File/createTempFile "shapes-test" ".ttl")
+    (.deleteOnExit)
+    (spit (str prefixes ttl))))
+
+(deftest validate-export-gate
+  (testing "conforming export passes the gate"
+    (is (:conforms? (shapes/validate-export!
+                      (.getPath (->ttl-file "
+dn:entry-1 a ontolex:LexicalEntry ;
+  rdfs:label \"hund\" ; wn:partOfSpeech wn:noun ;
+  ontolex:sense dn:sense-1 ; ontolex:canonicalForm dn:form-1 .
+dn:sense-1 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"hund\" ."))))))
+  (testing "baseline-tolerated violations do not abort the export"
+    ;; The shipped baseline accepts a small, known number of label-less dn:
+    ;; LexicalSenses in the live dataset, so exactly one such violation in
+    ;; an export stays within the per-shape allowance and does not abort;
+    ;; the anomaly is still reported in the returned result.
+    (let [result (shapes/validate-export!
+                   (.getPath (->ttl-file "
+dn:sense-71 a ontolex:LexicalSense .")))]
+      (is (map? result))
+      (is (path-violation? result :dn/sense-71 :rdfs/label))))
+  (testing "violations exceeding the baseline allowance abort the export"
+    ;; The accepted count of label-less dn: LexicalSenses is small (far
+    ;; below 100), so 100 label-less senses exceed the per-shape baseline
+    ;; allowance and abort the export. The specific exception type is
+    ;; unspecified; only `Throwable` is caught here.
+    (is (thrown? Throwable
+                 (shapes/validate-export!
+                   (.getPath (->ttl-file
+                               (apply str (for [i (range 100)]
+                                            (format "
+dn:sense-x%s a ontolex:LexicalSense ." i)))))))))
+  (testing "violations without a baseline allowance abort the export"
+    ;; The exported files contain ontolex:Word entries, so a label-less
+    ;; exported Word violates shapes with no baseline allowance.
+    (is (thrown? Throwable
+                 (shapes/validate-export!
+                   (.getPath (->ttl-file "
+dn:word-1 a ontolex:Word .")))))))
+
+(defn- ->temp-dir
+  []
+  (doto (.toFile (java.nio.file.Files/createTempDirectory
+                   "shapes-export-test"
+                   (into-array java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute [])))
+    (.deleteOnExit)))
+
+(defn- ->model
+  "Parse the Turtle string `ttl` (with the shared prefixes prepended) into
+  an in-memory Jena Model."
+  [ttl]
+  (ModelFactory/createModelForGraph (util/ttl->graph (str prefixes ttl))))
+
+(deftest rdf-export-gating
+  ;; The documented integration: exporting the dn: model with
+  ;; `:validate true` passes the exactly-written Turtle through the
+  ;; `validate-export!` gate, aborting the export when blocking violations
+  ;; exceed the accepted baseline.
+  (doseq [{:keys [suffix desc opts]}
+          [{:suffix ".zip" :desc "zipped export" :opts []}
+           {:suffix ".ttl" :desc "plain Turtle export"
+            :opts [:fmt RDFFormat/TURTLE_BLOCKS]}]]
+    (testing (str "export with validation enabled passes conforming data (" desc ")")
+      ;; A warning-only model (cross-POS hypernymy) doesn't conform, but
+      ;; warnings never count against the baseline, so the call completes
+      ;; and the artifact is written.
+      (let [model (->model
+                    (str (entry-triple "dn:word-21" "dn:sense-21" "dn:form-21" "hund")
+                         (entry-triple "dn:word-23" "dn:sense-w23" "dn:form-23" "gø")
+                         "
+dn:word-23 wn:partOfSpeech wn:verb .
+dn:sense-21 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"hund\" .
+dn:sense-w23 a ontolex:LexicalSense ; rdfs:label \"gø\" .
+dn:synset-21 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{a}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-21 ; wn:hypernym dn:synset-23 .
+dn:synset-23 a ontolex:LexicalConcept ; rdfs:label \"{b}\" ;
+  ontolex:lexicalizedSense dn:sense-w23 ."))
+            path  (str (.getPath (->temp-dir)) "/dn-export" suffix)]
+        (apply export.rdf/export-rdf-model! path model :validate true opts)
+        (is (.exists (io/file path)))))
+    (testing (str "export with validation enabled aborts on regressing data (" desc ")")
+      ;; A label-less dn: Word exceeds the (zero) baseline allowance of the
+      ;; entry shapes, so the export aborts; the leftover, partial artifact
+      ;; (if one was written at all) does not constitute a valid export.
+      (let [path (str (.getPath (->temp-dir)) "/dn-export-bad" suffix)]
+        (is (thrown? Throwable
+                     (apply export.rdf/export-rdf-model!
+                            path (->model "dn:word-43 a ontolex:Word .")
+                            :validate true opts)))
+        (when (.exists (io/file path))
+          ;; When an artifact file *is* left behind, SHACL validation must
+          ;; still reject it.
+          (is (thrown? Throwable (shapes/validate-export! path))))))))

+(ns dk.cst.dannet.test-util
+  "Shared helpers for DanNet test namespaces."
+  (:import [java.io ByteArrayInputStream]
+           [java.nio.charset StandardCharsets]
+           [org.apache.jena.graph Factory]
+           [org.apache.jena.riot RDFParser Lang]))
+
+(defn ttl->graph
+  "Parse a Turtle `ttl` string into an in-memory Jena Graph."
+  [^String ttl]
+  (let [g (Factory/createDefaultGraph)]
+    (.. (RDFParser/source (ByteArrayInputStream. (.getBytes ttl StandardCharsets/UTF_8)))
+        (lang Lang/TTL)
+        (parse g))
+    g))

problem_statement:
fix(protocol): tighten RequestId, ProgressToken, and sampling capability validation
## Problem

MCP/JSON-RPC wire IDs and progress tokens are constrained wire types, and sampling tool use must respect declared client capabilities. Current dynamic typing and permissive defaults can let malformed or unsupported wire shapes pass through too far.

Current audit findings:

- `lib/src/types/json_rpc.dart` still models `RequestId` and `ProgressToken` as `dynamic`, so bool/object/null-like malformed values can leak into some paths instead of failing at decode/boundary time.
- `lib/src/client/client.dart` does not reject sampling requests containing `tools` / `toolChoice` when `ClientCapabilities.sampling.tools` was not declared.
- `lib/src/shared/protocol.dart` has strict capability enforcement as opt-in behavior, which can hide peer capability violations.

## Proposed solution

[HIDDEN]

## Acceptance criteria

[HIDDEN]

## Notes

Keep this issue focused on wire validation and capability gating. Broader conformance/fuzz infrastructure can remain in the existing CLI/debugging roadmap issue.

### Additional contract requirements

# Wire scalar validation and sampling capability gating

This section defines the externally observable requirements for validating
MCP/JSON-RPC wire values and for gating incoming sampling requests on
negotiated client capabilities.

## Accepted wire scalar forms

- Request identifiers (the `id` member of a JSON-RPC request) must be JSON
  strings or integers. A message that carries a `method` together with an
  `id` that is missing, null, a boolean, a floating-point number, an object,
  or a list is malformed and must be rejected during JSON decoding rather

fix(protocol): gate lifecycle requests and validate elicitation variants
## Problem

A fresh MCP 2025-11-25 lifecycle/elicitation audit after #129/#136 found remaining request-gating and elicitation shape-validation gaps.

Spec anchors:

- `docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle.mdx`: initialization **MUST** be the first interaction; the client starts with `initialize`, then sends `notifications/initialized`, and operation messages must respect negotiated capabilities.
- `schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts`: `elicitation/create` params are a union of form and URL variants. Form mode requires `message` and `requestedSchema`; URL mode requires `mode: "url"`, `message`, `elicitationId`, and `url`.

Current source evidence:

- `lib/src/server/server.dart` handles `initialize` / `notifications/initialized`, but does not track enough lifecycle state to prevent arbitrary registered request handlers from running too early.
- `lib/src/shared/protocol.dart` generic `_onrequest` dispatches any registered handler without checking that initialization was completed first.
- `ProtocolOptions.enforceStrictCapabilities` remains opt-in, so operation-phase negotiated capability enforcement is not consistently defaulted for normal requests/notifications.
- `lib/src/client/client.dart` registers `elicitation/create` only when `_capabilities.elicitation?.form != null`; a client advertising only URL elicitation can fail to handle valid URL-mode `elicitation/create` requests.
- `lib/src/types/elicitation.dart` generic `ElicitRequest` construction/parsing can represent URL-mode requests without `url`/`elicitationId`, or form/default requests without `requestedSchema`, and `toJson()` then omits required fields.

## Proposed solution

[HIDDEN]
[HIDDEN]
[HIDDEN]
[HIDDEN]

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Raw wire regression proves normal requests before `initialize` are rejected and do not invoke business handlers.
- [ ] Regression proves operation requests before `notifications/initialized` are gated according to the lifecycle rules chosen for the SDK.
- [ ] Capability enforcement behavior is tested and documented for compatibility-sensitive paths.
- [ ] URL-only elicitation capability registers/handles URL-mode `elicitation/create` requests.
- [ ] Form and URL elicitation constructors/fromJson reject missing required fields, and `toJson()` cannot emit schema-invalid form or URL requests.

## Duplicate check

Searched existing issues/PRs for `notifications/initialized`, initialization first interaction, `ElicitRequest` URL mode, `requestedSchema`, and URL elicitation. No open issue/PR covers this gap.

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum

## Lifecycle gating

- The `initialize` request must be the first interaction on a connection.
  Before it is received, a server rejects non-lifecycle requests with an
  Invalid Request (`-32600`) JSON-RPC error response, and it does not invoke
  the registered business handler for such requests.
- Before receiving `initialize`, a server answers a `ping` request normally
  with a success result instead of rejecting it.
- After the server has sent the `initialize` result but before the client has
  sent `notifications/initialized`, the server rejects operation-phase
  requests other than `ping` with an Invalid Request (`-32600`) JSON-RPC
  error response and does not invoke their handlers. Once
  `notifications/initialized` is received, fully-initialized requests proceed
  normally.
- A client rejects server-initiated requests, other than `ping`, that arrive
  before the client has completed sending its `notifications/initialized`
  notification, replying with an Invalid Request (`-32600`) JSON-RPC error
  response and without invoking the registered handler. Notifications that
  arrive before then do not reach general notification handlers.
- A server rejects a duplicate `initialize` request with an Invalid Request
  error response, reports out-of-order lifecycle notifications (for example
  `notifications/initialized` arriving before `initialize`, or arriving more
  than once) through its error callback, and resets its lifecycle state when
  a connection closes so that a subsequent connection performs the handshake
  again.
- If sending the server's `initialize` result fails, the failure is reported
  through the server's error callback and the server does not treat that
  `initialize` request as received: a subsequent `initialize` request on the
  connection is accepted rather than rejected as a duplicate.
- If the server's notification handler for `notifications/initialized`
  throws, the failure is reported through the server's error callback and the
  server remains gated: afterwards it still rejects operation-phase requests
  with an Invalid Request (`-32600`) error response until
  `notifications/initialized` is accepted.
- If sending the client's `notifications/initialized` notification fails,
  the client's connect attempt fails and the transport is closed.

## Elicitation (`elicitation/create`)

- A client that advertises any elicitation capability registers a handler for
  `elicitation/create`. A client advertising only URL elicitation handles
  URL-mode `elicitation/create` requests.
- The client rejects an `elicitation/create` request whose mode is not among
  its advertised elicitation capabilities (for example a URL-mode request
  sent to a form-only client, or a form-mode request sent to a URL-only
  client) with an Invalid Params (`-32602`) JSON-RPC error response.
- `ElicitRequestParams.fromJson` rejects parameter objects that cannot be a
  valid form or URL elicitation request with a `FormatException`: a form-mode
  request without `requestedSchema`, a URL-mode request missing `url` or
  `elicitationId`, a URL-mode request carrying `requestedSchema`, or an
  unrecognized `mode`.
- `ElicitRequestParams` values cannot be serialized (`toJson`) into a
  schema-invalid combination, and the general-purpose constructor rejects
  invalid form/URL field combinations.

## Capability enforcement

- `ProtocolOptions.enforceStrictCapabilities` remains an opt-in configuration
  option and defaults to not enforcing strict capabilities. When strict
  capability enforcement is enabled for a connected server, outgoing normal
  requests and outgoing notifications whose required capabilities were not
  negotiated or advertised are rejected before they are sent over the
  transport.

- A server rejects a duplicate `initialize` request with an Invalid Request
  error response, reports out-of-order lifecycle notifications (for example
  `notifications/initialized` arriving before `initialize`, or arriving more
  than once) through its error callback, and resets its lifecycle state when
  a connection closes so that a subsequent connection performs the handshake
  again.
- If sending the server's `initialize` result fails, the failure is reported
  through the server's error callback and the server does not treat that
  `initialize` request as received: a subsequent `initialize` request on the
  connection is accepted rather than rejected as a duplicate.
- If the server's notification handler for `notifications/initialized`
  throws, the failure is reported through the server's error callback and the
  server remains gated: afterwards it still rejects operation-phase requests
  with an Invalid Request (`-32600`) error response until
  `notifications/initialized` is accepted.
- If sending the client's `notifications/initialized` notification fails,
  the client's connect attempt fails and the transport is closed.

## Elicitation (`elicitation/create`)

- A client that advertises any elicitation capability registers a handler for
  `elicitation/create`. A client advertising only URL elicitation handles
  URL-mode `elicitation/create` requests.
- The client rejects an `elicitation/create` request whose mode is not among
  its advertised elicitation capabilities (for example a URL-mode request
  sent to a form-only client, or a form-mode request sent to a URL-only
  client) with an Invalid Params (`-32602`) JSON-RPC error response.
- `ElicitRequestParams.fromJson` rejects parameter objects that cannot be a
  valid form or URL elicitation request with a `FormatException`: a form-mode
  request without `requestedSchema`, a URL-mode request missing `url` or
  `elicitationId`, a URL-mode request carrying `requestedSchema`, or an
  unrecognized `mode`.
- `ElicitRequestParams` values cannot be serialized (`toJson`) into a
  schema-invalid combination, and the general-purpose constructor rejects
  invalid form/URL field combinations.

## Capability enforcement

- `ProtocolOptions.enforceStrictCapabilities` remains an opt-in configuration
  option and defaults to not enforcing strict capabilities. When strict
  capability enforcement is enabled for a connected server, outgoing normal
  requests and outgoing notifications whose required capabilities were not
  negotiated or advertised are rejected before they are sent over the
  transport.

feat: configurable format string for :Gitsigns blame side panel
## Feature Request

The `:Gitsigns blame` side panel currently has a hardcoded line format in `lua/gitsigns/actions/blame.lua` (`render()` function):

```
âº <abbrev_sha> <author padded> <author_time>
```

There is no way for users to customize which fields are shown, the date format, or the column order.

## Proposed Solution

A new config option â e.g. `blame_opts.formatter` or a top-level `blame_formatter` â that accepts the same format specifier string (and optionally function) already supported by `current_line_blame_formatter`:

- `<abbrev_sha>`
- `<author>`, `<author_mail>`, `<author_time>`, `<author_time:FORMAT>`, `<author_tz>`
- `<committer>`, `<committer_mail>`, `<committer_time>`, `<committer_time:FORMAT>`, `<committer_tz>`
- `<summary>`
- `<filename>`

For example:

[HIDDEN]

## Motivation

- `current_line_blame_formatter` already provides a well-designed, flexible format string system â it would be natural and consistent to expose the same mechanism for the blame panel.
- Users may want to show/hide specific fields (e.g. omit the date, show committer instead of author, use relative time via `%R`, etc.).
- The date format is currently hardcoded to the default `%R` (relative time) with no way to change it.

## Related

- #184 â similar request for the `blame_line` floating window

### Additional contract requirements

For this task, the configuration key is the top-level option `blame_formatter`.

## Mandatory behavior

- `blame_formatter` is a top-level configuration option holding a format string. When it is set (an explicitly empty string counts as set), each commit entry in the `:Gitsigns blame` side panel is rendered by expanding that string, and the per-commit entry lines appear in the order and layout the string specifies.
- The first line of each commit block in the side panel starts with the `┍` graph glyph followed by a space, and the expanded entry text follows it. If the string expands to empty text, that line holds only the graph glyph (a trailing space is allowed) and no abbreviated SHA, author, date or other text.
- Supported format specifiers:
  - `<abbrev_sha>`
  - `<author>`, `<author_mail>`, `<author_time>`, `<author_time:FORMAT>`, `<author_tz>`
  - `<committer>`, `<committer_mail>`, `<committer_time>`, `<committer_time:FORMAT>`, `<committer_tz>`
  - `<summary>`
  - `<filename>`
- `<author_time>` and `<committer_time>` render the date as `%Y-%m-%d` when no `FORMAT` is given; `<author_time:FORMAT>` and `<committer_time:FORMAT>` render the corresponding timestamp using the `FORMAT` given to `os.date`, with `%R` meaning relative time (consistent with the existing behavior of the format string mechanism used by `current_line_blame_formatter`).
- When the format string omits `<summary>`, the trailing graph line of a multi-line commit block keeps its current behavior and shows the commit summary (e.g. `┕ <summary>`). When the format string contains `<summary>`, the summary is considered part of the formatted entry line and the trailing graph line shows only the graph character.
- `<filename>` expands to the repository-relative path of the blamed file.
- When `blame_formatter` is not set, the blame side panel keeps rendering exactly as before (per-commit line `┍ <abbrev_sha> <author> <author_time>` with the default date format, followed by `┕ <summary>` graph lines), unchanged.

+--- @field chunks Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+--- @field summary boolean
+
+--- @param hash_hl string
+--- @param info Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+--- @param max_author_len integer
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameLineFormat
+local function default_side_panel(hash_hl, info, max_author_len)
+  return {
+    chunks = {
+      { info.abbrev_sha, hash_hl },
+      { ' ' },
+      { lalign(max_author_len, info.author) },
+      { ' ' },
+      { util.expand_format('<author_time>', info) },
+    },
+    summary = true,
+  }
+end

+--- @param username string
+--- @param hash_hl string
+--- @param info Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+--- @param max_author_len integer
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameLineFormat
+local function format_side_panel(username, hash_hl, info, max_author_len)
+  local blame_formatter = config.blame_formatter
+  if not blame_formatter then
+    return default_side_panel(hash_hl, info, max_author_len)
+  end
+
+  if type(blame_formatter) == 'string' then
+    local chunks, saw_summary = BlameFormatter.expand_chunks(blame_formatter, username, info, {
+      token_hls = {
+        abbrev_sha = hash_hl,
+      },
+    })
+    return { chunks = chunks, summary = not saw_summary }
+  end
+
+  local ok, result, show_summary = pcall(blame_formatter, username, info, {
+    max_author_width = max_author_len,
+    hash_hl_group = hash_hl,
+  })
+
+  local function fallback()
+    return default_side_panel(hash_hl, info, max_author_len)
+  end
+
+  if not ok then
+    error_once('Failed running config.blame_formatter, using default:\n   %s', result)
+    return fallback()
+  end
+
+  local ok_norm, chunks = pcall(BlameFormatter.sanitize_chunks, result)
+  if not ok_norm then
+    error_once('Invalid return from config.blame_formatter, using default:\n   %s', chunks)
+    return fallback()
+  end
+
+  if show_summary ~= nil and type(show_summary) ~= 'boolean' then
+    error_once(
+      'Invalid second return from config.blame_formatter, using default:\n   %s',
+      tostring(show_summary)
+    )
+    return fallback()
+  end
+
+  return { chunks = chunks, summary = show_summary ~= false }
+end

+local util = require('gitsigns.util')
+
+local M = {}
+
+--- @class (exact) Gitsigns.BlameLineHighlight
+--- @field start_col integer
+--- @field end_col integer
+--- @field hl_group Gitsigns.HlName|Gitsigns.HlStack
+
+--- @param info Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+--- @param username string
+--- @param opts? { self_author_text?: string }
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+local function normalize_info(info, username, opts)
+  local self_author_text = opts and opts.self_author_text
+  if not (self_author_text and info.author == username) then
+    return info
+  end
+
+  info = vim.deepcopy(info)
+  info.author = self_author_text
+  return info
+end
+
+--- @param chunks Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+function M.sanitize_chunks(chunks)
+  if type(chunks) ~= 'table' then
+    error('blame formatter must return a list of [text, highlight] chunks')
+  end
+
+  local ret = {} --- @type Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+  for i, part in ipairs(chunks) do
+    if type(part) ~= 'table' or type(part[1]) ~= 'string' then
+      error(('invalid blame formatter chunk at index %d'):format(i))
+    end
+
+    local text = part[1]
+    if text:find('\n', 1, true) then
+      error('blame formatter chunks cannot contain newlines')
+    end
+
+    if text ~= '' then
+      ret[#ret + 1] = { text, part[2] }
+    end
+  end
+
+  return ret
+end
+
+--- @param fmt string
+--- @param username string
+--- @param info Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+--- @param opts? { self_author_text?: string }
+--- @return string
+function M.expand_string(fmt, username, info, opts)
+  return util.expand_format(fmt, normalize_info(info, username, opts))
+end
+
+--- @param fmt string
+--- @param username string
+--- @param info Gitsigns.BlameInfoPublic
+--- @param opts? { self_author_text?: string, token_hls?: table<string, Gitsigns.HlName|Gitsigns.HlStack> }
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+--- @return boolean
+function M.expand_chunks(fmt, username, info, opts)
+  local ret = {} --- @type Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+  local saw_summary = false
+  local token_hls = opts and opts.token_hls or nil
+  info = normalize_info(info, username, opts)
+
+  for _ = 1, 20 do -- loop protection
+    local scol, ecol, match, key = fmt:find('(<([^:>]+):?([^>]*)>)')
+    if not match then
+      break
+    end
+
+    --- @cast scol integer
+    --- @cast ecol integer
+    --- @cast key string
+
+    ret[#ret + 1], fmt = { fmt:sub(1, scol - 1) }, fmt:sub(ecol + 1)
+    ret[#ret + 1] = { util.expand_format(match, info), token_hls and token_hls[key] }
+    saw_summary = saw_summary or key == 'summary'
+  end
+
+  ret[#ret + 1] = { fmt }
+  return M.sanitize_chunks(ret), saw_summary
+end
+
+--- @param chunks Gitsigns.BlameFmtChunk[]
+--- @return string
+--- @return Gitsigns.BlameLineHighlight[]
+--- @return integer
+function M.render_line(chunks)
+  local highlights = {} --- @type Gitsigns.BlameLineHighlight[]
+  local text = {} --- @type string[]
+  local col = 0
+
+  for _, part in ipairs(chunks) do
+    local part_text, hl_group = part[1], part[2]
+    text[#text + 1] = part_text
+
+    local end_col = col + #part_text
+    if hl_group and end_col > col then
+      highlights[#highlights + 1] = {
+        start_col = col,
+        end_col = end_col,
+        hl_group = hl_group,
+      }
+    end
+    col = end_col
+  end
+
+  local line = table.concat(text)
+  return line, highlights, vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(line)
+end
+
+return M

+        for _, t in ipairs(list) do
+          local fullname = getFileLine(t.element) .. colors.bright(t.name)
+          s = s .. testString:format(fullname)
+          s = s .. getDescription(t)
+        end
+      end
+    end
+    return s
+  end
+
+  local getSummary = function(status, count)
+    local footer = summaryStrings[status].footer
+    if count > 0 and footer then
+      local tests = (count == 1 and 'TEST' or 'TESTS')
+      local errors = (count == 1 and 'ERROR' or 'ERRORS')
+      return footer:format(count, status == 'error' and errors or tests)
+    end
+    return ''
+  end
+
+  local getSummaryString = function()
+    local tests = (successCount == 1 and 'test' or 'tests')
+    return table.concat({
+      successStatus:format(successCount, tests),
+
+      getTestList('skipped', skippedCount, handler.pendings, pendingDescription),
+      getTestList('failure', failureCount, handler.failures, failureDescription),
+      getTestList('error', errorCount, handler.errors, failureDescription),
+
+      ((skippedCount + failureCount + errorCount) > 0 and '\n' or ''),
+      getSummary('skipped', skippedCount),
+      getSummary('failure', failureCount),
+      getSummary('error', errorCount),
+    })
+  end
+
+  handler.suiteReset = function()
+    fileCount = 0
+    fileTestCount = 0
+    testCount = 0
+    successCount = 0
+    skippedCount = 0
+    failureCount = 0
+    errorCount = 0
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.suiteStart = function(_suite, count, total, randomseed)
+    if total > 1 then
+      io.write(repeatSuiteString:format(count, total))
+    end
+    if randomseed then
+      io.write(randomizeString:format(randomseed))
+    end
+    io.write(globalSetup)
+    io.flush()
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  local function getElapsedTime(tbl)
+    if tbl.duration then
+      return tbl.duration * 1000
+    else
+      return tonumber('nan')
+    end
+  end
+
+  handler.suiteEnd = function(suite, _count, _total)
+    local elapsedTime_ms = getElapsedTime(suite)
+    local tests = testCount == 1 and 'test' or 'tests'
+    local files = fileCount == 1 and 'file' or 'files'
+    io.write(globalTeardown)
+    io.write(suiteEndString:format(testCount, tests, fileCount, files, elapsedTime_ms))
+    io.write(getSummaryString())
+    io.flush()
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.fileStart = function(file)
+    fileTestCount = 0
+    io.write(fileStartString:format(vim.fs.normalize(file.name)))
+    io.flush()
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.fileEnd = function(file)
+    local elapsedTime_ms = getElapsedTime(file)
+    local tests = fileTestCount == 1 and 'test' or 'tests'
+    fileCount = fileCount + 1
+    io.write(
+      fileEndString:format(fileTestCount, tests, vim.fs.normalize(file.name), elapsedTime_ms)
+    )
+    io.flush()
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.testStart = function(element, _parent)
+    local desc = (' %s'):format(handler.getFullName(element))
+    io.write(runString:format(desc))
+    io.flush()
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  local function write_status(element, string)
+    io.write(timeString:format(getElapsedTime(element)) .. ' ' .. string)
+    io.flush()
+  end
+
+  handler.testEnd = function(element, _parent, status, _debug)
+    local s --- @type string
+
+    fileTestCount = fileTestCount + 1
+    testCount = testCount + 1
+    if status == 'success' then
+      successCount = successCount + 1
+      s = successString
+    elseif status == 'pending' then
+      skippedCount = skippedCount + 1
+      s = skippedString
+    elseif status == 'failure' then
+      failureCount = failureCount + 1
+      s = failureString .. failureDescription(handler.failures[#handler.failures])
+    elseif status == 'error' then
+      errorCount = errorCount + 1
+      s = errorString .. failureDescription(handler.errors[#handler.errors])
+    else
+      s = 'unexpected test status! (' .. status .. ')'
+    end
+
+    -- rebench: emit a stable machine-readable per-test status line that the
+    -- execution parser understands, reflecting this test's real outcome.
+    local rebench_status = ({
+      success = 'Success',
+      pending = 'Skip',
+      failure = 'Fail',
+      error = 'Fail',
+    })[status]
+    if rebench_status then
+      local rebench_name = handler.getFullName(element):gsub('%s*#%d+#%s*$', '')
+      io.write(('%s || %s\n'):format(rebench_status, rebench_name))
+      io.flush()
+    end
+    write_status(element, s)
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.error = function(element, _parent, _message, _debug)
+    if element.descriptor ~= 'it' then
+      write_status(element, failureDescription(handler.errors[#handler.errors]))
+      errorCount = errorCount + 1
+    end
+
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  busted.subscribe({ 'suite', 'reset' }, handler.suiteReset)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'suite', 'start' }, handler.suiteStart)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'suite', 'end' }, handler.suiteEnd)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'file', 'start' }, handler.fileStart)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'file', 'end' }, handler.fileEnd)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'test', 'start' }, handler.testStart, { predicate = handler.cancelOnPending })
+  busted.subscribe({ 'test', 'end' }, handler.testEnd, { predicate = handler.cancelOnPending })
+  busted.subscribe({ 'failure' }, handler.error)
+  busted.subscribe({ 'error' }, handler.error)
+
+  return handler
+end

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Faithful per-test runner for the gitsigns.nvim rebench target tests.
+#
+# The stock nvim-test/busted runner only prints a human `RUN ... OK/FAIL` line
+# plus aggregate counters, which the execution parser (parse_log_lua_nvim)
+# cannot read. This wrapper invokes the real nvim-test runner once per target
+# test, captures the runner's real per-test status (emitted by a thin copy of
+# the stock output handler), and re-emits it on its own stdout line in the
+# `Success || name` / `Fail || name` / `Skip || name` form the parser accepts.
+# The wrapper exits nonzero whenever any selected test fails.
+set -u
+
+PJ_ROOT="${PJ_ROOT:-$PWD}"
+export XDG_DATA_HOME="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.data}"
+export PJ_ROOT
+export NVIM_LOG_FILE="${NVIM_LOG_FILE:-$PJ_ROOT/.nvimlog}"
+export NVIM_RUNNER_VERSION="${NVIM_RUNNER_VERSION:-v0.12.0}"
+export NVIM_TEST_VERSION="${NVIM_TEST_VERSION:-v0.12.0}"
+
+HANDLER_DIR="$PJ_ROOT/test/.rebench-handler"
+LOG="${REBENCH_LOG:-/tmp/rebench-test-results.log}"
+: >"$LOG"
+
+ulimit -n 1024 2>/dev/null || true
+
+# Ordered list of "<unique busted --filter pattern>|<stable test name>" pairs.
+TESTS=(
+  'blame renders the default side%-panel layout|blame renders the default side-panel layout'
+  'blame supports string side%-panel formatters|blame supports string side-panel formatters'
+  'blame supports author, committer, mail and timezone side%-panel specifiers|blame supports author, committer, mail and timezone side-panel specifiers'
+  'blame supports custom date formats and field ordering in side%-panel formatters|blame supports custom date formats and field ordering in side-panel formatters'
+  'blame supports bare, committer and relative%-time date specifiers|blame supports bare, committer and relative-time date specifiers'
+  'blame uses a repo%-relative path when running blame|blame uses a repo-relative path when running blame'
+  'blame expands an explicitly empty string formatter|blame expands an explicitly empty string formatter'
+  'blame expands filename to the repo%-relative path of a file in a subdirectory|blame expands filename to the repo-relative path of a file in a subdirectory'
+)
+
+overall=0
+for entry in "${TESTS[@]}"; do
+  filter="${entry%%|*}"
+  name="${entry##*|}"
+
+  out="$(
+    "$PJ_ROOT/deps/nvim-test/bin/nvim-test" test \
+      --lpath="$PJ_ROOT/lua/?.lua" \
+      --lpath="$HANDLER_DIR/?.lua" \
+      --output rebench_out \
+      --verbose \
+      --filter="$filter" 2>&1
+  )"
+
+  # Preserve the full runner output in the machine-readable log.
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -r 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' >>"$LOG"
+
+  # Extract the real per-test status line the handler emitted for this test.
+  line="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -r 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' \
+    | grep -oE '(Success|Fail|Skip) \|\| .*' | head -n 1)"
+
+  if [ -n "$line" ]; then
+    status="${line%% ||*}"
+    printf '%s || %s\n' "$status" "$name" | tee -a "$LOG"
+    if [ "$status" != "Success" ] && [ "$status" != "Skip" ]; then
+      overall=1
+    fi
+  else
+    # The runner did not report an outcome for this test (collection error).
+    printf 'Fail || %s\n' "$name" | tee -a "$LOG"
+    overall=1
+  fi
+done
+
+exit "$overall"

problem_statement:
Library plants Timber.DebugTree() globally, affecting host app logging
Hi!

LiveKit currently plants Timber.DebugTree() internally when loggingLevel != OFF
(if no DebugTree is present in the forest).

Since Timber is a global logger, this affects the entire host application,
not just LiveKit logs, and removes control over logging configuration
(e.g. custom Trees like Crashlytics-only logging).

Library code generally should not plant Timber trees, as this is an
application-level concern.

[HIDDEN]

Thanks!

### Additional contract requirements

## Logging configuration contract

Changing `LiveKit.loggingLevel` controls which SDK log messages are eligible for delivery. It must not register, remove, or otherwise alter logging destinations owned by the host application.

The SDK exposes a nullable `LiveKit.logger` for its own log output. Its initial value is the usable `LKLog.defaultLogger`; applications may replace it, restore that default, or set it to `null` to disable SDK logging. A configured logger receives the log level, any supplied throwable, and the message for enabled entries. Messages below the configured level, and messages while the logger is `null`, are not evaluated.

The default logger uses an SDK-owned `LKDebugTree` sink rather than a host-global logging tree. `LKDebugTree` derives a tag from the caller and prepares nullable messages and throwables before forwarding, and may be subclassed to redirect the prepared output. An entry with neither a message nor a throwable is ignored; throwable text is substituted for an empty message or appended to a nonempty one. Its default output writes bounded-size chunks to Android logcat.

+package io.livekit.android.util

+import android.os.Build
+import android.util.Log
+import java.io.PrintWriter
+import java.io.StringWriter
+import java.util.regex.Pattern

+/**
+ * This is a modified version of DebugTree from JakeWharton/timber for LiveKit.
+ * https://github.com/JakeWharton/timber
+ */
+
+/**
+ * A tree for debug builds. Automatically infers the tag from the calling class.
+ * @suppress
+ * */
+open class LKDebugTree {
+
+    private val fqcnIgnore =
+        listOf(
+            LKDebugTree::class.java.name,
+            LKLog.defaultLogger::class.java.name,
+        )
+
+    val tag: String?
+        get() =
+            Throwable()
+                .stackTrace
+                .first { it.className !in fqcnIgnore }
+                .let(::createStackElementTag)
+
+    fun prepareLog(priority: Int, t: Throwable?, message: String?) {
+        // Consume tag even when message is not loggable so that next message is correctly tagged.
+        val tag = tag
+
+        var message = message
+        if (message.isNullOrEmpty()) {
+            if (t == null) {
+                return // Swallow message if it's null and there's no throwable.
+            }
+            message = getStackTraceString(t)
+        } else {
+            if (t != null) {
+                message += "\n" + getStackTraceString(t)
+            }
+        }
+
+        log(priority, tag, message, t)
+    }
+
+    private fun getStackTraceString(t: Throwable): String {
+        // Don't replace this with Log.getStackTraceString() - it hides
+        // UnknownHostException, which is not what we want.
+        val sw = StringWriter(256)
+        val pw = PrintWriter(sw, false)
+        t.printStackTrace(pw)
+        pw.flush()
+        return sw.toString()
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Extract the tag which should be used for the message from the `element`. By default this will
+     * use the class name without any anonymous class suffixes (e.g., `Foo$1` becomes `Foo`).
+     *
+     * Note: This will not be called if a [manual tag][.tag] was specified.
+     */
+    private fun createStackElementTag(element: StackTraceElement): String? {
+        var tag = element.className.substringAfterLast('.')
+        val m = ANONYMOUS_CLASS.matcher(tag)
+        if (m.find()) {
+            tag = m.replaceAll("")
+        }
+        // Tag length limit was removed in API 26.
+        return if (tag.length <= MAX_TAG_LENGTH || Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 26) {
+            tag
+        } else {
+            tag.take(MAX_TAG_LENGTH)
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Break up `message` into maximum-length chunks (if needed) and send to either
+     * [Log.println()][Log.println] or [Log.wtf()][Log.wtf] for logging.
+     *
+     * {@inheritDoc}
+     */
+    open fun log(priority: Int, tag: String?, message: String, t: Throwable?) {
+        if (message.length < MAX_LOG_LENGTH) {
+            if (priority == Log.ASSERT) {
+                Log.wtf(tag, message)
+            } else {
+                Log.println(priority, tag, message)
+            }
+            return
+        }
+
+        // Split by line, then ensure each line can fit into Log's maximum length.
+        var i = 0
+        val length = message.length
+        while (i < length) {
+            var newline = message.indexOf('\n', i)
+            newline = if (newline != -1) newline else length
+            do {
+                val end = newline.coerceAtMost(i + MAX_LOG_LENGTH)
+                val part = message.substring(i, end)
+                if (priority == Log.ASSERT) {
+                    Log.wtf(tag, part)
+                } else {
+                    Log.println(priority, tag, part)
+                }
+                i = end
+            } while (i < newline)
+            i++
+        }
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private const val MAX_LOG_LENGTH = 4000
+        private const val MAX_TAG_LENGTH = 23
+        private val ANONYMOUS_CLASS = Pattern.compile("(\\$\\d+)+$")
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Tech Debt: Normalize ujson.Null at parsing boundaries across providers
## Context

Parent issue: #401 (P2 item)

Several provider clients return `ujson.Null` as a default when parsing tool-call arguments fails. This mixes Scala code with null-like semantics. The fix is to normalize these to `Option`-based or empty-object patterns right at the parsing boundary.

## What to do

Replace `ujson.Null` return values with safer patterns in argument parsing across these files:

| File | Location | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `OpenAIClient.scala` | `parseStreamingArguments` (~line 453) | `ujson.Null` default on parse failure |
| `OpenAIClient.scala` | `extractToolCalls` (~line 550) | `ujson.Null` default on parse failure |
| `OpenRouterClient.scala` | ~line 210 | Same pattern |
| `DeepSeekClient.scala` | ~line 216 | Same pattern |
| `ZaiClient.scala` | ~line 224 | Same pattern |
| `StreamingResponseHandler.scala` | ~line 177 | Same pattern |

### Recommended approach

[HIDDEN]
- Or normalize to `Option[ujson.Value]` if the API contract allows
- Some code already uses `.strOpt`/`.flatMap` (good) â follow that pattern

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No `ujson.Null` used as default for argument parsing in provider clients
- [ ] Downstream code handles the new pattern correctly
- [ ] Existing tests pass (`sbt +test`)
- [ ] Stream handling reads as Option-based logic rather than null-based logic

### Additional contract requirements

# Tool-call argument normalization

At the named streaming argument-parsing boundaries, an absent or empty argument payload is exposed as an empty JSON object. Valid non-empty JSON payloads are exposed as their parsed JSON values. A malformed non-empty payload, including whitespace-only text, is preserved verbatim as a JSON string during streaming.
At non-streaming OpenAI tool-call extraction, malformed non-empty argument payloads do not produce a tool call. Empty and absent arguments are exposed as an empty JSON object. Streaming accumulation and finalization retain empty-object normalization, and an empty placeholder does not corrupt later argument fragments.

+package org.llm4s.llmconnect.streaming

+
+final class OpenAIStreamingHandlerSpec extends AnyFlatSpec with Matchers {
+
+  "OpenAIStreamingHandler" should "treat empty tool-call arguments as empty object" in {
+    val handler = new OpenAIStreamingHandler()
+
+    val json = ujson.Obj(
+      "id" -> "chatcmpl-1",
+      "choices" -> ujson.Arr(
+        ujson.Obj(
+          "delta" -> ujson.Obj(
+            "tool_calls" -> ujson.Arr(
+              ujson.Obj(
+                "id"   -> "call-1",
+                "type" -> "function",
+                "function" -> ujson.Obj(
+                  "name"      -> "test",
+                  "arguments" -> ""
+                )
+              )
+            )
+          )
+        )
+      )
+    )
+
+    val chunk = s"data: ${ujson.write(json)}\n\n"
+
+    val result = handler.processChunk(chunk)
+
+    val streamed = result.getOrElse(fail("Expected Right but got Left"))
+    streamed match {
+      case Some(chunk) =>
+        chunk.toolCall match {
+          case Some(tc) => tc.arguments shouldBe ujson.Obj()
+          case None     => fail("Expected toolCall to be defined")
+        }
+      case None => fail("Expected Some(StreamedChunk) but got None")
+    }
+  }
+
+  it should "preserve invalid tool-call arguments as raw string" in {
+    val handler = new OpenAIStreamingHandler()
+
+    val json = ujson.Obj(
+      "id" -> "chatcmpl-1",
+      "choices" -> ujson.Arr(
+        ujson.Obj(
+          "delta" -> ujson.Obj(
+            "tool_calls" -> ujson.Arr(
+              ujson.Obj(
+                "id"   -> "call-1",
+                "type" -> "function",
+                "function" -> ujson.Obj(
+                  "name"      -> "test",
+                  "arguments" -> "{not json"
+                )
+              )
+            )
+          )
+        )
+      )
+    )
+
+    val chunk = s"data: ${ujson.write(json)}\n\n"
+
+    val result = handler.processChunk(chunk)
+
+    val streamed = result.getOrElse(fail("Expected Right but got Left"))
+    streamed match {
+      case Some(chunk) =>
+        chunk.toolCall match {
+          case Some(tc) => tc.arguments shouldBe ujson.Str("{not json")
+          case None     => fail("Expected toolCall to be defined")
+        }
+      case None => fail("Expected Some(StreamedChunk) but got None")
+    }
+  }
+
+  it should "ignore an empty argument object before later streamed argument fragments" in {
+    val accumulator = StreamingAccumulator.create()
+
+    accumulator.addChunk(StreamedChunk("msg-1", None, Some(ToolCall("call-1", "test", ujson.Obj())), None))
+    accumulator.addChunk(
+      StreamedChunk("msg-1", None, Some(ToolCall("call-1", "test", ujson.Str("{\"x\":1}"))), None)
+    )
+
+    val toolCalls = accumulator.getCurrentToolCalls
+    toolCalls should have size 1
+    toolCalls.head.arguments shouldBe ujson.Obj("x" -> 1)

+package org.llm4s.llmconnect.testsupport
+
+import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
+
+import java.net.InetSocketAddress
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+
+/** Test-only helper: serves a fixed SSE payload for chat completion streaming tests. */
+final class LocalSseServer(payload: String) extends AutoCloseable {
+  private val server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress("localhost", 0), 0)
+  server.createContext(
+    "/chat/completions",
+    exchange => {
+      val bytes = payload.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+      exchange.getResponseHeaders.add("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
+      exchange.sendResponseHeaders(200, bytes.length)
+      val os = exchange.getResponseBody
+      os.write(bytes)
+      os.close()
+    }
+  )
+  server.start()
+
+  val baseUrl: String = s"http://localhost:${server.getAddress.getPort}"
+
+  override def close(): Unit = server.stop(0)
+}
+
+object LocalSseServer {
+  def withServer(payload: String)(test: String => Unit): Unit =
+    scala.util.Using.resource(new LocalSseServer(payload))(server => test(server.baseUrl))
+}

A copula's default sampling extension point is an in-place matrix sampler. For
a dimensionality-`d` copula and a writable `d × n` `AbstractMatrix` whose
element type is a subtype of `Real`, in-place matrix sampling fills each column
with one sample and returns the identical matrix object. The contract applies
to every column count `n`, including an empty `d × 0` buffer. The contract
applies to non-dense buffers such as views and to real element types such as
`Float32`; storage outside a supplied view must remain untouched. Calling
in-place matrix sampling with a buffer whose first dimension differs from `d`
must raise an error, whatever its column count.

The generic in-place vector sampling path validates that the destination has
length `d`, reshapes that same storage as a `d × 1` matrix, delegates to the
matrix sampling extension point, and returns the original vector. A concrete
copula may retain its own vector specialization, but no vector specialization
is required for a copula that implements the matrix extension point.

These behaviors are observable through the public sampling API for every
built-in copula family — including Archimedean, nested Archimedean, bivariate
Archimax, elliptical, extreme-value, and the miscellaneous copula families,
as well as copulas obtained by selecting a subset of dimensions or by
conditioning. In-place vector and matrix sampling through a multivariate
distribution that couples a copula with marginal distributions follows the
same buffer, identity-return, and dimension-rejection behavior.

+using Copulas, Distributions, Random, StableRNGs, Test

+

+    ::Distributions.AbstractRNG,

+    A::AbstractMatrix{T},
+) where {T<:Real}

+    A[1, :] .= T(0.25)
+    A[2, :] .= T(0.75)
+    return A
+end
+
+# A test-only copula with only a lower-dimensional sampler defined. One marked
+# coordinate detects whether samples produced for one buffer can be silently
+# reused to fill a later buffer of a different first dimension.
+struct MarkedVectorTestCopula <: Copulas.Copula{2} end
+
+function Distributions._rand!(
+    ::Distributions.AbstractRNG,
+    ::MarkedVectorTestCopula,
+    x::AbstractVector{T},
+) where {T<:Real}

+end

+
+        A = zeros(Float32, 2, 3)

+        end
+        @test result === x

+        @test_throws Exception rand!(StableRNG(11), C, zeros(Float32, 3))
+        @test_throws Exception rand!(StableRNG(12), C, zeros(Float32, 3, 2))

+            BernsteinCopula(ClaytonCopula(3, 3.3); m = 5),

problem_statement:
Simple gated unit (`SGUCell`) and Deep simple gated unit (`DSGUCell`)
## Paper

https://proceedings.mlr.press/v63/gao30.pdf

## Equations

```math
\begin{align}
x_g &= W_{xh} x_t + b_g \\
z_g &= \sigma_1\!\left(W_{zzh}\left(x_g \cdot h(t-1)\right)\right) \\
z_{\text{out}} &= \sigma_2\!\left(z_g \cdot h(t-1)\right) \\
z_t &= \sigma_3\!\left(W_{xz} x_t + b_z + W_{hz} h(t-1)\right) \\
h(t) &= \left(1 - z_t\right) h(t-1) + z_t \cdot z_{\text{out}}
\end{align}
```

```math
\begin{align}
x_g &= W_{xh} x_t + b_g \\
z_g &= \sigma_1\!\left(W_{zxh}\left(x_g \cdot h(t-1)\right)\right) \\
z_{\text{out}} &= \sigma_2\!\left(W_{go}\left(z_g \cdot h(t-1)\right)\right) \\
z_t &= \sigma_3\!\left(W_{xz} x_t + b_z + W_{hz} h(t-1)\right) \\
h(t) &= \left(1 - z_t\right) h(t-1) + z_t \cdot z_{\text{out}}
\end{align}
```

## Official implementation

none

### Additional contract requirements

Both the `DSGUCell` recurrent cell and the `DSGU` sequence layer must be provided and exported.

- `DSGUCell(input_size => hidden_size; init_kernel = glorot_uniform, init_recurrent_kernel = glorot_uniform, bias = true, recurrent_bias = true, integration_mode = :addition, independent_recurrence = false)`
  constructs a cell exposing the fields `weight_ih` of size `(2 * hidden_size, input_size)`, `weight_hh` of size `(2 * hidden_size, hidden_size)` (a vector of length `2 * hidden_size` when `independent_recurrence = true`), `weight_out` of size `(hidden_size, hidden_size)`, `bias_ih` of length `2 * hidden_size`, and `bias_hh` of length `2 * hidden_size`. All weight fields are trainable parameters, and each bias field is trainable only when its corresponding keyword is `true`.
- The supplied weight initializers determine the values of `weight_ih`, `weight_hh`, and `weight_out` (so constant initializers make those fields exactly that constant).
- Calling the cell on an input of size `input_size` (or `input_size x batch_size`) and optionally a state of size `hidden_size` (or `hidden_size x batch_size`) returns a tuple of two equal elements, the updated state, of size `hidden_size` (or `hidden_size x batch_size`). When the state is not given it defaults to the zero state produced by `Flux.initialstates`, so `cell(inp)` equals `cell(inp, zeros(hidden_size))`, while a nonzero explicit state changes the result.
- The state update splits `weight_ih`, `bias_ih`, `weight_hh`, and `bias_hh` into an upper half (indices `1:hidden_size`) and a lower half (indices `hidden_size+1:2*hidden_size`) along the gate dimension and follows the documented gated equations:
  - `x_g = weight_ih[upper half] * x + bias_ih[upper half]`;
  - `z_g = tanh(weight_hh[upper half] * (x_g .∘ state) + bias_hh[upper half])`;
  - `z_out = sigmoid(weight_out * (z_g .∘ state))` (no bias is used in this projection);
  - `z_t = hardsigmoid(integration_mode(weight_ih[lower half] * x + bias_ih[lower half], weight_hh[lower half] * state + bias_hh[lower half]))`, where the two projections are combined by elementwise addition for `integration_mode = :addition` and by elementwise multiplication for `integration_mode = :multiplicative_integration`;
  - `new_state = (1 .- z_t) .∘ state .+ z_t .∘ z_out`.
  Here `hardsigmoid(v) = clamp(v / 6 + 1 / 2, 0, 1)`, elementwise per entry. Changing either bias alone must change the result under both integration modes. With all-zero weights, disabled biases, a nonzero hidden state, and any input, the updated state is exactly `0.75` times the previous state.
- `DSGU(input_size => hidden_size; return_state = false, kwargs...)` wraps a `DSGUCell` (accessible as the layer's `cell` field) and forwards all cell keyword arguments, including `bias`, `recurrent_bias`, both initializers, `integration_mode`, and `independent_recurrence`. Called on a sequence of size `input_size x len [x batch_size]`, optionally with an explicit initial state of size `hidden_size` that is applied to every batch element, it returns the hidden states of size `hidden_size x len [x batch_size]`; when `return_state = true` it returns a tuple of those hidden states and the last state of the iteration, which equals the last time step of the returned states.
