--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/unit_test_properties.jl
@@ -0,0 +1,229 @@
+# Physics property tests: invariants that must hold over the WHOLE space of
+# gases this package can construct — not at hand-picked points, and not by
+# agreement with the legacy implementation (see the migration tests for
+# that). Randomized with a fixed seed and deliberately small N: each @test
+# here is a distinct physical claim, not a coverage statistic.
+using Random
+using ForwardDiff
+
+@testset "physics properties (randomized, seeded)" begin
+
+    rng = Xoshiro(20260612)
+    uni(a, b) = a + (b - a) * rand(rng) #uniform random between a and b
+
+    air = FrozenGas(DryAir)
+    sysCH4 = Vitiator("CH4", DryAir)
+    sysJet = Vitiator("Jet-A(g)", DryAir)
+    vit = IdealGasThermo.vitiated_species("CH4", "Air", 0.04)
+
+    # a small pool of randomly-parameterized gases spanning what the
+    # constructors can produce
+    gas_pool() = [
+        air,
+        products(sysCH4, uni(0.005, 0.05)),
+        products(sysJet, uni(0.005, 0.045)),
+        mix(FrozenGas(DryAir), FrozenGas(vit), uni(0.1, 10.0)),
+        humid_air(SH = uni(0.001, 0.05)),
+    ]
+
+    @testset "positivity, monotonicity, gamma bounds (random gases)" begin
+        Tgrid = range(220.0, 2350.0; length = 40)
+        for gas in gas_pool()
+            hs = [IdealGasThermo.h(gas, T) for T in Tgrid]
+            ss = [IdealGasThermo.s0(gas, T) for T in Tgrid]
+            @test all(IdealGasThermo.cp(gas, T) > 0 for T in Tgrid)
+            @test all(diff(hs) .> 0)  # dh/dT = cp > 0 ⟹ strictly increasing
+            @test all(diff(ss) .> 0)  # ds0/dT = cp/T > 0
+            @test all(1.0 < IdealGasThermo.gamma(gas, T) < 1.7 for T in Tgrid)
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "second law: irreversible round trip generates entropy" begin
+        for _ = 1:5
+            st = GasState(air, uni(250.0, 800.0), 1.0e5)
+            PR, ηp = uni(2.0, 30.0), uni(0.85, 0.95)
+            rt = expand(compress(st, PR; ηp = ηp), PR; ηp = ηp)
+            @test rt.P ≈ st.P rtol = 1e-12      # pressure round trip exact
+            @test rt.T > st.T                   # lost work shows up as heat
+            @test entropy(rt) > entropy(st)     # ΔS > 0, strictly
+        end
+        # the reversible limit recovers the identity
+        st = GasState(air, 400.0, 1.0e5)
+        rt = expand(compress(st, 12.0), 12.0)
+        @test rt.T ≈ st.T rtol = 1e-9
+    end
+
+    @testset "process round trips (reversible limits)" begin
+        for _ = 1:3
+            st = GasState(air, uni(300.0, 900.0), uni(0.5e5, 5.0e5))
+            q = uni(1.0e4, 5.0e5)
+            back = add_heat(add_heat(st, q), -q)
+            @test back.T ≈ st.T rtol = 1e-9
+            @test back.P == st.P                # constant-P by construction
+            w = uni(1.0e4, 3.0e5)
+            rt = extract_work(add_work(st, w), w) # ηp = 1: thermodynamically reversible
+            @test rt.T ≈ st.T rtol = 1e-9
+            @test rt.P ≈ st.P rtol = 1e-9
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "entropy pressure-scaling: s(T, kP) = s(T, P) - R ln k" begin
+        for _ = 1:3
+            st = GasState(air, uni(250.0, 1800.0), uni(0.2e5, 2.0e5))
+            k = uni(0.1, 40.0)
+            @test entropy(GasState(air, st.T, k * st.P)) ≈
+                  entropy(st) - IdealGasThermo.R(air) * log(k) rtol = 1e-12
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "combustion: mass conservation and heat release vs LHV" begin
+        for (fuel, sys, FARmax) in (("CH4", sysCH4, 0.05), ("Jet-A(g)", sysJet, 0.045))
+            fsp = species_in_spdict(fuel)
+            ΣΔX = sum(IdealGasThermo.reaction_change_molar_fraction(fuel))
+            for _ = 1:3
+                f = uni(0.005, FARmax)
+                gp = products(sys, f)
+                # mass conservation through the mole-fraction algebra:
+                # (1 + molFAR·ΣΔX)·MW_products = MW_ox + molFAR·MW_fuel
+                molFAR = f * DryAir.MW / fsp.MW
+                @test (1 + molFAR * ΣΔX) * gp.MW ≈
+                      DryAir.MW + molFAR * fsp.MW rtol = 1e-12
+            end
+            # heat release at 298.15 K equals f·LHV — ties the products
+            # composition algebra, the formation-inclusive datum (b₁
+            # coefficients), and the independent Hf-header-based LHV()
+            # computation together
+            f = 0.03
+            fgas = FrozenGas(fsp)
+            release =
+                -(
+                    (1 + f) * IdealGasThermo.h(products(sys, f), 298.15) -
+                    IdealGasThermo.h(air, 298.15) - f * IdealGasThermo.h(fgas, 298.15)
+                )
+            @test release ≈ f * IdealGasThermo.LHV(fsp) rtol = 1e-5
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "mixing algebra: symmetry and self-identity" begin
+        gA = FrozenGas(DryAir)
+        gB = FrozenGas(vit)
+        for _ = 1:4
+            m = uni(0.1, 10.0)
+            g1 = mix(gA, gB, m)      # m kg of vit per kg of air
+            g2 = mix(gB, gA, 1 / m)  # the same mixture, described from the other side
+            @test g1.MW ≈ g2.MW rtol = 1e-12
+            for T in (300.0, 1600.0)
+                @test IdealGasThermo.cp(g1, T) ≈ IdealGasThermo.cp(g2, T) rtol = 1e-12
+                @test IdealGasThermo.h(g1, T) ≈ IdealGasThermo.h(g2, T) rtol = 1e-12
+                @test IdealGasThermo.s0(g1, T) ≈ IdealGasThermo.s0(g2, T) rtol = 1e-12
+            end
+        end
+        # mixing a gas with itself is the identity, at any ratio
+        for m in (0.0, uni(0.1, 10.0), 1.0e6)
+            g = mix(gA, gA, m)
+            @test IdealGasThermo.cp(g, 600.0) ≈ IdealGasThermo.cp(air, 600.0) rtol = 1e-12
+            @test IdealGasThermo.s0(g, 600.0) ≈ IdealGasThermo.s0(air, 600.0) rtol = 1e-12
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "entropy of mixing: blend s0 vs a hand-written −R·Σ X·ln X" begin
+        # A sign flip in the entropy-of-mixing fold (species.jl: alow[end] -=
+        # Δs_mix) is invisible to every pure-species check (X·ln X = 0 at X = 1)
+        # and to the legacy-agreement tests (they share the same fold). Pin it
+        # directly: the molar s0 of a blend must equal Σ Xᵢ·s0ᵢ(T) − R·Σ Xᵢ·ln Xᵢ,
+        # with the mixing term written out HERE, not taken from
+        # generate_composite_species. A flipped sign would shift this by
+        # 2R·|Σ X ln X| (~11.5 J/mol/K for a 50/50 blend). (test audit 2026-06-17)
+        R = IdealGasThermo.Runiv
+        for X in ([("N2", 0.5), ("O2", 0.5)],
+                  [("N2", 0.78), ("O2", 0.21), ("CO2", 0.01)])
+            xs = last.(X)
+            sps = [species_in_spdict(first(p)) for p in X]
+            comps = [FrozenGas(sp) for sp in sps]
+            blend = FrozenGas(IdealGasThermo.Xidict2Array(Dict(X)))
+            Δs_mix = sum(x * log(x) for x in xs)
+            for T in (300.0, 1000.0, 2200.0)
+                s0_blend = IdealGasThermo.s0(blend, T) * blend.MW / 1000   # molar
+                expected = sum(x * IdealGasThermo.s0(c, T) * sp.MW / 1000
+                               for (x, c, sp) in zip(xs, comps, sps)) - R * Δs_mix
+                @test s0_blend ≈ expected rtol = 1e-10
+            end
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "coefficient self-consistency: s0 and h against ∫cp" begin
+        # metamorphic check independent of any reference implementation:
+        # the h and s0 polynomials must be the integrals of the cp
+        # polynomial (composite Simpson, fine enough that quadrature error
+        # is far below the tolerance; one interval straddles the 1000 K
+        # coefficient breakpoint by construction)
+        simpson(f, a, b, n) =
+            (b - a) / (3n) * sum(
+                (i == 0 || i == n ? 1 : iseven(i) ? 2 : 4) * f(a + (b - a) * i / n)
+                for i = 0:n
+            )
+        cases = [(air, 300.0, 800.0), (products(sysJet, 0.03), 700.0, 1500.0)]
+        push!(cases, (gas_pool()[end], uni(250.0, 900.0), uni(1100.0, 2200.0)))
+        for (gas, T1, T2) in cases
+            ∫cp = simpson(T -> IdealGasThermo.cp(gas, T), T1, T2, 2048)
+            ∫cpT = simpson(T -> IdealGasThermo.cp(gas, T) / T, T1, T2, 2048)
+            @test IdealGasThermo.h(gas, T2) - IdealGasThermo.h(gas, T1) ≈ ∫cp rtol = 1e-8
+            @test IdealGasThermo.s0(gas, T2) - IdealGasThermo.s0(gas, T1) ≈ ∫cpT rtol = 1e-8
+        end
+    end
+
+    @testset "error paths: pathological inputs fail loudly, not silently" begin
+        # inversion driven into negative-temperature territory: the Newton
+        # iterate hits log(T ≤ 0)
+        @test_throws DomainError T_from_h(air, -1.0e10)
+        # inversion target beyond any representable temperature: the bounded
+        # Newton loop exhausts NEWTON_MAXITER and raises (the non-convergence
+        # branch is live code, not decoration)
+        @test_throws ErrorException T_from_h(air, 1.0e12)
+        # beyond-stoichiometric FAR would need negative O2 — errors loudly
+        # rather than returning an unphysical composition
+        @test_throws DomainError products(sysCH4, 0.5)
+    end
+
+    @testset "Dual-carrying gas: AD inversions match finite differences" begin
+        # products(sys, FAR::Dual) yields a FrozenGas{<:Dual} whose coefficients
+        # carry the FAR-tangent, so inverting through it exercises the full
+        # three-term IFT rule (the "composition moves" term). The invariant that
+        # actually defines the rule's correctness — independent of fuel, oxidizer
+        # composition, and the underlying NASA-9 data — is AD == central FD. (A
+        # single pinned physics value like dT4/dFAR would instead track
+        # thermo.inp and the air composition, not the rule.) We also assert the
+        # result is a real number, not the nested-Dual tree the constant-
+        # substance rule produced for a Dual-carrying gas.
+        D = ForwardDiff.derivative
+        δ = 1e-6
+        fdcheck(f, x) = (f(x + δ) - f(x - δ)) / (2δ)
+        for fuel in ["CH4", "H2", "Jet-A(g)"]   # distinct C/H/O ⟹ distinct ∂X/∂FAR
+            sys = Vitiator(fuel, DryAir)
+            fsp = species_in_spdict(fuel)
+            hF = 1000 * fsp.Hf / fsp.MW
+            # Stay sub-stoichiometric for the leanest-ceiling fuel in the pool
+            # (H2 reaches stoichiometric at FAR ≈ 0.029; beyond it `products`
+            # correctly throws on negative O₂).
+            FAR0 = uni(0.005, 0.02)
+
+            # (1) burner energy balance: Dual gas + Dual target
+            hA = IdealGasThermo.h(air, uni(500.0, 900.0))
+            T4of(far) = T_from_h(products(sys, far), (hA + far * hF) / (1 + far))
+            d1 = D(T4of, FAR0)
+            @test d1 isa Real                       # not a nested Dual
+            @test d1 ≈ fdcheck(T4of, FAR0) rtol = 1e-6
+
+            # (2) Dual gas + plain-Float target: invert a moving gas to fixed h
+            hfix = IdealGasThermo.h(products(sys, FAR0), uni(1200.0, 1900.0))
+            Tfix(far) = T_from_h(products(sys, far), hfix)
+            @test D(Tfix, FAR0) ≈ fdcheck(Tfix, FAR0) rtol = 1e-6
+
+            # (3) Dual gas through the isentropic inversion
+            T1, PR = uni(1100.0, 1500.0), uni(2.0, 10.0)
+            Tisen(far) = IdealGasThermo._T_polytropic(products(sys, far), T1, PR)
+            @test D(Tisen, FAR0) ≈ fdcheck(Tisen, FAR0) rtol = 1e-6
+        end
+    end
+
+end

problem_statement:
Mark  package symbols internal or gate behind @KsrpcInternal opt-in before 1.0.0
Audit from #4 found a large number of symbols living in `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.*.internal` packages that are nonetheless `public` and therefore frozen by BCV once 1.0.0 ships.

## Affected modules / symbols (non-exhaustive)

### ksrpc-core
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.HostSerializedChannelImpl` (+ all its overrides)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.MultiChannel`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.SubserviceChannel`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.ClientChannelContext` (+ `Key`)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.HostChannelContext` (+ `Key`)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.HostSerializedServiceImplKt.getAsClient`

### ksrpc-jsonrpc
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcChannel` (interface)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcError` (+ constants, serializer, Companion)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcRequest` (+ serializer)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcResponse` (+ serializer)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcSerializedChannel`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcServiceWrapper`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcTransformer` + `JsonRpcTransformerKt.jsonHeader/jsonLine`, `DEFAULT_CONTENT_TYPE`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.jsonrpc.internal.JsonRpcWriterBase`

### ksrpc-packets
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.packets.internal.Packet` (+ both constructors + component1..5 + serializer)
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.packets.internal.PacketChannelBase`
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.packets.internal.ConstantsKt.CONTENT_LENGTH`, `CONTENT_TYPE`

### ksrpc-ktor-websocket-shared
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.ktor.websocket.internal.WebsocketPacketChannel`

### ksrpc-sockets
- `com.monkopedia.ksrpc.sockets.internal.PacketUtilsKt.appendLine`, `readFields`, `swallow`

## Why this matters

BCV will lock every one of these names, positional argument orders, and serializer shapes into the 1.0 contract. The `.internal` naming strongly implies they were not meant as user-facing API, but they're currently indistinguishable from the real API to consumers and to BCV.

## Proposed fix

Two viable paths (can be combined):

1. Where the symbol is truly a module-private implementation detail, add the `internal` visibility modifier. BCV drops internal symbols from the dump, so they stop appearing in `*.api` / `*.klib.api` files.
2. Where the symbol genuinely has to be visible across modules (e.g. `PacketChannelBase` subclassed by `WebsocketPacketChannel` and `JniConnection`, `Packet` used as a cross-module data carrier, `JsonRpcChannel` used cross-module), introduce a module-level opt-in annotation, e.g.:

   ```kotlin
   @RequiresOptIn(level = RequiresOptIn.Level.ERROR, message = "This is a ksrpc implementation detail and may change at any time.")
   @Target(AnnotationTarget.CLASS, AnnotationTarget.FUNCTION, AnnotationTarget.PROPERTY, AnnotationTarget.FILE)
   annotation class KsrpcInternal
   ```

   Apply it to every symbol that has to stay public-for-linkage-but-not-public-API. That way the BCV dump keeps them recorded (so genuinely accidental breakage is still caught) but consumers have to opt in, and we reserve the right to break them behind the opt-in in minor releases.

Either approach needs to happen before the 1.0.0 tag â after, these become forever-supported API.

Refs #4

### Additional contract requirements

The implementation helpers identified by the internal-API audit are not supported consumer API. Each such declaration must either have Kotlin `internal` visibility or, if it remains link-visible, require the library's `KsrpcInternal` opt-in. This applies across the core, JSON-RPC, packets, websocket transport, and socket transport modules, including generated serializers, companions, accessors, and overrides exposed through those helpers.

`ServiceExecutor` remains required compiler-service plumbing. It may have Kotlin `internal` visibility in either package, or it may remain link-visible in either package only when access requires the `KsrpcInternal` opt-in. Moving it to an `.internal` package is neither required nor sufficient by itself. Its interface role and suspend invocation contract must remain available to generated service implementations.

### ksrpc-packets

### ksrpc-sockets

## Why this matters

BCV will lock every one of these names, positional argument orders, and serializer shapes into the 1.0 contract. The `.internal` naming strongly implies they were not meant as user-facing API, but they're currently indistinguishable from the real API to consumers and to BCV.

## Proposed fix

Two viable paths (can be combined):

1. Where the symbol is truly a module-private implementation detail, add the `internal` visibility modifier. BCV drops internal symbols from the dump, so they stop appearing in `*.api` / `*.klib.api` files.
2. Where the symbol genuinely has to be visible across modules (e.g. `PacketChannelBase` subclassed by `WebsocketPacketChannel` and `JniConnection`, `Packet` used as a cross-module data carrier, `JsonRpcChannel` used cross-module), introduce a module-level opt-in annotation, e.g.:

   ```kotlin
   @RequiresOptIn(level = RequiresOptIn.Level.ERROR, message = "This is a ksrpc implementation detail and may change at any time.")
   @Target(AnnotationTarget.CLASS, AnnotationTarget.FUNCTION, AnnotationTarget.PROPERTY, AnnotationTarget.FILE)
   annotation class KsrpcInternal
   ```

   Apply it to every symbol that has to stay public-for-linkage-but-not-public-API. That way the BCV dump keeps them recorded (so genuinely accidental breakage is still caught) but consumers have to opt in, and we reserve the right to break them behind the opt-in in minor releases.

Either approach needs to happen before the 1.0.0 tag â after, these become forever-supported API.

Refs #4
contract_addendum:
The implementation helpers identified by the internal-API audit are not supported consumer API. Each such declaration must either have Kotlin `internal` visibility or, if it remains link-visible, require the library's `KsrpcInternal` opt-in. This applies across the core, JSON-RPC, packets, websocket transport, and socket transport modules, including generated serializers, companions, accessors, and overrides exposed through those helpers.

`ServiceExecutor` remains required compiler-service plumbing. It may have Kotlin `internal` visibility in either package, or it may remain link-visible in either package only when access requires the `KsrpcInternal` opt-in. Moving it to an `.internal` package is neither required nor sufficient by itself. Its interface role and suspend invocation contract must remain available to generated service implementations.

+        } catch (_: ClassNotFoundException) {

+    )
+    return owner.getMethod("randomUuid").invoke(null) as String
+}
+
+private val prefixOwner: Class<*>
+    get() = firstClass(
+        "com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.ErrorPrefixesKt",
+        "com.monkopedia.ksrpc.RpcChannelKt"
+    )
+
+internal actual val compatibilityErrorPrefix: String
+    get() = prefixOwner.getField("ERROR_PREFIX").get(null) as String
+
+internal actual val compatibilityEndpointNotFoundPrefix: String
+    get() = prefixOwner.getField("ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND_PREFIX").get(null) as String
+
+@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+internal actual fun <S : RpcService, I, O> compatibilityRpcMethod(
+    endpoint: String,
+    inputTransform: Transformer<I>,
+    outputTransform: Transformer<O>,
+    metadata: List<MethodMetadata>
+): RpcMethod<S, I, O> {
+    val executorType = firstClass(
+        "com.monkopedia.ksrpc.internal.ServiceExecutor",
+        "com.monkopedia.ksrpc.ServiceExecutor"
+    )
+    val executor = Proxy.newProxyInstance(
+        executorType.classLoader,
+        arrayOf(executorType)
+    ) { _, method, _ ->
+        when (method.name) {
+            "toString" -> "test-service-executor"
+            "hashCode" -> 0
+            "equals" -> false
+            else -> Unit
+        }
+    }
+    val constructor = RpcMethod::class.java.constructors.single { it.parameterCount == 5 }
+    return constructor.newInstance(
+        endpoint,
+        inputTransform,
+        outputTransform,
+        executor,
+        metadata
+    ) as RpcMethod<S, I, O>
+}

problem_statement:
Allow type and constant definitions inside state machines
For example, one could define a type _T_ inside a state machine and use it in the signals of _T_.

- [x] Spec
- [x] Syntax
- [x] Semantics
- [x] Code gen
- [x] FppTest
- [x] User's Guide

### Additional contract requirements

The hidden evaluation runs the Scala test suite `fpp.compiler.test.ParserSpec`, selecting the
tests whose names contain `state machine M`. It adds test cases to the existing test source
`compiler/lib/src/test/scala/syntax/Parser.scala` (it changes only tests). The following compiler
behaviors are required:

1. **Parsing a state machine with nested definitions.** `Parser.defStateMachine` must parse a
   state machine whose body contains constant, abstract type, alias type, array, struct, and
   enum definitions, alongside action, signal, guard, initial-transition, state, and
   `on`-transition members.

2. **Local definitions are in scope inside the state machine body.** Within a state machine
   body, members must be able to reference definitions declared in that same body by their
   unqualified names, including: an abstract type used as the type of an action, signal, or
   guard; an alias type used as a member type; an array whose size is a locally defined
   constant; and a struct used as a member type. Both parsing and full semantic analysis of
   such a translation unit must succeed.

3. **Every supported category of local definition analyzes successfully.** A single state
   machine that defines a constant, an abstract type, an alias type, an array, a struct, and
   an enum, with other members referencing those local definitions, must pass full semantic
   analysis without error.

4. **Undefined references are rejected (local-scope boundary).** Full semantic analysis must
   report an error when a state machine member's type refers to a name that is not defined,
   confirming that the state machine introduces its own scope rather than accepting arbitrary
   names.

5. **FPP constants C++ output includes state-machine-local constants.** A constant declared in
   a state machine body must be registered in the state machine scope for the FPP constants
   output and must carry the generated name prefixed with the enclosing state machine name
   (for example, a constant `C` in state machine `M` is emitted as `M_C`).

6. **State machine C++ base class output uses state-machine-local types.** The generated C++
   base class for a state machine must reference state-machine-local definitions: the
   generated action function signature must use a state-machine-local abstract type (for
   example, an action taking a value of type `M_T&`), and the generated base class must
   include the generated C++ headers for state-machine-local alias type, array, struct, and
   enum definitions (including the enclosing state machine name as a prefix).

problem_statement:
check: totalDiagnostics contradicts zero errorCount/warningCount and the payload never explains the gap
## Field evidence

Reported three times in one multi-agent session (#100, comments of 2026-08-16, fslangmcp 0.13.1, reproduced verbatim in separate runs):

- `check(scope=project)` returned `errorCount: 0`, `warningCount: 0`, `diagnosticsFileCount: 0`, empty `diagnostics` — but `totalDiagnostics: 7` (later runs: 4, then 3, once alongside `verdict: clean, escalated: fcs-reanalyze, groundTruth: true`).
- Agents read the unexplained counter as "three hidden findings" and lost time hunting for them. Quote: "Drop the field or explain what it counts."

## Root cause (confirmed at HEAD)

The three numbers are computed from different filters and the payload never states the relationship:

- `errorCount`/`warningCount` — errors+warnings only (`countDiagnosticsBySeverity`, `FcsBridge.fs:2997`).
- `diagnostics`/`files` — filtered by the severity floor (`surfaceFcs`, `FcsBridge.fs:6331`), then capped at 50 (`diagnosticsCap`, `FcsBridge.fs:6302`).
- `totalDiagnostics` — the FULL diagnostic set across ALL severities, including Info/Hidden (call sites `FcsBridge.fs:6447`, `6795`, `~7150-7169`; FSAC fast path counts the full snapshot at `6698-6717`; snippet paths emit it at `3304`, `3398`).

So any project with info/hint-level diagnostics yields `totalDiagnostics > errorCount + warningCount` with nothing in the payload explaining the gap. This was a deliberate fix for #133 (an info-only snapshot used to show diagnostics with `totalDiagnostics: 0`) — the count is correct; the payload is just silent about what it counts.

## Required change (additive only, no field removals or renames)

1. Add `infoCount: int` — full-set tally of severity Info + Hidden diagnostics — to **every** payload that emits `totalDiagnostics` (the shared `build` at `FcsBridge.fs:6285` covers the check scopes; audit the snippet emitters at 3304/3398 and any other `totalDiagnostics` emitter and give them the same field). Invariant: `totalDiagnostics = errorCount + warningCount + infoCount` on every path.
2. Add `belowSeverityFloorCount: int` — diagnostics counted in `totalDiagnostics` but excluded from the `diagnostics` array by the severity floor. This counts ONLY severity-floor exclusions; the 50-item cap is already covered by `diagnosticsTruncated` and must not leak into this number.
3. When `belowSeverityFloorCount > 0`, add `diagnosticsNote: string`: `"<N> diagnostic(s) below the current severity floor are counted in totalDiagnostics but not listed; pass severity=\"all\" to list them."` Emit `null` (or omit) when 0.
4. Update the `check` tool description in `Program.fs` and the check section of `docs/tools-detailed.md` to state the identity in one sentence.

## Tests (CheckTests.fs)

- Reproduce the field shape: a check whose full set contains info/hint diagnostics and zero errors/warnings must now return `infoCount > 0`, matching `belowSeverityFloorCount`, and the note. Prefer factoring the count computation into a pure function if that is what it takes to test the identity without a live FCS run — but at least one integration-level test must go through a real check path.
- Identity test across paths: trusted FCS scope and FSAC fast path both satisfy `totalDiagnostics = errorCount + warningCount + infoCount`.
- Regression: `severity="all"` keeps `belowSeverityFloorCount = 0` and no note.

## Acceptance

- The exact field scenario (zero counts + nonzero totalDiagnostics) is covered by a test asserting the new fields explain the gap.
- All existing tests pass; no existing response field changed shape.

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 774a96c..7151cf8 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -10,6 +10,19 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- `check`'s `totalDiagnostics` now explains itself instead of silently disagreeing with
+  `errorCount + warningCount` (#190). `totalDiagnostics` counts the FULL diagnostic set across
+  every severity (including Info/Hidden) — a deliberate #133 fix — but nothing in the payload said
+  so, and agents read a nonzero `totalDiagnostics` alongside `errorCount: 0, warningCount: 0` as
+  hidden findings and burned time hunting for them. Two new fields close the identity:
+  `infoCount` (so `totalDiagnostics = errorCount + warningCount + infoCount`, always) and
+  `belowSeverityFloorCount` (how many of those full-set diagnostics the `severity` floor excluded
+  from the `diagnostics` array — never the 50-item cap, which stays `diagnosticsTruncated`'s job),
+  plus a `diagnosticsNote` pointing at `severity="all"` when the gap is nonzero. Also fixes
+  `fcs_check_file`'s internal `errorCount` (an internal `FcsBridge` member since the 0.11.0 tool
+  consolidation, not a registered tool — no consumer could have observed this), which was silently
+  always `0`: it read the JSON `severity` field as an int, but that field is serialized as text
+  (`"Error"`) — the read never matched.
 - `fcs_nuget_types` / `fcs_nuget_members` now resolve a NuGet **package id** whose
   assembly is named something else. Both matched the assembly `SimpleName` alone, so
   `Microsoft.Orleans.Core.Abstractions` (which ships `Orleans.Core.Abstractions.dll`)

problem_statement:
fcs_public_api / fcs_file_outline: size default pages by a character budget and hint the narrowing in-band
## Field evidence (#100, 2026-08-16 batch 6, fslangmcp 0.13.1)

- `fcs_public_api` on a 2.5k-line project blew the MCP client's token cap; the client (Claude Code) spilled the full payload to a side file. The overflow surface never suggested the narrowing that already exists (`namespaceFilter`, `maxResults` + cursor).
- `fcs_file_outline` with full entries overflowed twice (54KB and 65KB outlines), same spill.
- Follow-on confusion: the client's side file is a bare JSON object while inline responses use the `[{type:"text",...}]` envelope — a consumer parsing the documented inline shape gets a KeyError. **The spill and its shape belong to the client, not this server** — but the server can make the spill never happen.

## Root cause (HEAD)

`fcs_public_api` paginates by **type count** (`maxResults` default 100, `FcsBridge.fs:8524-8525`): 100 API-dense types with full member signatures can far exceed a typical client token cap (~25k tokens / ~72k chars), so the "paginated" default still produces spill-sized pages. `fcs_file_outline` with `summaryOnly=false` has no size guard at all for a single large file. Precedent for doing this right already exists in-repo: `find` sizes its default page against the token ceiling explicitly (`FcsBridge.fs:4651-4662` — "~527 chars per site, 80-site page ≈ 43k chars, under the ~25k-token ceiling ≈ ~72k chars").

## Required change

1. **Character-budget paging for `fcs_public_api`.** Keep `maxResults` (type-count cap) but additionally close each page when a serialized-size budget is reached (constant ~60k chars, named and commented like `find`'s); `nextCursor` resumes mid-list. `truncatedByBudget: true` (additive) distinguishes budget-closes from count-closes.
2. **In-band narrowing hint.** Whenever a page closes early (budget or count) with more items remaining, additively emit `hint`: name `namespaceFilter` (with 2–3 actual top namespaces from the remaining set, so the agent can copy-paste) and the cursor. This is the "retry with namespaceFilter='…'" line the field asked for, delivered before any client spill.
3. **`fcs_file_outline` size guard.** With `summaryOnly=false` on a file whose full outline would exceed the same budget: return the summary-level outline plus `hint` ("full outline for this file exceeds the response budget; narrow with …") rather than an over-budget payload. If a narrowing parameter lands via #157 (typeFilter), name it in the hint; do not implement #157 here.
4. Docs (`docs/tools-detailed.md` both tools): one paragraph on the budget behavior, plus a note that oversized responses may be spilled to a side file **by the MCP client** with a client-defined shape — so agents should prefer narrowing over parsing spill files.

## Tests

- Synthetic API surface big enough to trip the budget: page closes under budget, `truncatedByBudget` set, `hint` names real namespaces from the remainder, cursor resumes and the concatenation equals the unpaginated set.
- Count-close (existing behavior) still works; small surfaces unchanged (no hint, no truncation fields — additive-only regression guard).
- Outline guard: an over-budget file downgrades to summary + hint; a small file with `summaryOnly=false` is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- The field scenario (2.5k-line project, default call) returns a first page + cursor + copy-pasteable narrowing hint instead of an over-cap payload; no client spill.
- All existing tests pass; every new field additive.

### Additional contract requirements

# Public contract addendum

These are additional observable requirements for this task. All new response
fields are additive; none of the following may alter responses that previously
fit on a single page.

## fcs_public_api — early-close narrowing hint

Whenever a page closes early (whether closed by the serialized-size budget or
by `maxResults`) and more entities remain:

- The response additively includes a `hint` string field.
- The hint must name the `namespaceFilter` parameter.
- The hint must supply 2–3 copy-pasteable namespace values that are real
  namespaces of entities that did NOT make the returned page — never
  placeholders — and those values must together cover the unreturned entities,
  so that a few narrowed calls can retrieve the whole remainder.
- The hint must reference the `nextCursor` value as the way to keep paging for
  the rest.

A page whose shipped (rendered) response closes early on the size budget must
fit under the ~72,000-character MCP client ceiling.

## fcs_file_outline — over-budget downgrade

A `summaryOnly=false` request whose full outline exceeds the shared response
size budget is downgraded to the summary-level (header-only) outline. The
response additively includes a downgrade marker and an explanatory hint that
names the available narrowing knob; it never emits the over-budget payload.

## Documentation

`docs/tools-detailed.md` must document, in the section for each of
`fcs_public_api` and `fcs_file_outline`:

- The budget behavior: a page (or full outline) can close early on a
  serialized-size budget in addition to `maxResults`, and the response carries
  an explicit marker when that happens (`truncatedByBudget` for
  `fcs_public_api`; the downgrade marker for `fcs_file_outline`), plus how the
  emitted hint's narrowing suggestion (`namespaceFilter` / `maxResults`
  respectively) should be used.
- A note that an oversized response may be spilled to a side file by the MCP
  client, with a client-defined shape — so agents should prefer the in-band
  narrowing over parsing spill files.

+## fcs_public_api
+
+**Routing description:** Emit an F# project's public API surface — every public type and its
+public members with signatures — sorted stably by `fullName` then member name, so two version
+snapshots diff cleanly. Public-only by default (`includeInternal=true` adds `internal`; `private`
+is never emitted).
+
+### Response budget and `truncatedByBudget` (#206)
+
+A page is closed for either of two independent reasons, and the response tells you which:
+`maxResults` (default 100, hard ceiling 1000) caps the page by **type count**, and a shared
+45,000-character serialized-size budget (`responseCharBudget` in `FcsBridge.fs`, the same
+constant `fcs_file_outline` uses — see below) caps it by **response size**, closing the page early
+even when `maxResults` would still allow more entities. The 45,000 figure is deliberately below the
+~72,000-char MCP ceiling it targets: it is measured per-entity, standalone, before the entity is
+embedded two levels deeper in the actual response (`entities` inside the root object) and before
+the response envelope is added, both of which cost real characters the per-entity measurement can't
+see — the margin covers that gap even on signature-*sparse* shapes (short-field records,
+member-less modules) where the gap is largest. A handful of API-dense types — long member lists,
+verbose generic signatures — can also cross that budget well before the count cap does; this is
+what the field failure behind #206 looked like: a 2.5k-line project's default `fcs_public_api` call
+produced a page so large the MCP client spilled it to a side file instead of returning it inline.
+
+`truncated: true` means more entities remain regardless of which cap closed the page.
+`truncatedByBudget: true` is additive and appears **only** when the char budget was the reason —
+absent when the page closed at `maxResults` or reached the end of the (filtered) list. Either way,
+whenever a page closes early with entities left over, an additive `hint` field names
+`namespaceFilter` together with 2–3 real namespaces pulled from the remainder (not placeholders —
+copy-pasteable values from the actual unreturned entities), so the next call can narrow instead of
+re-fetching the same oversized shape. A page always contains at least one entity — a single
+oversized type is never dropped into an empty page just because it alone exceeds the budget.
+
+### Caveats
+
+1. **An entity's member list is never split across pages.** The budget close operates on whole
+   entities, so one page never returns half of a type's members.
+2. **The MCP client may still spill an oversized response to a side file, with a client-defined
+   shape.** `truncatedByBudget` and the char budget exist to make that spill unnecessary in the
+   common case, but a very large single entity (one type with an enormous member list) can still
+   exceed the budget on its own. Prefer `namespaceFilter` over parsing a spilled side file — that
+   file's shape belongs to the client, not this server.
+
+### Related tools
+
+- `fcs_project_outline` — whole-project structural overview; prefer `fcs_public_api` specifically
+  for API-stability/breaking-change diffs.
+- `fcs_file_outline` — shares the same response-char-budget mechanism for one file's outline.
+
+---
+
+## fcs_file_outline
+
+**Routing description:** Agent-friendly compact F# outline for one file. `summaryOnly=true`
+(default) returns module/type headers plus per-kind `memberCounts` only — no per-member
+signatures — which keeps the response small on large files by construction. `summaryOnly=false`
+restores full per-member `name`/`kind`/`range`/`signature`/`accessibility` entries.
+
+### `downgradedToSummary` size guard (#206)
+
+`summaryOnly=false` has no count-based ceiling of its own beyond `maxResults` (default 200), and a
+file with many signature-heavy top-level bindings can still serialize past the shared 45,000-
+character `responseCharBudget` within that count — two field-observed outlines hit 54KB and 65KB.
+Rather than ever return that oversized payload, a `summaryOnly=false` request whose full
+entries would cross the budget is downgraded to the same header-only shape `summaryOnly=true`
+produces (name/kind/fullName/range, no signatures), plus an additive `hint` explaining the
+downgrade and naming `maxResults` — the narrowing knob available today — as the way to fit full
+signatures in one page. The `summaryOnly` field in the response always echoes what was
+**requested**, not what was actually returned; check the additive `downgradedToSummary: true` flag
+to know the entries shape actually changed. Neither field appears when the full output already
+fits the budget — a small file with `summaryOnly=false` gets the unmodified pre-#206 response.
+`count` is the length of the returned `entries` slice — it is capped by `maxResults` exactly like
+`entries` itself (`count = min(definitionsInFile, maxResults)`), and unaffected only by the
+downgrade: lowering `maxResults` shrinks `count` on either shape, downgraded or not.
+`memberCounts` is the one field that is genuinely uncapped — it is computed from the full,
+untruncated definition set regardless of `maxResults` or the downgrade, so it is the field to read
+for "how many of kind X does this file really have," never `count`.
+
+### Caveats
+
+1. **`downgradedToSummary` only fires for an explicit `summaryOnly=false` request.**
+   `summaryOnly=true` is already small by construction and is never measured against the budget.
+2. **A future per-type narrowing parameter (tracked separately, #157) is not implemented here.**
+   Until it lands, `maxResults` is the only narrowing knob the downgrade hint can point to.
+3. **The MCP client may still spill an oversized response to a side file, with a client-defined
+   shape** — same caveat as `fcs_public_api` above.
+
+### Related tools
+
+- `fcs_project_outline` — whole-project structural overview; prefer `fcs_file_outline` for one
+  file's structure.
+- `find` (`kind="symbol"`) — raw, unfiltered, cross-file symbol search when this tool's
+  local/noisy-symbol filtering or summary/budget shaping gets in the way.
+- `fcs_symbol_at_word` — a single symbol at an exact position, no whole-file shaping at all.
+- `fcs_public_api` — shares the same response-char-budget mechanism for a project's public
+  surface.

+
+open System
+open System.IO
+open System.Text.Json.Nodes
+open System.Threading.Tasks
+open Xunit
+open FsLangMcp.Types
+open FsLangMcp.FcsBridge
+open FsLangMcp.Tools
+
+// ─── Fixtures ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+/// `count` top-level functions, each with a six-parameter signature. At the
+/// default maxResults=200 this is rich enough (name + fullName + kind +
+/// accessibility + range + declarationRange + signature per entry) that 200
+/// of them cross the shared responseCharBudget (FcsBridge.fs, `Types.fs`'s
+/// `renderedLength`).
+let private bigOutlineSource (count: int) =
+    let lines = ResizeArray<string>()
+    lines.Add("module Big.Outline")
+    lines.Add("")
+
+    for i in 0 .. count - 1 do
+        let n = i.ToString("D4")
+        lines.Add($"let compute{n} (alpha: string) (beta: string) (gamma: string) (delta: string) (epsilon: string) (zeta: string) : string =")
+        lines.Add("    alpha + beta + gamma + delta + epsilon + zeta")
+        lines.Add("")
+
+    String.concat "\n" lines
+
+let private smallOutlineSource =
+    String.concat
+        "\n"
+        [ "module Small.Outline"
+          ""
+          "let addOne (x: int) : int = x + 1"
+          ""
+          "let addTwo (x: int) : int = x + 2"
+          "" ]
+
+/// Write `source` as the single compiled file of a fresh temp fsproj. Returns
+/// (sourcePath, projectPath, tempRoot) — caller deletes tempRoot when done.
+let private writeFixture (dirTag: string) (source: string) : string * string * string =
+    let runId = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")
+    let root = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), $"fslangmcp_outline_budget_{dirTag}_{runId}")
+    Directory.CreateDirectory(root) |> ignore
+
+    let sourcePath = Path.Combine(root, "Outline.fs")
+    File.WriteAllText(sourcePath, source)
+
+    let projectPath = Path.Combine(root, "Outline.fsproj")
+
+    File.WriteAllText(
+        projectPath,
+        String.concat
+            Environment.NewLine
+            [ "<Project Sdk=\"Microsoft.NET.Sdk\">"
+              "  <PropertyGroup>"
+              "    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>"
+              "  </PropertyGroup>"
+              "  <ItemGroup>"
+              "    <Compile Include=\"Outline.fs\" />"
+              "  </ItemGroup>"
+              "</Project>" ]
+    )
+
+    sourcePath, projectPath, root
+
+// ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+let private optBool (node: JsonNode) (key: string) : bool option =
+    match node[key] with
+    | null -> None
+    | v -> Some(v.GetValue<bool>())
+
+let private optString (node: JsonNode) (key: string) : string option =
+    match node[key] with
+    | null -> None
+    | v -> Some(v.GetValue<string>())
+
+/// Fields that were already part of the file-outline response before this
+/// behavior was added. The response may carry any additional fields required
+/// to explain or identify a downgrade.
+let private legacyOutlineKeys =
+    Set.ofList
+        [ "status"; "file"; "optionsSource"; "includePrivate"; "includeLocal"
+          "summaryOnly"; "count"; "memberCounts"; "entries"
+          "parseDiagnostics"; "checkDiagnostics"; "hint" ]
+
+/// All *non-legacy* boolean properties present on the response object.
+let private additiveBoolFields (node: JsonNode) : (string * bool) list =
+    match node with
+    | :? JsonObject as obj ->
+        [ for kvp in obj do
+              if not (legacyOutlineKeys.Contains kvp.Key) then
+                  match kvp.Value with
+                  | null -> ()
+                  | :? JsonValue as v ->
+                      match v.TryGetValue<bool>() with
+                      | true, b -> yield (kvp.Key, b)
+                      | _ -> ()
+                  | _ -> () ]
+    | _ ->
+        Assert.Fail("expected the outline response to be a JSON object")
+        []
+
+/// All *non-legacy* properties present on the response object: (key, isBool).
+/// Used only inside assertion-failure diagnostics.
+let private additiveFields (node: JsonNode) : (string * bool) list =
+    match node with
+    | :? JsonObject as obj ->
+        [ for kvp in obj do
+              if not (legacyOutlineKeys.Contains kvp.Key) then
+                  let isBool =
+                      match kvp.Value with
+                      | :? JsonValue as v ->
+                          (match v.TryGetValue<bool>() with
+                           | true, _ -> true
+                           | _ -> false)
+                      | _ -> false
+
+                  yield (kvp.Key, isBool) ]
+    | _ -> []
+
+/// A downgrade is marked by at least one true additive boolean field. The
+/// contract does not constrain its name or prohibit other additive fields.
+let private hasDowngradeMarker (node: JsonNode) : bool =
+    additiveBoolFields node |> List.exists snd
+
+/// On a response that previously fit, there must be no unexpected additive
+/// fields. Downgraded responses are intentionally not constrained this way.
+let private assertStrictlyAdditive (exceptKeys: Set<string>) (node: JsonNode) : unit =
+    match node with
+    | :? JsonObject as obj ->
+        for kvp in obj do
+            Assert.True(
+                legacyOutlineKeys.Contains kvp.Key || exceptKeys.Contains kvp.Key,
+                $"response carries an unexpected additive field '{kvp.Key}' on a response that previously fit"
+            )
+    | _ -> Assert.Fail("expected the outline response to be a JSON object")
+
+let private baseArgs (path: string) (project: string) : FcsFileOutlineArgs =
+    { path = path
+      text = None
+      projectPath = Some project
+      projectOptions = None
+      includePrivate = None
+      includeLocal = None
+      summaryOnly = Some false
+      maxResults = None }
+
+// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``over-budget file downgrades summaryOnly=false to headers plus a hint`` () : Task =
+    task {
+        let sourcePath, projectPath, root = writeFixture "big" (bigOutlineSource 220)
+        let bridge = FcsBridge()
+
+        try
+            let! result = bridge.FileOutline(baseArgs sourcePath projectPath)
+
+            Assert.Equal("succeeded", result["status"].GetValue<string>())
+            Assert.NotNull(result["summaryOnly"])
+
+            // NOTE: a downgraded response carries the summary (header-only) shape,
+            // and the frozen contract does not pin whether `summaryOnly` then
+            // reports the REQUESTED flag (false) or the EMITTED shape (true) —
+            // both are contract-faithful, so only its presence is asserted here.
+
+            // The downgrade is identified by a true additive boolean marker;
+            // its key and any other additive fields are intentionally flexible.
+            Assert.True(
+                hasDowngradeMarker result,
+                $"expected an additive true boolean downgrade marker on a downgraded outline (additive fields present: {additiveFields result})"
+            )
+
+            match optString result "hint" with
+            | None -> Assert.Fail("expected a hint field when the outline is downgraded to summary")
+            | Some hint ->
+                Assert.Contains("maxResults", hint)
+                Assert.True(not (String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace hint), "the downgrade hint must explain how to narrow the response")
+
+            // Downgraded entries are header-shaped: no per-member `signature`. The
+            // fixture is 220 free `let` functions inside one module, so `headersOf`'s
+            // containerKinds filter leaves exactly the module header — Assert.NotEmpty
+            // makes sure that one entry is really there (#206 review Min-2: a loop with
+            // no NotEmpty check passes vacuously on an empty array).
+            match result["entries"] with
+            | :? JsonArray as entries ->
+                Assert.NotEmpty(entries)
+
+                for entry in entries |> Seq.cast<JsonNode> do
+                    Assert.Null(entry["signature"])
+            | _ -> Assert.Fail("expected entries to be a JsonArray")
+
+            // count is the post-truncation length (maxResults=200 caps `entries`, hence
+            // `count`, to 200 even though the fixture declares 221 definitions); only
+            // memberCounts describes the full, untruncated definition set (#206 review
+            // Imp-2 — the original comment here claimed count was also uncapped, which
+            // contradicted the very next assertion).
+            Assert.Equal(200, result["count"].GetValue<int>())
+            Assert.NotNull(result["memberCounts"])
+
+            // #206 review Min-1: assert the actual SHIPPED (indented) response fits the
+            // ~72k-char MCP ceiling, not just that the internal accumulator believes it
+            // closed under responseCharBudget — this is the assertion that would have
+            // caught round-1's Imp-1 (wrong unit) and round-2's depth residual alike.
+            let rendered = renderToken result
+            Assert.True(
+                rendered.Length <= 72_000,
+                $"downgraded outline rendered to {rendered.Length} chars, over the ~72k MCP ceiling"
+            )
+        finally
+            if Directory.Exists root then
+                Directory.Delete(root, true)
+    }
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``lowering maxResults after a downgrade resolves it: the response returns to full entries once small enough`` () : Task =
+    task {
+        // #206 review H5: the implementer flagged this round-trip as an untested but
+        // traced-sound gap. `entries` is truncated to maxResults BEFORE the budget
+        // measurement (FcsBridge.fs), so the measured payload is monotonic in
+        // maxResults — halving it roughly halves the measured size, and `overBudget`
+        // must eventually flip back to false. Pin that mechanism with a real call.
+        let sourcePath, projectPath, root = writeFixture "shrink" (bigOutlineSource 220)
+        let bridge = FcsBridge()
+
+        try
+            let! full = bridge.FileOutline(baseArgs sourcePath projectPath)
+
+            Assert.True(
+                hasDowngradeMarker full,
+                $"expected an additive true boolean downgrade marker on the over-budget outline (additive fields present: {additiveFields full})"
+            )
+
+            let! shrunk =
+                bridge.FileOutline({ baseArgs sourcePath projectPath with maxResults = Some 10 })
+
+            Assert.Equal("succeeded", shrunk["status"].GetValue<string>())
+            Assert.False(hasDowngradeMarker shrunk)
+            Assert.Equal(None, optString shrunk "hint")
+            assertStrictlyAdditive Set.empty shrunk
+            Assert.Equal(10, shrunk["count"].GetValue<int>())
+
+            // Full per-member entries are back — every returned entry carries a signature.
+            match shrunk["entries"] with
+            | :? JsonArray as entries ->
+                Assert.Equal(10, entries.Count)
+
+                for entry in entries |> Seq.cast<JsonNode> do
+                    Assert.NotNull(entry["signature"])
+            | _ -> Assert.Fail("expected entries to be a JsonArray")
+        finally
+            if Directory.Exists root then
+                Directory.Delete(root, true)
+    }
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``small file with summaryOnly=false is unchanged: full entries, no downgrade fields`` () : Task =
+    task {
+        let sourcePath, projectPath, root = writeFixture "small" smallOutlineSource
+        let bridge = FcsBridge()
+
+        try
+            let! result = bridge.FileOutline(baseArgs sourcePath projectPath)
+
+            Assert.Equal("succeeded", result["status"].GetValue<string>())
+            Assert.Equal(Some false, optBool result "summaryOnly")
+            Assert.False(hasDowngradeMarker result)
+            Assert.Equal(None, optString result "hint")
+            assertStrictlyAdditive Set.empty result
+
+            match result["entries"] with
+            | :? JsonArray as entries ->
+                Assert.True(entries.Count >= 2, $"expected >= 2 entries, got {entries.Count}")
+
+                for entry in entries |> Seq.cast<JsonNode> do
+                    Assert.NotNull(entry["signature"])
+            | _ -> Assert.Fail("expected entries to be a JsonArray")
+        finally
+            if Directory.Exists root then
+                Directory.Delete(root, true)
+    }

+module FsLangMcp.Tests.PublicApiCharBudgetDocsTests
+
+/// Documentation-coverage tests for the #206 budget behavior: the frozen
+/// statement (Required change item 4) and the contract addendum make
+/// docs/tools-detailed.md content an observable requirement — this module is
+/// the only executable gate for it. The assertions are wording-agnostic: they
+/// find each tool's section by its `##` heading (the file's single documented
+/// convention) and then require only the contract-mandated concepts elsewhere
+/// in the file — budget-close behavior plus its explicit marker, the hinted
+/// narrowing knob, and the client-owned spill note — never pinned field names
+/// (the downgrade marker's JSON key is deliberately unspecified) or pinned
+/// phrasing. The contract addendum's documentation requirement covers both
+/// tools, so both tool-name filters route the whole module.
+
+open System
+open System.IO
+open System.Text.RegularExpressions
+open Xunit
+
+// ─── Section extraction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+/// Absolute path to the repository's docs/tools-detailed.md, located relative
+/// to this test assembly (bin/Debug/<tfm> → tests/FsLangMcp.Tests → repo root).
+let private toolsDetailedPath : string =
+    let mutable d = DirectoryInfo(AppContext.BaseDirectory)
+    let mutable found: DirectoryInfo = null
+
+    while not (isNull d) && isNull found do
+        if File.Exists(Path.Combine(d.FullName, "FsLangMcp.slnx")) then
+            found <- d
+        else
+            d <- d.Parent
+
+    Assert.False(isNull found, $"could not locate the repository root from {AppContext.BaseDirectory}")
+
+    let path = Path.Combine(found.FullName, "docs", "tools-detailed.md")
+
+    Assert.True(File.Exists path, $"expected {path} to exist — the frozen statement requires this document")
+    path
+
+let private toolsDetailedText : string = File.ReadAllText toolsDetailedPath
+
+/// The body of the `## <name>` section: everything after its heading up to the
+/// next `##` heading (or the end of the file). Section contents move freely
+/// between files as the docs are reorganized, so a section-local claim is
+/// asserted within the corresponding section so each tool's documentation
+/// independently describes its behavior.
+let private toolSection (toolName: string) : string =
+    let pattern =
+        "(?ms)^##\\s+" + Regex.Escape(toolName) + "\\s*$(.+?)(?=^##\\s|\\z)"
+
+    let m = Regex.Match(toolsDetailedText, pattern)
+    Assert.True(m.Success, $"docs/tools-detailed.md must have a '## {toolName}' section")
+    m.Groups.[1].Value
+
+/// The `## <name>` section exists and names every required concept in that
+/// section. This ensures the guidance is available to readers of either tool.
+let private assertToolDocuments (toolName: string) (requiredConcepts: string list) =
+    let section = toolSection toolName
+
+    for concept in requiredConcepts do
+        Assert.True(
+            section.Contains(concept, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase),
+            $"docs/tools-detailed.md section '## {toolName}' must document '{concept}'"
+        )
+
+// ─── fcs_public_api ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``docs: fcs_public_api section documents the budget behavior and its explicit marker`` () =
+    assertToolDocuments
+        "fcs_public_api"
+        [ "maxResults" // the pre-existing count cap the budget complements
+          "budget" // pages can additionally close on the serialized-size budget
+          "truncatedByBudget" ] // the explicit marker that names a budget close
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``docs: fcs_public_api section documents the hint's namespaceFilter narrowing and the client spill note`` () =
+    assertToolDocuments
+        "fcs_public_api"
+        [ "hint" // the additive field carrying the narrowing suggestion
+          "namespaceFilter" // the knob the hint's suggestions are values for
+          "spill" // oversized responses may be spilled to a side file …
+          "client"
+          "shape" ] // the MCP client defines the side-file shape
+
+// ─── fcs_file_outline ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``docs: fcs_file_outline section documents the over-budget downgrade`` () =
+    assertToolDocuments
+        "fcs_file_outline"
+        [ "summaryOnly" // the mode the over-budget response is downgraded from/to
+          "budget" // the serialized-size budget the full response is measured against
+          "downgraded" ] // an explicit downgrade marker exists (its JSON key is
+    // deliberately unspecified by the contract, so only the concept is pinned)
+
+[<Fact>]
+let ``docs: fcs_file_outline section documents the hinted maxResults narrowing and the client spill note`` () =
+    assertToolDocuments
+        "fcs_file_outline"
+        [ "hint" // the additive field carrying the narrowing suggestion
+          "maxResults" // the narrowing knob the hint names
+          "spill" // oversized responses may be spilled to a side file …
+          "client"
+          "shape" ] // the MCP client defines the side-file shape
