@@ -0,0 +1,443 @@
+defmodule PaperTiger.Resources.ConnectPlatformTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
+
+  import PaperTiger.Test
+
+  alias PaperTiger.Router
+
+  setup do
+    :ok = checkout_paper_tiger(%{})
+
+    # The base sandbox helper does not clear Connect stores added by the
+    # Connect feature, so clear them from this test-owned support module.
+    ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit(fn ->
+      PaperTiger.ConnectCleanup.clear_namespace(PaperTiger.Test.current_namespace())
+    end)
+
+    :ok
+  end
+
+  defp request(method, path, params \\ nil, headers \\ []) do
+    conn = Plug.Test.conn(method, path, params)
+
+    headers_with_defaults =
+      headers ++
+        [
+          {"content-type", "application/json"},
+          {"authorization", "Bearer sk_test_connect_key"}
+        ] ++ sandbox_headers()
+
+    headers_with_defaults
+    |> Enum.reduce(conn, fn {key, value}, acc -> Plug.Conn.put_req_header(acc, key, value) end)
+    |> Router.call([])
+  end
+
+  defp json_response(conn), do: Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)
+  defp account_header(account_id), do: [{"stripe-account", account_id}]
+
+  describe "Accounts and Account Links" do
+    test "creates, updates, lists, retrieves, and deletes legacy connected accounts" do
+      create_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/accounts", %{
+          "business_type" => "individual",
+          "capabilities" => %{
+            "card_payments" => %{"requested" => true},
+            "transfers" => %{"requested" => true}
+          },
+          "country" => "US",
+          "email" => "seller@example.test",
+          "type" => "express"
+        })
+
+      assert create_conn.status in 200..299
+      account = json_response(create_conn)
+      assert String.starts_with?(account["id"], "acct_")
+      assert account["object"] == "account"
+      assert account["capabilities"]["transfers"] == "active"
+      assert is_boolean(account["charges_enabled"])
+      assert is_boolean(account["payouts_enabled"])
+
+      update_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/accounts/#{account["id"]}", %{
+          "metadata" => %{"seller_id" => "seller_123"}
+        })
+
+      assert update_conn.status in 200..299
+      assert json_response(update_conn)["metadata"] == %{"seller_id" => "seller_123"}
+
+      retrieve_conn = request(:get, "/v1/accounts/#{account["id"]}")
+      assert retrieve_conn.status in 200..299
+      assert json_response(retrieve_conn)["email"] == "seller@example.test"
+
+      list_conn = request(:get, "/v1/accounts")
+      assert list_conn.status in 200..299
+      assert [account["id"]] == Enum.map(json_response(list_conn)["data"], & &1["id"])
+
+      link_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/account_links", %{
+          "account" => account["id"],
+          "refresh_url" => "https://example.test/reauth",
+          "return_url" => "https://example.test/return",
+          "type" => "account_onboarding"
+        })
+
+      assert link_conn.status in 200..299
+      link = json_response(link_conn)
+      assert link["object"] == "account_link"
+      assert link["account"] == account["id"]
+      assert link["type"] == "account_onboarding"
+      assert String.starts_with?(link["url"], "https://connect.stripe.com/setup/s/link_")
+
+      delete_conn = request(:delete, "/v1/accounts/#{account["id"]}")
+      assert delete_conn.status in 200..299
+      deleted = json_response(delete_conn)
+      assert deleted["id"] == account["id"]
+      assert deleted["object"] == "account"
+      assert deleted["deleted"] == true
+    end
+
+    test "account listing includes multiple created accounts in a list envelope" do
+      first = create_account()
+      second = create_account()
+
+      list_conn = request(:get, "/v1/accounts")
+      assert list_conn.status in 200..299
+
+      listed = json_response(list_conn)
+      assert listed["object"] == "list"
+      assert is_list(listed["data"])
+      assert is_boolean(listed["has_more"])
+      listed_ids = Enum.map(listed["data"], & &1["id"])
+      assert first["id"] in listed_ids
+      assert second["id"] in listed_ids
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "Unsupported Accounts v2 API" do
+    test "returns an unrecognized request error" do
+      conn = request(:post, "/v2/core/accounts", %{})
+
+      assert conn.status == 404
+      error = json_response(conn)["error"]
+      assert error["type"] == "invalid_request_error"
+
+      assert String.contains?(
+               error["message"],
+               "Unrecognized request URL (POST /v2/core/accounts)"
+             )
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "Stripe-Account request scoping" do
+    test "isolates ordinary resources per connected account" do
+      account = create_account()
+
+      platform_customer =
+        request(:post, "/v1/customers", %{
+          "email" => "platform@example.test",
+          "id" => "cus_connect_shared"
+        })
+        |> json_response()
+
+      connected_customer =
+        request(
+          :post,
+          "/v1/customers",
+          %{"email" => "connected@example.test", "id" => "cus_connect_shared"},
+          account_header(account["id"])
+        )
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert platform_customer["id"] == connected_customer["id"]
+
+      platform_retrieve =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers/cus_connect_shared")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      connected_retrieve =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers/cus_connect_shared", nil, account_header(account["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert platform_retrieve["email"] == "platform@example.test"
+      assert connected_retrieve["email"] == "connected@example.test"
+
+      connected_list =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers", nil, account_header(account["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert ["connected@example.test"] == Enum.map(connected_list["data"], & &1["email"])
+
+      missing_account_conn =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers", nil, account_header("acct_missing"))
+
+      assert missing_account_conn.status == 404
+      assert json_response(missing_account_conn)["error"]["code"] == "resource_missing"
+    end
+
+    test "rejects customer creation for an unknown connected account" do
+      email = "unknown-connect-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.test"
+
+      conn =
+        request(
+          :post,
+          "/v1/customers",
+          %{"email" => email},
+          account_header("acct_missing")
+        )
+
+      assert conn.status == 404
+      assert json_response(conn)["error"]["code"] == "resource_missing"
+    end
+
+    test "keeps customer ids isolated between connected accounts" do
+      account_a = create_account()
+      account_b = create_account()
+
+      assert account_a["id"] != account_b["id"]
+
+      customer_a =
+        request(
+          :post,
+          "/v1/customers",
+          %{"email" => "first-connected@example.test", "id" => "cus_connect_shared"},
+          account_header(account_a["id"])
+        )
+        |> json_response()
+
+      customer_b =
+        request(
+          :post,
+          "/v1/customers",
+          %{"email" => "second-connected@example.test", "id" => "cus_connect_shared"},
+          account_header(account_b["id"])
+        )
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert customer_a["id"] == customer_b["id"]
+
+      retrieved_a =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers/cus_connect_shared", nil, account_header(account_a["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      retrieved_b =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers/cus_connect_shared", nil, account_header(account_b["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert retrieved_a["email"] == "first-connected@example.test"
+      assert retrieved_b["email"] == "second-connected@example.test"
+
+      listed_a =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers", nil, account_header(account_a["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      listed_b =
+        request(:get, "/v1/customers", nil, account_header(account_b["id"]))
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert ["first-connected@example.test"] == Enum.map(listed_a["data"], & &1["email"])
+      assert ["second-connected@example.test"] == Enum.map(listed_b["data"], & &1["email"])
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "Transfers and Transfer Reversals" do
+    test "creates transfers to connected accounts and reverses them coherently" do
+      account = create_account()
+
+      transfer_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/transfers", %{
+          "amount" => 1_500,
+          "currency" => "usd",
+          "description" => "Seller payout",
+          "destination" => account["id"],
+          "transfer_group" => "order_123"
+        })
+
+      assert transfer_conn.status in 200..299
+      transfer = json_response(transfer_conn)
+      assert String.starts_with?(transfer["id"], "tr_")
+      assert transfer["amount"] == 1_500
+      assert is_integer(transfer["amount"])
+      assert transfer["amount_reversed"] == 0
+      assert transfer["currency"] == "usd"
+      assert transfer["destination"] == account["id"]
+      assert transfer["reversed"] == false
+      assert transfer["reversals"]["data"] == []
+
+      reversal_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/transfers/#{transfer["id"]}/reversals", %{
+          "amount" => 500,
+          "metadata" => %{"reason" => "partial_refund"}
+        })
+
+      assert reversal_conn.status in 200..299
+      reversal = json_response(reversal_conn)
+      assert String.starts_with?(reversal["id"], "trr_")
+      assert reversal["amount"] == 500
+      assert reversal["transfer"] == transfer["id"]
+      assert reversal["metadata"] == %{"reason" => "partial_refund"}
+
+      updated_transfer =
+        request(:get, "/v1/transfers/#{transfer["id"]}")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert updated_transfer["amount_reversed"] == 500
+      assert updated_transfer["reversed"] == false
+      assert [reversal["id"]] == Enum.map(updated_transfer["reversals"]["data"], & &1["id"])
+
+      list_reversals_conn = request(:get, "/v1/transfers/#{transfer["id"]}/reversals")
+      assert list_reversals_conn.status in 200..299
+      assert [reversal["id"]] == Enum.map(json_response(list_reversals_conn)["data"], & &1["id"])
+
+      final_reversal_conn = request(:post, "/v1/transfers/#{transfer["id"]}/reversals")
+      assert final_reversal_conn.status in 200..299
+      final_reversal = json_response(final_reversal_conn)
+      assert final_reversal["amount"] == 1_000
+
+      fully_reversed =
+        request(:get, "/v1/transfers/#{transfer["id"]}")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert fully_reversed["amount_reversed"] == 1_500
+      assert fully_reversed["reversed"] == true
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "Application Fee Refunds" do
+    test "creates application fees from destination-charge payment intents and refunds them" do
+      account = create_account()
+
+      payment_intent =
+        request(:post, "/v1/payment_intents", %{
+          "amount" => 2_000,
+          "application_fee_amount" => 250,
+          "currency" => "usd",
+          "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa",
+          "transfer_data" => %{"destination" => account["id"]}
+        })
+        |> json_response()
+
+      confirmed =
+        request(:post, "/v1/payment_intents/#{payment_intent["id"]}/confirm")

+
+      charge =

+
+      assert String.starts_with?(charge["application_fee"], "fee_")

+      assert fee["amount_refunded"] == 0
+      assert fee["refunded"] == false
+
+      refund_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}/refunds", %{
+          "amount" => 100,
+          "metadata" => %{"reason" => "seller_refund"}
+        })
+
+      assert refund_conn.status in 200..299
+      refund = json_response(refund_conn)
+      assert String.starts_with?(refund["id"], "fr_")
+      assert refund["amount"] == 100
+      assert refund["fee"] == fee["id"]
+      assert refund["metadata"] == %{"reason" => "seller_refund"}
+
+      partial_over_refund =
+        request(:post, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}/refunds", %{"amount" => 151})
+
+      assert partial_over_refund.status == 400
+      assert json_response(partial_over_refund)["error"]["param"] == "amount"
+
+      partially_refunded_fee =
+        request(:get, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert partially_refunded_fee["amount_refunded"] == 100
+      assert partially_refunded_fee["refunded"] == false
+
+      final_refund =
+        request(:post, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}/refunds")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert final_refund["amount"] == 150
+
+      fully_refunded_fee =
+        request(:get, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}")
+        |> json_response()
+
+      assert fully_refunded_fee["amount_refunded"] == 250
+      assert fully_refunded_fee["refunded"] == true
+
+      over_refund_conn =
+        request(:post, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee["id"]}/refunds", %{"amount" => 1})
+
+      assert over_refund_conn.status == 400
+      assert json_response(over_refund_conn)["error"]["param"] == "amount"
+    end
+
+    test "keeps application fees linked to their respective destination accounts" do
+      destinations = [create_account(), create_account()]
+
+      for destination <- destinations do
+        payment_intent_conn =
+          request(:post, "/v1/payment_intents", %{
+            "amount" => 2_300,
+            "application_fee_amount" => 125,
+            "currency" => "usd",
+            "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa",
+            "transfer_data" => %{"destination" => destination["id"]}
+          })
+
+        assert payment_intent_conn.status in 200..299
+        payment_intent = json_response(payment_intent_conn)
+
+        confirm_conn = request(:post, "/v1/payment_intents/#{payment_intent["id"]}/confirm")
+        assert confirm_conn.status in 200..299
+        confirmed = json_response(confirm_conn)
+
+        charge =
+          request(:get, "/v1/charges/#{confirmed["latest_charge"]}")
+          |> json_response()
+
+        fee_id = charge["application_fee"]
+        assert is_binary(fee_id)
+
+        fee = request(:get, "/v1/application_fees/#{fee_id}") |> json_response()
+        assert fee["id"] == fee_id
+        assert fee["account"] == destination["id"]
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "Connect documentation" do
+    test "documents Accounts v2 as outside the supported Connect scope" do
+      paragraphs =
+        Path.wildcard("**/*.md")
+        |> Enum.reject(&String.starts_with?(&1, ".rebench_contract/"))
+        |> Enum.flat_map(&(File.read!(&1) |> String.split(~r/\n\s*\n/)))
+
+      assert Enum.any?(paragraphs, fn paragraph ->
+               Regex.match?(~r/accounts v2/i, paragraph) and
+                 Regex.match?(~r/unsupported|not supported|not implemented|out of scope/i, paragraph)
+             end)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp create_account do

+      request(:post, "/v1/accounts", %{
+        "capabilities" => %{"transfers" => %{"requested" => true}},
+        "country" => "US",
+        "type" => "express"
+      })
+
+    assert conn.status in 200..299
+    json_response(conn)
+  end
+end

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+defmodule PaperTiger.ConnectCleanup do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Test-only cleanup for Connect resources used by the Connect platform tests.
+
+  The production sandbox helper `PaperTiger.Test.cleanup_namespace/1` only
+  clears the stores that ship with the base release.  Connect stores are added
+  by the Connect feature, so Connect tests clear any optionally-loaded store
+  modules themselves.  Every referenced store contractually responds to
+  `clear_namespace/1`, so calls go through `apply/3` and are skipped when a
+  store module is not part of the running application.
+  """
+
+  @connect_stores [
+    PaperTiger.Store.Accounts,
+    PaperTiger.Store.ApplicationFeeRefunds,
+    PaperTiger.Store.TransferReversals,
+    PaperTiger.Store.Transfers
+  ]
+
+  @doc """
+  Clears every optionally loaded Connect store for the given namespace.
+
+  Intended to be registered with `ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit/1` after checking
+  out a PaperTiger sandbox:
+
+      setup do
+        :ok = checkout_paper_tiger(%{})
+
+        ExUnit.Callbacks.on_exit(fn ->
+          PaperTiger.ConnectCleanup.clear_namespace(PaperTiger.Test.current_namespace())
+        end)
+
+        :ok
+      end
+  """
+  @spec clear_namespace(pid() | :global) :: :ok
+  def clear_namespace(namespace) do
+    Enum.each(@connect_stores, fn store ->
+      if Code.ensure_loaded?(store), do: apply(store, :clear_namespace, [namespace])
+    end)
+
+    :ok
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
[FEAT] Name individual steps without needing the `name` list element
## Feature Request

### Description
The current step-naming syntax is:

```r
run(
  input = list(
    list(
      name = "Step 1",
      paths = c("path/to/script1.R")
    ),
    list(
      name = "Step 2",
      paths = c("path/to/script2.R")
    ),
    list(
      name = "Step 3",
      paths = c("path/to/script3.R", "path/to/script4.R")
    )
  ),
  n_workers = 2
)
```

This is a bit long.

### Proposed Solution

```r
run(
  input = list(
    "Step 1" = "path/to/script1.R",

    "Step 2" = 
      list(
        "path/to/script2.R"
      ),

    "Step 3" = 
      list(
        "Step 3a" = "path/to/script3.R", 
        "Step 3b" = "path/to/script4.R"
      )
  ),
  n_workers = 2
)
```

### Use Case
This is beneficial because it follows R's named list syntax.

### Additional Context
N/A

### Impact
This streamlines the naming process somewhat.

### Related Issues
N/A

      paths = c("path/to/script3.R", "path/to/script4.R")
    )
  ),
  n_workers = 2
)
```

This is a bit long.

### Proposed Solution

```r
run(
  input = list(
    "Step 1" = "path/to/script1.R",

    "Step 2" = 
      list(
        "path/to/script2.R"
      ),

    "Step 3" = 
      list(
        "Step 3a" = "path/to/script3.R", 
        "Step 3b" = "path/to/script4.R"
      )
  ),
  n_workers = 2
)
```

### Use Case
This is beneficial because it follows R's named list syntax.

### Additional Context
N/A

### Impact
This streamlines the naming process somewhat.

+# These tests exercise named inputs through run(), rather than asserting on the

+local_fake_run_session <- function() {
+  fake_r_session <- list(new = function(...) {
+    process <- NULL
+    list(
+      poll = function(timeout) {
+        if (is.null(process)) {
+          return("ready")
+        }
+        process$poll_io(0)
+        if (process$is_alive()) "timeout" else "ready"
+      },
+      check_status = function() {
+        if (!is.null(process) && !process$is_alive() &&
+            !identical(process$get_exit_status(), 0L)) {
+          stop("test script process failed")
+        }
+      },
+      get_state = function() {
+        if (is.null(process) || !process$is_alive()) "idle" else "running"
+      },
+      log_script = function(script) {
+        process <<- callr::r_bg(
+          function(path) sys.source(path, envir = globalenv()),
+          args = list(path = script),
+          stdout = "|",
+          stderr = "|"
+        )
+        invisible(NULL)
+      },
+      create_log = function() invisible(NULL),
+      log_finish = function(...) {
+        process$poll_io(0)
+        list(status = list(message = "success"))
+      }
+    )
+  })
+  testthat::local_mocked_bindings(
+    whirl_r_session = fake_r_session,
+    .package = "whirl",
+    .env = parent.frame()
+  )
+}
+
+r_string <- function(x) encodeString(x, quote = "\"")
+
+write_marker_script <- function(path, marker, value = "done") {
+  writeLines(
+    sprintf("writeLines(%s, %s)", r_string(value), r_string(marker)),
+    path
+  )
+}
+
+make_log_dir <- function(work_dir) {
+  path <- file.path(work_dir, "logs")
+  dir.create(path)
+  path
+}
+

+
+  selected_marker <- file.path(work_dir, "selected")
+  other_marker <- file.path(work_dir, "other")
+  selected_script <- file.path(work_dir, "selected.R")
+  other_script <- file.path(work_dir, "other.R")
+  write_marker_script(selected_script, selected_marker)
+  write_marker_script(other_script, other_marker)
+
+  result <- tryCatch(run(
+    input = list(
+      "Chosen step" = selected_script,
+      "Other step" = other_script
+    ),

+    n_workers = 1,
+    summary_file = NULL,

+    track_files = FALSE

+  if (!inherits(result, "error")) {
+
+  expect_true(file.exists(selected_marker))

+  write_barrier_script <- function(path, own_start, other_start,

problem_statement:
Picker multi-select is broken in the fzf-lua backend (only first entry acted on; tag-location picker errors)
### ð Describe the bug

### Description

The fzf-lua picker backend (`lua/obsidian/picker/_fzf.lua`) advertises multi-select via `<Tab>` (fzf-lua enables `--multi` by default), but selecting multiple entries either does nothing or only acts on the first item. This shows up in a few code paths:

1. **`find_files` / `grep` callbacks** â `get_selection_actions`'s `default` action hard-codes `entry_to_file(selected[1], ...)`, so even with several entries `<Tab>`-marked, only the first is opened/passed to the callback.

2. **`:Obsidian tags` location picker (`M.pick`)** â this picker is reached with `allow_multiple` unset, but fzf still allows `<Tab>` marking. Pressing `<Enter>` on multiple selections hits `get_values(selected, false)`, which logs `This mapping does not allow multiple entries` and opens nothing. So you *can* mark entries but the action silently fails.

3. **`M.pick` default note-open path** â `opts.callback(unpack(values))` is incompatible with `obsidian.api.open_note(entry, cmd)`: a second selected entry would be passed as the `cmd` argument, so multi-open can't work even if `allow_multiple` were set.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `picker = { name = "fzf-lua" }`.
2. Run `:Obsidian tags`, pick a tag, then in the location picker `<Tab>`-mark 2+ results and press `<Enter>`.
3. Observe: nothing opens; `:messages` shows `This mapping does not allow multiple entries`.

(Similarly, `:Obsidian quick_switch` / find with multiple `<Tab>` selections opens only the first note.)

### Expected behavior

Marking multiple entries with `<Tab>` and pressing `<Enter>` should act on **all** selected entries (e.g. open each note), or multi-select should be explicitly disabled (`--no-multi`) for pickers that only support a single action â not allow marking and then silently fail.

### Environment

- obsidian.nvim: `3.16.4`
- picker: fzf-lua
- OS: Windows (also reproducible cross-platform from the code paths)
- Neovim: `0.12.2`

### Notes / possible fix

[HIDDEN]

[HIDDEN]

```.```

### Additional contract requirements

The reported defect concerns only the fzf-lua picker backend (`lua/obsidian/picker/_fzf.lua`).
For that backend, the following behavior is required:

1. **Every marked `find_files` / `grep` entry reaches the existing callback.**
   When several entries are marked and confirmed, the selection callback route
   must deliver **every** marked entry, not only the first one. The delivery
   shape is unchanged from the established convention:
   - `find_files` delivers each entry's resolved path string.
   - `grep` delivers each entry as a location table (e.g. `{ filename = ... }`).
   A single invocation carrying a list of the resolved entries, as well as one
   invocation per entry, both satisfy this contract as long as each marked
   entry is delivered exactly once.
   A user-supplied `grep` callback must be honored at all (it must not be
   silently dropped in favor of the default file-opening behavior).

2. **`allow_multiple` selection mappings receive every marked value, and marking stays enabled for them.**
   When a custom selection mapping declares `allow_multiple = true`, the pick
   must leave fzf multi-select marking enabled (i.e. it must not pass fzf
   options that force marking off) so the user is actually able to mark the
   entries, and when several entries are marked the mapping's callback must be
   invoked with all marked values (list-shaped or varargs delivery are both
   acceptable). Mappings without `allow_multiple` remain single-selection.

3. **Single-action pickers explicitly disable marking.**
   Pickers where neither `allow_multiple` nor any selection mapping accepts
   multiple entries — including the `:Obsidian tags` location picker
   (`M.pick`) — must explicitly disable multi-select through the fzf options
   (i.e. pass fzf options that set `--multi` / `--no-multi` state) rather than
   leaving `--multi` enabled so that marking silently fails at confirm time.
   Confirming a single entry on such a picker must still deliver that entry
   through the established callback / note-opening path.

4. **The default note-open route opens every confirmed entry.**
   When several entries are marked and confirmed on a pick for which
   `allow_multiple` is set and no custom callback is supplied, the picker's
   default note-opening route must be driven with every confirmed entry, each
   delivered as its own value: mark identity is preserved per entry (entries
   that merely share a display label still resolve to their own value), no
   confirmed entry is silently dropped, and no extra entry is packed into a
   trailing argument of a single note-opening call instead of being opened.

These requirements are confined to the fzf-lua backend; they do not introduce
or require any new repository-wide picker interface, and other picker backends
keep their existing behavior.

+-- Run obsidian.nvim target tests verbosely with parser-compatible per-test lines.
+-- Emits one line per executed case at column zero derived from each case's real
+-- `exec.fails` (Success / Fail) and notes (Skip) result.
+local target = {
+  ["tests/actions/test_fzf_multi_select.lua"] = true,
+}
+
+local cases = MiniTest.collect {
+  find_files = function()
+    local found = {}
+    for file in pairs(target) do
+      table.insert(found, file)
+    end
+    table.sort(found)
+    return found
+  end,
+}
+
+local all_cases
+
+local reporter = {}
+
+reporter.start = function(c)
+  all_cases = c
+end
+
+reporter.update = function(_) end
+
+reporter.finish = function()
+  local n_fail = 0
+  for _, case in ipairs(all_cases or {}) do
+    local name = table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+    local exec = case.exec or { fails = {}, notes = {} }
+    local status
+    if #exec.fails > 0 then
+      status = "Fail"
+      n_fail = n_fail + 1
+    elseif #exec.notes > 0 then
+      status = "Skip"
+    else
+      status = "Success"
+    end
+    io.stdout:write(status .. " || " .. name .. "\n")
+  end
+  io.flush()
+  vim.cmd(string.format("cquit %d", n_fail > 0 and 1 or 0))
+end
+
+MiniTest.execute(cases, { reporter = reporter })

+-- Targeted contract tests for the fzf-lua picker backend's multi-select
+-- behavior. They replace the vendored `fzf-lua` dependency with a stub and
+-- require the obsidian modules fresh (lazily, inside each case) so they run
+-- without the dependency installed and without a full plugin setup.
+
+local T = MiniTest.new_set()
+local eq = MiniTest.expect.equality
+
+---Ensure `t[key]` is a table and return it.
+local function place(t, key)
+  t[key] = t[key] or {}
+  return t[key]
+end
+
+---Run `fn` with:
+---  * the global `Obsidian` table set to `obsidian`,
+---  * the vendored `fzf-lua` dependency replaced by `stub`, and
+---  * all `obsidian.*` modules fresh-loaded so every module top-level
+---    `require "obsidian.X"` happens while `Obsidian` exists and every
+---    `require "fzf-lua*"` sees the stub.
+---
+---A stub library named `fzf-lua.path` must be provided for find/grep cases;
+---`fzf-lua.previewer.builtin` is additionally needed for pick cases.
+---@param obsidian table
+---@param stub table
+---@param fn fun(fzf: table) receives the fresh `obsidian.picker._fzf` module
+local function run_case(obsidian, stub, fn)
+  local orig_global = Obsidian
+  local orig_fzf = {}
+  -- The picker reads the fzf-lua separator constant from `fzf-lua.utils`;
+  -- provide a stand-in unless the case supplies its own.
+  stub = vim.tbl_extend("keep", stub, { ["fzf-lua.utils"] = { nbsp = "\194\160" } })
+  for _, name in ipairs { "fzf-lua", "fzf-lua.path", "fzf-lua.previewer.builtin", "fzf-lua.actions", "fzf-lua.utils" } do
+    orig_fzf[name] = package.loaded[name]
+    package.loaded[name] = stub[name]
+  end
+  -- Base implementations may hard-require 'fzf-lua.actions' from inside
+  -- get_selection_actions; pre-populate a benign stub.
+  if package.loaded["fzf-lua.actions"] == nil then
+    package.loaded["fzf-lua.actions"] = { file_edit_or_qf = function() end }
+  end
+  local orig_obsidian = {}
+  for name in pairs(place(package, "loaded")) do
+    if name == "obsidian" or name:match "^obsidian%." then
+      orig_obsidian[name] = package.loaded[name]
+      package.loaded[name] = nil
+    end
+  end
+
+  Obsidian = obsidian
+  local ok, err = pcall(function()
+    fn(require "obsidian.picker._fzf")
+  end)
+  Obsidian = orig_global
+
+  for _, name in ipairs { "fzf-lua", "fzf-lua.path", "fzf-lua.previewer.builtin", "fzf-lua.actions", "fzf-lua.utils" } do
+    package.loaded[name] = orig_fzf[name]
+  end
+  for name in pairs(package.loaded) do
+    if name == "obsidian" or name:match "^obsidian%." then
+      package.loaded[name] = nil
+    end
+  end
+  for name, mod in pairs(orig_obsidian) do
+    package.loaded[name] = mod
+  end

+  if not ok then

+---Call the picker entry point, supporting both the original `M.pick(values,
+---opts)` API and a refactored `M.select(values, opts, on_choice)` API.
+---@param fzf table
+---@param values any[]
+---@param opts table|nil
+---@param on_choice fun(...)|nil
+local function call_picker(fzf, values, opts, on_choice)
+  if type(fzf.select) == "function" then
+    return fzf.select(values, opts, on_choice)
+  end
+  return fzf.pick(values, opts)
+end
+
+---Fetch an fzf-lua action handler from inside a stub (where the obsidian
+---modules are guaranteed to be the fresh ones loaded by `run_case`).
+---@param o table fzf_exec options captured by the stub
+---@param key string
+---@return function
+local function action(o, key)
+  assert(type(o.actions) == "table", "fzf_exec options must expose actions")
+  local handler = o.actions[key]
+  assert(type(handler) == "function", "missing fzf action handler for key " .. key)
+  return handler
+end
+
+---Invoke an fzf action handler with the exact selected entry strings the fzf
+---process would hand back: fzf always returns the full text of the marked
+---entry lines exactly as they were submitted to `fzf_exec` (`--with-nth` and
+---friends change only what is displayed, never the returned line text). This
+---helper therefore echoes back the entries the backend actually submitted,
+---so the test does not assume any internal selection-string format.
+---@param o table fzf_exec options captured by the stub
+---@param key string action key, e.g. "default" or "ctrl-l"
+---@param entries string[] raw entries as submitted to `fzf_exec`
+---@param displayed string[] displayed text of the marked entries, in the
+---  order they are confirmed
+---@param rank table|? `rank[i]` is the 1-based position of the i-th marked
+---  entry inside `entries`; defaults to `i`
+local function confirm(o, key, entries, displayed, rank)
+  local marked = {}
+  for i, shown in ipairs(displayed) do
+    local idx = rank and rank[i] or i
+    local entry = entries[idx]
+    assert(entry ~= nil, "test values must match the submitted fzf entries")
+    -- The submitted line is opaque: an implementation may encode extra
+    -- identity information in it, as long as the visible label is part of
+    -- the line fzf displays and returns.
+    assert(
+      entry:find(shown, 1, true) ~= nil,
+      "test values must match the submitted fzf entries; entry " .. entry .. " does not show " .. shown
+    )
+    marked[i] = entry
+  end
+  action(o, key)(marked)
+  return marked
+end

+---An fzf option set explicitly leaves multi-select marking enabled unless it
+---forces it off: either `--multi` is set to `false`, or `--no-multi` is set to
+---a truthy value. (The complementary `--multi` / `--no-multi` flags are
+---commonly passed as a boolean pair on this backend, so a `--no-multi = false`
+---flag means "marking enabled", just as `--multi = false` means "disabled".)
+---@param fzf_opts table|?
+---@return boolean
+local function multi_enabled(fzf_opts)
+  fzf_opts = fzf_opts or {}
+  return fzf_opts["--multi"] ~= false and not fzf_opts["--no-multi"]
+end

+  -- impossible and every delivery can be counted and shape-checked on

+  -- in a single call (legacy `open_note(value, ...)` style) each extra
+  -- entry must surface separately below.

+  ---accepting varargs (`open_note`-style callback with each entry as an
+  ---argument) or a single list argument (`on_choice`-style). Either way
+  ---each entry must arrive individually: a varargs drive is flattened
+  ---argument-by-argument and a list drive element-by-element.
+  local function record_targets(...)
+    local args = vim.F.pack_len(...)
+    if args.n == 1 and type(args[1]) == "table" and args[1][1] ~= nil and args[1].filename == nil and args[1].user_data == nil then
+      for _, v in ipairs(args[1]) do

+      end

+  run_case({ workspaces = {}, workspace = { root = "/vault" }, opts = { picker = { name = "fzf-lua" } } }, {

+      end },

+---Append the names of the values delivered to a selection mapping callback
+---to `list`. Values arrive either as varargs or as one list argument, and
+---each value is a path string or a location table.
+---@param list any[]
+---@param ... any
+local function record_names(list, ...)
+  local function add(v)
+    if type(v) ~= "table" then
+      list[#list + 1] = v
+    elseif v.filename == nil and v.path == nil and v.user_data == nil and v.value == nil and v[1] ~= nil then
+      for _, inner in ipairs(v) do

+    end
+  end
+end

+  for i = #list, 1, -1 do

### Additional contract requirements

For people born on February 29 of a leap year, `demographicsCohort()` and `trimDemographics()` derive age-based eligibility dates as follows:

- In years in which February 29 does not occur, the birthday anniversary is treated as occurring on March 1 of that year.
- The bounds of each age range are inclusive: a person enters at their minimum-age anniversary and remains eligible through the day before the anniversary at which they would exceed the maximum age.
- Records that end before the lower age bound is reached are excluded from the resulting cohort.

These rules apply across all supported age ranges and database backends.

problem_statement:
copyCohorts duplicates records

### Additional contract requirements

`copyCohorts()` must create one corresponding copy of every selected source cohort record in each resulting cohort. Repeated copy operations from the same cohort table must copy the selected records without introducing duplicates within any resulting cohort; the source cohort names need not be changed between operations. When a selected cohort was produced by an earlier copy operation, its current records are the records copied by the later operation.

problem_statement:
Report dropped count for attributes/events/links
The specification states that the count of dropped attributes, events, and links should be recorded in OTLP: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/mapping-to-non-otlp/#dropped-attributes-count

Currently this information is not tracked so the value is always set to 0 in OTLP. We should fix that in the implementation module.

### Additional contract requirements

This task uses the terms "dropped attributes count", "dropped events count", and "dropped links
count" with the meanings given in the OpenTelemetry specification section linked from the problem
statement. The following observable behavior is required:

- Local recording: attributes, events, and links that cannot be recorded on a span because a
  configured recording limit is exceeded, and attributes that cannot be recorded on a span event,
  span link, or log record because such a limit is exceeded, must be counted. The resulting counts
  must be observable on the corresponding readable span data, span event data, span link data, and
  readable log record, and their OTLP protobuf serialization must carry the same numbers in the
  corresponding `dropped_attributes_count`, `dropped_events_count`, and `dropped_links_count`
  fields.
- Count storage: non-zero dropped counts must round-trip through the readable model. Deserializing
  an OTLP protobuf span (including its nested events and links) or log record that carries
  non-zero dropped counts into the readable model, then serializing that model back to protobuf,
  must preserve the same counts on every entity involved: the span's `dropped_attributes_count`,
  `dropped_events_count`, and `dropped_links_count`, each span event's `dropped_attributes_count`,
  each span link's `dropped_attributes_count`, and the log record's `dropped_attributes_count`.

- Count accessors: the corresponding Kotlin readable interfaces expose the counts as read-only `Int`
  properties named `droppedAttributesCount` on span data, span event data, span link data, and
  readable log records, and `droppedEventsCount` and `droppedLinksCount` on span data. Readable
  and writable spans expose their dropped-attribute count through `droppedAttributesCount` as well.
problem_statement_base:
Report dropped count for attributes/events/links
The specification states that the count of dropped attributes, events, and links should be recorded in OTLP: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/mapping-to-non-otlp/#dropped-attributes-count

Currently this information is not tracked so the value is always set to 0 in OTLP. We should fix that in the implementation module.
contract_addendum:
This task uses the terms "dropped attributes count", "dropped events count", and "dropped links
count" with the meanings given in the OpenTelemetry specification section linked from the problem
statement. The following observable behavior is required:

- Local recording: attributes, events, and links that cannot be recorded on a span because a
  configured recording limit is exceeded, and attributes that cannot be recorded on a span event,
  span link, or log record because such a limit is exceeded, must be counted. The resulting counts
  must be observable on the corresponding readable span data, span event data, span link data, and
  readable log record, and their OTLP protobuf serialization must carry the same numbers in the
  corresponding `dropped_attributes_count`, `dropped_events_count`, and `dropped_links_count`
  fields.
- Count storage: non-zero dropped counts must round-trip through the readable model. Deserializing
  an OTLP protobuf span (including its nested events and links) or log record that carries
  non-zero dropped counts into the readable model, then serializing that model back to protobuf,
  must preserve the same counts on every entity involved: the span's `dropped_attributes_count`,
  `dropped_events_count`, and `dropped_links_count`, each span event's `dropped_attributes_count`,
  each span link's `dropped_attributes_count`, and the log record's `dropped_attributes_count`.

- Count accessors: the corresponding Kotlin readable interfaces expose the counts as read-only `Int`
  properties named `droppedAttributesCount` on span data, span event data, span link data, and
  readable log records, and `droppedEventsCount` and `droppedLinksCount` on span data. Readable
  and writable spans expose their dropped-attribute count through `droppedAttributesCount` as well.

+package io.opentelemetry.kotlin.tracing.export
+
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.attributes.AttributesMutator
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.createOpenTelemetry
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.Logger
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.export.FakeLogRecordProcessor
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.export.toProtobuf
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.export.toProtobufByteArray
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.export.toReadableLogRecord
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.model.FakeReadableLogRecord
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.logging.model.ReadWriteLogRecord
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.resource.FakeResource
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.tracing.FakeSpanContext
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.tracing.data.FakeSpanData
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.tracing.data.FakeSpanEventData
+import io.opentelemetry.kotlin.tracing.data.FakeSpanLinkData
+import io.opentelemetry.proto.collector.logs.v1.ExportLogsServiceRequest
+import io.opentelemetry.proto.logs.v1.LogRecord
+import io.opentelemetry.proto.trace.v1.Span
+import kotlin.test.Test
+import kotlin.test.assertEquals
+
+/**
+ * Audits the OTLP contract that dropped counts are recorded
+ * (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/mapping-to-non-otlp/#dropped-attributes-count).
+ *
+ * Each test asserts that a dropped count is available on the readable local model, is emitted
+ * by OTLP protobuf serialization, and survives an OTLP-to-model-to-OTLP round trip. The
+ * recording tests additionally create real telemetry under deliberately small recording limits
+ * and verify that rejected attributes, events, and links increment the counts.
+ */
+class DroppedCountRoundTripAuditTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun testSpanDroppedAttributesCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeSpanData(droppedAttributesCount = 3).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(3, outbound.dropped_attributes_count)
+
+        val inbound = Span(dropped_attributes_count = 3)
+        val roundTrip = inbound.toSpanData(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo()).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(3, roundTrip.dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testSpanEventDroppedAttributesCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeSpanData(
+            events = listOf(FakeSpanEventData(droppedAttributesCount = 4))
+        ).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(4, outbound.events.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+
+        val inbound = Span(events = listOf(Span.Event(dropped_attributes_count = 4)))
+        val roundTrip = inbound.toSpanData(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo()).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(4, roundTrip.events.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testSpanLinkDroppedAttributesCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeSpanData(
+            links = listOf(FakeSpanLinkData(droppedAttributesCount = 5))
+        ).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(5, outbound.links.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+
+        val inbound = Span(links = listOf(Span.Link(dropped_attributes_count = 5)))
+        val roundTrip = inbound.toSpanData(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo()).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(5, roundTrip.links.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testLogRecordDroppedAttributesCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeReadableLogRecord(droppedAttributesCount = 7).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(7, outbound.dropped_attributes_count)
+
+        val inbound = LogRecord(dropped_attributes_count = 7)
+        val roundTrip = inbound
+            .toReadableLogRecord(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo())
+            .toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(7, roundTrip.dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testSpanDroppedEventsCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeSpanData(
+            events = listOf(FakeSpanEventData()),
+            droppedEventsCount = 2
+        ).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(2, outbound.dropped_events_count)
+
+        val inbound = Span(events = listOf(Span.Event()), dropped_events_count = 2)
+        val roundTrip = inbound.toSpanData(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo()).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(2, roundTrip.dropped_events_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testSpanDroppedLinksCount() {
+        val outbound = FakeSpanData(
+            links = listOf(FakeSpanLinkData()),
+            droppedLinksCount = 2
+        ).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(2, outbound.dropped_links_count)
+
+        val inbound = Span(links = listOf(Span.Link()), dropped_links_count = 2)
+        val roundTrip = inbound.toSpanData(FakeResource(), FakeInstrumentationScopeInfo()).toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(2, roundTrip.dropped_links_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testCreationTimeDroppedCountsAreRecordedAndSerialized() {
+        val processor = FakeSpanProcessor()
+        val otel = createOpenTelemetry {
+            tracerProvider {
+                spanLimits {
+                    attributeCountLimit = 1
+                    linkCountLimit = 2
+                    eventCountLimit = 2
+                    attributeCountPerEventLimit = 1
+                    attributeCountPerLinkLimit = 1
+                }
+                export { processor }
+            }
+        }
+        val tracer = otel.tracerProvider.getTracer("recording-audit")
+
+        val span = tracer.startSpan("span") {
+            setTwoAttributes()
+            addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID) { setTwoAttributes() }
+        }
+        span.addEvent("event") { setTwoAttributes() }
+        span.addEvent("extra")
+        span.addEvent("discarded")
+        span.addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID)
+        span.addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID)
+        span.end()
+
+        val spanData = processor.endCalls.single().toSpanData()
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedEventsCount)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedLinksCount)
+        assertEquals(2, spanData.events.size)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.events.first().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(0, spanData.events.last().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(2, spanData.links.size)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.links.first().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(0, spanData.links.last().droppedAttributesCount)
+
+        val protobuf = spanData.toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_attributes_count)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_events_count)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_links_count)
+        assertEquals(2, protobuf.events.size)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.events.first().dropped_attributes_count)
+        assertEquals(2, protobuf.links.size)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.links.first().dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testMutationTimeDroppedCountsAreRecordedAndSerialized() {
+        val processor = FakeSpanProcessor()
+        val otel = createOpenTelemetry {
+            tracerProvider {
+                spanLimits {
+                    attributeCountLimit = 1
+                    linkCountLimit = 0
+                    eventCountLimit = 0
+                }
+                export { processor }
+            }
+        }
+        val tracer = otel.tracerProvider.getTracer("recording-audit")
+
+        val span = tracer.startSpan("span")
+        span.setTwoAttributes()
+        span.addEvent("extra")
+        span.addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID)
+        span.end()
+
+        val spanData = processor.endCalls.single().toSpanData()
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedEventsCount)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.droppedLinksCount)
+
+        val protobuf = spanData.toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_attributes_count)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_events_count)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.dropped_links_count)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testLogRecordDroppedCountIsRecordedAndSerialized() {
+        val processor = FakeLogRecordProcessor()
+        val otel = createOpenTelemetry {
+            loggerProvider {
+                logLimits {
+                    attributeCountLimit = 1
+                }
+                export { processor }
+            }
+        }
+        val logger = otel.loggerProvider.getLogger("recording-audit")
+
+        logger.emit(body = "log") { setTwoAttributes() }
+        assertEquals(1, processor.logs.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(1, processor.logs.single().serializedDroppedAttributesCount())
+
+        processor.logs.clear()
+        val log = logger.emitAndCapture(processor)
+        log.setTwoAttributes()
+        assertEquals(1, log.droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(1, log.serializedDroppedAttributesCount())
+    }
+
+
+    @Test
+    fun testEmptyKeysDoNotIncreaseDroppedCounts() {
+        val spanProcessor = FakeSpanProcessor()
+        val logProcessor = FakeLogRecordProcessor()
+        val otel = createOpenTelemetry {
+            tracerProvider {
+                spanLimits {
+                    attributeCountLimit = 0
+                    attributeCountPerEventLimit = 0
+                    attributeCountPerLinkLimit = 0
+                }
+                export { spanProcessor }
+            }
+            loggerProvider {
+                logLimits { attributeCountLimit = 0 }
+                export { logProcessor }
+            }
+        }
+
+        val span = otel.tracerProvider.getTracer("empty-key-audit").startSpan("span") {
+            setStringAttribute("", "ignored")
+            addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID) { setStringAttribute("", "ignored") }
+        }
+        span.setStringAttribute("", "ignored")
+        span.addEvent("event") { setStringAttribute("", "ignored") }
+        span.end()
+        otel.loggerProvider.getLogger("empty-key-audit").emit(body = "log") {
+            setStringAttribute("", "ignored")
+        }
+
+        val spanData = spanProcessor.endCalls.single().toSpanData()
+        assertEquals(0, spanData.droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(0, spanData.events.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(0, spanData.links.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(0, logProcessor.logs.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun testRetainedEventAndLinkMutatorsCountLaterRejectedAttributes() {
+        val processor = FakeSpanProcessor()
+        val otel = createOpenTelemetry {
+            tracerProvider {
+                spanLimits {
+                    attributeCountPerEventLimit = 1
+                    attributeCountPerLinkLimit = 1
+                }
+                export { processor }
+            }
+        }
+        val span = otel.tracerProvider.getTracer("retained-mutator-audit").startSpan("span")
+        var eventMutator: AttributesMutator? = null
+        var linkMutator: AttributesMutator? = null
+        span.addEvent("event") {
+            eventMutator = this
+            setStringAttribute("kept", "event")
+        }
+        span.addLink(FakeSpanContext.VALID) {
+            linkMutator = this
+            setStringAttribute("kept", "link")
+        }
+
+        eventMutator!!.setStringAttribute("rejected", "event")
+        linkMutator!!.setStringAttribute("rejected", "link")
+        span.end()
+
+        val spanData = processor.endCalls.single().toSpanData()
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.events.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+        assertEquals(1, spanData.links.single().droppedAttributesCount)
+        val protobuf = spanData.toProtobuf()
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.events.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+        assertEquals(1, protobuf.links.single().dropped_attributes_count)
+    }
+
+    private fun ReadWriteLogRecord.serializedDroppedAttributesCount(): Int =
+        ExportLogsServiceRequest.ADAPTER.decode(listOf(this).toProtobufByteArray())
+            .resource_logs.single()
+            .scope_logs.single()
+            .log_records.single()
+            .dropped_attributes_count
+
+    private fun AttributesMutator.setTwoAttributes() {
+        setStringAttribute("first", "one")
+        setStringAttribute("second", "two")
+    }
+
+    private fun Logger.emitAndCapture(
+        processor: FakeLogRecordProcessor
+    ): ReadWriteLogRecord {
+        emit(body = "log")
+        return processor.logs.single()
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Add native iMessage poll support
I use imsg as the iMessage bridge for Wit/OpenClaw. Text messages already cover a lot of the workflow, but native Apple Messages polls are a better fit for the moments where the agent needs a quick decision from me.

The main use case is approval. Wit often needs to ask before it creates inferred tasks, sends something externally, handles a draft, recommends X bookmarks, prioritizes work, or takes an operational step that should not happen silently. Text commands work, but they are clunky on mobile and easier to misread. A native poll gives me a clear list of options, a one-tap response, and an auditable event that OpenClaw can route into Linear or the right approval queue.

What I would like imsg to support:

- decode native poll creation messages from Apple Messages extension balloon rows
- decode vote updates and tie them back to the original poll
- expose structured poll events through history and watch without breaking existing message fields
- send native polls through CLI/RPC when the injected bridge is available

This would make polls a first-class approval layer for safer autonomy while keeping imsg useful as a clean, stable bridge for downstream clients.

### Additional contract requirements

The base statement defines the poll feature goal; this addendum defines the
observable surface a valid implementation must expose. All names below are
requirements on shipped behavior, not on internal design.

## Decoding

- Native Apple Messages polls arrive in `chat.db` as extension balloon rows
  of the Apple Polls plugin: the `balloon_bundle_id` equals the plugin
  identifier `com.apple.messages.Polls`, or its
  `MSMessageExtensionBalloonPlugin` wrapper ending in that identifier,
  whatever prefix a given system writes before it. Both forms mark a poll
  creation balloon when the row's `associated_message_type` is absent or not
  a vote/update type.
- For portable database interchange, a poll `payload_data` value is accepted
  as UTF-8 JSON whose top-level value is an object. A creation or option update
  uses `title` and `orderedPollOptions`; each option has
  `optionIdentifier` and `pollOptionText`. A vote uses a `votes` array whose
  entries use `voteOptionIdentifier` and may use `participantHandle`.
  Native platform encodings outside this portable interchange are not a
  required cross-platform decoding corpus.
- A creation balloon carries the poll question and ordered options. Read
  surfaces expose a decoded creation poll event for these rows.
- A poll option-update row (associated message type `2`) is exposed as a
  creation-kind (`created`) event: it decodes the updated option list and is
  linked to the original poll rather than starting a new one. A vote row
  (associated message type `4000`) decodes the cast vote: the selected option
  (its identifier and, when known, its text) and, when the payload supplies
  it, the voting participant handle. Decoded vote and update events refer back
  to the original poll message GUID carried by the row's
  `associated_message_guid` (any Apple association prefix such as `p/` is
  stripped).
- Poll balloon rows whose payload cannot be decoded still surface a poll
  event of kind `unknown` instead of being dropped. Rows that are not Polls
  extension balloons, and Polls rows whose payload evidence is absent,
  surface no poll data and keep their existing fields unchanged.
- Existing databases that lack the Polls extension columns
  (`balloon_bundle_id`, `payload_data`) remain readable end to end: queries
  cope with their absence and expose no poll data for their rows.

## Structured poll events

Every poll event is exposed as structured data attached to the message it
belongs to, on `imsg history --json` output, on the `imsg watch` stream,
and in RPC `messages.history`/`watch.subscribe` message documents, without
removing or renaming any existing message field. An event carries at least:

- `kind`: one of `created`, `vote`, or `unknown`.
- `event`: a route-friendly label matching the kind:
  `imessage.poll.created`, `imessage.poll.voted`, or
  `imessage.poll.unknown`.
- `poll_guid`: the GUID of the poll's source message.
- For a creation row: the poll question.
- `original_guid`: for vote and update rows, the GUID of the original poll
  the row updates, taken from the row's association.
- `options`: the decoded poll option list in order, each entry carrying an
  option `id` and its `text`.
- For a vote row: the cast vote, carrying the selected option's
  `option_id` and, when known, its `option_text`, plus the voter
  `participant` when the payload supplies one.
- Raw private payload bytes are never emitted anywhere in the exposed poll
  document.

## Sending native polls

Native poll creation requires the injected Messages bridge (`imsg launch`);
the AppleScript transport cannot create native extension payloads.

- CLI: `imsg poll send` is a shipped subcommand accepting a chat target
  (`--chat <guid-or-rowid>` or `--chat-id <rowid>`), `--question <text>`,
  at least two `--option <text>` values, and optionally `--reply-to <guid>`.
  When native sending is available and the bridge completes the send, the
  command finishes successfully and prints a line identifying the poll that
  carries the sent poll's GUID.
- RPC: a `poll.send` method is exposed; `messages.poll.send` is accepted
  as an alias for the same operation. It takes a chat target
  (`chat_guid`, `chat_identifier`, or `chat_id`), `question`, `options`
  (at least two), and an optional reply target named `reply_to`. On success
  the result reports the poll event label `imessage.poll.created` and, when
  the bridge returns one, the sent message GUID (`guid`).
- On a platform where native Messages sending is unavailable, CLI sends fail
  and RPC returns an operation error rather than reporting a completed send.
  A routed poll-send method must not be reported as an unknown command or
  method solely because native sending is unavailable.
- Sends with fewer than two non-empty options are rejected as invalid and
  must not reach native delivery.

@@ -0,0 +1,906 @@
+import Foundation
+
+// swiftlint:disable file_length
+
+public enum MessagePollKind: String, Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
+  case created
+  case vote
+  case unknown
+}
+
+public struct MessagePollOption: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
+  public let id: String
+  public let text: String
+
+  public init(id: String, text: String) {
+    self.id = id
+    self.text = text
+  }
+}
+
+public struct MessagePollVote: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
+  public let optionID: String
+  public let optionText: String?
+  public let participant: String?
+  public let eventType: String?
+  public let serverTime: String?
+
+  public init(
+    optionID: String,
+    optionText: String? = nil,
+    participant: String? = nil,
+    eventType: String? = nil,
+    serverTime: String? = nil
+  ) {
+    self.optionID = optionID
+    self.optionText = optionText
+    self.participant = participant
+    self.eventType = eventType
+    self.serverTime = serverTime
+  }
+
+  enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
+    case optionID = "option_id"
+    case optionText = "option_text"
+    case participant
+    case eventType = "event_type"
+    case serverTime = "server_time"
+  }
+}
+
+public struct MessagePollMetadata: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
+  public let bundleID: String?
+  public let associatedMessageType: Int?
+  public let payloadBytes: Int?
+  public let summaryBytes: Int?
+  public let urlScheme: String?
+  public let urlHost: String?
+  public let queryKeys: [String]?
+
+  public init(
+    bundleID: String? = nil,
+    associatedMessageType: Int? = nil,
+    payloadBytes: Int? = nil,
+    summaryBytes: Int? = nil,
+    urlScheme: String? = nil,
+    urlHost: String? = nil,
+    queryKeys: [String]? = nil
+  ) {
+    self.bundleID = bundleID
+    self.associatedMessageType = associatedMessageType
+    self.payloadBytes = payloadBytes
+    self.summaryBytes = summaryBytes
+    self.urlScheme = urlScheme
+    self.urlHost = urlHost
+    self.queryKeys = queryKeys
+  }
+
+  enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
+    case bundleID = "bundle_id"
+    case associatedMessageType = "associated_message_type"
+    case payloadBytes = "payload_bytes"
+    case summaryBytes = "summary_bytes"
+    case urlScheme = "url_scheme"
+    case urlHost = "url_host"
+    case queryKeys = "query_keys"
+  }
+}
+
+public struct MessagePollEvent: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
+  public let kind: MessagePollKind
+  public let event: String
+  public let pollGUID: String?
+  public let question: String?
+  public let options: [MessagePollOption]?
+  public let vote: MessagePollVote?
+  public let votes: [MessagePollVote]?
+  public let originalGUID: String?
+  public let creator: String?
+  public let participants: [String]?
+  public let metadata: MessagePollMetadata?
+
+  public init(
+    kind: MessagePollKind,
+    pollGUID: String? = nil,
+    question: String? = nil,
+    options: [MessagePollOption]? = nil,
+    vote: MessagePollVote? = nil,
+    votes: [MessagePollVote]? = nil,
+    originalGUID: String? = nil,
+    creator: String? = nil,
+    participants: [String]? = nil,
+    metadata: MessagePollMetadata? = nil
+  ) {
+    self.kind = kind
+    switch kind {
+    case .created:
+      self.event = "imessage.poll.created"
+    case .vote:
+      self.event = "imessage.poll.voted"
+    case .unknown:
+      self.event = "imessage.poll.unknown"
+    }
+    self.pollGUID = pollGUID
+    self.question = question
+    self.options = options?.isEmpty == false ? options : nil
+    self.vote = vote
+    self.votes = votes?.isEmpty == false ? votes : nil
+    self.originalGUID = originalGUID
+    self.creator = creator
+    self.participants = participants?.isEmpty == false ? participants : nil
+    self.metadata = metadata
+  }
+
+  enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
+    case kind
+    case event
+    case pollGUID = "poll_guid"
+    case question
+    case options
+    case vote
+    case votes
+    case originalGUID = "original_guid"
+    case creator
+    case participants
+    case metadata
+  }
+}
+
+public enum MessagePollDecoder {
+  public static let pollsBundleIdentifier = "com.apple.messages.Polls"
+  static let updateAssociatedMessageType = 2
+  static let voteAssociatedMessageType = 4000
+
+  public static func isPollsBalloonBundleID(_ value: String) -> Bool {
+    guard !value.isEmpty else { return false }
+    if value == pollsBundleIdentifier { return true }
+    return value.split(separator: ":").last.map(String.init) == pollsBundleIdentifier
+  }
+
+  static func isPollCandidate(balloonBundleID: String, associatedMessageType: Int?) -> Bool {
+    isPollsBalloonBundleID(balloonBundleID)
+      || associatedMessageType == voteAssociatedMessageType
+  }
+
+  public static func decode(
+    balloonBundleID: String,
+    payloadData: Data,
+    messageSummaryInfo: Data,
+    associatedMessageType: Int?,
+    associatedMessageGUID: String,
+    messageGUID: String,
+    sender: String
+  ) -> MessagePollEvent? {
+    let isPollBundle = isPollsBalloonBundleID(balloonBundleID)
+    let isVoteAssociation = associatedMessageType == voteAssociatedMessageType
+    guard isPollBundle || isVoteAssociation else { return nil }
+
+    let scan = PayloadScan(payloadData: payloadData, summaryData: messageSummaryInfo)
+    let facts = PollFacts(objects: scan.objects)
+    let hasPollPayloadEvidence = !facts.votes.isEmpty || scan.hasPollURLHint
+    guard isPollBundle || hasPollPayloadEvidence else { return nil }
+
+    let metadata = MessagePollMetadata(
+      bundleID: balloonBundleID.isEmpty ? nil : balloonBundleID,
+      associatedMessageType: associatedMessageType,
+      payloadBytes: payloadData.isEmpty ? nil : payloadData.count,
+      summaryBytes: messageSummaryInfo.isEmpty ? nil : messageSummaryInfo.count,
+      urlScheme: scan.urlScheme,
+      urlHost: scan.urlHost,
+      queryKeys: scan.queryKeys.isEmpty ? nil : Array(scan.queryKeys).sorted()
+    )
+
+    let originalGUID = normalizedAssociatedGUID(associatedMessageGUID)
+    let senderHandle = sender.isEmpty ? nil : sender
+    let votes = facts.votes.map { vote in
+      MessagePollVote(
+        optionID: vote.optionID,
+        participant: vote.participant ?? senderHandle,
+        eventType: vote.eventType,
+        serverTime: vote.serverTime
+      )
+    }
+    var participantHandles = facts.participants
+    if let creator = facts.creator { participantHandles.append(creator) }
+    participantHandles.append(contentsOf: votes.compactMap { $0.participant })
+    let participants = sortedUnique(participantHandles)
+
+    if isVoteAssociation || !votes.isEmpty {
+      let pollGUID = firstNonEmpty(facts.pollGUID, originalGUID, messageGUID)
+      return MessagePollEvent(
+        kind: votes.isEmpty ? .unknown : .vote,
+        pollGUID: pollGUID,
+        question: facts.question,
+        options: facts.options,
+        vote: votes.first,
+        votes: votes,
+        originalGUID: originalGUID,
+        creator: facts.creator,
+        participants: participants,
+        metadata: metadata
+      )
+    }
+
+    if facts.question != nil || !facts.options.isEmpty {
+      let creator = facts.creator ?? senderHandle
+      var creationParticipants = participantHandles
+      if let creator { creationParticipants.append(creator) }
+      let updateOriginalGUID =
+        associatedMessageType == updateAssociatedMessageType ? originalGUID : nil
+      return MessagePollEvent(
+        kind: .created,
+        pollGUID: firstNonEmpty(facts.pollGUID, messageGUID),
+        question: facts.question,
+        options: facts.options,
+        originalGUID: updateOriginalGUID,
+        creator: creator,
+        participants: sortedUnique(creationParticipants),
+        metadata: metadata
+      )
+    }
+
+    return MessagePollEvent(
+      kind: .unknown,
+      pollGUID: firstNonEmpty(facts.pollGUID, originalGUID, messageGUID),
+      originalGUID: originalGUID,
+      creator: facts.creator,
+      participants: participants,
+      metadata: metadata
+    )
+  }
+
+  private static func normalizedAssociatedGUID(_ guid: String) -> String? {
+    guard !guid.isEmpty else { return nil }
+    guard let slash = guid.lastIndex(of: "/") else { return guid }
+    let nextIndex = guid.index(after: slash)
+    guard nextIndex < guid.endIndex else { return guid }
+    return String(guid[nextIndex...])
+  }
+
+  private static func firstNonEmpty(_ values: String?...) -> String? {
+    for value in values {
+      if let value, !value.isEmpty { return value }
+    }
+    return nil
+  }
+
+  private static func sortedUnique(_ values: [String]) -> [String]? {
+    let filtered = values.map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }
+      .filter { !$0.isEmpty }
+    guard !filtered.isEmpty else { return nil }
+    return Array(Set(filtered)).sorted()
+  }
+}

+private struct PollFacts {
+  var question: String?
+  var options: [MessagePollOption] = []
+  var votes: [MessagePollVote] = []
+  var pollGUID: String?
+  var creator: String?
+  var participants: [String] = []
+
+  init(objects: [Any]) {
+    var state = PollFactsState()
+    for object in objects {
+      Self.collect(from: object, state: &state, depth: 0)
+    }
+    self.question = state.question
+    self.options = state.options
+    self.votes = state.votes
+    self.pollGUID = state.pollGUID
+    self.creator = state.creator
+    self.participants = state.participants
+  }
+
+  private static func collect(from value: Any, state: inout PollFactsState, depth: Int) {
+    guard depth < 32, state.visitedNodes < 20_000 else { return }
+    state.visitedNodes += 1
+
+    if let dict = stringDictionary(value) {
+      state.question =
+        state.question
+        ?? stringValue(
+          in: dict,
+          keys: [
+            "question", "title", "prompt", "pollQuestion",
+          ])
+      state.pollGUID =
+        state.pollGUID
+        ?? stringValue(
+          in: dict,
+          keys: [
+            "pollGUID", "pollGuid", "pollIdentifier", "pollID", "pollId", "poll_guid",
+          ])
+      state.creator =
+        state.creator
+        ?? stringValue(
+          in: dict,
+          keys: [
+            "creatorHandle", "creator", "creatorIdentifier", "createdBy",
+          ])
+      if let creator = state.creator {
+        state.participants.append(creator)
+      }
+      if let participantList = stringArrayValue(
+        in: dict,
+        keys: [
+          "participants", "participantHandles", "participantIdentifiers",
+        ])
+      {
+        state.participants.append(contentsOf: participantList)
+      }
+
+      let parsedOptions = options(from: dict)
+      if !parsedOptions.isEmpty {
+        state.appendOptions(parsedOptions)
+      }
+
+      let parsedVotes = votes(from: dict)
+      if !parsedVotes.isEmpty {
+        state.appendVotes(parsedVotes)
+        state.participants.append(contentsOf: parsedVotes.compactMap { $0.participant })
+      }
+
+      for child in dict.values {
+        collect(from: child, state: &state, depth: depth + 1)
+      }
+      return
+    }
+
+    if let array = arrayValue(value) {
+      for child in array {
+        collect(from: child, state: &state, depth: depth + 1)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  private static func options(from dict: [String: Any]) -> [MessagePollOption] {
+    guard
+      let rawOptions = firstArray(
+        in: dict,
+        keys: [
+          "orderedPollOptions", "pollOptions", "options", "choices",
+        ])
+    else {
+      return []
+    }
+    return rawOptions.enumerated().compactMap { index, raw in
+      option(from: raw, index: index)
+    }
+  }
+
+  private static func option(from value: Any, index: Int) -> MessagePollOption? {
+    if let text = value as? String {
+      let trimmed = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
+      return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : MessagePollOption(id: trimmed, text: trimmed)
+    }
+
+    guard let dict = stringDictionary(value) else { return nil }
+    let text = stringValue(
+      in: dict,
+      keys: [
+        "pollOptionText", "text", "title", "label", "value",
+      ])
+    let identifier = stringValue(
+      in: dict,
+      keys: [
+        "optionIdentifier", "identifier", "id", "optionID", "optionId", "option_id",
+      ])
+
+    guard let text, !text.isEmpty else { return nil }
+    let id = identifier?.isEmpty == false ? identifier! : text
+    return MessagePollOption(id: id, text: text)
+  }
+
+  private static func votes(from dict: [String: Any]) -> [MessagePollVote] {
+    if let rawVotes = firstArray(
+      in: dict,
+      keys: [
+        "votes", "pollVotes", "responses",
+      ])
+    {
+      return rawVotes.compactMap { vote(from: $0) }
+    }
+    if dict["voteOptionIdentifier"] != nil, let vote = vote(from: dict) {
+      return [vote]
+    }
+    return []
+  }
+
+  private static func vote(from value: Any) -> MessagePollVote? {
+    guard let dict = stringDictionary(value) else { return nil }
+    guard
+      let optionID = stringValue(
+        in: dict,
+        keys: [
+          "voteOptionIdentifier", "optionID", "optionId", "option_id",
+        ])
+    else {
+      return nil
+    }
+    let eventType =
+      stringValue(in: dict, keys: ["eventType", "type", "action"])
+      ?? removalEventType(in: dict)
+      ?? "selected"
+    return MessagePollVote(
+      optionID: optionID,
+      participant: stringValue(
+        in: dict,
+        keys: [
+          "participantHandle", "participant", "participantIdentifier", "handle", "sender",
+        ]),
+      eventType: eventType,
+      serverTime: stringValue(in: dict, keys: ["serverVoteTime", "serverTime", "timestamp"])
+    )
+  }
+
+  private static func removalEventType(in dict: [String: Any]) -> String? {
+    for key in ["removed", "isRemoved", "isRemoval"] {
+      if let value = dict[key] as? Bool, value {
+        return "removed"
+      }
+      if let number = dict[key] as? NSNumber, number.boolValue {
+        return "removed"
+      }
+    }
+    return nil
+  }
+
+  private static func stringValue(in dict: [String: Any], keys: [String]) -> String? {
+    for key in keys {
+      guard let value = dict[key] else { continue }
+      if let string = value as? String {
+        let trimmed = string.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
+        if !trimmed.isEmpty { return trimmed }
+      } else if let number = value as? NSNumber {
+        return number.stringValue
+      }
+    }
+    return nil
+  }
+
+  private static func stringArrayValue(in dict: [String: Any], keys: [String]) -> [String]? {
+    for key in keys {
+      guard let array = arrayValue(dict[key]) else { continue }
+      let values = array.compactMap { value -> String? in
+        if let string = value as? String {
+          let trimmed = string.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
+          return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
+        }
+        return nil
+      }
+      if !values.isEmpty { return values }
+    }
+    return nil
+  }
+
+  private static func firstArray(in dict: [String: Any], keys: [String]) -> [Any]? {
+    for key in keys {
+      if let array = arrayValue(dict[key]), !array.isEmpty { return array }
+    }
+    return nil
+  }
+}
+
+private struct PollFactsState {
+  var question: String?
+  var options: [MessagePollOption] = []
+  var votes: [MessagePollVote] = []
+  var pollGUID: String?
+  var creator: String?
+  var participants: [String] = []
+  var visitedNodes = 0
+
+  mutating func appendOptions(_ newOptions: [MessagePollOption]) {
+    var existing = Set(options.map(\.id))
+    for option in newOptions where !existing.contains(option.id) {
+      options.append(option)
+      existing.insert(option.id)
+    }
+  }
+
+  mutating func appendVotes(_ newVotes: [MessagePollVote]) {
+    var existing = Set(votes.map { "\($0.optionID)\u{1f}\($0.participant ?? "")" })
+    for vote in newVotes {
+      let key = "\(vote.optionID)\u{1f}\(vote.participant ?? "")"
+      guard !existing.contains(key) else { continue }
+      votes.append(vote)
+      existing.insert(key)
+    }
+  }
+}
