+(ns org.replikativ.spindel.engine.lost-wakeup-test
+  "Public-API liveness regression tests for the lost-wakeup defect
+  (mult/pub source pump and mailbox consumer freeze permanently when a
+  producer or waiter handoff dies mid-resume).
+
+  These tests are implementation-neutral: they only register consumers
+  through the public mailbox / mult / pub / deferred API, fail one
+  delivery through public cancellation and failure surface, and then
+  observe through the public API that
+
+  1. unaffected consumers keep consuming — queued work after the failed
+     handoff still flows, in FIFO order;
+  2. a failed delivery does not strand the pipeline permanently — there
+     is no silent forever-PENDING state; the delivery either completes
+     or fails loudly (spawn! :on-error fires), and the value handed to
+     the interrupted handoff is not silently dropped;
+  3. mailbox, deferred, mult/pub tap/stream and executor paths all
+     honour the same liveness guarantee (added spins still run).
+
+  No internal event shapes, state layouts, fault hooks or handoff
+  mechanisms are assumed: consumer-throw acceptance is throttled on
+  PUBLIC observation (err recorded / sibling saw it) rather than a
+  fixed post count, and every assertion polls until a deadline instead
+  of pinning thread interleavings."
+  (:refer-clojure :exclude [await])
+  (:require #?(:clj [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
+               :cljs [cljs.test :refer [deftest is testing] :include-macros true])
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.pubsub.mult :as mult]
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.pubsub.pub :as pub]
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.pubsub.buffer :as buf]
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.spin.core :as spin-core]
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.spin.sync :as sync]
+            [is.simm.partial-cps.sequence :refer [anext]]
+            #?(:clj [org.replikativ.spindel.spin.cps :refer [spin]])
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.effects.await :refer [await]]
+            [org.replikativ.spindel.test-helpers :as th])
+  #?(:cljs (:require-macros [org.replikativ.spindel.spin.cps :refer [spin]]
+                            [org.replikativ.spindel.test-helpers :refer [with-ctx async]])))
+
+#?(:clj
+   (defn- poll-until
+     "Poll pred every 10ms up to timeout-ms. Returns truthy success."
+     [pred timeout-ms]
+     (let [deadline (+ (System/currentTimeMillis) timeout-ms)]
+       (loop []
+         (cond
+           (pred) true
+           (>= (System/currentTimeMillis) deadline) (boolean (pred))
+           :else (do (Thread/sleep 10) (recur)))))))
+
+#?(:clj
+   (deftest failed-mailbox-handoff-does-not-stop-later-delivery
+     (testing "a callback that dies after a mailbox handoff was admitted does
+               not permanently stop the execution context; a later registered
+               consumer receives later work"
+       (th/with-ctx [ctx]
+         (let [mbx (sync/create-mailbox ctx)
+               failed (atom [])
+               received (atom [])]
+           ;; The two-arity mailbox invocation is the public callback form of
+           ;; a mailbox take.  Registration finishes before the post below,
+           ;; so this is an admitted handoff rather than a cancellation before
+           ;; an operation began.
+           (mbx (fn [message]
+                  (swap! failed conj message)
+                  (throw (ex-info "mailbox handoff stopped" {:message message})))
+                (fn [_] nil))
+           (sync/post! mbx :during-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @failed) 4000)
+               "the failed handoff was entered")
+           (mbx (fn [message] (swap! received conj message))
+                (fn [_] nil))
+           (sync/post! mbx :after-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:after-failure] @received) 5000)
+               "a consumer registered after the failure receives later work exactly once"))))))
+
+#?(:clj
+   (deftest failed-deferred-handoff-keeps-other-reader-live
+     (testing "a failed admitted deferred reader cannot strand another reader
+               or prevent a later deferred delivery"
+       (th/with-ctx [ctx]
+         (let [d (sync/create-deferred ctx)
+               entered (atom [])
+               sibling (atom [])]
+           ;; These are public Deferred read callbacks.  Both readers are
+           ;; registered before delivery, and the failing callback records
+           ;; entry before it dies, making the failed handoff observable
+           ;; without relying on runtime internals.
+           (d (fn [value]
+                (swap! entered conj value)
+                (throw (ex-info "deferred handoff stopped" {:value value})))
+              (fn [_] nil))
+           (d (fn [value] (swap! sibling conj value))
+              (fn [_] nil))
+           (sync/deliver! d :during-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @entered) 4000)
+               "the failing reader was entered")
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @sibling) 5000)
+               "the unaffected reader receives the admitted value exactly once")
+           (let [later (sync/create-deferred ctx)
+                 later-value (atom nil)]
+             (later (fn [value] (reset! later-value value)) (fn [_] nil))
+             (sync/deliver! later :after-failure)
+             (is (poll-until #(= :after-failure @later-value) 5000)
+                 "later deferred delivery remains live"))
+           ;; A deferred that already holds a value must keep handing that
+           ;; value to readers registered after delivery: the keyword below is

+           ;; delivery and confirms assignment through the public callback path.
+           (let [assigned (sync/create-deferred ctx)
+                 payload :org.replikativ.spindel.spin.sync/not-found
+                 early (atom [])
+                 early-errors (atom [])
+                 late (atom [])
+                 late-errors (atom [])
+                 awaited (atom nil)
+                 await-errors (atom [])]

+                       (fn [e] (swap! early-errors conj e)))
+             (sync/deliver! assigned payload)
+             (is (poll-until #(= [payload] @early) 5000)
+                 "the early reader observes the delivered value")
+             (assigned (fn [v] (swap! late conj v))
+                       (fn [e] (swap! late-errors conj e)))
+             (is (poll-until #(= [payload] @late) 5000)
+                 "a callback reader registered after delivery receives the delivered value")
+             (sync/spawn! (spin (reset! awaited (await assigned)))
+                          {:on-error (fn [e] (swap! await-errors conj e))})
+             (is (poll-until #(= payload @awaited) 5000)
+                 "a spin awaiting the already-delivered deferred resolves with the value")
+             (Thread/sleep 100)
+             (is (= [payload] @late) "the late reader is called exactly once")
+             (is (= [payload] @early) "the early reader is called exactly once")
+             (is (empty? @late-errors) "the late reader saw no error")
+             (is (empty? @await-errors) "the awaiting spin saw no error")))))))
+
+#?(:clj
+   (deftest await-thunk-mailbox-failure-rejects-owner-and-keeps-queue-live
+     (testing "a mailbox await-thunk that fails before resolve rejects its owning spin without re-queuing the consumed item"
+       (th/with-ctx [ctx]
+         (let [mbx (sync/create-mailbox ctx)
+               entered (atom [])
+               errors (atom [])
+               received (atom [])]
+           (sync/spawn!
+            (spin
+             (await
+              (fn [resolve reject]
+                (mbx (fn [message]
+                       (swap! entered conj message)
+                       (throw (ex-info "mailbox adapter failed" {})))
+                     reject))))
+            {:on-error #(swap! errors conj %)})
+           (sync/post! mbx :during-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @entered) 4000)
+               "the admitted mailbox item reaches the adapter")
+           (is (poll-until #(seq @errors) 5000)
+               "the failed adapter handoff reaches its owning spin's error path")

+            (spin
+             (loop []
+               (swap! received conj (await mbx))
+               (recur))))
+           (sync/post! mbx :after-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(seq @received) 5000)
+               "a consumer registered after rejection receives later work")
+           (is (= [:after-failure] @received)
+               "the already-consumed failing item is not re-queued to another mailbox consumer"))))))
+
+#?(:clj
+   (deftest await-thunk-deferred-failure-rejects-owner-and-keeps-readers-live
+     (testing "a deferred await-thunk that fails before resolve rejects its owning spin while sibling and later readers proceed"
+       (th/with-ctx [ctx]
+         (let [d (sync/create-deferred ctx)
+               entered (atom [])
+               sibling (atom [])
+               errors (atom [])]
+           (sync/spawn!
+            (spin
+             (await
+              (fn [resolve reject]
+                (d (fn [value]
+                     (swap! entered conj value)
+                     (throw (ex-info "deferred adapter failed" {})))
+                   reject))))
+            {:on-error #(swap! errors conj %)})
+           (d (fn [value] (swap! sibling conj value)) (fn [_] nil))
+           (sync/deliver! d :during-failure)
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @entered) 4000)
+               "the admitted deferred value reaches the adapter")
+           (is (poll-until #(seq @errors) 5000)
+               "the failed adapter handoff reaches its owning spin's error path")
+           (is (poll-until #(= [:during-failure] @sibling) 5000)
+               "the unaffected deferred reader receives the admitted value exactly once")
+           (let [later (sync/create-deferred ctx)
+                 later-value (atom nil)]
+             (sync/spawn! (spin (reset! later-value (await later))))
+             (sync/deliver! later :after-failure)
+             (is (poll-until #(= :after-failure @later-value) 5000)
+                 "a later deferred await remains live on the same execution context")))))))
+
+;; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+;; Mailbox: a producer future cancelled mid-post must not wedge the pipeline
+;; -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+#?(:clj
+   (deftest mailbox-post-cancelled-producer-pipeline-stays-live
+     (testing "a producer future cancelled while the consumer's resumed
+             delivery is parked mid-resume leaves the unaffected consumer
+             live: every post whose admission to the mailbox completed
+             before the cancellation is delivered exactly once, in FIFO
+             order, and the consumer still serves posts made after the
+             kill"
+       (th/with-ctx [ctx]
+         (let [mbx (sync/create-mailbox ctx)
+               resumed (java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch. 1)
+               unblock (java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch. 1)
+               parked? (atom true)
+               seen (atom [])]
+           ;; Consumer: the FIRST delivery parks mid-resume until the test
+           ;; releases it, so the producer's burst provably posts into a
+           ;; mailbox whose waiter handoff is in flight (the wedge window)
+           ;; on every run — no wall-clock luck involved.
+           (sync/spawn!
+            (spin
+             (loop []
+               (let [m (await mbx)]
+                 (when @parked?
+                   (reset! parked? false)
+                   (.countDown resumed)
+                   (is (.await unblock 10 java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit/SECONDS)
+                       "test released the parked resume"))
+                 (swap! seen conj m)
+                 (recur)))))
+           (sync/post! mbx :first)
+           (is (.await resumed 5 java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit/SECONDS)
+               "consumer resume parked deterministically")
+           ;; Producer burst from a future; cancelled while the consumer's
+           ;; resumed delivery is still parked. Every successfully
+           ;; submitted post counts down the admission barrier, so the
+           ;; test observes through the public API exactly which posts
+           ;; were admitted before the cancellation landed.
+           (let [admitted (java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch. 10)
+                 producer (future
+                            (doseq [m (range 1 50)]
+                              (sync/post! mbx m)
+                              (.countDown admitted)))]
+             (is (.await admitted 5 java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit/SECONDS)
+                 "at least 10 posts were provably admitted to the mailbox")
+             (future-cancel producer)
+             (try @producer (catch Throwable _ nil)))
+           (.countDown unblock)
+           ;; Delivery guarantee: everything posted BEFORE the kill —
+           ;; :first plus at least the 10 provably admitted posts — must
+           ;; surface, at most once, in order. How far the producer got
+           ;; beyond the 10th admission is deliberately unconstrained:
+           ;; a post whose admission did not complete before cancellation
+           ;; carries no delivery guarantee, so this test never pins the
+           ;; full attempted burst.
+           (is (poll-until #(<= 11 (count @seen)) 5000)
+               "the parked delivery plus the provably admitted posts drained after the kill")
+           (is (= :first (first @seen)) "the parked delivery surfaced first")
+           (is (every? number? (rest @seen)) "then the producer's posts")
+           (is (apply < (filter number? @seen))
+               "queued posts arrived in FIFO order")
+           (is (= (filter number? @seen) (distinct (filter number? @seen)))
+               "no admitted message was delivered twice")
+           ;; consumer still live for work posted after the kill —
+           ;; this is the reported wedge: posts arriving after the
+           ;; producer's death must not queue into the void
+           (sync/post! mbx :after-kill)
+           (is (poll-until #(= :after-kill (peek @seen)) 4000)
+               "consumer still live for work posted after the producer was cancelled mid-delivery")
+           ;; settling window: nothing may be re-delivered
+           (Thread/sleep 250)
+           (is (= @seen (distinct @seen))
+               "no message was delivered twice across the failed handoff"))))))

+           ;; The interrupted delivery: mail the trigger plus a run of
+           ;; ordinary traffic. Whatever handoff discipline the runtime

problem_statement:
Expose a transaction-only API separate from `Mutation`
`Mutation` currently bundles two separate concerns:

- provider lifetime / transaction semantics for an async side-effect
- built-in side-effect state (`idle` / `pending` / `error` / `success`)

The first part is useful on its own.

Sometimes I want the lifetime guarantees of `Mutation.run(...)/MutationTransaction.get(...)`, but I do not want to model the operation as a mutation, because I already have my own state management.

This is a fairly subtle topic with a few closely related behaviors. I may be mixing some of them up, so apologies in advance if any detail below is not quite phrased right.

## Problem

I have a notifier that already owns its UI state. Inside one action, I need to await one or more `autoDispose` providers safely until their results arrive.

A plain `ref.read(provider.future)` is not enough for that, because it does not keep the provider alive until the future completes.

- `ref.read(slowValueProvider.future)` does not keep the `autoDispose` provider alive until the future completes
- `MutationTransaction.get(slowValueProvider.future)` does keep it alive until completion

This is very close to the scenario discussed [here](https://github.com/rrousselGit/riverpod/issues/4336#issuecomment-4083687233):

```dart
final slowValueProvider = FutureProvider.autoDispose((ref) {
  final completer = Completer<String>();
  final timer = Timer(const Duration(seconds: 1), () {
    if (!completer.isCompleted) {
      completer.complete('first');
    }
  });

  ref.onDispose(() {
    timer.cancel();
    if (!completer.isCompleted) {
      completer.completeError(StateError('disposed before completion'));
    }
  });

  return completer.future;
});
```

Today, the only built-in high-level API I know for this is `Mutation`.

At a lower level, this can also be built manually with `ref.container.listen(...)` plus explicit subscription cleanup. But that is exactly the kind of plumbing I would rather not have to write in app code.

Using `Mutation`, it looks like this:

```dart
class ExampleNotifier extends Notifier<void> {
  static final _load = Mutation<String>();

  Future<String> loadValue() =>
      _load.run(ref, (tx) => tx.get(slowValueProvider.future));
}
```

Without `Mutation`, the obvious equivalent is:

```dart
class ExampleNotifier extends Notifier<void> {
  Future<String> loadValue() => ref.read(slowValueProvider.future);
}
```

But that does not keep the provider alive until the future completes.

What I would rather write is:

[HIDDEN]

As far as I understand, this could be a fairly small abstraction on top of the existing primitives. Conceptually it seems very close to:

- opening one or more `ref.container.listen(...)` subscriptions
- using them to read values safely during the async workflow
- closing those subscriptions when the workflow finishes

That is also why this feels like a missing first-class primitive rather than a new capability.

## Why

It would make it possible to:

- use the safe provider-lifetime semantics without introducing a mutation concept where it does not fit
- avoid duplicating UI state between a notifier and a mutation
- keep `Mutation` focused on the "UI-observable side-effect state machine" use case
- give notifier actions a clearer stable scope for provider access across async gaps, which seems adjacent to the broader invalid-`ref` problem even if it does not solve every such case

## Related context

This might be related to the broader "using `ref` across async gaps" topic, but it is not identical to it.

- https://github.com/rrousselGit/riverpod/issues/4096
- https://github.com/rrousselGit/riverpod/issues/4336#issuecomment-4083687233

That said, I suspect a transaction-only API would also help ergonomically with some of the broader async-gap cases, because it provides a stable scope for provider access during the workflow instead of relying on repeated `ref` access after awaits.

I also wonder whether an alternative would be to make `ref.read(provider.future)` keep the provider alive until the future completes.

The reason I bring that up is that the current behavior feels quite error-prone. It is easy to write `ref.read(provider.future)` and assume that the provider will stay alive until the future completes, when that is not actually true. This seems to be a fairly natural mistake. I have also observed LLMs often making exactly that incorrect assumption when generating Riverpod code.

So if a transaction-only API is not the right direction, changing `ref.read(provider.future)` might still be worth considering as a more practical fix for this specific footgun.

### Additional contract requirements

The requested capability is a **transaction-only "action" API**, separate
from `Mutation`. It provides the provider-lifetime guarantees previously
only available through `Mutation.run(...)` — keeping providers accessed
during an asynchronous side-effect alive until that workflow completes —
without the `idle`/`pending`/`error`/`success` side-effect state that
`Mutation` maintains. Implementations are free to choose how they scope
the workflow; only the observable behavior described below is required.

## API surface

- Two top-level functions are added. In `package:riverpod` they are
  exported from the **new entrypoint
  `package:riverpod/experimental/action.dart`**, and they are likewise
  exported from the corresponding new
  `flutter_riverpod/experimental/action.dart` and
  `hooks_riverpod/experimental/action.dart` entrypoints of those
  packages:

  ```dart
  /// Runs [cb], keeping providers read inside it alive until completion.
  Future<ResultT> action<ResultT>(Future<ResultT> Function() cb);

  /// Returns a callback whose invocation behaves like `action(cb)`.
  Future<T> Function() voidAction<T>(Future<T> Function() cb);
  ```

- `action` resolves with the value returned by `cb` and rethrows whatever
  `cb` throws, whether the error is raised synchronously or
  asynchronously.
- `voidAction(cb)` behaves exactly like wrapping `cb` in `action`: the
  returned callback resolves with the callback value, propagates its
  errors (synchronous or asynchronous), and preserves the same
  provider-lifetime behavior.

## Required semantics

- Providers accessed inside the callback through the existing imperative
  APIs — `ProviderContainer.read`, `Ref.read` — are kept alive for the
  whole duration of the action, including across asynchronous gaps. In
  particular, a pending `autoDispose` provider awaited via a read
  performed inside the action callback must **not** be disposed while the
  action is still running.
- When the callback completes (or throws), the subscriptions opened
  because of those accesses are closed; an otherwise unused
  `autoDispose` provider accessed only from within the action is then
  disposed.
- Behavior outside an action is unchanged: a plain
  `container.read(...)` / `ref.read(...)` performed outside any action
  does **not** keep an `autoDispose` provider alive until a returned
  future completes.
- Calling `action` from inside another pending `action` does not end the
  lifetime guarantee of the outer action: subscriptions opened in the
  outer scope stay open for as long as the outer callback is still
  pending.
- No additional restrictions are placed on what may be used inside the
  callback (for example, using `ref.watch`, `ref.listen`, or how
  provider builds triggered inside an action behave are not mandated by
  this contract).

## `Mutation` requirements

- As part of introducing the action facility, `Mutation.run`'s callback
  parameter is normalized to the plain, argument-less form
  `Future<ResultT> Function()` — the callback no longer receives a
  mutation-transaction argument, because providers can be read through
  the existing imperative APIs (`container.read`, `ref.read`) directly
  inside the callback. Callers pass a zero-argument callback.
- Existing `Mutation` behavior is otherwise unchanged: `Mutation.run`
  resolves with the value produced by its callback, propagates callback
  errors, and reports the corresponding success/error mutation states.
  Providers read during the mutation callback stay active until the end
  of the mutation and are released afterwards. These guarantees may be
  implemented by delegating the callback's execution to the action
  facility.

problem_statement:
Feature request: multiple repos via renv.config.repos.override
Setting multiple repos in the `renv.config.repos.override` option would be a great helper in case of managing multiple repositories

### Additional contract requirements

## Repository override syntax

The `renv.config.repos.override` config setting (environment variable
`RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE`) accepts repository overrides in the following
forms:

- A single unnamed repository URL, e.g.
  `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE=https://p3m.dev/cran/latest`. That URL is used as
  the repository override and is treated as the `CRAN` repository.

- One or more named repositories written as `NAME=URL` entries separated by
  semicolons, e.g.
  `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE=CRAN=https://p3m.dev/cran/latest;R_UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev`.
  Each entry maps the name on the left of the first `=` to the rest of the
  entry, so URLs may themselves contain `=` characters (for example, in query
  strings).

This syntax applies consistently wherever `renv` resolves the repository
override at startup, including the bootstrap code embedded in the `activate.R`
script that `renv` writes into projects.

diff --git a/tests/testthat/test-bootstrap.R b/tests/testthat/test-bootstrap.R
index 7b805208..cd31dd81 100644
--- a/tests/testthat/test-bootstrap.R
+++ b/tests/testthat/test-bootstrap.R
@@ -284,3 +284,111 @@ test_that("bootstrap version validation handles 'standard' remote types", {
   )
 
 })
+
+# repos override tests ----------------------------------------------------
+
+test_that("repos override supports unnamed repo", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  url <- "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest"
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = url)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_identical(repos, c(CRAN = url))
+})
+
+test_that("repos override can use 1 named repository", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- "CRAN=https://p3m.dev/cran/latest"
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_equal(repos["CRAN"], c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest"))
+})
+
+test_that("repos override can use 2+ named repositories", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- "CRAN=https://p3m.dev/cran/latest;R_UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev"
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_equal(repos["CRAN"], c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest"))
+  expect_equal(repos["R_UNIV"], c(R_UNIV = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev"))
+  expect_equal(length(repos), 2L)
+})
+
+test_that("repos override can handle `=` in repo urls", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- "R_UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?example=query"
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_equal(repos["R_UNIV"], c(R_UNIV = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?example=query"))
+})
+
+test_that("repos override preserves trailing equals signs and repository names", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- "R+UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?token="
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_identical(repos, c(`R+UNIV` = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?token="))
+})
+
+test_that("repos override can be supplied through the public config option", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest", R_UNIV = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev")
+  renv_scope_options(renv.config.repos.override = override)
+  expect_identical(config$repos.override(), override)
+})
+
+test_that("repos override handle paths", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  override <- "CRAN=https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/noble/latest"
+  renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+  repos <- renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  expect_equal(repos["CRAN"], c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/noble/latest"))
+})
+
+test_that("activate script repos override supports multiple named repos", {
+  renv_tests_scope()
+
+  # locate the activate script bundled with the installed renv package
+  activate <- system.file("resources/activate.R", package = "renv")
+  if (!nzchar(activate))
+    skip("renv is not installed; activate script is unavailable")
+
+  # extract the definition of 'renv_bootstrap_repos' from the activate script,
+  # so that the copy of the function embedded there is exercised directly
+  lines <- readLines(activate, warn = FALSE)
+  start <- grep("^[[:space:]]*renv_bootstrap_repos <- function()", lines)[1L]
+  if (is.na(start))
+    skip("could not locate 'renv_bootstrap_repos' in activate script")
+
+  depth <- 0L
+  end <- start
+  for (index in start:length(lines)) {
+    chars <- strsplit(lines[[index]], "", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
+    depth <- depth + sum(chars == "{") - sum(chars == "}")
+    if (depth == 0L) {
+      end <- index
+      break
+    }
+  }
+
+  definition <- paste(lines[start:end], collapse = "\n")
+  repos <- local({
+    renv_bootstrap_repos <- eval(parse(text = definition))
+
+    override <- "CRAN=https://p3m.dev/cran/latest;R_UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev"
+    renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = override)
+    renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  })
+
+  expect_equal(repos, c(
+    CRAN   = "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest",
+    R_UNIV = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev"
+  ))
+
+  repos <- local({
+    renv_bootstrap_repos <- eval(parse(text = definition))
+    renv_scope_envvars(RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE = "R+UNIV=https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?token=")
+    renv_bootstrap_repos()
+  })
+  expect_identical(repos, c(`R+UNIV` = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev/?token="))
+
+})

problem_statement:
renv::use() without checking repos?
I need help understanding the behavior of `renv::use(.)` outside of a "project".

I'm trying to use `renv::use()` in a fresh R instance in places where `options(repos=)` may not have been defined, so packages that have already been installed correctly in `renv::paths$cache()` with all of their dependencies are not immediately available.

```r
.libPaths(c("/Users/r2/Library/R/4.5", "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library"))
dir.exists("/Users/r2/Library/R/4.5/dplyr")
# [1] TRUE
dir.exists(renv::paths$cache("dplyr"))
# [1] TRUE
renv::use("dplyr", repos=NULL)
# Error in vapply(x, f, ..., FUN.VALUE = character(1)) : 
#   values must be length 1,
#  but FUN(X[[2]]) result is length 0

getOption("repos")
#     CRAN 
# "@CRAN@" 
dir.exists("/Users/r2/Library/R/4.5/mypkg")
# [1] TRUE
dir.exists(renv::paths$cache("mypkg"))
# [1] TRUE
renv::use("mypkg")
# Error: failed to resolve remote 'mypkg' -- package 'mypkg' is not available
```

In interactive use, our `repos=` includes the company repo for packages, and it generally works fine.

I've seen comments or documentation that suggests that `renv::use()` needs to determine the package dependencies from the repo, but all of that information should be readily available (and just as reliable/complete?) from each of the package's `DESCRIPTION` files, and finding the "most recent" version of the package is a trivial scan under `file.path(renv::paths$cache(), "mypkg")`.

When `repos=` is defined as it was when the package was installed, everything is found and `renv::use("mypkg")` works as expected (no warnings/errors).

Is there a reason I can't get `renv::use()` to get what it needs from just the existing pre-filled cache?

### Additional contract requirements

`renv::use()` must be usable with `repos = NULL`, indicating cache-only
operation. In this mode:

- `renv::use(..., repos = NULL)` must succeed for requested packages installed
  through `renv` earlier in the session, making those packages available on the
  library paths configured by `use()`;
- cache-only use must use the cached package records and contents without
  querying package repositories for metadata or installation sources; and
- cache-only restoration from a lockfile must make cached declared dependencies
  needed by the requested packages available as well.

Existing `renv::use()` behavior with regular repositories, with lockfiles, and
with project initialization must keep working.

+renv_use_cacheonly_restore <- function(lockfile, library) {
+
+  # read the lockfile

+renv_use_cacheonly_install <- function(records, library) {
+
+  # determine how to place packages from cache into library
+  linkable <- getOption("renv.cache.linkable", default = FALSE)
+  linker <- if (linkable) renv_file_link else renv_file_copy
+
+  installed <- list()
+
+  enumerate(records, function(package, record) {
+
+    # skip base packages
+    if (package %in% renv_packages_base())
+      return()
+
+    # skip packages that aren't cacheable
+    if (!renv_record_cacheable(record))
+      return()
+
+    # look up package in the cache
+    path <- renv_cache_find(record)
+
+    # if the record has no version (e.g. resolved with latest = FALSE),
+    # fall back to searching the cache for any available version
+    if (!nzchar(path) && is.null(record$Version)) {
+      paths <- renv_cache_list(packages = package)
+      path <- head(paths, n = 1L) %||% ""
+    }
+
+    if (!nzchar(path) || !renv_cache_package_validate(path)) {
+      writef("- Package '%s' is not available in the cache.", package)
+      return()
+    }
+
+    # skip if the target is already up-to-date
+    target <- file.path(library, package)
+    if (renv_file_same(path, target))
+      return()
+
+    # back up any existing installation, then link / copy from cache
+    callback <- renv_file_backup(target)
+    defer(callback())
+    linker(path, target)
+
+    installed[[package]] <<- record
+
+  })
+
+  invisible(installed)
+

+renv_use_package_is_usable <- function(package, libpath) {
+
+  path <- file.path(libpath, package)
+  if (!dir.exists(path))
+    return(FALSE)
+
+  description <- file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION")
+  if (!file.exists(description))
+    return(FALSE)
+
+  dcf <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(read.dcf(description)), error = function(e) NULL)
+  if (is.null(dcf) || nrow(dcf) == 0L)
+    return(FALSE)
+
+  version <- dcf[1L, "Version"]
+  valid <- identical(unname(dcf[1L, "Package"]), package) &&
+    length(version) == 1L && !is.na(version) && nzchar(version)
+  if (!valid)
+    return(FALSE)
+
+  found <- suppressWarnings(find.package(package, lib.loc = libpath, quiet = TRUE))
+  if (length(found) != 1L)
+    return(FALSE)
+
+  identical(renv_path_normalize(found), renv_path_normalize(path))
+
+}
+
+renv_use_expect_installed_package <- function(package, libpath) {
+  expect_true(renv_use_package_is_usable(package, libpath))
+}
+
+renv_use_repository_spy <- function() {
+
+  requests <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  requests$metadata <- character()
+  requests$sources <- character()
+  requests$downloads <- character()
+
+  # Observe repository boundaries rather than banning a particular resolver.
+  # A resolver may inspect local renv cache records without crossing these
+  # metadata or package-source boundaries.
+  local_mocked_bindings(
+    renv_available_packages_query_impl = function(url, ...) {
+      requests$metadata <- c(requests$metadata, "repository metadata")

+    },

+    },
+    download = function(url, ...) {
+      requests$downloads <- c(requests$downloads, "repository download")
+      stop("unexpected package repository download")
+    },
+    .env = parent.frame()
+  )
+
+  requests
+
+}

 })
+
+# Exercise the ordinary restore path with an installed package candidate in an
+# otherwise isolated user or site library. Positive cases have no repository
+# fallback; negative cases put a valid fallback behind an index whose package
+# archive is absent, forcing ordinary restore's sequential retrieval path.
+renv_test_restore_candidate <- function(location = "user",
+                                        remote = FALSE,
+                                        candidate_changes = list(),
+                                        record_changes = list(),
+                                        reuse = FALSE) {
+
+  renv_tests_scope()
+  renv_scope_options(
+    renv.tests.running = FALSE,
+    renv.config.filebacked.cache = FALSE,
+    renv.config.cache.enabled = FALSE,
+    renv.config.sysreqs.check = FALSE
+  )
+
+  init()
+
+  candidate_lib <- renv_scope_tempfile("renv-candidate-library-")
+  ensure_directory(candidate_lib)
+  install("bread", library = candidate_lib)
+
+  user_lib <- renv_scope_tempfile("renv-user-library-")
+  ensure_directory(user_lib)
+  if (identical(location, "user")) {
+    renv_scope_envvars(R_LIBS_USER = candidate_lib, RENV_DEFAULT_R_LIBS_USER = candidate_lib)
+    renv_scope_binding(the$default_libpaths, ".Library.site", user_lib)
+  } else {
+    renv_scope_envvars(R_LIBS_USER = user_lib, RENV_DEFAULT_R_LIBS_USER = user_lib)
+    renv_scope_binding(the$default_libpaths, ".Library.site", candidate_lib)
+  }
+
+  descpath <- file.path(candidate_lib, "bread", "DESCRIPTION")
+  text <- readLines(descpath)
+  text <- text[!startsWith(text, "Remotes:")]
+  text <- c(text, "Remotes: NA")
+  if (remote) {
+    text <- c(text, "RemoteType: github", "RemoteHost: github.com",
+              "RemoteUsername: rstudio", "RemoteRepo: renv")
+  }
+
+  for (field in names(candidate_changes)) {
+    value <- candidate_changes[[field]]
+    if (identical(field, "remove_built"))
+      next
+    text <- text[!startsWith(text, paste0(field, ":"))]
+    if (!is.null(value))
+      text <- c(text, paste0(field, ": ", value))
+  }
+  if (isTRUE(candidate_changes$remove_built))
+    text <- text[!startsWith(text, "Built:")]
+  writeLines(text, descpath)
+
+  # A file present only in the candidate lets restore distinguish it from
+  # the package selected from the valid fallback repository.
+  marker <- file.path(candidate_lib, "bread", "reuse-source.txt")
+  writeLines("installed package source", marker)
+
+  desc <- renv_description_read(file.path(candidate_lib, "bread"))
+  remote_fields <- grep("^Remote", names(desc), value = TRUE)
+  record <- list(
+    Package = "bread",
+    Version = "1.0.0",
+    Source = "Repository",
+    Repository = "CRAN"
+  )
+  record[remote_fields] <- as.list(desc[remote_fields])
+  for (field in names(record_changes))
+    record[[field]] <- record_changes[[field]]
+
+  lockfile <- renv_lockfile_init(project = getwd())
+  lockfile$Packages$bread <- record
+  if (reuse) {
+    lockfile$R$Repositories <- NULL
+  } else {
+    fallback <- getOption("repos")
+    shadow <- renv_scope_tempfile("renv-shadow-repository-")
+    contrib <- file.path(shadow, "src", "contrib")
+    ensure_directory(contrib)
+    repopath <- renv_tests_repopath()
+    fallback_archive <- file.path(repopath, "src", "contrib", "Archive", "bread")
+    ensure_directory(fallback_archive)
+    fallback_source <- file.path(repopath, "src", "contrib", "bread_1.0.0.tar.gz")
+    file.copy(fallback_source, file.path(fallback_archive, "bread_1.0.0.tar.gz"))
+    file.copy(file.path(repopath, "src", "contrib", "PACKAGES"), contrib)
+    packages <- file.path(contrib, "PACKAGES")
+    db <- read.dcf(packages)
+    if ("Remotes" %in% colnames(db)) {
+      db[, "Remotes"] <- "NA"
+    } else {
+      db <- cbind(db, Remotes = rep("NA", nrow(db)))
+    }
+    write.dcf(db, packages)
+    fmt <- if (renv_platform_windows()) "file:///%s" else "file://%s"
+    shadow_url <- sprintf(fmt, shadow)
+    record$Repository <- shadow_url
+    lockfile$Packages$bread <- record
+    repos <- c(SHADOW = shadow_url, fallback)
+    lockfile$R$Repositories <- repos
+  }
+  renv_lockfile_save(lockfile, project = getwd())
+
+  if (reuse)
+    renv_scope_options(repos = character())
+
+  if (!reuse) {
+    download <- get("renv_download_parallel", asNamespace("renv"))
+    renv_scope_binding(asNamespace("renv"), "renv_download_parallel", function(...) {
+      args <- list(...)
+      urls <- args$urls
+      unavailable <- grepl(shadow_url, urls, fixed = TRUE)
+      status <- rep(FALSE, length(urls))
+      names(status) <- names(urls)
+      if (any(!unavailable)) {
+        args$urls <- urls[!unavailable]
+        args$destfiles <- args$destfiles[!unavailable]
+        args$types <- args$types[!unavailable]
+        status[!unavailable] <- do.call(download, args)
+      }
+      status
+    })
+  }
+
+  result <- tryCatch({
+    restore(lockfile = "renv.lock", prompt = FALSE)
+    NULL
+  }, error = identity)
+
+  target <- file.path(renv_paths_library(), "bread")
+  expect_null(result)
+  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(target, "DESCRIPTION")))
+  description <- renv_description_read(target)
+  expect_identical(description$Package, "bread")
+  expect_identical(description$Version, "1.0.0")
+  if (reuse) {
+    marker <- file.path(target, "reuse-source.txt")
+    expect_true(file.exists(marker))
+    if (file.exists(marker))
+      expect_identical(readLines(marker), "installed package source")
+  }
+  if (!reuse)
+    expect_false(file.exists(file.path(target, "reuse-source.txt")))
+
+}
+
+
+test_that("restore reuses a matching package from the user library", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(reuse = TRUE)
+})
+
+
+test_that("restore reuses a matching package from the site library", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(location = "site", reuse = TRUE)
+})
+
+
+test_that("restore reuses a matching package with remote metadata", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(remote = TRUE, reuse = TRUE)
+})
+
+
+current <- as.integer(strsplit(as.character(getRversion()), ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
+patch <- if (length(current) < 3L || current[[3L]] == 0L) 1L else 0L
+compatible_built <- sprintf("R %d.%d.%d; %s", current[[1L]], current[[2L]], patch, R.version$platform)
+
+test_that("restore reuses a package built for the same R major and minor version", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(
+    candidate_changes = list(Built = compatible_built),
+    reuse = TRUE
+  )
+})
+
+
+test_that("restore does not reuse a differently named package", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(candidate_changes = list(Package = "different-package"))
+})
+
+
+test_that("restore does not reuse a different package version", {
+  renv_test_restore_candidate(candidate_changes = list(Version = "0.0.1"))
+})

problem_statement:
Feature: Improved Categories (Subcategories, Search, Sort)
## Feature: Improved Categories (Mihon Request)

**Effort:** Medium (1-1.5 weeks) | **Impact:** Medium | **Priority:** Tier 2
**Epic:** #234

### Problem
Categories are flat (no hierarchy), no search, no alphabetical auto-sort.

### Architecture

[HIDDEN]

**Enhancements:**

| Enhancement | Change | Effort |
|-------------|--------|--------|
| Alphabetical sort | [HIDDEN] | 1 day |
| Category search | Add search bar to category picker dialog | 1-2 days |
| Subcategories | [HIDDEN] | 3-4 days |
| Reading lists | [HIDDEN] | 2-3 days |

**Subcategories approach:**
[HIDDEN]
4. UI: Expandable/collapsible category groups in library tabs
5. Max depth: 2 levels (parent â child, no grandchildren)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Create category "Action" â create subcategory "Isekai" under it
- [ ] Library shows expandable "Action" with "Isekai" nested
- [ ] Search categories â type "ise" â "Isekai" appears
- [ ] Sort alphabetically â categories reorder
- [ ] Migration: existing categories become top-level (parent_id = NULL)
- [ ] Backup/restore preserves hierarchy

### Additional contract requirements

When the manga library sort (sort type or direction) is changed globally — that is, for the library as a whole rather than for a single category — the new sort must be applied to every manga category without disturbing any per-category flag bits that are unrelated to the library sort type/direction mask (for example, an alphabetical category sort flag). Applying the new sort must preserve, for each individual category, all of that category's unrelated flag bits while replacing its library sort type and direction bits with the newly selected values, and it must not drop or omit any category from the update.

+package tachiyomi.domain.category.model
+
+fun Category.hasAlphabeticalSortFlag(): Boolean {
+    return flags and CategoryFlags.CATEGORY_FLAG_SORT_ALPHABETICAL != 0L
+}
+
+fun List<Category>.isAlphabeticalCategorySortEnabled(): Boolean {
+    return any(Category::hasAlphabeticalSortFlag)
+}
+
+fun List<Category>.flattenForDisplay(): List<Category> {
+    if (isEmpty()) return emptyList()
+
+    val categoriesById = associateBy(Category::id)
+    val alphabetical = isAlphabeticalCategorySortEnabled()
+    val categoryComparator = if (alphabetical) {
+        compareBy<Category> { it.name.lowercase() }.thenBy { it.id }
+    } else {
+        compareBy<Category> { it.order }.thenBy { it.id }
+    }
+
+    // Display model is intentionally depth-limited to two levels (root + direct child).
+    val roots = filter { it.parentId == null || it.parentId !in categoriesById }
+        .sortedWith(categoryComparator)
+    val childrenByParent = filter { it.parentId != null && it.parentId in categoriesById }
+        .groupBy { it.parentId }
+        .mapValues { (_, value) -> value.sortedWith(categoryComparator) }
+
+    val flattened = buildList {
+        roots.forEach { root ->
+            add(root)
+            childrenByParent[root.id].orEmpty().forEach(::add)
+        }
+    }.toMutableList()
+
+    if (flattened.size < size) {
+        val included = flattened.asSequence().map { it.id }.toSet()
+        flattened += filterNot { it.id in included }.sortedWith(categoryComparator)
+    }
+
+    return flattened
+}
+
+fun Category.prefixedDisplayName(categoriesById: Map<Long, Category>): String {
+    val parentName = parentId?.let { categoriesById[it]?.name }
+    return if (parentName != null) {
+        "$parentName / $name"
+    } else {
+        name
+    }
+}

+package tachiyomi.domain.category.manga.interactor
+
+import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
+import io.mockk.every
+import io.mockk.mockk
+import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+import tachiyomi.core.common.preference.Preference
+import tachiyomi.domain.category.manga.repository.MangaCategoryRepository
+import tachiyomi.domain.category.model.Category
+import tachiyomi.domain.category.model.CategoryUpdate

+import tachiyomi.domain.library.model.plus
+import tachiyomi.domain.library.service.LibraryPreferences
+
+class SetSortModeForMangaCategoryTest {
+
+    private val preferences = mockk<LibraryPreferences>()
+    private val categoryRepository = RecordingMangaCategoryRepository()
+    private val interactor = SetSortModeForMangaCategory(preferences, categoryRepository)
+
+    // Bits 7 and 8 are outside the library sort type/direction mask, so they model
+    // unrelated per-category flags such as an alphabetical category sort flag.
+    private val unrelatedFlagBits = (1L shl 7) or (1L shl 8)
+
+    private val sortTypeMask = MangaLibrarySort.Type.Alphabetical.mask
+    private val sortDirectionMask = MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Ascending.mask
+
+    private val flaggedCategoryA = Category(
+        id = 1L,
+        name = "Action",
+        order = 0L,
+        flags = unrelatedFlagBits,
+        hidden = false,
+    )
+    private val flaggedCategoryB = Category(
+        id = 2L,
+        name = "Isekai",
+        order = 1L,
+        flags = 1L shl 7,
+        hidden = false,
+    )
+    private val plainCategory = Category(
+        id = 3L,
+        name = "Slice of Life",
+        order = 2L,
+        flags = 0L,
+        hidden = false,
+    )
+
+    private fun stubGlobalSortPreference() {
+        val globalSorting = mockk<Preference<MangaLibrarySort>>(relaxed = true)
+        every { preferences.mangaSortingMode() } returns globalSorting
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `changing global library sort preserves unrelated category flag bits`() = runTest {
+        stubGlobalSortPreference()
+        categoryRepository.allCategories = listOf(flaggedCategoryA, plainCategory)
+
+        interactor.await(null as Long?, MangaLibrarySort.Type.LastRead, MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Descending)
+
+        // Every pre-existing category must end up with the same unrelated flag bits it had
+        // before the global sort change, while its library sort type and direction bits move
+        // to the newly selected values. No category may be dropped from the update.
+        categoryRepository.applyUpdates()
+
+        val updated = categoryRepository.categoriesById()
+        updated.keys shouldBe setOf(1L, 3L)
+        updated.getValue(1L).flags and unrelatedFlagBits shouldBe unrelatedFlagBits
+        updated.getValue(3L).flags and unrelatedFlagBits shouldBe 0L
+        MangaLibrarySort.valueOf(updated.getValue(1L).flags).let {
+            it.type shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Type.LastRead
+            it.direction shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Descending
+        }
+        MangaLibrarySort.valueOf(updated.getValue(3L).flags).let {
+            it.type shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Type.LastRead
+            it.direction shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Descending
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `changing global library sort replaces prior sort bits without affecting other categories flags`() = runTest {
+        stubGlobalSortPreference()
+        // Category A already carries library sort bits from a previous sort mode on top of
+        // its unrelated flag; category B carries only an unrelated flag; the plain category
+        // carries no flags at all.
+        val baseSortBits = MangaLibrarySort.Type.UnreadCount + MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Ascending
+        val previouslySortedCategory = flaggedCategoryA.copy(flags = flaggedCategoryA.flags + baseSortBits)
+        categoryRepository.allCategories = listOf(previouslySortedCategory, flaggedCategoryB, plainCategory)
+
+        interactor.await(null as Long?, MangaLibrarySort.Type.DateAdded, MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Ascending)
+
+        categoryRepository.applyUpdates()
+
+        val updated = categoryRepository.categoriesById()
+        updated.getValue(1L).flags and unrelatedFlagBits shouldBe unrelatedFlagBits
+        updated.getValue(2L).flags and unrelatedFlagBits shouldBe (1L shl 7)
+        updated.getValue(3L).flags and unrelatedFlagBits shouldBe 0L
+        updated.values.forEach { category ->
+            // The stale sort bits from the previous mode must be replaced, not merged.
+            category.flags and sortTypeMask shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Type.DateAdded.flag
+            category.flags and sortDirectionMask shouldBe MangaLibrarySort.Direction.Ascending.flag
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * A recording fake repository that applies updates through the public category model
+     * instead of asserting repository method-call counts. Only the final flags state of
+     * the categories is checked, regardless of which update methods are used to reach it.
+     *
+     * The bulk flags update keeps the existing repository semantics of assigning one
+     * flags value to every category.
+     *
+     * Methods that the interactors under test do not use are delegated to an unstubbed
+     * mock, so the fake does not depend on the exact set of repository methods.
+     */

problem_statement:
Disable CompartmentResourceType Index Usage
The CompartmentResourceType index should no longer be used, because it misses important resource versioning information. In some cases its usage can cause false positives.

Instead we should switch the usage to the SearchParamValueResource index which contains essentially the same information including the version.

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract Addendum

* Compartment search results must reflect only the compartment relationships
  present in the current (latest) version of each resource. A resource whose
  latest version no longer links to a compartment — because the compartment
  reference was removed or changed to a different compartment in a later
  version — must not be returned by a compartment query of the former
  compartment, neither in the search result entries nor in the total count,
  regardless of which earlier versions of that resource carried the link.
  Resources whose latest version still links to the compartment must continue
  to be returned, both without search parameters and when search parameters
  are supplied.
* This version-exact behavior also applies to compartment retrievals made in
  the patient context of CQL expressions.

+(ns blaze.db.impl.query.compartment
+  (:refer-clojure :exclude [str])
+  (:require
+   [blaze.db.impl.codec :as codec]
+   [blaze.db.impl.index :as index]
+   [blaze.db.impl.protocols :as p]
+   [blaze.db.impl.query.util :as qu]
+   [blaze.db.impl.search-param :as search-param]
+   [blaze.util :refer [str]]))
+
+(defn- inject-values [compartment-clauses values]
+  (mapv
+   (fn [disjunction]
+     (mapv
+      (fn [[search-param modifier]]
+        [search-param modifier
+         values
+         (search-param/compile-values search-param modifier values)])
+      disjunction))
+   compartment-clauses))
+
+(defn- list-clauses [clauses code id]
+  (inject-values clauses [(str code "/" id)]))
+
+(defrecord CompartmentListQuery [code clauses tid]
+  p/Query
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1]
+    (index/ordered-resource-handles batch-db tid (list-clauses clauses code arg1)
+                                    nil))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1 arg2]
+    (index/ordered-resource-handles batch-db tid (list-clauses clauses code arg1)
+                                    nil (codec/id-byte-string arg2)))
+  (-query-clauses [_])
+  (-query-plan [_ batch-db]
+    (index/type-query-plan batch-db tid {:search-clauses clauses})))
+
+(defn- seek-clauses [clauses code id other-clauses]
+  {:search-clauses (into (inject-values clauses [(str code "/" id)]) other-clauses)})
+
+(defrecord CompartmentSeekQuery [code clauses tid other-clauses]
+  p/Query
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1]
+    (index/type-query batch-db tid (seek-clauses clauses code arg1 other-clauses)))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1 arg2]
+    (index/type-query batch-db tid (seek-clauses clauses code arg1 other-clauses)
+                      (codec/id-byte-string arg2)))
+  (-query-clauses [_]
+    (qu/decode-clauses {:search-clauses other-clauses}))
+  (-query-plan [_ batch-db]
+    (index/type-query-plan batch-db tid {:search-clauses (into clauses other-clauses)})))
+
+(defrecord CompartmentQuery [c-hash tid scan-clauses other-clauses]
+  p/Query
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1]
+    (index/compartment-query batch-db [c-hash (codec/id-byte-string arg1)]
+                             tid scan-clauses other-clauses))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db arg1 arg2]
+    (index/compartment-query batch-db [c-hash (codec/id-byte-string arg1)]
+                             tid scan-clauses other-clauses
+                             (codec/id-byte-string arg2)))
+  (-query-clauses [_]
+    (qu/decode-clauses {:search-clauses (into scan-clauses other-clauses)}))
+  (-query-plan [_ _]
+    (index/compartment-query-plan scan-clauses other-clauses)))

+(ns blaze.db.impl.query.type
+  (:require
+   [blaze.anomaly :as ba :refer [when-ok]]
+   [blaze.async.comp :as ac]
+   [blaze.coll.core :as coll]
+   [blaze.db.impl.codec :as codec]
+   [blaze.db.impl.index :as index]
+   [blaze.db.impl.index.resource-as-of :as rao]
+   [blaze.db.impl.index.resource-handle :as rh]
+   [blaze.db.impl.index.type-stats :as type-stats]
+   [blaze.db.impl.protocols :as p]
+   [blaze.db.impl.query.util :as qu]
+   [blaze.db.impl.search-param.chained :as spc]))
+
+(defrecord TypeQuery [tid clauses]
+  p/Query
+  (-count [_ batch-db]
+    (index/type-query-total batch-db tid (:search-clauses clauses)))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db]
+    (index/type-query batch-db tid clauses))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db start-id]
+    (index/type-query batch-db tid clauses (codec/id-byte-string start-id)))
+  (-query-clauses [_]
+    (qu/decode-clauses clauses))
+  (-query-plan [_ batch-db]
+    (index/type-query-plan batch-db tid clauses)))
+
+(def ^:private ^:const ^long patient-compartment-hash (codec/c-hash "Patient"))
+(def ^:private ^:const ^long patient-code-hash (codec/c-hash "patient"))
+
+(defn- resource-handle-not-found-msg [{:keys [t since-t]} tid id]
+  (format "Resource handle `%s/%s` not found in database with t=%d and since-t=%d."
+          (codec/tid->type tid) (codec/id-string id) t since-t))
+
+(defn- non-deleted-resource-handle* [batch-db tid id]
+  (when-let [handle (p/-resource-handle batch-db tid id)]
+    (when-not (rh/deleted? handle)
+      handle)))
+
+(defn- non-deleted-resource-handle [batch-db tid id]
+  (or (non-deleted-resource-handle* batch-db tid id)
+      (ba/fault (resource-handle-not-found-msg batch-db tid id))))
+
+(defn- first-referenced-patient-not-found-msg [{:keys [t since-t]} resource-handle]
+  (format "Patient resource handle referenced from `%s/%s` not found in database with t=%d and since-t=%d."
+          (name (:fhir/type resource-handle)) (:id resource-handle) t since-t))
+
+(defn- first-referenced-patient [batch-db resource-handle]
+  (or (coll/first (spc/targets batch-db resource-handle patient-code-hash))
+      (ba/fault (first-referenced-patient-not-found-msg batch-db resource-handle))))
+
+(defn- start-patient-id [batch-db tid start-id]
+  (when-ok [start-handle (non-deleted-resource-handle batch-db tid start-id)
+            start-patient-handle (first-referenced-patient batch-db start-handle)]
+    (codec/id-byte-string (:id start-patient-handle))))
+
+;; A type query over resources with `tid` and patients with `patient-ids`.
+(defrecord PatientTypeQuery [tid patient-ids compartment-clause scan-clauses
+                             other-clauses compartment-query]
+  p/Query
+  (-count [query batch-db]
+    (ac/completed-future (count (p/-execute query batch-db))))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db]
+    (coll/eduction (mapcat #(compartment-query batch-db %)) patient-ids))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db start-id]
+    (let [start-id (codec/id-byte-string start-id)]
+      (when-ok [start-patient-id (start-patient-id batch-db tid start-id)]
+        (coll/eduction
+         cat
+         [(compartment-query batch-db start-patient-id start-id)
+          (coll/eduction
+           (comp (drop-while #(not= start-patient-id %))
+                 (drop 1)
+                 (mapcat #(compartment-query batch-db %)))
+           patient-ids)]))))
+  (-query-clauses [_]
+    (qu/decode-clauses {:search-clauses (-> [[compartment-clause]]
+                                            (into scan-clauses)
+                                            (into other-clauses))}))
+  (-query-plan [_ _]
+    (index/compartment-query-plan scan-clauses other-clauses)))
+
+(defn patient-type-query
+  [tid patient-ids compartment-clause scan-clauses other-clauses]
+  (->PatientTypeQuery
+   tid patient-ids compartment-clause scan-clauses other-clauses
+   (fn
+     ([batch-db patient-id]
+      (index/compartment-query batch-db [patient-compartment-hash patient-id]
+                               tid scan-clauses other-clauses))
+     ([batch-db patient-id start-id]
+      (index/compartment-query batch-db [patient-compartment-hash patient-id]
+                               tid scan-clauses other-clauses start-id)))))
+
+(defrecord EmptyTypeQuery [tid]
+  p/Query
+  (-count [_ batch-db]
+    (ac/completed-future
+     (:total (type-stats/seek-value (:snapshot batch-db) tid (:t batch-db)) 0)))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db]
+    (rao/type-list batch-db tid))
+  (-execute [_ batch-db start-id]
+    (rao/type-list batch-db tid (codec/id-byte-string start-id)))
+  (-query-clauses [_])
+  (-query-plan [_ _]
+    {:query-type :type}))

problem_statement:
Fix FHIR _lastUpdated Inequality Search False Positives
In case a FHIR `_lastUpdated` search is done via a combination of greater-equal und less-equal, which forms an interval, false positives can be returned in certain situations.

### Preconditions

* a resource needs to be updated from state A to B and back to A
* the timestamp of the last transaction (B -> A) must be after the upper bound of the FHIR search query
* the timestamp of the first transaction (create A) must be before or equal the upper bound of the FHIR search query

### Result

The resource is returned, although its last update is not included in the search interval.

### Example

Three transactions:

```clojure
[[:put {:fhir/type :fhir/Patient :id "0" :active #fhir/boolean false}]] ;; (A)
[[:put {:fhir/type :fhir/Patient :id "0" :active #fhir/boolean true}]]  ;; (B)
[[:put {:fhir/type :fhir/Patient :id "0" :active #fhir/boolean false}]] ;; (A)
```

The initial transaction occurred at the epoch; every following transaction followed in one-second increments.

The FHIR search: `_lastUpdated=ge1970-01-01T00:00:01Z&_lastUpdated=le1970-01-01T00:00:01Z` should return nothing, but returns the patient.

### Additional contract requirements

# `_lastUpdated` Interval Search Semantics

For `_lastUpdated` searches, matching must only consider the current version of
each resource. When multiple `_lastUpdated` parameters are combined with
greater-equal (`ge`) and less-equal (`le`) prefixes, they form an instant
interval that is evaluated against the timestamp of the resource's most recent
update. Superseded historical states and their transaction timestamps must
never cause a resource to appear in the search results.

In particular, consider a single resource that is created in state A, then
updated to state B, and then updated back to state A, with the three
transactions occurring at 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, 1970-01-01T00:00:01Z and
1970-01-01T00:00:02Z respectively:

* The resource has three version-history entries, but its single current
  last-update instant is 1970-01-01T00:00:02Z.
* A search with `_lastUpdated=ge1970-01-01T00:00:01Z` and
  `_lastUpdated=le1970-01-01T00:00:01Z` must return no resources, because only
  the superseded intermediate state falls within that interval.
* A search with `_lastUpdated=ge1970-01-01T00:00:02Z` and
  `_lastUpdated=le1970-01-01T00:00:02Z` must return the resource, because its
  current last-update instant falls within that interval.

+(defn- last-updated-dual-bound-value [op date-time]
+  {:op op
+   :lower-bound (codec-date/encode-lower-bound date-time)
+   :upper-bound (codec-date/encode-upper-bound date-time)
+   :lower-bound-dt (system/date-time-lower-bound date-time)
+   :upper-bound-dt (system/date-time-upper-bound date-time)})
+
+(defn- last-updated [batch-db resource-handle]
+  (let [t (:t resource-handle)
+        tx (p/-tx batch-db t)
+        instant (:blaze.db.tx/instant tx)]
+    (.atOffset ^Instant instant ZoneOffset/UTC)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-equal?
+  "Returns true if the parameter value interval `[param-lb param-ub]` fully
+  contains the resource value interval `value`."
+  [value param-lb param-ub]
+  (and (<= param-lb (system/date-time-lower-bound value))
+       (<= (system/date-time-upper-bound value) param-ub)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-not-equal? [value param-lb param-ub]
+  (not (last-updated-equal? value param-lb param-ub)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-greater-than? [param-ub value]
+  (< param-ub (system/date-time-upper-bound value)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-less-than? [value param-lb]
+  (< (system/date-time-lower-bound value) param-lb))
+
+(defn- last-updated-greater-equal?
+  "The range above the parameter value intersects (i.e. overlaps) with the range
+  of the resource value, or the range of the parameter value fully contains the
+  range of the resource value."
+  [param-lb param-ub value]
+  (or (<= param-ub (system/date-time-upper-bound value))
+      (<= param-lb (system/date-time-lower-bound value))))
+
+(defn- last-updated-less-equal? [date-time param-lb param-ub]
+  (or (<= (system/date-time-lower-bound date-time) param-lb)
+      (<= (system/date-time-upper-bound date-time) param-ub)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-starts-after? [param-ub value]
+  (<= param-ub (system/date-time-lower-bound value)))
+
+(defn- last-updated-ends-before? [value param-lb]
+  (<= (system/date-time-upper-bound value) param-lb))
+
+(defn- last-updated-approximately?
+  "Returns true if the interval `v` overlaps with the interval `q`."
+  [value param-lb param-ub]
+  (let [v-lb (system/date-time-lower-bound value)
+        v-ub (system/date-time-upper-bound value)]
+    (or (<= param-lb v-lb param-ub)
+        (<= param-lb v-ub param-ub)
+        (and (< v-lb param-lb) (< param-ub v-ub)))))
+
+(defn- last-updated-matcher [batch-db compiled-values]
+  (filter
+   (fn [resource-handle]
+     (let [value (last-updated batch-db resource-handle)]
+       (some
+        (fn [{:keys [op] param-lb :lower-bound-dt param-ub :upper-bound-dt}]
+          (case op
+            :eq (last-updated-equal? value param-lb param-ub)
+            :ne (last-updated-not-equal? value param-lb param-ub)
+            :gt (last-updated-greater-than? param-ub value)
+            :lt (last-updated-less-than? value param-lb)
+            :ge (last-updated-greater-equal? param-lb param-ub value)
+            :le (last-updated-less-equal? value param-lb param-ub)
+            :sa (last-updated-starts-after? param-ub value)
+            :eb (last-updated-ends-before? value param-lb)
+            :ap (last-updated-approximately? value param-lb param-ub)))
+        compiled-values)))))
+

-           :lower-bound (codec-date/encode-lower-bound date-time-value)}
-          (ba/unsupported (u/unsupported-prefix-msg code op)))
+           :lower-bound (codec-date/encode-lower-bound date-time)
+           :lower-bound-dt (system/date-time-lower-bound date-time)})
         #(assoc % ::anom/message (invalid-date-time-value-msg code value)))))

problem_statement:
Report Modifier below as Unsupported for Type Non-Canonicals
The `below` modifier is only implemented for values of the primitive type `canonical`. Search parameters of type `uri` can also point to values of other primitive types like `uri` and `url`. We should report the `below` modifier as unsupported for search parameters pointing to such values.

### Additional contract requirements

The `below` modifier is only implemented for `uri` search parameters whose target values are of the FHIR primitive type `canonical`.

Using the `below` modifier on a `uri` search parameter whose target value has another primitive type (for example `uri` or `url`) is reported as an unsupported modifier. The result is the standard unsupported-modifier anomaly with category `unsupported` and a message of the form "Unsupported modifier `below` on search parameter `<code>`." identifying the search parameter code.

The rule applies to every `uri` search parameter according to the primitive type of its target value, including custom (nonstandard) search parameter definitions. A custom `uri` search parameter definition that targets a `canonical` value accepts the `below` modifier just like a standard `canonical`-targeting parameter, while a custom definition that targets a value of another primitive type (such as `uri` or `url`) is handled like any other non-canonical `uri` search parameter and reports `below` as unsupported.

For example, the standard `_profile` parameter targets `Resource.meta.profile`, which is a `canonical` value, so `_profile:below` remains valid. Standard `uri` search parameters that target `uri`- or `url`-typed values (such as the `url` parameter) reject the `below` modifier with the unsupported-modifier anomaly described above.

problem_statement:
Reduce Allocations in Temporal Entity Creation
Profiling with YourKit showed that `java-time.temporal/instant` accounts for a call tree of allocations in which the actual `java.time.Instant.now(Clock)` call contributes only about 1 % of the bytes.

The reason is that `clojure.java-time` defines its factory functions via `deffactory`. Only the explicitly written arities have a direct body; all *implicit* arities are routed through `java-time.defconversion/call-conversion`, which resolves the conversion through a graph at runtime, on every single call.

Measured with `ThreadMXBean.getThreadAllocatedBytes` (clojure.java-time 1.4.3, JDK 25):

| call | bytes/call | ns/call |
|---|---:|---:|
| `(.instant clock)` | 40 | 84 |
| `(time/instant clock)` | 2202 | 1681 |
| `OffsetDateTime/now(clock)` | 115 | 106 |
| `(time/offset-date-time clock)` | 1330 | 678 |

The one-argument clock arities allocate roughly 55× and 12× the bytes of the direct `java.time` call.

The zero-argument arities are cheap by comparison because `deffactory` gives them an explicit body, but they still go through `java-time.clock/make` and a dynamic var lookup.

## Solution

Add a namespace `blaze.time` to the `util` module that implements `instant` and `offset-date-time` for zero arguments and for a `Clock` argument, delegating directly to `java.time`, and use it at all call sites of those two arities.

Conversion arities such as `(time/instant (time/plus now timeout))` are out of scope and keep using `java-time.api`.

### Additional contract requirements

The `util` module provides a public namespace `blaze.time` with two functions,
`instant` and `offset-date-time`. Each function supports exactly two arities:

- With no arguments, `instant` returns the current `java.time.Instant`
  (equivalent to `Instant/now`), and with one `java.time.Clock` argument it
  returns the current instant of that clock (equivalent to
  `Instant/now(clock)`).
- With no arguments, `offset-date-time` returns the current
  `java.time.OffsetDateTime` in the system default zone (equivalent to
  `OffsetDateTime/now`), and with one `java.time.Clock` argument it returns
  the current date-time of that clock, whose offset is the offset of the
  clock's zone (equivalent to `OffsetDateTime/now(clock)`).

Whenever the codebase needs the current instant or the current offset
date-time in one of these two arities, it must do so through these two
functions rather than through the corresponding `java-time.api` factory
functions. In scope for this migration are the zero-argument factory calls
and the one-argument factory calls whose single argument is the
`java.time.Clock` used for the current time, however those calls are
expressed syntactically — for example under an alias for `java-time.api`
other than `time`, via directly referred factory names, or split across
several lines. The `java-time.api` factories route these implicit arity
calls through a runtime-resolved conversion graph and therefore allocate
substantially more per call than the direct `java.time` delegation required
of the `blaze.time` functions.

Calls whose single argument is an ad-hoc temporal value rather than such a
`java.time.Clock` are conversions, not current-time queries. These conversion
arities of the `java-time` temporal API remain out of scope, and retaining
them is valid.

Whether a call-site argument is a `java.time.Clock` can in general only be
decided at runtime, so for the known, finite codebase the migration is
verified at the known clock-typed call sites — recognisable by their
surrounding forms, not by the names of local bindings — while every
zero-argument factory call is a current-time query and remains in scope
wherever it appears.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..93ceed6ec8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/modules/util/src/blaze/time.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+(ns blaze.time
+  "Functions for creating temporal entities.
+
+  The `clojure.java-time` counterparts of these functions define only their
+  zero-argument arity explicitly. Every other arity is routed through a
+  conversion graph that is resolved at runtime, on every call, allocating about
+  2 KiB per call. The functions here delegate to `java.time` directly."
+  (:import
+   [java.time Clock Instant OffsetDateTime]))
+
+(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)
+
+(defn instant
+  "Returns the current instant, either from the system clock or from `clock`."
+  (^Instant [] (Instant/now))
+  (^Instant [^Clock clock] (Instant/now clock)))
+
+(defn offset-date-time
+  "Returns the current date-time, either from the system clock using the default
+  offset or from `clock` using its offset."
+  (^OffsetDateTime [] (OffsetDateTime/now))
+  (^OffsetDateTime [^Clock clock] (OffsetDateTime/now clock)))

+(ns blaze.time-spec
+  (:require
+   [blaze.time :as bt]
+   [clojure.spec.alpha :as s])
+  (:import
+   [java.time Clock Instant OffsetDateTime]))
+
+(s/fdef bt/instant
+  :args (s/cat :clock (s/? #(instance? Clock %)))
+  :ret #(instance? Instant %))
+
+(s/fdef bt/offset-date-time
+  :args (s/cat :clock (s/? #(instance? Clock %)))
+  :ret #(instance? OffsetDateTime %))
