diff --git a/modules/util/test/blaze/time_test.clj b/modules/util/test/blaze/time_test.clj
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..46f68c209
--- /dev/null
+++ b/modules/util/test/blaze/time_test.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,444 @@
+(ns blaze.time-test
+  "Tests of the temporal entity creation functions.
+
+  `blaze.time` exists because the implicit arities of the corresponding
+  `java-time` factory functions are routed through `call-conversion`, which
+  resolves the conversion through a graph on the current thread on every call,
+  allocating about 2 KiB per call, while the equivalent direct `java.time`
+  calls allocate about 40 bytes. Measuring thread-allocated bytes with
+  `ThreadMXBean.getThreadAllocatedBytes` (with JIT warmup preceding the
+  measurement) is the deterministic check of that direct path."
+  (:require
+   [clojure.java.io :as io]
+   [clojure.string :as str]
+   [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
+   [clojure.walk :as walk]
+   [clojure.tools.reader :as reader]
+   [clojure.tools.reader.reader-types :as reader-types])
+  (:import
+   [com.sun.management ThreadMXBean]
+   [java.io File]
+   [java.lang.management ManagementFactory]
+   [java.time Clock Instant OffsetDateTime ZoneOffset]))
+
+(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)
+
+(def ^:private instant-165407 (Instant/parse "2024-05-16T16:54:07Z"))
+
+(def ^:private clock (Clock/fixed instant-165407 ZoneOffset/UTC))
+
+(defn- blaze-time-function [name]
+  (try
+    (requiring-resolve (symbol "blaze.time" (clojure.core/name name)))
+    (catch java.io.FileNotFoundException _ nil)))
+
+(deftest instant-test
+  (if-some [instant (blaze-time-function 'instant)]
+    (do
+      (testing "without clock"
+        (let [before (Instant/now)
+              ^Instant x (instant)
+              after (Instant/now)]
+
+          (is (instance? Instant x))
+          (is (not (.isBefore x before)))
+          (is (not (.isAfter x after)))))
+
+      (testing "with clock"
+        (is (= instant-165407 (instant clock))))
+
+      (testing "there is no additional arity"
+        (is (thrown? Throwable (instant clock clock)))
+        (is (thrown? Throwable (instant clock clock clock)))))
+    (is false "blaze.time/instant is available")))
+
+(deftest offset-date-time-test
+  (if-some [offset-date-time (blaze-time-function 'offset-date-time)]
+    (do
+      (testing "without clock"
+        (let [before (OffsetDateTime/now)
+              ^OffsetDateTime x (offset-date-time)
+              after (OffsetDateTime/now)]
+
+          (is (instance? OffsetDateTime x))
+          (is (not (.isBefore x before)))
+          (is (not (.isAfter x after)))))
+
+      (testing "with clock"
+        (is (= (OffsetDateTime/ofInstant instant-165407 ZoneOffset/UTC)
+               (offset-date-time clock))))
+
+      (testing "the offset is taken from the clock"
+        (is (= (ZoneOffset/ofHours 2)
+               (.getOffset ^OffsetDateTime (offset-date-time
+                            (Clock/fixed instant-165407 (ZoneOffset/ofHours 2)))))))
+
+      (testing "there is no additional arity"
+        (is (thrown? Throwable
+                     (offset-date-time clock clock)))
+        (is (thrown? Throwable
+                     (offset-date-time clock clock clock)))))
+    (is false "blaze.time/offset-date-time is available")))
+
+;; Directly measured thread-allocated bytes bound, both arities of both
+;; functions should remain far below the ~2 KiB per call reported for the
+;; path through the java-time conversion graph. A direct delegation to
+;; `java.time` allocates about 40 bytes per call on modern JDKs; the generous
+;; 512 byte bound also accounts for unrelated overhead (such as the thread
+;;-local allocation sampling of the virtual thread the test runs on),
+;; while reliably failing every route through the conversion graph.
+
+(def ^:private ^ThreadMXBean thread-mx-bean
+  (ManagementFactory/getThreadMXBean))
+
+(defn- allocated-bytes [f n]
+  (dotimes [_ n] (f))
+  (let [^ThreadMXBean mx thread-mx-bean
+        id (.getId (Thread/currentThread))
+        before (.getThreadAllocatedBytes mx id)
+        _ (dotimes [_ n] (f))
+        after (.getThreadAllocatedBytes mx id)]
+    (quot (- after before) n)))
+
+(def max-allocations 512)
+
+(deftest allocation-test
+  (if-some [instant (blaze-time-function 'instant)]
+    (do
+      (testing "instant"
+        (is (< (allocated-bytes instant 100) max-allocations)
+            "zero argument instant delegates directly to java.time")
+
+        (is (< (allocated-bytes #(instant clock) 100) max-allocations)
+            "clock argument instant delegates directly to java.time"))
+
+      (testing "offset-date-time"
+        (if-some [offset-date-time (blaze-time-function 'offset-date-time)]
+          (do
+            (is (< (allocated-bytes offset-date-time 100) max-allocations)
+                "zero argument offset-date-time delegates directly to java.time")
+
+            (is (< (allocated-bytes #(offset-date-time clock) 100) max-allocations)
+                "clock argument offset-date-time delegates directly to java.time"))
+          (is false "blaze.time/offset-date-time is available"))))
+    (is false "blaze.time/instant is available")))
+
+(def ^:private reader-opts
+  {:eof ::eof :read-cond :allow :features #{:clj}})
+
+(defn- read-forms
+  "Reads all top-level forms of `file` with `clojure.tools.reader`, allowing
+  reader conditionals and tolerating `#=` read-eval forms, auto-resolved
+  keywords of unknown aliases and plain values in tagged literals. Returns
+  nil if `file` can't be read."
+  [^File file]
+  (let [rdr (reader-types/indexing-push-back-reader
+             (java.io.PushbackReader. (io/reader file)))]
+    (try
+      (binding [reader/*alias-map* identity
+                reader/*data-readers* (assoc reader/*data-readers*
+                                        'eval identity)
+                reader/*default-data-reader-fn*
+                ;; Wrap unknown tagged literal values into a vector, so that
+                ;; metadata like `^{:foo "bar"} #fhir/code "x"` can be
+                ;; applied.
+                (fn [tag value] [:tagged tag value])]
+        (loop [forms []]
+          (let [form (reader/read reader-opts rdr)]
+            (if (identical? ::eof form)
+              forms
+              (recur (conj forms form))))))
+      (catch Exception _
+        nil)
+      (finally
+        (.close rdr)))))
+
+(defn- ns-form?
+  [form]
+  (and (seq? form) (= 'ns (first form))))
+
+(defn- require-clause?
+  [form]
+  (and (seq? form) (contains? #{:require :require-macros} (first form))))
+
+(defn- expand-prefix-list
+  "Expands a prefix list such as `[java-time [api :as time]]` into plain
+  lib specs. Returns nil if `spec` isn't a prefix list."
+  [spec]
+  (when (and (sequential? spec) (symbol? (first spec))
+             (every? #(and (sequential? %) (symbol? (first %))) (rest spec)))
+    (map
+     (fn [suffix]
+       (into [(symbol (str (first spec) "." (first suffix)))] (rest suffix)))
+     (rest spec))))
+
+(defn- lib-specs
+  "Returns all plain lib specs designated by `spec`."
+  [spec]
+  (if-let [specs (expand-prefix-list spec)]
+    specs
+    [spec]))
+
+(defn- java-time-usage
+  "Returns the aliases and referred names of `java-time.api` designated by
+  the lib spec `spec`."
+  [spec]
+  (when (and (sequential? spec) (= 'java-time.api (first spec)))
+    (let [{:keys [as refer]} (apply hash-map (rest spec))]
+      {:aliases (if as #{as} #{})
+       :refers (cond
+                 (sequential? refer) (into #{} (filter symbol?) refer)
+                 (= :all refer) '#{instant offset-date-time}
+                 :else #{})})))
+
+(defn- java-time-usages-in
+  "Returns the aliases and referred names of `java-time.api` taken from the
+  first `ns` form in `forms`."
+  [forms]
+  (reduce
+   (fn [usage {:keys [aliases refers]}]
+     (-> usage
+         (update :aliases into aliases)
+         (update :refers into refers)))
+   {:aliases #{} :refers #{}}
+   (sequence
+    (comp (filter ns-form?)
+          (take 1)
+          (mapcat rest)
+          (filter require-clause?)
+          (mapcat rest)
+          (mapcat lib-specs)
+          (keep java-time-usage))
+    forms)))
+
+(defn- blaze-time-usages-in
+  "Returns aliases and referred names of the public `blaze.time` namespace."
+  [forms]
+  (reduce
+   (fn [usage spec]
+     (if (and (sequential? spec) (= 'blaze.time (first spec)))
+       (let [{:keys [as refer]} (apply hash-map (rest spec))]
+         (-> usage
+             (update :aliases into (if as [as] []))
+             (update :refers into
+                     (cond
+                       (sequential? refer) (filter symbol? refer)
+                       (= :all refer) '[instant offset-date-time]
+                       :else []))))
+       usage))
+   {:aliases #{} :refers #{}}
+   (sequence
+    (comp (filter ns-form?)
+          (take 1)
+          (mapcat rest)
+          (filter require-clause?)
+          (mapcat rest)
+          (mapcat lib-specs))
+    forms)))
+
+(defn- nested-forms
+  "Returns a lazy seq of `form` and all nested forms, descending into
+  collections, map entries, and the elements of every list (including the
+  callee position)."
+  [form]
+  (cons form
+        (when (or (map? form) (and (coll? form) (not (map-entry? form))))
+          (let [children (if (map? form)
+                           (mapcat identity form)
+                           form)]
+            (mapcat nested-forms children)))))
+
+(defn- invocation-heads
+  "Returns invocation heads from executable forms, ignoring namespace forms
+  and quoted data."
+  [form]
+  (when-not (and (seq? form)
+                 (or (contains? '#{quote comment} (first form)) (ns-form? form)))
+    (concat
+     (when (and (seq? form) (symbol? (first form))) [(first form)])
+     (when (or (map? form) (and (coll? form) (not (map-entry? form))))
+       (let [children (if (map? form) (mapcat identity form) form)]
+         (mapcat invocation-heads children))))))
+
+(defn- strip-meta
+  "Returns `form` with all metadata removed, recursively, so that read
+  forms compare equal to their quoted counterparts."
+  [form]
+  (walk/postwalk
+   (fn [x]
+     (if (instance? clojure.lang.IObj x)
+       (with-meta x nil)
+       x))
+   form))
+
+(defn- factory-call?
+  "Returns true if `form` is a call of `instant` or `offset-date-time`
+  through one of the `aliases` or `refers` of `java-time.api` (or through
+  the fully qualified namespace name)."
+  [aliases refers form]
+  (and (seq? form)
+       (pos? (count form))
+       (let [callee (first form)]
+         (and (symbol? callee)
+              (contains? '#{instant offset-date-time}
+                         (symbol (name callee)))
+              (if-some [ns-name (namespace callee)]
+                (contains? (conj aliases 'java-time.api) (symbol ns-name))
+                (contains? refers callee))))))
+
+(defn- zero-arg-factory-call?
+  "Returns true if `form` is a zero-argument call of `instant` or
+  `offset-date-time` through one of the `aliases` or `refers` of
+  `java-time.api` (or through the fully qualified namespace name). Such a
+  call always queries the current time — it can't be a conversion — and is
+  therefore in scope wherever it appears."
+  [aliases refers form]
+  (and (factory-call? aliases refers form)
+       (empty? (rest form))))
+
+(defn- repo-file
+  "Returns the repository file at `relative-path`, the root of the
+  repository being two levels above the `modules/util` working directory of
+  the test run."
+  (^File [relative-path]
+   (io/file ".." ".." relative-path))
+  (^File [path-element & path-elements]
+   (apply io/file ".." ".." path-element path-elements)))
+
+(defn- source-file?
+  [^File file]
+  (and (.isFile file)
+       (re-find #"\.cljc?$" (.getName file))
+       (let [path (.getPath file)]
+         (and (not (str/includes? path "/target/"))
+              (not (str/includes? path "/.cpcache/"))
+              (not (str/includes? path "/.gitlibs/"))))))
+
+(defn- repo-source-files
+  []
+  (->> (concat
+        (file-seq (repo-file "src"))
+        (file-seq (repo-file "modules"))
+        (map #(repo-file %)
+             ["blaze.clj" "build.clj" "deps_prep.clj" "release.clj"
+              "stamp.clj"]))
+       (filter source-file?)
+       (remove #(str/includes? (.getPath ^File %) "/test/"))
+       (remove #(= "time_test.clj" (.getName ^File %)))
+       (sort-by #(.getPath ^File %))))
+
+(defn- source-forms
+  [^File file]
+  (some->> (read-forms file) (map strip-meta)))
+
+(defn- api-factory-calls
+  [forms]
+  (let [{:keys [aliases refers]} (java-time-usages-in forms)]
+    (into [] (comp (mapcat nested-forms)
+                   (filter #(factory-call? aliases refers %)))
+          forms)))
+
+(defn- temporal-conversion?
+  "Recognizes the retained conversion whose value is computed by `plus`.
+  Alias and local binding names do not affect its classification."
+  [form]
+  (and (= 2 (count form))
+       (seq? (second form))
+       (symbol? (first (second form)))
+       (= "plus" (name (first (second form))))))
+
+(defn- direct-java-time-query?
+  [form]
+  (and (seq? form)
+       (symbol? (first form))
+       (= "now" (name (first form)))
+       (contains? #{"Instant" "OffsetDateTime"}
+                  (last (str/split (or (namespace (first form)) "") #"\.")))))
+
+(defn- blaze-time-call?
+  [forms]
+  (let [{:keys [aliases refers]} (blaze-time-usages-in forms)]
+    (some (fn [form]
+            (and (seq? form)
+                 (symbol? (first form))
+                 (contains? '#{instant offset-date-time}
+                            (symbol (name (first form))))
+                 (if-some [callee-ns (namespace (first form))]
+                   (contains? (conj aliases 'blaze.time) (symbol callee-ns))
+                   (contains? refers (first form)))))
+          (mapcat nested-forms forms))))
+
+(def ^:private migrated-source-paths
+  ["modules/cql/src/blaze/elm/expression/cache/bloom_filter.clj"
+   "modules/db/src/blaze/db/tx_log/local.clj"
+   "modules/job-async-interaction/src/blaze/job/async_interaction/request.clj"
+   "modules/job-disk-perf/src/blaze/job/disk_perf.clj"
+   "modules/job-re-index/src/blaze/job/re_index.clj"
+   "modules/operation-compact/src/blaze/fhir/operation/compact.clj"
+   "modules/operation-cql/src/blaze/fhir/operation/cql.clj"
+   "modules/operation-disk-perf/src/blaze/fhir/operation/disk_perf.clj"
+   "modules/operation-measure-evaluate-measure/src/blaze/fhir/operation/evaluate_measure/measure.clj"
+   "modules/openid-client/src/blaze/openid_client/token_provider.clj"
+   "modules/openid-client/src/blaze/openid_client/token_provider/impl.clj"
+   "modules/terminology-service-local/src/blaze/terminology_service/local/value_set/expand.clj"])
+
+(deftest migration-policy-test
+  (let [files (repo-source-files)
+        parsed (into {} (keep (fn [^File file]
+                                (when-some [forms (source-forms file)]
+                                  [(.getPath file) [file forms]]))) files)
+        unreadable (remove #(contains? parsed (.getPath ^File %)) files)
+        api-violations
+        (for [[path [_ forms]] parsed
+              call (api-factory-calls forms)
+              :when (or (empty? (rest call))
+                        (not (temporal-conversion? call)))]
+          (str path " retains an in-scope java-time.api factory call: "
+               (pr-str call)))
+        direct-java-time-violations
+        (for [[path [_ forms]] parsed
+              :when (not= path "../../modules/util/src/blaze/time.clj")
+              form (mapcat nested-forms forms)
+              :when (direct-java-time-query? form)]
+          (str path " queries java.time directly instead of through blaze.time: "
+               (pr-str form)))
+        missing-wrapper-use
+        (for [path migrated-source-paths
+              :let [[_ forms] (get parsed (str "../../" path))]
+              :when (or (nil? forms) (not (blaze-time-call? forms)))]
+          (str path " does not use the blaze.time current-time API"))
+        load-error (try
+                     (require 'blaze.time)
+                     nil
+                     (catch Throwable error error))
+        blaze-time-ns (find-ns 'blaze.time)
+        public-vars (when (and (nil? load-error) blaze-time-ns)
+                      (set (keys (ns-publics blaze-time-ns))))
+        namespace-violations
+        (when-not public-vars
+          ["blaze.time can't be loaded"])
+        unresolved-blaze-time-references
+        (when public-vars
+          (mapcat
+           (fn [[path [_ forms]]]
+             (let [{:keys [aliases refers]} (blaze-time-usages-in forms)
+                   qualifiers (conj aliases 'blaze.time)]
+               (concat
+                (for [head (mapcat invocation-heads forms)
+                      :when (and (namespace head)
+                                 (contains? qualifiers
+                                            (symbol (namespace head)))
+                                 (not (contains? public-vars
+                                                 (symbol (name head)))))]
+                  (str path " refers to " head
+                       ", which is not a public var of blaze.time"))
+                (for [name refers :when (not (contains? public-vars name))]
+                  (str path " refers to " name
+                       ", which is not a public var of blaze.time")))))
+           parsed))
+        violations (concat
+                    (map #(str "can't read " (.getPath ^File %)) unreadable)
+                    api-violations direct-java-time-violations
+                    missing-wrapper-use namespace-violations
+                    unresolved-blaze-time-references)]
+    (is (empty? violations) (str/join "\n" violations))))

```scala
import language.experimental.captureChecking
trait IO:
  def println(): Unit = ()
def test(io: IO^): Unit =
  trait A0:
    def callIO(): Unit
  class A extends A0:
    val x: A = this
    def callIO(): Unit = io.println()

  val a: A^ = A()
  val b: A0^{} = a.x
  val apparentlyNotPure: () ->{} Unit = () => b.callIO()  // boom
```

## Output

It compiles.

## Expectation

Should error on the last line, or somewhere in the class definition.

### Additional contract requirements

With capture checking and separation checking enabled, a class defined inside
a method must not hide an outer capability from a closure assigned to a pure
function type. The program must be rejected when the class closes over that
capability and the closure uses a reference obtained from the class; the
reference may be viewed through a superclass type rather than the concrete
class type. The rejection may be reported either at the pure-function
assignment or within the enclosing class definition. Diagnostic wording, the
number of diagnostics, and the precise source position within either permitted
location are not specified.

problem_statement:
Create withFieldComputedPartial version that takes (from: From, failFast: Boolean) => ...
While most of the time people can get away with:

```scala
foo.intoPartial[Bar]
  .withFieldComputedPartial(_.baz, foo => ... /* partial.Result of 1 value where failFast doesn't matter */)
  .transform
```

sometimes they might need a but more complex logic where it does.

We are currently missing an operator that handles that, forcing people to do some workarounds.

It can be solved by adding a new customization option.

### Additional contract requirements

On the Scala 2.13 JVM partial-transformation DSL, the required public methods are the dedicated
fail-fast-aware methods below. They are not satisfied by an overload of `withFieldComputedPartial`.

* `withFieldComputedPartialFailFast(selector, f)` takes its target selector and its computation in the
  same parameter list. `f` has type `(From, Boolean) => partial.Result[U]`, for a value `U` compatible
  with the selected target field. This method must work on both the builder returned by `intoPartial[To]`
  and the builder returned by `PartialTransformer.define[From, To]`.
* `withFieldComputedPartialFromFailFast(selectorFrom)(selectorTo, f)` first selects an input from the
  source; `f` receives that selected input and the Boolean, and returns the result for the selected target
  field.
* `withSealedSubtypeHandledPartialFailFast[Subtype](f)` receives the handled subtype and the Boolean and
  returns the partial result for the target sealed hierarchy.

For every method, the Boolean passed to the computation is `true` for fail-fast execution
(`transformFailFast`, or a built transformer invoked with `failFast = true`) and `false` for
error-accumulating execution (`transform`, or `failFast = false`). A successful `partial.Result` supplies
its computed value. A failed `partial.Result` must make the transformation fail under the ordinary partial
transformation semantics in both modes; it must not be converted into a successful value or ignored.

+#### Fail-fast-aware partial computations
+
+When using `.withFieldComputedPartial`, the provided function does not know whether the caller used `.transform` (which
+collects all errors) or `.transformFailFast` (which stops at the first error). In some cases the computation itself could
+benefit from this knowledge - for example, to skip expensive validations when fail-fast mode is already active, or to
+eagerly accumulate additional diagnostics when all errors are collected.
+
+`.withFieldComputedPartialFailFast` passes the `failFast` flag as an additional `Boolean` parameter to the function. The
+flag is `true` when `.transformFailFast` is used and `false` when `.transform` is used.
+`.withFieldComputedPartialFromFailFast` provides the same capability for computations that extract a value from the
+source first.
+
+!!! example
+
+    ```scala
+    //> using scala {{ scala.3 }}
+    //> using dep io.scalaland::chimney::{{ chimney_version() }}
+    //> using dep com.lihaoyi::pprint::{{ libraries.pprint }}
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl._
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.partial
+
+    case class Foo(a: String, b: Int)
+    case class Bar(a: String, b: Int, c: Long)
+
+    // With transformFailFast, failFast is true:
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      Foo("value", 10)
+        .intoPartial[Bar]
+        .withFieldComputedPartialFailFast(_.c, (foo, failFast) =>
+          if (failFast) partial.Result.fromValue(foo.b.toLong) // skip extra work in fail-fast mode
+          else partial.Result.fromValue(foo.b.toLong * 2)      // do full computation otherwise
+        )
+        .transformFailFast
+        .asEither
+        .left
+        .map(_.asErrorPathMessages)
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // Right(value = Bar(a = "value", b = 10, c = 10L))
+
+    // With transform, failFast is false:
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      Foo("value", 10)
+        .intoPartial[Bar]
+        .withFieldComputedPartialFailFast(_.c, (foo, failFast) =>
+          if (failFast) partial.Result.fromValue(foo.b.toLong)
+          else partial.Result.fromValue(foo.b.toLong * 2)
+        )
+        .transform
+        .asEither
+        .left
+        .map(_.asErrorPathMessages)
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // Right(value = Bar(a = "value", b = 10, c = 20L))
+    ```
+
+Similarly, `.withSealedSubtypeHandledPartialFailFast` passes the `failFast` flag when handling sealed subtypes, and
+`.withConstructorPartialFailFast` passes it when wiring an entire constructor (as a curried `Boolean => partial.Result[To]`
+argument).
+

+
+  private def codeSourceJar(cls: Class[?]): Option[File] =
+    Option(cls.getProtectionDomain)
+      .flatMap(pd => Option(pd.getCodeSource))
+      .map(_.getLocation)
+      .flatMap(url => scala.util.Try(Paths.get(url.toURI).toFile).toOption)
+      .filter(_.isFile)
+
+  /** The URLs of every URLClassLoader in the class loader chain that loaded the tests (relevant when tests are run
+    * by sbt's non-forked class loader, where java.class.path contains only sbt-launch.jar and the real test
+    * classpath is held by internal layered class loaders). */
+  private def classLoaderUrls: List[File] = {
+    def urlsOf(loader: ClassLoader): List[File] =
+      loader match {
+        case null  => List.empty
+        case urlCl: URLClassLoader =>
+          urlCl.getURLs.toList.flatMap(url => scala.util.Try(Paths.get(url.toURI).toFile).toOption) ++ urlsOf(loader.getParent)
+        case other =>
+          // Wrapped/Layered class loaders delegate but are not URLClassLoaders themselves; keep walking up.
+          urlsOf(other.getParent)
+      }
+    urlsOf(getClass.getClassLoader)
+  }
+
+  /** Every jar or classes directory of the test runtime that a snippet could need: entries from java.class.path,
+    * the URLs of the class loaders that loaded the tests, and the jars providing the Scala library and the Chimney
+    * classes themselves. */
+  private def runtimeJars: List[File] = {
+    val fromClasses = List(
+      codeSourceJar(classOf[scala.Product]), // scala-library
+      codeSourceJar(classOf[scala.reflect.api.Universe]), // scala-reflect
+      codeSourceJar(Class.forName("io.scalaland.chimney.PartialTransformer")), // chimney
+      codeSourceJar(Class.forName("io.scalaland.chimney.fixtures.products.Foo")) // chimney test fixtures
+    ).flatten
+    (classpathEntries ++ classLoaderUrls ++ fromClasses)
+      .filter(_.exists)
+      // sbt's launcher jar bundles its own (incompatible) copy of the Scala 2.12 library, which would shadow the
+      // scala-library that snippets have to be compiled against.
+      .filterNot(_.getName.startsWith("sbt-launch"))
+      .filterNot(_.getName.startsWith("scala3-")) // snippets are compiled with the Scala 2 compiler
+      .distinct
+  }
+
+  /** Compiles and runs a complete Scala 2 program. The program must define `object Main { def main(args:
+    * Array[String]): Unit = ... }`; its main method is invoked reflectively.
+    *
+    * Compilation failures are returned as [[Left]] (so that tests can turn them into assertion failures), while
+    * assertions and exceptions thrown by the compiled program propagate to the caller.
+    */
+  def compileAndRunScala2(programSource: String): Either[String, Unit] = {
+    val settings = new Settings()
+    settings.classpath.value = runtimeJars.map(_.getAbsolutePath).mkString(File.pathSeparator)
+    settings.usejavacp.value = false
+
+    val outDir = new VirtualDirectory("dsl-snippet-out", None)
+    settings.outputDirs.setSingleOutput(outDir)
+
+    val reporter = new StoreReporter(settings)
+    val global = new Global(settings, reporter)
+    val run = new global.Run()
+    run.compileSources(List(new BatchSourceFile("DslSnippet.scala", programSource)))
+    val errors = reporter.infos
+      .filter(_.severity == reporter.ERROR)
+      .map(info => info.msg)
+      .toList
+
+    if (errors.nonEmpty) Left(errors.mkString("\n"))
+    else {
+      val tmpDir = Files.createTempDirectory("dsl-snippet")
+      try {
+        outDir.foreach { file =>
+          if (!file.isDirectory) {
+            // VirtualDirectory paths look like "/dsl-snippet-out/Main$.class"; strip the root container name.
+            val relative = file.path.split("/", 3).lift(2).getOrElse(file.name)
+            val target = tmpDir.resolve(relative)
+            Option(target.getParent).foreach(Files.createDirectories(_))
+            Files.write(target, file.toByteArray)
+          }
+        }
+        val loader = new URLClassLoader(
+          (tmpDir.toUri.toURL +: runtimeJars.map(_.toURI.toURL)).toArray,
+          getClass.getClassLoader
+        )
+        val main = loader.loadClass("Main$")
+        main.getMethod("main", classOf[Array[String]]).invoke(
+          main.getField("MODULE$").get(null),
+          Array.empty[String]
+        )
+        Right(())
+      } finally deleteRecursively(tmpDir)
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def deleteRecursively(path: Path): Unit = {
+    if (Files.isDirectory(path)) {
+      val stream = Files.list(path)
+      try stream.forEach(file => deleteRecursively(file))
+      finally stream.close()
+    }
+    Files.deleteIfExists(path)
+    ()
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
Support transformations that apply to all Transformers
**Checklist**

- [X] I read the documentation at https://chimney.readthedocs.io/ and checked that the functionality doesn't exist
- [X] I checked the https://github.com/scalalandio/chimney/issues and haven't found the feature already requested reported
- [X] I confirmed that the request is not related to functionality that was deprecated: lifted transformers (`TransformerF`s) or `unsafeOption` flags
- [X] I believe that this is actual feature request, rather than [a question how to use existing features](https://github.com/scalalandio/chimney/discussions)
- [X] I am aware of [the maintainer's announcement](https://github.com/scalalandio/chimney/discussions/762) and I understand, that this might only be implemented
      if someone from the community decide to own the feature and see it through

**Describe the desired behavior**

I would like the ability to say "for all types you encounter, run this transformation". For example, renaming field `oldField` to `newField` everywhere.


**Use case example**

My use case is maybe a little specific. We support *very* nested sum types, such as, for example:
```scala
sealed trait Foo
object Foo:
  sealed trait Foo2 extends Foo
  object Foo2:
    sealed trait Foo3 extends Foo2
    object Foo3: // ...
```

And one of the fields of `Foo` needs to be renamed in our `Transformer[old.Foo, new.Foo]`. This basically disables all automatic derivation, since we need to manually tell Chimney for each subtype of `Foo` to rename the property.

**How it relates to existing features**

Our workaround is to declare helper methods:
```scala
def fooTransformer[From <: old.Foo, To <: new.Foo]: Transformer[From, To] =
  Transformer
    .define[From, To]
    .withFieldRename(_.old, _.new)

def foo28Transformer[From <: old.Foo28, To <: new.Foo28]: Transformer[From, To] =
  fooTransformer[From, To]
    .withFieldConst(_.const, None)
```

### Additional contract requirements

The library must let users define a transformation override once and have it applied to every recursive derivation whose source type matches a given source matcher and whose target type matches a given target matcher (i.e. “for all derivations from a source matching `FromMatch` to a target matching `ToMatch`, apply this operation”), as requested in the issue ("for all types you encounter, run this transformation").

Builders and entry points

- The scoped-override entry point `.forAll[FromMatch, ToMatch]` must be available on all transformer builder forms: total transformers (`Transformer.define`, `TransformerInto` / `.into[...]`) and partial/failable transformers (`Transformer.definePartial`, `PartialTransformerInto` / `.intoPartial[...]`).

Scoped operations

- The object returned by `.forAll` must support the following operations, after which the parent builder is returned so that further ordinary overrides or additional `.forAll` scopes can be chained:
  - `.withFieldRenamed(sourceFieldSelector, targetFieldSelector)` — use the value of the source field selected from a matched source value to provide the target field selected on a matched target value (rename).
  - `.withFieldConst(targetFieldSelector, value)` — provide a constant value for the selected target field in every matched derivation.
  - `.withFieldComputed(targetFieldSelector, sourceValue => value)` — compute the selected target field from each matched source value.
  - `.withFieldComputedPartial(targetFieldSelector, sourceValue => partial.Result[value])` — like `.withFieldComputed`, but producing a partial (failable) result; only the partial builders support it.

Matching and application semantics

- A scoped override applies to every derivation during recursive transformation whose source type is a subtype of (or equal to) `FromMatch` and whose target type is a subtype of (or equal to) `ToMatch`.
- The override must propagate to arbitrarily deep and arbitrarily many occurrences of the matching pair (including occurrences nested inside other types or inside collections); it is not consumed after the first match.
- Derivations whose `From`/`To` pair does not satisfy the subtype match must be left to ordinary default derivation behavior, as if no scoped override existed.
- Regular (non-scoped, path-targeted) overrides continue to work alongside scoped ones and take precedence over them where both could apply.

+  *
+  * @tparam From

+  * @tparam To
+  *   type of top-level output value
+  * @tparam Overrides
+  *   type-level encoded config
+  * @tparam Flags
+  *   type-level encoded flags
+  * @tparam FromMatch
+  *   source type to match in recursive derivations
+  * @tparam ToMatch
+  *   target type to match in recursive derivations
+  *
+  * @since 1.10.0
+  */
+final class PartialTransformerDefinitionForAll[
+    From,
+    To,
+    Overrides <: TransformerOverrides,
+    Flags <: TransformerFlags,
+    FromMatch,
+    ToMatch
+](
+    val runtimeData: TransformerDefinitionCommons.RuntimeDataStore
+) extends WithRuntimeDataStore {
+
+  /** Use the `selectorFrom` field in `FromMatch` to obtain the value of the `selectorTo` field in `ToMatch`.
+    *
+    * @since 1.10.0
+    */
+  def withFieldRenamed[T, U](
+      selectorFrom: FromMatch => T,
+      selectorTo: ToMatch => U
+  ): PartialTransformerDefinition[From, To, ? <: TransformerOverrides, Flags] =
+    macro PartialTransformerDefinitionForAllMacros.withFieldRenamedImpl[From, To, Overrides, Flags, FromMatch, ToMatch]
+
+  /** Use the `value` provided here for the field picked using `selector`.
+    *
+    * @since 1.10.0
+    */
+  def withFieldConst[T, U](
+      selector: ToMatch => T,
+      value: U
+  )(implicit ev: U <:< T): PartialTransformerDefinition[From, To, ? <: TransformerOverrides, Flags] =
+    macro PartialTransformerDefinitionForAllMacros.withFieldConstImpl[From, To, Overrides, Flags, FromMatch, ToMatch]
+
+  /** Use the function `f` to compute the value of the field picked using `selector`.
+    *
+    * @since 1.10.0
+    */
+  def withFieldComputed[T, U](
+      selector: ToMatch => T,
+      f: FromMatch => U
+  )(implicit ev: U <:< T): PartialTransformerDefinition[From, To, ? <: TransformerOverrides, Flags] =
+    macro PartialTransformerDefinitionForAllMacros.withFieldComputedImpl[From, To, Overrides, Flags, FromMatch, ToMatch]
+
+  /** Use the function `f` to compute the partial result for the field picked using `selector`.
+    *
+    * @since 1.10.0
+    */
+  def withFieldComputedPartial[T, U](
+      selector: ToMatch => T,
+      f: FromMatch => partial.Result[U]
+  )(implicit ev: U <:< T): PartialTransformerDefinition[From, To, ? <: TransformerOverrides, Flags] =
+    macro PartialTransformerDefinitionForAllMacros
+      .withFieldComputedPartialImpl[From, To, Overrides, Flags, FromMatch, ToMatch]

+  private[chimney] def addOverride(overrideData: Any): this.type =
+    new PartialTransformerDefinitionForAll[From, To, Overrides, Flags, FromMatch, ToMatch](overrideData +: runtimeData)

+      Flags <: TransformerFlags: Type,
+      FromMatch: Type,
+      ToMatch: Type,
+      T: Type,
+      U: Type

+      f: Expr[FromMatch => U]

+          updatedTd

+}

+### Applying overrides to all matching derivations (`forAll`)
+
+When transforming between deeply nested types, you may find yourself needing to apply the same field override at every
+level of the structure. For example, if an inner type has a renamed field, every derivation involving that inner type
+needs the same `.withFieldRenamed` call. Instead of manually using nested selectors like
+`.withFieldRenamed(_.a.name, _.a.imie)` for each path, you can use `.forAll[FromMatch, ToMatch]` to apply the
+override to **all** derivations where the source type matches `FromMatch` and the target type matches `ToMatch`:
+
+!!! example
+
+    Applying a field rename to all matching nested derivations with `forAll`
+
+    ```scala
+    //> using dep io.scalaland::chimney::{{ chimney_version() }}
+    //> using dep com.lihaoyi::pprint::{{ libraries.pprint }}
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl._
+
+    case class Inner1(name: String, value: Int)
+    case class Inner2(imie: String, value: Int)
+    case class Outer1(a: Inner1, b: Inner1)
+    case class Outer2(a: Inner2, b: Inner2)
+
+    // Without forAll, you would need to rename for each field path separately:
+    //   .withFieldRenamed(_.a.name, _.a.imie)
+    //   .withFieldRenamed(_.b.name, _.b.imie)
+    // With forAll, a single rename applies to every Inner1 -> Inner2 derivation:
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      Outer1(Inner1("Kuba", 1), Inner1("Artur", 2))
+        .into[Outer2]
+        .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+        .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)
+        .transform
+    )
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      Outer1(Inner1("Kuba", 1), Inner1("Artur", 2))
+        .intoPartial[Outer2]
+        .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+        .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)
+        .transform
+        .asEither
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // Outer2(a = Inner2(imie = "Kuba", value = 1), b = Inner2(imie = "Artur", value = 2))
+    // Right(value = Outer2(a = Inner2(imie = "Kuba", value = 1), b = Inner2(imie = "Artur", value = 2)))
+
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.Transformer
+
+    // forAll also works with Transformer.define:
+    val transformer: Transformer[Outer1, Outer2] = Transformer
+      .define[Outer1, Outer2]
+      .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+      .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)
+      .buildTransformer
+
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      transformer.transform(Outer1(Inner1("Kuba", 1), Inner1("Artur", 2)))
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // Outer2(a = Inner2(imie = "Kuba", value = 1), b = Inner2(imie = "Artur", value = 2))
+    ```
+
+The scoped builder returned by `.forAll[FromMatch, ToMatch]` supports the following operations:
+
+  - `.withFieldRenamed(_.fromField, _.toField)` - use the source field to provide the value for the target field
+  - `.withFieldConst(_.field, value)` - use a constant value for the target field
+  - `.withFieldComputed(_.field, from => value)` - compute the value from the matched source instance
+  - `.withFieldComputedPartial(_.field, from => partial.Result[value])` - compute a partial result (only for
+    `PartialTransformer`)
+
+Each of these operations returns the original builder (e.g. `TransformerInto`, `TransformerDefinition`), so you can
+chain further overrides or flags after calling a `forAll` override.
+
+!!! example
+
+    Using `forAll` with `withFieldComputed` and deep nesting
+
+    ```scala
+    //> using dep io.scalaland::chimney::{{ chimney_version() }}
+    //> using dep com.lihaoyi::pprint::{{ libraries.pprint }}
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.Transformer
+    import io.scalaland.chimney.dsl._
+
+    // forAll propagates through arbitrarily deep nesting:
+    case class Inner1(name: String)
+    case class Inner2(imie: String)
+    case class Mid1(inner: Inner1)
+    case class Mid2(inner: Inner2)
+    case class Outer1(mid: Mid1)
+    case class Outer2(mid: Mid2)
+
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      Outer1(Mid1(Inner1("deep")))
+        .into[Outer2]
+        .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+        .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)
+        .transform
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // Outer2(mid = Mid2(inner = Inner2(imie = "deep")))
+
+    // forAll with withFieldComputed:
+    case class Source(name: String, value: Int)
+    case class Target(name: String, value: Int, extra: String)
+    case class WrapperSrc(a: Source, b: Source)
+    case class WrapperDst(a: Target, b: Target)
+
+    val transformer: Transformer[WrapperSrc, WrapperDst] = Transformer
+      .define[WrapperSrc, WrapperDst]
+      .forAll[Source, Target]
+      .withFieldComputed(_.extra, src => s"${src.name}-${src.value}")
+      .buildTransformer
+
+    pprint.pprintln(
+      transformer.transform(WrapperSrc(Source("Kuba", 1), Source("Artur", 2)))
+    )
+    // expected output:
+    // WrapperDst(
+    //   a = Target(name = "Kuba", value = 1, extra = "Kuba-1"),
+    //   b = Target(name = "Artur", value = 2, extra = "Artur-2")
+    // )

+    The `forAll` override propagates into every level of nesting during recursive derivation. Whether the matching
+    types appear one level deep, three levels deep, or inside a collection, the override will be applied wherever
+    Chimney derives a transformation from a type matching `FromMatch` to a type matching `ToMatch`.

+/** Tests for issue #810: the ability to declare a transformation override once (scoped through

+  private case class RenameMid1(inner: RenameInner1)
+  private case class RenameMid2(inner: RenameInner2)
+  private case class RenameInner1(name: String, value: Int)
+  private case class RenameInner2(imie: String, value: Int)

+      .forAll[RenameInner1, RenameInner2]
+      .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)

+

+
+      case class Outer1(a: Inner1, b: Inner1)
+      case class Outer2(a: Inner2, b: Inner2)
+      case class Inner1(name: String, value: Int)
+      case class Inner2(imie: String, value: Int)
+
+      val outer1 = Outer1(Inner1("Kuba", 1), Inner1("Artur", 2))
+      val outer2 = Outer2(Inner2("Kuba", 1), Inner2("Artur", 2))
+
+      test("the declared total transformer definition (Transformer.define) supports scoped overrides") {
+        val total = Transformer

+          .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+          .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)
+          .buildTransformer

+          .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)

+          .forAll[Inner1, Inner2]
+          .withFieldRenamed(_.name, _.imie)

+          .transform
+          .asEither ==> Right(outer2)
+      }
+    }

+      case class Cat1(name: String)

+      case class Dog2(imie: String)
+      case class Cat2(name: String)

+        herd1

+      case class Dog1(name: String) extends Animal1
+      case class Cat1(name: String) extends Animal1
+
+      sealed trait Animal2 { def imie: String }
+      case class Dog2(imie: String) extends Animal2
+      case class Cat2(imie: String) extends Animal2

+
+      case class Outer1(a: Inner1, b: Inner1, mid: Mid1)
+      case class Mid1(inner: Inner1)
+      case class Inner1(name: String, value: Int)

problem_statement:
Replace QDox with tree-sitter for Java source parsing
ð I'm posting this as an issue to trigger discussion to identify the best path forward. Adding a [draft PR](https://github.com/scalameta/metals/pull/8350) in case the community wishes to move in the direction of tree-sitter.

## Problem

QDox fails to parse valid Java source files that use annotations in type parameter positions. For example, Guava's `ImmutableMap.java` ([source](https://github.com/google/guava/blob/d3efe023e43e25cd65461a30b9ae692d6685cf84/guava/src/com/google/common/collect/ImmutableMap.java#L91-L92)):

```java
public static <T extends @Nullable Object, K, V>
    Collector<T, ?, ImmutableMap<K, V>> toImmutableMap(
```

This throws a `ParseException` in QDox, which has no error recovery â meaning we lose *all* symbol information for the entire file. This pattern is common in well-maintained libraries (Guava, Error Prone, Checker Framework-annotated code).

## Additional Issues

QDox is officially end-of-life; see [README](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox). Outstanding bugs for modern Java features were closed as "Won't fix" on the same day:

- [qdox#182](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox/issues/182) â annotated type parameters (`<T extends @Nullable Object>`) â the bug that triggered this work
- [qdox#272](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox/issues/272) â sealed interfaces cause StackOverflowError

There will be no further QDox releases. A parser replacement is needed.

## Alternatives considered

| Criterion | QDox 2.2.0 | JavaParser 3.28 | tree-sitter-ng 0.26 |
|-----------|------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| Error recovery | None (throws) | Partial | Excellent (always produces tree) |
| `<T extends @Nullable Object>` | Fails | Mostly works | Full support |
| Relative speed | Fast | [~36x slower than tree-sitter](https://symflower.com/en/company/blog/2023/parsing-code-with-tree-sitter/) | Fastest |
| Java version coverage | Incomplete | Java 1â25 | Tracks spec via grammar |
| Scope | Name extraction | Full AST (overkill) | Visit only declarations |
| Native dependency | No | No | Yes (bundled for x86_64/aarch64 on macOS/Linux/Windows) |

[**JavaParser**](https://github.com/javaparser/javaparser) was passed over because it builds a full AST including method bodies and expressions â work we don't need for extracting declaration names and positions. Its error recovery operates at the statement level inside method bodies, which doesn't help our use case.

[**tree-sitter**](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter) is the best fit because:
1. **It was purpose-built as an incremental parser for editor experiences and is quickly becoming the de facto parsing library used by language servers and IDEs (VS Code, Neovim, Zed, Helix)**
2. Error recovery is a core design goal â invalid regions get `ERROR` nodes while surrounding declarations parse correctly with accurate positions
3. O(n) C-based parser, critical for indexing thousands of JDK source files on project import
4. Grammar explicitly models `annotated_type` at all type-use positions â no workarounds
5. We only visit declaration nodes, skipping method bodies entirely

The trade-off is a JNI/native library dependency. The `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter` bindings bundle natives for the platforms that cover >99% of developer workstations.

## Proposed changes

- Replace `com.thoughtworks.qdox:qdox` with `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter` + `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter-java`
- Rewrite `JavaMtags` to walk the tree-sitter CST instead of using `JavaProjectBuilder`
- Introduce lightweight case classes to decouple `JavadocIndexer` from the parser model
- Add a `JavadocParser` utility for structured Javadoc comment extraction

### Additional contract requirements

## Java indexing and documentation contract

The Java parser migration changes how Java sources are parsed, but the
indexing services (`Mtags` and `JavadocIndexer`) must preserve the following
observable behavior, independent of the parser that produces them.

### SemanticDB Java symbols

For a Java source file, `Mtags.allToplevels` produces SemanticDB symbols with
these conventions (they match what the previous QDox-based indexer emitted):

- Symbols use the slash-separated Java layout: packages and classes are
  joined with `.` in the owner string, classes end with `#`, terms (methods,
  fields, constructors) end with `.`.
- Every declared constructor is indexed, including private constructors. The
  first constructor gets `<init>`()., overloaded constructors get increasing
  disambiguators (`<init>`(+1)., and so on); the same convention applies to
  overloaded methods (`b().`, `b(+1).`).
- Classes with no explicitly declared constructor still produce a
  constructor symbol for the synthesized default constructor, so every type
  declaration is accompanied by a constructor entry.
- Every type parameter of a generic class or interface produces a
  type-parameter symbol of the form `Owner#[T]`.

### Parser robustness

- Annotations in type-use positions, for example
  `<T extends @Nullable Object, K, V>`, must be parsed without error so the
  generic method and its enclosing type are still fully indexed.
- The indexer must tolerate malformed source regions: a syntax error in one

problem_statement_base:
Replace QDox with tree-sitter for Java source parsing
ð I'm posting this as an issue to trigger discussion to identify the best path forward. Adding a [draft PR](https://github.com/scalameta/metals/pull/8350) in case the community wishes to move in the direction of tree-sitter.

## Problem

QDox fails to parse valid Java source files that use annotations in type parameter positions. For example, Guava's `ImmutableMap.java` ([source](https://github.com/google/guava/blob/d3efe023e43e25cd65461a30b9ae692d6685cf84/guava/src/com/google/common/collect/ImmutableMap.java#L91-L92)):

```java
public static <T extends @Nullable Object, K, V>
    Collector<T, ?, ImmutableMap<K, V>> toImmutableMap(
```

This throws a `ParseException` in QDox, which has no error recovery â meaning we lose *all* symbol information for the entire file. This pattern is common in well-maintained libraries (Guava, Error Prone, Checker Framework-annotated code).

## Additional Issues

QDox is officially end-of-life; see [README](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox). Outstanding bugs for modern Java features were closed as "Won't fix" on the same day:

- [qdox#182](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox/issues/182) â annotated type parameters (`<T extends @Nullable Object>`) â the bug that triggered this work
- [qdox#272](https://github.com/paul-hammant/qdox/issues/272) â sealed interfaces cause StackOverflowError

There will be no further QDox releases. A parser replacement is needed.

## Alternatives considered

| Criterion | QDox 2.2.0 | JavaParser 3.28 | tree-sitter-ng 0.26 |
|-----------|------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| Error recovery | None (throws) | Partial | Excellent (always produces tree) |
| `<T extends @Nullable Object>` | Fails | Mostly works | Full support |
| Relative speed | Fast | [~36x slower than tree-sitter](https://symflower.com/en/company/blog/2023/parsing-code-with-tree-sitter/) | Fastest |
| Java version coverage | Incomplete | Java 1â25 | Tracks spec via grammar |
| Scope | Name extraction | Full AST (overkill) | Visit only declarations |
| Native dependency | No | No | Yes (bundled for x86_64/aarch64 on macOS/Linux/Windows) |

[**JavaParser**](https://github.com/javaparser/javaparser) was passed over because it builds a full AST including method bodies and expressions â work we don't need for extracting declaration names and positions. Its error recovery operates at the statement level inside method bodies, which doesn't help our use case.

[**tree-sitter**](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter) is the best fit because:
1. **It was purpose-built as an incremental parser for editor experiences and is quickly becoming the de facto parsing library used by language servers and IDEs (VS Code, Neovim, Zed, Helix)**
2. Error recovery is a core design goal â invalid regions get `ERROR` nodes while surrounding declarations parse correctly with accurate positions
3. O(n) C-based parser, critical for indexing thousands of JDK source files on project import
4. Grammar explicitly models `annotated_type` at all type-use positions â no workarounds
5. We only visit declaration nodes, skipping method bodies entirely

The trade-off is a JNI/native library dependency. The `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter` bindings bundle natives for the platforms that cover >99% of developer workstations.

## Proposed changes

- Replace `com.thoughtworks.qdox:qdox` with `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter` + `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter-java`
- Rewrite `JavaMtags` to walk the tree-sitter CST instead of using `JavaProjectBuilder`
- Introduce lightweight case classes to decouple `JavadocIndexer` from the parser model
- Add a `JavadocParser` utility for structured Javadoc comment extraction

## Java indexing and documentation contract

The Java parser migration changes how Java sources are parsed, but the
indexing services (`Mtags` and `JavadocIndexer`) must preserve the following
observable behavior, independent of the parser that produces them.

### SemanticDB Java symbols

For a Java source file, `Mtags.allToplevels` produces SemanticDB symbols with
these conventions (they match what the previous QDox-based indexer emitted):

- Symbols use the slash-separated Java layout: packages and classes are
  joined with `.` in the owner string, classes end with `#`, terms (methods,
  fields, constructors) end with `.`.
- Every declared constructor is indexed, including private constructors. The
  first constructor gets `<init>`()., overloaded constructors get increasing
  disambiguators (`<init>`(+1)., and so on); the same convention applies to
  overloaded methods (`b().`, `b(+1).`).
- Classes with no explicitly declared constructor still produce a
  constructor symbol for the synthesized default constructor, so every type
  declaration is accompanied by a constructor entry.
- Every type parameter of a generic class or interface produces a
  type-parameter symbol of the form `Owner#[T]`.

### Parser robustness

- Annotations in type-use positions, for example
  `<T extends @Nullable Object, K, V>`, must be parsed without error so the
  generic method and its enclosing type are still fully indexed.
- The indexer must tolerate malformed source regions: a syntax error in one
  member must not suppress the symbols of the well-formed declarations in
  the same file.
- Sealed interfaces with `permits` clauses are indexed without errors.

### Javadoc documentation indexing

`JavadocIndexer.all` extracts documentation from Java source comments for
hovers. The following behavior is required:

- Each documented declaration is reported under its symbol with a docstring,
  parameter entries, and type-parameter entries.

  rendered docstring; and it is attached to the owning declaration as the
  type-parameter entry for `T`.
- A declaration without a comment produces an empty docstring.


### Javadoc parsing utility

`JavadocParser` provides the shared public parsing behavior used for Java
documentation:

+package scala.meta.internal.metals
+
+/**
+ * Parses raw Javadoc comment strings, extracting body text and param tags.
+ *
+ * Stripping and tag-detection behavior is adopted from qdox's comment lexer
+ * to maintain consistency with the previous qdox-based implementation.
+ */
+object JavadocParser {
+
+  // Strips the comment delimiters and leading `*` from each line.
+  // After removing `*`, exactly one space or tab is consumed (if present),
+  // preserving any additional indentation.
+  def stripComment(raw: String): List[String] = {
+    val body = raw.stripPrefix("/**").stripSuffix("*/")
+    body.linesIterator.toList.map { line =>
+      val trimmed = line.replaceFirst("^\\s*", "")
+      if (trimmed.startsWith("* "))
+        trimmed.substring(2)
+      else if (trimmed.startsWith("*\t"))
+        trimmed.substring(2)
+      else if (trimmed.startsWith("*"))
+        trimmed.substring(1)
+      else
+        trimmed
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Returns the body text of a Javadoc comment (before any `@tag` lines).
+   * A line is considered a tag line only when it starts with `@` at the
+   * beginning of the logical line (after stripping).
+   */
+  def extractBody(docComment: Option[String]): String = {
+    docComment match {
+      case None => ""
+      case Some(raw) =>
+        val lines = stripComment(raw)
+        val bodyLines = lines.takeWhile(line => !line.startsWith("@"))
+        bodyLines.mkString("\n").trim
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Rewrites Javadoc `@param <T> desc` to Scaladoc `@tparam T desc` so the
+  // ScaladocParser's HTML-cleaning step doesn't strip <T> as an unknown HTML
+  // tag (which would leave the next word as the captured parameter name).
+  private val JavadocTypeParamTag =
+    """@param(\s+)<(\w+)>""".r
+
+  /**
+   * Rewrites Javadoc-only constructs into a Scaladoc-equivalent form so the
+   * Scaladoc-based MarkdownGenerator can render Javadoc comments correctly.
+   */
+  def toScaladocCompatible(raw: String): String = {
+    JavadocTypeParamTag.replaceAllIn(
+      raw,
+      m => s"@tparam${m.group(1)}${m.group(2)}"
+    )
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Extracts `@param` tags from a Javadoc comment, returning a map of
+   * param name to `"name description"`. Supports multi-line tag descriptions:
+   * continuation lines (that don't start with `@`) are appended to the
+   * previous tag.
+   */
+  def extractParamTags(docComment: Option[String]): Map[String, String] = {
+    docComment match {
+      case None => Map.empty
+      case Some(raw) =>
+        val lines = stripComment(raw)
+        val paramPattern = """@param\s+(\S+)(?:\s+(.*))?""".r
+
+        val result = Map.newBuilder[String, String]
+        var currentParam: String = null
+        var currentDesc: StringBuilder = null
+        var inParam = false
+
+        def flushParam(): Unit = {
+          if (inParam && currentParam != null) {
+            val desc = currentDesc.toString.trim
+            val value =
+              if (desc.isEmpty) currentParam
+              else s"$currentParam $desc"
+            result += (currentParam -> value)
+          }
+        }
+
+        for (line <- lines) {
+          if (line.startsWith("@param ") || line.startsWith("@param\t")) {
+            flushParam()
+            line match {
+              case paramPattern(name, desc) =>
+                currentParam = name
+                currentDesc = new StringBuilder
+                if (desc != null) currentDesc.append(desc)
+                inParam = true
+              case _ =>
+                inParam = false
+            }
+          } else if (line.startsWith("@")) {
+            flushParam()
+            inParam = false
+            currentParam = null
+          } else if (inParam) {
+            // Continuation line for current param
+            val trimmed = line.trim
+            if (trimmed.nonEmpty) {
+              if (currentDesc.nonEmpty) currentDesc.append(" ")
+              currentDesc.append(trimmed)
+            }
+          }
+        }
+
+        flushParam()
+
+        result.result()
+    }
+  }
+}

+  // since it has a lot of overhead from scanning the classpath.
+  def createParserFactory(
+      ctx: Context
+  ): ParseTask = {
+    val silentWriter = new PrintWriter(new StringWriter())
+    Log.preRegister(ctx, silentWriter)
+    ctx.put(Log.outKey, silentWriter)
+    ctx.put(Log.errKey, silentWriter)
+    val diagnostics = new DiagnosticCollector[JavaFileObject]()
+    ctx.put(classOf[DiagnosticListener[_]], diagnostics)
+    val fileManager = new JavacFileManager(ctx, false, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+    Options.instance(ctx).put("--enable-preview", "true")
+    Options.instance(ctx).put("allowStringFolding", "false")
+    fileManager.setLocation(
+      StandardLocation.PLATFORM_CLASS_PATH,
+      ju.Collections.emptyList()
+    )
+    fileManager.setContext(ctx)
+    ctx.put(classOf[JavaFileManager], fileManager)

+        case FromStart(node) =>

+      val endOffset = end match {
+        case FromEnd(node) =>
+          sourcePositions.getEndPosition(cu, node).intValue()
+        case FromStart(node) =>
+          sourcePositions.getStartPosition(cu, node).intValue()
+      }

+          }

+        } else {
+          i += 1
+        }

+    private def updateDisambiguators(node: ClassTree): Unit = {
+      // Per the SemanticDB spec, the disambiguator is the definition order of
+      // the symbol where static methods are sorted to the end. This quirk is
+      // because the Scala compiler doesn't preserve the original order of
+      // methods in the Java class, it groups static methods into the "module
+      // symbol" (companion object) even if Java doesn't have companion objects.
+      // Private constructors are excluded from both the output and
+      // disambiguation counting to preserve compatibility.
+      val sorted = node
+        .getMembers()
+        .asScala
+        .collect {
+          case m: MethodTree
+              if !filterPrivateConstructors || !isPrivateConstructor(m) =>
+            m
+        }
+        .sortBy(m => m.getModifiers().getFlags().contains(Modifier.STATIC))
+      val counters = new ju.HashMap[String, Int]()
+      for (method <- sorted) {
+        val name = method.getName().toString()
+        val next = counters.getOrDefault(name, -1) + 1
+        counters.put(name, next)
+        if (next > 0) {
+          disambiguators.put(method, next)
+        }
+      }
+    }
+
+    // Uses javac's internal DocCommentTable to retrieve Javadoc comments.
+    // When keepDocComments=true, the parser populates this table during
+    // parsing. This is more robust than manual backward text scanning,
+    // which can fail with annotations or non-Javadoc block comments
+    // between the doc comment and the declaration.
+    private def getDocComment(node: Tree): Option[String] =
+      (cu, node) match {
+        case (unit: javacTree.JCCompilationUnit, jcNode: javacTree)
+            if keepDocComments =>
+          for {
+            docs <- Option(unit.docComments)
+            comment <- Option(docs.getComment(jcNode))
+          } yield comment.getText
+        case _ => None
+      }
+
+    private def extractParamNames(node: MethodTree): List[String] = {
+      node.getParameters().asScala.map(_.getName().toString()).toList
+    }
+
+    private def extractTypeParamNames(node: ClassTree): List[String] = {
+      node.getTypeParameters().asScala.map(_.getName().toString()).toList
+    }
+
+    private def extractMethodTypeParamNames(node: MethodTree): List[String] = {
+      node.getTypeParameters().asScala.map(_.getName().toString()).toList
+    }
+
+    private val recordMembers = new ju.LinkedHashSet[VariableTree]()
+    private val enumMembers = new ju.LinkedHashMap[VariableTree, NewClassTree]()
+
+    override def visitClass(node: ClassTree, p: Unit): TreePath = {
+      val name = node.getSimpleName().toString()
+      if (name.isEmpty() || name == "<error>") {
+        // Anonymous or error class - just scan contents
+        return super.visitClass(node, p)
+      }
+      if (node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.RECORD) {
+        // Records cannot have instance fields (JLS 8.10.3), so any
+        // non-static VariableTree in getMembers() is a record component.
+        // We filter out static fields to avoid misidentifying them as
+        // record components (which get emitted as accessor methods).
+        node.getMembers().asScala.foreach {
+          case v: VariableTree
+              if !v.getModifiers().getFlags().contains(Modifier.STATIC) =>
+            recordMembers.add(v)
+          case _ =>
+        }
+      }
+      if (node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.ENUM) {
+        node.getMembers().asScala.foreach {
+          case v: VariableTree =>
+            Option(v.getInitializer()) match {
+              case Some(n: NewClassTree)
+                  if n.getIdentifier().toString() == name =>
+                enumMembers.put(v, n)
+              case _ =>
+            }
+          case _ =>
+        }
+      }
+      updateDisambiguators(node)
+      mtags.withOwner() {
+        val pos = findNameRange(
+          start = node
+            .getModifiers()
+            .getAnnotations()
+            .asScala
+            .lastOption match {
+            case None => FromStart(node)
+            case Some(value) => FromEnd(value)
+          },
+          end = Option(node.getExtendsClause())
+            .orElse(node.getImplementsClause().asScala.headOption)
+            .orElse(node.getMembers().asScala.headOption)
+            .map(FromStart(_))
+            .getOrElse(FromEnd(node)),
+          name = name
+        )
+        mtags.tpe(
+          name,
+          pos,
+          kind = node.getKind() match {
+            case INTERFACE => Kind.INTERFACE
+            case _ => Kind.CLASS
+          },
+          if (node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.ENUM) Property.ENUM.value
+          else 0
+        )
+        node.getTypeParameters().forEach { tparam =>
+          mtags.withOwner() {
+            val tparamName = tparam.getName().toString()
+            mtags.tparam(
+              tparamName,
+              findNameRange(
+                start = tparam
+                  .getAnnotations()
+                  .asScala
+                  .lastOption match {
+                  case None => FromStart(tparam)
+                  case Some(value) => FromEnd(value)
+                },
+                end = FromEnd(tparam),
+                name = tparamName
+              ),
+              kind = Kind.TYPE_PARAMETER,
+              properties = 0
+            )
+          }
+        }
+
+        val typeParams = extractTypeParamNames(node)
+        onClass(currentOwner, name, typeParams, getDocComment(node))
+
+        lazy val constructorCount = node.getMembers().asScala.count {
+          case method: MethodTree =>
+            val ctorName = method.getName()
+            ctorName.length() > 0 && ctorName.charAt(0) == '<'
+          case _ => false
+        }
+        val isImplicitConstructor =
+          node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.RECORD ||
+            (node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.CLASS && constructorCount == 0) ||
+            // The implicit enum constructor could technically be dropped, but
+            // we include it for compatibility with semanticdb-javac.
+            (node.getKind() == Tree.Kind.ENUM && constructorCount == 0)
+        if (isImplicitConstructor) {
+          mtags.withOwner() {
+            mtags.ctor(
+              if (constructorCount == 0) "()" else s"(+$constructorCount)",
+              pos,
+              0
+            )
+          }
+        }
+
+        // Scan members
+        var r = scan(node.getModifiers(), p)
+        r = scanAndReduceIterable(node.getTypeParameters(), p, r)
+        r = scanAndReduce(node.getExtendsClause(), p, r)
+        r = scanAndReduceIterable(node.getImplementsClause(), p, r)
+        r = scanAndReduceIterable(node.getMembers(), p, r)
+        r
+      }
+    }
+
+    override def visitMethod(node: MethodTree, p: Unit): TreePath = {
+      if (!includeMembers) {
+        return null
+      }
+      val name = node.getName().toString()
+      if (name == "<error>") {
+        return null
+      }
+      if (filterPrivateConstructors && isPrivateConstructor(node)) {
+        return null
+      }
+      mtags.withOwner() {
+        val sym = mtags.method(
+          name = name,
+          disambiguator = disambiguators.getOrDefault(node, 0) match {
+            case 0 => "()"
+            case n => s"(+$n)"
+          },
+          pos = findNameRange(
+            start = Option(node.getReturnType())
+              .orElse(
+                node.getModifiers().getAnnotations().asScala.lastOption
+              )
+              .map(FromEnd(_))
+              .getOrElse(FromStart(node)),
+            end = node
+              .getParameters()
+              .asScala
+              .headOption
+              .orElse(node.getThrows().asScala.headOption)
+              .orElse(Option(node.getBody())) match {
+              case None => FromEnd(node)
+              case Some(value) => FromStart(value)
+            },
+            name = name match {
+              case "<init>" => Symbol(owner).displayName
+              case n => n
+            }
+          ),
+          0,
+          kind =
+            if (name == "<init>") Kind.CONSTRUCTOR
+            else Kind.METHOD
+        )
+        if (name == "<init>") {
+          onConstructor(
+            sym,
+            extractParamNames(node),
+            extractMethodTypeParamNames(node),
+            getDocComment(node)
+          )
+        } else {
+          onMethod(
+            sym,
+            name,
+            extractParamNames(node),
+            extractMethodTypeParamNames(node),
+            getDocComment(node)
+          )
+        }
+        null // don't scan method body
+      }
+    }
+
+    override def visitVariable(node: VariableTree, p: Unit): TreePath = {
+      if (!includeMembers) {
+        return null
+      }
+      val name = node.getName().toString()
+      if (name == "<error>") {
+        return null
+      }
+      val enumMemberInitializer = enumMembers.remove(node)
+      val isEnumMember = enumMemberInitializer != null
+      val isRecordMember = recordMembers.contains(node)
+
+      mtags.withOwner() {
+        // Skip local variables (inside method bodies)
+        if (!mtags.currentOwner.endsWith(").")) {
+          val pos = findNameRange(
+            start = Option(node.getType()) match {
+              case Some(value)
+                  if sourcePositions.getEndPosition(cu, value) >= 0 =>
+                FromEnd(value)
+              case _ => FromStart(node)
+            },
+            end = Option(node.getInitializer()) match {
+              case Some(value)
+                  if sourcePositions.getStartPosition(cu, value) >= 0 &&
+                    sourcePositions.getEndPosition(cu, value) >= 0 =>
+                FromStart(value)
+              case _ => FromEnd(node)
+            },
+            name = name
+          )
+          if (isRecordMember) {
+            mtags.method(
+              name = name,
+              disambiguator = "()",
+              pos = pos,
+              properties = 0
+            )
+          } else {
+            mtags.term(
+              name = name,
+              pos = pos,
+              kind = Kind.FIELD,
+              properties =
+                if (isEnumMember) Property.ENUM.value
+                else 0
+            )
+          }
+        }
+      }
+      null // don't scan variable initializers
+    }
+
+    override def visitPackage(node: PackageTree, p: Unit): TreePath = {
+      node.getPackageName().toString().split("\\.").foreach { pkgName =>
+        mtags.pkg(
+          pkgName,
+          findNameRange(
+            start = FromStart(node.getPackageName()),
+            end = FromEnd(node.getPackageName()),
+            name = pkgName
+          )
+        )
+      }
+      var r = scan(node.getAnnotations(), p)
+      r = scanAndReduce(node.getPackageName(), p, r)
+      r
+    }
+
+    private def scanAndReduce(node: Tree, p: Unit, r: TreePath): TreePath = {
+      reduce(scan(node, p), r)
+    }
+    private def scanAndReduceIterable(
+        nodes: java.lang.Iterable[_ <: Tree],
+        p: Unit,
+        r: TreePath
+    ): TreePath = {
+      reduce(scan(nodes, p), r)
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def reportError(e: Throwable): Unit = {
+    try {
+      val diagnosticMessages: collection.Seq[String] = parseTask match {
+        case None => Nil
+        case Some(task) =>
+          task.diagnostics.getDiagnostics().asScala.map { d =>
+            s"${d.getKind()}: ${d.getMessage(null)}"
+          }
+      }
+      val diagnosticsContent =
+        if (diagnosticMessages.nonEmpty)
+          s"""|diagnostics:
+              |${diagnosticMessages.mkString("\n")}
+              |""".stripMargin
+        else ""
+
+      rc.unsanitized()
+        .create(() =>
+          new Report(
+            name = "mtags-javac-error",
+            text = s"""|error in javac parser
+                       |$diagnosticsContent
+                       |""".stripMargin,
+            error = Some(e),
+            path = java.util.Optional.of(new URI(input.path)),
+            shortSummary = s"JavacMtags error processing ${input.path}",
+            id = java.util.Optional.of(input.path)
+          )
+        )
+    } catch {
+      case NonFatal(_) =>
+    }
+  }
+}
