problem_statement:
Allow Debug auth to use interactive OIDC while preserving TestAuth bootstrap
Objective:
- Make Grace Debug/TestAuth configuration accept normal interactive OIDC/MSA-authenticated CLI requests for authenticated endpoints such as `GET /auth/me` and `POST /auth/token/create`, while preserving the existing no-external-auth TestAuth bootstrap path for first-time local environments.

Context and evidence:
- Current Debug server logs show `GraceTest` challenged and 401 responses for `POST /auth/token/create` and `GET /auth/me` even when an Authorization header is present.
- `src/Grace.Server/Security/TestAuth.Server.fs` authenticates only when `x-grace-user-id` is present.
- `src/Grace.Server/Security/AuthSchemeSelection.Server.fs` currently routes non-PAT bearer requests to `GraceTest` when `GRACE_TESTING=1`.
- `src/Grace.Server/Startup.Server.fs` configures the testing auth branch with `GraceTest` and `GracePat`, but does not make OIDC/JWT bearer auth available in the testing branch.
- `src/Grace.CLI/Command/Auth.CLI.fs` gets interactive tokens for SDK calls, but `GRACE_TOKEN` intentionally remains PAT-only.
- `scripts/start-debuglocal.ps1` already proves the first-time local bootstrap path with explicit `x-grace-user-id` and PAT creation. Keep that path working.
- Local planning artifact: `docs/DebugAuthLocalBootstrapPlan.html`.

Owned paths:
- `src/Grace.Server/Startup.Server.fs`
- `src/Grace.Server/Security/AuthSchemeSelection.Server.fs`
- `src/Grace.Server/Security/TestAuth.Server.fs` only if the explicit TestAuth contract needs a small additive helper or test seam
- `src/Grace.Server/Security/*.Server.fs` only for auth-scheme composition directly required by this issue
- `src/Grace.SDK/Common.SDK.fs`
- `src/Grace.SDK/Auth.SDK.fs`
- `src/Grace.SDK/PersonalAccessToken.SDK.fs`
- `src/Grace.CLI/Command/Auth.CLI.fs`
- `src/Grace.Authorization.Tests/**`
- `src/Grace.Server.Unit.Tests/**`
- `src/Grace.Server.Tests/**` if HTTP-pipeline proof is needed
- `src/Grace.CLI.Tests/**`
- `src/docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`
- `docs/**` for first-time stand-up and Debug auth guidance
- nearby `AGENTS.md` files only if future agents need updated auth workflow context

Forbidden or sensitive paths:
- Do not re-enable local token-file persistence or broaden `GRACE_TOKEN` beyond Grace PATs.
- Do not make `/auth/token/create` anonymous or bypass authorization/role checks for token creation.
- Do not teach `GraceTest` to trust arbitrary bearer tokens.
- Do not log bearer tokens, PATs, authorization headers, secrets, or credential-bearing URLs.
- Do not change unrelated owner/repository command behavior, including the separate OwnerId issue, without updating the issue first.
- Do not edit Aspire resource, storage, Service Bus, Redis, or deployment infrastructure unless live evidence proves it is required and the issue is updated before editing.

Risk surfaces:
- Auth or secrets
- CLI public contract
- Server or API contract
- SDK or client contract
- Docs or workflow

Minimum detail gate:
- Invariant tuple:
  - Actor: Grace CLI user running against Debug/`GRACE_TESTING=1` server.
  - Routes: `GET /auth/me` and `POST /auth/token/create` remain authenticated endpoints.
  - Schemes: Grace PAT bearer uses `GracePat`; valid non-PAT OIDC/JWT bearer uses JwtBearer when OIDC config exists; explicit `x-grace-user-id` uses `GraceTest` only in testing mode.
  - Identity dimensions: the effective Grace user identity comes from the validated principal claim mapping for OIDC/PAT, or from the explicit TestAuth header for local/test bootstrap; mixed or stale identities must not silently collapse into the wrong user.
  - Durable source of truth: server authentication/authorization middleware and PAT issuance state, with RBAC/role assignment still authorizing token creation after authentication succeeds.
- Forbidden implementation shapes:
  - No accepting unvalidated bearer tokens in Debug.
  - No using TestAuth as a fallback for arbitrary Authorization headers.
  - No stripping Authorization headers client-side to force TestAuth.
  - No changing `GRACE_TOKEN` to accept Auth0/OIDC access tokens.
  - No broad catch-all exception handling that converts auth failures into success or hides server errors.
  - No docs that tell maintainers to manually mint tokens with raw `Invoke-RestMethod` as the normal path.
- Expected tests:
  - positive: PAT bearer still selects `GracePat` and authenticates.
  - positive: explicit `x-grace-user-id` still authenticates in Debug/TestAuth mode.
  - positive: valid non-PAT OIDC/JWT bearer is routed to JwtBearer in Debug/TestAuth mode when OIDC config exists.
  - positive: authenticated OIDC principal can call `/auth/token/create` when authorized.
  - negative: absent auth, invalid bearer, or OIDC bearer without OIDC config does not authenticate.
  - negative: TestAuth is not selected merely because a non-PAT Authorization header is present.
  - regression: `grace auth whoami -o Verbose` and token creation no longer surface empty-body 401 JSON parse exceptions.
  - boundary: PAT prefix checks remain exact and do not misclassify malformed, blank, or whitespace bearer values.
- High-risk adversarial examples:
  - Request contains both `Authorization: Bearer <Grace PAT>` and `x-grace-user-id`; PAT precedence must be explicit and tested or deliberately rejected.
  - Request contains non-PAT bearer plus `x-grace-user-id`; selector behavior must be deterministic and documented/test-covered.
  - `GRACE_TESTING=1` with no OIDC config must not attempt JwtBearer validation or produce misleading CLI guidance.
  - `GRACE_TESTING=0` must preserve production OIDC/PAT behavior.
  - Empty 401 response bodies must render actionable client errors without leaking token material.
- Selected risk-surface traps:
  - Auth ordering: prove scheme selection order, not only happy-path endpoint execution.
  - CLI side effects: preserve stdout/stderr cleanliness and `--output Json` contract where changed.
  - Contract propagation: update SDK/CLI error handling together if the error envelope behavior changes.
  - Docs freshness: document both first-time local TestAuth bootstrap and interactive OIDC/MSA bootstrap; call out first-admin authorization separately from authentication.
  - Security logging: keep Authorization/PAT material redacted in logs and tests.
- Explicit N/A waivers with reasons:
  - Orleans actor behavior: N/A unless implementation changes PAT issuance grain behavior; expected change is auth composition and client error handling.
  - Storage/Cosmos/Service Bus/Redis: N/A unless worker discovers token persistence semantics require integration proof beyond existing tests.
  - OpenAPI route shape: N/A if route paths, methods, request DTOs, and response DTOs do not change.

Validation:
- Focused command:
  - Worker should first add focused failing tests around auth scheme selection and client 401 handling, then run the smallest matching focused test commands needed for RED/GREEN evidence.
  - If using `dotnet test --no-build`, first build the matching project in Release.
- Formatting:
  - Run targeted Fantomas formatting/checks before build/test validation for touched F# files.
- Fast repo gate:
  - `pwsh ./scripts/validate.ps1 -Fast`
- Full or Aspire gate, if needed:
  - `pwsh ./scripts/validate.ps1 -Full` only if the worker changes Aspire/runtime startup behavior or cannot prove the HTTP auth pipeline through Fast-profile tests.
- Docs validation:
  - `npx --yes markdownlint-cli2 "src/docs/ENVIRONMENT.md"`
  - Include any other changed Markdown docs in the same MarkdownLint command.
- Final hygiene:
  - `git diff --check`
- Manual verification, if practical:
  - In Debug with OIDC configured: `grace auth login`, `grace auth whoami -o Verbose`, then `grace auth token create --token-name local-dev --expires-in 90d -o Verbose`.
  - In Debug without OIDC setup: `pwsh ./scripts/start-debuglocal.ps1 -GraceServerUri "http://localhost:5000"` still prints usable `GRACE_SERVER_URI` and `GRACE_TOKEN` values.

Definition of done:
- Debug/TestAuth mode is additive: PAT, OIDC/JWT bearer, and explicit TestAuth each route to the intended scheme.
- `grace auth token create` works after interactive OIDC/MSA login when the authenticated user is authorized.
- First-time stand-up remains easy through `start-debuglocal.ps1` with explicit TestAuth bootstrap.
- Empty-body 401s from auth endpoints no longer produce raw JSON parse exceptions in CLI/SDK-facing auth commands.
- `/docs` guidance is updated for Debug auth, first-time local bootstrap, interactive OIDC/MSA bootstrap, and first-admin authorization.
- Tests cover positive, negative, regression, and boundary cases from this issue.
- Coding and fix work completed through implementation subagents, with the main agent acting as orchestrator.
- Worker completed a bot-prevention self-review over the actual diff before handoff.
- Ready-for-review pull request opened and linked with `Closes #<issue>`.
- Validation evidence recorded on the PR.
- Codex Code Review Bot reviewed the latest PR commit and either reported no issues with a thumbs-up reaction on the PR body or all bot comments were fixed, answered, resolved, and followed by a no-issues bot review.
- Follow-ups named explicitly if any behavior is intentionally deferred.

### Additional contract requirements

This task clarifies two points of observable behavior for Debug/TestAuth scheme selection that the original statement leaves to deterministic, documented implementation choice:

- When a request in testing mode with OIDC configured presents both a non-PAT bearer token and the explicit TestAuth bootstrap user header, the public contract requires deterministic, test-covered selection and non-collapsing identities; it does not mandate one specific scheme for that combination. If the bearer-validation scheme is selected, an unverifiable bearer must not authenticate. If the TestAuth bootstrap is selected, the resulting identity must be exactly the explicit header user and never an identity derived from the bearer or PAT token.
- In testing mode, a credential-free request (no bearer and no explicit TestAuth bootstrap header) must not authenticate, and its routing must be deterministic; the public contract does not mandate which configured scheme handles it.

Token creation remains authorization-protected: authenticated admission of a validated principal to the token-creation route is the observable behavior covered by the tests, and downstream issuance depends on the surrounding environment. Authenticated requests to the identity-reporting route in Debug mode with OIDC configured must succeed and report the mapped user identity, without requiring the system permission gate used by token creation. Unauthenticated requests to both routes remain rejected before their handlers run.

+## Development without Auth0 (TestAuth)
+
+For local development, you can skip Auth0 entirely by enabling the built-in TestAuth handler.
+This is intended for **dev/test only**.
+
+Debug/TestAuth mode also supports normal JWT bearer authentication when OIDC is configured. Scheme selection is
+deterministic:
+
+1. Grace PAT bearer tokens use `GracePat`.
+1. Non-PAT bearer tokens use OIDC/JWT validation when server OIDC settings are present.
+1. Explicit `x-grace-user-id` requests use TestAuth in testing mode.
+1. Testing requests with no bearer token use TestAuth so local bootstrap can still challenge through the TestAuth path.
+
+TestAuth does not trust arbitrary bearer tokens, and the CLI's `GRACE_TOKEN` environment variable remains PAT-only.
 
 ### Enable TestAuth
 
@@ -126,8 +136,50 @@ When enabled, Grace authenticates requests using headers:
    curl -H "x-grace-user-id: dev-scott" "http://localhost:5000/auth/me"
    ```
 
-On first activation (with no existing assignments), Grace will seed `SystemAdmin` for `dev-scott`.
-After that, bootstrap is a no-op.
+On first activation (with no existing assignments), Grace will seed `SystemAdmin` for `dev-scott`.
+After that, bootstrap is a no-op.
+
+The canonical zero-external-auth bootstrap helper uses this path and prints a usable PAT:
+
+PowerShell:
+
+```powershell
+pwsh ./scripts/start-debuglocal.ps1 -GraceServerUri "http://localhost:5000" -SkipAuthProbe
+```
+
+bash / zsh:
+
+```bash
+pwsh ./scripts/start-debuglocal.ps1 --GraceServerUri "http://localhost:5000" -SkipAuthProbe
+```
+
+`-SkipAuthProbe` is required for the true zero-OIDC bootstrap path because the default auth probe checks
+`/auth/oidc/config` before TestAuth PAT creation. Omit `-SkipAuthProbe` when OIDC/MSA settings are configured and you
+want the startup helper to verify both `/auth/oidc/config` and `/auth/me` before creating the PAT.
+
+If OIDC/MSA is configured instead, use the interactive CLI path:
+
+PowerShell:
+
+```powershell
+$env:GRACE_SERVER_URI="http://localhost:5000"
+grace auth login
+grace auth whoami --output Verbose
+grace auth token create --name "local-dev" --expires-in 30d --output Verbose
+```
+
+bash / zsh:
+
+```bash
+export GRACE_SERVER_URI="http://localhost:5000"
+grace auth login
+grace auth whoami --output Verbose
+grace auth token create --name "local-dev" --expires-in 30d --output Verbose
+```
+
+`grace auth whoami` proves authentication. `grace auth token create` also requires authorization: the authenticated
+principal must already have a role such as `SystemAdmin`, either from first-admin bootstrap seeding or from an existing
+admin grant.

+    // Builds the authentication pipeline by invoking Startup.ConfigureServices,
+    // then observes its policy selector while authenticating real HttpContext
+    // requests. The test does not reproduce the application's routing or
+    // registration logic.
+    let buildPipeline (isTesting: bool) (hasOidc: bool) =
+        let configuration =
+            let builder = ConfigurationBuilder()
+
+            if hasOidc then
+                builder.AddInMemoryCollection(
+                    [ KeyValuePair<string, string>("grace:auth:oidc:authority", oidcIssuer)
+                      KeyValuePair<string, string>("grace:auth:oidc:audience", oidcAudience) ]
+                )
+                |> ignore
+
+            builder.Build()
+
+        let oidcConfig = ExternalAuthConfig.tryGetOidcConfig configuration
+        Assert.That(oidcConfig |> Option.isSome, Is.EqualTo(hasOidc), "Test setup must reflect the requested OIDC availability.")
+
+        // Configure the complete production service collection. GRACE_TESTING
+        // is restored immediately after registration so this nonparallel
+        // fixture does not leave process-wide state behind.
+        let previousTesting = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GRACE_TESTING")
+        let previousPubSub = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.GracePubSubSystem)
+        let previousStorageAccount = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.AzureStorageAccountName)
+
+        let services = ServiceCollection()
+
+        try
+            Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("GRACE_TESTING", (if isTesting then "1" else null))
+            Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.GracePubSubSystem, "Unknown")
+            Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.AzureStorageAccountName, "graceteststorage")
+            Utilities.memoryCache.Set(Constants.MemoryCache.GraceConfiguration, configuration) |> ignore
+
+            Application.Startup(configuration).ConfigureServices(services)
+
+            // Observes the selector installed by the production registration
+            // without replacing its decision. Authentication still runs
+            // through the production policy scheme and production handlers.
+            let forwardedSchemes = ResizeArray<string>()
+
+            // Keep JWT validation local and deterministic while retaining the
+            // production JWT bearer handler and registration.
+            services.PostConfigure<JwtBearerOptions>(
+                JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme,
+                fun options ->
+                    let oidc = OpenIdConnectConfiguration(Issuer = oidcIssuer)
+                    oidc.SigningKeys.Add(oidcSigningKey)
+                    options.ConfigurationManager <- StaticConfigurationManager<OpenIdConnectConfiguration>(oidc)
+                    options.TokenValidationParameters <-
+                        TokenValidationParameters(
+                            ValidateIssuer = true,
+                            ValidIssuer = oidcIssuer,
+                            ValidateAudience = true,
+                            ValidAudience = oidcAudience,
+                            ValidateLifetime = true,
+                            ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
+                            IssuerSigningKey = oidcSigningKey
+                        )
+            )
+            |> ignore
+
+            services.PostConfigure<PolicySchemeOptions>(
+                "GraceAuth",
+                fun options ->
+                    let productionSelector = options.ForwardDefaultSelector
+
+                    options.ForwardDefaultSelector <-
+                        Func<HttpContext, string>(fun context ->
+                            let scheme = productionSelector.Invoke(context)
+                            forwardedSchemes.Add(scheme)
+                            scheme)
+            )
+            |> ignore
+

+            // pipeline issues, together with their outcomes. Tests may
+            // record outcomes for later checks; with no recorded outcome the
+            // real permission evaluation runs against the in-memory
+            // assignment functions.

+
+            let recordedOutcomes = ResizeArray<PermissionCheckResult>()
+
+            services.AddSingleton<IGracePermissionEvaluator>(
+                { new IGracePermissionEvaluator with
+                    member _.CheckAsync(principalSet, effectiveClaims, operation, resource) =
+                        task {
+                            permissionChecks.Add((operation, resource))

+                            if recordedOutcomes.Count > 0 then
+                                let outcome = recordedOutcomes[recordedOutcomes.Count - 1]
+                                recordedOutcomes.RemoveAt(recordedOutcomes.Count - 1)
+                                return outcome
+                            else
+                                let productionEvaluator =
+                                    GracePermissionEvaluator(PermissionEvaluatorDefaults.getAssignmentsForScope, PermissionEvaluatorDefaults.getPathPermissionsForRepository)

+                                return!
+                                    (productionEvaluator :> IGracePermissionEvaluator)
+                                        .CheckAsync(principalSet, effectiveClaims, operation, resource)
+                        } }
+            )

+            Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.GracePubSubSystem, previousPubSub)
+            Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable(Constants.EnvironmentVariables.AzureStorageAccountName, previousStorageAccount)
+
+    let authenticateRequest (context: DefaultHttpContext) (authorization: string option) (testUserId: string option) =
+        task {
+            match authorization with
+            | Some value -> context.Request.Headers.Authorization <- StringValues(value)
+            | None -> ()
+
+            match testUserId with
+            | Some value -> context.Request.Headers[TestAuth.UserIdHeader] <- StringValues(value)
+            | None -> ()
+
+            return! context.AuthenticateAsync("GraceAuth")
+        }

+    let authenticatedScheme (forwardedSchemes: ResizeArray<string>) (result: AuthenticateResult) =
+        // A success ticket carries the scheme that established the identity;
+        // otherwise the most recently recorded forwarding decision names the
+        // scheme the request was routed to. The claim-transformation service
+        // may authenticate the request again, so consult the recorded
+        // decisions in order.
+        if result.Succeeded && not (isNull result.Ticket) then
+            result.Ticket.AuthenticationScheme
+        else
+            match Seq.tryLast forwardedSchemes with
+            | Some scheme -> scheme
+            | None -> failwith "The request was never routed to any authentication scheme."
+
+    // Asserts that the request is routed to the expected scheme and does not
+    // authenticate with unverifiable or absent credentials: the target handler
+    // reports no result for tokens it cannot validate, so only an
+    // identity-establishing source can produce a success ticket.
+    let assertRouting (isTesting: bool) (hasOidc: bool) (authorization: string option) (testUserId: string option) (expectedScheme: string) =
+        let provider, forwardedSchemes, _permissionChecks, _recordedOutcomes = buildPipeline isTesting hasOidc
+        use provider = provider
+
+        let context = DefaultHttpContext()
+        context.RequestServices <- provider
+        forwardedSchemes.Clear()
+
+        let result =
+            authenticateRequest context authorization testUserId
+            |> fun t -> t.Result
+
+        let scheme = authenticatedScheme forwardedSchemes result
+
+        Assert.That(scheme, Is.EqualTo(expectedScheme), $"Expected the request to be routed to scheme '{expectedScheme}' but it was routed to '{scheme}'.")
+
+        Assert.That(result.Succeeded, Is.False, $"The request must not authenticate through scheme '{expectedScheme}' with unverifiable or absent credentials.")
+
+    // Routes one HTTP request through a test pipeline composed only of the
+    // standard production authentication and authorization components; the
+    // test pipeline adds no gates of its own. A request authenticated through
+    // the production policy scheme and admitted by the production
+    // authorization middleware reaches the supplied production endpoint
+    // handler. Returns the response status code, response body, whether the
+    // endpoint handler ran, and any error the handler raised.
+    let runEndpointRequest (isTesting: bool) (hasOidc: bool) (method: string) (path: string) (authorization: string option) (body: string option) (endpoint: HttpHandler) =
+        task {
+            let provider, _forwardedSchemes, _permissionChecks, _recordedOutcomes = buildPipeline isTesting hasOidc
+
+            try
+                // Records whether the request cleared the production
+                // authentication/authorization middleware and reached the
+                // production endpoint handler.
+                let mutable endpointReached = false
+
+                let endpointDelegate: RequestDelegate =
+                    RequestDelegate(fun (context: HttpContext) ->
+                        endpointReached <- true
+                        let giraffeNext: HttpFunc = fun someContext -> Task.FromResult(Some someContext)
+
+                        task {
+                            let! _outcome = endpoint giraffeNext context
+                            return ()
+                        }
+                        :> Task)
+
+                let applicationBuilder: IApplicationBuilder = ApplicationBuilder(provider)
+                applicationBuilder.UseAuthentication() |> ignore
+                applicationBuilder.UseAuthorization() |> ignore
+                applicationBuilder.Run(endpointDelegate)
+                let app: RequestDelegate = applicationBuilder.Build()
+
+                let context = DefaultHttpContext()
+                context.RequestServices <- provider
+                context.Request.Method <- method
+                context.Request.Scheme <- "http"
+                context.Request.Host <- HostString("localhost")
+                context.Request.Path <- PathString(path)
+                // Marks the request as a matched endpoint route, mirroring
+                // the routing stage in the production pipeline.
+                context.SetEndpoint(Endpoint(endpointDelegate, EndpointMetadataCollection(), path))
+
+                match authorization with
+                | Some value -> context.Request.Headers.Authorization <- StringValues(value)
+                | None -> ()
+
+                match body with
+                | Some payload ->
+                    let payloadBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(payload)
+                    context.Request.Body <- new IO.MemoryStream(payloadBytes)
+                    context.Request.ContentLength <- Nullable(int64 payloadBytes.Length)
+                    context.Request.ContentType <- "application/json"
+                | None -> ()
+
+                let responseBody = new IO.MemoryStream()
+                context.Response.Body <- responseBody
+
+                let! handlerError =
+                    task {
+                        try
+                            do! app.Invoke(context)
+                            return None
+                        with
+                        | ex ->
+                            // An exception escaping from the endpoint handler
+                            // (for example from a downstream dependency that
+                            // is unavailable in this test environment) still
+                            // proves the request cleared the production
+                            // authentication/authorization middleware. Report
+                            // it as an internal error so the observed status
+                            // is never mistaken for an authorization denial.
+                            context.Response.StatusCode <- StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError
+                            return Some ex.Message
+                    }
+
+                responseBody.Position <- 0L
+
+                use reader = new IO.StreamReader(responseBody, Encoding.UTF8)
+                let! responseText = reader.ReadToEndAsync()
+
+                return (context.Response.StatusCode, responseText, endpointReached, handlerError)
+            finally
+                provider.Dispose()
+        }

CLI: derive --schema and --examples from actual ReturnValue types
# CLI: derive `--schema` and `--examples` from actual `ReturnValue` types

## Objective

Make the CLI's inert `--schema` and `--examples` introspection accurately describe the success value inside the existing `GraceReturnValue<T>` envelope for every JSON-success command that already has a declared result type. This lets people and agents discover the usable result shape without changing the `cli-json-v1` runtime envelope.

## Why this matters

Grace users need machine-readable output they can understand before running a command. Today the schema truthfully describes the wrapper, but most commands expose an `Unsupported command output contract` placeholder where an agent needs the actual `ReturnValue` shape. `--examples` has the same gap.

## Current-state evidence

- `grace refs --schema` reports `metadata-incomplete` and an unsupported `ReturnValue` contract, although its handler returns a `GraceReturnValue<BranchDto * ReferenceDto array>`.
- `grace refs -o Json` correctly retains the existing `GraceReturnValue` envelope; its `ReturnValue` serializes as the two-element F# tuple result.
- The command-output registry currently has 208 entries: 187 normal common-envelope commands, one conditional `watch --check` command, 11 deferred non-JSON-success paths, and nine source-only paths. Only ten entries currently have concrete nested schemas.
- Grace already centralizes JSON options, including the F# converter, in `Constants.Shared.fs`. .NET 10 provides [HIDDEN] for those serializer options and a declared result type.

## Quality contract

Product V1. This is public CLI serialization and discovery behavior. Preserve the published outer envelope and prove the nested contract through the real serializer configuration.

## Decision closure

Accepted decisions:

- Retain `cli-json-v1` and serialize the whole `GraceReturnValue<T>` or `GraceError` at runtime.
- Make registry metadata declare the actual existing success result type; derive its JSON Schema with Grace's configured serializer options.
- Generate representative `--examples` values [HIDDEN] so examples have the same nested shape as the schema.
- Treat the current `refs` tuple as its real contract. Naming or otherwise changing that return value is out of scope.

Deferred or waived:

- Do not change command handlers, API/SDK DTOs, the runtime JSON renderer, or error serialization.
- The 11 commands that do not have a normal JSON success value and the nine source-only entries remain explicitly documented as unsupported or deferred where applicable.
- Stale-authority, persistence, authorization, retry, and materialization concerns are N/A: introspection is pure process-local metadata and must not execute a command.

## Contract propagation map

| Surface | Required disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Shared serializer options | Reuse unchanged `Constants.Shared.JsonSerializerOptions`; do not duplicate F# conversion policy. |
| CLI command-output registry | Declare or infer each eligible command's actual success type; derive schema and representative example. |
| CLI runtime `-o Json` | N/A; retain existing full-envelope behavior and `cli-json-v1`. |
| Server routes, SDK, persisted shapes, generated clients | N/A; no runtime command or transport shape changes. |
| Machine-readable CLI documentation | Update the discovery contract and examples to explain the accurately shaped nested `ReturnValue`. |
| Tests | Add registry-wide coverage plus focused representative types and command-level introspection proof. |

## Owned paths

- `src/Grace.CLI/CommandOutputContract.CLI.fs`
- `src/Grace.CLI.Tests/CommandOutputContract.CLI.Tests.fs`
- `src/Grace.CLI.Tests/Program.CLI.Tests.fs` when command-level proof needs it
- `docs/Machine-readable CLI output.md`

## Forbidden or sensitive paths

- `src/Grace.CLI/Command/Common.CLI.fs`: do not alter the JSON envelope renderer.
- `src/Grace.CLI/Program.CLI.fs`: do not alter introspection dispatch unless a minimal correctness necessity is demonstrated.
- `src/Grace.Shared/Constants.Shared.fs`: reuse, rather than modify, shared serializer policy.
- Command handlers, shared DTOs, server, SDK, persistence, and generated artifacts are out of scope.
- Project files and package dependencies are out of scope; the platform schema exporter is already available.

## Invariant tuple and detail gate

For every routed command with an `ExistingGraceResultEnvelope` success path, and for the conditional success path of `watch --check`:

- `--schema` publishes a non-placeholder schema under the success envelope's `ReturnValue` property that matches the type the command currently returns under Grace's JSON options.
- `--examples` publishes a successful outer `GraceReturnValue` example with a representative `ReturnValue` that conforms to that derived schema.
- `--schema` and `--examples` stay inert: no command handler, configuration read, ID generation, network request, or mutation occurs.
- The outer `GraceReturnValue`/`GraceError` contracts, `cli-json-v1` identifier, and runtime `-o Json` behavior remain unchanged.

Forbidden implementation shapes:

- Do not hand-author field-by-field schemas or examples per command when the existing type and serializer can supply them.
- Do not execute commands or construct live configuration to discover schema or examples.
- Do not unwrap the envelope or relabel a tuple as a DTO merely to improve presentation.
- Do not convert an eligible JSON-success command to `metadata-incomplete` because it lacks bespoke metadata.

Required proof:

- Positive: `refs --schema` exposes the tuple's branch and reference-array shape, and `refs --examples` has a matching nested tuple-like JSON value.
- Positive: records, collections, scalar output, unions, optional or nullable fields, and a conditional `watch --check` result retain correct JSON shape under the configured F# converter.
- Negative: deferred and source-only entries do not falsely claim a JSON-success value.
- Regression: all registry entries remain discoverable and serializable; normal runtime JSON output remains the full outer envelope.
- Boundary: representative-example generation handles schemas with definitions, arrays, unions, and recursive or unsupported branches safely and deterministically without side effects.

## Validation

- Format each touched F# source file.
- Run the smallest focused `Grace.CLI.Tests` build and test command covering the output-contract registry and command-level introspection additions.
- Run MarkdownLint for the documentation update.
- Run `git diff --check` and a self-review against this issue before handoff.
- Do not run routine `validate.ps1 -Fast` or `-Full`; focused CLI proof is the local gate and GitHub `Validate` is the required broad current-head gate.

## Documentation impact

Update `docs/Machine-readable CLI output.md`. ADR 0004 already mandates the retained outer envelope and registry-derived DTO shape, so it needs no decision change unless implementation uncovers a contradiction.

## Definition of done

- Every eligible common-envelope entry and `watch --check` has a type-derived nested success schema and shape-compatible representative example.
- Existing wrapper/error behavior is unchanged.
- The focused proof, documentation lint, diff check, worker self-review, current-head GitHub `Validate`, and a fresh independent review are green.
- The implementation is committed, pushed, reviewed, merged, and cleaned up through the tracked workflow.

## Execution budget

Worker starts: 0 of 4 used before assignment. The first implementation worker is authorized as start 1 of 4; any later start must be recorded with its reason.

### Additional contract requirements

Observable contract requirements only:

- Every routed command whose envelope contract is a normal or conditional Grace result envelope publishes `schema-ready` inert introspection: its schema document exposes a non-placeholder success-envelope schema whose `ReturnValue` describes the command's declared success result type, and its examples document exposes a `success-envelope-shape` example and an `error-envelope-shape` example.
- `--schema` and `--examples` remain inert and require no configuration, handler execution, ID generation, or network access.
- Representative string example values only need to have the correct JSON type; no fixed literal string value is required. Representative GUID-shaped identifier values may be any valid UUID text.
- Representative schemas may use any equivalent standard JSON Schema encoding (inline `properties`, composition branches, local `$ref` indirection, or `type` expressed either as a single string or as a string array). A particular `anyOf` layout, a mandatory `prefixItems` rendering, or mandatory direct-inlined `properties` tables are not required.
- Every published representative example must conform to its published success-envelope schema.
- Deferred non-JSON-success paths and source-only paths remain explicitly marked as such and do not claim a JSON-success value.

+    /// Wraps JsonElement.TryGetProperty so inline boolean checks remain readable in fixed-shape schema assertions.
+    let private tryGetProperty (name: string) (element: JsonElement) : bool * JsonElement =
+        let mutable value = Unchecked.defaultof<JsonElement>
+        let found = element.TryGetProperty(name, &value)
+        found, value
+
+    /// Resolves local $ref indirections that nested schemas use across equivalent JSON Schema encodings.
+    let rec private dereferenceSchema (schemaRoot: JsonElement) (schema: JsonElement) : JsonElement =
+        if schema.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.True then
+            schema
+        else
+            let mutable referenceValue = Unchecked.defaultof<JsonElement>
+
+            if schema.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object
+               && schema.TryGetProperty("$ref", &referenceValue) then
+                let path = referenceValue.GetString()
+
+                if path = "#" then
+                    schemaRoot
+                elif path.StartsWith("#/", StringComparison.Ordinal) then
+                    let segments =
+                        path.Substring(2).Split('/')
+                        |> Array.map (fun segment ->
+                            segment
+                                .Replace("~1", "/")
+                                .Replace("~0", "~"))
+
+                    let target =
+                        segments
+                        |> Array.fold
+                            (fun (current: JsonElement) segment ->
+                                if current.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Array then
+                                    // JSON Pointer segments over arrays are zero-based indexes (e.g. refs into prefixItems).
+                                    match Int32.TryParse segment with
+                                    | true, index -> current.EnumerateArray() |> Seq.item index
+                                    | _ -> invalidOp $"JSON Pointer segment '{segment}' does not address an array index."
+                                else
+                                    current.GetProperty(segment))
+                            schemaRoot
+
+                    dereferenceSchema schemaRoot target
+                else
+                    invalidOp $"Only local $ref values are expected in published schemas, but found '{path}'."
+            else
+                schema
+
+    /// Returns the inline property table of a resolved object schema, when the encoding publishes one.
+    let private dereferencedProperties (schemaRoot: JsonElement) (schema: JsonElement) : JsonElement option =
+        let resolved = dereferenceSchema schemaRoot schema
+        let mutable properties = Unchecked.defaultof<JsonElement>
+
+        if resolved.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object
+           && resolved.TryGetProperty("properties", &properties)
+           && properties.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object then
+            Some properties
+        else
+            None
+
+    /// Finds a named property schema through local references and conjunctive composition encodings.
+    let rec private propertySchema (schemaRoot: JsonElement) (schema: JsonElement) (propertyName: string) (depth: int) : JsonElement option =
+        if depth > 64 then
+            None
+        else
+            let resolved = dereferenceSchema schemaRoot schema
+            let direct =
+                match dereferencedProperties schemaRoot resolved with
+                | Some properties ->
+                    let found, value = tryGetProperty propertyName properties
+                    if found then Some value else None
+                | None -> None
+
+            match direct with
+            | Some _ -> direct
+            | None when resolved.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object ->
+                let mutable branches = Unchecked.defaultof<JsonElement>
+                if resolved.TryGetProperty("allOf", &branches) && branches.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Array then
+                    branches.EnumerateArray()
+                    |> Seq.tryPick (fun branch -> propertySchema schemaRoot branch propertyName (depth + 1))
+                else None
+            | None -> None
+
+    /// Enumerates the composition branches (anyOf/oneOf/allOf/$ref-contained) of a schema with references resolved.
+    let private branchSubschemas (schemaRoot: JsonElement) (schema: JsonElement) : JsonElement list =
+        let resolved = dereferenceSchema schemaRoot schema
+
+        [
+            if resolved.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object then
+                for keyword in [ "anyOf"; "oneOf"; "allOf" ] do
+                    let mutable branchArray = Unchecked.defaultof<JsonElement>
+
+                    if resolved.TryGetProperty(keyword, &branchArray)
+                       && branchArray.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Array then
+                        for branch in branchArray.EnumerateArray() do
+                            yield branch
+        ]

+    /// Collects the JSON type names a schema declares, across a single "type" string, a "type" array, and reference indirection.
+    let rec private collectTypeNames (schemaRoot: JsonElement) (schema: JsonElement) (depth: int) : Set<string> =

+                if resolved.TryGetProperty("type", &typeElement) then

+                    | JsonValueKind.String -> Set.ofList [ typeElement.GetString() ]
+                    | JsonValueKind.Array ->

+                        |> Seq.choose (fun entry ->
+                            match entry.ValueKind with
+                            | JsonValueKind.String -> Some(entry.GetString())
+                            | _ -> None)

+                    | _ -> Set.empty
+                else

problem_statement:
Epic: Simplify single-process Grace Watch recovery
# Epic: Simplify single-process Grace Watch recovery

## Why this matters

In a one-user repository running against local emulators, `grace watch` currently reprocesses its own SQLite side
effects and receives its own saved References through SignalR. The result is resyncs with zero differences, blocked
catch-up retries, and repeated IPC writes. Grace Watch should remain safe for real multi-client repositories without
making the ordinary single-process path look or behave like a recovery incident.

## Quality contract

- Baseline: Product V1.
- Supported normal flow: one Watch process saves a user-file change on its current branch while the local server
  broadcasts the resulting current-branch Reference to that same process.
- User-visible outcome: routine Watch-owned local-state and self-reference echoes are silent and do not create pending
  work, resync, catch-up retries, or redundant IPC writes. Genuine external local-state changes and genuine
  different-root References remain safe and detectable.

## Accepted decisions

- Keep server-wide current-branch SignalR fan-out unchanged. The client makes the final materialization decision.
- Treat exact same-process Reference echoes as a process-local optimization, never as a persisted or machine-wide
  filter.
- Separate SQLite local-state coordination from filesystem observation candidates.
- Use one durable, transactional local-status revision in existing local state only for cross-process coordination.
- Serialize the leaves because both modify Watch runtime state and focused Watch tests.

## Explicit non-goals

- No public CLI, SDK, HTTP, SignalR payload, or server broadcast contract changes.
- No same-machine suppression, process identity registry, or persisted self-echo ledger.
- No logging redesign beyond removing the diagnosed routine noise.
- No parallel branches for these leaves.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Local-state revision coordination"] --> B["Exact self-reference echo suppression"]
```

The first leaf is the tracer slice. It must prove that Watch-owned SQLite writes cannot manufacture pending work while
an external local-state mutation remains visible. Its evidence establishes the clean local baseline that the second
leaf needs.

## Checklist

- [x] #795 Local-state revision coordination (merged via #797).
- [x] #796 Exact self-reference echo suppression (merged via #798).
- [x] Final epic acceptance run confirms the one-process local-emulator flow has no false resync, blocked catch-up,
      redundant IPC publication, or self-reference skip noise (exact head `36153653589e783801e0235b121ff4cc59f5c9c6`).

## Contract propagation map

| Surface | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Local SQLite schema and migration | Child 1 owns. |
| Watch callback, timer, pending-state, and IPC behavior | Child 1 owns. |
| Current-branch coordinator and lifecycle catch-up | Child 2 owns. |
| SignalR payload and server group broadcast | N/A; retain current contract. |
| CLI options, SDK, HTTP, OpenAPI, generated artifacts | N/A; no public contract change. |
| Documentation | N/A unless a worker finds existing Watch documentation that promises the removed noisy behavior. |

## Integration and completion

Use `epic/<parent-issue>-single-process-watch-recovery` from `origin/main`. Each leaf PR targets that integration
branch. The final epic PR targets `main` after both leaf PRs merge and the end-to-end acceptance proof is recorded.

No implementation starts until each child is independently claimed, assigned, and has a clean issue-owned worktree.

+    /// Identifies one process-local save attempt without exposing its mutable ledger entry.

+    /// Carries the exact locally emitted root identity that a returned Reference may later complete.
+    type private LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoIntentIdentity =

+            RepositoryId: RepositoryId
+            BranchId: BranchId
+            DirectoryId: DirectoryVersionId
+            Sha256Hash: Sha256Hash
+            Blake3Hash: Blake3Hash
+            CorrelationId: CorrelationId
+        }

+    /// Holds one bounded local intent while notification-before-response ordering settles.
+    type private LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoEntry =
+        {
+            Token: Guid
+            Identity: LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoIntentIdentity
+            ExpiresAtUtc: DateTime
+            Completion: TaskCompletionSource<ReferenceId option>
+            mutable ReferenceId: ReferenceId option
+        }

+    /// Tracks exact current-process save References long enough to silence every matching SignalR or lifecycle delivery.
+    type internal LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoLedger(capacity: int, lifetime: TimeSpan, utcNow: unit -> DateTime) =
+        let ledgerLock = obj ()
+        let entries = Dictionary<Guid, LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoEntry>()
+        let insertionOrder = LinkedList<Guid>()

+        let removeEntry token =
+            match entries.TryGetValue(token) with
+            | true, entry ->
+                entries.Remove(token) |> ignore
+                insertionOrder.Remove(token) |> ignore
+
+                entry.Completion.TrySetResult(None) |> ignore
+            | _ -> ()
+
+        /// Removes expired intents in insertion order before any admission decision uses them.
+        let pruneExpired nowUtc =
+            let mutable pruning = true
+
+            while pruning && not (isNull insertionOrder.First) do
+                let token = insertionOrder.First.Value

+                match entries.TryGetValue(token) with
+                | true, entry when entry.ExpiresAtUtc <= nowUtc -> removeEntry token

+        /// Reports whether a notification exactly matches the save identity known before the server assigns its response.

+            && identity.DirectoryId = payload.DirectoryId
+            && identity.Sha256Hash = payload.Sha256Hash
+            && identity.Blake3Hash = payload.Blake3Hash

+            && entry.Identity.RepositoryId = payload.RepositoryId
+            && entry.Identity.BranchId = payload.BranchId
+            && entry.Identity.DirectoryId = payload.DirectoryId
+            && entry.Identity.Sha256Hash = payload.Sha256Hash
+            && entry.Identity.Blake3Hash = payload.Blake3Hash

+                pruneExpired (utcNow ())

+                while entries.Count >= capacity
+                      && not (isNull insertionOrder.First) do
+                    removeEntry insertionOrder.First.Value

+                let token = Guid.NewGuid()
+
+                let entry =

+                        Identity =

+                                BranchId = branchId
+                                DirectoryId = directoryId
+                                Sha256Hash = sha256Hash
+                                Blake3Hash = blake3Hash
+                                CorrelationId = correlationId
+                            }
+                        ExpiresAtUtc = (utcNow ()).Add(lifetime)
+                        Completion = TaskCompletionSource<ReferenceId option>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously)
+                        ReferenceId = None
+                    }

+                entries.Add(token, entry)
+                insertionOrder.AddLast(token) |> ignore
+                LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoIntentHandle token)
+
+        /// Promotes a local intent only after the save response and local status application both succeed.
+        member _.Complete(LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoIntentHandle token, referenceId) =
+            lock ledgerLock (fun () ->
+                pruneExpired (utcNow ())
+
+                match entries.TryGetValue(token) with
+                | true, entry when referenceId <> ReferenceId.Empty ->

+        /// Removes a failed or uncertain save intent so its later notification follows ordinary coordinator behavior.
+        member _.Fail(LocalCurrentBranchReferenceEchoIntentHandle token) = lock ledgerLock (fun () -> removeEntry token)

+                                pruneExpired (utcNow ())

+                                | Some referenceId, (true, entry) when
+                                    referenceId = payload.ReferenceId
+                                    && completedReferenceMatchesPayload entry payload

+                                | _ -> false)
+            }

+-- | The protocol fixtures exist in two surface-syntax variants, because
+-- the exact surface syntax used to specify the optional layer 4 protocol
+-- of a port is left to the implementation: a positional second argument
+-- (@port 3833 "UDP"@) or a named property (@port 3833 protocol="UDP"@).
+-- An implementation only has to accept one of them, so each variant is
+-- tried in turn and only the first variant that decodes is asserted on;
+-- a variant that does not decode is skipped rather than failed on. The
+-- test fails only when neither variant decodes, or when the decoded
+-- model does not contain the declared service, its connection, and the
+-- declared port. The summary assertions are deliberately
+-- representation-agnostic: the concrete shape of a decoded port value
+-- changed when layer-4 protocols were introduced and the public
+-- contract leaves that shape to the implementation, so the parser test
+-- does not inspect the decoded port values themselves. What the
+-- declared protocol contributed to the decoded model is verified
+-- end-to-end by the Cilium rendering golden tests ("Service with a
+-- non-default port protocol" and "ToCIDRset with a non-default port
+-- protocol"), which render the protocol-aware port to a golden policy
+-- and thereby reject a parser or renderer that ignores it.
+testPortDecoding :: TestEff ()
+testPortDecoding = do
+  let fixturePaths =
+        [ "test/fixtures/service-definition-protocol.kdl"
+        , "test/fixtures/service-definition-protocol-property.kdl"
+        ]
+  declarations <-
+    assertJust
+      ( "None of the port protocol fixture variants could be decoded: "
+          <> show fixturePaths
+          <> ". The parser must accept a `port` node whose optional layer 4 protocol is specified, either as a positional second argument or as a named property."
+      )
+      =<< selectFirstDecodable decodeServiceDocument fixturePaths
+  service <-
+    assertJust "Expected the media-proxy service declaration" $
+      List.find (\Service {serviceName = n} -> display n == "media-proxy") [s | ServiceDeclaration s <- declarations]
+  assertEqual
+    "Expected media-proxy to declare its main-app connection with the declared port"
+    ( ServiceSummary
+        { summaryName = "media-proxy"
+        , summaryInfo = ServiceInfo {serviceFqdn = Nothing, serviceContext = Just (ServiceContext {contextName = "k8s"})}
+        , summaryConnections =
+            [ ConnectionSummary
+                { summaryConnectionWith = "main-app"
+                , summaryConnectionType = HTTPS
+                , summaryPortCount = 1
+                }
+            ]
+        , summaryCidrSetCount = 0
+        }
+    )
+    (summariseService service)
+
+-- | Ports declared without a protocol must keep decoding (backwards
+-- compatibility): the pre-existing fixture declares the connections of
+-- @media-proxy@ without any layer 4 protocol, so their decode summaries
+-- must still contain the declared connections and the declared ports,
+-- whatever default (implicit or explicit) the implementation assigns to
+-- the protocol of such a port. What the default protocol contributes to
+-- the rendered policy is verified end-to-end by the pre-existing Cilium
+-- rendering golden tests ("Services" and "ToCIDRset", whose expected
+-- policies keep their hard-coded TCP protocols).
+testPortProtocolDefault :: TestEff ()
+testPortProtocolDefault = do
+  fileContent <- decodeUtf8 <$> FileSystem.readFile "test/fixtures/multiple-service-definitions.kdl"
+  declarations <- assertRight "KDL file could not be parsed" $ KDL.decodeWith decodeServiceDocument fileContent
+  result <- assertJust "Expected a media-proxy service" $ List.find (\Service {serviceName = n} -> display n == "media-proxy") [s | ServiceDeclaration s <- declarations]
+  assertEqual
+    "Expected the protocol-free connections of media-proxy to keep decoding with their declared ports"
+    [ ConnectionSummary {summaryConnectionWith = "opensearch", summaryConnectionType = HTTPS, summaryPortCount = 0}
+    , ConnectionSummary {summaryConnectionWith = "otel-tracing", summaryConnectionType = HTTPS, summaryPortCount = 2}
+    ]
+    (summaryConnections (summariseService result))
+
+-- | Decodes the fixtures with the given document decoder and returns the
+-- declarations of the first fixture that decodes successfully, or
+-- 'Nothing' when no fixture decodes.
+selectFirstDecodable :: KDL.DocumentDecoder a -> [FilePath] -> TestEff (Maybe a)
+selectFirstDecodable decoder =
+  foldr tryFixture (pure Nothing)
+  where
+    tryFixture fixturePath fallback = do
+      fileContent <- decodeUtf8 <$> FileSystem.readFile fixturePath
+      tryVariants (protocolTextVariants fileContent) fallback
+
+    tryVariants [] fallback = fallback
+    tryVariants (fileContent : remaining) fallback =
+      case KDL.decodeWith decoder fileContent of
+        Right declarations -> pure (Just declarations)
+        Left _err -> tryVariants remaining fallback
+
+protocolTextVariants :: Text -> [Text]
+protocolTextVariants source =
+  [ source
+  , Text.replace "\"UDP\"" "\"udp\"" source
+  ]

+-- Extract the port/protocol mappings from the generated block-style Cilium
+-- YAML without constraining indentation, quoting of numeric values, or unrelated
+-- policy fields. A protocol is associated with the immediately preceding port
+-- mapping, so broadcasting one protocol across multiple ports is observable.
+selectPortProtocols :: [Text] -> Text -> [(Text, Text)]
+selectPortProtocols wanted rendered =
+  filter (\(port, _) -> port `elem` wanted) (Maybe.mapMaybe parsePair adjacentLines)
+  where
+    renderedLines = map Text.strip (Text.lines rendered)
+    adjacentLines = zip renderedLines (drop 1 renderedLines)
+
+    parsePair (portLine, protocolLine) = do
+      port <- fieldValue "port:" (dropListMarker portLine)
+      protocol <- fieldValue "protocol:" protocolLine
+      pure (port, protocol)
+
+    dropListMarker line = Maybe.fromMaybe line (Text.stripPrefix "- " line)
+
+    fieldValue key line = do
+      value <- Text.stripPrefix key line
+      pure . Text.dropAround (== '"') $ Text.strip value
+

problem_statement:
Support GCS savepoint paths
## Summary
Support writing and reading migration savepoints from Google Cloud Storage bucket paths, for example `gs://my-bucket/scylla-migrator/savepoints`.

The migrator should use Spark/Hadoop filesystem configuration for GCS access, so credentials and connector setup stay in the Spark runtime configuration rather than the migrator YAML.

## Motivation
Operators running migrations in GCP may need durable savepoints stored in a GCS bucket rather than on the Spark driver local filesystem.

## Related
- Jira: https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/CUSTOMER-400
- Draft PR: https://github.com/scylladb/scylla-migrator/pull/375

+target. The structured form below resolves to
+``gs://my-bucket/scylla-migrator/savepoints``:
+
+.. code-block:: yaml
+
+  savepoints:
+    intervalSeconds: 300

+      prefix: scylla-migrator/savepoints

+When ``credentials.serviceAccountJsonKeyfile`` is provided, the migrator configures
+the Hadoop GCS connector to use ``SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEYFILE`` authentication. If
+the configuration file itself is loaded from GCS, Spark/Hadoop runtime configuration
+must still contain credentials that can read that file before the migrator can parse
+these settings.
+
+AWS S3 savepoint locations can be written either as an ``s3a://`` filesystem URI or
+as a structured S3 target. The structured form below resolves to
+``s3a://my-bucket/scylla-migrator/savepoints``:
+
+.. code-block:: yaml
+
+  savepoints:
+    intervalSeconds: 300
+    target:
+      type: s3
+      bucket: my-bucket
+      prefix: scylla-migrator/savepoints
+      region: us-east-1

+that can read that file before the migrator can parse these settings.

+When GCS authentication is not configured in the migrator YAML file, provide it through
+Spark/Hadoop runtime configuration so it is available to the Spark driver when the
+migrator writes savepoints and when it later loads a savepoint file to resume.
+For example, when using a service account JSON keyfile with the GCS connector:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+  spark-submit \
+    --conf spark.hadoop.fs.gs.impl=com.google.cloud.hadoop.fs.gcs.GoogleHadoopFileSystem \
+    --conf spark.hadoop.fs.gs.auth.type=SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEYFILE \
+    --conf spark.hadoop.fs.gs.auth.service.account.json.keyfile=/path/to/key.json \
+    ...

+credentials on Dataproc, should be configured the same way: as Spark/Hadoop runtime
+configuration, not as ``savepoints`` fields.

+final ``savepoint_*.yaml`` name. On local filesystems this rename is atomic when the
+filesystem supports atomic moves. On object stores such as GCS, the exact rename
+semantics are provided by the Hadoop connector, so the operation may be implemented as
+a copy/delete, but the migrator still avoids writing partial YAML directly to the final

+  def normalize(path: String): String

+  def listFileNames(path: String): Seq[String]

+private[migrator] object PathIO {

+      case Some("file") | None => LocalPathIO
+      case Some(_) =>

+          path,
+          hadoopConfiguration.map(new Configuration(_)).getOrElse(new Configuration())

+    }

+
+  private object LocalPathIO extends PathIO {
+    private def toPath(path: String): NioPath =

+        case Some("file") => Paths.get(new HadoopPath(path).toUri).normalize()

+      }

+        case cleanupErr: Throwable =>

+      fs.listStatus(toPath(path)).iterator.map(_.getPath.getName).toSeq

+    override def readUtf8(path: String): String =

+        val out = new ByteArrayOutputStream()

+              s"is configured. ${connectorGuidance(pathScheme)}",

+          )
+      }
+
+    private def connectorGuidance(pathScheme: String): String =
+      pathScheme.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) match {
+        case "gs" =>
+          "For gs:// paths, include the Hadoop GCS connector in the Spark runtime and configure " +
+            "its credentials via Spark/Hadoop configuration."
+        case "s3" | "s3a" | "s3n" =>
+          "For s3a:// paths, include the Hadoop AWS/S3A connector in the Spark runtime and " +
+            "configure its credentials via Spark/Hadoop configuration."
+        case other =>
+          s"Include a Hadoop filesystem connector for '${other}' paths in the Spark runtime and " +
+            "configure it via Spark/Hadoop configuration."
+      }
+
+    private def deleteTemp(tempPath: HadoopPath): Unit =
+      try fs.delete(tempPath, false)
+      catch {
+        case cleanupErr: Throwable =>
+          log.warn(s"Failed to clean up temp savepoint ${tempPath}: ${cleanupErr.getMessage}")
+      }
+  }
+}

+package com.scylladb.migrator
+
+import com.scylladb.migrator.config.{ MigratorConfig, Savepoints, SourceSettings, TargetSettings }
+import com.scylladb.migrator.readers.ParquetSavepointsManager

+/** Exercises GCS savepoints through the Hadoop configuration assembled by Spark. The local
+  * filesystem stand-in below is intentionally registered only in that runtime configuration, so
+  * no cloud service or ambient Hadoop configuration is involved.
+  */
+class GcsSavepointsTest extends munit.FunSuite {
+
+  override def munitTimeout: scala.concurrent.duration.FiniteDuration =
+    scala.concurrent.duration.DurationInt(120).seconds
+
+  // A dedicated Spark session per test case: the gs filesystem implementation is only visible to
+  // the code under test via Spark's runtime Hadoop configuration, and each test stops its session
+  // afterwards so no gs filesystem state leaks between cases.
+  private val sparkSession = FunFixture[SparkSession](
+    setup = { _ =>
+      SparkSession
+        .builder()
+        .master("local[1]")
+        .appName("gcs-savepoints-test")
+        .config("spark.ui.enabled", "false")
+        .config("spark.hadoop.fs.gs.impl", classOf[LocalGsTestFileSystem].getName)
+        .config("spark.hadoop.fs.gs.impl.disable.cache", "true")
+        .getOrCreate()
+    },
+    teardown = { spark =>
+      try spark.stop()
+      finally LocalGsTestFileSystem.reset()
+    }
+  )
+
+  private def config(savepointsPath: String): MigratorConfig =
+    MigratorConfig(
+      source = SourceSettings.Parquet("unused-input", None, None, None),
+      // This deliberately unsupported source/target pair makes Migrator.main stop immediately
+      // after it has loaded the saved configuration, without contacting an external service.
+      target = TargetSettings.Parquet("unused-output", "snappy"),
+      renames = None,
+      savepoints = Savepoints(intervalSeconds = 3600, path = savepointsPath),
+      skipTokenRanges = None,
+      skipSegments = None,
+      skipParquetFiles = None,
+      validation = None
+    )
+
+  sparkSession.test(
+    "Spark runtime Hadoop configuration is used for gs:// savepoint write and resume"
+  ) { spark =>
+    val savepointsPath = "gs://bucket-a/migrator/savepoints"
+    val runtimeConf = spark.sparkContext.hadoopConfiguration
+    assertEquals(runtimeConf.get("fs.gs.impl"), classOf[LocalGsTestFileSystem].getName)
+    assertEquals(new Configuration().get("fs.gs.impl"), null)
+
+    // Use the public Parquet migration savepoint factory, which receives SparkContext just as
+    // the real migration entrypoint does. This avoids depending on SavepointsManager's internal
+    // constructor representation.
+    val manager = ParquetSavepointsManager(config(savepointsPath), spark.sparkContext)
+    try {
+      manager.markFileAsProcessed("file-a.parquet")
+      manager.dumpMigrationState("test")
+    } finally manager.close()
+
+    val fs = new HadoopPath(savepointsPath).getFileSystem(runtimeConf)
+    val saved =
+      fs.listStatus(new HadoopPath(savepointsPath)).filter(_.getPath.getName.endsWith(".yaml"))
+    assertEquals(saved.length, 1, "the savepoint must be written through the gs:// filesystem")
+    val remoteSavepoint = s"$savepointsPath/${saved.head.getPath.getName}"
+
+    // main is the configuration-loading entrypoint. It must use SparkContext.hadoopConfiguration
+    // to read the remote savepoint. Reaching this known unsupported pairing proves the remote
+    // YAML was loaded; the saved state is also checked before invoking the entrypoint.
+    val savedYaml = new String(
+      Files.readAllBytes(java.nio.file.Paths.get(saved.head.getPath.toUri)),
+      java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8
+    )
+    assert(savedYaml.contains("file-a.parquet"), "the saved migration state must be present")
+    spark.conf.set("spark.scylla.config", remoteSavepoint)
+    val error = intercept[RuntimeException](Migrator.main(Array.empty))
+    assert(error.getMessage.contains("Unsupported combination"))
+  }
+
+  sparkSession.test(
+    "DynamoDB migration savepoint factories use the Spark Hadoop configuration for gs:// savepoints"
+  ) { spark =>
+    // A behaviour-level probe for the DynamoDB-family migration path: the entrypoints hand the
+    // savepoint manager a SparkContext, and the manager must write through the filesystem that
+    // exists only in Spark's runtime Hadoop configuration. With a plain Hadoop configuration the
+    // gs scheme is unavailable, so this can only pass if the runtime configuration is used.
+    val rdd: RDD[(Text, DynamoDBItemWritable)] =
+      spark.sparkContext.emptyRDD[(Text, DynamoDBItemWritable)]
+
+    val savepointsPath = "gs://bucket-b/migrator/savepoints"
+    val manager = com.scylladb.migrator.alternator.DynamoDbSavepointsManager(
+      // The target is irrelevant to savepoint bookkeeping; DynamoDBS3Export simply avoids any
+      // ResumableTargetSettings redirect logic in implementations that run one.
+      config(savepointsPath).copy(
+        target = TargetSettings.DynamoDBS3Export("unused-export")
+      ),
+      rdd,
+      spark.sparkContext
+    )
+    try manager.dumpMigrationState("test")
+    finally manager.close()
+
+    val fs =
+      new HadoopPath(savepointsPath).getFileSystem(spark.sparkContext.hadoopConfiguration)
+    val saved =
+      fs.listStatus(new HadoopPath(savepointsPath)).filter(_.getPath.getName.endsWith(".yaml"))
+    assertEquals(
+      saved.length,
+      1,
+      "the DynamoDB savepoint manager must write through the Spark-configured gs:// filesystem"
+    )
+    val savedYaml = new String(
+      Files.readAllBytes(java.nio.file.Paths.get(saved.head.getPath.toUri)),
+      java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8
+    )
+    assert(
+      savedYaml.contains(savepointsPath),
+      "the savepoint must record the gs:// savepoint location"
+    )
+    // The gs filesystem implementation exists only in Spark's runtime Hadoop configuration, so
+    // an ambient Hadoop classpath cannot read or write these objects.
+    assertEquals(new Configuration().get("fs.gs.impl"), null)
+  }
+
+  private def writtenGsSavepointYamls(
+    spark: SparkSession,
+    savepointsPath: String
+  ): Seq[String] = {
+    val fs = new HadoopPath(savepointsPath).getFileSystem(spark.sparkContext.hadoopConfiguration)
+    val saved =
+      fs.listStatus(new HadoopPath(savepointsPath)).filter(_.getPath.getName.endsWith(".yaml"))
+    saved.map { status =>
+      new String(
+        Files.readAllBytes(java.nio.file.Paths.get(status.getPath.toUri)),
+        java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8
+      )
+    }.toSeq
+  }
+
+  sparkSession.test(
+    "CQL migration savepoint manager uses the Spark Hadoop configuration for gs:// savepoints"
+  ) { spark =>
+    val savepointsPath = "gs://bucket-cql/migrator/savepoints"
+    // The gs filesystem implementation is registered only in Spark's runtime Hadoop
+    // configuration, so an ambient Hadoop classpath cannot resolve gs:// locations.
+    assertEquals(new Configuration().get("fs.gs.impl"), null)
+
+    // Exercise the CQL migration path through its savepoint-manager wiring, which receives the
+    // migration configuration, the source DataFrame and the Spark session just as the real
+    // CQL migration entrypoint provides them.
+    val sourceDF = scylla.SourceDataFrame(
+      dataFrame           = spark.emptyDataFrame,
+      timestampColumns    = None,
+      savepointsSupported = true
+    )
+    val manager = scylla.ScyllaMigrator
+      .savepointsManagerForSource(config(savepointsPath), sourceDF)(spark)
+      .getOrElse(fail("CQL migrations must support savepoints"))
+    try manager.dumpMigrationState("test")
+    finally manager.close()
+
+    val savepointYamls = writtenGsSavepointYamls(spark, savepointsPath)
+    assertEquals(
+      savepointYamls.length,
+      1,
+      "the CQL savepoint manager must write through the Spark-configured gs:// filesystem"
+    )
+    assert(
+      savepointYamls.head.contains(savepointsPath),
+      "the savepoint must record the gs:// savepoint location"
+    )
+  }
+
+  sparkSession.test(
+    "CQL-to-Parquet migration savepoint manager uses the Spark Hadoop configuration for gs:// savepoints"
+  ) { spark =>
+    val savepointsPath = "gs://bucket-cql-parquet/migrator/savepoints"
+    // The gs filesystem implementation is registered only in Spark's runtime Hadoop
+    // configuration, so an ambient Hadoop classpath cannot resolve gs:// locations.
+    assertEquals(new Configuration().get("fs.gs.impl"), null)
+
+    // The public factory consumes the source DataFrame and the SparkContext, exactly as the real
+    // CQL-to-Parquet migration entrypoint provides them; an empty source DataFrame still
+    // exercises the savepoint write path.
+    val sourceDF = scylla.SourceDataFrame(
+      dataFrame           = spark.emptyDataFrame,
+      timestampColumns    = None,
+      savepointsSupported = true
+    )
+    val manager = scylla
+      .CqlParquetSavepointsManager(config(savepointsPath), sourceDF, spark.sparkContext)
+    try manager.dumpMigrationState("test")
+    finally manager.close()
+
+    val savepointYamls = writtenGsSavepointYamls(spark, savepointsPath)
+    assertEquals(
+      savepointYamls.length,
+      1,
+      "the CQL-to-Parquet savepoint manager must write through the Spark-configured gs:// filesystem"
+    )
+    assert(
+      savepointYamls.head.contains(savepointsPath),
+      "the savepoint must record the gs:// savepoint location"
+    )
+  }
+}
+
+/** Minimal local implementation of the gs Hadoop filesystem used only by this test. */
+class LocalGsTestFileSystem extends FileSystem {
+  private var fsUri: URI = _
+  private var wd: HadoopPath = _
+
+  override def initialize(name: URI, conf: Configuration): Unit = {
+    super.initialize(name, conf)
+    fsUri = new URI(name.getScheme, name.getAuthority, null, null, null)
+    wd = new HadoopPath(fsUri.toString + "/")
+  }
+  override def getUri: URI = fsUri
+
+  private def nio(path: HadoopPath): Path = {
+    val uri = path.toUri
+    val bucket = Option(uri.getAuthority).getOrElse("bucket")
+    val objectName = Option(uri.getPath).getOrElse("").stripPrefix("/")
+    LocalGsTestFileSystem.rootDir.resolve(bucket).resolve(objectName)
+  }
+
+  override def open(path: HadoopPath, bufferSize: Int): org.apache.hadoop.fs.FSDataInputStream = {
+    // Pragmatic stand-in behavior: a gs path containing a gs URI string would not round-trip
+    // through a plain local filesystem, so absolute local paths are treated as already-resolved
+    // local paths and everything else goes through the gs object store mapping.
+    val uri = path.toUri
+    val target =
+      if (uri.getScheme == null && uri.getPath.startsWith("/")) java.nio.file.Paths.get(uri.getPath)
+      else nio(path)
+    FileSystem.getLocal(getConf).getRawFileSystem.open(new HadoopPath(target.toUri), bufferSize)
+  }
+
+  override def create(
+    path: HadoopPath,
+    permission: FsPermission,
+    overwrite: Boolean,
+    bufferSize: Int,
+    replication: Short,
+    blockSize: Long,
+    progress: Progressable
+  ): org.apache.hadoop.fs.FSDataOutputStream = {
+    val target = nio(path)
+    if (target.getParent != null) Files.createDirectories(target.getParent)
+    if (!overwrite && Files.exists(target)) throw new java.io.IOException(s"File exists: $target")
+    new org.apache.hadoop.fs.FSDataOutputStream(Files.newOutputStream(target), null)
+  }
+
+  override def append(path: HadoopPath, bufferSize: Int, progress: Progressable) =
+    throw new UnsupportedOperationException("append")
+
+  override def rename(source: HadoopPath, destination: HadoopPath): Boolean =
+    try {
+      val target = nio(destination)
+      if (target.getParent != null) Files.createDirectories(target.getParent)
+      Files.move(nio(source), target, java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING)
+      true
+    } catch { case _: java.io.IOException => false }
+
+  override def delete(path: HadoopPath, recursive: Boolean): Boolean = {
+    val target = nio(path)
+    if (!Files.exists(target)) false
+    else {
+      if (recursive) Files.walk(target).iterator().asScala.toSeq.reverse.foreach(Files.deleteIfExists)
+      else Files.delete(target)
+      true
+    }
+  }
+
+  override def listStatus(path: HadoopPath): Array[org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileStatus] = {
+    val directory = nio(path)
+    if (!Files.isDirectory(directory)) Array.empty
+    else Files.list(directory).iterator().asScala.map { child =>
+      new org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileStatus(
+        Files.size(child), Files.isDirectory(child), 1, 4096, 0, new HadoopPath(child.toUri)
+      )
+    }.toArray
+  }
+
+  override def setWorkingDirectory(path: HadoopPath): Unit = wd = path
+  override def getWorkingDirectory: HadoopPath = wd
+  override def mkdirs(path: HadoopPath, permission: FsPermission): Boolean = {
+    Files.createDirectories(nio(path)); true
+  }
+  override def getFileStatus(path: HadoopPath): org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileStatus = {
+    val target = nio(path)
+    if (!Files.exists(target)) throw new java.io.FileNotFoundException(s"File $path does not exist")
+    new org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileStatus(
+      Files.size(target), Files.isDirectory(target), 1, 4096, 0, new HadoopPath(target.toUri)
+    )
+  }
+}
+
+private object LocalGsTestFileSystem {
+  private val root = new AtomicReference[Path](freshRoot())
+  private def freshRoot(): Path = Files.createTempDirectory("gcs-savepoints-test")
+  def rootDir: Path = root.get()
+  def reset(): Unit = {
+    val old = root.getAndSet(freshRoot())
+    if (Files.exists(old)) Files.walk(old).iterator().asScala.toSeq.reverse.foreach(Files.deleteIfExists)
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
Improve update flow for skills to prompt before bashing over manual edits to skills
## Part 1

One nice part about skills is you have the ability to edit them yourself, but currently `skills get` would bash over those changes. [HIDDEN]

Or we may want to add this data into each skills directory instead as they are copied over, this way we won't lose the information if somebody runs a `flutter clean` which will delete the manifest.

## Part 2

When updating today (via `skills get`) it will always prompt for the skills to install, even if they were already installed, and it doesn't even pre-select the already installed skills.

I think we should show this dialog but pre-select the already installed skills and surface any new skills in the top of the list with a (new) qualifier.

We also may want to provide a separate dialog with the lists of skills to be deleted, and give an opportunity to keep those if desired.

### Additional contract requirements

These requirements apply to `skills get` in both fresh-installation and
update scenarios.

## Skill-selection dialogs

- When `skills get` discovers skills that are not yet installed (including
  on a first installation), it must offer them in a per-package skill
  selection dialog.
- Each skill offered in the dialog must be annotated with its current
  state:
  - New skills must be annotated with a qualifier containing "new" (any
    capitalization, e.g. `(new)` or `(New)`), and must not be pre-selected.
  - Skills with a newer published version must be annotated as having an
    update available and must be pre-selected.
  - Skills that were modified locally must be annotated as having local
    edits and must not be pre-selected.
  - Skills whose source skill has been deleted must be annotated as
    removed in the per-package selection dialog and must be pre-selected.
    Accepting the removal deletes the installed copy and removes the skill
    from the manifest; declining the removal leaves the installed copy
    untouched, retains the skill in the manifest, and offers the removal
    again on subsequent runs until it is accepted.
  - When a skill's source has changed and its installed copy also has
    local edits, the skill must be surfaced as having local edits (not as
    an update), and the same accept/decline behavior for locally modified
    skills applies.
  - Skills that were offered but not selected on an earlier run behave
    like new skills on the next run: they are offered again, not
    pre-selected, and may be annotated as new or as previously skipped.
- The per-package selection dialog title must indicate that skills are
  being both installed and updated for that package (e.g.
  `Select skills to install/update from package <name>:`).
- If a run of `skills get` has nothing to change (all skills are installed
  and up to date), it must not show any skill prompt.
  When a prompt is needed for other changes, already-installed skills that are up to date may be omitted; if they are included, they must be pre-selected.

## Local edits must never be overwritten without consent

- Before replacing an installed skill, `skills get` must detect whether
  the installed copy has been modified locally since it was installed
  (i.e. its current content no longer matches the content that was
  installed). Local edits may be in any file of the installed skill,
  including auxiliary files besides the skill definition file.
- A locally modified skill must be surfaced to the user (interactively) or
  applied according to the requested operation (non-interactively). If the
  user is asked whether to replace it and declines (for example by leaving
  it deselected or answering "no"), the modified files must be preserved
  unchanged in every IDE the project is configured for; if the user
  accepts the offered reinstall, the installed copy is replaced and the
  skill becomes up to date on subsequent runs.
- If a skill's source is deleted while its installed copy has local edits,
  declining the offered removal must preserve the locally modified files
  unchanged in any IDE the project is configured for.

## Non-interactive updates

- `skills get --all` must apply all available changes (install new skills,
  update changed skills, and remove skills whose source was deleted)
  without prompting, in a single non-interactive run.
- A non-interactive run (`--all`) applies the requested changes without
  prompting, including when the installed copy has local edits: pending
  source updates are applied even to locally modified copies, and pending
  removals (installed copy deleted and skill removed from the manifest)
  are carried out even when the installed copy has local edits.
