index 00000000..743a3bc1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/TestsLinux/MistralProviderPresenceTests.swift
@@ -0,0 +1,432 @@
+import CodexBarCore
+@testable import CodexBarCLI
+import Foundation
+#if canImport(FoundationNetworking)
+import FoundationNetworking
+#endif
+import Testing
+
+// Behavioral coverage for the observable Mistral usage-retrieval contract:
+// with the signed-in console session supplied through the documented manual
+// cookie input, retrieving Mistral usage issues an authenticated HTTPS
+// consumption request to a mistral.ai host at /api/billing/v2/usage for the
+// current UTC calendar month, and the observable result carries the monthly
+// amount and currency that the consumption response reported — including
+// the zero-amount case, which must also complete retrieval.
+//
+// The retrieval tests drive the retrieval through the provider registry
+// exactly as a user invokes it, supplying the signed-in console session
+// cookie header exactly as the public contract documents it for automated
+// use: pasted as a complete `Cookie` header value through the provider's
+// user-facing manual cookie configuration. The tests do not require any
+// environment variable, any additional settings input, or any presentation
+// design. When Foundation routes a request through the registered
+// URLProtocol handler, the request and response are observed deterministically.
+// A platform may instead use a custom session that bypasses the handler; those
+// tests do not require a particular transport choice. Each fixture provides a successful monthly
+// consumption response that reports its monthly amount, so the assertions
+// only require the observable retrieval result to contain the amount and
+// currency that the answered response reported, and to complete retrieval
+// for a reported zero amount.
+@Suite(.serialized)
+struct MistralProviderRetrievalTests {
+    private struct StubClaudeFetcher: ClaudeUsageFetching {
+        func loadLatestUsage(model _: String) async throws -> ClaudeUsageSnapshot {
+            throw ClaudeUsageError.parseFailed("unused test stub")
+        }
+
+        func debugRawProbe(model _: String) async -> String { "unused test stub" }
+        func detectVersion() -> String? { nil }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    func `mistral registry fetch requests the current monthly consumption endpoint`() async throws {
+        let provider = try #require(ProviderDescriptorRegistry.cliNameMap["mistral"])
+        #expect(provider.rawValue == "mistral")
+
+        let observation = MistralConsumptionObserver.install()
+        defer { observation.uninstall() }
+
+        let context = try Self.makeContext(for: provider)
+        let descriptor = ProviderDescriptorRegistry.descriptor(for: provider)
+        let beforeFetch = Date()
+        _ = await descriptor.fetchOutcome(context: context)
+        let afterFetch = Date()
+
+        // FoundationNetworking on some platforms does not route custom URLSession
+        // configurations through globally registered URLProtocol handlers. In
+        // that case the request is not observable here; do not treat a valid
+        // alternative transport as a failed provider implementation.
+        guard let request = observation.capturedRequest() else { return }
+        let url = try #require(request.url)
+        let components = try #require(URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false))
+        let query = Dictionary(
+            uniqueKeysWithValues: (components.queryItems ?? []).map { ($0.name, $0.value ?? "") })
+
+        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
+        calendar.timeZone = try #require(TimeZone(identifier: "UTC"))
+        let periods = Set([beforeFetch, afterFetch].map {
+            "\(calendar.component(.month, from: $0))/\(calendar.component(.year, from: $0))"
+        })
+        let observedPeriod = "\(query["month"] ?? "")/\(query["year"] ?? "")"
+
+        let host = try #require(url.host)
+        #expect(url.scheme == "https")
+        #expect(host == "mistral.ai" || host.hasSuffix(".mistral.ai"))
+        #expect(components.path == "/api/billing/v2/usage")
+        #expect(
+            periods.contains(observedPeriod),
+            "month and year must select the current UTC calendar month.")
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    func `mistral registry fetch is authenticated with the supplied console session cookie`() async throws {
+        let provider = try #require(ProviderDescriptorRegistry.cliNameMap["mistral"])
+
+        let observation = MistralConsumptionObserver.install(
+            fixedResponsePayload: MistralConsumptionObserver.zeroAmountConsumptionPayload)
+        defer { observation.uninstall() }
+
+        let context = try Self.makeContext(for: provider)
+        let descriptor = ProviderDescriptorRegistry.descriptor(for: provider)
+        _ = await descriptor.fetchOutcome(context: context)
+
+        guard let request = observation.capturedRequest() else { return }
+        let headers = Dictionary(
+            uniqueKeysWithValues: (request.allHTTPHeaderFields ?? [:]).map {
+                ($0.key.lowercased(), $0.value)
+            })
+        let cookie = try #require(
+            headers["cookie"],
+            """
+            The consumption request must carry the supplied signed-in session as an HTTP Cookie \
+            header; observed headers were: \(headers.keys.sorted().joined(separator: ", "))
+            """)
+        let cookieValues = Set(cookie.split(separator: ";").map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) })
+        #expect(cookieValues == Set(mistralConsoleSessionCookieHeader.split(separator: ";").map {
+            $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
+        }))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    func `mistral registry fetch yields the consumption amount answered by the endpoint`() async throws {
+        let provider = try #require(ProviderDescriptorRegistry.cliNameMap["mistral"])
+
+        let observation = MistralConsumptionObserver.install()
+        defer { observation.uninstall() }
+
+        let context = try Self.makeContext(for: provider)
+        let descriptor = ProviderDescriptorRegistry.descriptor(for: provider)
+        let outcome = await descriptor.fetchOutcome(context: context)
+        guard observation.capturedRequest() != nil else { return }
+
+        let result = try Self.requireSuccessfulResult(outcome)
+        let fields = Self.observableConsumptionFieldsText(of: result)
+        #expect(
+            fields.contains("7.5"),
+            """
+            The endpoint answered the current month with a reported monthly amount of 7.5 EUR, \
+            so the retrieved Mistral usage must expose that amount; observed fields were: \(fields)
+            """)
+        #expect(
+            fields.contains("EUR") || fields.contains("€"),
+            """
+            The endpoint answered with currency EUR, so the retrieved Mistral usage must expose \
+            that currency; observed fields were: \(fields)
+            """)
+        if let cost = result.usage.providerCost {
+            #expect(cost.used == 7.5)
+            #expect(cost.currencyCode == "EUR")
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    func `mistral registry fetch completes when the consumption response reports a zero amount`() async throws {
+        let provider = try #require(ProviderDescriptorRegistry.cliNameMap["mistral"])
+
+        let observation = MistralConsumptionObserver.install(
+            fixedResponsePayload: MistralConsumptionObserver.zeroAmountConsumptionPayload)
+        defer { observation.uninstall() }
+
+        let context = try Self.makeContext(for: provider)
+        let descriptor = ProviderDescriptorRegistry.descriptor(for: provider)
+        let outcome = await descriptor.fetchOutcome(context: context)
+
+        guard observation.capturedRequest() != nil else { return }
+
+        // The successful zero response must present zero, not merely avoid
+        // the amount used by the other response fixture.
+        let result = try Self.requireSuccessfulResult(outcome)
+        let fields = Self.observableConsumptionFieldsText(of: result)
+        if let cost = result.usage.providerCost {
+            #expect(cost.used == 0)
+            #expect(cost.currencyCode == "EUR")
+        } else {
+            let hasZeroAmount = fields.range(
+                of: #"(?<![0-9.])0(?:[.,]0+)?(?![0-9.])"#,
+                options: .regularExpression) != nil
+            #expect(hasZeroAmount, "The reported zero EUR monthly amount must be observable; fields: \(fields)")
+        }
+    }
+
+    private static func makeContext(for provider: UsageProvider) throws -> ProviderFetchContext {
+        // Build the fetch settings through the same generic, user-facing
+        // provider configuration consumed by the command-line session flow.
+        // This deliberately avoids depending on a provider-specific settings
+        // initializer or credential-storage type.
+        let config = CodexBarConfig(providers: [
+            ProviderConfig(
+                id: provider,
+                enabled: true,
+                source: .web,
+                cookieHeader: mistralConsoleSessionCookieHeader,
+                cookieSource: .manual),
+        ])
+        let configuredSession = try TokenAccountCLIContext(
+            selection: TokenAccountCLISelection(label: nil, index: nil, allAccounts: false),
+            config: config,
+            verbose: false)
+
+        return ProviderFetchContext(
+            runtime: .app,
+            sourceMode: .auto,
+            includeCredits: false,
+            webTimeout: 2,
+            webDebugDumpHTML: false,
+            verbose: false,
+            env: [:],
+            settings: configuredSession.settingsSnapshot(for: provider, account: nil),
+            fetcher: UsageFetcher(),
+            claudeFetcher: StubClaudeFetcher(),
+            browserDetection: BrowserDetection(cacheTTL: 0))
+    }
+
+    private static func requireSuccessfulResult(_ outcome: ProviderFetchOutcome) throws -> ProviderFetchResult {
+        switch outcome.result {
+        case let .success(result):
+            return result
+        case let .failure(error):
+            throw MistralRetrievalExpectation.failure(
+                "Retrieving Mistral usage with a supplied console sign-in must succeed, but the retrieval failed with: \(error)")
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Every user-facing string the retrieval result carries that could
+    /// convey the monthly consumption (limit amounts, cost figures, reset
+    /// descriptions, identity fields, source labels), joined for assertions
+    /// that stay neutral about which presentation field is used.
+    private static func observableConsumptionFieldsText(of result: ProviderFetchResult) -> String {
+        var fragments: [String] = [result.sourceLabel, result.strategyID, String(describing: result.strategyKind)]
+        let windows = [result.usage.primary, result.usage.secondary, result.usage.tertiary].compactMap(\.self)
+        for window in windows {
+            if let resetDescription = window.resetDescription {
+                fragments.append(resetDescription)
+            }
+            fragments.append(String(window.usedPercent))
+            if let remaining = window.nextRegenPercent {
+                fragments.append(String(remaining))
+            }
+        }
+        if let cost = result.usage.providerCost {
+            fragments.append(String(cost.used))
+            fragments.append(String(cost.limit))
+            fragments.append(cost.currencyCode)
+            if let period = cost.period { fragments.append(period) }
+        }
+        if let identity = result.usage.identity {
+            if let email = identity.accountEmail { fragments.append(email) }
+            if let organization = identity.accountOrganization { fragments.append(organization) }
+            if let loginMethod = identity.loginMethod { fragments.append(loginMethod) }
+        }
+        return fragments.joined(separator: " | ")
+    }
+}
+
+/// A signed-in-console-session cookie header value, spelled exactly as a
+/// user would paste it into the provider's manual cookie configuration.
+private let mistralConsoleSessionCookieHeader = "ory_session_test=sessiontoken; csrftoken=csrf"
+
+private enum MistralRetrievalExpectation: Error {
+    case failure(String)
+}
+
+/// Intercepts outgoing HTTP(S) requests through Foundation's URL loading
+/// system and answers them with a fixed Mistral AI Studio consumption
+/// response, so the tests are deterministic and offline.
+private final class MistralConsumptionObserver: URLProtocol {
+    struct Handle {
+        let uninstall: () -> Void
+        let capturedRequest: () -> URLRequest?
+    }
+
+    private static let lock = NSLock()
+    private nonisolated(unsafe) static var storedRequest: URLRequest?
+    private nonisolated(unsafe) static var storedResponsePayload: Data = MistralConsumptionObserver.sessionConsumptionPayload
+
+    static func install(fixedResponsePayload: Data = MistralConsumptionObserver.sessionConsumptionPayload) -> Handle {
+        Self.lock.withLock {
+            Self.storedRequest = nil
+            Self.storedResponsePayload = fixedResponsePayload
+        }
+        URLProtocol.registerClass(Self.self)
+
+        return Handle(
+            uninstall: {
+                URLProtocol.unregisterClass(Self.self)
+                Self.lock.withLock {
+                    Self.storedRequest = nil
+                    Self.storedResponsePayload = Self.sessionConsumptionPayload
+                }
+            },
+            capturedRequest: {
+                Self.lock.withLock { Self.storedRequest }
+            })
+    }
+
+    override class func canInit(with _: URLRequest) -> Bool { true }
+
+    override class func canonicalRequest(for request: URLRequest) -> URLRequest { request }
+
+    override func startLoading() {
+        Self.lock.withLock {
+            if Self.storedRequest == nil {
+                Self.storedRequest = self.request
+            }
+        }
+
+        if let url = self.request.url,
+           let response = HTTPURLResponse(
+               url: url,
+               statusCode: 200,
+               httpVersion: "HTTP/1.1",
+               headerFields: ["Content-Type": "application/json"])
+        {
+            self.client?.urlProtocol(self, didReceive: response, cacheStoragePolicy: .notAllowed)
+        }
+        let payload = Self.lock.withLock { Self.storedResponsePayload }
+        self.client?.urlProtocol(self, didLoad: payload)
+        self.client?.urlProtocolDidFinishLoading(self)
+    }
+
+    override func stopLoading() {}
+
+    /// A successful monthly consumption response for a month whose console
+    /// report amounts to 7.5 EUR. The response reports that monthly amount
+    /// directly: the top-level ``total``, ``total_usage``, ``amount``, and
+    /// ``cost`` fields each carry the month's amount (7.5) together with the
+    /// ``currency`` (EUR), while the per-metric token activity entries and
+    /// their service-unit ``prices`` are additional billing detail that is
+    /// consistent with the reported amount. The test asserts only the
+    /// observable reported amount and currency, not how the amount is read.
+    static let sessionConsumptionPayload = Data("""

problem_statement:
Refactor and finalize support for the NGSI-LD Query Language (4.9)
- Parsing of `q` queries is done via a regex, do a more bulletproof parsing based on the ABNF grammar defined in the specification (using antlr for instance)
- Add support for missing parts (`expandValues` and `jsonKeys`, seed target value, specific processing for `JsonProperty` and `LanguageProperty`,...)

### Additional contract requirements

## NGSI-LD Query Language contract

### Applicable entry points

A `q` filter is parsed and validated wherever the broker accepts an NGSI-LD
Query Language filter:

- entity GET queries (`GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities`);
- temporal entity GET queries (`GET /ngsi-ld/v1/temporal/entities`);
- the Query payload submitted to the entity-operations query endpoint
  (`POST /ngsi-ld/v1/entityOperations/query`);
- the `q` member of a subscription.

Entity-query construction represents a supplied filter as a parsed,
structured query rather than as an opaque string. A null filter means no
filter was supplied.

### Supported syntax and behavior

The filter language supports:

- comparisons with `==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `~=` and `!~=`;
- AND (`;`) and OR (`|`), with AND binding more tightly than OR, and
  parentheses to override precedence;
- a bare attribute path as an existence test, and `!` followed by an
  attribute path as a non-existence test;
- single values, inclusive `lower..upper` ranges, and comma-separated value
  lists;
- composed attribute paths and bracket suffixes, including language-qualified
  `LanguageProperty` terms such as `name[fr]`.

A language suffix selects the requested language entry of a language map for
comparison.

The observable effect of precedence and grouping matters, not the internal
shape of a parsed representation: `speed>100|temperature>32;foodName==dietary fibres`
must behave like `speed>100|(temperature>32;foodName==dietary fibres)`, and both
must behave differently from `(speed>100|temperature>32);foodName==dietary fibres`.
Conformant implementations may represent the parsed filter with any classes they
choose.

Malformed filters are rejected as BadRequestData rather than being treated as
opaque text. Malformed forms include blank filters, missing operands or
comparison values, unknown operators, unbalanced parentheses or brackets,
unterminated quoted values, and trailing logical operators. HTTP query entry
points report BadRequestData with status 400; an invalid filter in a Query
payload or in a subscription fails that payload's validation with
BadRequestData. A rejection caused by a malformed `q` occurs even when the
surrounding request is otherwise valid (including a valid entity selector in
a Query payload).

### `jsonKeys` and `expandValues`

`jsonKeys` names JsonProperty attributes for which a bracketed path in a
filter addresses keys inside the attribute's JSON content; the comparison
matches against the addressed JSON value.

`expandValues` names attributes whose compact comparison values are expanded
using the request's JSON-LD context before comparison; a compact value then
matches an entity value that equals its expanded form, while a non-listed raw
form of the value no longer matches.

For entity-query requests these options are comma-separated query parameters;
in a Query payload and in a subscription they are collections of attribute
names. The options are observed through request outcomes, not through stored
fields: entity queries (both GET requests and Query payloads) return exactly
the entities matched by the filter interpreted with these options, and the
options determine, together with the filter, whether a subscription matches a
candidate entity. The options are already bound to the entity query at
validation time, so validation accepts them. Temporal entity queries do not
apply these entity-query matching options.

### Compatibility of entity-query construction in tests

Existing test callers that build an entity query from a `q` string, a
pagination configuration, and a list of contexts through the documented
single expression remain supported by the test source tree.

index 0000000000..5a1d4d013a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/user/query_language.md
@@ -0,0 +1,179 @@
+# Query Language
+
+Stellio implements the NGSI-LD Query Language as defined in [ETSI GS CIM 009 Â§4.9](https://cim.etsi.org/NGSI-LD/official/clause-4.html#4.9).
+It is available through the `q` query parameter on:
+
+- `GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities`
+- `GET /ngsi-ld/v1/temporal/entities`
+- `POST /ngsi-ld/v1/entityOperations/query`
+- Subscription `q` field
+
+---
+
+## Operators
+
+| Operator | Meaning                           |
+|----------|-----------------------------------|
+| `;`      | AND â both sides must match       |
+| `\|`     | OR â at least one side must match |
+| `( )`    | Grouping                          |
+
+Operator precedence: `;` (AND) binds more tightly than `|` (OR). Use parentheses to override.
+
+```
+# temperature above 20 AND humidity below 80
+q=temperature>20;humidity<80
+
+# temperature outside 10â30 OR device is inactive
+q=temperature<10|temperature>30|(status=="inactive")
+```
+
+---
+
+## Existence checks
+
+```
+# entity has a temperature attribute
+q=temperature
+
+# entity does NOT have a temperature attribute
+q=!temperature
+```
+
+---
+
+## Comparison operators
+
+| Syntax           | Meaning                           |
+|------------------|-----------------------------------|
+| `attr==value`    | Equal                             |
+| `attr!=value`    | Not equal                         |
+| `attr>value`     | Greater than                      |
+| `attr>=value`    | Greater than or equal             |
+| `attr<value`     | Less than                         |
+| `attr<=value`    | Less than or equal                |
+| `attr~=pattern`  | Matches regular expression        |
+| `attr!~=pattern` | Does not match regular expression |
+
+---
+
+## Value types
+
+Values are typed automatically; quoting a value forces it to be treated as a string.
+
+| Type     | Example                 | Notes                                                                           |
+|----------|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| Number   | `42`, `3.14`, `-5`      | Integer or decimal                                                              |
+| Boolean  | `true`, `false`         | Unquoted only                                                                   |
+| String   | `"active"`, `"open"`    | Must be double-quoted                                                           |
+| DateTime | `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`  | ISO 8601 with timezone                                                          |
+| Date     | `2025-01-01`            | ISO 8601 date only                                                              |
+| Time     | `12:00:00Z`             | ISO 8601 time only                                                              |
+| URI      | `urn:ngsi-ld:Sensor:01` | Matched against Relationship objects, Property values, and VocabProperty values |
+
+```
+q=temperature==22.5
+q=status=="active"
+q=createdAt>2025-01-01T00:00:00Z
+q=managedBy=="urn:ngsi-ld:Beekeeper:01"
+```
+
+---
+
+## Range values
+
+A range matches values inclusively between a lower and upper bound, separated by `..`.
+NEQ (`!=`) matches values outside the range.
+
+```
+# temperature between 18 and 26
+q=temperature==18..26
+
+# humidity outside 30â70
+q=humidity!=30..70
+
+# entries from January 2025
+q=observedAt==2025-01-01T00:00:00Z..2025-01-31T23:59:59Z
+```
+
+---
+
+## List values
+
+A comma-separated list matches any of the listed values.
+NEQ (`!=`) requires the attribute to match none of them.
+
+```
+# status is either "active" or "standby"
+q=status=="active","standby"
+
+# device is neither sensor-01 nor sensor-02
+q=device!="urn:ngsi-ld:Sensor:01","urn:ngsi-ld:Sensor:02"
+```
+
+---
+
+## Composed attribute paths
+
+A dot-separated path traverses sub-attributes. Each segment is a compact term resolved against the request context.
+
+```
+# sub-attribute 'precision' of 'temperature' has a value above 30
+q=temperature.precision>90
+
+# sub-attribute 'unitCode' of 'temperature' equals "CEL"
+q=temperature.unitCode=="CEL"
+```
+
+---
+
+## Language tag filtering
+
+Append `[lang]` to a LanguageProperty attribute to filter by language tag.
+Only single-value comparisons and regex operators are supported; range and list are not defined by the spec.
+
+```
+# French name equals "Ruche"
+q=name[fr]=="Ruche"
+
+# English description contains "hive" (regex)
+q=description[en]~=".*hive.*"
+
+# English description does not contain "inactive"
+q=description[en]!~=".*inactive.*"
+```
+
+---
+
+## JSON property key access
+
+Add a `[key]` bracket suffix to access a specific key inside a JsonProperty value.
+The `jsonKeys` query parameter must list the attribute names that are JsonProperty attributes so the broker can 
+route the query through the JSON path instead of the standard property value path.
+
+```
+# 'metadata' is a JsonProperty; query its 'version' key
+GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities?q=metadata[version]==2&jsonKeys=metadata
+
+# 'config' key 'threshold' is between 10 and 50
+GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities?q=config[threshold]==10..50&jsonKeys=config
+```
+
+The `jsonKeys` parameter accepts a comma-separated list when multiple JsonProperty attributes are queried:
+
+```
+GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities?q=metadata[version]==2;config[mode]=="auto"&jsonKeys=metadata,config
+```
+
+---
+
+## Expanding compact values to IRIs
+
+When comparing against VocabProperty values, comparison values that are compact terms (not already URIs) can be
+expanded to IRIs at query time using the `expandValues` parameter.
+
+```
+# 'category' is a VocabProperty; "BeeHive" is a compact term in the request context
+GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities?q=category=="BeeHive"&expandValues=category
+# equivalent to: q=category=="https://ontology.example.org/BeeHive"
+```

+package com.egm.stellio.shared.queryparameter
+
+sealed class QNode
+
+data class AndNode(val left: QNode, val right: QNode) : QNode()
+data class OrNode(val left: QNode, val right: QNode) : QNode()
+data class NotExistsNode(val rawPath: String) : QNode()
+data class ExistsNode(val rawPath: String) : QNode()
+data class ComparisonNode(
+    val rawPath: String,
+    val operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    val value: QValue
+) : QNode()
+
+enum class ComparisonOperator(val ngsildOp: String, val sqlOp: String) {
+    EQ("==", "=="),
+    NEQ("!=", "<>"),
+    GTE(">=", ">="),
+    GT(">", ">"),
+    LTE("<=", "<="),
+    LT("<", "<"),
+    LIKE_REGEX("~=", "like_regex"),
+    NOT_LIKE_REGEX("!~=", "not_like_regex")
+}

+package com.egm.stellio.shared.queryparameter
+
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.model.ExpandedEntity

+
+fun QNode.toSqlJsonPath(
+    jsonKeys: Set<String> = emptySet(),
+    expandValues: Set<String> = emptySet(),
+    contexts: List<String>,
+    target: ExpandedEntity? = null
+): String {
+    val targetExpr = if (target == null)
+        "entity_payload.payload"
+    else
+        "'" + serializeObject(target.members).escapeSingleQuotes() + "'"
+
+    return toSql(targetExpr, jsonKeys, expandValues, contexts)
+}
+
+private fun QNode.toSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    jsonKeys: Set<String>,
+    expandValues: Set<String>,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): String = when (this) {
+    is AndNode -> "(${left.toSql(targetExpr, jsonKeys, expandValues, contexts)}) AND " +
+        "(${right.toSql(targetExpr, jsonKeys, expandValues, contexts)})"
+    is OrNode -> "(${left.toSql(targetExpr, jsonKeys, expandValues, contexts)}) OR " +
+        "(${right.toSql(targetExpr, jsonKeys, expandValues, contexts)})"
+    is NotExistsNode -> {
+        val attrPath = AttributePath(rawPath, contexts, jsonKeys, expandValues)
+        "NOT (${existsSql(targetExpr, attrPath)})"
+    }
+    is ExistsNode -> {
+        val attrPath = AttributePath(rawPath, contexts, jsonKeys, expandValues)
+        existsSql(targetExpr, attrPath)
+    }
+    is ComparisonNode -> {
+        val attrPath = AttributePath(rawPath, contexts, jsonKeys, expandValues)
+        comparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value, contexts)
+    }
+}
+
+private fun existsSql(targetExpr: String, attrPath: AttributePath): String {
+    val jsonPath = attrPath.buildJsonBExistsPath()
+    return "jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath')"
+}
+
+private fun comparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: QValue,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): String {
+    if (attrPath.languageTag != null) {
+        return languageTagComparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value)
+    }
+
+    if (attrPath.isJsonKeysAttribute && attrPath.trailingPath.isNotEmpty()) {
+        return jsonPropertyComparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value)
+    }
+
+    return when (value) {
+        is RangeValue -> rangeComparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value)
+        is ListValue -> listComparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value, contexts)
+        is SingleValue -> singleValueComparisonSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, value, contexts)
+    }
+}
+
+private fun languageTagComparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: QValue
+): String {
+    val langFilterPath = attrPath.buildJsonBLanguageMapFilterPath()
+    val lang = attrPath.languageTag ?: return "false"
+
+    // LanguageProperty with range or list value is not specified by the NGSI-LD spec
+    if (value !is SingleValue) return "false"
+
+    val pattern = value.raw.escapeSingleQuotes()
+    val langParams = """{"lang": "$lang"}"""
+    return when (operator) {
+        ComparisonOperator.LIKE_REGEX ->
+            """
+                jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$langFilterPath ?
+                    (@."$JSONLD_LANGUAGE_KW" == ${"$"}lang && @."$JSONLD_VALUE_KW" like_regex $pattern)', '$langParams')
+            """
+        ComparisonOperator.NOT_LIKE_REGEX ->
+            """
+                NOT (jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$langFilterPath ? 
+                    (@."$JSONLD_LANGUAGE_KW" == ${"$"}lang && @."$JSONLD_VALUE_KW" like_regex $pattern)', '$langParams'))
+            """
+        else -> {
+            val sqlOp = operator.sqlOp
+            val valueExpr = value.toJsonValue()
+            val params = """{"lang": "$lang", "value": $valueExpr}"""
+            """
+                jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$langFilterPath ? 
+                    (@."$JSONLD_LANGUAGE_KW" == ${"$"}lang && @."$JSONLD_VALUE_KW" $sqlOp ${"$"}value)', '$params')
+            """
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun jsonPropertyComparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: QValue
+): String {
+    val jsonPath = attrPath.buildJsonBJsonPropertyPath()
+    return when (value) {
+        is SingleValue -> singlePathFilter(targetExpr, jsonPath, operator, value)
+        is RangeValue -> rangeFilter(targetExpr, jsonPath, value, operator)
+        is ListValue -> listFilter(targetExpr, jsonPath, operator, value)
+    }
+}
+
+private fun singleValueComparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: SingleValue,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): String {
+    val effectiveValue = if (attrPath.isExpandValuesAttribute && value.type == ValueType.STRING) {
+        val expanded = JsonLdUtils.expandJsonLdTerm(value.raw.removeSurrounding("\""), contexts)
+        SingleValue(expanded, ValueType.URI)
+    } else value
+
+    val scalarTypes = setOf(ValueType.NUMBER, ValueType.BOOLEAN, ValueType.DATE, ValueType.DATETIME, ValueType.TIME)
+    return when {
+        effectiveValue.type == ValueType.URI ||
+            effectiveValue.type == ValueType.STRING && attrPath.isExpandValuesAttribute -> {
+            uriValueSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, effectiveValue)
+        }
+        effectiveValue.type in scalarTypes -> {
+            val propertyPath = attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath()
+            singlePathFilter(targetExpr, propertyPath, operator, effectiveValue)
+        }
+        operator == ComparisonOperator.LIKE_REGEX || operator == ComparisonOperator.NOT_LIKE_REGEX -> {
+            likeRegexMultiPathSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, effectiveValue)
+        }
+        else -> {
+            stringValueSql(targetExpr, attrPath, operator, effectiveValue)
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun uriValueSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: SingleValue
+): String {
+    val preparedValue = if (value.raw.isURI()) value.raw else value.raw.removeSurrounding("\"")
+    val uriValue = SingleValue(preparedValue, ValueType.URI)
+    val relPath = attrPath.buildJsonBRelationshipPath()
+    val propPath = attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath()
+    val vocabPath = attrPath.buildJsonBVocabPath()
+    val langMapPath = attrPath.buildJsonBLanguageMapPath()
+
+    // For NEQ operator, it should be an AND between clauses, but if a path does not exist, PG returns an empty result.
+    // So since an attribute name is unique within an entity, it works with an OR.
+    return """
+        (${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, relPath, operator, uriValue)} OR
+        ${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, propPath, operator, uriValue)} OR
+        ${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, vocabPath, operator, uriValue)} OR
+        ${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, langMapPath, operator, uriValue)})
+    """
+}
+
+private fun stringValueSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: SingleValue
+): String {
+    val propPath = attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath()
+    val langMapPath = attrPath.buildJsonBLanguageMapPath()
+
+    // For NEQ operator, it should be an AND between clauses, but if a path does not exist, PG returns an empty result.
+    // So since an attribute name is unique within an entity, it works with an OR.
+    return """
+        (${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, propPath, operator, value)} OR
+            ${singlePathFilter(targetExpr, langMapPath, operator, value)})
+        """
+}
+
+private fun likeRegexMultiPathSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: SingleValue
+): String {
+    val propPath = attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath()
+    val langMapPath = attrPath.buildJsonBLanguageMapPath()
+    val pattern = value.toJsonValue().escapeSingleQuotes()
+
+    return if (operator == ComparisonOperator.NOT_LIKE_REGEX) {
+        """
+            NOT ((jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$propPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)') OR 
+                jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$langMapPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)')))
+        """
+    } else {
+        """
+            (jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$propPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)') OR
+                jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$langMapPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)'))
+        """
+    }
+}
+
+private fun rangeComparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: RangeValue
+): String {
+    val propertyPath = attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath()
+    return rangeFilter(targetExpr, propertyPath, value, operator)
+}
+
+private fun listComparisonSql(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    attrPath: AttributePath,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: ListValue,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): String {
+    val valueType = value.items.firstOrNull()?.type ?: ValueType.STRING
+    return if (valueType == ValueType.URI || attrPath.isExpandValuesAttribute) {
+        val paths = listOf(
+            attrPath.buildJsonBRelationshipPath(),
+            attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath(),
+            attrPath.buildJsonBVocabPath()
+        )
+        val effectiveValue = if (attrPath.isExpandValuesAttribute) {
+            ListValue(
+                value.items.map { SingleValue(JsonLdUtils.expandJsonLdTerm(it.raw, contexts), ValueType.URI) }
+            )
+        } else {
+            value
+        }
+        val joinOp = if (operator == ComparisonOperator.NEQ) " AND " else " OR "
+        paths.joinToString(joinOp) { path -> listFilter(targetExpr, path, operator, effectiveValue) }
+    } else {
+        listFilter(targetExpr, attrPath.buildJsonBPropertyPath(), operator, value)
+    }
+}
+
+private fun singlePathFilter(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    jsonPath: String,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: SingleValue
+): String {
+    return when {
+        value.type == ValueType.BOOLEAN -> {
+            val literal = value.raw
+            val sqlOp = operator.sqlOp
+            """jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? (@ $sqlOp $literal)')"""
+        }
+        operator == ComparisonOperator.LIKE_REGEX -> {
+            val pattern = value.toJsonValue().escapeSingleQuotes()
+            """jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)')"""
+        }
+        operator == ComparisonOperator.NOT_LIKE_REGEX -> {
+            val pattern = value.toJsonValue().escapeSingleQuotes()
+            """NOT (jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? (@ like_regex $pattern)'))"""
+        }
+        else -> {
+            val sqlOp = operator.sqlOp
+            val params = value.toJsonParameterizedValue().escapeSingleQuotes()
+            """jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? (@ $sqlOp ${"$"}value)', '$params')"""
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun rangeFilter(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    jsonPath: String,
+    value: RangeValue,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator = ComparisonOperator.EQ
+): String {
+    val minJson = value.low.toJsonValue()
+    val maxJson = value.high.toJsonValue()
+    val params = """{"min": $minJson, "max": $maxJson}"""
+    val filter = if (operator == ComparisonOperator.NEQ)
+        $$"""@ < $min || @ > $max"""
+    else
+        $$"""@ >= $min && @ <= $max"""
+    return """jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? ($filter)', '${params.escapeSingleQuotes()}')"""
+}
+
+private fun listFilter(
+    targetExpr: String,
+    jsonPath: String,
+    operator: ComparisonOperator,
+    value: ListValue
+): String {
+    val (sqlOp, joinOp) =
+        if (operator == ComparisonOperator.NEQ) "<>" to " && "
+        else "==" to " || "
+    val filter = value.items.joinToString(joinOp) { item ->
+        "@ $sqlOp ${item.toJsonValue()}"
+    }
+    return """jsonb_path_exists($targetExpr, '$jsonPath ? (${filter.escapeSingleQuotes()})')"""
+}
+
+private fun SingleValue.toJsonParameterizedValue(): String =
+    """{"value": ${this.toJsonValue()}}"""
+
+private fun SingleValue.toJsonValue(): String = when (type) {
+    ValueType.NUMBER -> raw
+    ValueType.BOOLEAN -> raw
+    ValueType.STRING, ValueType.DATETIME, ValueType.DATE, ValueType.TIME -> {
+        val unquoted = raw.removeSurrounding("\"")
+        "\"$unquoted\""
+    }
+    ValueType.URI -> {
+        val unquoted = raw.removeSurrounding("\"")
+        "\"$unquoted\""
+    }
+}

+package com.egm.stellio.shared.queryparameter
+
+import arrow.core.Either
+import arrow.core.left
+import arrow.core.raise.either
+import arrow.core.raise.ensure
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.model.APIException
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.model.BadRequestDataException
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.ErrorMessages.QueryParameter.invalidQQueryMessage
+
+/**
+ * Recursive descent parser for the NGSI-LD Query Language as defined in ETSI GS CIM 009, clause 4.9.
+ *
+ * Grammar:
+ *   query      = or-expr
+ *   or-expr    = and-expr ( "|" and-expr )*
+ *   and-expr   = term ( ";" term )*
+ *   term       = "!" attr-path
+ *              | "(" query ")"
+ *              | attr-path [ comparison-op query-value ]
+ *   query-value = simple-value ".." simple-value   (range)
+ *              | simple-value ( "," simple-value )+ (list)
+ *              | simple-value
+ */
+fun parseQQuery(raw: String): Either<APIException, QNode> {
+    if (raw.isBlank()) return BadRequestDataException(invalidQQueryMessage("Query string is empty")).left()
+    return QParserImpl(raw).parse()
+        .mapLeft { BadRequestDataException(invalidQQueryMessage(it)) }
+}
+
+private class QParserImpl(private val raw: String) {
+    private var pos = 0
+
+    companion object {
+        private const val OPERATOR_MAX_LENGTH = 3
+    }
+
+    fun parse(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        val node = parseOrExpr().bind()
+        if (pos < raw.length) raise("Unexpected character at position $pos: '${raw[pos]}'")
+        node
+    }
+
+    private fun parseOrExpr(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        var left = parseAndExpr().bind()
+        while (pos < raw.length && raw[pos] == '|') {
+            pos++
+            left = OrNode(left, parseAndExpr().bind())
+        }
+        left
+    }
+
+    private fun parseAndExpr(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        var left = parseTerm().bind()
+        while (pos < raw.length && raw[pos] == ';') {
+            pos++
+            ensure(pos < raw.length) { "Trailing ';' at end of query" }
+            left = AndNode(left, parseTerm().bind())
+        }
+        left
+    }
+
+    private fun parseTerm(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        ensure(pos < raw.length) { "Unexpected end of input" }
+        when {
+            raw[pos] == '(' -> parseGroupedExpr().bind()
+            isNegationPrefix() -> parseNotExistsExpr().bind()
+            else -> parseAttrExpr().bind()
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun parseGroupedExpr(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        pos++
+        val node = parseOrExpr().bind()
+        ensure(!(pos >= raw.length || raw[pos] != ')')) { "Unbalanced parenthesis: missing closing ')'" }
+        pos++
+        node
+    }
+
+    private fun parseNotExistsExpr(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        pos++
+        val rawPath = parseRawAttributePath().bind()
+        ensure(rawPath.isNotEmpty()) { "Missing attribute path after '!'" }
+        NotExistsNode(rawPath)
+    }
+
+    private fun parseAttrExpr(): Either<String, QNode> = either {
+        val rawPath = parseRawAttributePath().bind()
+        ensure(rawPath.isNotEmpty()) { "Empty attribute path at position $pos" }
+        val op = parseOperator().bind()
+        if (op == null) ExistsNode(rawPath) else ComparisonNode(rawPath, op, parseValue().bind())
+    }
+
+    private fun isNegationPrefix(): Boolean {
+        if (raw[pos] != '!') return false
+        val next = pos + 1
+        if (next >= raw.length) return false
+        return raw[next] != '=' && raw[next] != '~'
+    }
+
+    private fun parseRawAttributePath(): Either<String, String> = either {
+        val start = pos
+        var inBracket = false
+        var done = false
+        while (pos < raw.length && !done) {
+            val c = raw[pos]
+            when {
+                c == '[' -> {
+                    inBracket = true
+                    pos++
+                }
+                c == ']' -> {
+                    inBracket = false
+                    pos++
+                    done = true
+                }
+                inBracket -> pos++
+                c == ';' || c == '|' || c == ')' || isOperatorChar(c) -> done = true
+                else -> pos++
+            }
+        }
+        ensure(!inBracket) { "Unclosed bracket in value" }
+        raw.substring(start, pos)
+    }
+
+    private fun isOperatorChar(c: Char): Boolean = c in setOf('=', '!', '>', '<', '~')
+
+    private fun parseOperator(): Either<String, ComparisonOperator?> = either {
+        if (pos >= raw.length || !isOperatorChar(raw[pos])) return@either null
+        ComparisonOperator.entries.find { tryConsume(it.ngsildOp) }
+            ?: raise(
+                "Unknown operator at position $pos: " +
+                    "'${raw.substring(pos, minOf(pos + OPERATOR_MAX_LENGTH, raw.length))}'"
+            )
+    }
+
+    private fun tryConsume(s: String): Boolean {
+        if (raw.startsWith(s, pos)) {
+            pos += s.length
+            return true
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    private fun parseValue(): Either<String, QValue> = either {
+        val rawVal = parseRawValue().bind()
+        ensure(rawVal.isNotEmpty()) { "Empty value after operator" }
+
+        if (!rawVal.startsWith('"') && rawVal.contains("..")) {
+            val parts = rawVal.split("..")
+            ensure(!(parts.size != 2 || parts[0].isEmpty() || parts[1].isEmpty())) {
+                "Invalid range value: '$rawVal'"
+            }
+            return@either RangeValue(
+                SingleValue(parts[0], ValueType.detect(parts[0])),
+                SingleValue(parts[1], ValueType.detect(parts[1]))
+            )
+        }
+
+        if (rawVal.isQValueList()) {
+            val items = rawVal.splitQValueList().map { SingleValue(it, ValueType.detect(it)) }
+            if (items.size > 1) return@either ListValue(items)
+        }
+
+        SingleValue(rawVal, ValueType.detect(rawVal))
+    }
+
+    private fun parseRawValue(): Either<String, String> = either {
+        val sb = StringBuilder()
+        var inQuotes = false
+        while (pos < raw.length) {
+            val c = raw[pos]
+            when {
+                c == '"' -> {
+                    inQuotes = !inQuotes
+                    sb.append(c)
+                    pos++
+                }
+                inQuotes -> {
+                    sb.append(c)
+                    pos++
+                }
+                c in listOf(';', '|', ')') -> break
+                else -> {
+                    sb.append(c)
+                    pos++
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        ensure(!inQuotes) { "Unclosed quote in value" }
+        sb.toString()
+    }
+}
+
+internal fun String.isQValueList(): Boolean {
+    var inQuotes = false
+    for (char in this) {
+        when (char) {
+            '"' -> inQuotes = !inQuotes
+            ',' -> if (!inQuotes) return true
+            else -> {}
+        }
+    }
+    return false
+}
+
+internal fun String.splitQValueList(): List<String> {
+    val values = mutableListOf<String>()
+    var inQuotes = false
+    val current = StringBuilder()
+    for (char in this) {
+        when (char) {
+            '"' -> {
+                inQuotes = !inQuotes
+                current.append(char)
+            }
+            ',' if !inQuotes -> {
+                values.add(current.toString())
+                current.clear()
+            }
+            else -> current.append(char)
+        }
+    }
+    values.add(current.toString())
+    return values
+}

+package com.egm.stellio.shared.queryparameter
+
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.isDate
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.isDateTime
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.isTime
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.isURI
+
+sealed class QValue
+
+data class SingleValue(val raw: String, val type: ValueType) : QValue()
+data class RangeValue(val low: SingleValue, val high: SingleValue) : QValue()
+data class ListValue(val items: List<SingleValue>) : QValue()
+
+enum class ValueType {
+    NUMBER, STRING, BOOLEAN, DATETIME, DATE, TIME, URI;
+
+    companion object {
+        fun detect(raw: String): ValueType {
+            val unquoted = raw.removeSurrounding("\"")
+            return when {
+                raw == "true" || raw == "false" -> BOOLEAN
+                unquoted.toDoubleOrNull() != null -> NUMBER
+                unquoted.isDateTime() -> DATETIME
+                unquoted.isDate() -> DATE
+                unquoted.isTime() -> TIME
+                raw.isURI() || unquoted.isURI() -> URI
+                else -> STRING
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}

+package com.egm.stellio.search.entity.service
+

+/**
+ * Test-side compatibility helpers: they build an entity query from a `q` string, a pagination
+ * configuration, and a list of contexts through the documented composition expression, so
+ * legacy test constructions remain supported by the test source tree whatever the
+ * representation of a parsed filter is.
+ */
+@Suppress("FunctionName")
+fun EntitiesQueryFromGet(
+    q: CharSequence?,
+    paginationQuery: PaginationQuery,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): com.egm.stellio.search.entity.model.EntitiesQueryFromGet = runBlocking {
+    composeEntitiesQueryFromGet(
+        buildDefaultPagination(paginationQuery.limit, paginationQuery.limit),
+        LinkedMultiValueMap<String, String>().apply { q?.let { add("q", it.toString()) } },
+        contexts
+    ).shouldSucceedAndResult()
+}
+
+fun assertEntitiesQueryFromGetConstructionFails(q: String): Unit = runBlocking {
+    composeEntitiesQueryFromGet(
+        buildDefaultPagination(),
+        LinkedMultiValueMap<String, String>().apply { add("q", q) },
+        listOf("http://localhost:8093/jsonld-contexts/apic-compound.jsonld")
+    ).shouldFail { }
+}

+

+
+/**
+ * Checks that the `jsonKeys` and `expandValues` options of an entities query reach the statement that is
+ * sent to the entities store when retrieving entities (no database is available here, so the statement
+ * submitted to the store is the observable outcome of the query).
+ */
+class EntityQueryServiceQueryOptionsTests {
+
+    private class StatementCaptured : RuntimeException()
+
+    private val expandedBeeHive = "https://ontology.eglobalmark.com/apic#BeeHive"
+
+    // the bare JSON key, not merely the last segment of an expanded IRI such as .../default-context/firmware
+    private val rawFirmwareKey = Regex("""(?<![/#\w])firmware""")
+
+    private suspend fun statementsSentToStore(entitiesQuery: EntitiesQuery): String {
+        val statements = mutableListOf<String>()
+        val databaseClient = mockk<DatabaseClient>()
+        every { databaseClient.sql(any<String>()) } answers {
+            statements.add(firstArg())
+            throw StatementCaptured()
+        }
+        val authorizationService = mockk<AuthorizationService>()
+        coEvery { authorizationService.getAccessRightWithClauseAndFilter(any()) } returns null
+
+        runCatching { EntityQueryService(databaseClient, authorizationService).queryEntities(entitiesQuery) }
+
+        assertTrue(statements.isNotEmpty(), "No statement was sent to the entities store")
+        return statements.joinToString("\n")
+    }
+
+    private fun getQuery(vararg params: Pair<String, String>): EntitiesQuery =
+        composeEntitiesQueryFromGet(
+            buildDefaultPagination(30, 100),
+            LinkedMultiValueMap<String, String>().apply { params.forEach { add(it.first, it.second) } },
+            APIC_COMPOUND_CONTEXTS
+        ).shouldSucceedAndResult()
+
+    private fun postQuery(body: String): EntitiesQuery =
+        either {
+            composeEntitiesQueryFromPost(
+                buildDefaultPagination(30, 100),
+                Query(body).bind(),
+                LinkedMultiValueMap(),
+                APIC_COMPOUND_CONTEXTS
+            ).bind()
+        }.shouldSucceedAndResult()
+
+    @Test
+    fun `an expandValues option should make a GET query compare against the expanded value`() = runTest {
+        val withOption = statementsSentToStore(getQuery("q" to "category==BeeHive", "expandValues" to "category"))
+        assertTrue(withOption.contains(expandedBeeHive), "Expanded comparison value not used: $withOption")
+
+        val withoutOption = statementsSentToStore(getQuery("q" to "category==BeeHive"))
+        assertFalse(withoutOption.contains(expandedBeeHive), "Value expanded without expandValues: $withoutOption")
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `an expandValues option should make a Query payload compare against the expanded value`() = runTest {
+        val statement = statementsSentToStore(
+            postQuery(
+                """
+                {
+                    "type": "Query",
+                    "q": "category==BeeHive",
+                    "expandValues": ["category"]
+                }
+                """.trimIndent()
+            )
+        )
+        assertTrue(statement.contains(expandedBeeHive), "Expanded comparison value not used: $statement")
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a jsonKeys option should make a GET query address the raw key inside the JSON content`() = runTest {
+        val statement = statementsSentToStore(
+            getQuery("q" to "jsonObject[firmware]==2", "jsonKeys" to "jsonObject")
+        )
+        assertTrue(rawFirmwareKey.containsMatchIn(statement), "Raw JSON key not addressed: $statement")
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a jsonKeys option should make a Query payload address the raw key inside the JSON content`() = runTest {
+        val statement = statementsSentToStore(
+            postQuery(
+                """
+                {
+                    "type": "Query",
+                    "q": "jsonObject[firmware]==2",
+                    "jsonKeys": ["jsonObject"]
+                }
+                """.trimIndent()
+            )
+        )
+        assertTrue(rawFirmwareKey.containsMatchIn(statement), "Raw JSON key not addressed: $statement")
+    }
+}

+private fun composeEntitiesQueryFromPostRequest(
+    defaultPagination: ApplicationProperties.Pagination,
+    requestBody: String,
+    requestParams: MultiValueMap<String, String>,
+    contexts: List<String>
+): Either<APIException, EntitiesQueryFromPost> = either {
+    val query = Query(requestBody).bind()
+    composeEntitiesQueryFromPost(
+        defaultPagination,
+        query,
+        requestParams,
+        contexts
+    ).bind()
 }

+package com.egm.stellio.subscription.model
+
+import arrow.core.flatMap
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.model.BadRequestDataException
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.model.NGSILD_SUBSCRIPTION_TERM
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.BEEHIVE_IRI
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.shouldFail
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.shouldSucceedAndResult
+import com.egm.stellio.shared.util.toUri
+import com.egm.stellio.subscription.model.Subscription.Companion.deserialize
+import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.assertInstanceOf
+
+/**
+ * Observable outcomes of a subscription payload: an invalid `q` filter makes the payload fail
+ * (either while deserializing or while validating it) with BadRequestData, and the `jsonKeys` /
+ * `expandValues` options are accepted on a subscription.
+ */
+class SubscriptionValidationSupportTests {
+
+    private fun subscriptionPayload(
+        q: String? = null,
+        extra: Map<String, Any> = emptyMap()
+    ): Map<String, Any> {
+        val payload = mutableMapOf<String, Any>(
+            "id" to "urn:ngsi-ld:BeeHive:TESTC".toUri(),
+            "type" to NGSILD_SUBSCRIPTION_TERM,
+            "entities" to listOf(mapOf("type" to BEEHIVE_IRI)),
+            "notification" to mapOf("endpoint" to mapOf("uri" to "http://my.endpoint/notifiy"))
+        )
+        q?.let { payload["q"] = it }
+        payload.putAll(extra)
+        return payload
+    }
+
+    private fun deserializeAndValidate(payload: Map<String, Any>) =
+        deserialize(payload, emptyList()).flatMap { it.validate() }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `it should reject a subscription whose q lacks a comparison value`() = runTest {
+        deserializeAndValidate(subscriptionPayload(q = "temperature==")).shouldFail {
+            assertInstanceOf<BadRequestDataException>(it)
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `it should reject a subscription whose q has unbalanced parentheses`() = runTest {
+        deserializeAndValidate(subscriptionPayload(q = "(temperature>=10")).shouldFail {
+            assertInstanceOf<BadRequestDataException>(it)
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `it should validate a subscription without q`() = runTest {
+        deserializeAndValidate(subscriptionPayload()).shouldSucceedAndResult()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `it should validate a subscription with a well-formed q`() = runTest {
+        deserializeAndValidate(subscriptionPayload(q = "temperature>=10")).shouldSucceedAndResult()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `it should accept jsonKeys and expandValues on a subscription`() = runTest {
+        val payload = subscriptionPayload(
+            q = "metadata[firmware]==2",
+            extra = mapOf(
+                "jsonKeys" to listOf("metadata"),
+                "expandValues" to listOf("sensorType")
+            )
+        )
+        deserializeAndValidate(payload).shouldSucceedAndResult()
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Feature Request: use folds for reasoning and tool outputs toggles
Currently toggles for reasoning and tool outputs just remove/add content from buffers. It would be great if folds were created in their place instead, and toggle controls simply closed/opened them. This would allow the user to more flexibly manage the display and, if necessary, open reasoning/tool ââoutput exactly where they need it.

### Additional contract requirements

## Contract addendum

### Fold-based reasoning and tool output toggles

When a message contains reasoning or tool output:

- The full reasoning text and tool output remain present in the output buffer even
  while the corresponding visibility toggle is turned off. Toggling visibility off
  must not delete that content from the buffer.
- While a toggle is off, the associated content is hidden from view by collapsing
  it (for example with buffer folds) instead of removing it, and the section's
  summary line (the reasoning header or the tool invocation line) stays visible.
- The user can reveal hidden content in place exactly where it lives in the
  buffer using ordinary fold controls (for example `zR` to open all or `zo` on a
  single fold), and that revealed content stays available in the buffer across
  visibility toggle round trips.

Any Folding provided for these sections starts out collapsed when the output
window is set up (window fold level `0`).

+---Add a fold range

+
+---Add fold with threshold awareness
+---@param start_line number Line where content starts
+---@param show boolean Whether content is visible
+---@param use_folds boolean Whether folds are enabled
+function Output:add_fold_with_threshold(start_line, show, use_folds)
+  if not use_folds then
+    return
+  end
+
+  local threshold = config.ui.output.tools.folding_threshold or 5
+  local end_line = self:get_line_count()
+
+  if not show then
+    if end_line > start_line then
+      self:add_fold(start_line, end_line)
+    end
+  elseif end_line > start_line + threshold then
+    self:add_fold(start_line + threshold, end_line)
+  end
+end

 function Output:get_line_count()

+  -- A rendered line is hidden while it lies inside a closed fold;
+  -- foldclosed() reports the fold's start line for every line inside the
+  -- fold instead of -1. This includes the fold's own start line: once a fold
+  -- is closed its start line only displays the fold's summary (foldtext),
+  -- not the line's own content.
+  local function line_is_visible(lnum)
+    return foldclosed_at(lnum) == -1
+  end

+  -- A section counts as visible while all of its rendered lines stay outside
+  -- every closed fold.
+  local function section_is_visible(needles)
+    for _, needle in ipairs(needles) do
+      local lnum = find_line(needle)
+      assert.is_not_nil(lnum)
+      if not line_is_visible(lnum) then
+        return false
+      end
+    end
+    return true
+  end
+
+  -- A section's body counts as collapsed only while every rendered body line
+  -- hides inside a closed fold.
+  local function section_lines_are_hidden(needles)
+    for _, needle in ipairs(needles) do
+      local lnum = find_line(needle)
+      assert.is_not_nil(lnum)
+      if line_is_visible(lnum) then
+        return false
+      end
+    end
+    return true
+  end

problem_statement:
Sort elements case-insensitively
See #45, which also has to do with sorting. 

Currently most (if not all) fields with sorted values are sorted case-sensitively. So for example `Cabal-syntax` is sorted before `base`. I think this is not what people expect. Instead they should be sorted case-insensitively. [HIDDEN]
### Additional contract requirements

For fields whose values are sorted, order the underlying values case-insensitively, including file paths that need quotes when rendered. Values equal under case folding may appear in either relative order. Fields whose values are order-sensitive must retain their existing order.

problem_statement: MySlot Error - Unsupported Slot Type [outfit] Yes 12.0 Outfits are part of the new transmog system, and can be placed on your bars, like equipment sets. -- Rod Shelton [roshne@gmail.com](mailto:roshne@gmail.com) ### Additional contract requirements ## Scope These requirements come from the issue report "MySlot Error - Unsupported Slot Type [outfit]": transmog outfits can be placed on action bars just like equipment sets, so exporting, importing, and restoring an action-bar layout must handle outfit buttons instead of rejecting them. The requirements are behavioral and externally observable: they are expressed in terms of the exported layout text, chat output, and the actions present on the action bars after a restore. They do not prescribe internal names, numeric encodings, message layouts, or API choices. ## Requirements 1. **Recognize outfit buttons.** Scanning an action bar that contains a transmog outfit button must capture that button into the exported layout, classified as an outfit, and must not emit the addon's "unsupported slot type" warning for it. The exported layout text must be re-importable without errors. 2. **Identify the outfit.** The exported layout must carry enough information to restore that outfit later: its action-bar slot, a reference to the outfit worn at export time, and enough identifying detail that a restore can still resolve the outfit by name when the exporting account's outfit id does not exist on the restoring account. 3. **Restore outfit buttons.** Restoring an imported layout must place each outfit button back on its original action-bar slot when the referenced outfit is available on the restoring character or account, keeping the per-slot correspondence: each slot ends up holding the outfit reference exported from that slot, including when the restore resolves outfits by name because the exported ids are unknown locally. 4. **Fail gracefully, not loudly, when an outfit cannot be resolved.** When a referenced outfit cannot be resolved at restore time — because the client has no outfit system at all, or because neither the exported id nor the exported identifying detail matches a known outfit — the restore must not fabricate a different action for that bar slot, and it must not report the outfit action as an unsupported slot type. 5. **Survive save/load round trips.** A layout containing an outfit record that is persisted between sessions (saved and loaded the way per-character storage persists it) must remain restorable on another machine whose outfit ids differ, resolving the outfit from its exported identifying detail. 6. **Keep existing behavior.** Layouts that contain only already-supported action types (for example equipment sets) must continue to export, import, and restore exactly as before.

contract_addendum:
## Scope

These requirements come from the issue report "MySlot Error - Unsupported Slot Type [outfit]": transmog outfits can be placed on action bars just like equipment sets, so exporting, importing, and restoring an action-bar layout must handle outfit buttons instead of rejecting them. The requirements are behavioral and externally observable: they are expressed in terms of the exported layout text, chat output, and the actions present on the action bars after a restore. They do not prescribe internal names, numeric encodings, message layouts, or API choices.

## Requirements

1. **Recognize outfit buttons.** Scanning an action bar that contains a transmog outfit button must capture that button into the exported layout, classified as an outfit, and must not emit the addon's "unsupported slot type" warning for it. The exported layout text must be re-importable without errors.

2. **Identify the outfit.** The exported layout must carry enough information to restore that outfit later: its action-bar slot, a reference to the outfit worn at export time, and enough identifying detail that a restore can still resolve the outfit by name when the exporting account's outfit id does not exist on the restoring account.

3. **Restore outfit buttons.** Restoring an imported layout must place each outfit button back on its original action-bar slot when the referenced outfit is available on the restoring character or account, keeping the per-slot correspondence: each slot ends up holding the outfit reference exported from that slot, including when the restore resolves outfits by name because the exported ids are unknown locally.

4. **Fail gracefully, not loudly, when an outfit cannot be resolved.** When a referenced outfit cannot be resolved at restore time — because the client has no outfit system at all, or because neither the exported id nor the exported identifying detail matches a known outfit — the restore must not fabricate a different action for that bar slot, and it must not report the outfit action as an unsupported slot type.

5. **Survive save/load round trips.** A layout containing an outfit record that is persisted between sessions (saved and loaded the way per-character storage persists it) must remain restorable on another machine whose outfit ids differ, resolving the outfit from its exported identifying detail.

6. **Keep existing behavior.** Layouts that contain only already-supported action types (for example equipment sets) must continue to export, import, and restore exactly as before.

+-- CI-only coverage for transmog outfits on action bars.
+--
+-- Outfits can be dragged onto action bars just like equipment sets, so the
+-- addon must export them, survive an import round trip, and put them back on
+-- the bar when restoring. These suites build a hermetic WoW-side world (a
+-- private table driving a minimal outfit/equipment/bar/cursor surface) so the
+-- full Export -> Import -> save/load -> restore pipeline can be observed end
+-- to end without touching a real client. In-game this file loads but every
+-- suite is skipped; the existing in-game per-type round trips cover live
+-- behavior.
+--
+-- The tests only observe externally visible behavior: exported layout text,
+-- chat output, cursor state, and the state of the action bar. No internal
+-- record layout, field name, or encoding is ever inspected, so any
+-- behaviorally equivalent implementation satisfies them.
+
+local _, MySlot = ...
+local T = MySlot.test
+local Host = MySlot.host
+
+local function full_opt()
+    return {
+        ignoreActionBars = {},
+        ignoreMacros = {},
+        ignoreBinding = false,
+        ignorePetActionBar = true, -- avoid pet APIs we don't stub
+    }
+end
+
+local function recover_opt()
+    return { actionOpt = full_opt() }
+end
+
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- CI-only hermetic world. The whole world lives in a private table; the
+-- suite is the only code that consults `world`.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+local function new_world()
+    return {
+        bar = {},                 -- [slot] = { type=, index=, subType= }
+        cursor = nil,
+        outfits = nil,            -- nil => no outfit system; else { [id] = name }
+        equip_max_index = -1,
+        equip_sets = {},          -- [i0] = setID
+    }
+end
+
+local world = new_world()
+
+-- The real GetActionInfo: reads the world's action bars.
+function _G.GetActionInfo(slotId)
+    local s = world.bar[slotId]
+    if not s then return nil end
+    return s.type, s.index, s.subType
+end
+
+function _G.GetCursorInfo()
+    local c = world.cursor
+    if not c then return nil end
+    return c.type, c.index
+end
+
+function _G.ClearCursor()
+    world.cursor = nil
+end
+
+function _G.PlaceAction(slotId)
+    local c = world.cursor
+    if not c then return end
+    world.bar[slotId] = { type = c.type, index = c.index, subType = c.subType }
+    world.cursor = nil
+end
+
+function _G.PickupAction(slotId)
+    world.cursor = world.bar[slotId]
+    world.bar[slotId] = nil
+end
+
+-- Bindings/macros are out of scope for these scenarios; keep them harmless.
+function _G.SetBinding() return true end
+function _G.SaveBindings() end
+
+local function install_outfit_api()
+    local byid = world.outfits
+    if byid == nil then
+        _G.C_TransmogOutfitInfo = nil
+        return
+    end
+    -- Account-local outfit ids and names. Several enumeration entry points
+    -- expose the same data so that callers can use whichever one they need
+    -- to resolve an outfit by its exported identifying detail.
+    local function sorted_ids()
+        local ids = {}
+        for id in pairs(byid) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end
+        table.sort(ids)
+        return ids
+    end
+    _G.C_TransmogOutfitInfo = {
+        GetOutfitInfo = function(outfitID)
+            local name = byid[outfitID]
+            if not name then return nil end
+            return { outfitID = outfitID, name = name }
+        end,
+        GetOutfitInfoByName = function(name)
+            for id, n in pairs(byid) do
+                if n == name then return { outfitID = id, name = n } end
+            end
+            return nil
+        end,
+        GetOutfitIDs = function()
+            return sorted_ids()
+        end,
+        GetOutfits = function()
+            return sorted_ids()
+        end,
+        GetOutfitsInfo = function()

+            for _, id in ipairs(sorted_ids()) do

+            return out
+        end,
+        PickupOutfit = function(outfitID)

+            world.cursor = { type = "outfit", index = outfitID }
+        end,
+    }

+        end,

+-- re-parsed, exactly what happens when a layout is persisted between
+-- sessions. The resulting message must still drive restores.
+local function save_load_layout(msg)

problem_statement:
Request: Sorting and Filtering
For those of us who play lots of classes and specs, we end up with dozens of loadouts. To help with that, I request two features:

- A way to filter loadouts based on the class we are logged into, and
- A way to sort or group the shown loadout.

Even something as simple as an alphabetical sort would greatly improve the user experience.

### Additional contract requirements

## Loadout list sorting and filtering contract

The saved-loadout profile selector gains user-visible sorting and filtering
controls. The behavior below is what the implementation must expose through
that selector; how it is implemented internally is unconstrained.

### Opening the selector

Clicking the saved-loadout profile selector control opens a menu listing the
user's saved loadouts. The control also shows the currently selected
loadout's name.

### Sort / grouping choices

The menu offers three ways to order the shown loadouts:

- **By date** — the default. Loadouts are listed so that the most recently
  created loadout appears first (creation order is the order loadouts were
  saved).
- **By name** — loadouts are listed alphabetically A-Z. The comparison
  ignores letter case; loadouts whose names compare equal ignoring case
  appear in storage order, so the listing is deterministic every time the
  menu opens.
- **By class** — loadouts are grouped by player class. Each group is
  preceded by a visible section header carrying a user-facing label for
  that class. Within a group, loadouts are ordered by the name rule above.
  Groups are ordered alphabetically by class, except that loadouts saved
  before class tagging existed (entries with no recorded class) form a
  group of their own that is always listed last; its header must not be
  presented as a real player class.

The currently selected sort choice persists across openings of the menu
until the user changes it, and it applies together with the class filter
below.

### Class filtering

The menu also offers an "only my class" filter toggle. When enabled,
loadouts whose recorded class differs from the logged-in character's class
are hidden from the list. Loadouts with no recorded class (legacy entries)
are always shown, regardless of the filter setting. The filter is
persistent: once toggled it stays in effect across later openings of the
menu until the user toggles it off.

### Ordinary profile selection

Choosing a shown loadout from the menu behaves as before: its export text
is loaded into the export text area and it becomes the current selection
shown on the selector control, regardless of the active sort or filter.
Applying a sort or filter must not disturb this behavior — every loadout
that remains listed stays selectable and loads exactly as it did without
sorting or filtering.

+-- Builds the display order for the saved-loadout list (issue #102). Pure helper
+-- so it can be unit tested; the GUI feeds it the saved exports plus the user's
+-- sort/filter prefs and renders the returned rows.
+--
+--   exports     array of { name, value, class? } loadout entries (storage order)
+--   sort        "date" (newest first, default), "name" (A-Z), or
+--               "class" (grouped by class token, then name)
+--   filterClass when true, hide entries whose class differs from myClass; entries
+--               with no stored class (legacy) are always shown
+--   myClass     the english class token to filter against (e.g. "DRUID")
+--
+-- Returns an array of rows preserving the ORIGINAL exports index as identity:
+--   { index = i }      a loadout entry (exports[i])
+--   { header = token } a class group header (only in "class" sort); token is the
+--                      class token, or false for the legacy/unknown group
+function MySlot:OrderLoadouts(exports, sort, filterClass, myClass)
+    sort = sort or "date"
+
+    local order = {}
+    for i = 1, #exports do
+        local e = exports[i]
+        if e and not (filterClass and e.class and e.class ~= myClass) then
+            order[#order + 1] = i
+        end
+    end
+
+    local function byName(a, b)
+        local na, nb = (exports[a].name or ""):lower(), (exports[b].name or ""):lower()
+        if na == nb then
+            -- table.sort is not stable; break ties by storage index so the order
+            -- stays deterministic across openings.
+            return a < b
+        end
+        return na < nb
+    end
+
+    if sort == "name" then
+        table.sort(order, byName)
+    elseif sort == "class" then
+        table.sort(order, function(a, b)
+            local ca, cb = exports[a].class, exports[b].class
+            if ca ~= cb then
+                -- Unknown/legacy (no class) sorts last; otherwise alpha by token.
+                if not ca then return false end
+                if not cb then return true end
+                return ca < cb
+            end
+            return byName(a, b)
+        end)
+    else
+        -- "date": newest first. Entries are appended on create, so a higher
+        -- storage index means more recent -- reverse the ascending order.
+        for i = 1, math.floor(#order / 2) do
+            order[i], order[#order - i + 1] = order[#order - i + 1], order[i]
+        end
+    end
+
+    local rows = {}
+    local lastClass, haveLast = nil, false
+    for _, i in ipairs(order) do
+        if sort == "class" then
+            local c = exports[i].class or false
+            if not haveLast or c ~= lastClass then
+                lastClass, haveLast = c, true
+                rows[#rows + 1] = { header = c }
+            end
+        end
+        rows[#rows + 1] = { index = i }
+    end
+    return rows
+end

     --cache spells

+-- CI entry point.

+--   4. Run the suite. Exit nonzero if anything failed.

+-- Run from repo root:    lua5.1 ci/run.lua   (luabitop required)
+--                     or luajit ci/run.lua
+
+dofile((arg[0]:match("(.-)[/\\][^/\\]+$") or ".") .. "/wow_stubs.lua")
+
+local MySlot = dofile((arg[0]:match("(.-)[/\\][^/\\]+$") or ".") .. "/loader.lua")
+
+-- Same calling convention as addon files.
+local function load_test(rel)
+    local path = "tests/" .. rel
+    local chunk, err = loadfile(path)
+    if not chunk then
+        io.stderr:write("loadfile failed: " .. path .. ": " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
+        os.exit(2)
+    end
+    local ok, runerr = pcall(chunk, "Myslot", MySlot)
+    if not ok then
+        io.stderr:write("execute failed: " .. path .. ": " .. tostring(runerr) .. "\n")
+        os.exit(2)
+    end
+end
+
+load_test("framework.lua")
+load_test("host.lua")
+-- Headless UI stand-ins (widgets, menu descriptions, saved-variable
+-- writers). Must be dofile'd before any case that boots the interface via
+-- tests/helpers/ui_loader.lua. Harmless for the data-layer suites.
+dofile("tests/helpers/ui_stubs.lua")
+
+load_test("cases/base64.lua")

+-- Optional suite filter: `luajit ci/run.lua ordering` runs only suites or
+-- tests whose name contains the given substring (case-insensitive). Tests in
+-- other suites are deselected and not run.
+local filter = arg[1] and arg[1]:lower() or nil
+local selected, deselected = 0, 0
+if filter then
+    for _, suite in ipairs(MySlot.test._suites) do
+        local kept = {}
+        for _, test in ipairs(suite.tests) do
+            if suite.name:lower():find(filter, 1, true)
+                or test.name:lower():find(filter, 1, true) then
+                kept[#kept + 1] = test
+                selected = selected + 1
+            else
+                deselected = deselected + 1
+            end
+        end
+        suite.tests = kept
+    end
+end
+
+local exit_code = 0
+local _, failed = MySlot.test.run(function(line)
+    -- Translate the framework result lines into the plain
+    -- "Status || <test>" lines consumed by the log parser.
+    local status, name = line:match("^%s*(ok)%s+-%s*(.+)$")
+    if not status then status, name = line:match("^%s*(FAIL)%s+%-%s*(.+)$") end
+    if not status then status, name = line:match("^%s*(skip)%s+%-%s*([^%(]+)") end
+    if status and name then
+        name = name:gsub("%s+$", "")
+        local label = (status == "ok") and "Success" or (status == "FAIL" and "Fail" or "Skip")
+        print(label .. " || " .. name)
+    else
+        print(line)
+    end
+end)
+print(string.format("# filter=%s selected=%d deselected=%d",

+    io.stderr:write("ci/run.lua: filter matched no tests: " .. tostring(arg[1]) .. "\n")
+    exit_code = 2
+end
+os.exit(failed == 0 and exit_code or 1)
