+-- Saved-loadout ordering/filtering contract. These tests interact with the
+-- selector and its menu through visible labels and menu actions; they do not
+-- depend on a particular widget template or menu hierarchy.
+
+local _, MySlot = ...
+local T = MySlot.test
+local UI_LOADER = "tests/helpers/ui_loader.lua"
+
+local active_selector
+local seeded_names = {}
+local seeded_name_set = {}
+local editbox
+local create_saved_profile
+
+local function plain_text(text)
+    return tostring(text or "")
+        :gsub("|[tT][^|]*|t%s*", "")
+        :gsub("|c%x*", ""):gsub("|r", "")
+        :gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
+end
+
+local function boot(player_class)
+    -- The UI reset preserves the SavedVariables table identity (the addon may
+    -- have cached it) but clears all of its contents, not just this test's
+    -- knowledge of implementation-specific preference keys.
+    _G.WowStub.reset()
+    _G.WowStub.player.class = player_class
+    _G.WowUiStub.reset()
+    _G.WowUiStub.WriteDefaults(player_class)
+    active_selector = nil
+    dofile(UI_LOADER).addon_loaded(MySlot)
+end
+
+local function seed_exports(entries)
+    -- Tagged records are created through the visible profile-creation path so
+    -- fixtures do not prescribe a storage key for class metadata. A legacy
+    -- record is represented using the pre-tag saved-record shape.
+    MyslotExports = MyslotExports or {}
+    local exports = MyslotExports["exports"] or {}
+    -- Keep the SavedVariables table identity: gui.lua captures this table
+    -- during addon load, just as the client does.
+    for i = #exports, 1, -1 do exports[i] = nil end
+    MyslotExports["exports"] = exports
+    MyslotExports["backups"] = {}
+    seeded_names, seeded_name_set = {}, {}
+    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
+        local name = e.name
+        seeded_names[#seeded_names + 1] = name
+        seeded_name_set[name] = true
+        if e.class then
+            create_saved_profile(name, e.value or name, e.class)
+        else
+            exports[#exports + 1] = { name = name, value = e.value or name }
+        end
+    end
+    MyslotExports = MyslotExports or {}
+    MyslotExports["exports"] = exports
+    MyslotExports["backups"] = {}
+    MyslotSettings = MyslotSettings or {}
+    return exports
+end
+
+local function has_seeded_item(menu)
+    local seen = {}
+    local function visit(desc)
+        if not desc or seen[desc] then return false end
+        seen[desc] = true
+        for _, child in ipairs(desc.children or {}) do
+            if seeded_name_set[plain_text(child:GetText())] then
+                return true
+            end
+            local sub = child:Sub()
+            if sub and visit(sub) then return true end
+        end
+        return false
+    end
+    return visit(menu)
+end
+
+-- Find the selector by what it does: a click opens the menu containing the
+-- saved names seeded for this case. This permits standard button templates,
+-- legacy dropdown widgets, and other conforming controls.
+local function frame_shows_seeded_selection(frame)
+    if frame.GetText and seeded_name_set[plain_text(frame:GetText())] then return true end
+    local function belongs_to_frame(widget)
+        local parent = widget and widget.GetParent and widget:GetParent()
+        while parent do
+            if parent == frame then return true end
+            parent = parent.GetParent and parent:GetParent()
+        end
+        return false
+    end
+    for _, child in ipairs(_G.WowUiStub.frames) do
+        if child.kind == "FontString" and belongs_to_frame(child)
+            and seeded_name_set[plain_text(child:GetText())] then
+            return true
+        end
+    end
+    return false
+end
+
+local function discover_selector()
+    -- Candidate selection is based on the visible current-profile label, then
+    -- confirmed by opening the menu with saved rows. Other visible actions are
+    -- never clicked merely to probe them.
+    for _, frame in ipairs(_G.WowUiStub.frames) do
+        if frame.IsShown and frame:IsShown() and frame.IsEnabled and frame:IsEnabled()
+            and frame.GetScript and frame:GetScript("OnClick")
+            and frame_shows_seeded_selection(frame) then
+            _G.WowUiStub.last_menu = nil
+            local ok = pcall(function() frame:Click() end)
+            local opened = ok and _G.WowUiStub.last_menu or nil
+            if opened and has_seeded_item(opened) then
+                active_selector = frame
+                return opened
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    error("clicking the saved-profile selector did not open its saved-loadout menu")
+end
+
+local function open_menu()
+    if not active_selector then return discover_selector() end
+    _G.WowUiStub.last_menu = nil
+    active_selector:Click()
+    local menu = _G.WowUiStub.last_menu
+    T.assert.not_nil(menu, "clicking the saved-profile selector must open its menu")
+    T.assert.is_true(has_seeded_item(menu),
+        "the selector menu must contain saved loadout entries")
+    return menu
+end
+
+local function find_descendant(menu, predicate)
+    local seen = {}
+    local function visit(desc)
+        if not desc or seen[desc] then return nil end
+        seen[desc] = true
+        for _, child in ipairs(desc.children or {}) do
+            if predicate(child) then return child end
+            local sub = child:Sub()
+            if sub then
+                local found = visit(sub)
+                if found then return found end
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    return visit(menu)
+end
+
+local function find_sort_choice(menu, mode)
+    local choice = find_descendant(menu, function(child)
+        if child:Title() or child:Divider() then return false end
+        local text = plain_text(child:GetText()):lower()
+        if text == mode or text == ("by " .. mode) then return true end
+        -- Control captions may include a harmless prefix such as "Sort:" or
+        -- "Sort by"; identify the requested choice by its visible mode word.
+        return text:find("sort", 1, true) ~= nil
+            and text:find(mode, 1, true) ~= nil
+    end)
+    T.assert.not_nil(choice, "selector must offer the " .. mode .. " sort choice")
+    return choice
+end
+
+local function choose_sort(menu, mode)
+    find_sort_choice(menu, mode):Click()
+    return _G.WowUiStub.last_menu or menu
+end
+
+local function find_filter(menu)
+    return find_descendant(menu, function(child)
+        local text = plain_text(child:GetText()):lower()
+        return text:find("my class", 1, true) ~= nil
+            and (text:find("only", 1, true) ~= nil or text:find("show", 1, true) ~= nil)
+    end)
+end

+local function set_filter(menu, desired)
+    local toggle = find_filter(menu)
+    T.assert.not_nil(toggle, "selector must offer an only-my-class filter toggle")
+    local function is_checked(widget)
+        if widget.IsChecked then return widget:IsChecked() and true or false end
+        if widget.IsSelected then return widget:IsSelected() and true or false end
+        return false
+    end
+    local checked = is_checked(toggle)
+    if checked ~= desired then
+        toggle:Click()
+        menu = _G.WowUiStub.last_menu or menu
+        toggle = find_filter(menu)
+        T.assert.not_nil(toggle, "filter toggle remains available after changing it")
+    end
+    local checked_after = is_checked(toggle)
+    T.assert.equal(desired, checked_after, "filter reaches the explicitly requested state")
+    return menu
+end

+local function find_profile(menu, name)
+    return find_descendant(menu, function(child)
+        return plain_text(child:GetText()) == name
+    end)
+end

+local function find_profiles(menu, name)
+    local found, seen, seen_children = {}, {}, {}
+    local function visit(desc)
+        if not desc or seen[desc] then return end
+        seen[desc] = true
+        for _, child in ipairs(desc.children or {}) do
+            if not seen_children[child] then
+                seen_children[child] = true
+                if plain_text(child:GetText()) == name then found[#found + 1] = child end
+                local sub = child:Sub()
+                if sub then visit(sub) end
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    visit(menu)
+    return found
+end

+-- Visible loadout entries (no controls or headings), in displayed order.
+-- Labels are observed independently of MenuDescription element type and depth.
+local function menu_view(menu)
+    local names, seen, seen_children = {}, {}, {}
+    local function visit(desc)
+        if not desc or seen[desc] then return end
+        seen[desc] = true
+        for _, child in ipairs(desc.children or {}) do
+            if not seen_children[child] then
+                seen_children[child] = true
+                local text = plain_text(child:GetText())
+                if seeded_name_set[text] then names[#names + 1] = text end
+                local sub = child:Sub()
+                if sub then visit(sub) end
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    visit(menu)
+    return names
+end
+
+local function is_menu_control(text)
+    local lower = plain_text(text):lower()
+    -- Captions describe the menu rather than selectable saved loadouts.
+    if lower:find("sort", 1, true) or lower:find("filter", 1, true) then return true end
+    if lower:find("only my class", 1, true) or lower:find("show my class", 1, true) then return true end
+    return lower == "before last import" or lower == "loadout" or lower == "loadouts"
+        or lower == "saved loadouts" or lower == "profile" or lower == "profiles"
+end
+
+-- Collect visible rows and possible headings in display order. Unrecognized
+-- captions are deliberately retained here; checks below associate the
+-- headings that identify class groups without requiring captions to be absent.
+local function class_menu_rows(menu)
+    local rows, seen, seen_children = {}, {}, {}
+    local function visit(desc)
+        if not desc or seen[desc] then return end
+        seen[desc] = true
+        for _, child in ipairs(desc.children or {}) do
+            if not seen_children[child] then
+                seen_children[child] = true
+                local text = plain_text(child:GetText())
+                if seeded_name_set[text] then
+                    rows[#rows + 1] = { kind = "item", text = text }
+                elseif text ~= "" and not is_menu_control(text) then
+                    rows[#rows + 1] = { kind = "header", text = text }
+                end
+                local sub = child:Sub()
+                if sub then visit(sub) end
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    visit(menu)
+    return rows
+end

+local function localized_class_label(token)
+    local labels = _G.LOCALIZED_CLASS_NAMES_MALE
+    if labels and labels[token] and labels[token] ~= "" then return tostring(labels[token]) end
+    return token
+end
+
+local function contains_label(haystack, needle)
+    haystack, needle = plain_text(haystack):lower(), plain_text(needle):lower()
+    return needle ~= "" and haystack:find(needle, 1, true) ~= nil
+end

+local CLASS_TOKENS = {
+    "WARRIOR", "PALADIN", "HUNTER", "ROGUE", "PRIEST", "DEATHKNIGHT",
+    "SHAMAN", "MAGE", "WARLOCK", "MONK", "DRUID", "DEMONHUNTER", "EVOKER",

+local function header_identifies(text, token)
+    local label = localized_class_label(token)
+    return contains_label(text, label) or contains_label(text, token)
+end

+local function header_is_real_class(text)
+    for _, token in ipairs(CLASS_TOKENS) do

+    end
+    return false
+end

+local function assert_names_unordered(expected, actual, message)

+-- CI-only loader for the addon's interface files (event.lua, gui.lua,
+-- options.lua), which ci/loader.lua deliberately skips. Requires
+-- tests/helpers/ui_stubs.lua to have been dofile'd first: it replaces the
+-- event plumbing (event.lua is NOT loaded; regevent/firing is provided via
+-- _G.WowUiStub.framer) and then executes the remaining interface files with
+-- the same (addon_name, shared_table) varargs WoW provides.
+--
+-- Loading is lazy: the files must only be read after the caller has written
+-- fresh saved variables via WowUiStub.WriteDefaults(), because the interface
+-- reads them at ADDON_LOADED dispatch time only, but the scripts themselves
+-- must only ever be executed once per process (their frames are upvalues).
+
+local ADDON_NAME = "Myslot"
+local REPO_ROOT = (arg and arg[0] and arg[0]:match("(.-)[/\\][^/\\]+$") or ".") .. "/.."
+
+local Ui = assert(_G.WowUiStub, "load tests/helpers/ui_stubs.lua before tests/helpers/ui_loader.lua")
+
+local loaded = false
+
+local function load_chunk(path, MySlot)
+    local chunk, err = loadfile(REPO_ROOT .. "/" .. path)
+    if not chunk then
+        io.stderr:write("loadfile failed: " .. path .. ": " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
+        os.exit(2)
+    end
+    local ok, runerr = pcall(chunk, ADDON_NAME, MySlot)
+    if not ok then
+        io.stderr:write("execute failed: " .. path .. ": " .. tostring(runerr) .. "\n")
+        os.exit(2)
+    end
+end
+
+-- Registers a callback for a script event and remembers it on
+-- WowUiStub.framer so headless tests can dispatch it.
+local function make_regevent(MySlot)
+    MySlot.regevent = function(event, cb)
+        local fr = Ui.framer
+        if not fr.cbs[event] then fr.cbs[event] = {} end
+        fr:RegisterEvent(event)
+        fr.cbs[event][#fr.cbs[event] + 1] = cb
+    end
+end
+
+-- Fire an event exactly as the WoW client would: each registered callback
+-- is invoked with the event payload. ADDON_LOADED receives the addon name.
+local function fire(MySlot, event, ...)
+    local fr = Ui.framer
+    local cbs = fr.cbs[event]
+    if not cbs then return end
+    for _, cb in pairs(cbs) do
+        if event == "ADDON_LOADED" then
+            cb(...)
+        else
+            cb(...)
+        end
+    end
+end
+
+-- Load event-free interface scripts once, then partition event dispatch.
+local function ensure_loaded(MySlot)
+    if loaded then return end
+    loaded = true
+    make_regevent(MySlot)
+    -- event.lua is replaced by the WowUiStub.framer plumbing above; loading
+    -- it would try to build a real frame dispatch chain. The remaining
+    -- interface files are pure WoW-widget construction against ui_stubs.
+    load_chunk("gui.lua", MySlot)
+    load_chunk("options.lua", MySlot)
+end
+
+-- Boot the addon interface exactly as the client does: dispatch ADDON_LOADED
+-- with this addon's name so the deferred initializers run.
+local function addon_loaded(MySlot)
+    ensure_loaded(MySlot)
+    fire(MySlot, "ADDON_LOADED", ADDON_NAME)
+end
+
+return {
+    ensure_loaded = ensure_loaded,
+    addon_loaded = addon_loaded,
+    fire = fire,
+}

+OPTION_SHOW_ACTION_BAR = OPTION_SHOW_ACTION_BAR or "Action Bar %d"
+OPTION_TOOLTIP_SHOW_ACTION_BAR = OPTION_SHOW_ACTION_BAR
+ACTION_BAR_LABEL = ACTION_BAR_LABEL or "Action Bars"

+CHARACTER_SPECIFIC_BINDINGS = CHARACTER_SPECIFIC_BINDINGS or "Character Specific Bindings"

+function Ui.reset()
+    Ui.frames = {}
+    Ui.cmds = {}
+    Ui.popup_shown = {}
+    Ui.last_menu = nil
+    Ui.framer.registered = {}
+    Ui.framer.cbs = {}
+    -- Reset preferences without naming implementation-specific SavedVariable
+    -- keys. Preserve the table identity because loaded interface code may hold
+    -- a reference to it; the next ADDON_LOADED callback recreates defaults.
+    local function clear_saved_variables(saved)
+        if saved then
+            for key in pairs(saved) do saved[key] = nil end
+        end
+    end
+    clear_saved_variables(MyslotSettings)
+    clear_saved_variables(MyslotExports)
+end
+
+-- Write a fresh, deterministic set of saved variables for the addon under
+-- test. Mirrors what an ADDON_LOADED of a character on first login would
+-- have written (empty containers only); ui_stubs does not seed any
+-- sort/filter preference keys, so defaults come from the addon itself.
+function Ui.WriteDefaults(player_class)
+    MyslotExports = MyslotExports or {}
+    MyslotExports["exports"] = MyslotExports["exports"] or {}
+    MyslotExports["backups"] = MyslotExports["backups"] or {}
+    MyslotSettings = MyslotSettings or {}
+    MyslotSettings.minimap = MyslotSettings.minimap or { hide = false }
+    return MyslotExports, MyslotSettings
+end
+
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Legacy UIDropDownMenu API (pre-8.x style). These are FUNCTIONAL stand-ins
+-- on the same headless menu-description model used by the modern
+-- MenuUtil/Menu path, so a loadout selector implemented with either widget
+-- toolkit produces an observable menu of entries under the harness.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+local legacy_state = { target = nil }
+
+-- Record a frame as the current candidate for the loadout selector's legacy
+-- dropdown. Called by CreateFrame on the UIDropDownMenu template and by the
+-- Initialize/Set* entry points below.
+function UIDropDownMenu_RegisterTarget(t) legacy_state.target = t end
+
+-- Open/build the target's menu: run its initializer (which declares entries
+-- through UIDropDownMenu_AddButton) and publish the resulting description as
+-- the currently open menu.
+function legacy_build_menu(t)
+    t = t or legacy_state.target
+    if not (t and t.legacy_init) then return nil end
+    local desc = setmetatable({ children = {}, owner_widget = t, menu_mode = true }, MenuDesc)
+    t.legacy_menu = desc
+    -- The refreshed description closes over itself; MenuDesc:refresh() calls
+    -- root.rebuild() with no argument, so rebuild must not take parameters.
+    desc.rebuild = function()
+        desc.children = {}
+        legacy_state.target = t
+        t.legacy_init(t)
+    end
+    desc.owner_widget = t
+    t.legacy_init(t)
+    Ui.last_menu = desc
+    return desc
+end
+
+function UIDropDownMenu_CreateInfo() return {} end
+
+function UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(t, fn)
+    UIDropDownMenu_RegisterTarget(t)
+    t.legacy_init = fn
+end
+
+-- Classify legacy button text so flat legacy menus produce the same
+-- observable control surface as nested modern menus: a known sort ordering
+-- label ("By date" / "By name" / "By class") is a Radio() child under the
+-- selector's own sort section (reachable through the sort section's :Sub()),
+-- and an only-my-class toggle is Checkable(). This matches the classic
+-- UIDropDownMenu visual contract (checked = round radio dot vs square
+-- toggle) and lets behavior stay addressable regardless of widget toolkit.
+local function legacy_strip(text)
+    return tostring(text or ""):lower()
+        :gsub("|[tT][^|]*|t", ""):gsub("|c%x*", ""):gsub("|r", "")
+        :match("^%s*(.-)%s*$")
+end
+
+local function legacy_classify(plain)
+    if plain == "by date" or plain == "by name" or plain == "by class"
+        or plain == "date" or plain == "name" then
+        return "radio"
+    end
+    if plain:find("only my class", 1, true) then
+        return "checkbox"
+    end
+    return nil
+end
+
+function UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info)
+    local t = legacy_state.target
+    if not (t and t.legacy_menu and type(info) == "table") then return end
+    local kind = "button"
+    if info.isTitle then kind = "title" end
+    -- Wrap the handler so it honours the classic handler contract the addon's
+    -- own interface code relies on: the callback receives a control carrying
+    -- the entry's declared value (info.value / arg1) instead of nothing.
+    local func, value = info.func, info.value
+    if value == nil then value = info.arg1 end
+    local handler
+    if func then
+        -- Classic UIDropDownMenu handlers read .value (and arg1/arg2) off
+        -- the clicked control; dispatch with a control table so the base
+        -- addon's own onclick-self.value calling convention works.
+        handler = function()
+            return func({ value = value }, info.arg1, info.arg2)
+        end
+    end
+    local menu = t.legacy_menu
+    local el
+    local plain = legacy_strip(info.text)
+    local shape = (kind == "button") and legacy_classify(plain) or nil
+    local function checked()
+        local value = info.checked
+        if type(value) == "function" then value = value(info) end
+        return value and true or false
+    end
+    if shape == "radio" then
+        -- Nest under the sort section: reuse the enclosing sort title when
+        -- one exists (legacy models add e.g. a "Sort loadouts" section
+        -- title), else reuse/create a "Sort by" group.
+        local host
+        local seen_title = false
+        for _, c in ipairs(menu.children) do
+            if c.kind == "title" and c.text:lower():find("sort", 1, true) then
+                host = c
+                seen_title = true
+                break
+            end
+        end
+        if not host then
+            host = menu:Child("Sort by")
+        end
+        if not host then
+            host = menu:CreateButton("Sort by")
+        end
+        el = host:CreateRadio(info.text or "", checked, handler)
+    elseif shape == "checkbox" then
+        el = menu:CreateCheckbox(info.text or "", checked, handler)
+    else
+        el = menu:CreateButton(info.text or "", handler)
+        el.kind = kind
+    end
+    if info.value ~= nil then el.legacy_value = info.value end
+end
+
+function ToggleDropDownMenu(_, _, t) legacy_build_menu(t) end
+function CloseDropDownMenus() Ui.last_menu = nil end
+
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetSelectedValue(t, v)
+    UIDropDownMenu_RegisterTarget(t)
+    t.selected_value = v
+end
+function UIDropDownMenu_GetSelectedValue(t) return t.selected_value end
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetSelectedID() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetSelectedName() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetText(t, s)
+    UIDropDownMenu_RegisterTarget(t)
+    Widget.SetText(t, s)
+end
+
+-- Cosmetic / layout entry points carry no observable list state.
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetWidth() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_JustifyText() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_RefreshAll() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_EnableButton() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_DisableButton() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_SetButtonText() end
+function UIDropDownMenu_ClearAll() end

problem_statement:
[ML 0.1/UI.04.2] - Implement legacy message list loading bridge
## Blocked by

- #10774

## Description
Implement the bridge between the legacy message loading system and the Compose UI. This includes creating the `LegacyMessageListBridge` interface, the `LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect` that invokes the bridge to load messages from the legacy data source, and the mapping from `MessageListItem` to `MessageItemUi`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `LegacyMessageListBridge` interface defined in the API module.
- `LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect` loads messages from legacy and maps them to `MessageItemUi`.
- `MessageItemUi` includes `messageReference` for identifying messages.
- `MessageListFragment` implements the bridge, converting `MessageListItem` -> `MessageItemUi`.
- Manual refresh on sort criteria change is removed (handled by bridge).
- Action mode finish is guarded to only trigger when inactive and no messages are selected.
- New state feature is enabled alongside Compose for message list items.
- Unit tests for `LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect`.

### Additional contract requirements

The Compose message list loading contract is extended as follows:

- `UpdateLoadingProgress` carries the messages loaded so far in addition to its 0.0-1.0 progress value. In `LoadingMessages`, a value of 1.0 finishes loading and displays those messages; lower values retain the loading state with the supplied progress and messages.
- `net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.ui.legacy.LegacyMessageListBridge` is the integration seam for legacy loading. Its `loadMessages(MessageListPreferences, MessageListMetadata)` function returns a cold `Flow<List<MessageItemUi>>` for the current inputs.
- The bridge is consumed by `LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect.Factory` at `net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.internal.ui.state.sideeffect.legacy`. The factory accepts a logger and bridge and creates a message-list state-side-effect handler from a coroutine scope, event dispatcher, and UI-effect dispatcher. The application's state-side-effect wiring registers that factory.
- Entering the loading state starts one bridge load using the current preferences and metadata. A trigger that does not enter loading starts none. Every bridge emission is forwarded as `UpdateLoadingProgress`: 1.0 for a non-empty list and 0.0 for an empty list, preserving the emitted list. A new load cancels an active prior load. Failures are logged and do not crash the state machine.
- `MessageItemUi.messageReference` identifies the underlying legacy message.

+import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope

+import net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.ui.state.sideeffect.MessageListStateSideEffectHandlerFactory
+
+private const val TAG = "LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect"
+
+/**
+ * Side effect handler responsible for loading messages through the legacy message list bridge.
+ *
+ * @property scope The coroutine scope in which the message loading operation will be launched
+ * @property logger Logger instance for tracking loading operations and debugging
+ * @property legacyBridge Bridge to the legacy message list system for loading messages
+ * @property dispatch Function to dispatch events back to the state machine
+ */
+internal class LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect(
+    private val scope: CoroutineScope,
+    private val logger: Logger,
+    private val legacyBridge: LegacyMessageListBridge,
+    dispatch: suspend (MessageListEvent) -> Unit,
+) : MessageListStateSideEffectHandler(logger, dispatch) {
+    private var running: Job? = null
+    override fun accept(event: MessageListEvent, oldState: MessageListState, newState: MessageListState): Boolean =
+        oldState != newState && newState is MessageListState.LoadingMessages
+
+    override suspend fun consume(
+        event: MessageListEvent,
+        oldState: MessageListState,
+        newState: MessageListState,
+    ): ConsumeResult {
+        if (newState !is MessageListState.LoadingMessages) return ConsumeResult.Ignored
+        running?.cancel()
+        running = legacyBridge
+            .loadMessages(newState.preferences, newState.metadata)
+            .onEach { messages ->
+                logger.verbose(TAG) { "LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect.handle() messages: $messages" }
+                // this is oversimplified as we currently don't track the loading progress
+                // in the legacy implementation.
+                val progress = if (messages.isEmpty()) 0f else 1f
+                dispatch(MessageListEvent.UpdateLoadingProgress(progress = progress, messages = messages))
+            }
+            .onCompletion { running = null }
+            .catch { throwable ->
+                logger.error(TAG) { "LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect failed: $throwable" }
+            }
+            .launchIn(scope)
+        return ConsumeResult.Consumed
+    }
+
+    class Factory(
+        private val logger: Logger,
+        private val legacyBridge: LegacyMessageListBridge,
+    ) : MessageListStateSideEffectHandlerFactory {
+        override fun create(
+            scope: CoroutineScope,
+            dispatch: suspend (MessageListEvent) -> Unit,
+            dispatchUiEffect: suspend (MessageListEffect) -> Unit,
+        ): MessageListStateSideEffectHandler = LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect(
+            scope = scope,
+            logger = logger,
+            legacyBridge = legacyBridge,
+            dispatch = dispatch,
+        )
+    }
+}

+    private fun MessageListScope.handleMessageListEffect(effect: MessageListEffect) {
+        when (effect) {
+            is MessageListEffect.ScrollToMessage -> scrollToMessage(effect.message)
+            is MessageListEffect.UpdateToolbarActionMode -> {
+                println(
+                    "[MessageList] UpdateToolbarActionMode called with title: ${effect.title}, state = $stateSnapshot",
+                )
+                if (actionMode == null) {
+                    startAndPrepareActionMode()
+                }
+                actionMode?.let { actionMode ->
+                    actionMode.title = effect.title
+                    actionModeCallback.showSelectAll(!effect.isAllSelected)
+                    actionMode.invalidate()
+                }
+            }
+
+            is MessageListEffect.ResetToolbarActionMode -> {
+                println("[MessageList] ResetToolbarActionMode called with state = $stateSnapshot")
+                resetActionMode()
+            }
+
+            is MessageListEffect.RefreshMessageList -> {
+                val (primarySortType, secondarySortType) = effect.currentState.metadata.currentSortCriteria
+                val (sortType, sortAscending) = primarySortType.toDomainSortType()
+                updateCurrentSortCriteria(
+                    sortType = sortType,
+                    sortAscending = sortAscending,
+                    sortDateAscending = when (primarySortType) {
+                        SortType.DateAsc -> true
+                        SortType.DateDesc -> false
+                        else -> secondarySortType == SortType.DateAsc
+                    },
+                )

+            }
+
+            is MessageListEffect.OpenMessage -> {
+                val messageReference = checkNotNull(MessageReference.parse(effect.message.messageReference)) {
+                    "The message reference should not be null when opening a message. Message: $effect"
+                }
+                openMessage(messageReference)
+            }
+
+            else -> Unit
+        }
+    }

+            .filter { method -> method.parameterCount == 0 && List::class.java.isAssignableFrom(method.returnType) }
+            .sortedBy { method -> if (method.name == "getMessages") 0 else 1 }
+            .map { method -> method.invoke(update) as? List<MessageItemUi> }
+            .firstOrNull()
+            ?: error("The loading-progress event must expose the carried messages through a public list getter.")
+
+    /**
+     * Creates a fixture from the public data-class property names, not constructor positions.
+     *
+     * The public contract requires the message item to carry a reference identifying it in the
+     * legacy data source, but does not pin the type of that reference. The reference property is
+     * therefore filled with a value built for its declared constructor parameter type: identity
+     * strings stay strings, while a legacy reference object is created through its public factory
+     * (or primary constructor) so the identity round-trip documented in the contract is preserved.
+     */
+    private fun createMessage(id: String): MessageItemUi {
+        val account = Account(AccountIdFactory.of("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"), Color.Unspecified)
+        val constructor = requireNotNull(MessageItemUi::class.primaryConstructor)
+        val values = mutableMapOf<String, Any?>(
+            "state" to MessageItemUi.State.Read,
+            "id" to id,
+            "account" to account,
+            "senders" to ComposedAddressUi(displayName = "Sender"),
+            "subject" to "Subject $id",
+            "excerpt" to "Excerpt $id",
+            "formattedReceivedAt" to "Now",
+            "hasAttachments" to false,
+            "starred" to false,
+            "encrypted" to false,
+            "answered" to false,
+            "forwarded" to false,
+            "selected" to false,
+            "threadCount" to 0,
+            "active" to false,
+        )
+        val referenceParameter = constructor.parameters.firstOrNull { it.name in REFERENCE_PROPERTY_NAMES }
+        if (referenceParameter != null) {
+            values[requireNotNull(referenceParameter.name)] = buildMessageReferenceValue(id, referenceParameter.type)
+        }
+        return constructor.callBy(constructor.parameters.associateWith { parameter ->
+            values[parameter.name] ?: error("Missing public MessageItemUi property: ${parameter.name}")
+        })
+    }
+
+    /** Builds the legacy identity string used for the reference of a fixture message. */
+    private fun messageReferenceIdentity(id: String): String = "reference-$id"
+
+    /**
+     * The identity a reference carries for the contract assertion. Identity strings are compared
+     * as-is; a reference object of an arbitrary contract-conformant type is instead round-tripped
+     * through its public parse/toIdentityString contract so the comparison stays type-agnostic.
+     */
+    private fun messageReferenceIdentity(reference: Any?): String {
+        requireNotNull(reference) { "A message reference must not be null; it identifies the legacy message." }
+        if (reference is String) return reference
+        for (method in reference.javaClass.methods) {
+            if (method.name.equals("toIdentityString", ignoreCase = true) && method.parameterCount == 0) {
+                val identity = runCatching { method.invoke(reference) as? String }.getOrNull()
+                if (!identity.isNullOrEmpty()) return identity
+            }
+        }
+        error(
+            "The message reference (${reference.javaClass.name}) must either be an identity string or " +
+                "round-trip to one through toIdentityString() as documented.",
+        )
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Builds a value matching the declared reference property type so the fixture can be passed
+     * into the reflective data-class constructor. A String-typed reference receives the identity
+     * string directly; any other type is constructed via its public parse()/valueOf()/constructor
+     * from the same identity when possible, so the retained identifier round-trips to the fixture
+     * identity used by the assertions.
+     */
+    private fun buildMessageReferenceValue(id: String, referenceType: KType): Any? {
+        val rawClass = ((referenceType.classifier as? KClass<*>)?.java)
+            ?: error("The message-reference property must declare a class type, but was: $referenceType")
+        if (rawClass == String::class.java) return messageReferenceIdentity(id)
+        val identity = buildFixtureIdentity(rawClass, id)
+        return invokeStaticFactory(rawClass, listOf("parse", "valueOf", "of"), String::class.java, identity)
+            ?: runCatching { rawClass.getConstructor(String::class.java).newInstance(identity) }.getOrNull()
+            ?: error(
+                "Cannot build a message reference of type ${rawClass.name}: it must accept the " +
+                    "identity string through a public static parse(), valueOf(), of(), or a public String constructor.",
+            )
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * The identity passed into the fixture reference. For the bundled legacy reference type the
+     * identity must be parseable by its own parser (which only consumes the toIdentityString()
+     * envelope), because that parser rejects free-form strings; for every other type a plain
+     * assertion identity string is used. Both round-trip to the same comparison identity.
+     */
+    private fun buildFixtureIdentity(referenceClass: Class<*>, id: String): String =
+        if (referenceClass.name == LEGACY_MESSAGE_REFERENCE_CLASS) {
+            val reference = referenceClass.getConstructor(
+                String::class.java,
+                Long::class.javaPrimitiveType,
+                String::class.java,
+            ).newInstance("fixture-account", 1L, messageReferenceIdentity(id))
+            referenceClass.getMethod("toIdentityString").invoke(reference) as String
+        } else {
+            messageReferenceIdentity(id)
+        }
+
+    private fun invokeStaticFactory(
+        target: Class<*>,
+        names: List<String>,
+        parameterType: Class<*>,
+        argument: Any?,
+    ): Any? =
+        target.methods
+            .firstOrNull { method ->
+                java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isStatic(method.modifiers) &&
+                    names.any { method.name.equals(it, ignoreCase = true) } &&
+                    method.parameterTypes.size == 1 &&
+                    method.parameterTypes[0].isAssignableFrom(parameterType)
+            }
+            ?.invoke(null, argument)
+
+    /** Reads the documented legacy reference of a message item, whichever property name carries it. */
+    private fun readMessageReference(message: MessageItemUi): Any? = sequenceOf("messageReference", "reference")
+        .mapNotNull { name -> message.readProperty(name) }
+        .firstOrNull()
+        ?: error(
+            "A message item must expose the reference identifying it in the legacy data source, " +
+                "but no readable message-reference property was found on ${message.javaClass.name}.",
+        )
+
+    private fun MessageItemUi.readProperty(propertyName: String): Any? = runCatching {
+        val capitalized = propertyName.replaceFirstChar { it.uppercaseChar() }
+        val getter = javaClass.methods.firstOrNull { method ->
+            method.parameterCount == 0 && method.name.equals("get$capitalized", ignoreCase = true)
+        } ?: return null
+        getter.invoke(this)
+    }.getOrNull()
+
+    // endregion
+
+}

+/**
+ * A one-way cancellation marker that can be awaited without racing the test-scheduler drain: the
+ * deferred is completed eagerly, so a later await never depends on the test body's own turn.
+ */
+private class AwaitableBoolean {
+    private val signal = CompletableDeferred<Unit>()
+
+    fun mark() {
+        signal.complete(Unit)
+    }
+
+    suspend fun await(): Boolean {
+        signal.await()
+        return true
+    }
+}

+/**
+ * Adapter for the explicit bridge/factory seam. The new public types are loaded by their
+ * documented names so this source can also compile on the revision before they were introduced.
+ */
+private object LegacyLoadingContract {
+    private const val BRIDGE_CLASS =
+        "net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.ui.legacy.LegacyMessageListBridge"
+    private const val FACTORY_CLASS =
+        "net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.internal.ui.state.sideeffect.legacy." +
+            "LoadMessagesLegacySideEffect\$Factory"
+
+    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+    fun createHandler(
+        scope: kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope,
+        logger: TestLogger,
+        bridge: Any,
+        onDispatch: (MessageListEvent) -> Unit,
+    ): StateSideEffectHandler<MessageListState, MessageListEvent, *> {
+        val bridgeType = Class.forName(BRIDGE_CLASS)
+        val bridgeProxy = Proxy.newProxyInstance(bridgeType.classLoader, arrayOf(bridgeType)) { _, method, arguments ->
+            when (method.name) {
+                "loadMessages" -> bridge.javaClass.getMethod("loadMessages", Any::class.java, Any::class.java)
+                    .invoke(bridge, arguments?.get(0), arguments?.get(1))
+                "toString" -> "RecordingLegacyMessageListBridge"
+                "hashCode" -> System.identityHashCode(bridge)
+                "equals" -> bridge === arguments?.get(0)
+                else -> error("Unexpected LegacyMessageListBridge method: ${method.name}")
+            }
+        }
+        val factoryType = Class.forName(FACTORY_CLASS)
+        val factory = factoryType.getDeclaredConstructor(Logger::class.java, bridgeType)
+            .newInstance(logger, bridgeProxy)
+        val dispatch: suspend (MessageListEvent) -> Unit = { event -> onDispatch(event) }
+        val dispatchUiEffect: suspend (MessageListEffect) -> Unit = {}
+        val handler = factoryType.getMethod(
+            "create",
+            kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope::class.java,
+            kotlin.jvm.functions.Function2::class.java,
+            kotlin.jvm.functions.Function2::class.java,
+        ).invoke(factory, scope, dispatch, dispatchUiEffect)
+        return handler as? StateSideEffectHandler<MessageListState, MessageListEvent, *>
+            ?: error("The documented legacy-loading factory must create a state side-effect handler.")
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Whether the application exposes the legacy-loading seam consumed by its registered
+     * state-side-effect wiring. A classpath-width probe is used because the application
+     * registration module lives outside this test classpath.
+     */
+    fun registrationSeamPresent(): Boolean =
+        runCatching { Class.forName(FACTORY_CLASS) }.isSuccess ||
+            runCatching {
+                Class.forName(
+                    "net.thunderbird.feature.mail.message.list.internal.ui.state.sideeffect.inject." +
+                        "MessageListSideEffectsModuleKt",
+                )
+            }.isSuccess
+
+}

Adapting an equation must convert its user-entered real-valued parameters to the requested real type across equation families, not only for compressible Euler. If an equation contains a user-supplied callable field, the adapted equation must retain a usable callable.

+    @timed_testset "Adapt user-entered equation parameters" begin
+        # The parameter must follow the requested real type, not its original type.
+        equations_euler = CompressibleEulerEquations2D(1.4)

+        @test eltype(adapted_multicomponent.gammas) === Float32

## Describe the bug
Fail to connect v6 server if no app password set error check ip/port.
(App password, not API password)

## To Reproduce
Try to connect a server and leave app password blank empty


## Expected behavior
When try to connect v6 pihole server with no app password set. App returns a misleading error "failed to connect. Check IP and Port"

There was nothing wrong with IP port.
Solution was to set the app password in terminal:

pihole setpassword PASSWORD

After using this password connected immediately.

Please check error notification logic and separate wrong password message from IP/Port check error. It's confusing to users.


## Screenshots


## Environments
 - Device: any
 - OS: android 16
 - Browser: mobile app android
 - Browser Version: 
 - Pi-hole Client Version: latest 1.9.2
 - Pi-hole Version: 6.3

### Additional contract requirements

Pi-hole v6 servers can be configured without an app password ("no password set").
The following observable behavior is required:

- A Pi-hole v6 server with no configured app password answers the
  authentication endpoint with a valid sign-in response whose session
  carries no credential values (they are absent or null) and a message such
  as "no password set". Treating such a response as valid or connected must
  never crash or fail merely because those credential fields are empty.
- Connecting to a Pi-hole v6 server while leaving the app password blank must
  succeed when the server is reachable and reports that no authentication is
  required. The user must see the normal successful-connection feedback, not
  an error snackbar, and the connection must be treated as established
  without depending on a stored session credential. When the user later
  performs actions that need a session on such a password-less connection,
  the app must behave as if no session credential is needed rather than
  surfacing a missing-credential error.
- When editing an existing v6 connection, clearing the app password field is
  a valid state: the save action must remain enabled so that a password-less
  connection can be saved.
- Connection failures must be reported with feedback that distinguishes their
  cause. A rejected app password must surface authentication feedback that
  clearly refers to the password, while an unreachable host or wrong
  address/port must surface address/port (connectivity) feedback. It is not
  acceptable to show an IP/port error message when authentication alone
  failed, nor a password error for a connection that could not be reached.
  No specific message wording or localization keys are required.
- A successful authenticated sign-in that returns session credentials
  continues to establish and reuse a session as before, and network-layer
  failures (socket errors, timeouts, unreachable hosts) continue to surface
  connectivity error feedback unchanged.

problem_statement:
Group capacity limit for available units
### Description

Current the [group capacity limit](https://tulipaenergy.github.io/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/stable/40-scientific-foundation/40-formulation/#investment-group-constraints) applies only to the investments per milestone year , it would be useful to have another constraint (or change the existing?) to limit the available units per milestone year.

### Validation and testing

_No response_

### Motivation

Previous discussions
- https://github.com/TulipaEnergy/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/issues/1299#issuecomment-3135218970
- https://github.com/TulipaEnergy/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/issues/1299#issuecomment-3139071018
- https://github.com/TulipaEnergy/TulipaEnergyModel.jl/issues/1299#issuecomment-3139084985

### Target audience

users

### Can you help?

always

### Additional contract requirements

# Investment-group limit methods

`investment_group_asset.invest_method` is a text field with one of these values:

- `use_only_investment_units` limits the weighted investment units of the group's
  members in the row's milestone year.
- `use_available_units` limits the weighted available units of the group's members
  in that milestone year. Available units include units already in service and
  qualifying investments from relevant vintages.
- `none` disables the row; it creates no group limit.

The row's `constraint_sense`, `rhs`, and membership coefficients apply to the
selected quantity. An available-unit or disabled group may include an asset that
is not investable in that year. An investment-only group member must be
investable in the group year.

For input migration, map the former enabled value `true` to
`use_only_investment_units` and the former disabled value `false` to `none`.

+"""Migrate boolean invest_method values to investment-group methods."""
+
+import os
+
+import duckdb
+
+
+INPUTS = "test/inputs"
+BENCHMARK = "benchmark/EU"
+TUTORIALS = "docs/src/10-tutorials/my-awesome-energy-system"
+
+
+def migrate_folder(folder_path):
+    path = os.path.join(folder_path, "investment-group-asset.csv")
+    if not os.path.exists(path):
+        return
+
+    con = duckdb.connect()
+    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE investment_group_asset AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('{path}')")
+
+    columns = [row[0] for row in con.execute("DESCRIBE investment_group_asset").fetchall()]
+    if "invest_method" not in columns:
+        con.close()
+        return
+
+    legacy_count = con.execute(
+        """
+        SELECT COUNT(*)
+        FROM investment_group_asset
+        WHERE lower(CAST(invest_method AS VARCHAR)) IN ('true', 'false')
+        """
+    ).fetchone()[0]
+    if legacy_count == 0:
+        con.close()
+        return
+
+    con.execute(
+        f"""
+        COPY (
+            SELECT * REPLACE (
+                CASE lower(CAST(invest_method AS VARCHAR))
+                    WHEN 'true' THEN 'use_only_investment_units'
+                    WHEN 'false' THEN 'none'
+                    ELSE CAST(invest_method AS VARCHAR)
+                END AS invest_method
+            )
+            FROM investment_group_asset
+        ) TO '{path}' (HEADER, DELIMITER ',')
+        """
+    )
+    print(f"{folder_path}: migrated {legacy_count} invest_method values")
+    con.close()
+
+
+for folder in sorted(os.listdir(INPUTS)):
+    migrate_folder(os.path.join(INPUTS, folder))
+
+migrate_folder(BENCHMARK)
+
+for folder in sorted(os.listdir(TUTORIALS)):
+    migrate_folder(os.path.join(TUTORIALS, folder))

+@testitem "Available-unit groups include only qualifying prior vintages" setup =
+    [CommonSetup, ConsInvestmentGroupSetup] tags = [:integration, :constraint, :fast] begin
+    # Only schema-documented tables are populated by hand, mirroring the other
+    # constraint tests that construct DuckDB fixtures directly. The setup
+    # builds on the "Multi-year Investments" input data, whose documented
+    # columns carry the relevant semantics: the wind vintage commissioned in
+    # 2030 has a technical lifetime of 21 years, so 2050 is its final
+    # qualifying milestone year, and its investments are
+    # capped at zero, providing 0.02 units -> 1.0 production units at 50.0
+    # capacity; the ens asset holds exactly 1.0 unit in service in 2050 and
+    # is not investable there. A use_available_units group row over
+    # (wind, ens) with "==" 2.0 units can therefore be met exactly when the
+    # group limit counts the qualifying prior wind vintage alongside the
+    # in-service ens units. An implementation whose available-unit semantics
+    # do not count such prior vintages leaves the 2050 milestone infeasible,
+    # so the single solve below only terminates successfully when the
+    # semantics are valid.
+    connection = DBInterface.connect(DuckDB.DB)
+    _read_csv_folder(connection, joinpath(@__DIR__, "inputs", "Multi-year Investments"))
+    TEM.populate_with_defaults!(connection)
+    DuckDB.query(
+        connection,
+        "UPDATE asset SET technical_lifetime = 21 WHERE asset = 'wind'; UPDATE asset_milestone SET investable = false WHERE asset = 'wind' AND milestone_year = 2050;",
+    )
+
+    # Group tables follow the documented investment-group schema; wind uses
+    # compact_profiles and ens uses the aggregated available-unit expression.
+    DuckDB.query(
+        connection,
+        """
+        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE investment_group_asset (
+            name VARCHAR, milestone_year INT, invest_method VARCHAR,
+            constraint_sense VARCHAR, rhs DOUBLE
+        );
+        INSERT INTO investment_group_asset VALUES
+            ('prior_vintages', 2050, 'use_available_units', '==', 2.0);
+        CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE investment_group_asset_membership (
+            group_name VARCHAR, milestone_year INT, asset VARCHAR, coefficient DOUBLE
+        );
+        INSERT INTO investment_group_asset_membership VALUES
+            ('prior_vintages', 2050, 'wind', 50.0),
+            ('prior_vintages', 2050, 'ens', 1.0);
+        """,
+    )
+
+    energy_problem = try
+        problem = TEM.EnergyProblem(connection)
+        TEM.create_model!(problem)
+        problem
+    catch
+        nothing
+    end
+    @test energy_problem !== nothing
+    if !isnothing(energy_problem)
+        JuMP.set_optimizer(
+            energy_problem.model,
+        JuMP.optimizer_with_attributes(HiGHS.Optimizer, "output_flag" => false),
+    )
+        JuMP.optimize!(energy_problem.model)
+        @test JuMP.termination_status(energy_problem.model) == JuMP.OPTIMAL
+        group_row = only(_get_cons_object(energy_problem.model, :investment_group))
+        @test isapprox(JuMP.value(group_row.func), 0.0; atol=1e-6)
+        prior_wind = group_investment_variable(energy_problem, "wind", 2030)
+        @test isapprox(JuMP.coefficient(group_row.func, prior_wind), 50.0; atol=1e-8)
+    end
+end

problem_statement:
Track upvalue names in prototypes (for debug.getupvalue / setupvalue)
## Problem

`debug.getupvalue(f, n)` and `debug.setupvalue(f, n, v)` are stubbed to return nil. Implementing them requires knowing the *name* of each upvalue, which the compiler currently does not store on the `%Prototype{}`. As a result `locals.lua` is fully deferred — it expects `debug.getupvalue(load"a=3", 1)` to return `("_ENV", ...)`.

## Scope

1. Extend `%Lua.Compiler.Prototype{}`[HIDDEN].
2. `lib/lua/vm/stdlib/debug.ex`:
   - `debug.getupvalue({:lua_closure, proto, upvalues}, n)`[HIDDEN].
   - `debug.setupvalue(...)`[HIDDEN].
3. The chunk-level prototype's first upvalue is `_ENV`; verify the name is recorded correctly. Suite test `locals.lua:73` asserts exactly this.
4. While here: surface upvalue names in `Lua.VM.Display` / stack traces for better error reporting.

## Acceptance

- `debug.getupvalue(load"a=3", 1) == ("_ENV", _G)`.
- [HIDDEN]
- Unit tests in `test/lua/vm/stdlib/debug_test.exs` (new) covering name lookup, bounds, and the `_ENV` chunk-upvalue case.

### Additional contract requirements

These requirements are part of the observable contract for upvalue tracking and the debug library.

## Upvalue naming and ordering

- Every chunk-level function (any code loaded via `load`) has exactly one upvalue, named `_ENV`, at 1-based upvalue index 1.
- For nested closures, the captured `_ENV` is always upvalue index 1; explicitly captured locals follow as upvalues 2, 3, ... in their declaration order, using the captured variable's name. Example: within `local x = 10; local function outer() return function() return x end end`, the returned inner closure's upvalues are `"_ENV"` at index 1 and `"x"` at index 2.

## `load` with a custom environment

- `load(chunk [, chunkname [, mode [, env]]])` accepts an optional environment table as its fourth argument. That table becomes the loaded chunk's `_ENV` upvalue: `debug.getupvalue(f, 1)` on the loaded function returns `"_ENV"` together with a value that equals (is `==` to) the supplied table.
- Global writes performed by the loaded chunk are routed to the supplied environment: a later read of that name from the environment table returns the assigned value, while the name was absent from the table before the chunk ran. When no environment is supplied, the chunk's `_ENV` is the current global table `_G`.

## `debug.getupvalue(f, n)`

- For a Lua closure, `debug.getupvalue(f, n)` returns the upvalue's name and its current value, e.g. `debug.getupvalue(load"a=3", 1)` returns `"_ENV"` and a value equal to `_G`.
- An index beyond the closure's upvalue count returns `nil`.
- Calling it on a value that is not a Lua closure (e.g. a native function such as `print`, or a number) returns `nil`.

## `debug.setupvalue(f, n, v)`

- For a Lua closure with a valid 1-based upvalue index, `debug.setupvalue(f, n, v)` assigns `v` to that upvalue and returns the upvalue's name; subsequent reads of the upvalue observe the new value (e.g. setting upvalue 2 (`x`) of a closure to `99` makes the closure return `99`).
- An out-of-range index returns `nil` and must not modify any existing upvalue of the closure.
- Calling it on a value that is not a Lua closure returns `nil`.

## Closure display rendering

- Inspecting a returned closure wrapper includes its upvalue names when it has any: a closure with an `_ENV` upvalue renders exactly as `#Lua.Closure<source: "<eval>", line: 1, arity: 2, upvalues: [_ENV]>` (with the actual source and line reported by the evaluation context). The existing rendering fields (`source`, `line`, `arity`, and the `+...` variadic marker) are unchanged.

+    code = """
+    local name, val = debug.getupvalue(load"a=3", 1)
+    return name, val == _G

+
+    assert {["_ENV", true], _} = Lua.eval!(lua, code)

+    code = """
+    local c = {}
+    local f = load("a = 3", nil, nil, c)
+    local name, val = debug.getupvalue(f, 1)
+    local before = c.a
+    f()
+    return name, val == c, before, c.a
+    """
+
+    assert {["_ENV", true, nil, 3], _} = Lua.eval!(lua, code)
+  end
+

+    # Every nested function captures `_ENV` as upvalue 1; explicit captures
+    # follow in declaration order. `debug.getupvalue(_, 3)` is out of range.
+    code = """
+    local x = 10
+    local function outer() return function() return x end end
+    local inner = outer()
+    local env_name = debug.getupvalue(inner, 1)
+    local name, val = debug.getupvalue(inner, 2)
+    return env_name, name, val, debug.getupvalue(inner, 3)
+    """
+
+    assert {["_ENV", "x", 10, nil], _} = Lua.eval!(lua, code)
+  end
+

+    code = """
+    local x = 1
+    local function getx() return x end
+    local name = debug.setupvalue(getx, 2, 99)
+    return name, getx()
+    """

+  end

+    """

+

problem_statement:
Classify each block's route and blank span from the untyped syntax tree
## Parent

Sub-task of #96.

## What to build

`BlockLocator` decides how a Run will reach each `http { }` block in a script. The decision comes from the untyped syntax tree. It needs no type-check, no project load, and no NuGet resolution.

Each located block carries four new facts:

- the route: R1, R2 with the invocation it needs, or a refusal with its family and its reason,
- the span to blank when the block is **not** the target,
- the names of the enclosing nested modules, outermost first,
- the `private` keywords on the block's own path.

The `Statement` field and `enclosingStatementRange` go away. `BlockRunner` blanks the new `Blank` span in place of the `Statement` span.

A Run behaves as it behaves today after this ticket. This ticket produces the verdict only. The next ticket makes the Run consume it. The refusal-lens spec (#97) consumes the same verdict, which is why `classify` belongs beside the location that it reads.

The blank span is the smallest enclosing statement that can hold an expression. A module-level binding blanks its whole declaration, which keeps the value-leakage protection. A member or inner binding blanks its right side only, because a blanked `member _.Get() = …` leaves a type with no members, and that does not parse.

+        // value. What is left to decide is whether the binding is module-level: an inner `let`
+        // or a member is out of reach from a later FSI interaction.
+        let access = if access.IsSome then access else patternAccess headPat

+            | NeedsArguments ->

+            // invoke and no value the invocation could name. The spec's table has no row for this

+            | NoName -> Refused(ValueIsNotTheBlock, "the binding does not give a name to invoke"), access

+        | SyntaxNode.SynExpr(SynExpr.Lambda _) :: _ ->

+        | SyntaxNode.SynModule(SynModuleDecl.Let(range = r)) :: _ -> r

+              assertRoute 12 "#18 try/with handler (with handler)" (isRefused DecidedAtRunTime)
+              assertRoute 13 "#23 tuple binding (first element)" (isRefused ValueIsNotTheBlock)
+              assertRoute 14 "#23 tuple binding (second element)" (isRefused ValueIsNotTheBlock)
+              assertRoute 15 "#24 outer binding that holds a nested block" (isNamedByTheBinding "nested")
+              assertRoute 16 "#24 block inside another block's expression" (isRefused ValueIsNotTheBlock)
+              assertRoute 17 "sweeper block (structural, not a numbered position)" isNamedByTheRun
+              assertRoute 18 "module Tail bare block (boundary probe, not a numbered position)" isNamedByTheRun
+          }
+
+          test "extra.fsx: module bindings blank their complete declarations for tuple and control-flow values" {
+              let source = fixture "extra.fsx"
+              let blocks = locateBlocks source
+
+              for index, position, declarationStart in
+                  [ 13, "tuple binding first value", "let tupleA, tupleB ="
+                    14, "tuple binding second value", "let tupleA, tupleB ="
+                    9, "match clause first value", "let matched ="
+                    10, "match clause second value", "let matched =" ] do
+                  let blankText = slice source blocks.[index].Blank
+                  Expect.stringStarts blankText declarationStart (position + ": module binding blank starts with its declaration")
+                  Expect.isTrue (blankText.Contains (slice source blocks.[index].Block)) (position + ": blank includes its block")
+          }
+
+          // Positions 13 to 15 are the rows that exist to exercise `Qualifier` and
+          // `PrivateSpans`, so the route alone does not cover what the spec asks of them.
+          test "extra.fsx: the qualifier and the private spans match the enclosing module chain" {
+              let blocks = locateBlocks (fixture "extra.fsx")
+
+              let assertQualifier = assertQualifier blocks
+              let assertPrivateSpans = assertPrivateSpans blocks
+
+              assertQualifier 0 "#13 let private x = http { }" []
+              assertPrivateSpans 0 "#13 let private x = http { }" 1
+
+              assertPrivateSpans 1 "internal binding stays unblanked" 0
+
+              assertQualifier 2 "#14 module private, bare block" [ "Vault" ]
+              assertPrivateSpans 2 "#14 module private, bare block" 1
+
+              assertQualifier 3 "#15 nested modules, Outer.Inner.deep" [ "Outer"; "Inner" ]
+              assertPrivateSpans 3 "#15 nested modules, Outer.Inner.deep" 0
+
+              assertPrivateSpans 4 "#16 attributed private binding" 1
+
+              assertQualifier 18 "module Tail bare block" [ "Tail" ]
+          }

+          // Decision 6's second trap: "Locate the keyword. Do not assume its position -- an
+          // attributed binding's statement range starts at its attribute line." Slicing each
+          // span, not counting it, is what fails a declaration-range or attribute-offset span.
+          test "extra.fsx: each private span slices to the `private` keyword itself" {
+              let blocks = locateBlocks (fixture "extra.fsx")
+              let source = fixture "extra.fsx"

+              let sliceAt index position spanIndex =
+                  match List.tryItem index blocks with
+                  | None -> failtestf "%s: no block at index %d" position index

+// The shapes the twelve-case corpus does not have, plus both blanking hazards from Decision 5 of
+// docs/spec/0002-reach-a-block-anywhere.md, and an explicit probe for the Decision 1 truncation
+// boundary. Every block carries the verdict the spec's position table assigns it, so this file
+// can be read against the decision directly.
+//
+// Order matters: the last two blocks exist to be run *after* every hazard above them, so their
+// Setup has to blank all of it and still compile.
+
+#r "nuget: FsHttp, 15.0.3"
+
+open FsHttp
+open System
+
+
+// [13] private binding -- R2, with the `private` blanked to spaces rather than refused
+let private secret = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/secret" }
+
+
+// internal binding -- deliberately NOT blanked, because `accessRange` matches `private` only.
+// Decision 6 measured `internal` as accessible from a later interaction, so it needs no
+// treatment. This block is the guard on that measurement.
+let internal semiSecret = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/semi-secret" }
+
+
+// [14] bare block in a private module -- R1, with the module's `private` blanked one level up
+module private Vault =
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/vault" }
+
+
+// [15] nested modules -- R2, qualified by the enclosing module chain, outermost first
+module Outer =
+    module Inner =
+        let deep = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/deep" }
+
+
+// [16] attributed binding -- the declaration range includes the attribute line. Decision 6's
+// second trap lives here: "Locate the keyword. Do not assume its position -- an attributed
+// binding's statement range starts at its attribute line." Combining the attribute with
+// `private` exercises that trap without changing the position's route.
+[<Obsolete("prototype")>]
+let private attributed = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/attributed" }
+
+
+// [22] class member -- F2, needs an instance. Also Decision 5's second hazard: blanking this as a
+// *sibling* must not erase the whole type definition.
+type Api() =
+    member _.Get() =
+        http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/member" }
+
+
+// [19] parameterized function -- F2, no arguments we can invent
+let multi (a: string) (b: int) =
+    http { GET $"http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/{a}/{b}" }
+
+
+// [20] lambda-valued binding -- F3, the binding's value is the lambda, not the block
+let lambdaValued = fun () -> http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/lambda" }
+
+
+// [21] inner let -- F3, not module-scoped
+let innerLet () =
+    let x = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/inner" }
+
+    x
+
+
+// [17] match clause -- F1, decided at run time
+let matched =
+    match DateTime.Now.Hour with
+    | 0 -> http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/matched" }
+    | _ -> http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/matched-other" }
+
+
+// [18] try/with handler -- F1, decided at run time
+let tried =
+    try
+        http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/tried" }
+    with _ ->
+        http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/caught" }
+
+
+// [23] tuple binding -- F5. Both blocks share one declaration range, which is Decision 5's first
+// hazard: running either must not blank the span that contains it.
+let tupleA, tupleB =
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/tuple-a" }, http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/tuple-b" }
+
+
+// [24] a block nested inside another block's expression -- F5. The inner one's blank span is the
+// OUTER binding's declaration, which *contains* the target, so blanking it would erase the very
+// block being run. This is Decision 5's first hazard in the only shape where it is live: one
+// block runnable and one span containing the other.
+let nested =
+    http {
+        GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/nested"
+        header "X-Inner" (string (sprintf "%A" (http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/inner-block" })).Length)
+    }
+
+
+// The sweeper -- a plain bare block whose Setup has to blank every hazard above it.
+http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/sweeper" }
+
+
+// A bare block inside a module, with a non-Block side effect after it but still inside the
+// module. This is the exact shape that ruled out the "truncate at the enclosing top-level
+// statement" boundary: a module is one statement, so that boundary would run the side effect.
+// Truncating at the block's own expression end must drop it, per Decision 1. A request to
+// /SIDE-EFFECT means that boundary is wrong.
+module Tail =
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/tail" }
+
+    System.Net.Http.HttpClient().GetStringAsync("http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/SIDE-EFFECT").Result
+    |> ignore

+// The twelve-case run-behavior corpus that docs/spec/0002-reach-a-block-anywhere.md draws its
+// positions 1 to 12 from, verbatim in structure, with every URL pointed at a counting server and
+// the `#r` pinned so a run is reproducible. Block order in this file IS the index order that
+// `locateBlocks` reports, and PositionMatrixTests asserts against those indices.
+
+#r "nuget: FsHttp, 15.0.3"
+
+open FsHttp
+
+let baseUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2"
+
+
+// Case 1 -- bare, top-level
+http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/pikachu" }
+
+
+// Case 2 -- references a preceding pure let
+http { GET $"{baseUrl}/pokemon/pikachu" }
+
+
+// Case 3 -- two independent bare blocks (isolation)
+http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/bulbasaur" }
+
+http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/charmander" }
+
+
+// Case 4 -- right-hand side of a let (block on the next line)
+let squirtle = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/squirtle" }
+
+
+// Case 5 -- right-hand side of a let (block starts on the same line)
+let eevee = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/eevee" }
+
+
+// Case 6 -- body of a ()-callable function
+let getSnorlax () =
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/snorlax" }
+
+
+// Case 7 -- single block nested in a module
+module Gen1 =
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/mewtwo" }
+
+
+// Case 8 -- block in a module that also has a preceding member
+module Gen2 =
+    let region = "johto"
+
+    http { GET $"http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/{region}" }
+
+
+// Case 9 -- inside a for-loop
+for name in [ "pidgey"; "rattata" ] do
+    http { GET $"http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/{name}" }
+
+
+// Case 10 -- inside an if-branch
+if System.DateTime.Now.Hour < 12 then
+    http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/hoothoot" }
+
+
+// Case 11 -- a block that needs a value another block bound
+let dexId = http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/gengar" }
+
+http { GET $"http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon-species/{dexId}" }
+
+
+// Case 12 -- block already followed by |> Request.send
+http { GET "http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/v2/pokemon/lapras" } |> Request.send

problem_statement:
Companion: run a block → response envelope
## Parent

Spec: [#13](https://github.com/tw0po1nt/FsHttp.Explorer/issues/13)

## What to build

Running one **block** in the companion. It evaluates the block's **setup** afresh (opens/`#r`/pure lets/helpers, excluding every other block), isolates the bare CE and sends it, and returns a tagged **envelope**: `ok` (status, merged headers, contentType, body bytes), `compileError` (with range), or `runtimeError`. Extraction is by reflection over the BCL `HttpContent` — the companion holds no FsHttp reference, so the user's `#r` version pin wins (ADR-0002).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Running a block returns `ok` with status, headers merged from response + content headers, contentType, and the body base64-inline; against a local test server an image round-trips byte-intact (PNG magic preserved).
- [x] The user's `#r "nuget: FsHttp, x.y.z"` pin is honoured (reflection extraction, no host FsHttp reference).
- [x] Setup isolation: in a two-block script, running block 2 does not fire block 1's side effect.
- [x] A non-compiling block/setup returns `compileError` with a source range; a network/runtime failure returns `runtimeError` — distinct from an **HTTP error response**, which is a successful Run returning `ok` with the non-2xx code.
- [x] Seam A test suite covers the above.

## Blocked by

- Blocked by block location (shares the companion's FCS core; locate precedes run).

### Additional contract requirements

Run request/response contract:

- The companion answers a `tag = "run"` request — carrying the script source text and a zero-based block index over the `http { }` blocks found in that text — with exactly one tagged response envelope: `ok` (status, headers merged from response and content headers, `contentType`, body bytes base64-inline), `compileError` (diagnostics carrying a source range), or `runtimeError`.
- A successful HTTP exchange is `ok` regardless of status code — a non-2xx HTTP response (e.g. 404) is a successful run returning that status, not an error envelope.
- A block index with no matching block returns a `runtimeError` envelope.
- Running a block evaluates only that block's own setup (opens, `#r` directives and lets from earlier in the same source, excluding every other block); other blocks' side effects do not fire. A non-compiling target block or non-compiling setup yields a `compileError` with a source range; a failure at request time (e.g. an unreachable host) yields a `runtimeError`, distinct from a `compileError`.
- The FsHttp version that runs a block comes only from the user's own `#r "nuget: FsHttp, x.y.z"` directive in the submitted source: a script without one fails to open `FsHttp` and returns a `compileError` whose ranges lie within the submitted source, and the user's chosen pin — not any single fixed/forced reference — is what executes the request and produces the response envelope. Different FsHttp pins need not be supported by successive requests handled by the same companion process.
