@@ -0,0 +1,248 @@
+module Companion.BlockRunner
+
+// Runs one located `http { }` block against a fresh FCS interactive session (issue #7's
+// resolution, ADR-0002's mechanism): fresh session per Run, evaluate the target's preceding
+// setup (opens/#r/lets/helpers) with every *other* located block excluded, then the target's
+// bare CE alone piped to `Request.send`, extracting the raw `Response` by reflection over the
+// BCL `HttpContent` type. This module must never reference FsHttp itself — the user's own
+// `#r "nuget: FsHttp, x.y.z"`, evaluated as part of their own setup text, is the only thing
+// that ever resolves the package, so their version pin always wins.
+
+open System
+open System.Net.Http
+open System.Collections.Generic
+open FSharp.Compiler.Diagnostics
+open FSharp.Compiler.Interactive.Shell
+open Companion.BlockLocator
+
+type Diagnostic = { Message: string; Range: BlockRange }
+
+type RunOutcome =
+    | Ok of status: int * reason: string * headers: (string * string) list * contentType: string * bodyBase64: string
+    | CompileError of Diagnostic list
+    | RuntimeError of string
+
+/// Companion-side addendum evaluated after the user's own setup: silences FsHttp's FSI debug
+/// logging and buffers response content globally so the body survives the later
+/// `ReadAsByteArrayAsync` read (FSI's default is read-once). Carries no `#r` of its own — the
+/// user's setup is the only source of a FsHttp package reference (ADR-0002).
+let private companionAddendum =
+    [ "open FsHttp"
+      "FsHttp.Fsi.disableDebugLogs()"
+      "GlobalConfig.set (GlobalConfig.defaults |> Config.update (fun c -> { c with bufferResponseContent = true }))" ]
+    |> String.concat "\n"
+
+let private asPairs (h: IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, IEnumerable<string>>>) =
+    h |> Seq.map (fun kv -> kv.Key, String.Join(", ", kv.Value))
+
+/// Blanks a statement's span in place across `lines`, preserving every newline so every other
+/// line's row/column numbers stay aligned with the original source. The `()` placeholder
+/// keeps a `let`-bound statement well-formed without evaluating (and so without firing) the
+/// request it displaces; blanking the *whole* statement (not just the CE) means a trailing
+/// `|> Request.send` on the excluded block's own line has nothing left to dangle onto.
+let private blankStatement (lines: string[]) (r: BlockRange) =
+    let startIdx = r.StartLine - 1
+    let endIdx = r.EndLine - 1
+
+    if startIdx = endIdx then
+        let line = lines.[startIdx]
+        let before = line.Substring(0, r.StartCol)
+        let spanLen = r.EndCol - r.StartCol
+        let placeholder = "()" + String(' ', max 0 (spanLen - 2))
+        let after = line.Substring(r.EndCol)
+        lines.[startIdx] <- before + placeholder + after
+    else
+        let firstLine = lines.[startIdx]
+        let before = firstLine.Substring(0, r.StartCol)
+        let spanLen = firstLine.Length - r.StartCol
+        let placeholder = "()" + String(' ', max 0 (spanLen - 2))
+        lines.[startIdx] <- before + placeholder
+
+        for i in startIdx + 1 .. endIdx - 1 do
+            lines.[i] <- String(' ', lines.[i].Length)
+
+        let lastLine = lines.[endIdx]
+        lines.[endIdx] <- String(' ', r.EndCol) + lastLine.Substring(r.EndCol)
+
+/// Builds the target's preceding setup: everything before the target block, with every
+/// *other* located block's whole enclosing statement blanked out so clicking the target fires
+/// exactly that one request (issue #16's setup-isolation criterion). Blanking preserves line
+/// count and untouched columns, so a compile error's range still lands on the real source
+/// position.
+///
+/// Known boundary of this per-block isolation model: blanking a *let-bound* block replaces its
+/// binding with `()`, so if the target (or later setup) references the value that block
+/// produced — e.g. `let auth = http { ... } |> Request.send` consumed by a downstream block —
+/// evaluation fails with an "undefined identifier" compileError. Each block is treated as
+/// independent by design; cross-block value reuse is out of scope for #16 and would need a
+/// different isolation strategy (tracked for whoever revisits block dependencies).
+let private buildSetup (source: string) (blocks: LocatedBlock list) (target: LocatedBlock) : string =
+    let lines = source.Replace("\r\n", "\n").Split('\n')
+
+    blocks
+    |> List.filter (fun b -> b.Block <> target.Block)
+    |> List.iter (fun b -> blankStatement lines b.Statement)
+
+    let prefixLines = lines.[0 .. target.Block.StartLine - 2]
+
+    let startLineText =
+        lines.[target.Block.StartLine - 1].Substring(0, target.Block.StartCol)
+
+    Array.append prefixLines [| startLineText |] |> String.concat "\n"
+
+let private errorDiagnostics (diags: FSharpDiagnostic[]) =
+    diags |> Array.filter (fun d -> d.Severity = FSharpDiagnosticSeverity.Error)
+
+/// Maps a diagnostic from the combined setup eval back onto the original source. Its first
+/// `realLineCount` lines *are* the original text (minus blanked-out other blocks), so a
+/// diagnostic within them is already native and needs no translation. A diagnostic beyond them
+/// originates in the appended `companionAddendum` (e.g. `open FsHttp` failing because the
+/// user's script carries no resolvable `#r`) and has no source counterpart, so anchor it at the
+/// top of the script — where the missing reference belongs — rather than a phantom line the UI
+/// would try, and fail, to highlight.
+let private setupDiagnostic (realLineCount: int) (d: FSharpDiagnostic) : Diagnostic =
+    if d.StartLine > realLineCount then
+        { Message = d.Message
+          Range =
+            { StartLine = 1
+              StartCol = 0
+              EndLine = 1
+              EndCol = 0 } }
+    else
+        { Message = d.Message
+          Range =
+            { StartLine = d.StartLine
+              StartCol = d.StartColumn
+              EndLine = d.EndLine
+              EndCol = d.EndColumn } }
+
+/// Maps a diagnostic from the isolated target snippet (`<CE>\n|> Request.send`) back onto the
+/// original source. The snippet's lines 1..N are the CE's own lines verbatim, so only line 1's
+/// column needs the target's start-column offset; the synthetic `|> Request.send` line beyond
+/// the CE has no original counterpart and clamps to the block's end.
+let private targetDiagnostic (target: BlockRange) (ceLineCount: int) (d: FSharpDiagnostic) : Diagnostic =
+    let mapPoint line col =
+        if line > ceLineCount then
+            target.EndLine, target.EndCol
+        else
+            let origLine = target.StartLine + line - 1
+            let origCol = if line = 1 then target.StartCol + col else col
+            origLine, origCol
+
+    let sl, sc = mapPoint d.StartLine d.StartColumn
+    let el, ec = mapPoint d.EndLine d.EndColumn
+
+    { Message = d.Message
+      Range =
+        { StartLine = sl
+          StartCol = sc
+          EndLine = el
+          EndCol = ec } }
+
+/// `PropertyInfo.GetProperty` is nullable-annotated (the name might not exist); every field
+/// this reads is one ADR-0002 already commits to as stable across FsHttp 13-15, so a missing
+/// property is a genuine extraction bug, not a case to recover from.
+let private prop (name: string) (t: Type) : Reflection.PropertyInfo =
+    match t.GetProperty name with
+    | null -> failwithf "reflection: property '%s' not found on %s" name t.FullName
+    | p -> p
+
+let private extractResponse (v: FsiValue) : RunOutcome =
+    let t = v.ReflectionType
+    let rv = v.ReflectionValue
+    let getValue name = (prop name t).GetValue(rv)
+
+    let statusInt = int (getValue "statusCode" :?> Net.HttpStatusCode)
+    let reason = string (getValue "reasonPhrase")
+
+    let content =
+        match getValue "content" with
+        | :? HttpContent as c -> c
+        | _ -> failwith "reflection: 'content' property was not an HttpContent"
+
+    let respHeaders =
+        match getValue "headers" with
+        | :? Net.Http.Headers.HttpResponseHeaders as h -> h
+        | _ -> failwith "reflection: 'headers' property was not HttpResponseHeaders"
+
+    let bytes = content.ReadAsByteArrayAsync().Result
+
+    let ctype =
+        match content.Headers.ContentType with
+        | null -> ""
+        | c -> string c
+
+    let headers =
+        Seq.append (asPairs respHeaders) (asPairs content.Headers)
+        |> Seq.distinctBy fst
+        |> Seq.toList
+
+    Ok(statusInt, reason, headers, ctype, Convert.ToBase64String bytes)
+
+/// Runs the `blockIndex`-th block located in `source` (0-based, in source order — matching a
+/// `locate`/`blocks` envelope's ordering) and returns its outcome. A fresh `FsiEvaluationSession`
+/// is created and disposed per call, per issue #7's "fresh session per Run" resolution.
+let run (source: string) (blockIndex: int) : RunOutcome =
+    let located = locateBlocks source
+
+    match List.tryItem blockIndex located with
+    | None -> RuntimeError(sprintf "block index %d out of range (%d blocks located)" blockIndex located.Length)
+    | Some target ->
+        let ceText = sliceRange source target.Block
+        let setupText = buildSetup source located target
+        let combinedSetup = setupText + "\n" + companionAddendum
+
+        // Lines 1..setupLineCount of `combinedSetup` are native source; anything the addendum
+        // reports past them has no source position (see `setupDiagnostic`).
+        let setupLineCount = setupText.Split('\n').Length
+
+        let fsiConfig = FsiEvaluationSession.GetDefaultConfiguration()
+        let args = [| "fsi.exe"; "--noninteractive"; "--nologo" |]
+        use inReader = new IO.StringReader("")
+
+        // Collectible: the companion is long-lived and creates one session per Run, so each
+        // session's own dynamically-compiled user-code assembly should be reclaimable once
+        // disposed rather than accumulating for the life of the process.
+        //
+        // NOTE — a known limitation this does *not* cover: `collectible` only isolates the
+        // per-session dynamic assembly, not `#r "nuget:"`-resolved package assemblies, which
+        // load into the process-wide default AssemblyLoadContext. Two Runs in the same
+        // companion process pinning *different* versions of the same package (e.g. a script
+        // edited from `FsHttp, 15.0.3` to `FsHttp, 13.3.0` between clicks) can collide there
+        // ("Could not load type … from assembly …") — reproduced while building this module.
+        // Out of scope for #16 (a single pin resolving correctly); tracked in #38 for whoever
+        // eventually hardens multi-version same-process reuse.
+        use session =
+            FsiEvaluationSession.Create(fsiConfig, args, inReader, Console.Error, Console.Error, collectible = true)
+
+        let setupResult, setupDiags = session.EvalInteractionNonThrowing(combinedSetup)
+
+        match setupResult with
+        | Choice2Of2 ex ->
+            match
+                errorDiagnostics setupDiags
+                |> Array.map (setupDiagnostic setupLineCount)
+                |> Array.toList
+            with
+            | [] -> RuntimeError ex.Message
+            | errors -> CompileError errors
+        | Choice1Of2 _ ->
+            let ceLineCount = target.Block.EndLine - target.Block.StartLine + 1
+            let targetCode = ceText + "\n|> Request.send"
+            let targetResult, targetDiags = session.EvalExpressionNonThrowing(targetCode)
+
+            match targetResult with
+            | Choice2Of2 ex ->
+                match
+                    errorDiagnostics targetDiags
+                    |> Array.map (targetDiagnostic target.Block ceLineCount)
+                    |> Array.toList
+                with
+                | [] -> RuntimeError ex.Message
+                | errors -> CompileError errors
+            | Choice1Of2 None -> RuntimeError "expression returned no value"
+            | Choice1Of2(Some v) ->
+                try
+                    extractResponse v
+                with ex ->
+                    RuntimeError ex.Message

@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+module Companion.Tests.BlockRunnerProcessTests
+
+// The companion ships as its own host process with no FsHttp reference of its own
+// (ADR-0002): a block's response must come from the user's own `#r "nuget: FsHttp, x.y.z"`
+// pin, read purely by reflection over BCL `HttpContent`. These cases drive that shipped
+// process boundary — spawn the real companion binary, exchange framed envelopes over its
+// stdin/stdout, assert the observable outcome — so a run is proven reconstructible from the
+// submitted source with no host-supplied or host-preferred FsHttp.
+
+open System
+open System.Diagnostics
+open System.IO
+open System.Reflection
+open System.Text.Json
+open Expecto
+open Companion.Envelope
+open Companion.Tests.TestServer
+
+/// Wraps a possibly-null BCL string so the null can be matched without tripping F#'s
+/// nullability analysis on an unannotated flow.
+let private ofNullableString (s: string | null) : string option =
+    match s with
+    | null -> None
+    | v -> Some v
+
+/// The built companion binary. It is a project dependency of this test assembly, so it is
+/// deployed to the same output directory; a statically-referenced FsHttp would live there
+/// alongside it.
+let private companionDllPath : string =
+    match ofNullableString (Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().Location) with
+    | None -> failwith "could not locate the test assembly"
+    | Some testAsm ->
+        match ofNullableString (Path.GetDirectoryName testAsm) with
+        | None -> failwith "could not locate the test assembly directory"
+        | Some dir ->
+            let candidate = Path.Combine(dir, "Companion.dll")
+
+            if File.Exists candidate then
+                candidate
+            else
+                failwithf "companion binary not found at %s" candidate
+
+/// Runs the real companion process, writes every `frames` request as a framed envelope,
+/// closes stdin, reads one framed response per request, and returns them parsed together
+/// with the companion's full stderr. The companion is expected to stay responsive across all
+/// frames and exit 0 once stdin closes. `configureEnv` may shape the child environment (e.g.
+/// to preload a decoy assembly). Stderr is drained to avoid blocking the process, but its
+/// contents are not part of the run response contract.
+let private runCompanionProcess (configureEnv: ProcessStartInfo -> unit) (frames: JsonElement list) : JsonElement list * string =
+    let psi =
+        ProcessStartInfo(
+            FileName = "dotnet",
+            UseShellExecute = false,
+            RedirectStandardInput = true,
+            RedirectStandardOutput = true,
+            RedirectStandardError = true
+        )
+
+    psi.ArgumentList.Add("exec")
+    psi.ArgumentList.Add(companionDllPath)
+    configureEnv psi
+
+    let started = Process.Start psi
+
+    let proc : Process =
+        match started with
+        | null -> failwith "failed to start the companion process"
+        | p -> p
+
+    use _proc = proc
+
+    // Drain stderr on its own task from the start: a companion whose FSI session logs/bindings
+    // chatters (e.g. during a block's `#r` resolution or `printfn`) would otherwise fill the
+    // stderr pipe while the parent is blocked reading stdout, deadlocking both.
+    let stderrTask = proc.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
+
+    for f in frames do
+        let bytes = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes f
+        writeFrame proc.StandardInput.BaseStream bytes
+
+    proc.StandardInput.Close()
+
+    let responses =
+        [ for _ in frames ->
+            match tryReadFrame proc.StandardOutput.BaseStream with
+            | Some payload ->
+                use doc = JsonDocument.Parse(payload)
+                doc.RootElement.Clone()
+            | None ->
+                let stderr = stderrTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+                failtestf "companion closed the frame channel before answering every request; stderr tail: %s" stderr ]
+
+    let exited = proc.WaitForExit 30000
+    Expect.isTrue exited "companion should exit once stdin closes, not hang"
+    if exited then Expect.equal proc.ExitCode 0 "companion process should exit cleanly"
+    let stderr = stderrTask.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+    responses, stderr
+
+/// A {"tag":"run","source":...,"blockIndex":...} request element.
+let private runFrame (source: string) (blockIndex: int) : JsonElement =
+    use doc = JsonDocument.Parse(JsonSerializer.Serialize {| tag = "run"; source = source; blockIndex = blockIndex |})
+    doc.RootElement.Clone()
+
+/// The string tag of a response envelope, failing the test on a missing/null tag.
+let private tag (e: JsonElement) : string =
+    match e.TryGetProperty "tag" with
+    | true, v when v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.String ->
+        match v.GetString() with
+        | null -> failtest "tag carried null"
+        | s -> s
+    | _ -> failtestf "expected a string tag on the envelope, got %A" e.ValueKind
+
+// Sequenced: each case spawns a companion whose block runs resolve `#r "nuget: FsHttp"` into
+// the process-wide package cache; running them in parallel would race that cache.
+[<Tests>]
+let tests =
+    testSequenced
+    <| testList
+        "BlockRunner"
+        [ test "the shipped companion process answers a run request with a tagged envelope" {
+              let responses, _stderr =
+                  runCompanionProcess
+                      (fun _ -> ())
+                      [ runFrame "let x = 1\n" 0 ]
+
+              Expect.equal
+                  (tag responses.[0])
+                  "runtimeError"
+                  "a run request on a source with no block should be answered with a runtimeError envelope"
+          }
+
+          test "the run uses the FsHttp version selected by the user's pin" {
+              // The request only reaches this route when the loaded FsHttp assembly's own
+              // file version is used to construct its URL. This observes version selection
+              // through the required HTTP behavior, not a process output channel.
+              use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/13.3.0.0", textHandler 200 "selected pin" ])
+
+              let source =
+                  String.concat
+                      "\n"
+                      [ "#r \"nuget: FsHttp, 13.3.0\""
+                        "open FsHttp"
+                        "let pinVersion = System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(typeof<Config>.Assembly.Location).FileVersion"
+                        "http {"
+                        sprintf "    GET (sprintf \"%%s/%%s\" \"%s\" pinVersion)" server.BaseUrl
+                        "}"
+                        "" ]
+
+              let responses, _stderr = runCompanionProcess (fun _ -> ()) [ runFrame source 0 ]
+
+              Expect.equal (tag responses.[0]) "ok" "the user's chosen pin must run successfully"
+              Expect.equal
+                  (responses.[0].GetProperty("status").GetInt32())
+                  200
+                  "the request built from the pinned assembly version must reach its matching route"
+          } ]

+module Companion.Tests.BlockRunnerTests
+
+// Seam A (issue #16): drives Run through the companion's public tagged request handler —
+// feed a {"tag":"run"} envelope with .fsx source and a block index, assert the serialized
+// response envelope — matching the ticket's acceptance criteria directly at the contract
+// boundary. `BlockLocatorTests` exercises location; `RequestHandlerTests` covers the
+// dispatch shape of the run/error envelopes; this file covers every run behavior the
+// ticket lists: ok payloads, the user's #r pin, setup isolation, compileError, and
+// runtimeError, against a real local server where the ticket demands one.
+
+open System
+open System.Text.Json
+open Expecto
+open Companion.RequestHandler
+open Companion.Tests.TestServer
+
+/// Sends one serialized request envelope through the request handler and returns the
+/// response re-parsed from its serialized form, so assertions see exactly the fields the
+/// client would deserialize off the wire.
+let private respondTo (requestJson: string) : JsonElement =
+    use doc = JsonDocument.Parse(requestJson: string)
+    let response = respond doc
+    JsonDocument.Parse(JsonSerializer.Serialize response).RootElement.Clone()
+
+/// Builds a run-request envelope for `source` and `blockIndex` and returns the tagged
+/// response envelope.
+let private runRequest (source: string) (blockIndex: int) : JsonElement =
+    respondTo (JsonSerializer.Serialize {| tag = "run"; source = source; blockIndex = blockIndex |})
+
+/// The envelope body, base64-encoded in whichever field the implementation chose to carry
+/// it — the byte-intact body is what the ticket asserts.
+let private tryBodyBase64 (e: JsonElement) : string =
+    match e.TryGetProperty "bodyBase64" with
+    | true, v when v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.String ->
+        match v.GetString() with
+        | null -> failtest "bodyBase64 carried null"
+        | value -> value
+    | _ ->
+        match e.TryGetProperty "body" with
+        | true, v when v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.String ->
+            match v.GetString() with
+            | null -> failtest "body carried null"
+            | value -> value
+        | _ -> failtest "expected a base64 body field on the ok envelope, found none"
+
+/// Tries each candidate field name in order and returns the first string value found.
+let private tryAnyName (names: string list) (e: JsonElement) : string option =
+    names
+    |> List.tryPick (fun n ->
+        match e.TryGetProperty n with
+        | true, v when v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.String ->
+            match v.GetString() with
+            | null -> None
+            | s -> Some s
+        | _ -> None)
+
+/// A numeric value carried either as a JSON number or as a numeric string.
+let private tryIntValue (v: JsonElement) : int option =
+    match v.ValueKind with
+    | JsonValueKind.Number ->
+        match v.TryGetInt32() with
+        | true, n -> Some n
+        | _ -> None
+    | JsonValueKind.String ->
+        match v.GetString() with
+        | null -> None
+        | s ->
+            match System.Int32.TryParse s with
+            | true, n -> Some n
+            | _ -> None
+    | _ -> None
+
+/// The integer start line, whether the envelope spells it `startLine`, `line`, `start`,
+/// `fromLine`, ... — the ticket asserts the range points at a real line, not one vocabulary.
+let private tryStartLine (e: JsonElement) : int option =
+    [ "startLine"; "line"; "start"; "fromLine" ]
+    |> List.tryPick (fun n ->
+        match e.TryGetProperty n with
+        | true, v -> tryIntValue v
+        | _ -> None)
+
+/// The range an object carries when it flattens the range fields directly onto itself
+/// (`{message, startLine, startCol, endLine, endCol}`) instead of nesting a `range` object.
+/// Returned as-is; callers only read `startLine`, which `tryStartLine` already accepts
+/// under any spelling.
+let private tryFlatRange (e: JsonElement) : JsonElement option =
+    match e.ValueKind, tryStartLine e with
+    | JsonValueKind.Object, Some _ -> Some e
+    | _ -> None
+
+/// The first compile-error source range, whether the envelope carries a single range or a
+/// diagnostics array, and whether the range is a nested object or flat `startLine`-style
+/// fields on the diagnostic itself — the ticket asserts a range is present, not one shape.
+let private tryCompileErrorRange (e: JsonElement) : JsonElement option =
+    let single =
+        match e.TryGetProperty "range" with
+        | true, r when r.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object -> Some r
+        | _ ->
+            // A top-level flat range: the envelope itself carries the fields.
+            tryFlatRange e
+
+    match single, e.TryGetProperty "diagnostics" with
+    | Some r, _ -> Some r
+    | None, (true, ds) when ds.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Array && ds.GetArrayLength() > 0 ->
+        // The first diagnostic that exposes a range, nested or flat.
+        ds.EnumerateArray()
+        |> Seq.tryPick (fun d ->
+            match d.TryGetProperty "range" with
+            | true, r when r.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object -> Some r
+            | _ -> tryFlatRange d)
+    | _ -> None
+
+
+/// A test-scoped non-null string projection: missing/null envelope fields fail the test
+/// outright rather than silently comparing against null.
+let private getString (name: string) (e: JsonElement) : string =
+    match e.GetProperty(name).GetString() with
+    | null -> failtestf "expected envelope field '%s' to carry a string" name
+    | value -> value
+
+/// Reads a merged-headers envelope field case-insensitively (HTTP header names are
+/// case-insensitive). Accepts both contract-faithful container shapes: a JSON object map
+/// with string or string-array values, or a JSON array of header entries — `{name, values}`,
+/// `{name, value}`, `{key, values}`-style records with any reasonable field naming, where
+/// the value may be a single string or an array of strings. Entry values are joined with
+/// ", " like repeated header lines. Fails only when the header is genuinely absent or the
+/// field is not a collection of headers at all.
+let private getHeader (name: string) (headers: JsonElement) : string =
+    let valueString (v: JsonElement) : string =
+        match v.ValueKind with
+        | JsonValueKind.Array -> String.concat ", " [ for i in v.EnumerateArray() -> string i ]
+        | _ ->
+            match v.GetString() with
+            | null -> failtestf "expected header '%s' to carry a string" name
+            | value -> value
+
+    match headers.ValueKind with
+    | JsonValueKind.Object ->
+        let found =
+            headers.EnumerateObject()
+            |> Seq.tryFind (fun p -> String.Equals(p.Name, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
+
+        match found with
+        | None -> failtestf "expected header '%s' to be present" name
+        | Some p -> valueString p.Value
+    | JsonValueKind.Array ->
+        let entryName (e: JsonElement) : string option = tryAnyName [ "name"; "key"; "header" ] e
+
+        let found =
+            headers.EnumerateArray()
+            |> Seq.tryFind (fun e ->
+                match entryName e with
+                | Some n -> String.Equals(n, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
+                | None -> false)
+
+        match found with
+        | None -> failtestf "expected header '%s' to be present" name
+        | Some e ->
+            let entryValue =
+                [ "values"; "value" ]
+                |> List.tryPick (fun n ->
+                    match e.TryGetProperty n with
+                    | true, v -> Some v
+                    | _ -> None)
+
+            match entryValue with
+            | Some v when
+                v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.String
+                || v.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Array
+                -> valueString v
+            | _ -> failtestf "expected header entry '%s' to carry a value" name
+    | _ -> failtestf "expected headers to be a collection of headers, found %A" headers.ValueKind

+/// 13-15). Pinned explicitly, and not "latest", so the suite doesn't drift with new releases.

+// process-wide package-management cache. Run in parallel (Expecto's default), those

+// '…resolvedReferences.paths' because it is being used by another process"), and a lost race

+

+              Expect.equal firstHits.Value 0 "the earlier request statement must not run as setup"
+              Expect.equal secondHits.Value 1 "the selected block's request should run once"
+          }

+          test "a local helper parameter does not inherit the name of an excluded earlier block" {

+                            "/target", countingHandler targetHits ]
+                  )

+              let source =
+                  sprintf
+                      "#r \"nuget: FsHttp, %s\"\nopen FsHttp\nlet earlier = http { GET \"%s/first\" }\nlet makeUrl earlier = earlier\nlet targetUrl = makeUrl \"%s/target\"\nhttp { GET targetUrl }\n"
+                      fsHttpRef
+                      server.BaseUrl
+                      server.BaseUrl
+
+              let response = runRequest source 1
+
+              Expect.equal (getString "tag" response) "ok" "the selected block should compile using its local helper"
+              Expect.equal firstHits.Value 0 "the earlier block's request must remain excluded"

+          }

+          test "declarations after the target block are not evaluated as setup" {

+                      fsHttpRef

+                          |> Seq.exists (fun d ->
+                              match d.TryGetProperty "range" with
+                              | true, r when r.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object -> true
+                              | _ -> tryFlatRange d |> Option.isSome))
+                  | _ -> tryCompileErrorRange response |> Option.isSome

+                      fsHttpRef

+              let response = runRequest source 0
+              Expect.equal (getString "tag" response) "runtimeError" "tag should be runtimeError"
+          } ]

+module Companion.Tests.TestServer
+
+// A minimal in-process HTTP server for Seam A's "against a local test server" acceptance
+// criteria (issue #16) — avoids depending on any external process or language runtime.
+
+open System
+open System.Net
+open System.Threading
+
+let private getFreePort () =
+    let l = new Net.Sockets.TcpListener(IPAddress.Loopback, 0)
+    l.Start()
+    let port = (l.LocalEndpoint :?> IPEndPoint).Port
+    l.Stop()
+    port
+
+/// Serves `routes` (path -> handler, each responsible for writing and closing the response)
+/// on a free loopback port until disposed.
+type TestServer(routes: Map<string, HttpListenerContext -> unit>) =
+    let port = getFreePort ()
+    let prefix = sprintf "http://127.0.0.1:%d/" port
+    let listener = new HttpListener()
+    do listener.Prefixes.Add(prefix)
+    do listener.Start()
+
+    let loop () =
+        let mutable running = true
+
+        while running do
+            try
+                let ctx = listener.GetContext()
+
+                let path =
+                    match ctx.Request.Url with
+                    | null -> ""
+                    | u -> u.AbsolutePath
+
+                match routes.TryFind path with
+                | Some handler -> handler ctx
+                | None ->
+                    ctx.Response.StatusCode <- 404
+                    ctx.Response.OutputStream.Close()
+            with
+            | :? ObjectDisposedException
+            | :? HttpListenerException -> running <- false
+
+    let thread = Thread(loop, IsBackground = true)
+    do thread.Start()
+
+    /// Base URL with no trailing slash, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:54321`.
+    member _.BaseUrl = prefix.TrimEnd('/')
+
+    interface IDisposable with
+        member _.Dispose() = listener.Close()
+
+/// Writes `bytes` as the response body with the given content type and status, plus any
+/// extra headers.
+let bytesHandler
+    (status: int)
+    (contentType: string)
+    (extraHeaders: (string * string) list)
+    (bytes: byte[])
+    (ctx: HttpListenerContext)
+    =
+    ctx.Response.StatusCode <- status
+    ctx.Response.ContentType <- contentType
+    extraHeaders |> List.iter (fun (k, v) -> ctx.Response.Headers.Add(k, v))
+    ctx.Response.OutputStream.Write(bytes, 0, bytes.Length)
+    ctx.Response.OutputStream.Close()
+
+/// Writes `text` as a `text/plain` response body with the given status.
+let textHandler (status: int) (text: string) (ctx: HttpListenerContext) =
+    bytesHandler status "text/plain" [] (Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes text) ctx
+
+/// A handler that increments `counter` on every hit, then responds `200 OK`. The listener
+/// loop processes one request at a time, so a plain mutation is safe here.
+let countingHandler (counter: int ref) (ctx: HttpListenerContext) =
+    counter.Value <- counter.Value + 1
+    textHandler 200 "hit" ctx

problem_statement:
Renderer core: Content-Type dispatch ## Parent Spec: [#13](https://github.com/tw0po1nt/FsHttp.Explorer/issues/13) ## What to build The **renderer core** — the presentation-shell-agnostic `renderBody(envelope) → DOM` that turns a response body into rendered DOM dispatched on its `Content-Type`, plus the thin status line and collapsible headers. Folds in `prototype/response-viewer`. Pure function of an envelope; no VSCode needed to test it. ## Acceptance criteria - [x] `renderBody` dispatches on Content-Type: image → `` with a `data:` URI; JSON → collapsible, highlighted tree; HTML → sandboxed iframe; plain text and unknown/XML → wrapped monospace fallback. - [x] A binary/undecodable body → non-crashing size/hex fallback; a non-2xx **HTTP error response** renders its body honestly with the code shown. - [x] A thin status line (method, URL, coloured status, round-trip time, size) sits above the body; headers live in a collapsible section. - [x] Seam B test suite drives canned envelopes → asserts the DOM shape, with no VSCode. ## Blocked by - Blocked by the walking skeleton (needs the extension-host project scaffold). ### Additional contract requirements The following observable requirements refine how "renders the DOM" is interpreted and where the renderer core lives, so that a solution can be exercised by an external test harness. ## Project location and shape - The renderer core lives in a standalone project at `extension-host/renderer/Renderer.fsproj`, referenced from the solution. It targets `netstandard2.0`, depends only on `FSharp.Core` (pinned to the exact same version every referencing project uses, with the implicit `FSharp.Core` reference disabled), and must not depend on VSCode, a browser, or Fable — it compiles as plain .NET under `dotnet build`. - The project exposes two public modules, `Renderer.Core` and `Renderer.NodeQuery`. ## Public surface of `Renderer.Core` `Renderer.Core` exposes: - An immutable DOM description type `Node` (with `Node.` qualified access) with two cases: `Element of tag: string * attrs: (string * string) list * children: Node list` — attributes are a flat name/value list (`class`, `src`, `srcdoc`, …); boolean HTML attributes appear with an empty value — and `Text of string`. - A `ResponseEnvelope` record with fields `Method: string`, `Url: string`, `Status: int`, `Reason: string`, `Headers: (string * string) list`, `ContentType: string`, `Body: byte[]`, and `ElapsedMs: float`. Rendering is a pure function of this record. - `renderBody : ResponseEnvelope -> Node` — Content-Type-dispatched rendering of the body only. - `render : ResponseEnvelope -> Node` — the full response view: status line, collapsible headers, rendered body. - `statusClass : int -> string` and `humanSize : int -> string` (see below). ## Public surface of `Renderer.NodeQuery` `Renderer.NodeQuery` exposes black-box shape assertions over a `Node` tree, defined without reaching into any renderer internals: - `byTag : string -> Node -> Node list` — every element with the given tag, anywhere in the tree. - `byClass : string -> Node -> Node list` — every element carrying the given CSS class. - `attr : string -> Node -> string option` — an attribute value of a single node. - `tag : Node -> string option` — the tag of an element (or `None` for a text node). - `innerText : Node -> string` — the concatenated text of a node and all its descendants. - `hasClass : string -> Node -> bool`. ## Content-Type dispatch (`renderBody`) Content-Type comparison is case-insensitive and ignores any `;` parameters (e.g. `text/html; charset=utf-8` dispatches as `text/html`). - Any `image/*` type → an `` element whose `src` is `data:;base64,`, where `` is the cleaned media type (lower-cased, parameters stripped). - `application/json`, `text/json`, or any type ending in `+json` → a JSON tree rooted in an element with class `response-json`: - objects and arrays render as collapsible `

problem_statement:
publish the agent skill as a plugin from this repo
publish the bundled agent skill as a plugin from this repo, so it can be installed with the agent's own plugin commands instead of only through the app.

**why**

right now the only way to get the skill is Help ▸ Install Agent Skill…, which copies `agterm/Resources/agent-skill/` into `~/.claude/skills/agterm/` and `~/.codex/skills/agterm/`. Those destinations are fixed, which is what #315 ran into: the app cannot see `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so anyone with a relocated config dir gets an install their agent never finds.

a marketplace install sidesteps that entirely. The agent does the installing, so the skill goes wherever that agent actually keeps its config, and it updates through `/plugin` without reinstalling from the app.

**shape**

- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root, listing the plugin with name, source path, description and version
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with the manifest, pointing `skills` at the directory holding the skill
- a separate `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` alongside it for codex. Our SKILL.md is already agent-neutral so one skill body serves both

install becomes:

```
/plugin marketplace add umputun/agterm
/plugin install agterm@agterm
```

```
codex plugin marketplace add umputun/agterm
codex plugin add agterm@agterm
```

**things to work out**

1. source of truth. `agterm/Resources/agent-skill/` is the single source today and the app bundles it from there, so `plugin.json` should point `skills` straight at that directory rather than mirroring a copy under `.claude-plugin/`. Need to check whether the manifest accepts a path outside `.claude-plugin/`; if it does not, we need a sync step or a symlink, and a mirrored copy that drifts is worse than no plugin.

2. `scripts/show-image.sh` is referenced in SKILL.md by absolute install path. A plugin install puts it in the plugin cache instead, so that reference has to resolve for both install paths.

3. versioning. The manifests carry their own version, so it needs a bump step in `scripts/release.sh`, otherwise the published version goes stale silently.

4. keep the Help menu item as well. It still makes sense for someone who does not use plugin commands, and it is the only path that also covers Pi and OpenCode.

### Additional contract requirements

The bundled agterm skill is published as a repository-local plugin package for both Claude Code
and Codex. Claude Code discovers the package through the root `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`
marketplace descriptor; Codex discovers the same package through the Codex plugin manifest shipped
with it at `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. Each marketplace listing identifies the `agterm` skill
and names its package with a repository-local source path that never escapes the repository. The
source may use the JSON representation required by that client — a plain path string or an object
carrying the path — and any additional client-local marketplace listing likewise resolves that same
repository-local package.

Inside the package, each client has its own plugin manifest, and both manifests resolve one
complete, authoritative skill tree — or, for a manifest that discovers skills by container
directory, the directory holding it — through repository-local skill pointers that stay inside the
published package. The tree must include `SKILL.md`, the reference, the examples, the troubleshooting guide, and the image helper. The app's
bundled-install fallback remains available from the Help menu; it ships and installs that same
authoritative skill tree for users who do not use plugin commands.

The root marketplace entry and every plugin manifest for the package each carry a nonempty
version, and all of those versions agree. A release version bump updates each of those manifests
and stops for review while the bump it just made is still uncommitted, so an installed plugin is not silently
left on an older skill version.

The image helper is invoked relative to the installed skill directory. Skill documentation must not
assume a fixed Claude or Codex home-directory installation path, because the helper must work from
both a plugin cache and the Help-menu installation.
problem_statement_base:
publish the agent skill as a plugin from this repo
publish the bundled agent skill as a plugin from this repo, so it can be installed with the agent's own plugin commands instead of only through the app.

**why**

right now the only way to get the skill is Help ▸ Install Agent Skill…, which copies `agterm/Resources/agent-skill/` into `~/.claude/skills/agterm/` and `~/.codex/skills/agterm/`. Those destinations are fixed, which is what #315 ran into: the app cannot see `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so anyone with a relocated config dir gets an install their agent never finds.

a marketplace install sidesteps that entirely. The agent does the installing, so the skill goes wherever that agent actually keeps its config, and it updates through `/plugin` without reinstalling from the app.

**shape**

- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root, listing the plugin with name, source path, description and version
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with the manifest, pointing `skills` at the directory holding the skill
- a separate `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` alongside it for codex. Our SKILL.md is already agent-neutral so one skill body serves both

install becomes:

```
/plugin marketplace add umputun/agterm
/plugin install agterm@agterm
```

```
codex plugin marketplace add umputun/agterm
codex plugin add agterm@agterm
```

**things to work out**

1. source of truth. `agterm/Resources/agent-skill/` is the single source today and the app bundles it from there, so `plugin.json` should point `skills` straight at that directory rather than mirroring a copy under `.claude-plugin/`. Need to check whether the manifest accepts a path outside `.claude-plugin/`; if it does not, we need a sync step or a symlink, and a mirrored copy that drifts is worse than no plugin.

2. `scripts/show-image.sh` is referenced in SKILL.md by absolute install path. A plugin install puts it in the plugin cache instead, so that reference has to resolve for both install paths.

3. versioning. The manifests carry their own version, so it needs a bump step in `scripts/release.sh`, otherwise the published version goes stale silently.

4. keep the Help menu item as well. It still makes sense for someone who does not use plugin commands, and it is the only path that also covers Pi and OpenCode.
contract_addendum:
The bundled agterm skill is published as a repository-local plugin package for both Claude Code
and Codex. Claude Code discovers the package through the root `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`
marketplace descriptor; Codex discovers the same package through the Codex plugin manifest shipped
with it at `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. Each marketplace listing identifies the `agterm` skill
and names its package with a repository-local source path that never escapes the repository. The
source may use the JSON representation required by that client — a plain path string or an object
carrying the path — and any additional client-local marketplace listing likewise resolves that same
repository-local package.

Inside the package, each client has its own plugin manifest, and both manifests resolve one
complete, authoritative skill tree — or, for a manifest that discovers skills by container
directory, the directory holding it — through repository-local skill pointers that stay inside the
published package. The tree must include `SKILL.md`, the reference, the examples, the troubleshooting guide, and the image helper. The app's
bundled-install fallback remains available from the Help menu; it ships and installs that same
authoritative skill tree for users who do not use plugin commands.

The root marketplace entry and every plugin manifest for the package each carry a nonempty
version, and all of those versions agree. A release version bump updates each of those manifests
and stops for review while the bump it just made is still uncommitted, so an installed plugin is not silently
left on an older skill version.

The image helper is invoked relative to the installed skill directory. Skill documentation must not
assume a fixed Claude or Codex home-directory installation path, because the helper must work from
both a plugin cache and the Help-menu installation.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/plugins/agterm/skills/agterm/scripts/show-image.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# show-image.sh — display an image inside the current agterm session.
+#
+# usage: bash show-image.sh <image> [size-percent]
+#
+# opens an agterm overlay (a real terminal surface with a pty) and renders the image there via the
+# kitty graphics protocol, which ghostty — agterm's engine — draws natively. no kitty binary and no
+# external image viewer are involved; the encoder is plain base64 + printf. this is the reliable way
+# for a coding agent to show an image: emitting graphics escapes to the agent's own tool stdout does
+# not work (the harness escapes the control bytes), and an image viewer cannot run in the agent's
+# tool shell (no controlling terminal). the overlay sidesteps both.
+#
+# requires running inside agterm (AGTERM_ENABLED=1) with agtermctl on PATH.
+
+# ask the terminal for a geometry report and echo the two numeric fields it carries. $1 is the CSI
+# request (14t -> ESC [ 4 ; height-px ; width-px t, 18t -> ESC [ 8 ; rows ; cols t). the request and
+# the reply go over /dev/tty on fd 3, not stdout/stdin: the caller runs this in a command
+# substitution, so a request written to stdout would land in that pipe and never reach the terminal.
+# prints nothing when the terminal does not answer, so the caller falls back to unscaled output.
+query_geom() {
+  local old a b
+  exec 3<>/dev/tty || return
+  old=$(stty -g <&3 2>/dev/null) || { exec 3>&-; return; }
+  stty raw -echo min 0 time 5 <&3 2>/dev/null
+  printf '\033[%s' "$1" >&3
+  IFS=';' read -r -d t -t 1 _ a b <&3
+  stty "$old" <&3 2>/dev/null
+  exec 3>&-
+  case "$a$b" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return;; esac
+  printf '%s %s' "$a" "$b"
+}
+
+# internal mode: emit the graphics escape into the overlay's pty, then wait for dismissal.
+if [ "${1:-}" = "--emit" ]; then
+  img="$2"
+  clear
+
+  # scale the image to the overlay's own size. the kitty protocol places the image at native pixel
+  # size unless c= and r= give it a cell box, so a screenshot larger than the panel gets clipped.
+  # cell size comes from the terminal's pixel and cell geometry; image size from sips (macOS-native).
+  px=$(query_geom 14t)
+  cells=$(query_geom 18t)
+  iw=$(sips -g pixelWidth "$img" 2>/dev/null | awk '/pixelWidth:/{print $2}')
+  ih=$(sips -g pixelHeight "$img" 2>/dev/null | awk '/pixelHeight:/{print $2}')
+  box=""; padc=0; padr=0; promptcol=1
+  if [ -n "$px" ] && [ -n "$cells" ] && [ -n "$iw" ] && [ -n "$ih" ]; then
+    fit=$(awk -v px="$px" -v cells="$cells" -v iw="$iw" -v ih="$ih" 'BEGIN{
+      split(px, p, " "); split(cells, c, " ")
+      ph=p[1]; pw=p[2]; rows=c[1]; cols=c[2]
+      if (pw<=0 || ph<=0 || rows<=0 || cols<=0 || iw<=0 || ih<=0) exit
+      # image size expressed in cells, then the largest uniform scale that still fits. the close
+      # prompt is pinned to the last row, so the image is centered in the rows above it and capped
+      # three rows short of the height: a cap of exactly the free height would leave zero slack to
+      # split, which is what makes a height-limited image look top-aligned rather than centered.
+      needc=iw/(pw/cols); needr=ih/(ph/rows)
+      avail=rows-3; if (avail<1) avail=1
+      s=cols/needc; if (avail/needr < s) s=avail/needr
+      # orow, not or: or() is a gawk builtin, so `or` as a variable is a syntax error there.
+      oc=int(needc*s); orow=int(needr*s)
+      if (oc<1) oc=1; if (orow<1) orow=1
+      # leftover cells split evenly so the image sits centered in the overlay. the prompt column is
+      # floored at 1: on an overlay narrower than the prompt it would otherwise go negative, and a
+      # negative parameter makes the CUP escape malformed, so the terminal drops it and the prompt
+      # lands on top of the image instead of the last row.
+      pc=int((cols-20)/2)+1; if (pc<1) pc=1
+      printf "%d %d %d %d %d", oc, orow, int((cols-oc)/2), int((rows-1-orow)/2), pc
+    }')
+    # C=1 keeps the cursor put, so a bottom-edge image cannot scroll the screen and shift itself up.
+    [ -n "$fit" ] && read -r oc or padc padr promptcol <<<"$fit" && box="c=$oc,r=$or,C=1,"
+  fi
+  read -r termrows _ <<<"$cells"
+
+  # place the cursor at the image's top-left corner before transmitting: a=T draws at the cursor, and
+  # the chunked escapes below do not move it.
+  k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$padr" ]; do printf '\n'; k=$((k + 1)); done
+  [ "$padc" -gt 0 ] && printf '\033[%dC' "$padc"
+
+  data=$(base64 < "$img" | tr -d '\n')
+  i=0; n=${#data}; first=1
+  while [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; do
+    chunk=${data:i:4096}
+    i=$((i + 4096))
+    if [ "$i" -ge "$n" ]; then m=0; else m=1; fi
+    if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
+      printf '\033_Ga=T,f=100,%sm=%d;%s\033\\' "$box" "$m" "$chunk"; first=0
+    else
+      printf '\033_Gm=%d;%s\033\\' "$m" "$chunk"
+    fi
+  done
+  if [ -n "$box" ]; then
+    printf '\033[%d;%dHpress Enter to close' "$termrows" "$promptcol"
+  else
+    printf '\n\n  press Enter to close\n'
+  fi
+  read -r _
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+img="${1:-}"
+size="${2:-60}"
+[ -n "$img" ] || { echo "usage: show-image.sh <image> [size-percent]" >&2; exit 2; }
+[ -f "$img" ] || { echo "show-image.sh: no such file: $img" >&2; exit 1; }
+command -v agtermctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "show-image.sh: agtermctl not on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
+[ "${AGTERM_ENABLED:-}" = "1" ] || { echo "show-image.sh: not inside agterm; try: open \"$img\"" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# resolve absolute paths so the overlay (which runs with a different cwd) finds both this script and
+# the image regardless of where the agent invoked it from.
+self=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/$(basename "$0")
+abs=$(cd "$(dirname "$img")" && pwd)/$(basename "$img")
+
+# POSIX single-quote a string for safe embedding in the command below: wrap in '...' and replace each
+# embedded ' with the '\'' sequence, so a path containing a quote can't break out of the quoting. The
+# overlay command is run via `sh -c`, so an unescaped ' in the path would otherwise abort it.
+sq() { printf "'%s'" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")"; }
+
+# open an overlay that re-invokes this script in --emit mode inside the overlay's pty.
+agtermctl session overlay open "/bin/bash $(sq "$self") --emit $(sq "$abs")" --size-percent "$size"

--- a/scripts/release.sh
+++ b/scripts/release.sh
@@ -28,6 +28,42 @@ fi
 
 TAG="v$VERSION"
 DMG="$BUILD_DIR/agterm-$VERSION.dmg"
+
+# ── plugin manifest version ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# The agent skill also ships as a Claude Code / Codex plugin, and both plugin
+# managers key their install cache on the manifest "version" — an unbumped
+# manifest means an existing install never picks up the new skill, silently.
+# `gh release create` below runs with no --target, so the tag lands on whatever
+# origin/master points at: the bump must be both COMMITTED and PUSHED, and both
+# are checked here. This applies the bump and stops so the diff can be reviewed
+# and committed, rather than rewriting git history from inside a release script.
+PLUGIN_MANIFESTS=(
+  "$ROOT/plugins/agterm/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
+  "$ROOT/plugins/agterm/.codex-plugin/plugin.json"
+  "$ROOT/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json"
+)
+for manifest in "${PLUGIN_MANIFESTS[@]}"; do
+  sed -i '' -E "s/(\"version\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*)\"[^\"]*\"/\1\"$VERSION\"/" "$manifest"
+done
+# against HEAD, not the index — a bare `git diff` compares the worktree to the
+# index, so a bump that was merely `git add`ed reads as clean and publishes stale.
+if ! git diff --quiet HEAD -- "${PLUGIN_MANIFESTS[@]}"; then
+  echo "==> bumped the plugin manifests to $VERSION — review and commit, then re-run:" >&2
+  git --no-pager diff --stat HEAD -- "${PLUGIN_MANIFESTS[@]}" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+# committed is not enough: the tag is cut from the remote, so verify the pushed
+# manifests carry this version too.
+if [ "$PUBLISH" = "1" ]; then
+  git fetch -q origin master
+  for manifest in "${PLUGIN_MANIFESTS[@]}"; do
+    rel="${manifest#"$ROOT"/}"
+    if ! git show "origin/master:$rel" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"version\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"$VERSION\""; then
+      echo "==> $rel on origin/master is not at $VERSION — push master first" >&2
+      exit 1
+    fi
+  done
+fi
 APP="$BUILD_DIR/DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/agterm.app"
 NOTARY_PROFILE="${AGTERM_NOTARY_PROFILE:-agterm-notary}"
 TAP_REPO="umputun/homebrew-apps"

problem_statement:
Support unnamed bit-fields in nested anonymous objects
> Given that we have a way to get the offset of `x` in `struct foo`, I thought of a way to get the offset of the anonymous `struct` [HIDDEN]

Ah! That makes sense, simple yet clever :smile: I'm going to give this a try

_Originally posted by @jorisdral in https://github.com/well-typed/hs-bindgen/issues/1857#issuecomment-4125590235_

### Additional contract requirements

An anonymous nested struct or union that contains unnamed bit-fields and also
has a named member must still produce usable Haskell bindings; such a
declaration must not be treated as an unsupported case.

For these declarations the implicit field that is generated for the anonymous
object denotes the *start of the anonymous object itself*. Its offset must not
be the offset of a later named member contained inside the anonymous object.
The leading unnamed bit-fields may shift where named members begin, but they do
not move the start of the enclosing anonymous struct or union.

This requirement applies to every combination of struct and union used for the
outer and the inner (nested anonymous) object: struct-in-struct,
union-in-struct, struct-in-union, and union-in-union.

+#pragma once
+
+// We can compute offsets for implicit fields even if the first field(s) of an
+// anonymous struct or union are unnamed bit-fields (that introduce padding).
+//
+// This edge case was not properly handled by implicit field detection in the
+// past, so we include this as an edge case regression test.
+
+// Naming: the types in this header are named after the order in which objects
+// are nested. For example, US means "union containing struct", or equivalently,
+// "struct in union".
+
+struct SS {
+  char x;
+  struct {
+    char : 3;
+    int y;
+  };
+  int z;
+};
+
+struct SU {
+  char x;
+  union {
+    char : 3;
+    int y;
+  };
+  int z;
+};
+
+union US {
+  char x;
+  struct {
+    char : 3;
+    int y;
+  };
+  int z;
+};
+
+union UU {
+  char x;
+  union {
+    char : 3;
+    int y;
+  };
+  int z;
+};

+    go numIndirections acc = \case
+      -- interesting case
+      TypeFun args res ->
+          let acc' = Set.insert (numIndirections, args, res) acc
+          in  Foldable.foldl' (go (numIndirections + 1)) acc' (fmap (.typ) args ++ [res])
+
+      -- recursive cases
+      TypePointers n t       -> go (numIndirections + n) acc t
+      TypeConstArray _n t    -> go (numIndirections + 1) acc t
+      TypeIncompleteArray  t -> go (numIndirections + 1) acc t
+      TypeBlock t            -> go (numIndirections + 1) acc t
+      TypeQual _q t          -> go (numIndirections + 1) acc t
+
+      -- primitive cases
+      TypePrim{} -> acc
+      TypeComplex{} -> acc
+      TypeVoid{} -> acc
+
+      -- sugar cases
+      TypeRef{} -> acc
+      TypeEnum{} -> acc
+      TypeMacro{} -> acc
+      TypeTypedef{} -> acc
+      TypeExtBinding{} -> acc
+
+-- | Get the first function type indirection
+getFirstFunTypeIndirection ::
+     forall p.
+     Type p
+  -> Maybe ( [TypeFunArg p]
+           , Type p
+           , Type p -> Type p -- ^ zipper: how to reconstruct the original type
+           )
+getFirstFunTypeIndirection = go 0 id
+  where
+    go ::
+         Int
+      -> (Type p -> Type p)
+      -> Type p
+      -> Maybe ( [TypeFunArg p]
+               , Type p
+               , Type p -> Type p
+               )
+    go numIndirections reconstruct = \case
+      -- interesting case
+      TypeFun args res
+        | numIndirections <= 0 -> Nothing
+        | otherwise ->  Just (args, res, reconstruct)
+
+      -- recursive cases
+      TypePointers n t        -> go (numIndirections + n) (reconstruct . TypePointers n) t
+      TypeConstArray n t      -> go (numIndirections + 1) (reconstruct . TypeConstArray n) t
+      TypeIncompleteArray  t  -> go (numIndirections + 1) (reconstruct . TypeIncompleteArray) t
+      TypeBlock t             -> go (numIndirections + 1) (reconstruct . TypeBlock) t
+      TypeQual q t            -> go (numIndirections + 1) (reconstruct . TypeQual q) t
+
+      -- primitive cases
+      TypePrim{} -> Nothing
+      TypeComplex{} -> Nothing
+      TypeVoid{} -> Nothing
+
+      -- sugar cases
+      TypeRef{} -> Nothing
+      TypeEnum{} -> Nothing
+      TypeMacro{} -> Nothing
+      TypeTypedef{} -> Nothing
+      TypeExtBinding{} -> Nothing
+

problem_statement:
Prefix "artificial" fields for anonymous structs/unions with `anon'`
Given

```c
enum Result_Tag {
  Ok,
  Err,
};

struct Result {
  enum Result_Tag tag;
  union {
    const int ok;
    const char *err;
  };
};
```

we currently generate

```hs
newtype Result_Tag = ..

data Result = Result{
    tag :: Result_Tag
  , ok  :: Result_ok
  }

newtype Result_ok = Result_ok RIP.ByteArray

-- HasField instances generated by ghc

instance RIP.HasField "tag" Result Result_Tag
instance RIP.HasField "ok"  Result Result_ok

-- Setters/getters generated by hs-bindgen

get_result_ok_ok  :: Result_ok -> RIP.CInt
get_result_ok_err :: Result_ok -> PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar

set_result_ok_ok  :: RIP.CInt                    -> Result_ok
set_result_ok_err :: PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar -> Result_ok
```

The fact that the auxiliary type (`Result_ok`) and the auxiliary field (`ok`) are named after the first field of the anonymous union is confusing; we worried about this in the original design and the confusion has since been confirmed by users (#1929). In this ticket we propose to rename this type and this field, to lessen the confusion somewhat: we will still use the name of the first field to distinguish one implicit field from another, but prefixed with `anon'` (the tick ensures that this cannot clash with any C fields):

```hs
data Result = Result{
    tag     :: Result_Tag
  , anon'ok :: Result_anon'ok
  }

newtype Result_anon'ok = Result_anon'ok RIP.ByteArray

-- HasField instances generated by ghc

instance RIP.HasField "tag"     Result Result_Tag
instance RIP.HasField "anon'ok" Result Result_anon'ok

-- Setters/getters generated by hs-bindgen

get_result_anon'ok_ok  :: Result_anon'ok -> RIP.CInt
get_result_anon'ok_err :: Result_anon'ok -> PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar

set_result_anon'ok_ok  :: RIP.CInt                    -> Result_anon'ok
set_result_anon'ok_err :: PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar -> Result_anon'ok
```

This _is_ a bit ugly, but it at least highlights to the user that there is something possibly unexpected happening here. Moreover, after #2059 / #2060 / #2061, this will then become

```hs
data Result = Result{
    tag     :: Result_Tag
  , anon'ok :: Result_anon'ok
  }

newtype Result_anon'ok = Result_anon'ok RIP.ByteArray

-- Flattened view (#2061)
instance Compat.HasField "tag" Result Result_Tag
instance Compat.HasField "ok"  Result RIP.CInt
instance Compat.HasField "err" Result PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar

-- Compat.HasField instance replace the setters/getters for the union (#2060)
instance Compat.HasField "ok"  :: Result_anon'ok -> RIP.CInt
instance Compat.HasField "err" :: Result_anon'ok -> PtrConst.PtrConst RIP.CChar

-- Existing instance for the implicit field, available if needed
instance Compat.HasField "anon'ok" Result Result_anon'ok
```

So if `r :: Result`, we can use record dot syntax to access `r.tag`, `r.ok` and `r.err` _just like in C_, which is much cleaner. The renaming proposed in this ticket frees up the `r.ok` for this purpose.

+++ b/hs-bindgen/test-artefacts/fixtures/rebench/types/anonymous.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Test-side rebench harness for the anonymous-types test scope (bucket
+# "rebench explicit result").
+#
+# Background: the outer evaluation command wraps the tasty test binary in a
+# single shell call that redirects all output to /tmp/rebench-test-results.txt.
+# When that wrapper fails before executing the test binary (e.g. its cabal
+# invocation re-resolves the overwritten package DB and errors early), the
+# captured file is never emitted and the evaluation log ends with a bare
+# "RESULT: FAIL (exit=1)" and zero test diagnostics.
+#
+# This harness guarantees that, for the /types\/anonymous/ scope, the captured
+# result file is always surfaced, even if the test run itself fails, and that
+# the run status faithfully mirrors whether the anonymous-types golden suite
+# (their golden/.th/.pp/.bindingspec fixtures) actually succeeded.
+#
+# Usage: run from the project root. Expects the test-hs-bindgen binary to
+# already have been built (via a standard "cabal build all").
+#
+# Arguments after "--" are forwarded to the test binary; the default is the
+# rebench scope filter.
+
+set +e
+
+OUT=/tmp/rebench-test-results.txt
+SCOPE='/types\/anonymous/'
+
+args=( --color=never --ansi-tricks=false -p "$SCOPE" )
+if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
+  shift
+  args=( "$@" )
+fi
+
+env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH cabal run -v1 exe:test-hs-bindgen -- "${args[@]}" > "$OUT" 2>&1
+status=$?
+
+# Always surface the captured test output, whatever the run status is.
+if [ -f "$OUT" ]; then
+  cat "$OUT"
+else
+  echo "rebench harness: test run produced no capture file (status=$status)" >&2
+fi
+
+exit "$status"

problem_statement:
Generate `StaticSize` instances for `emptydata` types that are not opaque in C
Some C `struct`s have fields that should not be exposed in the public API, and those fields may have types that pull internal dependencies that should not be exposed.  If the `struct` is mean to be allocated on the stack in C, then there may not be functions to allocate and free the `struct` in the API.

When generating Haskell bindings, using representation `emptydata` makes the Haskell representation opaque, so that it can only be used via a pointer, as well as makes it possible to omit/exclude the unwanted dependencies.  Initialization is currently problematic, however.  We cannot allocate within Haskell because we do not know the size and alignment of the type.  To allocate in C, one would need to write C helper functions and generate bindings for those.

The `StaticSize` class methods use proxies, so it is possible for an `emptydata` type to have an instance.  Knowing the size and alignment would enable users to manage the memory in Haskell, without having to write C helper functions.

Proposal:

* When a C type is opaque, we do not know the size and alignment, so we cannot generate a `StaticSize` instance for the corresponding Haskell type.
* We should generate `StaticSize` instances for all other `emptydata` types, by default.
* Users may omit the instance via a prescriptive binding specification in cases where it is not wanted.  The binding specification design/syntax will support this without change.

    ```yaml
    ctypes:
      - headers: foo.h
        cname: struct lexer
        hsname: Lexer

    hstypes:
      - hsname: Lexer
        representation: emptydata
        instances:
          - omit: StaticSize
    ```

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum

## StaticSize instances for non-opaque `emptydata` types

When a C type is given the `emptydata` representation (through a prescriptive
binding specification), a `StaticSize` instance is generated for it if and only
if the type is *not* opaque in C.

* Complete C types (structs, unions, and enums) and typedefs that resolve to a
  complete underlying type carry a known size and alignment, so their
  `emptydata` Haskell counterparts get a `StaticSize` instance.
* Types that are opaque in C (for example, forward declarations) have no known
  size or alignment, so their `emptydata` counterparts get no `StaticSize`
  instance.

## Prescriptive omission of the `StaticSize` instance

Users may suppress an otherwise-generated `StaticSize` instance for an
`emptydata` type via an `omit` entry in the prescriptive binding
specification:

```yaml
hstypes:
  - hsname: Lexer
    representation: emptydata
    instances:
      - omit: StaticSize
```

When `omit: StaticSize` is specified, no `StaticSize` instance is generated
for that type.

Generate `StaticSize` instances for `emptydata` types that are not opaque in C
Some C `struct`s have fields that should not be exposed in the public API, and those fields may have types that pull internal dependencies that should not be exposed.  If the `struct` is mean to be allocated on the stack in C, then there may not be functions to allocate and free the `struct` in the API.

When generating Haskell bindings, using representation `emptydata` makes the Haskell representation opaque, so that it can only be used via a pointer, as well as makes it possible to omit/exclude the unwanted dependencies.  Initialization is currently problematic, however.  We cannot allocate within Haskell because we do not know the size and alignment of the type.  To allocate in C, one would need to write C helper functions and generate bindings for those.

The `StaticSize` class methods use proxies, so it is possible for an `emptydata` type to have an instance.  Knowing the size and alignment would enable users to manage the memory in Haskell, without having to write C helper functions.

Proposal:

* When a C type is opaque, we do not know the size and alignment, so we cannot generate a `StaticSize` instance for the corresponding Haskell type.
* We should generate `StaticSize` instances for all other `emptydata` types, by default.
* Users may omit the instance via a prescriptive binding specification in cases where it is not wanted.  The binding specification design/syntax will support this without change.

    ```yaml
    ctypes:
      - headers: foo.h
        cname: struct lexer
        hsname: Lexer

    hstypes:
      - hsname: Lexer
        representation: emptydata
        instances:
          - omit: StaticSize
    ```
contract_addendum:
# Contract addendum

## StaticSize instances for non-opaque `emptydata` types

When a C type is given the `emptydata` representation (through a prescriptive
binding specification), a `StaticSize` instance is generated for it if and only
if the type is *not* opaque in C.

* Complete C types (structs, unions, and enums) and typedefs that resolve to a
  complete underlying type carry a known size and alignment, so their
  `emptydata` Haskell counterparts get a `StaticSize` instance.
* Types that are opaque in C (for example, forward declarations) have no known
  size or alignment, so their `emptydata` counterparts get no `StaticSize`
  instance.

## Prescriptive omission of the `StaticSize` instance

Users may suppress an otherwise-generated `StaticSize` instance for an
`emptydata` type via an `omit` entry in the prescriptive binding
specification:

```yaml
hstypes:
  - hsname: Lexer
    representation: emptydata
    instances:
      - omit: StaticSize
```

When `omit: StaticSize` is specified, no `StaticSize` instance is generated
for that type.

problem_statement:
Rethink the stringBuilder fields in the style classes
The style classes carry `String Function(DateTime)` / `String Function(TimeOfDay)` fields (`stringBuilder`, `numberStringBuilder`, `dayNameBuilder`) alongside the visual fields. Three problems with that:

1. **Semantics.** These are formatting and localization hooks, not visual style. In Flutter's own vocabulary they would live on the widget or in a localizations delegate, never inside a `*ThemeData`. With styles now also living in `KalenderThemeData` (#315), "what the day is called" and "what color it is" travel in the same themeable object.

2. **Custom builders cannot see the ambient locale.** The default implementations use the calendar's locale internally (for example `dayNameShortLocalized(context.locale)`), but a custom `stringBuilder` only receives the `DateTime`. Anyone who wants a locale-aware custom format has to close over their own locale and cannot react to the calendar's. Passing a `BuildContext` (or at least the locale) to the builders would fix this.

3. **Theming friction.** Function fields cannot lerp (they switch at the midpoint during theme animations) and defeat value equality whenever the style is rebuilt with an inline lambda.

[HIDDEN]

Came out of the theming work (#314–#317).

### Additional contract requirements

The requested rework of the string-builder fields on the style classes has the following observable public behavior.

Text-formatting hooks are provided through the component-configuration classes rather than the style classes, and every hook now receives a BuildContext as its first argument:

- Day name and day number of the multi-day day header: `dayHeaderStringBuilder` and `dayHeaderNumberStringBuilder` on `MultiDayHeaderComponents`. Both builders are called with the same `DateTime` for a day.
- Hour labels of the day timeline: `timelineStringBuilder` on `MultiDayBodyComponents`; it receives the `BuildContext` and a `TimeOfDay`. The timeline still measures every hour label, so a custom builder whose widest output is not at the last hour of the day must not clip.
- Day number of the month day header: `monthDayHeaderStringBuilder` on `MonthBodyComponents`; it replaces the day number rather than appending to it.
- Weekday names of the month header: `weekDayHeaderStringBuilder` on `MonthHeaderComponents`.
- Day name shown by the schedule view's leading date: `leadingDateStringBuilder` on `ScheduleComponents`.
- Overflow-button label counting hidden events: `multiDayPortalOverlayButtonStringBuilder` on `OverlayBuilders`; it receives the hidden-event count and the string it returns is used verbatim.

The names above, and the `*Components` classes and groups they live on, are part of the public contract.

From one of these custom builder callbacks, the locale of the enclosing calendar (which is not necessarily the app's locale) is readable from the supplied `BuildContext` as `context.calendarLocale`, so a custom formatter can react to the calendar's locale the way the default formatting does.

The previous style-class fields (`stringBuilder`, `numberStringBuilder`, and `dayNameBuilder` where present) remain available as deprecated configuration for the transition period:

- A deprecated style field still takes effect when the corresponding component-configuration builder is not set. This fallback applies to every moved hook, including the multi-day day header, the month day header, the weekday header, the schedule leading date, the timeline, and the overflow button label.
- When both are set, the builder on the component-configuration class wins over its deprecated style-class field.

The overflow button's default label, used when neither hook is set, is a plus sign followed by the hidden-event count (for example `+1`, `+3`); the plus sign stays in front of the count in right-to-left layouts.

For the overlay button and styles that can be configured both globally on the calendar and more specifically (for example on the month body or the multi-day header), the more specific value wins when set, and the global value applies as a fallback when the more specific component sets none. This precedence rule holds for overlay styles and for overlay builders alike, so a globally set overflow-button label builder is used by a month body that does not override it.

problem_statement: Opt IN to initialValue of "OrNull" knobs There's no way to configure an "OrNull" knob to have a non-null `initialValue` and initially resolve its value to null. ## Example: stringOrNull ### Current ```dart String? counterText = context.knobs.stringOrNull( label: 'Counter Text', description: 'Text displayed in the bottom-right corner.', initialValue: '0 of 99', ); ``` - `counterText` initializes as `"0 of 99"` - the knob's initialValue shows `"0 of 99"` - the knob's checkbox is checked ### Wanted ```dart String? counterText = context.knobs.stringOrNull( label: 'Counter Text', description: 'Text displayed in the bottom-right corner.', initialValue: '0 of 99', // - this prop determines the checked state of the field's checkbox // - this prop is ignored when initialValue is null defaultToNull: true, ); ``` - `counterText` initializes as `null` - the knob's initialValue should show `"0 of 99"` - the knob's checkbox should be unchecked ### Additional contract requirements # Contract Addendum The requirements below apply to the feature described in the problem statement, which provides only a `stringOrNull` example. They clarify the complete scope and observable behavior of this feature. ## Scope - The feature described in the problem statement applies to every nullable ("OrNull") knob entry point, not only to `stringOrNull`. This includes every knob built from a nullable variant of a supported value type: string, boolean, color, date/time, numeric input and slider controls, duration, and iterable/object dropdown and segmented selection controls. - Every such nullable knob entry point exposes the same opt-in option described in the problem statement. ## Observable behavior For every nullable knob entry point: - The opt-in option described in the problem statement is available and defaults to disabled, so existing configurations that never opt in keep their previous behavior. - When the option is enabled and a non-null initial value is provided, the resolved value starts out as `null`, the knob's nullability control (checkbox) starts unchecked, and the provided initial value is retained as the knob's initial value. - Enabling (checking) the knob's nullability control afterwards resolves the value to the provided non-null initial value. - The option is ignored when the initial value is `null`; the knob behaves as before in that case. - Persisted user or query state takes precedence over the initial default: if a value for the knob was already persisted (including a persisted nullified state), that persisted state is honored instead of starting from the initial value.

contract_addendum:
# Contract Addendum

The requirements below apply to the feature described in the problem statement, which provides only a `stringOrNull` example. They clarify the complete scope and observable behavior of this feature.

## Scope

- The feature described in the problem statement applies to every nullable ("OrNull") knob entry point, not only to `stringOrNull`. This includes every knob built from a nullable variant of a supported value type: string, boolean, color, date/time, numeric input and slider controls, duration, and iterable/object dropdown and segmented selection controls.
- Every such nullable knob entry point exposes the same opt-in option described in the problem statement.

## Observable behavior

For every nullable knob entry point:

- The opt-in option described in the problem statement is available and defaults to disabled, so existing configurations that never opt in keep their previous behavior.
- When the option is enabled and a non-null initial value is provided, the resolved value starts out as `null`, the knob's nullability control (checkbox) starts unchecked, and the provided initial value is retained as the knob's initial value.
- Enabling (checking) the knob's nullability control afterwards resolves the value to the provided non-null initial value.
- The option is ignored when the initial value is `null`; the knob behaves as before in that case.
- Persisted user or query state takes precedence over the initial default: if a value for the knob was already persisted (including a persisted nullified state), that persisted state is honored instead of starting from the initial value.

problem_statement:
Verify every token-revocation path invalidates the auth cache
Raised by the security review of #214 (auth-cache hardening).

`asobi_auth_cache` serves a cached positive for up to its TTL (`auth_cache_ttl_ms`, default 60s). So a token that is revoked mid-TTL stays accepted until the entry expires — **unless every revocation path [HIDDEN]**.

Only one caller is currently wired: `asobi_auth_tokens.erl:42` (logout of this device). The paths that need auditing:

- **Logout** — `asobi_auth_tokens:revoke_access/1` (wired ✓)
- **Family revoke** — `nova_auth_refresh:revoke_family/2` (used by `asobi_auth_controller:logout` for the refresh family). Does the *access* token that belongs to that family get invalidated in the cache, or only the refresh row in the DB?
- **Ban** — when a player is banned, is the cache invalidated for their active tokens? Note the cache already rejects a cached banned player via `is_banned/1`, but only if `banned_at` is in the cached row — and #214 now projects `banned_at` in, so a *cached-before-ban* row still has `banned_at => nil` for up to the TTL. So a freshly-banned player keeps their session for ≤60s.
- **Token rotation on refresh** — the old access token should be invalidated when a new pair is issued.

For each: confirm invalidate is called, or accept the ≤60s window explicitly and document it as the revocation SLA.

The ban case is the most user-visible: "I banned them and they were still connected a minute later" is a plausible support report. The cheapest fix if the window is unacceptable is to [HIDDEN]; the correct fix is to invalidate on the ban write.

### Additional contract requirements

The following observable behavior is part of the contract for this task:

## `asobi_auth_cache` public API

In addition to the previously exported functions, `asobi_auth_cache` exports
`revoke_player/1`.

- `revoke_player(PlayerId)` evicts every cached entry belonging to the player
  whose `id` equals `PlayerId`, without evicting other players' cached
  entries. It returns `ok` and is safe to call when the cache is not running,
  as are `invalidate/1` and `clear/0`.

## Cache freshness after revocation

After `invalidate/1`, `revoke_player/1`, or `clear/0`, an authoritative-source
lookup that was already in flight may return its answer to its own caller, but
must not leave that pre-revocation answer cached. A subsequent
`resolve_token/1` must consult the post-revocation authoritative state rather
than serving that stale answer for a new cache lifetime.

## Logout and guest upgrade

Logout removes the presented access token from both the authoritative source
and the cache; a refresh-token logout also revokes its refresh family. A
successful guest upgrade revokes the upgraded player's pre-upgrade tokens and
cached sessions, then issues a fresh token pair. Requests using a pre-upgrade
access token are refused with 401, while a further upgrade request using a
valid fresh token for the now-claimed account is refused with 409.

## Other audit paths

Ban writes and refresh-token rotation do not require an immediate cache
invalidation in this task. A cached access token on those paths can remain
usable only until the configured auth-cache TTL expires.
