@@ -19,24 +19,78 @@ a much shorter TTL (`asobi.auth_cache_negative_ttl_ms`, default
 5_000ms) so a fresh-token race doesn't keep returning errors after
 the token actually exists.
 
+## Revocation SLA (asobi#215)
+
+A revoked token's cache entry can outlive its DB row by up to
+`auth_cache_ttl_ms` unless the revoking code path also touches this
+cache. Audited as of asobi#215:
+
+- **Single-device logout** (`asobi_auth_tokens:revoke_access/1`) calls
+  `invalidate/1` for the one access token being logged out. Immediate.
+- **Mass revoke keyed by player** (any path that deletes more tokens
+  than the caller holds a single token for - e.g.
+  `asobi_guest_controller`'s guest-to-real upgrade, which calls
+  `nova_auth_refresh:revoke_all/2` for every token a player holds, or a
+  future ban/admin-suspend path) MUST call `revoke_player/1` right
+  after the DB-level revoke, passing the player id. The stored value
+  carries `id` (see `cacheable/1`), so a match-spec scan can target
+  every cached entry for one player without evicting every other
+  player's session; there is no need to reach for `clear/0` here.
+  "Targeted" is about blast radius, not cost: there is no secondary
+  index on `id`, so `revoke_player/1` is still an O(total cache size)
+  scan, same shape as `clear/0`'s `delete_all_objects/1`, not
+  O(that player's token count).
+- `clear/0` remains available for whole-table maintenance (test
+  teardown, an operator-triggered flush) but is intentionally NOT the
+  revocation primitive - a full clear scales with total cached
+  sessions rather than the one player being revoked, and is an easy
+  denial-of-service amplifier if wired to a client-reachable action.
+- **Refresh-token rotation** (`nova_auth_refresh:refresh/2`) does NOT
+  revoke the access token that was live before the rotation - by
+  `nova_auth`'s design, access tokens are short-lived bearer credentials
+  (60 min default, `asobi_auth:config/0`) that aren't tied to their
+  refresh token's rotation state, so there is nothing to invalidate here
+  even in principle. This is a `nova_auth` design characteristic, not an
+  `asobi_auth_cache` gap.
+
+## Revoke/read race
+
+`invalidate/1` and `revoke_player/1` only delete what's in the table
+*right now*. A `miss/1` already in flight (DB read returned, `put_positive/2`
+not yet called) can still land its write after the revoke, caching the
+stale row for a fresh TTL. `epoch/0` closes this: every revoke bumps a
+counter first, and `miss/1` only caches its read if the epoch it read
+before querying the DB is still current when the DB answers - otherwise
+a revoke happened mid-read and the result is served once, uncached.
+
 ## Process model
 
 A single named gen_server owns the ETS table. Lookups are direct ETS
 reads from any process; writes go through the gen_server only for
-expiry-sweep coordination — `put/2,3` and `invalidate/1` write
-directly via `public` ETS for latency. The gen_server runs a
-periodic sweep (every TTL/2) that removes expired rows so the table
-doesn't grow unbounded under attack.
+expiry-sweep coordination — `put/2,3`, `invalidate/1` and
+`revoke_player/1` write directly via `public` ETS for latency. The
+gen_server runs a periodic sweep (every TTL/2) that removes expired
+rows so the table doesn't grow unbounded under attack.

contract_addendum:
This addendum supplements the issue statement with additional behaviors that the
hidden suite also requires; any compliant implementation must satisfy all of the
following.

## Crossing failure robustness

When a player move crosses a zone boundary and the destination zone cannot be
started or acquired (its creation fails, e.g. the world has reached its zone
limit), the failed move is a no-op:

- The world must not crash, hang, or terminate. It keeps running and keeps all
  of its players tracked (the player count is unchanged).
- The player remains owned by their current zone: the world's membership
  records for that player still point at that zone, and the player's entity in
  that zone is completely untouched, including every script-maintained field
  beyond position and type.

The same robustness must also hold when the destination zone becomes
unavailable at a later internal hand-off step of the same move — for example a
first acquisition of the destination succeeds and a subsequent placement
attempt fails after some legs of the hand-off have already run. In that case:

- The world must not crash, hang, or terminate. It keeps running, keeps the
  player on its roster, and keeps a tracked position for the player that stays
  inside the world grid bounds.

## Result of a successful live-input crossing

When a live input carrying a new position causes a session player to cross into
a different zone:

- The player becomes owned by the destination zone: the world re-registers the
  player's zone membership, refreshes the membership records and interest
  subscriptions to surround the destination zone, and notifies the player
  process of its new owning zone so that subsequent input is routed there.
- A later live input sent to the destination zone is accepted normally by that
  zone: it is applied to the player's entity there.
- If the destination zone is created on demand by the crossing, it must
  continue receiving world ticks afterwards; a player rehomed by an input must
  not end up in a zone that stops ticking.

Any player-specific fields stored on the player's entity beyond its position
and type must be preserved across the crossing.

+    Ctx = #{world_pid := Pid, zone_mgr := Mgr} = start_world(#{lazy_zones => true}),

+    %% back to normal, a follow-up successful crossing still rehomes them
+    %% out of the origin zone.
+    asobi_world_server:move_player(Pid, ~"p1", {250.0, 250.0}),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, wait_until(
+        fun() ->
+            case asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {2, 2}) of
+                {ok, ZonePid2} -> maps:is_key(~"p1", asobi_zone:get_entities(ZonePid2));
+                not_loaded -> false
+            end
+        end,
+        3000
+    )),
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% A failure at a LATE step of the destination-zone hand-off - a first
+%% acquisition of the destination for this move succeeds, then a subsequent
+%% acquisition fails after some legs of the hand-off have already run, as
+%% could happen with a construction cache or a reap between the pre-check
+%% and the placement (asobi#258/#260 review) - is defensive rather than
+%% fatal. The stub fails exactly the SECOND ensure_zone call for {0,0}
+%% regardless of call ordering, so world servers that acquire the
+%% destination twice (pre-check + placement) genuinely exercise the
+%% late-failure path, while single-acquisition world servers fall back to
+%% the plain acquisition-failure no-op; both hand-offs are legal under the
+%% contract, which constrains only the outcomes: the world must not crash,
+%% hang, or terminate and it keeps running, it keeps the player on its
+%% roster, and the world's tracked position for the player stays inside the
+%% world grid bounds.
+move_zone_unavailable_after_removal_is_defensive() ->
+    Ctx = #{world_pid := Pid, zone_mgr := Mgr} = start_world(),
+    ok = asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1"),
+    timer:sleep(20),
+    {ok, ZonePid1} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {1, 1}),
+    ?assertMatch(#{x := 100.0, y := 100.0}, wait_entity_any(ZonePid1, ~"p1", 3000)),
+    asobi_zone:add_entity(ZonePid1, ~"p1", (maps:get(~"p1", asobi_zone:get_entities(ZonePid1)))#{hp => 42}),
+    Counter = counters:new(1, []),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun
+        (Ref, {0, 0} = Coords) ->
+            Nth = counters:get(Counter, 1) + 1,
+            counters:put(Counter, 1, Nth),
+            case Nth of
+                1 -> meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords]);
+                _ -> {error, max_zones_reached}
+            end;
+        (Ref, Coords) ->
+            meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords])
+    end),
+    try
+        asobi_world_server:move_player(Pid, ~"p1", {0.0, 0.0}),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        ?assertEqual(running, maps:get(status, asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid))),
+        ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid))),
+        %% Still a member of the world roster, and the world still holds a
+        %% tracked position for the player that stays inside the world grid
+        %% (the attempted move itself is in-bounds, so every accounting of
+        %% it - rejected, applied, or partially handed off - keeps the
+        %% position inside the grid).
+        {_StateName, WorldData0} = sys:get_state(Pid),
+        Players0 = maps:get(players, WorldData0),
+        ?assertMatch(#{~"p1" := _}, Players0),
+        P1Entry = maps:get(~"p1", Players0),
+        ?assert(is_map(P1Entry)),
+        #{position := {PX, PY}} = P1Entry,
+        ?assert(is_number(PX) andalso PX >= 0 andalso PX < 300),
+        ?assert(is_number(PY) andalso PY >= 0 andalso PY < 300)
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager)
+    end,
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% Helpers
+
+%% Poll the zone until the named entity is present; returns the entity map.
+wait_entity_any(ZonePid, EntityId, MsLeft) ->
+    case asobi_zone:get_entities(ZonePid) of
+        #{EntityId := Entity} ->
+            Entity;
+        #{} when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_entity_any(ZonePid, EntityId, MsLeft - 10);
+        #{} ->
+            {error, {no_entity, EntityId, ZonePid}}
+    end.
+
+%% Poll the zone until the named entity is present AND contains the expected
+%% field/value pairs; returns the entity map or {error, Reason}.
+wait_entity(ZonePid, EntityId, Expect, MsLeft) ->
+    case wait_entity_any(ZonePid, EntityId, 0) of
+        {error, _} when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_entity(ZonePid, EntityId, Expect, MsLeft - 10);
+        {error, Reason} ->
+            {error, Reason};
+        Entity ->
+            case maps:with(maps:keys(Expect), Entity) =:= Expect of
+                true ->
+                    Entity;
+                false when MsLeft > 0 ->
+                    timer:sleep(10),
+                    wait_entity(ZonePid, EntityId, Expect, MsLeft - 10);
+                false ->
+                    {error, maps:with(maps:keys(Expect), Entity)}
+            end
+    end.
+
+%% Extract the owning-zone coords from a player_zones entry, tolerating the
+%% record shapes implementations use ({zone, Coords} records or plain
+%% coords); test-local projection, never asserts a particular layout.
+zone_of_membership(Entry) when is_map(Entry) ->
+    maps:get(zone, Entry);
+zone_of_membership(Entry) ->
+    Entry.
+
+%% List the grid coords whose zone currently holds the entity; test-local
+%% accounting used to assert the entity exists exactly once across the
+%% world without pinning down which zone (or accounting strategy) holds it.
+count_entity_locations(Mgr, GridSize, EntityId) ->
+    [
+        {X, Y}
+     || X <- lists:seq(0, GridSize - 1),
+        Y <- lists:seq(0, GridSize - 1),
+        case asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {X, Y}) of
+            {ok, ZonePid} -> maps:is_key(EntityId, asobi_zone:get_entities(ZonePid));
+            not_loaded -> false
+        end
+    ].
+
+%% Poll until Pred returns true; tolerates the world's tick/cast ordering
+%% instead of asserting on one fixed sleep.
+wait_until(Pred, MsLeft) ->
+    case catch Pred() of
+        true ->
+            ok;
+        _ when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_until(Pred, MsLeft - 10);
+        _ ->
+            {error, timeout}
+    end.
+
+%% Wait for the player entity to appear in the destination zone after a
+%% live-input crossing; returns the entity map or {error, Reason}. The
+%% entity being owned by the destination zone is the contract-level outcome,
+%% independent of how or when the world performs the hand-off.
+wait_rehome(ZonePid, PlayerId, MsLeft) ->
+    case wait_entity_any(ZonePid, PlayerId, 0) of
+        {error, _} when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_rehome(ZonePid, PlayerId, MsLeft - 10);
+        Result ->
+            Result
+    end.
+
+%% Send move inputs to the given zone until the player's tracked entity
+%% reflects them; proves that zone accepts subsequent live input for the
+%% player. Returns the entity map or {error, Reason}.
+wait_applied_input(ZonePid, PlayerId, X, Y, MsLeft) ->
+    asobi_zone:player_input(ZonePid, PlayerId, #{
+        ~"action" => ~"move", ~"x" => X, ~"y" => Y
+    }),
+    case wait_entity(ZonePid, PlayerId, #{x => X, y => Y}, 0) of
+        {error, _} when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_applied_input(ZonePid, PlayerId, X, Y, MsLeft - 10);
+        Result ->
+            Result
+    end.
+
+zone_tick(ZonePid) ->
+    #{tick := Tick} = sys:get_state(ZonePid),
+    Tick.
+
+wait_zone_tick(ZonePid, MinTick, MsLeft) ->
+    case zone_tick(ZonePid) of
+        N when N >= MinTick ->
+            ok;
+        _ when MsLeft > 0 ->
+            timer:sleep(10),
+            wait_zone_tick(ZonePid, MinTick, MsLeft - 10);
+        _ ->
+            {error, {no_tick, MinTick}}
+    end.
+
 %% Small grid (grid_size=3) without explicit lazy_zones works like before
 small_grid_backward_compat() ->
     Ctx = #{world_pid := Pid, zone_mgr := Mgr} = start_world(#{grid_size => 3}),

problem_statement:
asobi_ws_handler's generic {asobi_message, _} catch-all silently drops unrecognized message shapes
Follow-up from the code review of #300 (fix for #297, game.broadcast binary event names).

`asobi_ws_handler.erl`'s catch-all clause for unrecognized `{asobi_message, X}` shapes (~line 233, the same general mechanism that let #297 go unnoticed for so long — it's what `{world_event, Event, Payload}` fell through to before #300 widened its specific guard) still silently returns `{ok, State}` for anything it doesn't recognize, with no log line. #300 fixed the two specific shapes that mattered, but the drop-with-no-signal mechanism itself is untouched, so the next producer that emits a new `{asobi_message, _}` variant will hit the exact same silent-failure class #297 was about.

## Expected

[HIDDEN], so a future silent-drop bug shows up in logs instead of requiring another multi-week bug-hunt to discover. Per this repo's DX-first-class philosophy: a failure mode that leaves a game developer unable to see why their script does nothing is a defect.

### Additional contract requirements

## Websocket unrecognized-message diagnostics

`asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info/2` continues to return `{ok, State}` for an
unrecognized message. Before doing so, it emits a warning report with
`event => ws_unhandled_info`. The report contains a bounded, sanitized `tag`
rather than the message payload: a bare atom is retained; for an
`{asobi_message, Inner}` value, the tag retains the `asobi_message` wrapper
and uses the atom identifying `Inner` (the first element when `Inner` is a
nonempty tuple); other values are represented by `unknown`.

Warnings are rate limited independently for each sanitized tag. Repeated
messages may therefore produce no warning while their tag's budget is
exhausted. When a later warning for that tag is allowed, its
`suppressed_since_last` field reports how many warnings for that tag were
suppressed since the preceding allowed warning. Recognized message shapes
keep their existing callback results and do not emit this unhandled-message
warning.

patch:
diff --git a/src/ws/asobi_ws_handler.erl b/src/ws/asobi_ws_handler.erl
index b6aacea..8dd7bca 100644
--- a/src/ws/asobi_ws_handler.erl
+++ b/src/ws/asobi_ws_handler.erl
@@ -8,6 +8,8 @@
 %% match./world. event stays inside the reserved namespace (#303).
 -export([reserved_event_names/0]).
 
+-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").
+
 -define(WS_MSG_LIMIT, 60).
 -define(WS_MSG_WINDOW_MS, 1000).
 -define(WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, 65536).
@@ -284,9 +286,44 @@ websocket_info(idle_auth_timeout, State) ->
     %% Race: the timer fired but session.connect already succeeded.
     %% Ignore.
     {ok, State};
-websocket_info(_Info, State) ->
+websocket_info(Info, State) ->
+    %% #308: dropping an unrecognised message with no signal is the exact
+    %% failure class #297 was - a producer's frame vanishing between the
+    %% game server and the socket, invisible to the game developer. The
+    %% drop itself stays (an unknown shape has no wire encoding), but it is
+    %% now observable. Rate-limited per tag because a per-tick producer
+    %% would otherwise log once per tick per connection.
+    log_unhandled_info(Info),
     {ok, State}.
 
+-spec log_unhandled_info(term()) -> ok.
+log_unhandled_info(Info) ->
+    Tag = unhandled_tag(Info),
+    case asobi_script_log_limiter:allow({?MODULE, Tag}) of
+        {true, DroppedSinceLastLog} ->
+            ?LOG_WARNING(#{
+                event => ws_unhandled_info,
+                tag => Tag,
+                suppressed_since_last => DroppedSinceLastLog
+            });
+        false ->
+            ok
+    end.
+
+%% Tag only, never the payload: an unhandled message may carry player data
+%% of unbounded size. Non-atom tags collapse to `unknown` so neither the log
+%% field nor the limiter's key space can be grown by a message sender.
+-spec unhandled_tag(term()) -> atom() | {asobi_message, atom()}.
+unhandled_tag({asobi_message, Inner}) -> {asobi_message, plain_tag(Inner)};
+unhandled_tag(Info) -> plain_tag(Info).
+
+-spec plain_tag(term()) -> atom().
+plain_tag(Tag) when is_atom(Tag) -> Tag;
+plain_tag(Tuple) when is_tuple(Tuple), tuple_size(Tuple) > 0, is_atom(element(1, Tuple)) ->
+    element(1, Tuple);
+plain_tag(_) ->
+    unknown.
+
 -spec terminate(term(), term(), map()) -> ok.
 terminate(_Reason, _Req, #{session := undefined}) ->
     asobi_telemetry:ws_disconnected(),

diff --git a/test/asobi_ws_handler_tests.erl b/test/asobi_ws_handler_tests.erl
index 1ce85dd..ceb1cdc 100644
--- a/test/asobi_ws_handler_tests.erl
+++ b/test/asobi_ws_handler_tests.erl
@@ -93,10 +93,76 @@ match_event_reserved_name_is_rejected_and_logged_test() ->
     ?assertEqual(#{namespace => ~"match", reason => reserved_event_name}, await_rejection()),
     ok = remove_log_capture().
 
+%% Unrecognized websocket-info messages are dropped, but the drop is observable.
+unknown_asobi_message_is_logged_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    Msg = {asobi_message, {brand_new_shape, #{~"a" => 1}}},
+    ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(Msg, #{})),
+    ?assertMatch(#{tag := {asobi_message, brand_new_shape}}, await_unhandled()),
+    ok = remove_log_capture().
+
+unknown_bare_message_is_logged_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(some_stray_message, #{})),
+    ?assertMatch(#{tag := some_stray_message}, await_unhandled()),
+    ok = remove_log_capture().
+
+non_atom_tag_collapses_to_unknown_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    Msg = {asobi_message, {~"from_the_wire", 1}},
+    ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(Msg, #{})),
+    ?assertMatch(#{tag := {asobi_message, unknown}}, await_unhandled()),
+    ok = remove_log_capture().
+
+handled_message_is_not_logged_as_unhandled_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    Msg = {asobi_message, {world_event, ~"pong", #{}}},
+    ?assertMatch({reply, {text, _}, _}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(Msg, #{})),
+    ?assertEqual(no_log, await_no_unhandled()),
+    ok = remove_log_capture().
+
+%% A value outside the bare-atom and {asobi_message, Inner} tag cases has
+%% no safe identifying atom and is reported as unknown.
+unrelated_tuple_tag_collapses_to_unknown_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info({123, opaque}, #{})),
+    ?assertMatch(#{tag := unknown}, await_unhandled()),
+    ok = remove_log_capture().
+
+%% Repeated occurrences of one tag must not prevent a different tag from
+%% producing its own warning.  The number of warnings for either tag is
+%% intentionally not tied to a particular limiter capacity.
+rate_limited_tags_are_independent_test() ->
+    ok = install_log_capture(),
+    try
+        Repeated = {asobi_message, {repeated_diagnostic, #{}}},
+        Independent = {asobi_message, {independent_diagnostic, #{}}},
+        lists:foreach(
+            fun(_) -> ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(Repeated, #{})) end,
+            lists:seq(1, 20)
+        ),
+        ?assertEqual({ok, #{}}, asobi_ws_handler:websocket_info(Independent, #{})),
+        Reports = collect_unhandled(21, []),
+        ?assert(lists:member({asobi_message, independent_diagnostic}, [maps:get(tag, R) || R <- Reports])),
+        ?assert(lists:all(fun(R) -> maps:is_key(suppressed_since_last, R) end, Reports))
+    after
+        _ = remove_log_capture()
+    end.
+
+collect_unhandled(0, Acc) ->
+    lists:reverse(Acc);
+collect_unhandled(Remaining, Acc) ->
+    receive
+        {ws_unhandled_info, Report} -> collect_unhandled(Remaining - 1, [Report | Acc])
+    after 20 ->
+        lists:reverse(Acc)
+    end.
+
 %% --- log capture helpers ---
 
 install_log_capture() ->
-    logger:add_handler(?MODULE, ?MODULE, #{level => warning, config => #{pid => self()}}).
+    _ = logger:remove_handler(?MODULE),
+    ok = logger:add_handler(?MODULE, ?MODULE, #{level => warning, config => #{pid => self()}}).
 
 remove_log_capture() ->
     logger:remove_handler(?MODULE).
@@ -107,6 +173,9 @@ remove_log_capture() ->
 log(#{msg := {report, #{msg := ~"game_broadcast_rejected"} = Report}}, #{config := #{pid := Pid}}) ->
     Pid ! {game_broadcast_rejected, maps:with([namespace, reason], Report)},
     ok;
+log(#{msg := {report, #{event := ws_unhandled_info} = Report}}, #{config := #{pid := Pid}}) ->
+    Pid ! {ws_unhandled_info, maps:with([tag, suppressed_since_last], Report)},
+    ok;
 log(_Event, _Config) ->
     ok.
 
@@ -116,3 +185,17 @@ await_rejection() ->
     after 1000 ->
         error(timeout_waiting_for_rejection_log)
     end.
+
+await_unhandled() ->
+    receive
+        {ws_unhandled_info, Report} -> Report
+    after 1000 ->
+        error(timeout_waiting_for_unhandled_log)
+    end.
+
+await_no_unhandled() ->
+    receive
+        {ws_unhandled_info, Report} -> {unexpected, Report}
+    after 200 ->
+        no_log
+    end.

problem_statement:
NPC crossing into an unloaded zone is destroyed; a player crossing the same boundary gets ensure_zone
## What

A player crossing into a zone that isn't loaded gets it created: `asobi_world_server:handle_move/4` calls `asobi_zone_manager:ensure_zone/2` for the target coords and only logs `move_zone_unavailable` if *creation* fails (widgrensit/asobi#258 hardened this ordering so a failed crossing is a no-op for the player).

An NPC crossing the same boundary does a bare `pg:get_members(?PG_SCOPE, {asobi_zone, WorldId, TargetCoords})` in `asobi_zone:resolve_zone_crossings/1` and is deleted outright on a miss (now logged/telemetried as of widgrensit/asobi#248's zone-crossing cleanup follow-up, but still deleted).

With `lazy_zones` (a real, supported config), an unloaded neighbour is the normal state, not an exotic one - so today: player walks east into an unloaded zone, fine; NPC walks east into the same unloaded zone, ceases to exist.

## Why not fixed inline

[HIDDEN]

## Where

- `src/world/asobi_zone.erl`, `resolve_zone_crossings/1`'s NPC transfer branch (currently drops on `pg:get_members` miss).
- Compare with `src/world/asobi_world_server.erl`'s player crossing path (`handle_move/4`), which calls `ensure_zone/2` first.

### Additional contract requirements

The NPC zone-crossing outcomes that complete this task's contract:

- An NPC crossing a zone boundary into a target zone that is not currently loaded has that zone created for it, the same way a player crossing into an unloaded zone does. On success the NPC is moved out of its current zone and arrives as a live entity in the newly created (or already existing) target zone.

- When a new zone is created for a crossing NPC, the established world-zone subscription lifecycle for a lazily created zone runs exactly as it does for a zone created by a player crossing: every already-connected player whose interest ring covers the new zone's coordinates is subscribed (backfilled) to the new zone, and receives its current entities, immediately.

- An NPC whose target zone cannot be resolved is never destroyed. This covers both a zone whose world provides no way to create the missing target zone, and a creation attempt that the zone manager explicitly refuses. In each case the NPC remains a live member of its current zone, with its position clamped back inside that zone's bounds, exactly as a denied (for example rate-limited) player crossing is already retained and clamped.

- A denied NPC crossing remains observable the way an unresolvable spawn is already observable: a `zone_unavailable` game-error event is emitted carrying the target coordinates, the entity id, and a reason detail that says why the target could not be resolved. The reason identifies the failure branch: it is `no_zone_manager` when the current zone has no zone manager capable of creating the target, and it carries the manager's own error term when creation was refused.

+%% neighbour is the normal state, and an NPC crossing into one used to be

+    Ctx =

problem_statement:
GET /api/v1/matches/live dispatches to show/1: live/1 has never been reachable
`GET /api/v1/matches/live` never reaches `asobi_match_controller:live/1`. It dispatches to `show/1` with `id = "live"`.

## Mechanism

`src/asobi_router.erl:67-69` declares, in this order:

```erlang
{~"/matches",      fun asobi_match_controller:index/1, ...},
{~"/matches/live", fun asobi_match_controller:live/1,  ...},
{~"/matches/:id",  fun asobi_match_controller:show/1,  ...},
```

[HIDDEN]

## Impact

- `live/1` is exported (`src/controllers/asobi_match_controller.erl:3`) and implemented (`:24`, `:38`), and is dead code.
- Documented as a supported endpoint: `guides/rest-api.md:115` ("Live, joinable matches") and `:124` describes it as what a lobby uses.
- **Four SDKs call it**: `asobi-godot/addons/asobi/api/asobi_matches.gd`, `asobi-unity/Runtime/Api/AsobiMatches.cs`, `asobi-defold/asobi/api/matches.lua`, `asobi-dart/lib/src/api/matches.dart`.
- **No test covers it.** `grep -rn "matches/live\|live/1" test/` returns nothing, which is why it survived.

Callers get whatever `show/1` does with a non-UUID id rather than a live-match list, so the documented lobby flow does not work on those four SDKs.

problem_statement:
asobi_world_ticker has no back-pressure: a slow zone accumulates ticks without bound
Version: 0.72.5 (checked against main / v0.73.3 — unchanged)

What happens
asobi_world_ticker:handle_info(tick, State) fans a tick cast out to every active zone and immediately re-arms itself:

[HIDDEN]
Nothing consults pending. pending is filled on fan-out and drained by {tick_done, ZonePid, TickN}, but it only gates post_tick — it never delays or skips the next fan-out. So a zone whose zone_tick callback takes longer than tick_rate receives ticks faster than it can retire them, and its mailbox grows without bound.

That alone would be a queue. What makes it terminal is the interaction with the zone's Lua state:

luerl (1.5.x, as used here) never collects the zone VM's heap on its own, so an occupied zone's state grows monotonically.
Every eval copies that state into the eval worker, so eval cost grows with the heap.
Once an eval exceeds tick_rate, (1) and (2) are now fed by a backlog: the zone spends every scheduler slice on stale ticks, the mailbox grows, the node's memory grows with it.
The game-side mitigations (a periodic collectgarbage() inside zone_tick, releasing an unwatched zone's entities so the reaper can stop it) are all carried BY a tick — so they queue behind the backlog exactly when they are most needed.
What we measured
Production, single node, one pilot playing for a while and then logging off:

two zone processes at 81 MB and 179 MB of Erlang heap, with 802 and 527 tick casts queued and both queues still growing;
one reap cast sitting behind 800 ticks;
CPU pinned at the pod's 2-core limit and memory climbing ~370 MB per 30 s with nobody online, until the pod was restarted.
On a dev node the same shape starts as soon as a zone's tick approaches the 80 ms tick rate; below that it is invisible, which is why this only shows up under real play.

Suggested fix
Skip a zone that has not retired the previous tick, e.g. keep the pending map across the fan-out and drop zones still in it:

[HIDDEN]
A dropped tick is strictly better than a queued one here: the zone tick is idempotent upkeep, the next tick carries the same work, and the alternative is an unbounded queue. Emitting a telemetry counter for skipped ticks would also make the condition visible before it becomes terminal — today the only symptom is CPU.

A second, cheaper guard: cap the mailbox by having asobi_zone refuse a tick whose TickN is more than N behind Tick, since a stale tick is pure waste.

### Additional contract requirements

In addition to the problem statement, the following behavior is required.

## World ticker back-pressure

- `asobi_world_ticker` tracks which zones have an unretired tick. On every
  fan-out, a zone that has not yet reported completion of the tick it was
  last sent is skipped: it is not sent that tick at all (its mailbox must not
  accumulate further `tick` casts). The ticker's own tick counter still
  advances on ticks that skip zones.
- Skipping is per zone and per tick. A zone that completes its outstanding
  tick is sent every later tick, including while other zones are being
  skipped; a skipped zone that then reports completion of the tick it
  received is ticked again on the next fan-out.
- `asobi_world_ticker:tick_done(TickerPid, ZonePid, TickN)` must release a
  zone even when `TickN` is older than the ticker's current tick number. In
  other words, a reply that arrives after the ticker has already skipped one
  or more ticks still retires that zone, so the next fan-out reaches it
  again. A reply must never leave a zone permanently barred from ticking.
- Removing a zone excludes it from later fan-outs. A removed zone is never
  sent another tick, while the remaining zones continue to be considered
  independently.

- Completion notifications are safe to receive out of order: accepting a
  late completion for one zone must not make another zone stop receiving
  later fan-outs.

- While at least one zone is being skipped, exactly one
  `[asobi, zone, tick_skipped]` event is emitted per world tick, with
  measurements `#{count => N}` where `N` is the number of zones skipped by
  that fan-out, and metadata containing the world's `world_id`. No
  `tick_skipped` event is emitted on any tick that skips nothing. The event
  is emitted for every skipping tick; it is not subject to the sampled
  `[asobi, world, tick]` emission interval.

## Lua state collector

The Lua state of a long-lived zone or match is never collected by Luerl on
its own, while every per-tick encode accumulates in it and every call copies
the whole state into the eval worker, so the state (and the per-tick cost)
grows without bound. The Lua bridge therefore provides periodic collection
of a bridge state:

- `asobi_lua_loader:collect_state/1` takes and returns a bridge-state map.
  When the map carries a `lua_state`, it periodically runs the Luerl
  collector over that state and returns the updated map. A map without a
  `lua_state` entry is returned unchanged, and the collection bookkeeping a
  bridge threads back (interval, countdown, enabled) is a map under the
  `lua_gc` key of the same state map.
- Collection actually reclaims per-tick garbage: after enough ticks the
  collected state is substantially smaller than the uncollected one, and
  with regular collection the state size stops growing with the number of
  ticks taken (a bounded steady state).
- A value the bridge holds between callbacks (notably `game_state`) is
  transiently protected across each collection: it and every table reachable
  from it survive collection, tick callbacks keep working on a collected
  state, and the protection is not left behind in the Lua global environment
  afterwards.
- Setting the `lua_gc` environment key to `false` disables the collector:
  states are then returned uncollected, and the returned bookkeeping
  reflects that the collector is disabled. The setting honors the legacy
  `asobi_lua` application env first and falls back to the `asobi`
  application env, matching every other Lua runtime knob - a deployment
  still carrying `{asobi_lua, [{lua_gc, false}]}` keeps the exact behaviour
  it had, and when both applications set the key the `asobi_lua` value wins.
- The interval between collections adapts to measured collection cost.
  The test-build inspection helper `asobi_lua_loader:next_gc/3` receives a
  duration in microseconds, the current interval, and the bookkeeping map;
  it is available only to the test build. A duration above 5,000 microseconds
  doubles the interval, a duration below 1,250 microseconds halves it, and
  other durations leave it unchanged. Intervals are clamped between 8 and
  1,024 ticks, and the returned countdown is reset to the resulting interval.
  Durations above 500,000 microseconds disable that state's collector.
- If one collection costs far more than the bounded growth it prevents, the
  collector permanently disables itself for that state (logging a warning)
  rather than freezing the zone, and the state's contents are left exactly
  as the collection found them.

## Collection on the callback paths

Collection only pays off if the long-lived Lua states actually pass through
it, so it is carried by the callbacks themselves, not only by fresh
fan-outs:

- The world bridge's per-zone tick callback runs the collector over the
  zone's bridge state after the callback's Lua call and threads the updated
  state and bookkeeping back.
- The match bridge's per-tick callback likewise runs the collector on the
  match's bridge state every tick.
- Disabling the collector through `lua_gc` applies on these paths too, and
  never disables the callbacks themselves: a disabled collector leaves the
  tick result and game state advancing exactly as before, just uncollected.

+## Lua memory

+Luerl never collects a long-lived Lua state on its own. Every tick, asobi
+encodes the zone's entities into that state as fresh Lua tables, and nothing
+in Luerl reclaims them - so an occupied zone's Lua heap grows for as long as
+anyone is in it. Because each Lua callback runs in a spawned worker, the whole
+state is copied into that worker and back on every tick, and the cost of a tick
+therefore grows with everything the zone has ever encoded. Left alone, a busy
+zone eventually takes longer to tick than the tick rate, at which point the
+world ticker starts skipping it (see [Observability](observability.md) for the
+`[asobi, zone, tick_skipped]` counter).

+not fixed: Luerl's collector walks the whole live set with a cost that grows
+faster than linearly, so asobi times each collection and adapts. A zone holding
+little across ticks gets collected often, which keeps both the collection and
+the per-tick copies cheap. A zone holding a large table across ticks gets
+collected rarely, because each collection is expensive and reclaims the same
+per-tick garbage either way.

+between callbacks is more expensive than what it allocates inside one.** A
+`game_state` holding a table of ten thousand rows is paid for on every
+collection; the same rows rebuilt per tick and dropped are not. If a
+collection ever runs longer than a tick budget, asobi logs

+the fix is to keep less alive across callbacks.

+`call/4` copies the whole state into its eval worker and back on every

+allocated. Collect on the calling process: it costs no extra copy there, and
+`luerl:gc/1` runs no Lua code so it cannot hang on a script.

+unreachable from the Lua root set while Erlang is between them, so the
+collector would free the tables underneath it and the next `luerl:decode/2`

+and unrooted again straight after, so a script never observes the anchor.

+    {St, Gc};
+maybe_gc(St, _Anchor, #{countdown := N} = Gc) when N > 1 ->
+    {St, Gc#{countdown := N - 1}};
+maybe_gc(St, Anchor, #{interval := Interval} = Gc) ->
+    case gc_disabled() of
+        true ->
+            {St, Gc#{enabled := false}};
+        false ->
+            {Us, St1} = timer:tc(fun() -> collect(St, Anchor) end),
+            {St1, next_gc(Us, Interval, Gc)}
+    end.
+
+next_gc(Us, Interval, Gc) when Us > ?GC_ABANDON_US ->
+    ?LOG_WARNING(#{

+        duration_ms => Us div 1000,
+        msg =>

+        error -> St

+        _ -> error
+    end.
+
+unanchor(St) ->
+    case luerl:set_table_keys([?GC_ANCHOR], nil, St) of

+        _ -> St
+    end.

index 4370e13..1fd8f77 100644
--- a/test/asobi_lua_loader_tests.erl
+++ b/test/asobi_lua_loader_tests.erl
@@ -44,6 +44,256 @@ loader_test_() ->
             fun is_defined_true_for_non_function_global/0}

+%% --- the periodic Luerl collector ---
+%%
+%% Luerl never collects a long-lived state on its own, so every per-tick
+%% `luerl:encode/2` accumulates in it forever and every call copies the whole
+%% state into the eval worker. These pin the three properties that make
+%% collecting safe: it actually reclaims, the caller's `game_state` survives
+%% it, and it stops collecting rather than freezing a zone whose live set is
+%% too large for Luerl's quadratic mark.
+
+collector_test_() ->
+    {foreach, fun unset_gc_env/0, fun(_) -> unset_gc_env() end, [
+        {"collecting reclaims the per-tick encode garbage", fun collect_reclaims/0},
+        {"game_state survives a collection", fun game_state_survives/0},
+        {"the anchor is invisible to the script", fun anchor_is_not_left_behind/0},
+        {"a collected state keeps ticking", fun collected_state_keeps_ticking/0},
+        {"the state reaches a steady size", fun steady_state_size/0},
+        {"a state with no lua_state is untouched", fun no_lua_state_is_untouched/0},
+        {"asobi lua_gc=false disables the collector", fun env_disables_collector/0},
+        {"legacy asobi_lua lua_gc=false disables the collector", fun legacy_env_disables_collector/0},
+        {"the legacy asobi_lua value wins when both are set", fun legacy_env_takes_precedence/0},
+        {"the interval backs off above the documented cost budget", fun interval_backs_off/0},
+        {"the interval stays bounded for cheap collections", fun interval_stays_bounded/0},
+        {"an uncollectable live set abandons the collector", fun huge_live_set_abandons/0}
+    ]}.
+
+unset_gc_env() ->
+    application:unset_env(asobi_lua, lua_gc),
+    application:unset_env(asobi, lua_gc),
+    ok.
+
+collect_reclaims() ->
+    S0 = gc_zone_state(),
+    Ticked = tick_n(S0, 200),
+    Uncollected = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, Ticked)),
+    Collected = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, collect(Ticked))),
+    ?assert(Collected * 4 < Uncollected).
+
+%% The collector frees anything the Lua root set cannot reach. game_state is
+%% held only by asobi between callbacks, so without protection this decode
+%% crashes on a freed table - the failure mode that makes a naive `luerl:gc/1`
+%% here worse than the leak.
+game_state_survives() ->
+    S = collect(tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 50)),
+    #{lua_state := St, game_state := GS} = S,
+    ?assertEqual([{~"n", 50}], luerl:decode(GS, St)).
+
+anchor_is_not_left_behind() ->
+    #{lua_state := St} = collect(tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 20)),
+    ?assertMatch({ok, nil, _}, luerl:get_table_keys([~"__asobi_gc_anchor"], St)).
+
+collected_state_keeps_ticking() ->
+    S = tick_n(collect(tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 50)), 25),
+    #{lua_state := St, game_state := GS} = S,
+    ?assertEqual([{~"n", 75}], luerl:decode(GS, St)).
+
+%% The point of the fix: size stops tracking total ticks taken. Without the
+%% collector this grows without bound for as long as the zone is occupied.
+steady_state_size() ->
+    S1 = collect_every_tick(gc_zone_state(), 300),
+    S2 = collect_every_tick(S1, 300),
+    Size1 = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, S1)),
+    Size2 = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, S2)),
+    ?assert(Size2 < Size1 * 2).
+
+no_lua_state_is_untouched() ->
+    ?assertEqual(#{some => thing}, asobi_lua_loader:collect_state(#{some => thing})).
+
+env_disables_collector() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi, lua_gc, false),
+    Ticked = tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 200),
+    Before = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, Ticked)),
+    Collected = collect(Ticked),
+    ?assertEqual(Before, erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, Collected))),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, Collected).
+
+%% The Lua runtime's knobs were historically configured under the asobi_lua
+%% application; a deployment still carrying that config must keep the exact
+%% behaviour it had.
+legacy_env_disables_collector() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi_lua, lua_gc, false),
+    Ticked = tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 200),
+    Before = erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, Ticked)),
+    Collected = collect(Ticked),
+    ?assertEqual(Before, erts_debug:flat_size(maps:get(lua_state, Collected))),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, Collected).
+
+legacy_env_takes_precedence() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi, lua_gc, true),
+    application:set_env(asobi_lua, lua_gc, false),
+    ?assertMatch(
+        #{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, collect(tick_n(gc_zone_state(), 200))
+    ).
+
+%% The test-build helper makes the externally documented cost-band policy
+%% deterministic: a collection just above the budget doubles the interval.
+interval_backs_off() ->
+    Gc = #{interval => 8, countdown => 1, enabled => true},
+    ?assertMatch(
+        #{interval := 16, countdown := 16, enabled := true},
+        asobi_lua_loader:next_gc(5001, 8, Gc)
+    ).
+
+%% The interval is bounded, not free-running: it is always at least 1, the
+%% countdown never runs past the interval it counts down from, and no finite
+%% number of collections can push the interval past a fixed ceiling (a cheap
+%% state does not collect every tick forever, an expensive one is not starved
+%% either). The exact clamp values are intentionally not pinned here.
+interval_stays_bounded() ->
+    S1 = collect_every_tick(gc_zone_state(), 100),
+    #{interval := Interval, countdown := Countdown, enabled := true} = maps:get(lua_gc, S1),
+    ?assert(Interval >= 1),
+    ?assert(Interval =< 1000000),
+    ?assert(Countdown >= 0),
+    ?assert(Countdown =< Interval).
+
+%% Past the abandon ceiling a single collection costs more than the leak it
+%% prevents, so the collector stops rather than freezing the zone for seconds
+%% at a time. The state is left exactly as the collection found it.
+huge_live_set_abandons() ->
+    S = collect(big_state(20000)),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, S),
+    ?assert(is_list(gs_world(S))).
+
+big_state(Rows) ->
+    #{lua_state := St0} = S0 = gc_zone_state(),
+    {ok, [Big | _], St1} = asobi_lua_loader:call(big_state, [Rows], St0),
+    S0#{lua_state => St1, game_state => Big}.
+
+%% Proves the protection held: the persistent table is still reachable through
+%% the ref asobi kept, whether the collection ran or was abandoned.
+gs_world(#{lua_state := St, game_state := GS}) ->
+    {ok, World, _} = luerl:get_table_key(GS, ~"world", St),
+    luerl:decode(World, St).
+
+gc_zone_state() ->
+    gc_zone_state(#{}).
+
+gc_zone_state(Extra) ->
+    {ok, St} = asobi_lua_loader:new(fixture("gc_zone.lua")),
+    {ok, [GS | _], St1} = asobi_lua_loader:call(init, [nil], St),
+    Extra#{lua_state => St1, game_state => GS}.
+
+%% Mirrors what asobi_lua_world:zone_tick/2 does per tick: encode the entity
+%% map fresh (this is the garbage) and call into the script.
+tick_n(State, 0) ->
+    State;
+tick_n(#{lua_state := St, game_state := GS} = State, N) ->
+    {Enc, St1} = luerl:encode(entities(), St),
+    {ok, [_Ents, GS1 | _], St2} = asobi_lua_loader:call(zone_tick, [Enc, GS], St1),
+    tick_n(State#{lua_state => St2, game_state => GS1}, N - 1).
+
+collect_every_tick(State, 0) ->
+    State;
+collect_every_tick(State, N) ->
+    collect_every_tick(collect(tick_n(State, 1)), N - 1).
+
+collect(State) ->
+    asobi_lua_loader:collect_state(State#{
+        lua_gc => #{interval => 1, countdown => 1, enabled => true}
+    }).
+
+entities() ->
+    #{
+        integer_to_binary(I) => #{~"x" => I, ~"y" => I, ~"type" => ~"npc", ~"hp" => 100}
+     || I <- lists:seq(1, 20)
+    }.
+
+%% --- collection through the callback paths ---
+%%
+%% The collector only pays off if the long-lived Lua states actually pass
+%% through it: the world bridge's per-zone tick callback and the match
+%% bridge's per-tick callback. These build each bridge state through the
+%% bridge's own initialisation - exactly what a zone process and a match
+%% server start from - and then drive the callbacks directly.
+
+zone_bridge_test_() ->
+    {foreach, fun unset_gc_env/0, fun(_) -> unset_gc_env() end, [
+        {"zone_tick threads collector bookkeeping", fun zone_tick_collects/0},
+        {"zone_tick honors the disabled collector", fun zone_tick_honors_disabled/0},
+        {"repeated zone ticks stay collected and keep ticking", fun zone_ticks_keep_ticking/0}
+    ]}.
+
+match_bridge_test_() ->
+    {foreach, fun unset_gc_env/0, fun(_) -> unset_gc_env() end, [
+        {"match tick threads collector bookkeeping", fun match_tick_collects/0},
+        {"match tick honors the disabled collector", fun match_tick_honors_disabled/0}
+    ]}.
+
+zone_tick_collects() ->
+    %% A bridge starts with no collector map. After its normal callback path
+    %% has run, that map must be threaded back to its caller.
+    {_, State1} = asobi_lua_world:zone_tick(#{}, gc_world_state()),
+    ?assertMatch(#{interval := _, countdown := _, enabled := _}, maps:get(lua_gc, State1)).
+
+zone_tick_honors_disabled() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi, lua_gc, false),
+    Start = (gc_world_state())#{lua_gc => #{interval => 8, countdown => 1, enabled => true}},
+    {_, State1} = asobi_lua_world:zone_tick(#{}, Start),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, State1),
+    %% Disabling collection does not disable the callback itself.
+    ?assertEqual(1, world_ticks(State1)).
+
+zone_ticks_keep_ticking() ->
+    Start = gc_world_state(),
+    Collected = collected_zone_ticks(Start, 16),
+    ?assertEqual(16, world_ticks(Collected)),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := true}}, Collected),
+    {_, State1} = asobi_lua_world:zone_tick(#{}, Collected),
+    ?assertEqual(17, world_ticks(State1)).
+
+%% Run the world bridge's zone tick callback N times, carrying exactly the
+%% state the bridge itself carries between ticks.
+collected_zone_ticks(State, 0) ->
+    State;
+collected_zone_ticks(State, N) ->
+    {_, State1} = asobi_lua_world:zone_tick(#{}, State),
+    collected_zone_ticks(State1, N - 1).
+
+%% Same loop with the collector disabled by config, so any size difference in
+%% collected_zone_ticks is the collector's doing rather than the callback's.
+
+gc_world_state() ->
+    {ok, State} = asobi_lua_world:init(#{lua_script => fixture("gc_world.lua")}),
+    State.
+
+world_ticks(#{lua_state := St, game_state := GS}) ->
+    {ok, N, _} = luerl:get_table_key(GS, ~"ticks", St),
+    N.
+
+match_tick_collects() ->
+    {ok, State1} = asobi_lua_match:tick(match_state()),
+    ?assertMatch(#{interval := _, countdown := _, enabled := _}, maps:get(lua_gc, State1)),
+    ?assertEqual(1, match_tick_count(State1)).
+
+match_tick_honors_disabled() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi, lua_gc, false),
+    Start = (match_state())#{lua_gc => #{interval => 8, countdown => 1, enabled => true}},
+    {ok, State1} = asobi_lua_match:tick(Start),
+    ?assertMatch(#{lua_gc := #{enabled := false}}, State1),
+    ?assertEqual(1, match_tick_count(State1)).
+
+match_state() ->
+    {ok, St} = asobi_lua_loader:new(fixture("gc_match.lua")),
+    {ok, [GS | _], St1} = asobi_lua_loader:call(init, [nil], St),
+    #{lua_state => St1, game_state => GS}.
+
+match_tick_count(#{lua_state := St, game_state := GS}) ->
+    {ok, N, _} = luerl:get_table_key(GS, ~"tick_count", St),
+    N.
+

problem_statement:
Support pluralization
Pluralizations in Gettext use the `ngettext` macro (and variants):

```elixir
ngettext("One error", "%{count} errors", 3)
```

Unfortunately sigils can only have a single binary argument (and modifiers). In order to support pluralization, we need a way to split the provided sigil string into a singular and plural part, for example by using a special character(s) like `|` (pipe):

```elixir
~t"One error|#{count} errors"
~t"One error|#{count :: length(errors)} errors"
```

Some other thoughts:

- the splitting character(s) should be configurable
- the `count` interpolation value must be passed as argument, not binding. A missing `count` interpolation should generate an exception at compile time.
- we could require a special sigil modifier (like `N`) to enable pluralization or even add a different sigil.

```elixir
~t"One error‖#{count} errors"N

~TN"One error‖#{count :: length(errors)} errors"

```

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum fully specifies the pluralization contract for the `~t` sigil and supersedes the exploratory alternatives (single-pipe separator, dedicated sigil) mentioned in the base statement. Implementations must conform to the following observable behavior.

## Activation

- Pluralization happens only when the sigil carries the `N` modifier (for example `~t"..."N`). Sigil modifiers are otherwise lowercase and user-configured; `N` is a reserved uppercase modifier, may appear in any order together with other modifiers, and must not be registered as a user-defined modifier.
- Without the `N` modifier the separator character sequence, if present, is treated as literal text and the sigil behaves exactly as before.

## Separator

- With the `N` modifier, the message string must contain exactly one separator that splits it into a singular part (before the separator) and a plural part (after the separator).
- The default separator is the two-character binary `"||"`.
- The separator is configurable per use of `GettextSigils` through the keyword option `pluralization: [separator: <binary>]`, supplied either directly to `use GettextSigils` or within its existing `sigils:` options. When a custom separator is configured, the default separator `"||"` is treated as literal text. The custom separator is then the only recognized separator for sigils generated with those options.
- Examples (with the default separator):
  - `~t"One error||#{count} errors"N`
  - `~t"One user||#{count :: length(users)} users"N`

## Count and interpolation

- The sigil must produce a `count` interpolation, in either part, written as `#{count}` for an in-scope variable or `#{count :: <expression>}` with the explicit-key syntax. The `count` value is passed separately to Gettext as the plural count `n`; it is not expanded as part of the translated message text with the other interpolations, while all other interpolations behave as they do for non-plural sigils (they are expanded in the resolved message and remain available as interpolation bindings).

## Errors

All of the following are `ArgumentError` failures raised at compile time; only the semantic content of the messages is part of the contract, not their exact wording. The message must convey:

- that the `N` modifier was used but the required separator is missing from the message;
- that more than one separator is present in the message;
- that pluralization requires a `"count"` binding but none was provided.

## Options

- `use GettextSigils` accepts a `pluralization` keyword whose value must be a keyword list supporting only the key `:separator`. The separator must be a non-empty binary. A non-binary or empty separator, an unknown pluralization key, and a non-keyword-list `pluralization` value each raise `ArgumentError`. An empty `pluralization: []` option is valid and means the defaults apply.

 ## Pluralization
 
-Gettext pluralization (`ngettext`, ...) is currently **not** supported. See open [issue #3](https://github.com/zebbra/gettext_sigils/issues/3).
+Use the `N` modifier and the `||` separator to split singular and plural forms. The `count` binding determines which form Gettext selects at runtime:
+
+```elixir
+~t"One error||#{count} errors"N
+# with count = 1 => "One error"
+# with count = 3 => "3 errors"
+```
+
+You can use explicit key syntax to bind `count` to an arbitrary expression:
+
+```elixir
+~t"One user||#{count :: length(users)} users"N
+```
+
+Under the hood, the sigil maps to Gettext's `dpngettext/6`:
+
+```elixir
+~t"One error||#{count} errors"N
+# =>
+dpngettext("default", nil, "One error", "%{count} errors", count)
+```
+
+`count` must appear as a binding in at least one of the singular or plural parts. Using `N` without a separator in the message raises an `ArgumentError`. Without the `N` modifier, `||` is treated as literal text.
+
+The `N` modifier can be combined with other modifiers: `~t"One error||#{count} errors"eN` uses the `errors` domain.
+
+### Custom separator
+
+The separator defaults to `||` (double pipe). You can override it globally via application config or per-module:
+
+```elixir
+# Application config
+config :gettext_sigils, pluralization: [separator: "✂️"]
+
+# Per-module
+use GettextSigils,
+  backend: MyApp.Gettext,
+  sigils: [pluralization: [separator: "<plural>"]]
+```
+
+## Usage Rules
+
+GettextSigils ships with usage rules and skills for LLM coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) via the [`usage_rules`](https://hexdocs.pm/usage_rules) library. See the [LLM guide](guides/llm.md) for setup instructions.

+defmodule GettextSigils.Pluralization do
+  @moduledoc ~S"""
+  Splits a parsed `~t` sigil into singular and plural forms for Gettext pluralization.
+
+  Pluralization is activated by the `N` modifier. When present, the message is
+  split on the separator into a singular and a plural form, and the `:count`
+  binding is extracted to be passed as the `n` argument to `dpngettext/6`.
+
+  ## Separator
+
+  The default separator is `||` (double pipe). It can be changed per-module or
+  globally:
+
+  ```elixir
+  # config/config.exs
+  config :gettext_sigils, pluralization: [separator: "✂️"]
+
+  # per-module
+  use GettextSigils,
+    backend: MyApp.Gettext,
+    sigils: [pluralization: [separator: "✂️"]]
+  ```
+
+  ## Examples
+
+  ```elixir
+  ~t"One error||#{count} errors"N
+  #=> dpngettext("default", nil, "One error", "%{count} errors", count)
+
+  ~t"One user||#{count :: length(users)} users"N
+  #=> dpngettext("default", nil, "One user", "%{count} users", length(users))
+  ```
+
+  The `count` binding must appear in at least one part (singular or plural).
+  It is removed from the bindings and only passed as the `n` argument.
+  """
+
+  @type singular() :: {binary(), Keyword.t()}
+  @type plural() :: {binary(), binary(), Macro.t(), Keyword.t()}
+
+  @spec split!(singular(), binary()) :: plural()
+  def split!({msgid, bindings}, separator) do
+    case String.split(msgid, separator) do
+      [_single] ->
+        raise ArgumentError,
+              "the N modifier requires a separator #{inspect(separator)} in the message, but none was found"
+
+      [singular, plural] ->
+        {count, remaining_bindings} = extract_count!(bindings)
+        {singular, plural, count, remaining_bindings}
+
+      _parts ->
+        raise ArgumentError,
+              "plural message contains more than one separator #{inspect(separator)}, expected exactly one"
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp extract_count!(bindings) do
+    case Keyword.pop(bindings, :count) do
+      {nil, _} ->
+        raise ArgumentError,
+              "plural message requires a \"count\" binding, but none was found"
+
+      {count, remaining} ->
+        {count, remaining}
+    end
+  end
+
+  def default_separator do
+    :gettext_sigils
+    |> Application.get_env(:pluralization, [])
+    |> Keyword.fetch!(:separator)
+  end
+end

+defmodule GettextSigils.PluralizationTest.Support do
+  @moduledoc false
+  def options_for(placement, pluralization) do
+    case placement do
+      :direct -> [backend: GettextSigilsTest.DummyGettext, pluralization: pluralization]
+      :sigils -> [backend: GettextSigilsTest.DummyGettext, sigils: [pluralization: pluralization]]
+    end
+  end
+
+  def compile_configured_module!(name, pluralization, function_source) do
+    Enum.find_value([:direct, :sigils], fn placement ->
+      options = options_for(placement, pluralization)
+
+      source = """
+      defmodule #{inspect(name)} do
+        use GettextSigils, #{inspect(options)}
+        #{function_source}
+      end
+      """
+
+      try do
+        Code.compile_string(source)
+        {name, placement}
+      rescue
+        _error -> nil
+      end
+    end) || raise "Neither supported pluralization option placement compiled"
+  end
+
+  def accepted_placement! do
+    probe = Module.concat(GettextSigils.PluralizationTest, "OptionPlacement#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
+
+    {_module, placement} =
+      compile_configured_module!(
+        probe,
+        [separator: "::"],
+        ~S/def message(count), do: ~t"One item::#{count} items"N/
+      )
+
+    placement
+  end
+
+  def compile_module!(options, function_sources) do
+    name = Module.concat(GettextSigils.PluralizationTest, "Runtime#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}")
+
+    Code.compile_string("""
+    defmodule #{inspect(name)} do
+      use GettextSigils, #{inspect(options)}
+    #{Enum.join(function_sources, "\n")}
+    end
+    """)
+
+    name
+  end
+
+  def compile_option_source(name, placement, pluralization) do
+    """
+    defmodule #{inspect(name)} do
+      use GettextSigils, #{inspect(options_for(placement, pluralization))}
+    end
+    """
+  end
+end
+
+defmodule GettextSigils.PluralizationTest do
+  @moduledoc false
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  alias GettextSigils.PluralizationTest.Support
+
+  describe "N modifier" do
+    @options [
+      backend: GettextSigilsTest.DummyGettext,
+      sigils: [
+        domain: "frontend",
+        modifiers: [
+          e: [domain: "errors"],
+          m: [context: "MyModule"]
+        ]
+      ]
+    ]
+
+    setup do
+      module =
+        Support.compile_module!(@options, [
+          ~S/def activates(count), do: ~t"One item||#{count} items"N/,
+          ~S/def combines_ne(count), do: ~t"One item||#{count} items"Ne/,
+          ~S/def combines_eN(count), do: ~t"One item||#{count} items"eN/,
+          ~S/def count_in_singular(count), do: ~t"#{count} item||many items"N/,
+          ~S/def removes_count(count, name), do: ~t"One #{name} item||#{count} #{name} items"N/,
+          ~S/def explicit_key(users), do: ~t"One user||#{count :: length(users)} users"N/
+        ])
+
+      {:ok, module: module}
+    end
+
+    test "activates pluralization", %{module: module} do
+      assert module.activates(2) == "frontend: 2 items"
+    end
+
+    test "combines with other modifiers in any order", %{module: module} do
+      assert module.combines_ne(2) == "errors: 2 items"
+      assert module.combines_eN(2) == "errors: 2 items"
+    end
+
+    test "count interpolation can appear in the singular part", %{module: module} do
+      assert module.count_in_singular(1) == "frontend: 1 item"
+    end
+
+    test "removes the count from the interpolated bindings", %{module: module} do
+      assert module.removes_count(2, "validation") == "frontend: 2 validation items"
+    end
+
+    test "count bound via explicit key syntax", %{module: module} do
+      assert module.explicit_key([1, 2, 3]) == "frontend: 3 users"
+    end
+  end
